1897 年汤姆孙（J. J. Thomson）在剑桥卡文迪许实验室证明阴极射线: In 1897, J. J. Thomson at Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratory proved that cathode rays consist of negatively charged particles; these particles were later called 'electrons.' He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1906 for this achievement.
线圈通电就有磁性、断电就消失，是继电器、电机和磁悬浮的基础。: When a coil carries current, it becomes magnetic; when the current stops, magnetism disappears. This is the basis for relays, motors, and magnetic levitation.
电流周围会产生磁场（[[p:lorentz|电磁力]]）；把导线绕成线圈，每一圈: Current generates a magnetic field ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]); by winding wire into a coil, the magnetic fields of each turn superimpose; inserting an iron core further amplifies the magnetized field hundreds or thousands of times.
电磁铁的好处是磁性可以\"开关\"和\"调节\"：通电就有磁性，断电就消失，电流: The advantage of an electromagnet is that its magnetism can act as a "switch" and a "regulator": it has magnetism when current flows, but disappears when the current stops; the stronger the current, the stronger the magnetic force. Changing the direction of the current reverses the magnetic poles. Electromagnets used in factories for lifting scrap steel, [[relay|relays]], loudspeakers, and nuclear magnetic resonance instruments all rely on this principle.
1820 年丹麦的奥斯特（Hans Christian Ørsted）发现电流能: In 1820, Hans Christian Ørsted from Denmark discovered that electric current causes a magnetic needle to deflect. In 1824, William Sturgeon from the UK created the first iron-core electromagnet; in the 1830s, Joseph Henry from the US used insulated wire wound densely in multiple layers to create a powerful electromagnet capable of lifting tons of weight.
电磁铁把电能变成可控的机械力，是电报、电动机和 [[maglev|磁悬浮]] 等: Electromagnets convert electric energy into controllable mechanical force, serving as the foundation for inventions such as telegraphy, electric motors, and [[maglev|maglev]] systems (see [[electric-motor]]).
用小电流控制电磁铁去开关大电流，是电报和早期计算机的\"开关\"。: Using a small current to control an electromagnet for switching large currents served as the "switch" for telegraphy and early computers.
一个小电流通过线圈产生磁力（[[p:lorentz|电磁力]]），吸动一片金属触: A small current flowing through a coil generates magnetic force ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]), attracting a metal contact point to connect or disconnect another circuit carrying large current; the two states of "connected/disconnected" can exactly represent 1 and 0 ([[p:boolean|Boolean logic & binary]]).
继电器就是\"用电控制的开关\"。线圈通电，衔铁被吸下，触点闭合；断电后弹簧把衔: A relay is essentially a "switch controlled by electricity." When the coil is energized, the armature is pulled down, closing the contacts; when power is cut, a spring pulls the armature back, opening the contacts. It can use weak current to control strong current. By connecting relays in series or parallel, one can achieve "AND, OR, NOT" logic.
1835 年美国的亨利（Joseph Henry）发明了继电器的原型，后被用于延: In 1835, Joseph Henry from the US invented the prototype of the relay, which was later used to extend telegraph lines: when signals weakened, the relay would "relay" and retransmit them at intermediate points.
继电器是电报网、电话交换机和第一代计算机（如 1941 年楚泽的 Z3）的核心元: Relays were core components of telegraph networks, telephone exchanges, and first-generation computers (such as Z3 by Konrad Zuse in 1941); later they were replaced by vacuum tubes and transistors, but are still ubiquitous in today's automobiles and appliances (see [[logic-gate]]).
让线圈在磁场中旋转产生电流，把机械能变成电能，几乎所有电力都来自它。: Allowing a coil to rotate within a magnetic field generates electric current, converting mechanical energy into electric energy; almost all electric power originates from this process.
穿过线圈的磁场一旦发生变化，线圈里就会产生电压（[[p:induction|电磁: Once the magnetic field passing through a coil changes, a voltage is generated within the coil ([[p:induction|Electromagnetic induction]]); therefore, by continuously rotating a coil within a magnetic field, one can generate power endlessly. Generators do not "create" energy; they merely convert the mechanical energy driving the rotor into electric energy ([[p:energy|Conservation of energy]]).
发电机由两部分组成：产生磁场的**磁极**和切割磁力线的**线圈**。线圈转到正: A generator consists of two parts: the **magnetic poles** that generate the magnetic field and the **coils** that cut across magnetic field lines. When the coil rotates directly facing the magnetic pole, the rate of change of magnetic flux passing through it is fastest, resulting in the highest voltage; after rotating 90°, the voltage becomes zero; upon further rotation, the voltage direction reverses—thus, a rotating generator naturally produces sinusoidal **alternating current**. To obtain direct current, a commutator must be added to reverse the current direction.
大型电站发电机通常让磁极（转子）旋转、线圈（定子）固定，这样大电流不必经过滑动接: Large-scale power station generators typically rotate the magnetic poles (**rotor**) while keeping the coils (**stator**) fixed, so that large currents do not need to pass through sliding contacts for output. The faster the generator is turned, the greater the output current; simultaneously, the electromagnetic "resistance" experienced by the rotor increases—therefore, when grid electricity usage increases, more steam must be supplied to the steam turbine to maintain rotational speed.
1831 年英国的法拉第（Michael Faraday）发现电磁感应，并做出第: In 1831, Michael Faraday from the UK discovered electromagnetic induction and created the first "disk generator." In 1866, Werner von Siemens and others from Germany invented self-exciting generators (using the generated electricity to excite electromagnets), making generators powerful and practical.
除了光伏和电池，世界上几乎所有的电都来自发电机——无论是被蒸汽、燃气、水流还是风: Except for photovoltaics and batteries, almost all electric power worldwide comes from generators—whether driven by steam, gas, water flow, or wind. It made [[power-grid|Power grid]] and [[electrification|Electrification]] possible.
发电机和 [[electric-motor|电动机]] 本质上是同一种机器：给它: Generators and [[electric-motor|Electric motor]]s are essentially the same machine: turning it generates electricity, while passing current through it makes it rotate. When an electric vehicle brakes, the motor is used as a generator to recover energy for battery charging.
线圈在磁场中旋转，穿过线圈的磁通量周期性变化，产生正弦交流电。: When a coil rotates within a magnetic field, the magnetic flux passing through the coil changes periodically, producing sinusoidal alternating current.
让通电线圈在磁场中受力旋转，把电能变成机械能，驱动从风扇到高铁的一切。: Allowing a current-carrying coil to experience force and rotate within a magnetic field converts electric energy into mechanical energy, driving everything from fans to high-speed trains.
磁场中的通电导线会受到一个力，方向与电流和磁场都垂直（[[p:lorentz|电: A current-carrying wire within a magnetic field experiences a force whose direction is perpendicular to both the current and the magnetic field ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]); when the wire is wound into a coil and placed in a magnetic field, the forces on opposite sides act in opposite directions, causing the coil to rotate.
直流电机的线圈转到一定位置后受力方向会反过来，所以需要**换向器**：每转半圈自: When a DC motor's coil rotates to a certain position, the direction of the force acting on it reverses; therefore, a **commutator** is required: every half rotation, the current direction is automatically reversed once, allowing the coil to continue rotating in one direction. AC motors instead utilize the inherent direction changes of alternating current, combined with three-phase windings to produce a **rotating magnetic field**, dragging the rotor along (see [[induction-motor]]). Modern motors increasingly use electronic circuits to replace mechanical commutation (see [[bldc-motor]]), paired with variable frequency drives for precise control of speed and torque.
电动机的效率很高，大型电机可达 95% 以上，远超内燃机；它从零转速起就能输出最: Electric motors have high efficiency; large-scale motors can exceed 95%, far surpassing internal combustion engines; they can output maximum torque from zero speed, making electric vehicles accelerate particularly quickly at startup.
1821 年法拉第做出了第一个能连续旋转的电磁装置。1834 年德国出生的雅可比: In 1821, Michael Faraday created the first electromagnetic device capable of continuous rotation. In 1834, Moritz von Jacobi, born in Germany, built the first practical rotating electric motor in Königsberg; in 1837, Thomas Davenport from the US obtained a patent for an electric motor. In 1888, Tesla's AC induction motor made electric motors truly widespread.
电动机是电力最大的用户：据国际能源署估计，电机系统消耗了全球约 45% 的电。从: Electric motors are the largest consumers of electricity: according to the International Energy Agency, motor systems consume approximately 45% of global electricity. From fans, washing machines, elevators, machine tools, water pumps, to high-speed trains and [[electric-vehicle|Electric vehicle (EV)]], they allow power to be distributed to every machine, fundamentally changing factory layouts (see [[electrification]]).
直流电动机：磁场中的通电线圈两侧受力方向相反而旋转，换向器每半圈翻转一次电流方向: DC electric motors: current-carrying coils within a magnetic field experience forces acting in opposite directions on opposite sides, causing rotation; the commutator flips the current direction once every half rotation, allowing continuous motion.
用三相交流电产生旋转磁场，\"拖着\"转子转，无需电刷，结实耐用。: Using three-phase alternating current to generate a rotating magnetic field "drags" the rotor along without brushes, making it robust and durable.
定子上的三组线圈通入相位相差 120° 的三相交流电，合成一个以固定速度旋转的磁: Three sets of coils on the stator are fed with three-phase alternating current with phase differences of 120°, synthesizing a magnetic field that rotates at a fixed speed. The rotor is typically an aluminum-cast "squirrel cage." When the rotating magnetic field sweeps over it, it induces current; the force on this current causes the rotor to follow along. The rotor always rotates slightly slower than the magnetic field (slip); otherwise, there would be no relative motion and no induced current. It has no brushes or slip rings, making its structure simple, robust, durable, and requiring almost no maintenance.
1885 年意大利的费拉里斯（Galileo Ferraris）和 1887–1: Induction motors were independently invented by Galileo Ferraris in Italy in 1885 and by Nikola Tesla in 1887–1888; Tesla's patent was acquired by Westinghouse.
用电子电路代替电刷换向的电机，高效安静，用于无人机、硬盘和电动车。: Motors that use electronic circuits to replace mechanical commutation via brushes are efficient and quiet, used in drones, hard drives, and electric vehicles.
无刷直流电机把永磁体放在转子上，线圈放在定子上。控制器根据霍尔传感器或反电动势判: Brushless DC motors place permanent magnets on the rotor and coils on the stator. The controller determines rotor position based on Hall sensors or back electromotive force, sequentially energizing sets of coils to form a magnetic field that chases the rotor. There is no brush wear or sparking; they are efficient, have long lifespans, produce little noise, and allow precise speed control.
1960 年代初，晶体管让电子换向成为可能；随着廉价功率半导体和高性能钕铁硼永磁: In the early 1960s, transistors made electronic commutation possible; with the widespread adoption of inexpensive power semiconductors and high-performance neodymium-iron-boron permanent magnets, it rapidly spread after the 1990s.
两组线圈共用一个铁芯，靠电磁感应把交流电升压或降压。: Two sets of coils share a single iron core, using electromagnetic induction to step up or step down alternating voltage.
1831 年法拉第用绕在铁环上的两组线圈发现电磁感应，这其实就是变压器的雏形。1: In 1831, Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction using two sets of coils wound around an iron ring; this was essentially the prototype of a transformer. In 1885, ZBD—Zipeľnovský, Bráša, and Déri from the Hungarian Guntz Factory—produced a practical closed-iron-core transformer; in 1886, William Stanley in the United States built the first AC power supply system for Westinghouse.
变压器：初级线圈中的交流电在铁芯里产生交变磁场，次级线圈按匝数比感应出更高或更低: Transformer: Alternating current in the primary coil produces an alternating magnetic field in the iron core, inducing higher or lower voltage in the secondary coil according to the turns ratio.
方向周期性来回变化的电流，最大优点是能用变压器轻松改变电压。: Current that periodically changes direction back and forth; its greatest advantage is the ability to easily change voltage using a transformer.
交流电的电压按正弦曲线变化，中国和欧洲每秒来回 50 次（50 赫兹），北美是: The voltage of alternating current changes according to a sine curve; in China and Europe, it reverses 50 times per second (50 Hertz), while North America uses 60 Hertz. The "220 volts" marked on household outlets represents the root mean square value, equivalent to a direct current voltage with the same heating effect, with an actual peak of approximately 311 volts. Alternating current also has the concept of "phase": motors and inductors cause current to lag behind voltage; the grid must compensate for this "reactive power".
1830 年代起人们就能造出交流发电机；19 世纪 80 年代，随着变压器和交流: Since the 1830s, people could build AC generators; in the 1880s, with the invention of transformers and AC motors, alternating current began to be used for transmission and distribution. The two standards of 50 and 60 Hertz were fixed in Europe and the United States respectively at the beginning of the 20th century.
三路相位错开 120° 的交流电，输电省铜，天然产生旋转磁场驱动电机。: Three sets of alternating current with phase offsets of 120° save copper in transmission and naturally produce a rotating magnetic field to drive motors.
三相输电用三根（或加一根中性线共四根）导线就能输送单相需要六根导线才能输送的功率: Three-phase transmission uses three wires (or four wires including a neutral line), delivering power that would require six wires for single-phase transmission, saving copper and money; power output is also more stable without pulsation like in single-phase electricity. Direct connection to an induction motor produces a rotating magnetic field without needing additional starting devices. Household electricity typically only draws one phase.
1891 年德国劳芬到法兰克福的 175 公里三相输电示范成功，俄国出生的工程师: In 1891, a three-phase power transmission demonstration of 175 kilometers from Laufen to Frankfurt in Germany succeeded. The engineer Mikhail Dolivo-Dobrovolsky, born in Russia, was the key designer.
三相电成为世界各地发电、输电和工业用电的标准（见 [[induction-mot: Three-phase electricity became the standard for generating, transmitting, and industrial power consumption worldwide (see [[induction-motor]], [[power-grid]]).
三相交流电：三条正弦波依次错开 120°，任意时刻相加为零，在电机中合成一个平稳: Three-phase alternating current: three sine waves are sequentially offset by 120°. At any moment, their sum is zero; in a motor, they synthesize a smooth rotating magnetic field.
保险丝、断路器和漏电保护在电流异常时自动断电，防止火灾和触电。: Fuses, circuit breakers, and ground-fault protection automatically cut off power when current anomalies occur, preventing fires and electric shocks.
电流的大小取决于电压和电阻（[[p:ohm|欧姆定律]]）；人体电阻有限，几十毫: The magnitude of current depends on voltage and resistance ([[p:ohm|Ohm's law]]); human body resistance is limited, and currents of tens of milliamperes passing through the heart can be fatal. Electrical safety provides a path for abnormal current that is better than the human body and cuts off power rapidly.
**保险丝**在电流过大时自己熔断；**断路器**（空气开关）在过载、短路时跳闸: **Fuses** melt themselves when current exceeds limits; **circuit breakers** (air switches) trip during overloads or short circuits and can be reused; **ground-fault protection devices** detect a difference of approximately 30 milliamperes between outgoing and returning currents and cut off power within tens of milliseconds; **ground wires** connect the metal casing of appliances to the earth, causing current to flow directly into the earth and trigger protection when the casing becomes live.
19 世纪 80 年代爱迪生的电力系统就使用了保险丝；1961 年美国的达尔泽尔: Edison's electrical power system in the 1880s used fuses; in 1961, Charles Dalziel of the United States invented a ground-fault circuit interrupter (GFCI).
这些装置让电从危险品变成了放心使用的日用品（见 [[power-grid]]、[: These devices transformed electricity from a dangerous substance into a safe daily commodity (see [[power-grid]], [[lightning-rod]]).
用电网把电送进工厂和家庭，让动力可以按需分配，重塑了生产和生活。: Using the power grid to deliver electricity to factories and homes allows power to be allocated on demand, reshaping production and life.
电能可以用细细的电线瞬间送到任何地方，再在终端变成光、热和动力；用户越多、电网越: Electricity can be sent instantly to any place via thin wires and then converted into light, heat, and power at terminals; the more users there are and the larger the grid, the lower the cost per kilowatt-hour ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]], [[p:network|Network effects]]).
电气化之前，工厂靠一台大蒸汽机通过长长的天轴和皮带带动所有机器，布局受制于动力传: Before electrification, factories relied on a single large steam engine driving all machines via long shafts and belts, with layout constrained by power transmission. With electric motors, each machine could have its own motor, allowing factories to reorganize layouts according to process flows, greatly increasing efficiency, making assembly lines possible. In homes, appliances such as light bulbs, refrigerators, and washing machines delegated a large amount of household labor to machines.
1880 年代起欧美城市开始建设电网；1920 年列宁提出\"共产主义就是苏维埃: Starting in the 1880s, European and American cities began constructing power grids; in 1920, Lenin proposed "Communism is Soviet power plus the electrification of the whole country"; in 1936, the United States passed the Rural Electrization Act to bring electricity to rural areas. According to international institutions, as of 2023, approximately 670 million people worldwide still lacked access to electricity, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa.
电气化被美国国家工程院评为 20 世纪最伟大的工程成就，是 [[second-i: Electrification was rated by the National Academy of Engineering as one of the greatest engineering achievements of the 20th century and is the core of [[second-industrial-revolution|the Second Industrial Revolution]] (see [[power-grid]], [[electric-motor]]).
用高速开关的半导体把电\"切碎再拼接\"，自由变换电压、频率和交直流。: Using semiconductors with high-speed switches to "cut" and then "splice" electricity allows free transformation of voltage, frequency, and alternating or direct current.
电压、电流在电路中的分配服从欧姆定律和基尔霍夫定律（[[p:ohm|欧姆定律与电: Voltage and current distribution in circuits obeys Ohm's law and Kirchhoff's laws ([[p:ohm|Ohm's law & circuits]]); by using semiconductor switches to rapidly turn on and off, and then using inductors and capacitors to "smooth out" pulses, desired voltages and waveforms can be synthesized while the switches themselves consume almost no power.
电力电子的基本动作是\"斩波\"：开关每秒通断几千到几百万次，调节\"通\"的时: The basic action of power electronics is "chopping": switches turn on and off thousands to millions of times per second, regulating the time proportion of "on" (duty cycle), causing the average voltage to change accordingly. This enables four types of conversion: alternating current to direct current (rectification), direct current to alternating current ([[inverter|Inverter]]), direct current to direct current, and alternating current to alternating current (frequency converter). Core devices evolved from thyristors to MOSFETs, [[igbt|IGBT]], to silicon carbide and gallium nitride (see [[wide-bandgap-semiconductor|Wide-bandgap semiconductors (SiC, GaN)]]).
1956 年美国贝尔实验室发明晶闸管（可控硅），通用电气公司随后将其商业化，电力: In 1956, the Bell Laboratory in the United States invented the thyristor (controllable rectifier); General Electric subsequently commercialized it, making power electronics a discipline from then on.
从充电器、变频空调到电动车、高铁、[[hvdc|高压直流输电]] 和风光并网，都: From chargers and variable-frequency air conditioners to electric vehicles, high-speed rail, [[hvdc|High-voltage direct current (HVDC)]] transmission, and grid-connected wind and solar power, all rely on power electronics.
把直流电变成交流电，是光伏、电池储能和电动车驱动的关键部件。: Converting direct current to alternating current is a key component for photovoltaics, battery energy storage, and electric vehicle drives.
交流电不过是方向和大小按正弦规律变化的电流；用半导体开关快速切换直流电的方向和通: Alternating current is merely current whose direction and magnitude change according to a sine law; by using semiconductor switches to rapidly switch the direction and on-off duration of direct current, and then filtering, a smooth alternating sine wave can be "spliced" ([[p:ohm|Ohm's law & circuits]]).
逆变器内部用四个或六个功率开关组成\"桥\"，按照脉宽调制（PWM）算法开关：需: Inside an inverter, four or six power switches form a "bridge," switching according to pulse-width modulation (PWM) algorithms: when high levels of the sine wave are needed, the forward conduction time is long; when low levels are needed, conduction time is short; then high-frequency components are filtered out using inductors and capacitors. Photovoltaic inverters also track the maximum power point, ensuring battery panels always operate at optimal voltage, and synchronize with the grid's frequency and phase.
早期逆变器用电子管和机械振子；20 世纪后半叶功率晶体管成熟后，逆变器变得小巧高: Early inverters used vacuum tubes and mechanical oscillators; after the maturity of power transistors in the second half of the 20th century, inverters became small and efficient, with efficiencies reaching over 98%.
光伏板、电池储能和电动车的电池输出的都是直流电，逆变器是它们与电网和交流电机之间: Photovoltaic panels, battery energy storage, and electric vehicle batteries all output direct current; the inverter acts as the "translator" between them and the grid and alternating current motors (see [[solar-pv|Solar photovoltaics]], [[electric-vehicle|Electric vehicle (EV)]], [[power-electronics|Power electronics]]).
兼具 MOSFET 易驱动和双极管耐大电流特点的功率开关，被称作电力电子的\"C: Power switches combining the easy drive characteristics of MOSFETs with the high-current tolerance of bipolar transistors are called the "CPU" of power electronics.
MOSFET 用电压控制、驱动省力（[[p:band|能带与半导体]]）；双极晶: MOSFETs are voltage-controlled devices that require little drive power (see [[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]); bipolar transistors can handle large currents with low conduction losses. IGBTs combine both structures, using the MOSFET gate to "turn on" a bipolar device structure.
IGBT 是一个电压控制的大功率开关：栅极加十几伏电压就导通，撤掉就关断，能控制: An IGBT is a voltage-controlled high-power switch: applying a voltage of several tens of volts turns it on, and removing it turns it off, controlling currents from hundreds to thousands of volts and hundreds to over a thousand amperes. Switching frequencies can reach tens of kilohertz. Many IGBT chips are packaged in parallel modules for use in motor drives and power conversion.
1980 年前后，美国通用电气公司的巴利加（B. Jayant Baliga）等: Around 1980, B. Jayant Baliga and others at General Electric Company in the United States developed the IGBT; it was published in 1982 and began commercialization in the late 1980s.
IGBT 是变频空调、电动车电驱、高铁牵引、风电变流器和柔性直流输电的核心器件（: IGBTs are core components in variable-frequency air conditioners, electric vehicle drives, high-speed rail traction systems, wind power converters, and flexible DC transmission (see [[power-electronics|Power electronics]], [[high-speed-rail|High-speed rail]]).
禁带更宽的半导体耐压、耐热、开关更快，让快充头和电动车电驱更小更省电。: Semiconductors with wider bandgaps offer higher voltage ratings, better heat tolerance, and faster switching, making fast-charging heads and electric vehicle drives smaller and more energy-efficient.
禁带越宽，电子越难被热或强电场\"激发\"成自由电子（[[p:band|能带与半: The wider the bandgap, the harder it is for electrons to be "excited" into free electrons by heat or strong electric fields (see [[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]); therefore, wide-bandgap materials can withstand higher voltages and temperatures, allowing devices to be made thinner, switch faster, and have lower losses.
Silicon's bandgap is approximately 1.1 electron volts; silicon carbide (SiC) is about 3.3, and gallium nitride (GaN) is about 3.4. Silicon carbide excels at high voltage and high power, used in electric vehicle main drive inverters, charging piles, and photovoltaic systems; gallium nitride excels at high frequency with extremely fast switching speeds, making fast-charging heads small blocks. The disadvantages are low yield rates and high prices.
2018 年前后，特斯拉 Model 3 在主驱逆变器中率先大规模采用碳化硅 M: Around 2018, Tesla's Model 3 was the first to adopt silicon carbide MOSFETs on a large scale in its main drive inverter; gallium nitride fast-charging heads also began to become popular at that time. Gallium nitride is also the material for blue light [[led|Light-emitting diode (LED)]].
它们让电能转换的损耗再降一截，续航更长、充电更快（见 [[power-elect: They further reduce power conversion losses, extending range and enabling faster charging (see [[power-electronics|Power electronics]], [[igbt|Insulated-gate bipolar transistor (IGBT)]]).
用每秒几万到几百万次的通断来变压，比老式变压器电源小而高效。: Voltage transformation is achieved by switching on and off tens of thousands to millions of times per second, which is smaller and more efficient than old-style transformer power supplies.
变压器的体积与工作频率成反比——频率越高，铁芯和线圈可以越小（[[p:induc: Transformer volume is inversely proportional to operating frequency—higher frequencies allow the iron core and coils to be smaller (see [[p:induction|Electromagnetic induction]]). Converting electricity into high-frequency pulses above tens of kilohertz before transformation can reduce the transformer size by over a hundred times.
开关电源先把市电整流成直流，再由 MOSFET 以每秒几万到上百万次的频率开关，: Switched-mode power supplies first rectify mains electricity into DC, then switch it using MOSFETs at frequencies from tens of thousands to over a million times per second, sending it into a small high-frequency transformer for step-down voltage, followed by rectification and filtering to output stable low-voltage DC. Control circuits adjust the duty cycle of the switches to regulate voltage. Efficiency can exceed 90%, whereas old-style linear power supplies often reach only about 50%.
开关电源在 1970 年代开始用于计算机；1977 年苹果 Apple II 采: Switched-mode power supplies began to be used in computers in the 1970s; in 1977, Apple II adopted the switched-mode power supply designed by Rod Holt, eliminating the need for a chassis fan.
今天的手机充电器、电脑电源、LED 灯驱动和电视几乎都用开关电源（见 [[pow: Today's mobile phone chargers, computer power supplies, LED lamp drivers, and televisions almost all use switched-mode power supplies (see [[power-electronics|Power electronics]], [[transformer-electrical|Transformer]]).
在真空中用电压控制电子流，第一次实现了电信号的放大和开关。: Controlling electron flow in a vacuum using voltage was the first realization of signal amplification and switching for telecommunications.
金属被加热后，表面的电子会\"蒸发\"出来（热电子发射），在真空中它们会被正电压: When metals are heated, surface electrons can "evaporate" out (thermal electron emission); in a vacuum, they are attracted and flown away by positive voltages (see [[p:charge|Electric charge & field]]); placing a negatively charged metal grid in between allows the flow of flying electrons to be controlled significantly with only small voltage changes.
最简单的**二极管**有两个电极：加热的阴极发射电子，带正电的阳极（板极）吸收电: The simplest **diode** has two electrodes: a heated cathode that emits electrons and a positively charged anode (plate) that absorbs them, allowing current to flow in only one direction for rectification and demodulation. A **transistor** adds a **gate** between the two: a slightly negative gate voltage blocks many electrons; a slightly positive one causes a large increase in electron flow. Thus, a weak signal on the gate is replicated as a strong signal in the anode circuit—this is **amplification**. Switching it between "fully on" and "fully off" also creates an electronic **switch**.
缺点是耗电发热、体积大、易烧毁：[[eniac]] 用了约 1.8 万个真空管，: The disadvantages are high power consumption and heat generation, large volume, and susceptibility to burning out: [[eniac|ENIAC]] used about 18,000 vacuum tubes, with one failing on average every few days.
1904 年英国的弗莱明（John Ambrose Fleming）发明真空二极: In 1904, John Ambrose Fleming in the United Kingdom invented the vacuum diode for detecting radio signals. In 1906, Lee de Forest in the United States added a gate to invent the triode "Audion"; its amplification capability was understood around 1912. In 1915, the United States used vacuum tube relay amplifiers to open long-distance telephone lines crossing the continent.
真空管开创了电子学：无线电广播、长途电话、电视、雷达和第一代电子计算机都靠它。1: Vacuum tubes pioneered electronics: radio broadcasting, long-distance telephony, television, radar, and the first generation of electronic computers all relied on them. After the 1950s, they were gradually replaced by [[transistor|Transistors]] that are small, energy-efficient, and have long lifespans; today they can still be seen in high-power transmitters and some audio equipment.
真空三极管：阴极发射的电子飞向阳极，栅极上的小电压变化控制着大电流——这就是放大: Vacuum triode: electrons emitted from the cathode fly to the anode, with a small voltage change on the gate controlling large current—this is amplification and switching.
三种最基本的被动元件：电阻限流、电容存电荷、电感存磁能，组合起来能滤波、定时、选: The three most basic passive components are resistors that limit current, capacitors that store charge, and inductors that store magnetic energy; combined, they can filter, time, and select frequencies.
电阻阻碍电流并把电能变成热（[[p:ohm|欧姆定律]]）；电容用两块隔开的极板: Resistors impede current and convert electrical energy into heat (see [[p:ohm|Ohm's law & circuits]]); capacitors store charge using two separated plates (see [[p:charge|Electric charge & field]]); inductors store energy using coil magnetic fields and impede sudden changes in current (see [[p:induction|Electromagnetic induction]]).
三者对变化快慢的反应各不相同：电阻对直流和交流一视同仁；电容\"通交流、隔直流\: Their responses to the rate of change differ: resistors treat DC and AC equally; capacitors "pass AC, block DC," becoming easier to pass at higher frequencies; inductors are exactly opposite, "passing DC and blocking AC." Combining them can accomplish various functions: resistors for voltage division and current limiting; capacitors for filtering power ripple, storing instantaneous energy, and timing with resistors; inductors and capacitors form resonant circuits that "select" one frequency from countless others, which is the principle of radio tuning (see [[p:wave|Interference, diffraction & resonance]]).
1745 年发明的莱顿瓶是最早的电容器；欧姆（Georg Ohm）1827 年发: The Leyden jar, invented in 1745, was the earliest capacitor; Georg Ohm published Ohm's law in 1827; Henry and Faraday discovered self-inductance and mutual inductance in the 1830s. Today, a single mobile phone contains thousands of tiny surface-mount resistors and capacitors.
这些不起眼的被动元件是所有电子电路的\"基本词汇\"（见 [[pcb]]、[[c: These unassuming passive components are the "basic vocabulary" of all electronic circuits (see [[pcb]], [[crystal-oscillator]]).
把一部分输出反向送回输入，牺牲一点增益换来稳定和低失真，是电子学最重要的技巧之一: Sending a portion of the output back to the input, sacrificing some gain in exchange for stability and low distortion, is one of the most important techniques in electronics.
把输出的一部分反向送回输入端，与原始信号比较，用差值来修正输出（[[p:feed: Sending a portion of the output back to the input end, comparing it with the original signal, and using the difference to correct the output (see [[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]); this makes the amplifier's gain determined primarily by several stable resistors, rather than being affected by parameter drifts in transistors or vacuum tubes.
一个原本增益很高但不稳定的放大器，加上负反馈后增益降低了，却换来了稳定、低失真和: An amplifier that originally had high but unstable gain, when equipped with negative feedback, lowers its gain but gains stability, low distortion, and a wider bandwidth. Poor design can lead to self-oscillation, like the whine heard when a microphone is placed near a speaker.
1927 年 8 月，贝尔实验室的布莱克（Harold Black）在上班的渡轮: In August 1927, Harold Black at Bell Labs conceived this idea on a ferry during his commute, wrote it down on a newspaper; the patent was not approved until 1937.
负反馈让跨越几千公里、串联几百个放大器的长途电话成为可能，也是 [[op-amp: Negative feedback made long-distance telephone calls spanning thousands of kilometers and chaining hundreds of amplifiers possible, and is also the foundation of [[op-amp|Operational amplifier]] and the entire field of [[control-theory|Control theory & PID]].
增益极高的通用放大器，配几个电阻电容就能加减、积分、滤波。: A general-purpose amplifier with extremely high gain, paired with a few resistors and capacitors, can perform addition, subtraction, integration, and filtering.
一个增益极高的放大器配上负反馈，整体性能就只由外接的电阻、电容决定（[[p:fe: An amplifier with extremely high gain equipped with negative feedback has overall performance determined solely by the externally connected resistors and capacitors (see [[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
运算放大器有两个输入端和一个输出端，放大两个输入之差，增益可达几十万倍。实际使用: Operational amplifiers have two input terminals and one output terminal, amplifying the difference between the two inputs with a gain reaching hundreds of thousands. In actual use, a feedback network must always be connected: connecting two resistors creates a precise amplifier, connecting a capacitor creates an integrator, and combining them can perform addition, subtraction, filtering, and comparison. It is called "operational" because it was originally used in analog computers for mathematical operations.
1947 年美国的拉加齐尼（John Ragazzini）等人在论文中命名了\": In 1947, John Ragazzini and others at the University of Illinois named "Operational amplifier" in a paper. In 1968, Fairchild Semiconductor launched the μA741 integrated operational amplifier, becoming one of the best-selling analog chips in history.
它是传感器信号调理、音频、仪器仪表等几乎所有模拟电路的基本积木（见 [[feed: It is the basic building block for almost all analog circuits including sensor signal conditioning, audio, and instrumentation (see [[feedback-amplifier|Negative-feedback amplifier]], [[analog-digital|Analog vs. digital signals]]).
利用石英片的压电共振产生极稳定的频率，是电脑、手机和石英表的\"心跳\"。: Utilizing the piezoelectric resonance of a quartz crystal to generate an extremely stable frequency serves as the "heartbeat" of computers, mobile phones, and quartz watches.
石英晶体受压会产生电压，加电压又会变形（压电效应）；切成特定形状的石英片有一个极: Applying pressure to a quartz crystal generates voltage, while applying voltage causes deformation (Piezoelectric effect); a quartz crystal cut into a specific shape possesses an extremely stable mechanical resonance frequency. Maintaining its vibration with a circuit yields a precise "heartbeat" (see [[p:wave|Interference, diffraction & resonance]]).
石英片两面镀上电极，接入放大电路组成振荡器，晶片只在自己的固有频率附近才能有效振: Electrodes are plated on both sides of the quartz crystal; when connected to an amplification circuit to form an oscillator, the crystal can only vibrate effectively near its natural resonant frequency. Thus, the circuit output provides a very stable frequency signal with errors as small as parts per million. Digital circuits use it as a clock, and the CPU's main frequency in computers is derived from multiplying the crystal oscillator's frequency.
1921 年美国的卡迪（Walter Cady）造出第一个石英晶体振荡器；192: In 1921, Walter Cady at Bell Labs built the first quartz crystal oscillator; in 1927, Warren Marrison at Bell Labs used it to build the first quartz clock.
晶振是电脑、手机、无线电和 [[quartz-watch|石英表]] 的\"节拍: The crystal oscillator serves as the "metronome" for computers, mobile phones, radio communications, and [[quartz-watch|Quartz watch]] (see [[piezoelectric-effect|Piezoelectric effect]], [[cpu|Central processing unit (CPU)]]).
用蚀刻铜箔代替手工飞线连接元件，让电子产品可以大规模制造。: Using etched copper foil to replace manual flying wire connections between components allows for mass production of electronic products.
元件之间的连线只是让电流按规定路径流动（[[p:ohm|欧姆定律与电路]]）；与: The wiring between components merely allows current to flow along prescribed paths (see [[p:ohm|Ohm's law & circuits]]; it is better to "print" the entire connection diagram at once on an insulating board than to solder wires individually, ensuring every board is identical (see [[p:standard|Standardization & interchangeability]]).
印刷电路板以玻璃纤维环氧树脂为基板，表面覆铜箔。工厂用光刻或丝印把线路图形转移到: Printed circuit boards use fiberglass epoxy resin as a substrate with copper foil plated on the surface. Factories transfer line patterns onto the copper foil using photolithography or screen printing, then etch away unnecessary copper to leave wires; multi-layer boards press multiple layers together, connected by drilled and electroplated "vias" between layers. Components can be inserted into holes for soldering, or mounted using Surface Mount Technology (SMT) where machines place them at high speeds and reflow solder them. Mobile phone mainboards can have as many as ten or more layers.
1936 年奥地利工程师艾斯勒（Paul Eisler）在英国做出第一块印刷电路: In 1936, Austrian engineer Paul Eisler made the first printed circuit board in Britain; during World War II, the United States used it for radio proximity fuses on artillery shells, and after the war, it became widespread in radios and televisions.
PCB 让电子产品可以自动化大规模生产，是从收音机到服务器一切电子设备的\"骨架: PCB allows electronic products to be automated for mass production, serving as the "skeleton" of all electronic equipment from radios to servers (see [[integrated-circuit|Integrated circuit (IC)]]).
导电性介于导体和绝缘体之间、能被精确调控的材料，硅是其中的主角。: Materials with conductivity between that of conductors and insulators, which can be precisely controlled; silicon is the protagonist among them.
固体里电子的能量只能落在一段段\"能带\"里，带与带之间是不允许停留的\"禁带\: In solids, electron energy can only fall into discrete "energy bands"; the space between bands is a forbidden "band gap" (see [[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]. Electrons in metals can flow freely; in insulators, the band gap is too wide for electrons to jump over; in semiconductors, the band gap is neither wide nor narrow, allowing electrons to "tip-toe" and jump over. Therefore, with slight changes, its conductivity can change by tens of thousands of times.
纯净的硅导电性很差：每个硅原子用 4 个电子和邻居手拉手，电子被牢牢\"锁\"在: Pure silicon has poor conductivity: each silicon atom holds hands with four electrons and its neighbors, with electrons firmly "locked" in covalent bonds. There are three ways to change its conductivity:
**掺杂**（最重要）：掺入百万分之一量级的磷，磷有 5 个电子，多出的那个能自: **Doping** (most important): Introduce phosphorus at a level of one part per million; phosphorus has five electrons, and the extra one can move freely, becoming **N-type** (negative charge conduction); introduce boron, which has only three electrons, leaving a "hole"—a **hole**, where adjacent electrons can jump in to fill it. The hole moves like a positive charge, becoming **P-type** (see [[doping]]).
**加电场**：在表面加电压，就能把电子吸过来或推开，这是 [[mosfet]]: **Apply an electric field**: Applying voltage at the surface attracts or repels electrons; this is the principle of [[mosfet]].
**加光和热**：光子或热能把电子激发过禁带，这是光伏电池和光电探测器的原理。: **Apply light and heat**: Photons or thermal energy excite electrons across the band gap, which is the principle of photovoltaic cells and photoelectric detectors.
1874 年德国的布劳恩（Karl Ferdinand Braun）发现某些晶体: In 1874, Karl Ferdinand Braun in Germany discovered that certain crystals allow current to pass only in one direction. In the 1930s, quantum mechanics' band theory explained why semiconductors behave this way. During World War II, crystal detectors used in radar research promoted high-purity germanium and silicon studies, paving the way for [[transistor|Transistors]].
半导体是现代电子工业的地基。硅储量丰富、能长出近乎完美的单晶、表面能生成优质绝缘: Semiconductors are the foundation of modern electronics industry. Silicon is abundant, can grow nearly perfect single crystals, and its surface can generate high-quality insulating layers, making it the protagonist; arsenide gallium, nitride gallium, etc., are used for radio frequency, LEDs, and lasers.
能带示意：金属的电子随意流动，绝缘体的禁带太宽，半导体的禁带窄到掺杂、电场、光照: Band diagram: Electrons in metals flow freely; the band gap of insulators is too wide; the band gap of semiconductors is narrow enough that doping, electric fields, and light can significantly change their conductivity.
把 P 型和 N 型半导体贴在一起，电流只能单向通过；它是二极管、LED、太阳能: When P-type and N-type semiconductors are joined together, current can only pass in one direction; it is the core of diodes, LEDs, and solar cells.
把 P 型和 N 型半导体贴在一起，交界处的电子和空穴互相扩散、中和，留下一层没: When P-type and N-type semiconductors are joined together, electrons and holes at the junction diffuse and neutralize each other, leaving a "depletion layer" without free charge carriers. Inside this layer, an internal built-in electric field forms ([[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]). This field acts like a one-way valve: current can only flow from P to N.
**正向偏置**（P 接正、N 接负）时，外加电压抵消了内建电场，耗尽层变薄，电: **Forward bias** (P connected to positive, N connected to negative): the external voltage cancels out the built-in electric field, the depletion layer becomes thinner, and electrons and holes cross the junction in large quantities; current flows smoothly through silicon diodes requiring about 0.6–0.7 volts to turn on; **Reverse bias**: the depletion layer becomes thicker, with almost no current—this is the rectification effect of the diode.
同一个 PN 结还能做很多事：电子和空穴在结区复合时放出光子，就是 [[led|: The same PN junction can do many things: electrons and holes recombine in the junction region releasing photons, which is [[led|LED]]; conversely, photons excite electron-hole pairs in the junction region, separated by the built-in electric field, which is [[solar-pv|Solar photovoltaics]] and photoelectric diodes; combining two PN junctions back-to-back forms a bipolar [[transistor|Transistor]].
1940 年 2 月，美国贝尔实验室的奥尔（Russell Ohl）在研究一块有: In February 1940, Russell Ohl at Bell Labs in America discovered that when studying a silicon sample with cracks, it produced voltage under light illumination, with different impurities on both sides of the crack—he thus discovered the PN junction and created the earliest prototype of a silicon solar cell.
PN 结是几乎所有半导体器件的基本结构：整流电源、充电器、LED 照明、光伏、激: The PN junction is the basic structure of almost all semiconductor devices: rectification power supplies, chargers, LED lighting, photovoltaics, lasers, and image sensors all rely on it.
PN 结：交界处形成耗尽层和内建电场。正向偏置时电流畅通，反向偏置时几乎截止——: PN Junction: A depletion layer and built-in electric field form at the junction. Under forward bias, current flows smoothly; under reverse bias, it is almost cut off—acting as a one-way valve for current.
用一个小信号控制大电流的半导体开关和放大器，是现代电子学的基本单元。: Using a small signal to control large current in semiconductor switches and amplifiers is the basic unit of modern electronics.
在半导体中，一个很小的电流或电压可以改变另一处载流子的多少，从而控制一个大得多的: In semiconductors, a very small current or voltage can change the amount of charge carriers elsewhere, thereby controlling a much larger current ([[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]). This "small controls large" function can both **amplify** signals and act as a **switch**—and the on/off states of the switch exactly represent 0 and 1 ([[p:boolean|Boolean logic & binary]]).
晶体管有三个电极。以双极型晶体管为例：在发射极和基极之间注入一个小电流，就能让集: Transistors have three electrodes. Taking bipolar transistors as an example: injecting a small current between the emitter and base allows a large current of tens to hundreds of times to flow through the collector. A slight change in base current causes a proportional, significant change in collector current—this is amplification; when base current is zero, the transistor cuts off; when it is sufficiently large, it fully turns on—this is switching.
和 [[vacuum-tube|真空管]] 相比，晶体管不需要加热灯丝、不需要真: Compared with [[vacuum-tube|Vacuum tubes]], transistors do not require heated filaments or vacuum, have small volume and low power consumption, almost infinite lifespan, and switching speeds continue to improve. Today, most transistors in chips are of another structure—field-effect transistors (see [[mosfet]]), controlled by voltage rather than current.
1947 年 12 月，美国贝尔实验室的巴丁（John Bardeen）和布拉顿: In December 1947, John Bardeen and Walter Brattain at Bell Labs in America made the first germanium point-contact transistor; their supervisor William Shockley subsequently proposed a more practical junction transistor in 1948. The three shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics. Shockley later founded a company in California; his eight departing "traitors" established Fairchild Semiconductor, from which Silicon Valley arose.
晶体管被许多人视为 20 世纪最重要的发明。它让收音机装进口袋（见 [[tran: Transistors are regarded by many as the most important invention of the 20th century. They allowed radios to fit into pockets (see [[transistor-radio]]), computers to shrink from a room to a desk, and further into a single [[integrated-circuit|chip]].
晶体管的两种用法：放大（小信号控制大电流）和开关（0 与 1）。左为 1947: Two uses of transistors: amplification (small signal controls large current) and switching (0 and 1). Left shows a schematic of the point-contact transistor from 1947.
用栅极电压在硅表面\"打开\"一条导电沟道的晶体管，几乎所有芯片都由它构成。: A transistor that "opens" a conductive channel on the silicon surface using gate voltage constitutes almost all chips.
在硅表面隔着一层极薄的绝缘层放一个金属电极（栅极），加上电压后，电场会把电子吸引: Placing a metal electrode (gate) separated by an extremely thin insulating layer on the silicon surface; adding voltage attracts electrons to the silicon surface, forming a "channel" that can conduct electricity ([[p:charge|Electric charge & field]], [[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]). The gate and channel are separated by an insulating layer, with almost no current flowing through it, so controlling it consumes almost no power.
MOSFET（金属—氧化物—半导体场效应晶体管）有源极、漏极和栅极三个端。以 N: MOSFET (Metal–oxide–semiconductor field-effect transistor) has three terminals: source, drain, and gate. Taking an N-channel device as an example: the source and drain are two N-type regions separated by P-type silicon; normally, no current flows. Adding positive voltage to the gate attracts electrons from the P-type silicon surface, forming an N-type channel connecting source and drain—the switch "turns on"; removing the voltage causes the channel to disappear—the switch "turns off".
MOSFET 结构简单，可以像印刷一样在硅片上平面地做出来，而且尺寸越小，开关越: The MOSFET has a simple structure and can be fabricated planarly on a silicon wafer like printing. Smaller dimensions result in faster switching, lower power consumption, and lower cost, making it the fundamental building block of integrated circuits. When scaled down to the nanometer scale, the channel becomes too short for the gate to control effectively, leading to severe leakage; consequently, three-dimensional [[finfet|FinFET and GAA]] structures were developed.
1959 年，美国贝尔实验室的埃及裔工程师阿塔拉（Mohamed Atalla）: In 1959, Egyptian engineer Mohamed Atalla and Korean engineer Dawon Kahng at Bell Labs in the United States invented the MOSFET, which was published publicly in 1960.
MOSFET 是人类制造数量最多的器件，美国计算机历史博物馆估计到 2018 年: The MOSFET is the most manufactured device by humans. The US Computer History Museum estimates that approximately 1.3×10²² units have been produced cumulatively as of 2018. CPUs, memory, flash storage, image sensors, and power switches are almost entirely composed of it (see [[cmos]], [[process-node]]).
MOSFET：栅极加正电压，电场在 P 型硅表面吸出一条电子沟道，源极和漏极之间: MOSFET: Applying a positive voltage to the gate creates an electric field that attracts electrons from the P-type silicon surface, forming a channel; conduction occurs between the source and drain terminals.
把 N 型和 P 型 MOSFET 成对使用，静止时几乎不耗电，成为数字芯片的标: Using N-type and P-type MOSFETs in pairs results in nearly zero power consumption when static, becoming the standard process for digital chips.
把一个 N 型 MOSFET 和一个 P 型 MOSFET 串在一起，同一个输入: Connecting an N-type MOSFET and a P-type MOSFET in series ensures that a single input voltage always turns one on while turning the other off ([[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]); since one is always open between power and ground, there is almost no current when static, consuming power only during switching transitions. These two transistors form exactly one NOT gate ([[p:boolean|Boolean logic & binary]]).
输入为 1（高电压）时，N 管导通把输出拉到地（0），P 管关断；输入为 0 时: When input is 1 (high voltage), the N-channel transistor conducts, pulling output to ground (0), while the P-channel transistor turns off; when input is 0, it reverses, and the output is pulled up to power by the P-channel transistor. Using such complementary pairs allows construction of NAND gates, NOR gates, and ultimately all digital circuits. Power consumption primarily comes from switching transitions and is proportional to frequency—this is also a reason why chip clock frequencies cannot be increased infinitely (see [[dennard-scaling]]).
1963 年仙童半导体的万拉斯（Frank Wanlass）和萨支唐（Chih-: In 1963, Frank Wanlass and Chih-Tang Sah at Fairchild Semiconductor proposed the CMOS circuit. It was initially used for power-sensitive electronic watches and calculators, becoming the mainstream process for digital chips from the 1980s onward.
低功耗让在一颗芯片上集成几十亿个晶体管成为可能；CMOS 工艺还被用来做图像传感: Low power consumption made it possible to integrate billions of transistors on a single chip; CMOS processes are also used for image sensors (see [[image-sensor]], [[logic-gate]]).
CMOS 非门：输入 1 时下方 N 管导通、输出 0；输入 0 时上方 P 管: CMOS NOT gate: When input is 1, the lower N-channel transistor conducts and output becomes 0; when input is 0, the upper P-channel transistor conducts and output becomes 1. At any moment, there is no direct conduction from power to ground.
把晶体管、电阻和连线一次性做在同一块硅片上，开启了芯片时代。: Fabricating transistors, resistors, and interconnects simultaneously on a single silicon wafer ushered in the chip era.
晶体管、电阻、电容和连线都能用同一种材料（硅）、同一套工序（光刻、掺杂、沉积）一: Transistors, resistors, capacitors, and interconnects can all be fabricated using the same material (silicon) and the same set of processes (photolithography, doping, deposition); it is better to "print" the entire circuit on a single wafer ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]]) than to manufacture them separately and solder them one by one. When processes remain unchanged, smaller graphics allow more elements per unit area, making each element cheaper ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]).
集成电路的制造像在硅片上一层层\"盖楼\"：先在晶圆上用 [[photolith: IC manufacturing is like "building a building" layer by layer on a wafer: first defining graphics using [[photolithography|Photolithography]] to create source/drain regions and grow gates for transistors, then covering with dozens of layers of metal interconnects, separated by insulating materials between layers and connected via tiny vias. Hundreds of chips can be simultaneously fabricated on a 300mm wafer; after dicing, packaging, and testing, we see the "chip".
集成解决了\"数字暴政\"：电路越复杂，手工焊点越多，一个出错整机就失灵；集成后: Integration solved "digital tyranny": as circuits become more complex, manual solder points increase, causing entire systems to fail with a single error; integration turns connections into lithographically defined metal lines, resulting in qualitative changes in reliability and cost.
1958 年 9 月，德州仪器的基尔比（Jack Kilby）在一块锗片上做出第: In September 1958, Jack Kilby at Texas Instruments created the first integrated circuit on a germanium wafer, but elements were still connected by gold wires; in 1959, Robert Noyce at Fairchild Semiconductor proposed single-wafer silicon ICs based on [[planar-process|Planar process]], with connections made directly on the chip surface—this became the mass-producible solution. Kilby received the 2000 Nobel Prize in Physics (Noyce had passed away in 1990).
集成电路开启了芯片时代：从 1960 年代阿波罗飞船的导航计算机，到 1971: Integrated circuits ushered in the chip era: from navigation computers on Apollo spacecraft in the 1960s to the first microprocessor in 1971, to today's GPUs integrating trillions of transistors (see [[moores-law]], [[soc]]).
从晶圆到芯片：一片晶圆上同时制造数百颗芯片，每颗芯片里是层层叠叠的晶体管和金属连: From wafer to chip: hundreds of chips are simultaneously manufactured on a single wafer, each containing stacked layers of transistors and metal interconnects.
用氧化层保护硅表面、层层光刻扩散制造器件，让集成电路可以批量生产。: Using an oxide layer to protect the silicon surface and performing layered photolithographic diffusion to fabricate devices enables batch production of integrated circuits.
硅表面能长出一层致密的二氧化硅，它既绝缘又能挡住杂质（[[p:structure: The silicon surface can grow a dense layer of silicon dioxide; it is both insulating and blocks impurities ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]); by opening windows in the oxide layer according to graphics, impurities diffuse only through the openings, allowing devices to be "printed" layer by layer while the surface remains protected.
先把硅片氧化，再用光刻在氧化层上刻出窗口，从窗口扩散掺杂形成 PN 结，然后重新: First oxidize the silicon wafer, then use photolithography to etch windows on the oxide layer; diffusion doping forms PN junctions through these windows, followed by re-oxidation, window opening, further doping, and finally evaporating aluminum for interconnects. All processes are completed on a single plane, resulting in stable and reliable devices capable of batch replication.
1959 年仙童半导体的瑞士裔物理学家赫尔尼（Jean Hoerni）发明平面工: In 1959, Swiss physicist Jean Hoerni at Fairchild Semiconductor invented the planar process; Noyce subsequently proposed single-wafer integrated circuits based on this foundation.
平面工艺是现代芯片制造的起点，\"光刻—掺杂—沉积\"的基本流程沿用至今（见 [: The planar process is the starting point for modern chip manufacturing; the basic workflow of "photolithography—doping—deposition" has been used to this day (see [[integrated-circuit]], [[photolithography]]).
芯片上的晶体管数量大约每两年翻一番——它是经验规律和行业目标，而非物理定律。: The number of transistors on a chip approximately doubles every two years—it is an empirical rule and industry target, not a physical law.
在同一块硅片上，图形尺寸缩小一半，就能放下约四倍的晶体管，而每片晶圆的加工成本增: On the same wafer, reducing graphic dimensions by half allows approximately four times more transistors to be placed, while processing costs per wafer increase only slightly; thus, each transistor becomes increasingly cheaper ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]); this "doubling every fixed time" growth is [[p:exponential|Exponential growth]], resulting in astronomical numbers over decades.

但市场要的汽油比原油\"天然含有\"的多，于是用**裂化**：在高温和催化剂作用: However, the market demands more gasoline than crude oil "naturally contains," so we use **cracking**: breaking long-chain molecules in heavy oil into short chains of gasoline size under high temperature and catalysts (see [[catalytic-cracking]]). There are also processes like reforming and hydrodesulfurization to increase octane rating and remove sulfur.
炼油让一桶原油变成汽油、柴油、航空煤油、润滑油和 [[petrochemical: Refining turns one barrel of crude oil into gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, lubricants, and [[petrochemicals|petrochemical raw materials]]. Plastics, synthetic fibers, and fertilizers all start here.
天然气常与石油共生，或单独存在于气田和页岩中。开采出来后经过净化脱去水、硫和二氧: Natural gas often coexists with petroleum or exists independently in gas fields and shale. After extraction, it is purified to remove water, sulfur, and carbon dioxide, then transported via high-pressure pipelines to cities before being depressurized for household use; for cross-ocean transport, it must first be liquefied (see [[lng]]). Its uses are broad: power generation, heating, cooking, and it is also a primary raw material for producing hydrogen and synthetic ammonia fertilizers.
它把分散的家庭和企业变成电网的\"调节器\"，是 [[smart-grid|智能: It turns dispersed households and enterprises into the grid's "regulators," serving as an important application of [[smart-grid|smart grids]] and [[grid-storage|grid-scale energy storage]].
LCOE 曲线的下滑是过去十几年能源转型最有说服力的证据（见 [[solar-p: The decline in the LCOE curve is one of the most compelling evidences of the energy transition over the past decade-plus (see [[solar-pv]], [[wind-turbine]]).
它用很低的成本削减了尖峰负荷，是 [[virtual-power-plant|虚: It reduces peak load at very low cost, serving as a key component of [[virtual-power-plant|virtual power plants]] and [[smart-grid|smart grids]].
市场化提高了效率，也带来价格剧烈波动和\"谁为备用容量买单\"等新问题（见 [[: Marketization has improved efficiency but also brought severe price fluctuations and new problems like "who pays for reserve capacity" (see [[lcoe]], [[demand-response]]).
电子的发现让人们知道电流是什么，也让\"控制电子的运动\"成为可能——[[vac: The discovery of electrons taught people what electric current is, making "controlling the motion of electrons" possible—[[vacuum-tube|vacuum tubes]], [[crt|cathode-ray tubes]], and later transistors all stem from this.
变化的磁场会在导体中感应出电流（[[p:induction|电磁感应]]），而这: A changing magnetic field induces current in a conductor ([[p:induction|electromagnetic induction]]), and these currents experience force within a magnetic field ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]); a rotating magnetic field can "drag" a rotor that itself carries no current to rotate.
感应电机是工厂里数量最多的电机，驱动着水泵、风机、压缩机和传送带；特斯拉公司早期: Induction motors are the most numerous motors in factories, driving pumps, fans, compressors, and conveyer belts; Tesla's early electric vehicles also used them (see [[three-phase-power]], [[electric-motor]]).
电脑风扇、硬盘、无人机、电动工具和大多数电动车都使用无刷电机或其变体永磁同步电机: Computer fans, hard drives, drones, electric power tools, and most electric vehicles use brushless motors or their variants, permanent magnet synchronous motors (see [[drone]], [[power-electronics]]).
它只能变换交流电：直流电产生的磁场恒定不变，次级线圈里感应不出电压。这正是 19: It can only transform AC: a DC current produces a constant, unchanging magnetic field, so no voltage is induced in the secondary coil. This was the fundamental reason why AC won over DC at the end of the 19th century (see [[war-of-currents]]).
变压器让高压远距离输电成为现实，是整个 [[power-grid|电网]] 的\: Transformers made high-voltage long-distance transmission possible, serving as the "hub" of the entire [[power-grid|power grid]]. From power plants to your home, electricity typically undergoes four or five transformations; even mobile phone chargers contain a miniature transformer (see [[switching-power-supply]]).
摩尔定律不是自然规律，而是被整个行业当作路线图\"自我实现\"的经验观察：大家都: Moore's law is not a natural law but an empirical observation that the entire industry treats as a roadmap for "self-fulfillment": everyone plans investments on a "one generation every two years" schedule, with each generation shrinking line width by about 30% and halving area.
从 1971 年英特尔 4004 的约 2300 个晶体管，到 2024 年英伟: From approximately 2,300 transistors in Intel's 4004 in 1971 to approximately 208 billion in NVIDIA's Blackwell GPU in 2024, growth over fifty years was about one hundred million times.
1965 年 4 月，仙童半导体的摩尔（Gordon Moore）在《电子学》杂: In April 1965, Gordon Moore of Fairchild Semiconductor published an article in Electronics magazine predicting that the number of elements on a chip would double every year; in 1975 he revised the prediction to doubling every two years. This name was promoted by Carver Mead of Caltech.
它是半个多世纪信息革命的总引擎：手机、互联网和人工智能都建立在算力指数级变便宜的: It has been the total engine of information revolution for more than half a century: smartphones, the internet, and artificial intelligence all rest on the foundation of computing power becoming exponentially cheaper.
说\"摩尔定律已死\"，准确地讲是尺寸缩小在放慢、成本不再同步下降，晶体管总数仍: Saying "Moore's law is dead" accurately means that size shrinkage is slowing down, costs are no longer declining in sync, but the total number of transistors continues to grow.
芯片晶体管数（对数坐标）：从 1971 年的约 2300 个到 2024 年的: Chip transistor count (on a logarithmic scale): from approximately 2,300 in 1971 to over 200 billion in 2024, roughly doubling every two years.
晶体管缩小时电压和电流同比缩小，功率密度不变；约 2005 年失效后 CPU 转: When transistors shrink, voltage and current shrink proportionally; power density remains unchanged; after failing around 2005, CPUs turned toward multicore architectures.
按登纳德的理论，尺寸缩小到原来的 0.7 倍，晶体管面积减半、速度提高约 40%: According to Dennard's theory, shrinking dimensions to 0.7 times the original halves transistor area, increases speed by about 40%, and halves power consumption per transistor; overall chip power density remains unchanged. This allowed CPUs from the 1980s to 2000s to "freely" gain higher clock speeds each generation. But when voltage dropped to around 1 volt, further reduction would cause transistors to close improperly and leakage to surge dramatically; with voltage unable to drop further, power density would skyrocket with frequency, causing chips to become too hot to cool.
把 CPU、GPU、内存控制器、基带、AI 单元等整个系统做进一颗芯片，是手机的: Putting an entire system including CPU, GPU, memory controller, baseband, AI units, etc., into a single chip is the heart of a smartphone.
手机的片上系统把 CPU（多个大小核）、GPU、神经网络处理器（NPU）、图像信: The smartphone's system-on-chip integrates multiple CPU cores (big and little), GPU, neural processing unit (NPU), image signal processor, video encoder/decoder, memory controller, modem (baseband), security module, etc., into a single chip. The system assigns tasks to the most power-efficient units: imaging goes to ISP, voice wake-up to low-power small cores, AI inference to NPU.
1970 年代的电子表和计算器芯片已是简单的片上系统；2000 年代智能手机兴起: Electronic watches and calculator chips from the 1970s were already simple system-on-chips; after smartphones rose in the 2000s, Qualcomm Snapdragon, Apple A-series, Huawei Kirin, etc., became the core of smartphones. In 2023, Apple's A17 Pro integrated approximately 19 billion transistors.
把高纯硅熔化拉成单晶硅棒再切成薄圆片，芯片就\"印\"在这张圆片上。: High-purity silicon is melted and drawn into single-crystal ingots, then sliced into thin wafers; chips are "printed" on these circular wafers.
先把石英砂还原成冶金级硅，再经化学提纯得到多晶硅。然后用**直拉法**：在 14: First, quartz sand is reduced to metallurgical-grade silicon, then chemically purified to get polysilicon. Then using the Czochralski method: melt polysilicon in a crucible at over 1,400 degrees Celsius, immerse a small seed crystal into the molten liquid, rotate it while slowly pulling upward; silicon atoms arrange along the seed crystal's lattice and solidify, drawing out cylindrical single-crystal ingots with diameters of 300 millimeters and lengths of about two meters. The ingots are sliced into thin sheets less than 1 millimeter thick, then ground and polished to mirror-like flatness with undulations not exceeding a few nanometers.
1916 年波兰化学家丘克拉斯基（Jan Czochralski）在研究金属结晶: In 1916, Polish chemist Jan Czochralski, while studying metal crystallization speed, accidentally dipped his pen into molten tin, drawing out a thin wire; this led to the invention of the Czochralski method. In the 1950s it was used for growing semiconductor single crystals.
晶圆越大，一次能做的芯片越多、单颗成本越低；主流尺寸从 1960 年代的 1 英: The larger the silicon wafer, the more chips can be produced in a single run and the lower the cost per chip; mainstream sizes grew from 1-inch wafers in the 1960s to today's 12-inch (300 millimeter) wafers (see [[semiconductor]], [[photolithography]]).
像照相一样用光把电路图案投影到涂了光刻胶的晶圆上，是芯片制造最关键的一步。: Projecting circuit patterns onto a silicon wafer coated with photoresist using light, like taking a photograph, is the most critical step in chip manufacturing.
光能改变某些材料的溶解性；让光透过印有电路图案的\"底片\"照射晶圆，就能像洗照: Light can change the solubility of certain materials; shining light through a "negative" film printed with circuit patterns onto a silicon wafer replicates the pattern like developing a photograph (see [[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]]). However, since light is a wave, images become blurred when features approach the wavelength scale due to diffraction, so the minimum feature size depends on the wavelength (see [[p:wave|Interference, diffraction & resonance]]).
一次光刻包括几步：: A single photolithography step includes several stages:
**涂胶**：在晶圆上旋涂光刻胶。**曝光**：把掩模上的图案经透镜缩小四倍投影: **Coating**: Spin-coat photoresist onto the silicon wafer. **Exposure**: Project a pattern from a mask through lenses at four times magnification onto the resist. **Development**: Wash away exposed (or unexposed) portions of the resist. **Etching or ion implantation**: Process underlying layers using the remaining resist as a template (see [[etching-deposition]]). Finally, remove the resist.
先进芯片要光刻几十次，每层对准误差在几纳米内。分辨率约与\"波长 ÷ 数值孔径\: Advanced chips require dozens of photolithography steps, with alignment errors between layers kept within a few nanometers. Resolution is approximately proportional to "wavelength ÷ numerical aperture"; therefore, engineers shorten the wavelength (436 nm → 193 nm, then to 13.5 nm [[euv-lithography|Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography]]), increase the numerical aperture (such as immersion lithography), and use multiple exposures to break resolution limits.
1957 年美国陆军实验室的拉斯罗普（Jay Lathrop）和纳尔（James: In 1957, Jay Lathrop and James Nall from the U.S. Army Research Laboratory first used photolithography to fabricate transistors; when they published this in 1958, they adopted the term "photolithography"; starting in 1959, it became central to [[planar-process|Planar process]] and integrated circuit manufacturing.
光刻是芯片制造中最关键、最昂贵的一步，决定了晶体管能做多小（见 [[proces: Photolithography is the most critical and expensive step in chip manufacturing, determining how small transistors can be made (see [[process-node]]).
光刻的基本流程：光透过掩模、经透镜缩小投影到涂胶的晶圆上，显影后留下的图形作为刻: The basic photolithography flow: light passes through a mask, is magnified four times by lenses, and projects onto a photoresist-coated silicon wafer; after development, the remaining pattern serves as a template for etching or doping.
用 13.5 纳米波长的极紫外光刻出更细的线条；目前只有荷兰 ASML 能造整机: Use 13.5-nanometer wavelength extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light to expose finer lines; currently, only Dutch company ASML can manufacture complete machines.
光刻能刻出的最细线条与光的波长成正比（[[p:wave|衍射]]）；把波长从 1: The finest lines that photolithography can resolve are proportional to the wavelength of light (see [[p:wave|Diffraction]]); shortening the wavelength from 193 nm down to 13.5 nm allows a single exposure to create patterns that would otherwise require three or four exposures. However, this light is almost absorbed by all materials, including air, so it must be guided using mirrors in a vacuum (see [[p:optics|Reflection]]).
EUV 光刻机用高功率二氧化碳激光每秒约五万次轰击下落的微小锡滴，把锡打成等离子: EUV lithography machines use high-power carbon dioxide lasers to strike falling tin droplets approximately 50,000 times per second, turning the tin into plasma and emitting 13.5-nanometer extreme ultraviolet light. The light passes through ultra-flat mirrors composed of molybdenum-silicon multilayer films (manufactured by Zeiss in Germany) and reflects layer after layer before finally projecting the mask pattern onto the silicon wafer. Each machine weighs over 150 tons and requires several cargo planes for batch transportation.
极紫外光刻的研究始于 1980 年代，荷兰 ASML 历经约二十年研发，2019: Research into EUV lithography began in the 1980s; ASML of the Netherlands spent approximately twenty years developing it, and Samsung and TSMC first used EUV for mass production of 7-nanometer chips in 2019. Newer high numerical aperture (High-NA) EUV lithography machines have begun delivery in the mid-2020s.
EUV 是 7 纳米以下先进芯片的必需品，而全球只有 ASML 能制造整机，这使: EUV is essential for advanced chips below 7 nanometers, and since only ASML can manufacture complete machines globally, it has become a focal point of technological competition (see [[semiconductor-geopolitics]], [[photolithography]]).
每立方米空气中尘埃颗粒被严格控制的车间，一粒灰尘就可能毁掉一颗芯片。: In cleanrooms where dust particles per cubic meter are strictly controlled, even a single grain of dust can destroy a chip.
微粒会随气流飘动、在静止空气中慢慢沉降（[[p:diffusion|扩散]]）；: Particles float with airflow and slowly settle in still air (see [[p:diffusion|Diffusion & membranes]]); by continuously forcing filtered air to flow unidirectionally from ceiling to floor, dust generated by people and machines is constantly "flushed" down to the floor for removal.
一粒灰尘落在芯片上，就像巨石压在马路上。洁净室用高效过滤器过滤空气，最高等级的车: A single grain of dust landing on a chip is like a boulder crushing a road. Cleanrooms use high-efficiency filters; in the highest-grade cleanrooms, there are no more than 10 particles larger than 0.1 micrometer in diameter per cubic meter, whereas ordinary outdoor air contains tens of millions. Staff wear full-body "rabbit suits" and must pass through an air shower to enter; wafers are typically transported automatically inside sealed boxes.
1960 年前后美国桑迪亚国家实验室的惠特菲尔德（Willis Whitfiel: Around the early 1960s, Willis Whitfield from Sandia National Laboratory in the U.S. invented laminar flow cleanrooms, which were widely adopted by the semiconductor and aerospace industries within a few years.
向硅中加入微量硼或磷，精确改变它导电的方式和强弱。: Adding trace amounts of boron or phosphorus to silicon precisely changes its conductivity method and strength.
在硅晶格里替换进极少量外来原子，就能凭空多出可移动的电子或空穴（[[p:band: Replacing an extremely small number of foreign atoms within the silicon crystal lattice creates mobile electrons or holes out of thin air (see [[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]); how much is doped, where it is doped, and to what depth determines device performance.
早期用高温**扩散**：把晶圆放进含硼或磷的高温炉里，杂质原子从表面慢慢渗进去（: Early doping used high-temperature **diffusion**: placing the silicon wafer in a high-temperature furnace containing boron or phosphorus, allowing impurity atoms to slowly diffuse inward from the surface (see [[p:diffusion|Diffusion & membranes]]). Modern manufacturing primarily uses **ion implantation**: ionizing impurity atoms and accelerating them into high-speed "bullets" using electric fields to drive them into the silicon wafer, with depth and dose precisely controlled; subsequent high-temperature annealing repairs the disordered lattice, allowing impurities to "return to their positions".
1950 年代贝尔实验室发展出扩散掺杂技术；离子注入在 1970 年代成为芯片制: Diffusion doping technology was developed by Bell Labs in the 1950s; ion implantation became a standard process for chip manufacturing in the 1970s.
精确掺杂让晶体管的源极、漏极和阱区可以按纳米精度\"画\"出来（见 [[semi: Precise doping allows the source, drain, and well regions of transistors to be "drawn" with nanometer precision (see [[semiconductor]], [[pn-junction|p–n junction & diode]]).
一层层\"长膜\"再按图形\"挖掉\"，重复几十上百次堆出芯片的立体结构。: Layers of 'grown films' are then 'carved away' according to patterns, repeated dozens or hundreds of times to build the three-dimensional structure of a chip.
芯片的立体结构靠\"加法\"和\"减法\"交替完成：沉积是让原子或分子在表面结合: The three-dimensional structure of a chip is completed by alternating 'addition' and 'subtraction': deposition allows atoms or molecules to combine on a surface to form a thin film, while etching removes unwanted parts using chemical reactions or ion bombardment ([[p:bond|Chemical bonds & chemical energy]]).
**沉积**有多种方法：化学气相沉积让气体在晶圆表面反应生成薄膜；物理气相沉积把: **Deposition** has several methods: Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) allows gases to react on the wafer surface to generate a thin film; Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) 'sputters' metal onto the surface; **Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD)** grows only one layer of atoms at a time, enabling uniform film deposition in deep trenches. **Etching** uses the photoresist pattern as a template, using active ions from plasma to 'dig' vertically downward, creating trenches and vias with very large aspect ratios. A single chip must undergo over a thousand such processes.
原子层沉积由芬兰的松托拉（Tuomo Suntola）在 1974 年发明；等离: Atomic Layer Deposition was invented by Tuomo Suntola at the University of Helsinki in 1974; plasma etching replaced wet etching during the 1970–1980s.
沉积和刻蚀设备与光刻机一起构成芯片制造的三大核心装备（见 [[photolith: Deposition and etching equipment, along with lithography machines, constitute the three core pieces of equipment for chip manufacturing (see [[photolithography]], [[finfet]]).
把晶体管沟道立成\"鳍\"或\"纳米片\"，让栅极从多面包住它，以抑制漏电继续微: Transistor channels are formed into 'fins' or 'nanosheets', allowing the gate to surround them from multiple sides to suppress leakage and continue miniaturization.
晶体管越小，栅极到沟道底部的\"控制力\"越弱，电子会从下面偷偷溜过去——这就是: The smaller the transistor, the weaker the 'control force' from the gate to the bottom of the channel; electrons can sneak past from below—this is leakage. At the nanometer scale, [[p:tunneling|Quantum tunneling]] also occurs. By standing up the channel and letting the gate surround it from three or even four sides, control becomes much stronger ([[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]).
传统平面晶体管的栅极只在沟道上方。**FinFET** 把沟道做成一片竖起的薄\: Traditional planar transistors have gates only above the channel. **FinFET** forms the channel as a vertical thin 'fin', with the gate spanning over it like a saddle, controlling it from the left, right, and top sides. **GAA** (Gate-All-Around) goes further, forming the channel as stacked horizontal nanosheets, completely wrapped by the gate from all four sides. These three-dimensional structures allow transistors to turn off more tightly and save more power while shrinking.
1999 年加州大学伯克利分校胡正明（Chenming Hu）团队提出 FinF: Chenming Hu's team at UC Berkeley proposed FinFET in 1999; Intel announced 'trigate' (22nm) transistors in 2011, which were mass-produced the following year. Samsung first mass-produced GAA at 3nm in 2022; TSMC's 2nm (N2) was mass-produced in Q4 of 2025, also using a GAA structure.
立体晶体管让摩尔定律在平面晶体管\"失效\"后又延续了十多年（见 [[mosfe: Three-dimensional transistors allowed Moore's Law to continue for over a decade after becoming 'invalid' for planar transistors (see [[mosfet]], [[process-node]]).
从平面晶体管到 FinFET 再到 GAA：栅极从一面、三面到四面包住沟道，对电: From planar transistors to FinFET to GAA: the gate surrounds the channel from one side, three sides, and then four sides, providing increasingly strong control over current.
\"7nm、3nm\"等是工艺代际的商业名称，已不再等于任何实际尺寸，但越小代表: '7nm', '3nm', etc. are commercial names for process generations; they no longer equal any actual physical dimension, but smaller numbers represent higher density and lower power consumption.
晶体管和连线越小，同样面积放下的越多、开关越快、越省电（[[p:scale|规模: The smaller the transistors and interconnects, the more that can be placed in the same area, the faster the switching, and the more power-efficient ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]); however, when shrinking to a few nanometers, the limited number of atoms leads to increased leakage and tunneling ([[p:tunneling|Quantum tunneling]]), requiring each generation to tackle these challenges with new structures and materials.
工艺节点原本指晶体管栅极的长度，例如 1990 年代的 0.35 微米确实如此。: Process nodes originally referred to the length of the transistor gate; for example, 0.35 microns in the 1990s was indeed so. Starting from the late 1990s, names began to decouple from actual dimensions, becoming 'generation numbers': a so-called '3nm' process has a transistor gate spacing of about 48nm and metal line spacing of twenty to thirty nanometers. Different companies have different densities for their named nodes; therefore, Intel renamed its own processes in 2021 as 'Intel 7', 'Intel 4', etc., to benchmark against competitors.
台积电 3 纳米于 2022 年底量产，2 纳米于 2025 年第四季度量产；英: TSMC mass-produced its 3nm process at the end of 2022 and its 2nm process in Q4 of 2025; Intel began mass production of its 18A process in 2025.
读懂这一点就不会被营销数字迷惑：比较工艺要看晶体管密度、性能和功耗，而不是名字里: Understanding this point prevents being misled by marketing numbers: when comparing processes, look at transistor density, performance, and power consumption, not the 'nanometer' name (see [[moores-law]], [[finfet]], [[foundry-model]]).
台积电开创\"只制造、不设计\"的代工模式，让无晶圆厂芯片公司大量涌现。: TSMC pioneered the 'manufacture-only, no design' foundry model, leading to the emergence of numerous chip design companies without their own fabrication plants.
建一座先进晶圆厂要花几百亿美元，只有极大的产量才能摊薄成本（[[p:scale|: Building an advanced semiconductor fab costs hundreds of billions of dollars; only extremely high volumes can amortize these costs ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]); allowing one company to specialize in manufacturing and serve all design companies enables both design and manufacturing to focus on their respective strengths ([[p:division|Division of labor]]).
在代工模式出现前，芯片公司都要自己设计、自己制造（IDM 模式）。代工厂不设计自: Before the foundry model emerged, chip companies had to design and manufacture themselves (IDM model). Foundries do not design chips for their own brands; therefore, they do not compete with customers. They provide customers with process 'design rules' and standard cell libraries; clients use [[eda|Electronic design automation (EDA)]] software to design layouts and deliver them to foundries for production. This led to the emergence of 'foundry-less' companies that only design but do not manufacture, such as NVIDIA, Qualcomm, Apple's chip division, and AMD.
1987 年张忠谋（Morris Chang）在台湾创办台积电（TSMC），首创: In 1987, Morris Chang founded TSMC in Taiwan, creating the pure foundry model. According to TrendForce, TSMC accounted for 72.5% of global top ten foundry revenue in Q2 of 2026.
代工模式大大降低了做芯片的门槛，催生了数以千计的芯片设计公司；但先进制造也因此高: The foundry model greatly lowered the threshold for making chips, spawning thousands of chip design companies; however, advanced manufacturing has also become highly concentrated in a few regions (see [[semiconductor-geopolitics|Semiconductor supply chain & export controls]]).
用软件设计、仿真和验证有数十亿晶体管的芯片，没有它现代芯片无法被设计出来。: Using software to design, simulate, and verify chips with billions of transistors makes modern chip design impossible without it.
再聪明的工程师也无法手工画出几百亿个晶体管；把设计分成系统、逻辑、电路、版图等层: Even the smartest engineers cannot manually draw hundreds of billions of transistors; by dividing design into layers such as system, logic, circuit, and layout, each layer uses software to automatically generate and check the next layer ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]]).
芯片设计流程大致是：用硬件描述语言（如 Verilog）写出功能 → 仿真验证功: The chip design flow is roughly: write functionality using hardware description languages (such as Verilog) → simulate and verify correct functionality → **Synthesis** tools translate code into logic gate netlists → **Place and Route** tools arrange billions of gates and connect them → check timing, power, and manufacturing rules → output layout files to the foundry. Every step depends on EDA software; verification often consumes most of the workload because a chip cannot be changed once it is fabricated.
1973 年加州大学伯克利分校发布电路仿真程序 SPICE；1979 年米德和康: In 1973, the University of California, Berkeley released the circuit simulation program SPICE. In 1979, Mead and Conway's "Introduction to VLSI Systems" made chip design teachable in a systematic way. Today, the market is dominated by Synopsys, Cadence, and Siemens EDA.
EDA 是芯片产业中规模不大却不可替代的环节，也是出口管制的对象之一（见 [[f: EDA is a small but indispensable link in the semiconductor industry, and it is also one of the targets of export controls (see [[foundry-model|Foundry model]], [[integrated-circuit|Integrated circuit (IC)]]).
把大芯片拆成几块小芯片再紧密封装在一起，良率更高，也能混用不同工艺。: Breaking large chips into several smaller chips and then tightly packaging them together improves yield and allows mixing different processes.
一块硅片越大，上面出现致命缺陷的概率越高，良率按面积急剧下降（[[p:scale: The larger a silicon wafer, the higher the probability of fatal defects appearing on it; yield drops sharply with area (see [[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]). Breaking large chips into smaller chips for separate manufacturing, then selecting the good ones to assemble together, results in lower overall costs (see [[p:division|Division of labor]]).
小芯片（chiplet）各自负责计算、输入输出、缓存等功能，可以用不同的工艺制造: Small chips (chiplets) are responsible for computing, input/output, cache, and other functions; they can be manufactured using different processes: compute cores use the most advanced process, while interface parts use cheaper mature processes. They are packaged together via extremely short and dense interconnections through silicon interposers, silicon bridges, or 3D stacking, communicating with each other almost as if on a single chip. AI chips also package compute chips and multi-layer stacked high-bandwidth memory (HBM) together.
2019 年 AMD 第二代霄龙处理器把 CPU 拆成多个计算小芯片加一个输入输: In 2019, AMD's second-generation Ryzen processor split the CPU into multiple compute small chips plus an input/output chip, bringing this approach to mainstream use. In 2022, Intel, AMD, TSMC, and others formed the UCIe alliance to establish standards for chiplet interconnection.
先进封装已成为延续摩尔定律的主要手段之一，台积电的 CoWoS 封装产能一度成为: Advanced packaging has become one of the main means to extend Moore's Law; TSMC's CoWoS packaging capacity once became a bottleneck for AI chip supply (see [[gpu|Graphics processing unit (GPU)]], [[process-node|Process node]]).
芯片供应链高度集中在少数国家和公司，已成为大国科技竞争的焦点。: The semiconductor supply chain is highly concentrated among a few countries and companies, becoming a focal point of great-power technological competition.
芯片制造链条极长，每一环都被少数最擅长的国家和公司占据（[[p:division: The chip manufacturing chain is extremely long; each link is occupied by the few most capable countries and companies (see [[p:division|Division of labor & specialization]]); efficiency is extremely high, but if any link is blocked, the entire chain will halt.
