设计软件和高端芯片设计集中在美国，光刻机集中在荷兰，先进制造集中在台湾地区和韩国: Design software and high-end chip design are concentrated in the United States; lithography machines are concentrated in the Netherlands; advanced manufacturing is concentrated in Taiwan and South Korea; materials and some equipment are concentrated in Japan; packaging/testing and large volumes of mature processes are in mainland China and Southeast Asia. The "chip shortage" during the COVID-19 pandemic caused mass production stoppages for car manufacturers, making countries realize the fragility of the supply chain.
2022 年 8 月美国通过《芯片与科学法案》补贴本土制造；同年 10 月出台针: In August 2022, the United States passed the "Chips and Science Act" to subsidize domestic manufacturing; in October of the same year, it issued export controls targeting advanced computing chips and manufacturing equipment, which has been expanded multiple times since. The Netherlands and Japan have also followed suit.
芯片已成为与石油同等重要的战略资源，各国纷纷投入巨资建设本土产能（见 [[fou: Chips have become a strategic resource equally important to oil; countries are investing heavily to build local capacity (see [[foundry-model|Foundry model]], [[euv-lithography|Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography]]).
模拟信号连续变化、容易受噪声影响；数字信号只取 0 和 1，可以无损复制和纠错。: Analog signals change continuously and are easily affected by noise; digital signals only take 0 and 1, allowing lossless copying and error correction.
模拟信号的每一点细微变化都携带信息，所以噪声一混进来就分不开；数字信号只区分 0: Every subtle change in an analog signal carries information, so once noise mixes in, it cannot be separated; digital signals only distinguish 0 and 1, so as long as the noise is not large enough to cause a 0 to be mistaken for a 1, perfect restoration is possible, and error-correcting codes can automatically correct mistakes (see [[p:redundancy|Redundancy & error correction]]). Continuous sounds and images can become lossless digital data if sampled densely enough (see [[p:sampling|Sampling & digitization]]).
模拟信号像一条连续起伏的曲线，例如话筒输出的电压随声音连续变化；数字信号则先按固: Analog signals are like continuous undulating curves; for example, the voltage output by a microphone changes continuously with sound. Digital signals first **sample** at fixed time intervals, then **quantize** each sample's magnitude into a finite number of digital levels. The cost of digitization is requiring more bandwidth and computation, but it brings the ability to copy infinitely without distortion, compress, encrypt, and process all types of information with the same chip set.
1928 年奈奎斯特（Harry Nyquist）、1949 年香农（Claud: Nyquist (Harry Nyquist) in 1928 and Shannon (Claude Shannon) in 1949 laid the foundation for the sampling theorem; Reeves (Alec Reeves) in Britain in 1937 invented pulse-code modulation (PCM).
从唱片到 CD、从模拟电视到数字电视、从 1G 到 2G 手机，\"数字化\"是: From records to CDs, from analog television to digital television, from 1G to 2G mobile phones, "digitization" was the main theme of information technology in the late 20th century (see [[adc|ADC / DAC]], [[digital-signal-processing|Digital signal processing (DSP)]]).
模拟信号连续变化；按时间采样、按大小量化后，变成一串可以无损复制的数字。: Analog signals change continuously; after sampling by time and quantizing by magnitude, they become a string of digital data that can be copied without loss.
把连续的电压按时间采样、按大小量化成数字，或反过来还原成电压。: Sampling continuous voltage by time and quantizing by magnitude into numbers, or conversely, restoring it to voltage.
连续的信号只要以高于其最高频率两倍的速度采样，就能被一串数字完整描述（[[p:s: Continuous signals can be completely described by a string of numbers if sampled at a rate higher than twice their highest frequency (see [[p:sampling|Sampling & digitization]]).
模数转换器（ADC）每隔固定时间\"拍一张快照\"，把当时的电压与一系列参考电压: Analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) take a "snapshot" at fixed intervals, comparing the current voltage against a series of reference voltages and recording it with several bits of binary numbers: more bits mean finer scales; for example, 16-bit means 65536 levels. Digital-to-analog converters (DACs) do the reverse, turning numbers back into voltage, then smoothing them into continuous waveforms. CDs use 44.1 kilohertz and 16-bit because the human ear hears at most about 20 kilohertz.
二战后随着脉冲编码调制通信发展，ADC 逐步成熟；1980 年代起它们被大量集成: After World War II, with the development of pulse-code modulation communications, ADCs gradually matured; starting in the 1980s, they were integrated into consumer electronics chips in large volumes.
ADC 和 DAC 是物理世界与数字世界之间的\"海关\"，手机里的话筒、摄像头: ADCs and DACs are the "customs" between the physical world and the digital world; microphones, cameras, and wireless transceivers inside mobile phones cannot function without them (see [[analog-digital|Analog vs. digital signals]], [[mp3|MP3 & audio compression]], [[image-sensor|Image sensor (CCD / CMOS)]]).
出厂后还能反复\"重新接线\"的芯片，用于原型验证、通信和低延迟计算。: Chips that can be repeatedly "re-wired" after manufacturing are used for prototype verification, communications, and low-latency computing.
FPGA 内部有成千上万个可编程逻辑单元，每个单元用一张小真值表实现任意逻辑函数: Inside an FPGA there are hundreds of thousands of programmable logic cells; each cell implements any arbitrary logic function using a small truth table, while connections between cells are controlled by configuration bits stored in the chip. Engineers write circuits using hardware description languages, and tools automatically generate configuration files downloaded into the chip; new hardware can be "created" in minutes; changing designs only requires re-downloading. It is slower, more expensive, and consumes more power than dedicated chips but is much faster than general-purpose CPUs, making it suitable for applications requiring parallelism and low latency.
1985 年美国赛灵思（Xilinx）公司推出第一款商用 FPGA XC2064: In 1985, Xilinx Corporation of the United States launched the first commercial FPGA, the XC2064; its co-founder Ross Freeman was a key inventor. Xilinx was acquired by AMD in 2022.
为单一任务定制的芯片，效率最高但设计贵、改不了，比特币矿机和 AI 芯片都属于此: Chips customized for single tasks offer the highest efficiency but are expensive to design and cannot be modified; Bitcoin mining machines and AI chips belong to this category.
ASIC 从逻辑到版图都为单一算法定制，同样的任务往往比 CPU 快成百上千倍、: ASICs are customized from logic to layout for a single algorithm; the same task is often hundreds or thousands of times faster and far more energy-efficient than CPU-based solutions. The cost is that design and manufacturing masks can run into tens of millions of dollars, with cycles lasting one or two years; once a chip is fabricated, it cannot be modified, and if the algorithm changes, the chip may become worthless.
2013 年起比特币挖矿从 GPU 转向专用 ASIC 矿机；2016 年谷歌公: Starting in 2013, Bitcoin mining shifted from GPUs to dedicated ASIC mining machines; in 2016, Google publicly released TPU for neural network inference, launching a competition of AI-specific chips.
把电压随时间的变化画成波形，是电子工程师的\"眼睛\"。: Plotting voltage changes over time as waveforms is the "eyes" of electronic engineers.
示波器横轴是时间、纵轴是电压，把一个快速变化的信号\"定格\"成稳定的波形图。关: The oscilloscope's horizontal axis is time and the vertical axis is voltage, "freezing" a rapidly changing signal into a stable waveform diagram. The key is trigger: each time the signal crosses a certain level, scanning starts from the same point; repeated waveforms will stack steadily together. Modern digital oscilloscopes sample billions of times per second, capable of capturing nanosecond-level spikes and automatically measuring frequency and amplitude.
1897 年布劳恩（Karl Ferdinand Braun）发明阴极射线管，被: In 1897, Karl Ferdinand Braun of Germany invented the cathode-ray tube, considered the starting point of the oscilloscope; in 1947, Tektronix Corporation of the United States launched the Model 511 oscilloscope with trigger scanning.
用磁场偏转电子束扫描荧光屏发光，统治电视和显示器半个多世纪。: Using magnetic fields to deflect electron beams scanning a phosphor screen ruled television and monitors for more than half a century.
显像管尾部的电子枪发射电子束，经电场加速后，由管颈上的偏转线圈控制方向，从左到右: The electron gun at the tail of the cathode-ray tube emits an electron beam; after acceleration by electric fields, its direction is controlled by deflection coils on the neck, scanning row by row from left to right and top to bottom across the entire screen dozens of times per second. The strength of the electron beam varies with image signals; it becomes strong at bright areas and weak at dark areas. Due to human visual persistence, rapidly scanned bright spots become a complete picture. Color cathode-ray tubes have three electron guns, each striking red, green, or blue phosphor dots respectively.
用电压扭转液晶分子来控制背光能否透过，让显示器变得又薄又省电。: Using voltage to twist liquid crystal molecules controls whether backlight can pass through, making displays both thin and energy-efficient.
液晶屏本身不发光，背后有一块背光板（早期是荧光灯管，现在是 LED）。光先经过第: The LCD itself does not emit light; behind it lies a backlight panel (early fluorescent tubes, now LEDs). Light first passes through the first polarizing filter to become polarized light; when passing through the liquid crystal layer, it is twisted 90°, exactly allowing it to pass through the second polarizing filter—the pixel is bright. When voltage is applied to a pixel, liquid crystal molecules stand upright and no longer twist light; light is blocked by the second polarizing filter—the pixel is dark. Each pixel consists of three sub-pixels (red, green, blue); each sub-pixel has a thin-film transistor (TFT) behind it for independent control.
1968 年美国 RCA 公司的海尔迈耶（George Heilmeier）团队: In 1968, George Heilmeier's team at RCA Corporation of the United States demonstrated the first liquid crystal display; in 1973, Sharp launched a pocket calculator using LCDs.
液晶像素的\"百叶窗\"：不加电时液晶扭转偏振光让光通过，加电后液晶竖起，光被第: The "blinds" of liquid crystal pixels: Without power, the twisted liquid crystals rotate polarized light to let it pass; with power applied, the liquid crystals stand upright, blocking the light from a second polarizer.
电子与空穴在 PN 结复合时直接发光；蓝光 LED 突破后诞生了白光照明。: Electrons and holes recombine directly at a p–n junction to emit light; after the breakthrough in blue LED technology, white lighting became possible.
不同材料发不同颜色的光：砷化镓发红外光，磷砷化镓发红光，氮化镓发蓝光。**白光: Different materials emit different colors of light: gallium arsenide emits infrared light, phosphorus-gallium-arsenide emits red light, and gallium nitride emits blue light. White LED lighting most commonly uses a blue LED to excite yellow phosphor; the mixture of blue and yellow light appears as white light to the human eye.
1962 年美国通用电气公司的何伦亚克（Nick Holonyak）做出第一个可: In 1962, Nick Holonyak from General Electric Company in the United States created the first visible-light (red) LED. Red and green LEDs quickly became popular as indicator lights, but bright blue LEDs troubled scientists for thirty years: the difficulty lay in growing high-quality gallium nitride crystals and achieving p-type doping. In the late 1980s to early 1990s, Isamu Akasaki, Hiroshi Amano, and Shuji Nakamura from Japan overcame this challenge; the three shared the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics.
LED 发光：电子从导带落入价带与空穴复合，放出光子；禁带越宽，光越偏蓝。蓝光: LED emission: electrons fall from the conduction band into the valence band to recombine with holes, releasing photons; the wider the bandgap, the bluer the light. Blue LED plus yellow phosphor yields white light.
每个像素自己发光的有机材料显示，黑色更纯、可以弯折。: Organic materials that emit light from each pixel themselves: black is purer and can be bent.
OLED 屏幕的每个子像素都是一个极薄的有机发光\"三明治\"：阳极、空穴传输层: Each sub-pixel of an OLED screen is an extremely thin organic-emitting "sandwich": anode, hole-transport layer, emissive layer, electron-transport layer, cathode; total thickness is only a few hundred nanometers. When powered on, electrons and holes meet and recombine in the emissive layer to emit light directly, without needing backlighting. When pixels are off, they emit absolutely no light, so black is true black with extremely high contrast; screens can be made extremely thin and even bent or curled. The disadvantage is that organic materials age over time, and prolonged display of the same image may cause "burn-in," especially for blue materials.
1987 年美国柯达公司的邓青云（Ching W. Tang）和范斯莱克（Ste: In 1987, Ching W. Tang and Steven Van Slyke from Kodak Company in the United States invented efficient double-layer OLEDs. Starting in the 2010s, Samsung began using AMOLED screens on a large scale for smartphones.
用微米级 LED 当像素，亮度高寿命长，量产难度大。: Using micrometer-scale LEDs as pixels offers high brightness and long lifespan, but mass production is difficult.
Micro LED 把 LED 芯片缩小到几微米到几十微米，红、绿、蓝三颗组成一: Micro LED shrinks LED chips to a few micrometers to tens of micrometers; red, green, and blue three chips form one pixel, arranged directly on the driver board. It has extremely high brightness, does not suffer from burn-in, and responds quickly. The greatest challenge is "mass transfer": a 4K screen requires placing approximately 25 million tiny LED chips precisely in position; any bad spot must be repaired, resulting in extremely high costs.
电容屏感知手指引起的微小电容变化来定位触点，使手机可以全屏交互。: Capacitive screens sense touch points by detecting minute changes in capacitance caused by fingers.
手机上的**投射式电容屏**在玻璃下方布有横竖交错的透明导电线（常用氧化铟锡）。: **Projected capacitive screens** on smartphones have transparent conductive wires arranged in a cross pattern under the glass (commonly indium tin oxide). Control chips scan the capacitance value at each crossing point hundreds of times per second; when touched by a finger, the capacitance at that crossing point undergoes a slight change, and the chip calculates the touch coordinates based on this. Because each crossing point can be measured independently, multiple fingers can be recognized simultaneously, enabling gestures such as zooming and sliding. Early common **resistive screens** relied on pressure to make two conductive films contact, requiring forceful pressing and supporting only single-point touch.
1965 年英国皇家雷达研究所的约翰逊（E. A. Johnson）发表了电容触: In 1965, E. A. Johnson from the Royal Radar Establishment in the United Kingdom published a paper on capacitive touch screens for air traffic control. In 2007, Apple's iPhone brought multi-touch capacitive screens to the public.
用电场移动带电颜料微粒显示图像，断电也能保持，像纸一样不刺眼。: Images are displayed by moving charged pigment particles using an electric field; they remain visible even when power is off, like paper, and are not eye-straining.
旋转发电机天然发出方向周期性反转的电流（[[p:induction|电磁感应]]: A rotating generator naturally produces current that reverses direction periodically ([[p:induction|Electromagnetic induction]]); precisely because the current is constantly changing, it can be stepped up or down by a transformer.
交流电成为全球电网的标准，因为它能方便地变压、远距离输送，并直接驱动结构简单的感: Alternating current became the standard for global power grids because it can be easily transformed, transmitted over long distances, and directly drive simple induction motors (see [[transformer-electrical]], [[three-phase-power]], [[war-of-currents]]).
三路交流电的相位依次错开 120°，任何时刻三者之和为零（[[p:inducti: The three phases of alternating current are offset by 120° in sequence; at any given moment, the sum of the three is zero ([[p:induction|Electromagnetic induction]]); when connected to three sets of coils spatially offset by 120°, the resulting magnetic field rotates smoothly.
晶体管尺寸缩小时，如果电压和电流按同样比例减小，单位面积的功率就保持不变（[[p: When transistor dimensions shrink, if voltage and current decrease by the same proportion, power per unit area remains unchanged ([[p:heat|Heat transfer]], [[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]): chips can be faster and denser, but not hotter.
1974 年 IBM 的登纳德（Robert Dennard，也是 DRAM 的: In 1974, Robert Dennard of IBM (who also invented DRAM) and others published a paper proposing this scaling rule. Around 2005 it became invalid; Intel canceled its Pentium 4 plan for frequencies above 4 GHz, and the industry shifted to [[multicore|Multicore & parallelism]].
登纳德缩放的终结意味着\"免费的午餐\"结束了：软件必须学会并行，才能继续从新硬: The end of Dennard scaling means the "free lunch" is over: software must learn to parallelize in order to continue benefiting from new hardware (see [[moores-law|Moore's law]], [[cpu|Central processing unit (CPU)]]).
芯片之间的连线又长又慢又耗电，把它们搬进同一块硅片里，距离缩短上千倍，速度更快、: Connections between chips are long, slow, and power-hungry; moving them onto the same silicon wafer shortens distances by over a thousand times, resulting in faster speeds and lower power consumption ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]); additionally, assigning dedicated processing units to each type of task allows them to perform their respective roles (see [[p:division|Division of labor]]).
SoC 让一部手机拥有过去一台电脑的算力，同时还能靠电池用一整天（见 [[sma: SoCs allow a single smartphone to possess the computing power of a past computer, while still being able to run on battery for an entire day (see [[smartphone|Smartphone]], [[arm-architecture|ARM architecture]]).
晶体中原子排列得越整齐，电子的运动就越可预测（[[p:structure|结构决: The more orderly the atomic arrangement in crystals, the more predictable electron motion becomes (see [[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]); chips require silicon purity exceeding "nine nines" (99.9999999%), and the entire ingot must be a single perfect monocrystal.
任何数字电路都能由查找表和可编程连线组合出来（[[p:boolean|布尔逻辑]: Any digital circuit can be constructed from lookup tables and programmable interconnections (see [[p:boolean|Boolean logic & binary]]); making chips into large areas of blank "logic blocks" and switch matrices, then writing configurations by users after manufacturing, allows them to become any circuit (see [[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]]).
FPGA 广泛用于芯片设计验证、通信基站、高频交易和数据中心加速（见 [[asi: FPGAs are widely used for chip design verification, communication base stations, high-frequency trading, and data center acceleration (see [[asic|Application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC)]], [[logic-gate|Logic gate]]).
专门为一件事设计的电路，可以省掉所有通用功能的开销，把每一个晶体管都用在刀刃上；: Circuits designed specifically for one task can eliminate the overhead of all general-purpose functions, using every transistor to its fullest extent; the larger the production volume, the thinner the expensive design cost becomes (see [[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]).
手机里的视频编解码、网络交换芯片和 AI 加速器都是 ASIC 的身影（见 [[: Video encoding/decoding chips, network switching chips, and AI accelerators inside smartphones are manifestations of ASICs (see [[fpga|Field-programmable gate array (FPGA)]], [[ai-accelerator|AI accelerators (GPU, TPU)]]).
人看不到电压，但可以让电子束随电压偏转在荧光屏上画线（[[p:lorentz|电: Humans cannot see voltage, but can make electron beams deflect according to voltage to draw lines on a fluorescent screen (see [[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]); or rapidly sampling and then drawing digital images on the screen (see [[p:sampling|Sampling & digitization]]).
示波器是电子工程师调试电路最基本的\"眼睛\"（见 [[crt]]、[[anal: Oscilloscopes are the most basic "eyes" for electronic engineers debugging circuits (see [[crt|Cathode-ray tube (CRT)]], [[analog-digital|Analog vs. digital signals]]).
运动的电子在磁场中会受力偏转（[[p:lorentz|电磁力]]）；控制偏转线圈: Moving electrons experience a deflecting force in a magnetic field (see [[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]); controlling the current in deflection coils allows the electron beam to point to any point on the screen, striking phosphors to emit light.
1897 年德国的布劳恩（Karl Ferdinand Braun）发明阴极射线: In 1897, Karl Ferdinand Braun of Germany invented the cathode-ray tube; it was used for electronic [[television|Television]] from the 1920s to the 1930s.
显像管统治了电视机和电脑显示器半个多世纪，直到 2000 年代被更薄更轻的液晶和: Cathode-ray tubes ruled television and computer monitors for over half a century until they were replaced in the 2000s by thinner, lighter LCDs and plasma screens. They were large and heavy because electron beams needed sufficient distance to deflect to the screen edges (see [[lcd|Liquid-crystal display (LCD)]], [[electron-discovery|Discovery of the electron]]).
液晶分子像一根根小棒，既能流动又能整齐排列，排列方式会影响光的偏振方向；加上电场: Liquid crystal molecules are like tiny rods that can both flow and align orderly; their arrangement affects the polarization direction of light; with an electric field, they turn (see [[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]); sandwiched between two polarizers with perpendicular polarization directions, it can control whether light passes through like a shutter (see [[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]]).
液晶让显示器变得又薄又省电，催生了笔记本电脑、平板电视和智能手机（见 [[ole: Liquid crystals made displays thin and energy-efficient, giving birth to laptops, flat-screen televisions, and smartphones (see [[oled|OLED]], [[touchscreen|Touchscreen]]).
在 PN 结里，电子从高能的导带掉进低能的价带与空穴复合，多出的能量以一个光子的: Inside a p-n junction, electrons drop from the high-energy conduction band into the low-energy valence band to recombine with holes; excess energy is released in the form of a photon (see [[p:levels|Quantized energy levels]]); the color of light depends on the semiconductor's bandgap width—a wider bandgap means higher photon energy and a bluer color (see [[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]).
蓝光 LED 让白光 LED 照明成为可能。LED 灯的光效约是白炽灯的十倍左右: Blue light LEDs made white light LED lighting possible. The luminous efficacy of LED lights is about ten times that of incandescent bulbs, and their lifespan is tens of times longer; they have basically replaced incandescent bulbs and fluorescent lamps (see [[incandescent-bulb]], [[fluorescent-lamp]]). They also form the foundation for backlighting in LCDs, large screens, car headlights, and [[microled|Micro LED]] displays.
某些有机分子在电子和空穴复合时会被激发，回到基态时发出特定颜色的光（[[p:le: Certain organic molecules are excited when electrons and holes recombine; upon returning to their ground state, they emit light of a specific color ([[p:levels|Quantized energy levels]]).
OLED 已成为高端手机、手表、电视的主流屏幕，折叠屏手机也靠它实现（见 [[l: OLED has become the mainstream screen technology for high-end smartphones, watches, and TVs. Foldable smartphone screens also rely on it (see [[lcd]], [[led]], [[microled]]).
每个像素都是一颗自己发光的无机 LED（[[p:levels|量子化能级]]），: Each pixel is an inorganic LED that emits its own light ([[p:levels|Quantized energy levels]], combining the self-emission of OLED with the long lifespan and high brightness of inorganic materials).
人体是导体，手指靠近屏幕时会和电极之间形成一个小电容，改变电极上的电荷分布（[[: The human body is a conductor; when a finger approaches the screen, a small capacitor forms between the finger and the electrode, changing the charge distribution on the electrode ([[p:charge|Electric charge & field]]).
触摸屏让手指成为最直观的输入设备，取代了物理键盘，使\"一块玻璃\"的智能手机和: Touch screens make the finger the most intuitive input device, replacing physical keyboards and enabling "a single piece of glass" smartphones and tablets (see [[smartphone]], [[lcd]]).
带电微粒在电场中会移动，正电荷被负极吸引、负电荷被正极吸引（[[p:charge: Charged particles move in an electric field: positive charges are attracted to negative electrodes, and negative charges are attracted to positive electrodes ([[p:charge|Electric charge & field]]); once stopped, they remain in place without needing electricity.
电子墨水屏里有数百万个比头发丝还细的微胶囊，每个胶囊里装着带正电的白色颗粒和带负: Electronic ink screens contain millions of microcapsules thinner than human hair; each capsule contains positively charged white particles and negatively charged black particles suspended in a transparent liquid. Applying a positive voltage to the top of a pixel attracts the black particles upward to display black; conversely, it displays white. It displays by reflecting ambient light, like paper, without being glaring; it remains clear in sunlight. When the image does not change, it consumes absolutely no power. Its disadvantages are slow refresh rates and limited color effects.
电子书阅读器、超市电子价签和部分手表都在用它（见 [[lcd]]）。: E-book readers, supermarket electronic price tags, and some watches use it (see [[lcd]]).
把光变成电荷再读出成数字的芯片，是相机和手机摄像头的\"胶片\"。: Chips that convert light into charge and then read it as digital numbers are the "film" of camera phones and smartphone cameras.
光子打进硅里能激发出电子（[[p:photoelectric|光电效应]]），光: When photons strike silicon, they excite electrons ([[p:photoelectric|Photoelectric effect]]; the stronger the light, the more electrons). By dividing the chip into millions of small cells to collect electrons separately, then reading them one by one and quantifying them into numbers, a digital image is obtained ([[p:sampling|Sampling & digitization]]).
每个像素是一个光电二极管，曝光期间积累电子。**CCD** 像传递水桶一样，把每: Each pixel is a photodiode that accumulates electrons during exposure. **CCD** works like passing buckets: it moves the charge from each row of pixels sequentially to the chip's edge for unified reading, offering good image quality but higher power consumption; **CMOS sensors** place transistors next to each pixel to amplify locally, enabling faster and more power-efficient reading that can be integrated with processing circuits. A red-green-blue color filter array covers the pixels above; each pixel records only one color, which algorithms then "guess" to reconstruct full-color images.
1969 年贝尔实验室的博伊尔（Willard Boyle）和史密斯（Georg: In 1969, Willard Boyle and George Smith at Bell Labs invented CCD, winning the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physics. In the early 1990s, Eric Fossum at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory invented the modern CMOS active pixel sensor.
图像传感器取代了胶片，让 [[digital-camera|数码相机]] 和手机: Image sensors replaced film, making [[digital-camera|Digital cameras]] and smartphone cameras mainstream; they are also the "eyes" of machine vision, autonomous driving, and astronomical observation (see [[cmos]], [[photography]]).
用芯片工艺造出微米级的机械结构，如手机里的加速度计、陀螺仪和麦克风。: Using chip fabrication processes to create micron-scale mechanical structures, such as accelerometers, gyroscopes, and microphones in smartphones.
用制造芯片的光刻和刻蚀工艺，同样能在硅上\"雕\"出微米级的可动机械结构；微小的: Using photolithography and etching processes for chip manufacturing, one can also "carve" micron-scale movable mechanical structures on silicon; a tiny mass block produces displacement under acceleration ([[p:newton|Newton's laws of motion]]; this displacement changes the capacitance, which can be measured by circuits ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
手机里的**加速度计**有一个用细梁悬挂的微型质量块，手机一动，质量块因惯性相对: Smartphones contain **accelerometers** with a micro-mass block suspended by thin beams; when the phone moves, the mass block shifts relative to the casing due to inertia, changing the capacitance between it and adjacent electrodes; **gyroscopes** cause micro-structures to vibrate continuously, and during rotation, the Coriolis force induces lateral offset; **MEMS microphones** use a tiny thin film to sense sound pressure. Digital micromirror devices in projectors consist of millions of flipable micro-mirrors.
1980 年代后期 MEMS 走向实用；1991 年美国亚德诺公司推出用于汽车安: In the late 1980s, MEMS moved toward practicality; in 1991, Analog Devices (USA) launched an integrated accelerometer for automotive airbags; in 2007, iPhone used accelerometers to enable automatic screen rotation.
把温度、压力、光、加速度等物理量变成电信号的器件，是机器的\"感官\"。: Devices that convert physical quantities such as temperature, pressure, light, and acceleration into electrical signals are the "senses" of machines.
几乎每一种物理效应都可以用来把某个物理量变成电信号，测量结果再用来调节动作，就构: Almost every physical effect can be used to convert a certain physical quantity into an electrical signal; measuring the result and using it to adjust actions forms a closed-loop control system ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
温度传感器利用电阻或 PN 结电压随温度变化；压力传感器利用应变或电容变化；光传: Temperature sensors utilize the change in resistance or PN junction voltage with temperature; pressure sensors utilize strain or capacitance changes; light sensors utilize the photoelectric effect; magnetic sensors utilize the Hall effect; gas sensors utilize the change in resistance after materials adsorb gases. The weak analog signals output by sensors are amplified, filtered, and converted to digital via [[adc|ADC / DAC]] before being sent to a processor. A modern car has over a hundred sensors, and a smartphone also has several dozen.
温度计、压力计古已有之；20 世纪后半叶半导体和 [[mems|MEMS]] 工: Thermometers and barometers have existed since ancient times; in the latter half of the 20th century, semiconductor and [[mems|MEMS]] processes made sensors small and inexpensive, allowing them to be mass-embedded into various devices.
廉价的传感器是 [[iot|物联网]]、自动驾驶、机器人和可穿戴设备的前提——机: Inexpensive sensors are a prerequisite for [[iot|IoT]], autonomous driving, robotics, and wearable devices—machines must first "perceive" before they can be "intelligent" (see [[image-sensor]]).
磁场让导体中电流偏向一侧形成电压，用来测转速、位置和电流。: A magnetic field causes current in a conductor to deviate to one side, forming a voltage used to measure rotational speed, position, and current.
电流在磁场中流动时，载流子受洛伦兹力偏向导体一侧，两侧之间就出现一个与磁场强度成: When current flows through a magnetic field, charge carriers are deflected to one side of the conductor by the Lorentz force, creating a voltage between the two sides that is proportional to the magnetic field strength ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]).
霍尔传感器是一小片半导体，通上恒定电流，测量两侧的霍尔电压就能知道磁场有多强。它: A Hall sensor is a small piece of semiconductor; passing a constant current through it and measuring the Hall voltage on both sides reveals the strength of the magnetic field. It does not require contact with the object being measured, causing no wear: it can measure rotor position in motors, wheel rotational speed, current magnitude (current generates a magnetic field), and whether a phone case is open or closed.
1879 年美国约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的研究生霍尔（Edwin Hall）发现这一: In 1879, graduate student Edwin Hall at Johns Hopkins University in the United States discovered this effect.
霍尔传感器广泛用于汽车、[[bldc-motor|无刷电机]] 和工业控制（见: Hall sensors are widely used in automobiles, [[bldc-motor|brushless DC motors]], and industrial control (see [[sensors]]).
某些晶体受压会产生电压、加电压会变形，用于点火器、超声和石英钟。: Certain crystals generate voltage when compressed and deform when voltage is applied; these are used for ignition systems, ultrasound, and quartz clocks.
某些晶体内部正负电荷的中心在受压变形时会错开，晶体表面因此出现电压；反过来，加上: In certain crystals, the centers of positive and negative charges shift apart when the crystal is compressed and deformed, causing a voltage to appear on the crystal surface; conversely, applying voltage causes the crystal to expand or contract ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
石英、压电陶瓷等材料既能把力变成电，也能把电变成力。打火机和燃气灶的点火器用力敲: Materials such as quartz and piezoelectric ceramics can convert force into electricity and vice versa. Ignition systems for lighters and gas stoves use a mechanical impact on a piezoelectric crystal to generate an electric spark of over a thousand volts; ultrasound probes use voltage to make a piezoelectric sheet vibrate at high frequencies to emit ultrasound, then receive the returning echo; quartz crystal oscillators utilize this property to maintain precise vibration.
1880 年法国的居里兄弟（Pierre Curie 与 Jacques Cur: In 1880, the Curie brothers (Pierre Curie and Jacques Curie) of France discovered the piezoelectric effect. During World War I, Paul Langevin of France used piezoelectric quartz to create sonar for detecting submarines.
压电效应应用于声呐、[[medical-ultrasound|医用超声]]、[[: The piezoelectric effect is applied in sonar, [[medical-ultrasound|medical ultrasound]], [[crystal-oscillator|crystal oscillators]], and precise positioning.
两种金属接头有温差就产生电压（反之亦然），用于测温和无运动部件的制冷。: A temperature difference between two metal junctions generates a voltage (and vice versa), used for measuring temperature and cooling without moving parts.
两种不同导体连成回路，两个接头温度不同时，回路中就会产生电压（塞贝克效应）；反过: When two different conductors are connected in a loop, a voltage is generated in the loop if the temperatures of the two junctions differ (Seebeck effect); conversely, passing current causes one junction to absorb heat and the other to release heat (Peltier effect) ([[p:heat|Heat transfer]]).
热电偶利用塞贝克效应测温，结构简单、耐高温，炼钢炉里也能用。半导体热电模块利用帕: Thermocouples utilize the Seebeck effect for temperature measurement; they have a simple structure, withstand high temperatures, and can be used in steelmaking furnaces. Semiconductor thermoelectric modules utilize the Peltier effect to create small refrigerators without moving parts or refrigerants, used for car fridges and laser cooling; conversely, using a temperature difference to generate electricity results in very low efficiency, only a few percent.
1821 年德国的塞贝克（Thomas Seebeck）发现温差产生电压；183: In 1821, Thomas Seebeck of Germany discovered that a temperature difference generates voltage; in 1834, Jean Peltier of France discovered the reverse effect.
深空探测器的 [[nuclear-rtg|放射性同位素温差发电机]] 用放射性衰: The [[nuclear-rtg|Radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG)]] on deep space probes generates power from heat produced by radioactive decay; the Voyager probe relied on it for nearly half a century.
用约 2.45 GHz 的微波让食物中的水分子来回转动摩擦生热。: Food is heated by causing water molecules in the food to rotate back and forth using microwaves at approximately 2.45 GHz, generating heat through friction.
微波是频率约 2.45 吉赫的电磁波（[[p:emwave|电磁波]]）；水分子: Microwaves are electromagnetic waves ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]) with a frequency of approximately 2.45 gigahertz; water molecules have one end with a positive charge and the other with a negative charge, causing them to twist and turn continuously in a rapidly flipping electric field, colliding and rubbing against surrounding molecules to convert electromagnetic energy into heat.
[[magnetron|磁控管]] 产生微波，经波导送入金属腔体，在腔壁之间来回: A [[magnetron|Cavity magnetron]] generates microwaves, which are sent into a metal cavity via waveguide and reflect back and forth between the cavity walls; a rotating disk ensures more uniform heating. The holes in the metal mesh on the door are much smaller than the microwave wavelength of approximately 12 centimeters, blocking the microwaves.
1945 年美国雷神公司的工程师斯潘塞（Percy Spencer）在雷达磁控管: In 1945, engineer Percy Spencer of Raytheon Company in the United States discovered that a chocolate bar in his pocket melted while working next to a radar magnetron, leading to the invention of the microwave oven; in 1947, the first commercial microwave oven was introduced, standing approximately 1.8 meters tall.
微波炉让加热剩饭和冷冻食品只需几分钟。: Microwave ovens allow reheating leftovers and frozen foods in just a few minutes.
2.45 吉赫并不是水分子的\"共振频率\"，选它主要因为这是工业、科学和医疗专: 2.45 GHz is not the "resonant frequency" of water molecules; it is selected primarily because this is an industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) band, and the penetration depth is appropriate.
但翻倍越来越难：约 2005 年起频率停止提升（见 [[dennard-scal: But doubling has become increasingly difficult: starting around 2005, frequency growth stopped (see [[dennard-scaling]]); dimensions approached the atomic scale, causing increased leakage and tunneling, with [[euv-lithography|Extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography]] costing hundreds of millions of dollars per unit. The industry shifted to rely on [[chiplet|Chiplets & advanced packaging]], three-dimensional transistors, and specialized chips to continue growth.
LED 是一个特殊的 [[pn-junction|PN 结]] 二极管。通上正向: An LED is a special type of [[pn-junction|PN Junction]] diode. When forward voltage is applied, electrons in the N-region and holes in the P-region rush toward the junction region, where they recombine and emit light. Unlike incandescent lamps, it does not rely on "heating up" to emit light; instead, it directly converts electrical energy into light of a specific color, so it has high efficiency, generates almost no heat, and can last for tens of thousands of hours.
1997 年美国麻省理工学院媒体实验室的雅各布森（Joseph Jacobson: In 1997, Joseph Jacobson and others at the Media Laboratory of MIT in the United States founded E Ink; in 2007, Amazon's Kindle made electronic ink screens mainstream.
MEMS 让手机能计步、导航、防抖，让汽车能及时弹出气囊，也是 [[inkjet: MEMS enables smartphones to count steps, navigate, and reduce shake, allows cars to deploy airbags timely, and is also the foundation for [[inkjet-printing|Inkjet printing]] nozzles (see [[sensors]], [[smartphone]]).
在磁场中让电子绕圈产生大功率微波的真空管，先用于雷达后用于微波炉。: A vacuum tube that generates high-power microwaves by causing electrons to orbit in a magnetic field was first used for radar and later for microwave ovens.
电子在相互垂直的电场和磁场中会绕圈飞行（[[p:lorentz|电磁力]]）；让: Electrons flying in mutually perpendicular electric and magnetic fields will orbit ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]); letting them pass through a carefully designed resonant cavity once, like blowing into a bottle mouth, excites powerful oscillations ([[p:wave|Interference, diffraction & resonance]]), producing high-power microwaves.
磁控管中心是发射电子的阴极，外圈是开有多个谐振腔的铜阳极，外加永磁体产生轴向磁场: The center of the magnetron is a cathode that emits electrons; the outer ring is a copper anode with multiple resonant cavities; an additional permanent magnet generates an axial magnetic field. Electrons bent into spiral orbits by the magnetic field while flying toward the anode continuously give energy to electromagnetic oscillations inside the cavity, finally outputting in microwave form with efficiency reaching over 70%.
1940 年 2 月英国伯明翰大学的兰德尔（John Randall）和布特（H: In February 1940, John Randall and Harry Boot at the University of Birmingham in the United Kingdom invented the cavity magnetron. That same year, the United Kingdom brought it to the United States, greatly accelerating the development of the Allied forces' [[radar|Radar]].
它让雷达装上了飞机和军舰，战后又成为每台 [[microwave-oven|微波: It mounted radar on aircraft and warships; after the war, it became the heart of each [[microwave-oven|Microwave oven]].
第一种大众化的晶体管产品，让收音机变得能装进口袋。: The first transistor product for mass consumption, making radios portable enough to fit in pockets.
晶体管只需几伏电压、几毫安电流就能放大微弱的无线电信号（[[p:band|能带与: A transistor can amplify weak radio signals ([[p:band|Band theory & semiconductors]]) with just a few volts and a few milliamps; several batteries can power it for a long time.
晶体管收音机用几只晶体管完成选台、放大和检波，取代了需要预热、耗电大的真空管，装: Transistor radios used only a few transistors for channel selection, amplification, and demodulation, replacing vacuum tubes that required warm-up and consumed high power; they were housed in plastic cases the size of a pocket and driven by a single 9-volt battery.
1954 年 10 月美国德州仪器与 IDEA 公司推出第一款商用晶体管收音机: In October 1954, Texas Instruments and IDEA in the United States launched the first commercial transistor radio, Regency TR-1. In 1955, Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo in Japan launched TR-55, and changed its company name to Sony in 1958.
它是晶体管第一次进入大众生活，让年轻人可以随身听音乐、听摇滚，也让日本电子工业在: It was the first time transistors entered mass life, allowing young people to carry music and rock music with them; it also enabled Japanese electronics industry to rise globally (see [[transistor]], [[radio]]).
把计算从机械齿轮搬到芯片上，直接催生了第一款商用微处理器。: Moving computation from mechanical gears onto chips directly catalyzed the first commercial microprocessor.
任何算术运算都能分解成二进制的加法和移位，由逻辑门组成的电路完成（[[p:boo: Any arithmetic operation can be decomposed into binary addition and shifting; circuits composed of logic gates complete this ([[p:boolean|Boolean logic & binary]]).
电子计算器把键盘输入的十进制数字转换成二进制，在芯片内运算后再转换回来显示。早期: Electronic calculators converted decimal numbers input via keyboards into binary, performed calculations inside chips, then converted back for display. Early calculators were as large as typewriters; integrated circuits shrank them to the size of a palm.
1961 年英国推出第一台全电子台式计算器 ANITA。1967 年德州仪器的基: In 1961, the United Kingdom launched the first all-electronic desktop calculator, ANITA. In 1967, Kilby and others at Texas Instruments created a handheld calculator prototype called "Cal Tech." In 1969, Busicom in Japan commissioned Intel to design a calculator chip; Intel engineers proposed using one programmable general-purpose chip instead of multiple dedicated chips, which became the 1971 Intel 4004.
计算器的激烈竞争直接催生了第一款商用 [[microprocessor|微处理器: Fierce competition among calculators directly catalyzed the first commercial [[microprocessor|Microprocessor]], and also caused slide rules to exit history.
用每秒振动 32768 次的石英晶体计时，误差比机械表小一个数量级以上。: Using a quartz crystal vibrating 32,768 times per second for timing, the error is smaller than that of mechanical watches by an order of magnitude or more.
石英晶体的机械共振频率极其稳定（[[p:wave|共振]]）；把它切成音叉形状，: The mechanical resonance frequency of quartz crystals is extremely stable ([[p:wave|Interference, diffraction & resonance]]); cutting it into a tuning fork shape gives a vibration frequency of exactly 32,768 times per second, which is 2 to the power of 15.
电池驱动电路让石英音叉持续振动，分频电路把频率连续除以 2 共 15 次，得到精: Battery-driven circuits keep the quartz tuning fork vibrating continuously; frequency division circuits divide the frequency by 2 repeatedly 15 times to obtain an accurate pulse once per second, driving a stepper motor to move the pointer or refresh the liquid crystal display. Mechanical watches often have daily errors of several seconds to over ten seconds; quartz watches typically have monthly errors of only over ten seconds.
1969 年 12 月日本精工推出世界上第一款石英手表 Astron。: In December 1969, Seiko of Japan launched the world's first quartz watch, the Astron.
石英表价格迅速降到人人买得起，1970–1980 年代沉重打击了瑞士传统机械表业: The price of quartz watches rapidly dropped to a level where everyone could afford them. During the 1970s and 1980s, this severely impacted the Swiss traditional mechanical watch industry, an event known as the "Quartz Crisis" (see [[crystal-oscillator]]).
手表、手环、耳机等贴身电子设备，持续采集心率、运动、睡眠等数据。: Wearable electronic devices such as watches, fitness bands, and earphones continuously collect data on heart rate, exercise, sleep, and other metrics.
把传感器贴近身体，持续测量并把结果反馈给用户，就能帮助人调整行为（[[p:fee: By placing sensors close to the body to continuously measure and feed results back to the user, people can adjust their behavior ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
智能手表和手环用加速度计和陀螺仪计步、识别运动和睡眠；用绿光照射皮肤，检测血液对: Smartwatches and fitness bands use accelerometers and gyroscopes to count steps, identify activities, and detect sleep; they use green light to shine on the skin to measure heart rate by detecting changes in blood absorption of light (photoplethysmography); some products can also measure blood oxygen levels and perform single-lead electrocardiograms. Data is synchronized to smartphones via Bluetooth and analyzed for trends by algorithms. True wireless earphones and smart glasses also belong to wearable devices.
2009 年 Fitbit 推出第一代运动追踪器；2015 年 Apple Wa: In 2009, Fitbit launched the first generation of fitness trackers; in 2015, Apple Watch was released, driving the popularization of smartwatches.
可穿戴设备把健康监测从医院搬到手腕上，但测量精度和数据隐私仍需关注（见 [[se: Wearable devices have moved health monitoring from hospitals to wrists, but measurement accuracy and data privacy still require attention (see [[sensors]], [[continuous-glucose-monitor]]).
设计公开、价格低廉的开发板，让学生和创客也能做出电子原型。: Development boards designed with open specifications and low prices allow students and makers to create electronic prototypes.
统一、公开的硬件接口和设计，让任何人都能复用、修改和组合，社区越大，可用的扩展和: Unified, public hardware interfaces and designs enable anyone to reuse, modify, and combine components; the larger the community, the more available extensions and tutorials ([[p:standard|Standardization & interchangeability]]).
Arduino 是一块带微控制器的小电路板，用简单的编程环境就能读取传感器、控制: Arduino is a small circuit board with a microcontroller that can read sensors, control lights, and drive motors using simple programming environments; its schematics and design files are all public. The Raspberry Pi is a complete computer the size of a credit card capable of running Linux. Both are low-cost; combined with abundant expansion boards and open-source code, a prototype can be built in just a few hours.
2005 年意大利伊夫雷亚交互设计学院的班齐（Massimo Banzi）等人推: In 2005, Massimo Banzi and others from the Interaction Design Institute Ivrea in Italy launched Arduino; in 2012, the Raspberry Pi Foundation in the UK launched the Raspberry Pi at a price of $35.
它们让电子开发走进中小学课堂和车库创客空间，降低了硬件创业的门槛（见 [[emb: They brought electronic development into primary and secondary school classrooms and garage maker spaces, lowering the threshold for hardware entrepreneurship (see [[embedded-system]], [[open-source]]).
发射线圈的交变磁场在接收线圈中感应出电流，不插线就能充电。: An alternating magnetic field generated by the transmitting coil induces a current in the receiving coil without needing physical connections to charge.
发射线圈中的交变电流产生交变磁场，磁场穿过附近的接收线圈，在其中感应出电流（[[: An alternating current in the transmitting coil produces an alternating magnetic field; this field passes through a nearby receiving coil, inducing a current ([[p:induction|Electromagnetic induction]]) — essentially equivalent to a transformer with its primary and secondary windings separated.
充电板里的线圈以一百多千赫的频率通电，手机背面的接收线圈感应出交流电，经整流后给: The coils inside the charging board are energized at frequencies over 100 kilohertz; the receiving coil on the back of the phone induces an alternating current, which is then rectified to charge the battery. The two coils must be aligned and kept close together, otherwise magnetic flux loss occurs, efficiency drops, and heat generation increases. Magnetic alignment allows the coils to automatically align.
19 世纪 90 年代特斯拉就做过无线输电实验；2008 年无线充电联盟（WPC: Tesla conducted wireless power transmission experiments in the 1890s; the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC) was established in 2008, released the Qi standard in 2010, and launched Qi2 with magnetic alignment in 2023.
无线充电已成为手机、耳机和手表的常见功能（见 [[transformer-ele: Wireless charging has become a common feature for smartphones, earphones, and watches (see [[transformer-electrical]], [[smartphone]]).
用看不见的红外光或无线电把按键指令\"扔\"给电视等设备，让人不用起身就能操作。: Using invisible infrared light or radio waves to "throw" button commands to devices like televisions allows users to operate them without getting up.
信息可以\"骑\"在看不见的电磁波上传送（[[p:emwave|电磁波]]）：红: Information can be transmitted riding on invisible electromagnetic waves ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]): both infrared light and radio waves can send encoded button commands several meters away.
常见的红外遥控器里，按下按键后芯片生成一串代表该按键的二进制编码，用约 38 千: In common infrared remote controls, after a button is pressed, the chip generates a binary code representing that button, modulated at approximately 38 kilohertz to flash the infrared [[led|Light-emitting diode (LED)]]; the television's receiver head is sensitive only to this frequency, filtering out light interference. Infrared requires alignment; garage door openers and smart homes often switch to radio waves or [[bluetooth|Bluetooth]].
1950 年美国真力时（Zenith）公司推出带电线的电视遥控器；1955 年该: In 1950, Zenith of America launched a wired television remote control; in 1955, the company's engineer Eugene Polley invented the wireless beam-controlled remote "Flash-Matic"; in 1956, Robert Adler designed an ultrasonic remote control. Infrared remotes became mainstream in the 1980s.
遥控器改变了看电视的方式（见 [[television]]、[[smart-ho: Remote controls changed the way people watch television (see [[television]], [[smart-home]]).
封闭压缩机让冰箱安静可靠地走进家庭，改变了买菜和饮食方式。: Enclosed compressors allowed refrigerators to become quiet and reliable enough to enter homes, changing how people buy groceries and eat.
家用冰箱就是一台小型蒸气压缩制冷机，把箱内的热量搬到箱外（[[p:phase|相: A household refrigerator is essentially a small vapor-compression refrigeration machine that moves heat from inside the box to outside ([[p:phase|Phase change & latent heat]], [[p:entropy|Entropy & the second law]]).
压缩机把制冷剂压缩后送到冰箱背后或两侧的冷凝管放热，经毛细管节流降压后进入箱内蒸: The compressor compresses the refrigerant and sends it to the condenser coils located behind or on the sides of the refrigerator, where heat is released. After passing through a capillary tube for throttling and pressure reduction, it enters the evaporator inside the cabinet to absorb heat. The thermostat automatically starts and stops the compressor based on the temperature inside the cabinet. A fully enclosed compressor seals the motor and compressor together in one unit; it does not leak refrigerant, produces low noise, and is a key factor enabling refrigerators to enter households.
1927 年美国通用电气推出\"Monitor-Top\"冰箱，压缩机封闭在顶部: In 1927, General Electric in the United States launched the "Monitor-Top" refrigerator. The compressor was enclosed within a cylindrical housing at the top, making it the first household electric refrigerator to be widely popularized.
冰箱让家庭可以储存一周的食物，减少了食物腐败，也改变了购物和饮食习惯（见 [[r: Refrigerators allow families to store food for a week, reducing food spoilage and also changing shopping and eating habits (see [[refrigeration]], [[cold-chain]]).
电动洗衣机把每周最繁重的家务交给电机，是解放家务劳动的标志。: Electric washing machines assign the most labor-intensive weekly chores to motors, marking a milestone in liberating household labor.
电动机把电能变成稳定的机械运动，替代人手搓洗衣物（[[p:leverage|机械: Electric motors convert electrical energy into stable mechanical motion, replacing manual hand-washing of clothes ([[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]]).
波轮洗衣机用底部转盘搅动水流；滚筒洗衣机让衣物在旋转的滚筒中被反复提起摔下，用水: Top-tube washing machines use a bottom rotating disk to stir water flow; drum washing machines allow clothes to be repeatedly lifted and dropped inside a rotating drum, using less water and being gentler. Detergent is responsible for chemical cleaning, while mechanical motion is responsible for "shaking" dirt out of the fibers. Finally, high-speed rotation for dehydration relies on centrifugal force to fling water out. Modern washing machines use microcontrollers to control the entire process of water intake, washing, rinsing, and dehydration.
1908 年美国赫尔利机器公司推出由费舍尔（Alva Fisher）设计的\"雷: In 1908, the Hurley Machine Company in the United States launched the "Thor" electric washing machine designed by Alva Fisher, which is often regarded as the first commercial electric washing machine.
洗衣机把妇女从每周最繁重的家务中解放出来，常被视为家庭电气化对社会影响最大的电器: Washing machines liberated women from the most labor-intensive weekly chores and are often regarded as one of the appliances with the greatest impact on socialization due to household electrification (see [[electric-motor]], [[detergent]]).
用电动风机制造负压吸走灰尘，后来发展出能自主导航的扫地机器人。: Electric fans were used to create negative pressure to suck away dust; later, autonomous mobile robots capable of self-navigation for sweeping were developed.
风机把空气抽走，在吸口形成低于外界的气压，外面的空气带着灰尘冲进来（[[p:fl: Fans suck air out, creating a pressure lower than the outside atmosphere at the intake, causing outside air carrying dust to rush in ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]).
电动机带动高速风扇制造负压，灰尘随气流进入集尘袋或尘杯，过滤后的空气排出。无袋式: Electric motors drive high-speed fans to create negative pressure; dust enters collection bags or dust cups with the airflow, and filtered air is expelled. Bagless vacuum cleaners utilize cyclone separation: allowing airflow to rotate at high speed causes dust to be flung outward by centrifugal force and fall onto the outer wall. Sweeping robots added collision sensors, laser radars, and navigation algorithms to plan their own routes.
1901 年英国工程师布斯（Hubert Cecil Booth）发明了第一台电: In 1901, British engineer Hubert Cecil Booth invented the first electric vacuum cleaner, which was huge in size and required a horse-drawn carriage to transport it to customers' doorsteps for work; in 1907, James Spangler of the United States invented a portable vacuum cleaner, later selling the patent to Hoover Company.
吸尘器让家庭清洁更加轻松卫生（见 [[electric-motor]]、[[mo: Vacuum cleaners make household cleaning easier and more hygienic (see [[electric-motor]], [[mobile-robot]]).
线圈产生交变磁场，在铁锅底部感应出涡流直接发热，灶面本身不热。: Coils generate an alternating magnetic field, inducing eddy currents directly in the bottom of iron pots to heat them; the stovetop surface itself does not become hot.
交变磁场穿过导电的锅底时，会在锅底里感应出旋涡状的电流（涡流），电流在金属电阻中: When an alternating magnetic field passes through a conductive pot bottom, it induces a vortex-like current (eddy current) inside the pot bottom; this current heats up due to metal resistance ([[p:induction|Electromagnetic induction]]).
电磁炉面板下有一个扁平线圈，[[power-electronics|电力电子]]: Under the electromagnetic induction stove panel lies a flat coil. The power electronics circuit ([[power-electronics|Power electronics]]) allows it to pass high-frequency currents of tens to hundreds of kilohertz, generating an alternating magnetic field. This magnetic field passes through the ceramic panel and induces eddy currents in the bottom of iron pots; the pot itself heats up, while the panel is only indirectly heated by the heat from the pot bottom. Pots with ferromagnetic properties work best; aluminum pots and glass pots are basically unusable. Heat is generated directly inside the pot, achieving an efficiency of approximately 85%–90%, which is much higher than gas stoves.
1971 年美国西屋公司展示了电磁炉，1973 年推出商用产品；日本和中国在 1: In 1971, Westinghouse in the United States demonstrated the electromagnetic induction stove; it launched commercial products in 1973. Japan and China popularized it during the 1980s and 1990s.
电磁炉安全、无明火、热效率高，是厨房电气化的重要一步（见 [[transform: Electromagnetic induction stoves are safe, have no open flame, and high heat efficiency, representing an important step in kitchen electrification (see [[transformer-electrical]]).
水烧干后锅底温度超过 100°C，感温元件自动断电——一个巧妙的物理开关。: After water boils dry, the pot bottom temperature exceeds 100°C, causing the temperature sensing element to automatically cut power—a clever physical switch.
只要锅里还有水，温度就被\"钉\"在 100°C 左右（[[p:phase|相变: As long as there is still water in the pot, the temperature is "pinned" around 100°C ([[p:phase|Phase change & latent heat]]); once water is absorbed by rice or evaporated completely, the pot bottom temperature rises rapidly—this sudden temperature change is the signal that "the rice is cooked" ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
传统电饭煲锅底中央有一个磁钢限温器：一块感温磁铁在约 103°C 时会失去磁性。: Traditional rice cookers have a magnetic steel temperature limiter at the center of the pot bottom: a temperature-sensitive magnet loses its magnetism around 103°C. During cooking, it holds the switch to maintain heating; when water dries out and the temperature exceeds this point, the magnet demagnetizes and releases, causing the switch to jump to the warming mode. The entire process requires no electronic components. Modern rice cookers use microcomputers and temperature sensors to segmentally control heat intensity, while electromagnetic induction types can make the inner pot heat evenly throughout.
1955 年日本东芝推出第一款商业成功的自动电饭锅。: In 1955, Toshiba in Japan launched the first commercially successful automatic rice cooker.
电饭煲让亚洲家庭不用再守着灶台煮饭，是最受欢迎的家电之一（见 [[thermos: Rice cookers allow Asian families no longer to stand by the stove cooking rice, making them one of the most popular home appliances (see [[thermostat]]).
测量温度，与设定值比较，偏低就加热、偏高就停止——这是最简单也最典型的负反馈控制: Measure the temperature, compare it with the setpoint: heat if it is low, stop if it is high. This is the simplest and most typical form of negative feedback control ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
1883 年美国的约翰逊（Warren Johnson）取得电动恒温器专利；18: In 1883, Warren Johnson of the United States obtained a patent for an electric thermostat; in 1885, Albert Butz of the United States invented an "attenuator" for automatic control of furnace doors, and his company later developed into Honeywell. In 2011, Nest launched a learning smart thermostat.
恒温器无处不在：空调、冰箱、热水器、电熨斗、烤箱里都有它（见 [[control: Thermostats are everywhere: they are found in air conditioners, refrigerators, water heaters, electric irons, ovens (see [[control-theory]], [[smart-home]], [[air-conditioning]]).
巴贝奇设计的机械计算机；分析机已具备存储、运算、条件跳转，洛夫莱斯为它写下第一个: The mechanical computer designed by Babbage; the Analytical Engine already possessed storage, computation, and conditional jumps, and Lovelace wrote its first program for it.
把计算拆成只需要做加法的重复步骤（差分法），再用齿轮的转动来\"数数\"——计算: Break computation down into repeated steps requiring only addition (the method of differences), then use gear rotation to "count"—computation can be fully mechanized.
差分机利用多项式的\"差分\"恒定这一性质，只用齿轮做加法就能逐行算出数学用表，: The Difference Engine exploits the property that the "differences" of a polynomial remain constant; using only gears to perform addition, it can compute mathematical tables line by line, avoiding errors from manual calculation and transcription. The Analytical Engine went further: it used punched cards to input programs, had a "warehouse" (store) for storing numbers (equivalent to memory) and a "factory" (mill) for performing operations (equivalent to CPU), and could decide the next step based on results (conditional jumps).
1822 年英国数学家查尔斯·巴贝奇（Charles Babbage）提出差分机: In 1822, British mathematician Charles Babbage proposed the Difference Engine; in 1837 he described the Analytical Engine, but neither was fully built during his lifetime. In 1843, Ada Lovelace added extensive notes while translating the paper on the Analytical Engine, and the steps for computing Bernoulli numbers are often called "the first computer program." In 1991, the London Science Museum built Difference Engine No. 2 according to the drawings, proving the design was feasible.
它第一次把\"通用计算机\"的结构想清楚了，比电子计算机早了约一百年。: It clearly defined the structure of a "general-purpose computer" for the first time, about one hundred years before electronic computers.
信息可以用\"有孔/无孔\"两种状态记录，机器读孔就能读信息——这就是最早的二进: Information can be recorded in two states: "punched" or "unpunched"; a machine reading the holes can read information—this is the earliest form of binary storage.
卡片上每个位置打孔或不打孔，读卡机用电刷或探针穿过孔接通电路，计数器就加一。把卡: Each position on a card is either punched or not; a card reader uses an electric brush or probe to pass through the hole and close the circuit, incrementing the counter. By classifying cards according to different hole patterns and accumulating them, data for over a thousand people can be processed (not ten thousand).
1804 年雅卡尔（Joseph Marie Jacquard）用穿孔卡片控制织: In 1804, Joseph Marie Jacquard used punched cards to control weaving patterns (see [[jacquard-loom]]). In 1890, Herman Hollerith used a punched-card tabulating machine to process the United States census, greatly shortening the time required for statistics. The company he founded was later acquired by IBM.
穿孔卡片统治数据处理近一个世纪，直到 1970 年代程序员还在用它写程序。\"一: Punched cards ruled data processing for nearly a century; programmers were still using them to write programs in the 1970s. The habit of "one card per line of code" even influenced the early programming language limit of eighty characters per line.
一条纸带、一个读写头和一张规则表组成的抽象机器，定义了\"什么是可计算的\"。: An abstract machine consisting of a strip of paper, a read/write head, and a rule table defines "what is computable."
任何能写成\"一步一步的明确规则\"的计算，都可以交给一台只会读、写、移动的极简: Any computation that can be expressed as "clear step-by-step rules" can be handed to a minimalist machine that only reads, writes, and moves; conversely, anything this machine cannot do, no computer can do.
想象一条无限长的纸带，被分成一个个格子，每格写一个符号。一个读写头停在某一格上，: Imagine an infinitely long strip of paper divided into individual cells, with each cell containing a symbol. A read/write head stops at one cell; the machine internally has a "current state." At each step, the machine does only three things: read the symbol in the current cell, consult the rule table based on "state + symbol," then **write a symbol, shift left or right by one cell, and switch to a new state**.
就这么简单，却足以完成加法、排序乃至运行任何程序。更关键的是**通用图灵机**：: So simple, yet sufficient to perform addition, sorting, and even run any program. More critically, the **Universal Turing Machine**: it writes another Turing machine's rule table onto the tape as "program"; one machine can simulate all machines—this is the mathematical source of the concept of "software."
1936 年，24 岁的英国数学家艾伦·图灵（Alan Turing）在论文《论: In 1936, twenty-four-year-old British mathematician Alan Turing proposed it in the paper "On Computable Numbers." He wanted to answer a pure mathematical question: does there exist a mechanical method to determine the truth or falsity of any mathematical proposition? His answer was negative (see [[halting-problem]]). In the same year, Alonzo Church of the United States reached an equivalent conclusion using lambda calculus; together they are called the "Church-Turing thesis."
图灵机给了\"计算\"一个精确定义。今天说一种编程语言\"图灵完备\"，意思就是: The Turing Machine gave a precise definition to "computation." Today, when we say a programming language is "Turing-complete," it means it can compute everything a Turing machine can compute. Real computers have finite memory, but in principle they are all approximations of the Turing Machine.
图灵机不是一台真的机器，也不是为了造电脑而设计的；它是一个思想实验，用来划定\": The Turing Machine is not a real machine, nor was it designed to build computers; it is a thought experiment used to delineate the boundary of "what is computable."
图灵机 = 纸带 + 读写头 + 规则表。每一步只做\"读、写、移、换状态\"四: Turing Machine = tape + read/write head + rule table. At each step, it does only four things: "read, write, move, change state."
Z3、ABC、曼彻斯特\"宝贝\"、EDSAC、UNIVAC 等机器先后实现了程: Machines such as Z3, ABC, Manchester Baby, EDSAC, and UNIVAC sequentially achieved program control, electronic computation, stored-program architecture, and commercialization.
把\"开关\"从齿轮换成继电器、再换成真空管，速度就能提高成千上万倍；而把程序也: Replacing the "switch" from gears to relays, then to vacuum tubes, increases speed by over a thousand times (not ten thousand); while storing programs in memory allows machines to modify themselves and run automatically continuously.
这些机器各自突破了一个关键点：德国楚泽（Konrad Zuse）1941 年的: Each of these machines broke through a key milestone: Konrad Zuse's Z3 in Germany (1941) achieved program-controlled binary floating-point calculation using relays; the American Atanasoff-Berry Computer (ABC) around 1942 was the first to use vacuum tubes for electronic computation but could not be programmed; Manchester Baby in Britain (1948) was the first to run a program stored in memory; EDSAC at Cambridge (1949) became one of the first storage-program computers put into daily use; and UNIVAC I in 1951 became America's first commercial computer.
这些机器共同把\"计算机\"从专用计算器变成了今天意义上的通用机器。: Together, these machines transformed "computer" from a specialized calculator into the general-purpose machine we mean today.
二战中英国用于破译德军洛伦兹密码的电子计算机，长期保密。: The electronic computer used by Britain during World War II for decrypting German Lorenz cipher was kept secret for a long time.
破译密码本质上是在海量可能的密钥中快速试错和统计，电子开关比人和机械快几个数量级: Cryptanalysis essentially involves rapid trial-and-error and statistical analysis among a massive number of possible keys; electronic switches are orders of magnitude faster than humans and mechanical devices.
Colossus 以每秒约 5000 个字符的速度读取纸带上的截获密文，用真空管: Colossus read intercepted ciphertext on paper tape at a speed of about 5,000 characters per second, using vacuum tube circuits to analyze character patterns under various key settings, helping cryptanalysts deduce the settings of the German Lorenz cipher machine.
英国邮政局工程师汤米·弗劳尔斯（Tommy Flowers）设计，1944 年初: Designed by British Post Office engineer Tommy Flowers, it was put into use at Bletchley Park in early 1944; by the end of the war, there were 10 units in total.
它是最早的可编程电子数字计算机之一，但因战后长期保密，直到 1970 年代才为世: It was one of the earliest programmable electronic digital computers, but due to long-term secrecy after the war, it was not known to the public until the 1970s, and its influence was therefore less than [[eniac]].
第一台通用可编程电子计算机之一，用约 1.8 万个真空管，最初靠插线编程。: One of the first general-purpose programmable electronic computers; it used about 18,000 vacuum tubes and initially relied on plug-based programming.
真空管开关没有机械运动，每秒可以通断成千上万次，电子计算比继电器快约一千倍。: Vacuum tube switches have no mechanical motion; they can switch on and off thousands or even tens of thousands of times per second, making electronic computation about a thousand times faster than relays.
ENIAC 用约 1.8 万个真空管组成累加器、乘法器等单元，每秒可做约 500: ENIAC was composed of about 18,000 vacuum tubes forming adders, multipliers, and other units, performing about 5,000 additions per second. It initially had no stored-program architecture: to switch problems, staff had to rewire cables and toggle switches, often taking several days.
美国宾夕法尼亚大学的莫奇利（John Mauchly）和埃克特（J. Presp: John Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert at the University of Pennsylvania built it for the military to calculate artillery trajectory tables; it was completed by the end of 1945 and made public in February 1946. The first programmers were six women who learned "programming" by studying wiring diagrams.
ENIAC 让世界看到了电子计算机的威力，也暴露了\"插线编程\"的笨拙，直接催: ENIAC showed the power of electronic computers to the world and exposed the clumsiness of "plug-based programming," directly catalyzing the design concept of stored-program architecture (see [[von-neumann-architecture]]).
程序和数据存放在同一个存储器里，由 CPU 逐条取出执行——今天几乎所有计算机都: Programs and data are stored in the same memory; the CPU retrieves and executes them one by one—today, almost all computers work this way.
程序本身也是数据。把指令和数据放进同一个存储器，计算机就能像读数据一样读程序，换: The program itself is also data. By placing instructions and data into the same memory, a computer can read programs like it reads data; changing the program only requires changing the memory content without rewiring.
一台冯·诺依曼结构的计算机有五个部分：**运算器**（做加减和逻辑运算）、**控: A Von Neumann architecture computer has five parts: **Arithmetic Logic Unit** (performs addition, subtraction, and logical operations), **Control Unit** (retrieves instructions in sequence and directs all components), **Memory** (stores both instructions and data simultaneously), **Input Device**, and **Output Device**.
它的运行就是一个永不停止的循环：控制器根据\"程序计数器\"从内存取出下一条指令: Its operation is an endless loop: the Control Unit retrieves the next instruction from memory based on the "Program Counter" → decodes it → lets the Arithmetic Logic Unit execute it → writes the result back → increments the Program Counter to continue with the next one. When encountering a "jump" instruction, it modifies the Program Counter, thereby achieving branching and looping.
1945 年 6 月，数学家约翰·冯·诺依曼（John von Neumann）: In June 1945, mathematician John von Neumann systematically described this structure in the "EDVAC Report Preliminary Draft." Core ideas were also contributed by ENIAC team members like Eckert and Mauchly, but the report only listed John von Neumann's name, a naming controversy that has persisted to this day.
从 1940 年代末到今天的手机芯片，几乎所有计算机都沿用这一结构。它的代价是*: From the late 1940s to today's mobile phone chips, almost all computers have followed this structure. Its cost is the **Von Neumann bottleneck**: the channel between CPU and memory becomes the speed limit; the CPU often waits for data. Cache (see [[cache]]), [[memory-hierarchy|Memory hierarchy]], and near-memory computing are all used to alleviate this bottleneck.
现代 CPU 内部的一级缓存常把指令和数据分开存放（哈佛结构的思路），但从程序员: The first-level cache inside modern CPUs often stores instructions and data separately (following the Harvard architecture approach), but from the programmer's perspective of memory, it remains a Von Neumann structure.
冯·诺依曼结构：指令和数据共用一个存储器，CPU 循环执行\"取指—译码—执行—: Von Neumann architecture: instructions and data share one memory; the CPU cycles through "fetch-decode-execute-write-back." That middle bus is the famous bottleneck.
供整个机构共用的大型计算机；IBM System/360 首次让一系列机型兼容同: A large computer shared by an entire organization; IBM System/360 was the first to make a series of machines compatible with the same software suite.
一台昂贵的大机器让许多人和部门共用，并保证软件可以在新旧机型之间直接搬迁，就能分: Sharing one expensive large machine among many people and departments, and guaranteeing that software can be moved directly between old and new models, allows cost sharing and protects user investment.
大型机追求的是可靠和吞吐量，而不是单次计算快：它能同时处理成千上万笔交易，硬件部: Large machines pursue reliability and throughput rather than single-calculation speed: they can process tens of thousands of transactions simultaneously; hardware components can be replaced while running; downtime is measured in minutes per year. Core banking systems, airline ticketing, and government social security still have large amounts of systems running on mainframes today.
1964 年 4 月 IBM 发布 System/360，首次让一整个系列从小到: In April 1964, IBM released System/360, the first time an entire series of machines from small to large shared the same instruction set (see [[instruction-set-architecture]]); customers did not need to rewrite software when upgrading to larger machines. This project cost a huge amount and was called "IBM's bet on the company's fate," resulting in great success.
System/360 确立了\"架构与实现分离\"的思想，也让 8 位一个字节成: System/360 established the concept of 'separation of architecture and implementation,' making an 8-bit byte the industry standard.
价格降到实验室和中小企业买得起的计算机，Unix 就诞生在它上面。: Prices dropped to levels affordable for laboratories and small-to-medium enterprises, giving birth to Unix on it.
当晶体管和集成电路让计算机变得便宜，计算就可以从\"整个机构共用一台\"变成\": When transistors and integrated circuits made computers cheap, computing could shift from 'shared by an entire institution' to 'one machine per laboratory'.
小型机的价格从大型机的数百万美元降到数万美元，体积从一个房间降到一个机柜，研究人: The price of minicomputers fell from millions of dollars for mainframes to tens of thousands of dollars; volume shrank from a room-sized enclosure to a cabinet. Researchers could sit directly in front of terminals and use them interactively.
1965 年美国 DEC 公司推出 PDP-8，售价约 1.8 万美元，是第一款: In 1965, the American DEC company launched the PDP-8, priced at approximately $18,000, becoming the first commercially successful minicomputer. In 1969, Thompson at Bell Labs began writing [[unix]] on an idle PDP-7.
小型机培养了第一代\"自己动手\"的程序员文化，Unix、C 语言和早期网络都诞: Minicomputers cultivated a culture of 'do-it-yourself' programming among the first generation; Unix, C language, and early networking all emerged from minicomputers.
一人一台、放在桌上的计算机；1977 年的 Apple II 等和 1981 年: A personal computer placed on a desk; Apple II in 1977 and IBM PC in 1981 brought it into homes and offices.
芯片价格按 [[p:exponential|指数]] 下降，跌破个人能承受的门槛: Chip prices fell according to [[p:exponential|Exponential growth]]; after dropping below the threshold of affordability for individuals, computers shifted from 'institutional assets' to 'personal tools'. The more users there were, the more people wrote software for them, forming a positive cycle.
个人电脑把微处理器、内存、键盘、显示器和存储设备装进一台桌面机器，由一个人独占使: Personal computers packed microprocessors, memory, keyboards, displays, and storage devices into a single desktop machine, exclusively used by one person. Its value lay not in the hardware itself but in the software above it: spreadsheets, word processing, games, and later browsers.
1975 年 MITS 的 Altair 8800 以套件形式出售，点燃了爱好者: In 1975, MITS' Altair 8800 was sold as a kit, igniting enthusiast enthusiasm; Bill Gates and Paul Allen wrote a BASIC interpreter for it and founded Microsoft. In 1977, Apple II, Commodore PET, TRS-80, and other complete systems were launched; the starting price of the Apple II was $1298. In 1981, the IBM PC was released; it adopted an open architecture and off-the-shelf components (Intel CPU, Microsoft DOS), leading to a rapid emergence of compatible machine manufacturers, making 'PC-compatible' the standard. In 1984, Apple brought [[gui|Graphical User Interface]] to the masses.
计算第一次成为个人能力的延伸，催生了微软、苹果等巨头和整个软件产业。IBM 开放: Computing became an extension of personal ability for the first time, spawning giants like Microsoft and Apple and the entire software industry. IBM's choice to open its architecture caused it to quickly lose control; profits flowed to Intel and Microsoft, which held the CPU and operating system—this is a classic case of 'controlling the interface standard is more profitable than building complete machines'.
个人电脑的关键几步：从爱好者套件到整机，再到兼容机标准和图形界面。: Key steps in personal computers: from enthusiast kits to complete systems, then to compatible machine standards and graphical interfaces.
比特是信息的最小单位（0 或 1），8 个比特组成 1 个字节，可表示 256: A bit is the smallest unit of information (0 or 1); 8 bits make up 1 byte, capable of representing 256 states.
任何能区分的东西都能编码成一串\"是/否\"。区分 2 种情况要 1 个比特，区: Anything that can be distinguished can be encoded into a string of 'yes/no'. Distinguishing 2 conditions requires 1 bit; distinguishing N conditions requires approximately log₂N bits—this is the natural unit of information.
1 个比特（bit）只能是 0 或 1；8 个比特组成 1 个字节（byte），: 1 bit can only be 0 or 1; 8 bits make up 1 byte, with 2⁸ = 256 combinations, exactly enough to represent an English letter, an integer from 0–255, or a shade of gray. Text, images, sound, and programs are all just long strings of bytes in memory; their meaning depends on how the program interprets them.
比特让信息脱离了载体：同一份数据可以存在纸带、磁盘、光纤和闪存里，复制千万次也不: Bits allowed information to detach from its carrier: the same data could exist on paper tape, disk, fiber optics, and flash memory; copying it thousands of times did not alter it.
存储厂商常用 1 KB = 1000 字节，而操作系统常按 1024 计算，所以: Storage vendors commonly use 1 KB = 1000 bytes, while operating systems often calculate by 1024, so the 'actual capacity' of a new hard drive always appears slightly smaller.
同一个字节 01000001，当作整数是 65，当作 ASCII 字符就是大写字: The same byte 01000001 is 65 as an integer and the uppercase letter A as an ASCII character.
用 0/1 和与或非来演算逻辑的数学；香农 1937 年指出它可以直接用开关电路: Logic mathematics using 0/1 and AND/OR/NOT operations; Shannon pointed out in 1937 that it could be directly implemented with switch circuits.
逻辑推理可以写成只有 0 和 1 两个值的代数运算；而开关的\"断/通\"恰好也: Logical reasoning can be written as algebraic operations with only two values, 0 and 1; the 'open/closed' state of a switch is also exactly two values, so logic can be directly implemented by circuits.
布尔代数只有三种基本运算：与（AND，全真才真）、或（OR，有真就真）、非（NO: Boolean algebra has only three basic operations: AND (true only if all are true), OR (true if any is true), and NOT (inversion). Any complex conditional judgment can be derived from their combinations.
1854 年英国数学家布尔（George Boole）在《思维规律的研究》中提出: In 1854, British mathematician George Boole proposed it in 'The Laws of Thought', which was purely mathematical at the time. In 1937, the 21-year-old Shannon proved in his master's thesis that relay switch circuits could be designed and simplified using Boolean algebra; this paper is hailed as 'the starting point for digital circuit design'.
从此\"设计电路\"变成了\"化简公式\"，计算机硬件有了严格的数学基础（见 [: From then on, 'designing circuits' became 'simplifying formulas'; computer hardware gained a strict mathematical foundation (see [[logic-gate]]).
实现与、或、非等布尔运算的电路；把它们层层组合，就能做加法、存数据、执行程序。: Circuits that implement Boolean operations such as AND, OR, and NOT; by stacking them in layers, one can perform addition, store data, and execute programs.
用晶体管做成的开关可以实现\"与、或、非\"三种布尔运算；而任何计算——加法、比: Switches made from transistors can realize the three Boolean operations of AND, OR, and NOT; and any computation—addition, comparison, storage, or program execution—can be derived by layering these three operations together.
逻辑门有一个或多个输入、一个输出，输入输出都只取 0（低电压）或 1（高电压）。: A logic gate has one or more inputs and one output, where both inputs and outputs take only 0 (low voltage) or 1 (high voltage). An **AND gate** outputs 1 only when all inputs are 1; an **OR gate** outputs 1 if any input is 1; a **NOT gate** inverts the input. There is also a **NAND gate**, which is particularly important: using only this type of gate, all other gates can be constructed.
把门组合起来就能做事：两个门可以搭成\"半加器\"，算出两个比特相加的和与进位；: By combining gates, one can perform tasks: two gates can form a "half-adder" to compute the sum and carry from adding two bits; by chaining many adders together, one can add 64-bit integers; by crossing connections between gates as [[flip-flop|Flip-flop]], one can remember 1 bit. A modern CPU contains billions of transistors, which are essentially a vast number of logic gates organized in layers.
继电器逻辑电路在 1930 年代已经出现；真空管逻辑门用于 1940 年代的 [: Relay-based logic circuits appeared in the 1930s; vacuum tube logic gates were used for the [[eniac]] in the 1940s; since the 1960s, logic gates have been integrated into [[integrated-circuit|Integrated circuit (IC)]], and today they are implemented by [[cmos]] transistors.
逻辑门是硬件和数学之间的\"翻译层\"：工程师设计电路时只需要思考 0 和 1: Logic gates serve as the "translation layer" between hardware and mathematics: when engineers design circuits, they only need to think about the logic of 0s and 1s without worrying about physical details of voltage and current—this is one of the most important abstractions in computer history.
三种基本逻辑门和真值表，以及用两个门搭成的半加器：1 + 1 = 进位 1、和: The three basic logic gates and their truth tables, plus a half-adder built from two gates: 1 + 1 = carry 1, sum 0 (binary 10).
把两个逻辑门首尾交叉相连就能\"记住\"一个比特，寄存器和内存由此而来。: By connecting the outputs of two logic gates to each other's inputs in a cross-over manner, one can "remember" a bit; registers and memory thus originate.
把两个逻辑门的输出交叉接到对方的输入上，电路就形成一个自我维持的\"回路\"，会: By crossing the outputs of two logic gates to connect to each other's inputs, the circuit forms a self-sustaining "loop," which will stably settle into one of two states—this is the circuit's memory.
触发器有\"置 1\"和\"清 0\"两个输入，触发之后即使输入撤掉，它也保持状: Flip-flops have two inputs: "set 1" and "clear 0"; after triggering, even if the input is removed, it maintains its state unchanged. By arranging 32 or 64 flip-flops in a row, controlled simultaneously by a single clock signal for updates, one obtains **registers** inside a CPU; high-speed cache (SRAM) inside the CPU also uses similar cross-coupled circuits to store each bit.
1918 年英国物理学家埃克尔斯（William Eccles）和乔丹（F. W: In 1918, British physicist Eccles (William Eccles) and Jordan (F. W. Jordan) invented this circuit using two vacuum tubes.
有了触发器，逻辑电路就能\"记住\"中间结果，计算才能一步步进行下去。: With flip-flops, logic circuits can "remember" intermediate results, allowing computation to proceed step by step.
计算机的\"大脑\"：不断地取指令、译码、执行、写回，每秒数十亿次。: The "brain" of the computer: continuously fetching instructions, decoding, executing, and writing back, tens of billions of times per second.
CPU 只会做极简单的事——取一条指令、做一次加法或比较、把结果存起来——但它每: A CPU only does extremely simple things—fetch an instruction, perform addition or comparison, store the result—but it can repeat these dozens of billions of times per second; the massive repetition of simple steps constitutes complex computation.
CPU 主要由三部分组成：**控制单元**负责取指令、译码和调度；**算术逻辑单: A CPU mainly consists of three parts: the **Control Unit** is responsible for fetching instructions, decoding, and scheduling; the **Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)** performs addition, subtraction, multiplication, comparison, and logic operations; **registers** are extremely small and extremely fast storage inside the CPU. It continuously executes the cycle of "fetch instruction—decode—execute—write back," advancing one step per clock cycle.
现代 CPU 为了更快，加了大量\"预测\"和\"并行\"的技巧：[[pipel: Modern CPUs have added numerous techniques for "prediction" and "parallelism" to achieve higher speeds: [[pipeline|Assembly line]] allows multiple instructions to overlap in execution; branch prediction guesses in advance which path the program will take; out-of-order execution performs instructions that are already ready first; multicore enables several CPUs to work simultaneously (see [[multicore]]). These techniques are transparent to programmers—the program still appears to execute one instruction after another in order.
1971 年 [[microprocessor|微处理器]] 出现前，CPU 由: Before the appearance of [[microprocessor|Microprocessor]] in 1971, a CPU was composed of many blocks of circuit boards. Today, the clock frequency of CPUs in mobile phones and computers is approximately 2–5 GHz, meaning 20–50 billion clock cycles per second.
CPU 是通用计算的\"发动机\"，同一块芯片可以运行游戏、表格和编译器。它的弱: A CPU is the "engine" of general-purpose computation; the same chip can run games, spreadsheets, and compilers. Its weakness is that it is not good at large-scale repetitive operations of the same type; such work has gradually been handed over to [[gpu]] and specialized chips.
主频不等于性能。每个时钟周期能完成多少工作（IPC）、缓存大小和内存速度同样重要: Clock frequency does not equal performance. The amount of work completed per clock cycle (IPC), cache size, and memory speed are equally important. Around 2005, single-core clock frequency basically stopped growing (see [[dennard-scaling]]).
CPU 的基本循环。程序计数器（PC）指向下一条指令，循环一圈就执行完一条指令。: The basic cycle of a CPU. The Program Counter (PC) points to the next instruction; after one loop, one instruction is executed.
把整个 CPU 做进一颗芯片；Intel 4004 只有约 2300 个晶体管。: Putting the entire CPU onto a single chip; the Intel 4004 had only about 2300 transistors.
