当集成电路能容纳足够多的晶体管时，整个 CPU 就能做进一颗芯片；芯片可以像印刷: When integrated circuits can accommodate enough transistors, the entire CPU can be made onto a single chip; chips can be mass-produced like printed materials, causing the price of CPUs to plummet.
微处理器把控制单元、运算单元和寄存器集成在一块硅片上，外接内存和输入输出就是一台: A microprocessor integrates the Control Unit, Arithmetic Logic Unit, and registers onto a single silicon wafer; with external memory and input/output connected, it becomes a computer. It was originally designed for calculators, later installed in cash registers, automobiles, personal computers, and almost all electronic appliances.
1971 年 11 月英特尔推出 4004，由霍夫（Ted Hoff）提出构想、: In November 1971, Intel launched the 4004, proposed by Hoff (Ted Hoff), led by Faggin (Federico Faggin) for chip design, with participation from Ishizaki (Masatoshi Ishizaki) for logic design, initially developed for Busicom Company's calculator. It is a 4-bit processor with about 2300 transistors and a maximum clock frequency of 740 kHz. The 8080 in 1974 and the 8086 in 1978 laid the foundation for personal computer chips; the instruction set of the latter evolved into today's x86.
今天一颗手机处理器有数百亿个晶体管，比 4004 多了约一千万倍。微处理器让\": Today, a single mobile phone processor contains hundreds of billions of transistors, approximately ten million times more than the 4004. Microprocessors have enabled "computation" to be embedded into everything (see [[embedded-system]]).
软件和硬件之间的\"合同\"，规定 CPU 认识哪些指令；x86、ARM、RIS: The "contract" between software and hardware specifies which instructions the CPU recognizes; x86, ARM, and RISC-V are the three major families.
在软件和硬件之间定一份稳定的\"合同\"，双方就能各自独立进化——软件不用为每代: By establishing a stable "contract" between software and hardware, both sides can evolve independently—software does not need to be rewritten for every new generation of chips, and chip designers can freely improve internal implementations.
指令集架构（ISA）规定 CPU 认识哪些指令（如加法、读内存、跳转）、有哪些寄: The Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) defines which instructions the CPU recognizes (such as addition, memory access, and jump), how many registers exist, and how instructions are encoded in binary. As long as the same ISA is followed, chips from different manufacturers and different eras can run the same programs. The specific internal implementation of a chip (called "microarchitecture") can be completely different.
ISA 一旦拥有庞大的软件生态就极难被替代，这就是 x86 能延续四十多年的原因: Once an ISA possesses a vast software ecosystem, it becomes extremely difficult to replace; this is the reason x86 has continued for over forty years. Whoever holds the license for an ISA controls a key position in the industry.
用少量简单、等长的指令换取更快的流水线；如今的高性能 CPU 内部大多是 RIS: Using a small number of simple, equal-length instructions trades off for faster pipelines; today's high-performance CPUs are mostly RISC-style internally.
编译器生成的程序其实只频繁使用少数简单指令；把硬件集中在把这些简单指令做到极快，: Programs generated by compilers actually use only a few simple instructions frequently; concentrating hardware on making these simple instructions extremely fast results in an overall faster system.
精简指令集（RISC）使用数量较少、长度固定、格式规整的指令，内存访问只通过专门: Reduced Instruction Set Computer (RISC) uses fewer, fixed-length, and well-formatted instructions, with memory access completed only through dedicated read/write instructions. This allows each instruction to be completed in approximately the same time, which is suitable for [[pipeline|Assembly line]]. Complex Instruction Set Computer (CISC), such as x86, allows a single instruction to do many things, resulting in more compact code, but hardware is harder to parallelize.
IBM 的科克（John Cocke）在 1970 年代的 801 项目中率先实: IBM's John Cocke pioneered practice in the 801 project during the 1970s. Starting in 1980, David Patterson from UC Berkeley and John Hennessy from Stanford led the RISC and MIPS projects respectively, earning them the Turing Award in 2017.
RISC 之争最终以\"融合\"收场：今天的 x86 芯片在内部先把复杂指令拆成: The RISC debate ultimately ended with "convergence": today's x86 chips internally decompose complex instructions into RISC-style micro-operations before execution, while ARM inside mobile phones is itself RISC.
以低功耗著称的 RISC 架构，靠授权模式统治了手机，并进入服务器和 Mac。: RISC architectures known for low power consumption ruled over mobile phones through licensing models and have entered servers and Macs.
手机靠电池供电，能效（每焦耳能做多少计算）比峰值性能更重要；而只卖设计授权、不自: Mobile phones rely on battery power; energy efficiency (how much computation can be done per joule) is more important than peak performance. Selling only design licenses without manufacturing chips oneself allows chip factories worldwide to become customers.
ARM 公司设计指令集和处理器核，授权给苹果、高通、华为海思、联发科等厂商，由它: ARM Company designs instruction sets and processor cores, licensing them to Apple, Qualcomm, Huawei HiSilicon, MediaTek, and other manufacturers. They design their own chips themselves and then hand them over to foundries such as TSMC for production (see [[foundry-model]]).
1985 年英国 Acorn 公司造出第一颗 ARM 处理器；1990 年 AR: In 1985, the British Acorn Company created the first ARM processor; in 1990, ARM Company was established independently. Starting in 2020, Apple Macs switched to self-developed ARM chips.
ARM 芯片已出货数千亿颗，几乎每部智能手机都用它，它也正在进入笔记本和数据中心: ARM chips have shipped over hundreds of billions of units, almost every smartphone uses it, and it is also entering laptops and data centers.
加州大学伯克利分校发起的开放指令集，任何人都可免授权费使用。: The open instruction set initiated by UC Berkeley allows anyone to use it without licensing fees.
指令集只是一份规范，把它像开源软件一样免费公开，任何人都可以设计兼容芯片，不必支: An instruction set is merely a specification; making it publicly available like open-source software means anyone can design compatible chips without paying licensing fees or being controlled by a single company.
RISC-V 采用\"小核心 + 可选扩展\"的模块化设计：最基础的整数指令集只: RISC-V adopts a modular design of "small core + optional extensions": the basic integer instruction set has only dozens of instructions, with floating-point, vector, compressed instructions, etc., added as needed, making it very suitable for various custom chips ranging from microcontrollers to AI accelerators.
2010 年由加州大学伯克利分校的阿萨诺维奇（Krste Asanović）、帕: Initiated in 2010 by Krste Asanović and others from UC Berkeley, the foundation was established in 2015 to promote it (later relocated to Switzerland).
RISC-V 已广泛用于物联网芯片和各种处理器内部的控制核心，中国厂商也大量采用: RISC-V is widely used for IoT chips and control cores inside various processors. Chinese manufacturers also adopt it extensively, viewing it as a choice to break dependence on licensing.
把一条指令拆成多个阶段，像流水线一样让多条指令重叠执行，时钟每\"滴答\"一次推: Breaking a single instruction into multiple stages, like a pipeline, allows multiple instructions to overlap execution; the clock advances one stage every "tick".
把一项工作切成几个阶段，每个阶段由不同的部件负责，就能让多项工作同时处于不同阶段: Dividing a task into several stages, with each stage handled by different components, allows multiple tasks to be in different stages simultaneously—total time remains unchanged, but the number of items completed per unit of time increases exponentially ([[p:division|Division of labor]]).
经典的五级流水线把一条指令拆成取指、译码、执行、访存、写回。第 1 个时钟周期取: The classic five-stage pipeline breaks an instruction into fetch, decode, execute, memory access, and write-back. During the first clock cycle, the first instruction is fetched; during the second cycle, the first instruction is decoded while the second is fetched... Once the pipeline is full, one instruction completes every clock cycle. The clock is the "metronome" of the entire chip; all components advance one step in unison.
麻烦在于\"冒险\"：后一条指令需要前一条的结果，或者遇到跳转不知道下一条在哪。: The challenge lies in "risk": the second instruction requires the result of the first, or if a jump occurs, it is unknown where the next instruction will be. CPUs use techniques such as data forwarding and branch prediction to reduce pipeline "stalls".
流水线是 CPU 提速最重要的手段之一，和工厂的装配线是同一个思路（见 [[as: Pipelining is one of the most important means for speeding up CPUs, following the same logic as an assembly line (see [[assembly-line]]).
五级流水线像阶梯一样错开执行，从第 5 个周期起每个周期都完成一条指令。: A five-stage pipeline executes stages offset like steps; starting from the 5th cycle, a new instruction completes every cycle.
单核提速撞上功耗墙后，芯片改为放多个核心并行干活，软件也必须学会并行。: After single-core speed improvements hit power walls, chips began placing multiple cores to work in parallel, and software also had to learn parallelism.
功耗大约随频率的三次方增长，单核再提速就会热到无法散热；放两个慢一点的核心，用更: Power consumption grows approximately with the cube of frequency; further speeding up a single core would make it too hot to cool. Placing two slower cores allows more work to be done using less electricity—provided the work can be split for parallel execution.
多核处理器在一块芯片上放多个完整的 CPU 核心，它们共享部分缓存和内存。操作系: Multi-core processors place multiple complete CPU cores on a single chip, sharing parts of cache and memory. The operating system assigns different programs or threads to run on different cores (see [[process-thread]]).
IBM 在 2001 年推出双核的 POWER4 服务器芯片；2005 年英特尔: IBM launched the dual-core POWER4 server chip in 2001; Intel and AMD released dual-core processors for personal computers in 2005. Today, mobile chips typically have over eight cores, while server chips can reach hundreds of cores.
免费的性能提升结束了，程序员必须学会写并行程序。著名的阿姆达尔定律指出：程序中无: Free performance gains ended; programmers must learn to write parallel programs. Amdahl's Law states that the portion of a program that cannot be parallelized determines the upper limit of speedup.
拥有成千上万个小核心、擅长同时做大量相同运算的处理器，从画游戏画面走向训练 AI: Processors with tens of thousands of small cores, skilled at performing large amounts of identical operations simultaneously, have evolved from rendering game graphics to training AI models.
画面上几百万个像素、神经网络里几十亿次乘法，都是\"对大量数据做同一种运算\"；: Rendering involves millions of pixels; neural networks involve billions of multiplications. Both are cases of "performing the same operation on a large amount of data." It is better to use tens of thousands of simple small cores working in parallel ([[p:division|Division of labor]]) than to rely on a few smart large cores calculating one by one.
CPU 像几位能力全面的教授，擅长复杂的逻辑判断；GPU 像几千名小学生，每人只: CPUs act like professors with broad capabilities, skilled at complex logic judgments; GPUs act like thousands of elementary school students, each knowing only simple arithmetic, but achieving remarkable throughput when working together. GPUs group cores so that cores in the same group execute the same instruction and process different data at the same time (known as SIMT). They are also equipped with extremely high-bandwidth memory (see [[hbm]]) to ensure data is fed in.
原本用于图形的 GPU 后来被开放为通用计算平台：程序员可以用 CUDA 等工具: GPUs originally used for graphics were later opened up as general-purpose computing platforms: programmers can use tools like CUDA to assign scientific computing and machine learning tasks to GPUs. Neural network training involves a large number of matrix multiplications, and GPU speed can be tens to hundreds of times faster than CPU.
1999 年英伟达（NVIDIA）发布 GeForce 256，并首次以\"GP: In 1999, NVIDIA released the GeForce 256 and first named it "GPU." In 2007, NVIDIA released the CUDA platform. In 2012, AlexNet trained using two GPUs, leading significantly in image recognition competitions (see [[imagenet]]), opening the era of deep learning. Since then, GPU has become the core hardware for AI training (see [[ai-accelerator]]).
GPU 让游戏画面越来越逼真，也让深度学习从理论变为现实。算力需求的爆发使英伟达: GPUs have made game graphics increasingly realistic and enabled deep learning to move from theory to reality. The explosion in computing power requirements placed NVIDIA among the globally highest market-value companies during the 2020s.
CPU 用少数复杂核心处理复杂逻辑；GPU 用大量简单核心同时处理相同的运算。: CPUs use a few complex cores to handle complex logic; GPUs use many simple cores to process identical operations simultaneously.
寄存器、缓存、内存、硬盘由快到慢、由贵到便宜排成金字塔，用局部性让整体又快又大。: Registers, cache, memory, and hard drives are arranged in a pyramid from fast to slow and expensive to cheap, using locality to make the whole system both fast and large.
存储器总是\"快的小而贵、大的慢而便宜\"，物理上无法兼得；但程序访问数据有很强: Memory is always "fast small and expensive, large slow and cheap"; physically, one cannot have both. However, program access to data has strong [[p:locality|Locality & caching]]; by placing frequently used data in smaller, faster layers, the overall system can appear "both fast and large".
从 CPU 往外，存储排成一座金字塔：**寄存器**（不到 1 纳秒，几百字节）: From CPU outward, storage is arranged like a pyramid: **registers** (under 1 nanosecond, hundreds of bytes) → **cache levels** (about 1–40 nanoseconds, KB to MB level) → **DRAM memory** (about 100 nanoseconds, GB level) → **solid-state drives SSD** (tens to hundreds of microseconds, TB level) → **magnetic hard drives/tape** (millisecond level, almost infinite). The speed difference between adjacent upper and lower layers is often 10 to 1000 times.
数据会被自动\"搬\"到离 CPU 更近的层级：CPU 要读一个数时先查缓存，命: Data will be automatically "moved" to layers closer to the CPU: when a CPU reads a number, it first checks cache; if hit, it is fast; if not hit, it goes to the next layer to fetch and brings up an entire nearby block of data at once, because they are likely to be used soon.
时间局部性：刚用过的数据很可能再用（如循环变量）；空间局部性：用过的数据附近的数: Temporal locality: recently used data is likely to be used again (such as loop variables); spatial locality: data near used data is also likely to be used (such as sequential array traversal).
存储层次是计算机设计中最普遍的思想，同样的原理也用在浏览器缓存、[[cdn]]: The storage hierarchy is the most common design principle in computer architecture; the same principle is also used in browser caching, [[cdn]], and databases. If programmers write code following this principle (such as accessing arrays sequentially), speed may increase tenfold.
图中的时间只代表数量级，具体数值因硬件而异。把 1 纳秒想象成 1 秒，读内存就: The time in the figure represents only order of magnitude; specific values vary by hardware. Imagine 1 nanosecond as 1 second; reading memory is like waiting about 2 minutes, while seeking on a magnetic hard drive takes several months.
存储层次金字塔：越往上越快、越小、越贵。延迟为典型数量级。: Storage hierarchy pyramid: higher up means faster, smaller, and more expensive. Latency represents typical order of magnitude.
在快的部件旁放一小块更快的存储，保存最近用过的数据；从 CPU 到 CDN 处处: Placing a small block of faster storage next to fast components saves recently used data; from CPU to CDN, caching is everywhere.
给慢的东西前面放一个快的小副本，保存最近用过和可能马上要用的数据，大多数访问就不: Place a fast small copy in front of the slow thing, saving data that was recently used and might be needed soon; most accesses do not need to reach the slow layer ([[p:locality|Locality & caching]]).
CPU 缓存由硬件自动管理，通常分为 L1、L2、L3 三级，越靠近核心越小越快: CPU cache is automatically managed by hardware, typically divided into three levels: L1, L2, and L3. The closer to the core, the smaller and faster it is. Data is moved in units called "cache lines" (commonly 64 bytes). When cache is full, old data is evicted according to some strategy (such as "least recently used"). Multi-core chips must also ensure that the same data in each core's cache remains consistent, known as cache coherence.
1965 年英国计算机科学家威尔克斯（Maurice Wilkes）提出\"从属: In 1965, British computer scientist Maurice Wilkes proposed the concept of "auxiliary memory"; in 1968, IBM System/360 Model 85 used cache for the first time on a commercial machine.
缓存命中率常常比 CPU 主频更能决定程序快慢。\"缓存\"这个思想遍布计算的各: Cache hit rate often determines program speed more than CPU clock frequency. The idea of "cache" is widespread across all levels of computation: CPU, hard disk, browser, [[cdn]], database queries; it is used everywhere.
用一个晶体管加一个电容存一个比特，便宜密集但要不断\"刷新\"，是电脑的内存条。: Storing one bit with a transistor plus a capacitor is cheap and dense but requires constant "refreshing"; this is the computer's memory stick.
用一个电容里有没有电荷表示 1 和 0，再配一个晶体管做开关，一个比特只需两个元: Representing 1 and 0 by whether there is charge in a capacitor, paired with a transistor as a switch; one bit only needs two components, allowing it to be made extremely dense and cheap.
电容会慢慢漏电，所以 DRAM 必须每隔几十毫秒把所有数据读出来再写回去，称为\: Capacitors slowly leak charge, so DRAM must read all data back and write it again every few tens of milliseconds; this is called "refreshing"—this is the meaning of "dynamic." After power-off, all data disappears. DRAM chips are mounted on memory sticks, exchanging data with the CPU through a memory controller.
1966 年 IBM 的登纳德（Robert Dennard）发明单晶体管 DR: In 1966, IBM's Robert Dennard invented the single-transistor DRAM unit; in 1970, Intel launched the first commercial DRAM chip, model 1103. Today it is mainly produced by Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron.
DRAM 是计算机的\"工作台\"，它的容量决定了能同时打开多少程序。AI 时代: DRAM is the computer's "workbench"; its capacity determines how many programs can be opened simultaneously. In the AI era, the bottleneck is often not computing power but memory bandwidth, which has driven the development of [[hbm]].
把多层 DRAM 竖着堆叠并紧贴处理器封装，为 GPU 和 AI 芯片提供超高带: Stack multiple DRAM layers vertically and mount them close to the processor package, providing ultra-high bandwidth for GPUs and AI chips.
数据搬运的速度取决于\"路有多宽、有多远\"。把内存芯片竖着叠起来、贴着处理器放: The speed of data transfer depends on "how wide the road is and how far it goes." Stacking memory chips vertically, placing them next to the processor, and adding tens of thousands of channels can increase bandwidth by an order of magnitude.
高带宽内存（HBM）把 8–12 层甚至更多 DRAM 芯片垂直堆叠，用穿透硅片: High-bandwidth memory (HBM) stacks 8–12 or even more DRAM chips vertically, connects them using vertical wires that penetrate the silicon wafer (TSV), and packages them together with the GPU on a single intermediate layer (see [[chiplet]]); bus width reaches over a thousand bits.
2013 年由 AMD 和 SK 海力士等推动成为 JEDEC 标准，2015: In 2013, AMD and SK Hynix and others promoted it to become a JEDEC standard; in 2015, it was first used in AMD graphics cards.
今天的 AI 加速器几乎都依赖 HBM，HBM 产能一度成为 AI 芯片供应的瓶: Today's AI accelerators almost all rely on HBM; HBM production capacity once became the bottleneck for AI chip supply.
把电荷困在绝缘层包围的\"浮栅\"里存数据，断电不丢，用于 U 盘、SSD 和手: Trapping charge inside an "floating gate" surrounded by an insulator to store data; data is not lost after power-off, used for USB drives, SSDs, and mobile phones.
在晶体管的栅极下面加一层被绝缘体包围的\"浮栅\"，电子靠量子隧穿被推进去后就出: Add a "floating gate" surrounded by an insulator under the transistor's gate; electrons pushed in via quantum tunneling cannot come out, so data can be saved even after power-off ([[p:tunneling|Quantum tunneling]]).
写入时加高电压，让电子隧穿进入浮栅（或电荷陷阱层）；浮栅里有没有电子，决定了这个: During writing, apply high voltage to let electrons tunnel into the floating gate (or charge trap layer); whether there are electrons in the floating gate determines if this transistor is easy to conduct, thus representing 0 or 1. Each unit can also store multiple charge levels; one unit stores 3–4 bits (TLC/QLC). Erasing must be done in large blocks, and each unit has a limited number of write cycles, so the controller performs "wear leveling." Modern 3D NAND stacks storage units vertically to over two hundred layers.
东芝的舛冈富士雄（Fujio Masuoka）在 1980 年代初发明闪存，19: Fujio Masuoka at Toshiba invented flash memory in the early 1980s; published NOR-type flash memory in 1984; published NAND-type flash memory in 1987.
用闪存代替旋转磁盘的硬盘，没有机械部件，随机读写快上百倍。: Replacing spinning-disk hard disks with flash memory eliminates mechanical parts; random read/write speed is over a hundred times faster.
没有旋转盘片和移动磁头，读写任何位置都一样快，随机访问速度比机械硬盘快上百倍。: Without rotating platters and moving magnetic heads, read/write speed at any position is the same; random access speed is over a hundred times faster than mechanical hard disks.
SSD 由多颗 NAND [[flash-memory|闪存]] 芯片和一个控制: An SSD consists of multiple NAND [[flash-memory|Flash memory]] chips and a controller; the controller distributes data writing to various chips for parallel read/write, performs error correction, and manages wear leveling. When connected directly to high-speed buses via the NVMe protocol, read speeds can reach several GB per second.
SSD 让电脑开机和打开软件从几十秒缩短到几秒，也让数据库和云服务的性能大幅提升: SSDs shorten computer boot time and software opening from tens of seconds to a few seconds, and significantly improve performance for databases and cloud services. Mechanical hard disks are gradually relegated to large-capacity cold data storage.
磁头在高速旋转的磁盘上方几纳米处读写磁化方向；每比特成本仍然最低。: The magnetic head reads/writes magnetization direction just a few nanometers above the rapidly spinning disk; cost per bit remains the lowest.
用磁性材料微小区域的磁化方向记录 0 和 1，磁化状态不需要电力就能长期保持；盘: Store 0s and 1s by recording the magnetization direction of tiny regions of magnetic material; the magnetized state can be maintained for a long time without power. Rotating the platters and moving the read/write head allow access to any position.
一块或几块涂有磁性材料的盘片以每分钟 5400–15000 转高速旋转，磁头悬浮: One or more platters coated with magnetic material rotate at high speeds of 5400–15000 rpm. The read/write head hovers just a few nanometers above the platter surface, comparable to an airplane flying just a few millimeters above the ground. To read or write at a specific location, one must wait for the head to move (seeking) and the platter to rotate into position; therefore, random access is slow while sequential access is fast.
1956 年 IBM 推出 350 RAMAC，有 50 张 24 英寸盘片，容: In 1956, IBM launched the 350 RAMAC with 50 twenty-four-inch platters, offering a capacity of approximately 5 MB and weighing about one ton. The discovery of the giant magnetoresistance effect in 1988 made read heads more sensitive, significantly increasing storage density (see [[spintronics]]). Today, a single hard drive can reach approximately 30 TB.
硬盘让\"随机访问大量数据\"成为可能，是数据库和个人电脑的基础。每 TB 成本: Hard drives made 'random access to large amounts of data' possible, forming the foundation for databases and personal computers. The cost per TB remains far lower than that of SSDs; thus, high-capacity storage in data centers still relies heavily on them.
可插拔的磁性存储盘，曾是软件分发和文件交换的主要媒介；\"保存\"图标至今是它的: Removable magnetic storage discs were once the primary medium for software distribution and file exchange; the 'save' icon still resembles a floppy disk.
把磁盘做成可以插拔、邮寄的薄片，数据和软件就能在不同计算机之间搬运。: Making the disc thin enough to be removable and mailable allowed data and software to be transferred between different computers.
软盘是装在保护套里的柔软磁性圆片，插入驱动器后由磁头接触读写。尺寸从 8 英寸、: The floppy disk is a soft, magnetic circular disc housed in a protective sleeve. After inserting it into a drive, the read/write head contacts it for reading and writing. The size shrank from 8 inches to 5.25 inches and then to 3.5 inches; the most common 3.5-inch high-density floppy disk has a capacity of 1.44 MB.
IBM 在 1971 年推出 8 英寸软盘。1990 年代后期起被光盘和 U 盘: IBM launched the 8-inch floppy disk in 1971. Starting in the late 1990s, it was replaced by optical discs and USB flash drives.
软盘是个人电脑时代分发软件的主要方式，\"保存\"按钮的图标至今还是一张软盘。: The floppy disk was the primary method for distributing software during the personal computer era; the icon for the 'save' button still depicts a floppy disk.
顺序读写、极其便宜耐久，至今用于数据中心的冷备份。: Sequential read/write, extremely cheap, and durable; it is still used for cold backups in data centers.
只能从头到尾顺序读写的长条磁带，单位容量成本极低、离线保存几十年不耗电，最适合\: A long strip of tape that can only be read sequentially from start to finish. With an extremely low cost per unit capacity and the ability to remain offline for decades without power consumption, it is best suited for backup data that requires 'write once, rarely read'.
磁带缠在卷盘上，读写时在磁头下匀速移动，读取某个位置需要先把磁带卷到那里，可能要: The tape is wound around a reel; during read/write operations, it moves at a constant speed under the head. Reading a specific location requires winding the tape there, which may take tens of seconds. Modern LTO tapes can store dozens of TB on a single reel.
1951 年的 UNIVAC I 首次用磁带作为计算机存储。: UNIVAC I in 1951 first used tape as computer storage.
大型云服务商至今用自动化磁带库保存冷备份；磁带离线存放，还可以抵御勒索软件（见: Large cloud service providers still use automated tape libraries to preserve cold backups; since the tape is kept offline, it can also resist ransomware (see [[ransomware]]).
用激光读取盘面上微小凹坑的反射差异，配合纠错码，划伤也能正常播放。: Read differences in reflection from tiny pits on the disc surface using a laser, combined with error-correcting code, allowing normal playback even if scratched.
用激光照射盘面，凹坑和平面反射的光强不同，读出来就是 0 和 1；配合强大的 [: Illuminate the disc surface with a laser; the difference in light intensity reflected from pits and flat areas is read as 0s and 1s. Combined with a powerful [[p:redundancy|Error-correcting code]], data can be completely read out even if there are scratches.
CD 的螺旋轨道上压制着微小的凹坑，激光头沿轨道读取反射光。从 CD 到 DVD: Tiny pits are pressed onto a spiral track on the disc. The laser head reads reflected light along the track. From CD to DVD to Blu-ray, the laser wavelength shortens sequentially (infrared, red, blue-violet), making the pits smaller and increasing capacity from approximately 700 MB to 4.7 GB and then to over 25 GB.
1982 年索尼和飞利浦推出音乐 CD；1995 年 DVD 规格确定，2006: Sony and Philips launched the music CD in 1982; the DVD specification was finalized in 1995, and Blu-ray discs were released in 2006.
光盘是 1990 年代软件、音乐和电影的主要载体，后来被网络下载和流媒体取代。: Optical discs were the primary carrier for software, music, and movies during the 1990s, later being replaced by online downloads and streaming media.
统一电脑外设接口和充电的标准，从键盘到手机充电都用它。: Standardize computer peripheral interfaces and charging methods; from keyboards to mobile phone charging, they all use it.
统一接口标准，所有设备都能\"即插即用\"，厂商和用户都不必再为每种设备准备专用: Standardize interface specifications so that all devices can 'plug and play'; manufacturers and users no longer need to prepare dedicated interfaces for each type of device ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
USB 用一根线同时传输数据和电力，主机自动识别新插入的设备并加载驱动。新版 U: USB transmits data and power simultaneously via a single cable. The host automatically recognizes newly inserted devices and loads drivers. New versions of USB increased speed from an initial 12 Mbit per second to over 40 Gbit per second; the USB-C interface can be inserted in either direction, with power supply reaching up to 240 W.
1996 年由英特尔、微软、康柏、IBM 等公司联合推出 USB 1.0，阿杰伊: USB 1.0 was jointly launched by Intel, Microsoft, Compaq, IBM, and others in 1996. Ajay Bhatt is often called the 'father of USB'. Starting at the end of 2024, the European Union requires that mobile phones and other devices on sale use the USB-C charging interface uniformly.
USB 取代了串口、并口等五花八门的接口，也成为全球最通用的充电接口。: USB replaced a variety of interfaces such as serial ports and parallel ports and became the most universal charging interface globally.
把电脑装进可携带的机身，电池和低功耗芯片决定了它们的形态。: Putting computers into portable chassis is determined by batteries and low-power chips.
便携设备受电池能量限制，所以一切围绕\"每瓦性能\"设计：低功耗芯片、高效屏幕和: Portable devices are limited by battery energy, so everything revolves around 'performance per watt': low-power chips, efficient screens, and high energy density batteries ([[p:energydensity|Energy density]]).
笔记本把屏幕、键盘、电池和主板装进可折叠的机身；平板电脑去掉键盘，用触摸屏直接操: Laptops put screens, keyboards, batteries, and motherboards into foldable chassis; tablets remove the keyboard and use touchscreens for direct operation. Their development depends on the joint progress of low-power processors, [[lithium-ion|Lithium-ion battery]], LCDs, and solid-state storage.
1981 年的 Osborne 1 被认为是第一台商业成功的便携式电脑，重约 1: The 1981 Osborne 1 is considered the first commercially successful portable computer, weighing about 11 kilograms; the 1982 GRiD Compass established the clamshell structure. Apple's iPad in 2010 made tablets a mass-market product.
计算从书桌搬进了背包，又从背包搬进了口袋（见 [[smartphone]]）。: Computing moved from the desk into a backpack, and then from the backpack into a pocket (see [[smartphone]]).
藏在洗衣机、汽车、路由器里的专用小电脑，通常要求实时、省电、可靠。: Specialized small computers hidden inside washing machines, cars, and routers usually require real-time operation, low power consumption, and reliability.
很多设备只需要一种固定功能，把一台专用的小电脑\"嵌\"进去，用软件代替复杂的机: Many devices only need one fixed function; embedding a dedicated small computer 'into' them, using software to replace complex mechanical and circuitry, makes products cheaper and more flexible.
嵌入式系统通常以微控制器（MCU）为核心，把 CPU、少量内存和输入输出接口集成: Embedded systems typically center on microcontrollers (MCUs), integrating CPUs, small amounts of memory, and input/output interfaces onto a single chip, running solidified programs or real-time operating systems. They often require guaranteed response within specified time limits (real-time), and must run stably for years.
1960 年代的阿波罗导航计算机是早期著名的嵌入式计算机。今天一辆汽车里可能有上: The Apollo navigation computer from the 1960s was an early famous embedded computer. Today, a single car may contain hundreds of electronic control units.
嵌入式系统让洗衣机、微波炉、汽车、路由器和医疗设备都变成了\"计算机\"，也是: Embedded systems turned washing machines, microwaves, cars, routers, and medical devices into 'computers', and also form the foundation of [[iot|Internet of Things (IoT)]].
把成千上万个处理器联网并行，用于气候、核物理、药物模拟等最重的计算。: Connecting tens of thousands of processors in a network for parallel processing is used for the heaviest computations: climate modeling, nuclear physics, drug simulation, etc.
单个处理器的速度有物理上限，但把成千上万个处理器用高速网络连起来、把大问题拆成小: The speed of a single processor has a physical upper limit, but connecting tens of thousands of processors via high-speed networks and splitting large problems into small blocks for simultaneous calculation allows total computing power to grow linearly ([[p:division|Division of labor]]).
超级计算机由大量计算节点组成，每个节点有 CPU、往往还有 GPU，节点之间用专: Supercomputers consist of many computing nodes; each node contains a CPU and often also a GPU, with nodes interconnected using specialized low-latency networks. Scientists partition physical models of climate, nuclear fusion, materials, or drugs into grids, assigning each node to calculate a block while continuously exchanging boundary data (see [[scientific-computing]]). Performance is measured in floating-point operations per second (FLOPS); the global TOP500 list is published twice yearly to rank solutions for large linear equation sets using the Linpack test.
1964 年西摩·克雷设计的 CDC 6600 被视为第一台超级计算机；1976: Seymour Cray's 1964-designed CDC 6600 is considered the first supercomputer; the 1976 [[cray|Cray-1 & vector computers]] became a classic. In 2022, the US Frontier officially broke through exascale (E-scale) for the first time (see [[exascale-computing]]). On the June 2026 list, China's Shenzhen 'LineShine' topped the rankings with approximately 2.2 E-scale performance, using only CPUs and no GPUs.
超算让\"数值实验\"成为科学研究的支柱，天气预报、核武器维护和新药研发都依赖它: Supercomputers make 'numerical experiments' a pillar of scientific research; weather forecasting, nuclear weapons maintenance, and new drug development all depend on them.
西摩·克雷设计的经典超级计算机，一条指令同时处理一整串数据。: Seymour Cray's classic supercomputer processes an entire stream of data with a single instruction.
科学计算里大量是\"对一整列数据做同一个运算\"，设计一种一条指令就处理一整串数: In scientific computing, there is much 'applying the same operation to an entire column of data'; designing a processor that handles an entire stream of data with a single instruction saves the overhead of repeated instruction fetching.
Cray-1 有专门的向量寄存器，一次可装 64 个数，一条指令就让它们流水线式: Cray-1 had dedicated vector registers capable of holding 64 numbers at once; a single instruction allowed them to pass through the computation unit in a pipelined manner. Its unique C-shaped chassis was designed to shorten internal wiring length, because at that speed, signal propagation time in wires was already non-negligible.
1976 年由\"超级计算机之父\"西摩·克雷（Seymour Cray）设计，: Designed in 1976 by 'father of supercomputing' Seymour Cray (Seymour Cray), it achieved a peak speed of approximately 160 million floating-point operations per second.
向量计算的思想后来被 CPU 的 SIMD 指令和 [[gpu]] 继承下来。: The concept of vector computing was later inherited by CPU SIMD instructions and [[gpu]].
解决一类问题的明确、有限的步骤；好的算法比更快的机器更重要。: A clear, finite set of steps to solve a class of problems; good algorithms are more important than faster machines.
机器再快也只能线性地快，而好算法能让工作量按 [[p:complexity|数量: Machines can only get faster linearly, but good algorithms allow workload to decrease according to [[p:complexity|Computational complexity]]—in big data scenarios, the difference between algorithms far exceeds the difference between hardware.
算法是解决一类问题的明确步骤：输入什么、每一步做什么、什么时候停、输出什么。它必: An algorithm is a clear set of steps to solve a class of problems: what input, what to do at each step, when to stop, and what output. It must provide correct results within a finite number of steps for all valid inputs. Algorithm evaluation mainly focuses on two things: **time** (how fast the step count grows as data size increases) and **space** (how much extra memory is needed), commonly described using [[big-o]].
举个例子：在 100 万个按顺序排好的名字里找一个人。从头一个个找，最坏要找 1: For example: finding a person among 1 million names sorted in order. Searching from the head one by one requires up to 1 million searches; using **binary search**, comparing with the middle element each time and eliminating half, it can find the target in at most 20 steps. When data grows to 1 billion, the former method requires 1 billion steps, while the latter only needs 30 steps.
2000 年美国得州理工大学的江红星（Hongxing Jiang）团队首次展示: In 2000, Hongxing Jiang's team at Texas A&M University first demonstrated a miniature LED array; since then, multiple companies have launched tiled large screens and prototype devices.
它被视为下一代显示技术的候选，目前主要用于超大拼接屏和小尺寸近眼显示，消费级大规: It is regarded as a candidate for next-generation display technology, currently mainly used for ultra-large tiled screens and small-size near-eye displays; mass production for consumer applications is still under development (see [[led]], [[oled]]).
感知温度并自动开关加热或制冷，是最常见的负反馈装置；如今的智能温控器还能学习习惯: Perceiving temperature and automatically switching heating or cooling is the most common negative feedback mechanism; modern smart thermostats can also learn user habits.
传统机械恒温器用双金属片：两种热膨胀系数不同的金属贴在一起，受热时向一侧弯曲，推: Traditional mechanical thermostats use bimetallic strips: two metals with different coefficients of thermal expansion are bonded together, bending toward one side when heated to push contacts open or closed. Electronic thermostats measure temperature using thermistors and control them via microcontrollers. Smart thermostats, when connected to the internet, can learn users' schedules, automatically save energy when people are away from home, and allow remote adjustment via smartphone.
用卡片上孔的有无记录信息，先控制提花织机，后用于人口普查制表，开创了数据处理业。: Information was recorded by the presence or absence of holes on cards; this method first controlled jacquard looms, then enabled census tabulation, founding the data processing industry.
1948 年香农（Claude Shannon）在《通信的数学理论》中使用并推广: In 1948, Claude Shannon used and popularized the term "bit" in "A Mathematical Theory of Communication," noting that the word was proposed by statistician John Tukey. The 8-bit byte became a standard with IBM System/360 in 1964.
1964 年 IBM System/360 首次把 ISA 和具体实现分开（见: In 1964, IBM System/360 first separated ISA from specific implementations (see [[mainframe]]). Today's three major families are: x86 (Intel, AMD, ruling computers and servers), ARM (ruling mobile phones, entering servers and Macs, see [[arm-architecture]]), and open-source free [[risc-v]].
常见的算法设计思路有：分治（拆成小问题分别解决再合并，如归并排序）、贪心（每步选: Common algorithm design approaches include: divide-and-conquer (splitting into small problems to solve separately then merging, such as merge sort), greedy (choosing the best option at each step), [[dynamic-programming|Dynamic programming]] (remembering answers to subproblems), and randomized methods.
公元前 300 年左右的欧几里得求最大公约数算法至今仍在使用。\"算法\"（al: Euclid's algorithm for finding the greatest common divisor, dating back to around 300 BCE, is still in use today. The term "algorithm" comes from the Latinized name of 9th-century Persian mathematician al-Khwārizmī. Starting in 1968, Donald Knuth's published "The Art of Computer Programming" systematically established the field of algorithm analysis.
从搜索引擎排名、地图导航、视频压缩到加密和机器学习，现代技术的核心竞争力往往是一: From search engine rankings and map navigation to video compression and encryption, modern technology's core competitiveness often lies in a set of algorithms.
在 100 万个有序元素中查找：逐个查找最坏 100 万步，二分查找最多 20: Searching among 1 million ordered elements: linear search takes up to 1 million steps in the worst case; binary search takes at most 20 steps.
组织数据的方式（数组、链表、树、哈希表、图），决定了哪些操作快、哪些慢。: The way data is organized (arrays, linked lists, trees, hash tables, graphs) determines which operations are fast and which are slow.
同样的数据，组织方式不同，各种操作的代价就天差地别；选择数据结构就是在\"查找快: With the same data, different organizational methods lead to vastly different costs for various operations; choosing a data structure involves trade-offs between "fast lookup, fast insertion, and low memory usage".
**数组**把元素挨个放在连续内存里，按位置访问极快，但在中间插入要挪动后面所有: **Arrays** place elements consecutively in continuous memory, allowing extremely fast access by position, but inserting in the middle requires moving all subsequent elements; **linked lists** use pointers to chain elements together, enabling fast insertion and deletion, but finding the k-th element requires counting from the head; **hash tables** use [[hashing|Hashing]] to directly calculate positions, requiring only one step on average for lookup; **trees** (such as binary search trees, B-trees) keep data ordered, making lookup and insertion logarithmic time operations, forming the basis of database indexes; **graphs** represent networks such as city roads and social relationships (see [[graph-algorithms]]); **stacks** (last-in-first-out) and **queues** (first-in-first-out) are used for function calls and task queuing.
1976 年沃斯（Niklaus Wirth）出版《算法 + 数据结构 = 程序: In 1976, Niklaus Wirth published "Algorithms + Data Structures = Programs"; the book title itself reveals the relationship between the two.
程序员面试最常考的就是这些结构，因为选错一个数据结构，程序就可能慢上千倍。: Programmer interviews most frequently test these structures, because choosing the wrong data structure can slow a program down over a thousand times.
用 O(n)、O(n log n)、O(n²) 描述算法耗时随数据规模增长的速度: Using O(n), O(n log n), O(n²) to describe how algorithm runtime grows with data size, ignoring constants to observe trends.
数据量足够大时，决定速度的是\"增长的形状\"，而不是常数因子：n² 的算法哪怕: When data volume is large enough, what determines speed is the "shape of growth" rather than constant factors: an O(n²) algorithm will eventually be surpassed by an O(n log n) algorithm even on a machine 100 times faster ([[p:exponential|Exponential growth]]).
大 O 记号描述算法步数随输入规模 n 增长的上限，只保留最高阶项、忽略常数。常: Big O notation describes the upper limit of algorithm steps as input size n grows, retaining only the highest-order term and ignoring constants. Common complexities from fastest to slowest are: O(1) constant time (hash table lookup), O(log n) (binary search), O(n) (traversing once), O(n log n) (good sorting algorithms), O(n²) (pairwise comparison), O(2ⁿ) (exhaustively enumerating all subsets).
直观感受：n = 100 万时，n log n 约 2000 万步，电脑不到一秒: Intuitive sense: when n = 1 million, n log n is about 20 million steps, taking less than a second on a computer; n² is 1 trillion steps, taking a long time to compute; 2ⁿ is an astronomical number that exceeds the age of the universe.
它给程序员一种统一的语言来比较算法、预估性能，也是区分\"能解\"和\"实际上解: It gives programmers a unified language to compare algorithms and estimate performance, serving as a tool to distinguish between problems that "can be solved" and those that are "practically unsolvable" (see [[p-vs-np]]).
几种常见复杂度的增长曲线。指数型 2ⁿ 很快冲出图外。: Growth curves of several common complexities. Exponential 2ⁿ shoots out of the graph quickly.
最经典的算法问题：快速排序、归并排序、二分查找让海量数据可以被快速定位。: The most classic algorithmic problems: quick sort, merge sort, and binary search allow massive amounts of data to be located rapidly.
排好序的数据可以用\"每次排除一半\"的方式查找；而基于比较的排序，最快也需要约: Sorted data can be searched using the 'halve-and-exclude' method; whereas sorting based on comparison requires at least approximately n log n comparisons—this is a provable lower bound.
经典排序算法有：**快速排序**（选一个基准，把小的放左边、大的放右边，再分别排: Classic sorting algorithms include: **Quick Sort** (selecting a pivot, placing smaller elements to the left and larger ones to the right, then recursively sorting both sides, proposed by Hoare between 1959–1961); **Merge Sort** (splitting into halves, sorting each half separately, then merging them, proposed by von Neumann in 1945); **Heap Sort**, and others. Once sorted, elements can be found in logarithmic time using binary search.
排序和查找是数据库、搜索引擎和几乎所有软件的基础操作，编程语言的标准库都内置了高: Sorting and searching are fundamental operations for databases, search engines, and virtually all software; standard libraries of programming languages include highly optimized sorting functions.
函数调用自己、把大问题化为同样形式的小问题，是分治算法和树形数据的天然写法。: A function calling itself, breaking a large problem into smaller problems of the same form, is the natural implementation style for divide-and-conquer algorithms and tree data structures.
如果一个大问题能拆成几个形式相同的小问题，那就只需要写清楚\"怎么拆\"和\"最: If a large problem can be split into several small problems of identical form, you only need to clearly define 'how to split' and 'how to solve the smallest problem'; the rest is left for the function to call itself recursively.
计算 5 的阶乘：5! = 5 × 4!，4! = 4 × 3!……直到 1!: Calculating 5 factorial: 5! = 5 × 4!, 4! = 4 × 3! ... until this 'base case' stops at 1! = 1. Each call pushes a layer onto the memory's 'call stack', and pops it upon return. If the base case is forgotten, the function will call itself infinitely until a stack overflow (stack overflow).
递归是处理树形结构（文件夹、网页 DOM、语法树）最自然的方式，也是分治算法的基: Recursion is the most natural way to handle tree structures (folders, web page DOMs, syntax trees) and is also the basic implementation style for divide-and-conquer algorithms. The famous programmer Q&A website Stack Overflow got its name from this error.
把城市、网页、人际关系抽象成点和边，用迪杰斯特拉等算法求最短路线。: Abstract cities, web pages, and interpersonal relationships into nodes and edges, then use algorithms like Dijkstra's to find shortest routes.
把现实中的地点、网页、人和关系抽象成\"点\"和\"边\"，很多看似无关的问题就: Abstract real-world locations, web pages, people, and relationships into 'nodes' and 'edges'; many seemingly unrelated problems become the same mathematical problem.
**广度优先搜索**一层层向外探索，可以找到步数最少的路径；**迪杰斯特拉算法*: **Breadth-First Search** explores outward layer by layer, finding paths with the fewest steps; **Dijkstra's Algorithm** starts from each confirmed node, 'expanding' the node with the currently shortest distance to find shortest paths in weighted graphs; **A* Algorithm** adds an estimate of remaining distance on top of this, making search faster and commonly used in games and navigation. Additionally, there are classic algorithms for finding maximum flow in networks and minimum spanning trees.
荷兰计算机科学家迪杰斯特拉（Edsger Dijkstra）1956 年构思出最: Dutch computer scientist Dijkstra (Edsger Dijkstra) conceived the shortest path algorithm in 1956; according to his recollection, it took only about 20 minutes, published in 1959.
地图导航（见 [[digital-maps]]）、网络路由（见 [[router: Map navigation (see [[digital-maps]]), network routing (see [[router]]), logistics delivery, and social recommendations all rest on graph algorithms.
迪杰斯特拉算法在带权图中找到从 A 到 E 的最短路径（粗线），总长 7。: Dijkstra's Algorithm finds the shortest path from A to E in a weighted graph (thick line), with a total length of 7.
把问题拆成重叠的子问题、记住每个子问题的答案避免重复计算。: Split a problem into overlapping subproblems and remember the answer for each subproblem to avoid redundant calculations.
如果一个问题的很多子问题会被反复计算，那就把每个子问题的答案记下来，以后直接查表: If many subproblems of a given issue will be repeatedly calculated, store the answers for each subproblem so they can be looked up directly later—trading space for time (a close relative of [[p:locality|Locality & caching]]).
经典例子是斐波那契数列：直接递归计算第 50 项要算上百亿次，因为同样的子项被反: A classic example is the Fibonacci sequence: directly computing the 50th term recursively requires trillions of calculations because identical subterms are repeatedly computed; if each calculated item is stored in a table, only 50 calculations are needed. Dynamic programming decomposes problems into mutually overlapping subproblems and fills the table in increasing order.
美国数学家贝尔曼（Richard Bellman）在 1950 年代提出这个方法: American mathematician Bellman (Richard Bellman) proposed this method and its name in the 1950s.
DNA 序列比对、文本差异比较（diff）、语音识别、最短路径和背包问题等都用动: DNA sequence alignment, text difference comparison (diff), speech recognition, shortest path problems, and knapsack problems all use dynamic programming for solutions.
用一行简洁的模式描述一类字符串，用于搜索、校验和文本处理。: Use a concise pattern description in a single line to describe a class of strings, used for searching, validation, and text processing.
许多文本模式（邮箱地址、电话号码、日期）都可以用\"字符 + 重复 + 选择\": Many text patterns (email addresses, phone numbers, dates) can be described using three basic combinations of 'characters + repetition + selection', and such patterns can be efficiently recognized by a minimal machine (finite automaton).
正则表达式用一串特殊符号描述模式，例如 `\\d{3}-\\d{4}` 表示\": Regular expressions describe patterns using a string of special symbols; for example, `\d{3}-\d{4}` represents 'three digits, a hyphen, four digits'. Programs compile these into automata and then rapidly scan for matches within text.
1951 年数学家克莱尼（Stephen Kleene）提出\"正则集合\"的数: In 1951, mathematician Kleene (Stephen Kleene) proposed the mathematical theory of 'regular sets'; in 1968, Thompson introduced it into text editors, later becoming the core of Unix tools like grep.
从代码编辑器的搜索替换到网站表单校验和日志分析，正则表达式是程序员最常用的工具之: From code editor search-and-replace to website form validation and log analysis, regular expressions are one of the most commonly used tools for programmers.
让人用接近自然语言和数学的方式写指令，再翻译成机器能执行的代码。: Enable users to write instructions in a manner close to natural language and mathematics, then translate them into machine-executable code.
人擅长用接近自然语言和数学的方式思考，机器只认识二进制指令；在两者之间建一层可以: People are good at thinking in ways that closely resemble natural language and mathematics; machines only understand binary instructions. By building a layer between the two that can automatically translate, people can direct machines using "human ways" ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]]).
编程语言有严格的语法（怎么写才合法）和语义（写出来是什么意思）。程序员写好源代码: Programming languages have strict syntax (how to write something legally) and semantics (what it means when written out). After programmers write source code, it is either translated into machine code in one pass by [[compiler|Compiler]], or executed line-by-line as it is read by [[interpreter|Interpreter]]. The more "advanced" a language is, the further it is from the machine: one line of Python may correspond to dozens of machine instructions.
不同语言体现不同的思维方式（编程范式）：**命令式**告诉机器\"一步步怎么做\: Different languages reflect different modes of thinking (programming paradigms): **Imperative** tells the machine "step-by-step how to do it"; **Object-oriented** packages data and operations into objects (see [[object-oriented-programming]]); **Functional** views programs as combinations of functions (see [[functional-programming]]); **Declarative** only describes "what is needed," such as SQL (see [[relational-database]]).
1950 年代出现了第一批高级语言（[[fortran|FORTRAN]]、[[: In the 1950s, the first batch of high-level languages appeared ([[fortran|FORTRAN]], [[lisp|Lisp]], [[cobol|COBOL]]); in the 1970s, [[c-language|C (programming language)]] ruled system programming; in the 1990s, [[java|Java & the JVM]], [[python|Python]], and [[javascript|JavaScript]] spread with the popularization of the Internet. To date, thousands of programming languages have emerged.
编程语言让写软件的人从少数专家扩大到数千万开发者；而大语言模型正在让自然语言本身: Programming languages allowed software developers to expand from a few experts to tens of millions; while large language models are now making natural language itself into a kind of "programming language" (see [[ai-coding]]).
没有\"最好\"的语言，只有更适合某类问题的语言：C 适合贴近硬件，Python: There is no "best" language, only languages better suited for certain types of problems: C is suitable for close-to-hardware work, Python for rapid experimentation and data analysis, JavaScript for web development, and Rust for pursuing memory safety while ensuring speed.
抽象的阶梯：一行高级语言代码，层层翻译成 CPU 能执行的二进制指令。: The ladder of abstraction: one line of high-level language code is translated layer by layer into binary instructions that the CPU can execute.
机器码是 CPU 直接执行的二进制指令，汇编给每条指令起了人能读的助记名。: Machine code consists of binary instructions executed directly by the CPU; assembly gives mnemonic names to each instruction that humans can read.
机器码只是一串数字，人很难读写；给每条指令起个英文助记名（如 ADD、MOV、J: Machine code is just a string of numbers, which people find difficult to read and write; giving an English mnemonic name to each instruction (such as ADD, MOV, JMP), and then translating it back into numbers one-to-one by the program, greatly reduces the rate of errors.
汇编语言与 [[instruction-set-architecture|指令集: Assembly language corresponds one-to-one with [[instruction-set-architecture|Instruction set architecture (ISA)]]; programmers directly operate registers and memory addresses. An "assembler" translates it into machine code. It can write the most precise and efficient code, but must be rewritten when switching to a different CPU.
英国数学家凯瑟琳·布斯（Kathleen Booth）1947 年为 ARC 计: British mathematician Kathleen Booth designed an early assembly language for the ARC computer in 1947.
今天大多数程序已不再直接用汇编编写，但操作系统内核、驱动和性能极致优化的代码中仍: Today, most programs are no longer written directly in assembly; however, it still appears in operating system kernels, drivers, and code optimized for extreme performance; understanding assembly is also a prerequisite course for understanding how computers work.
把高级语言程序翻译成机器码的程序，让程序员不用再手写机器指令。: The program that translates high-level language programs into machine code allows programmers to stop writing machine instructions by hand.
翻译本身也是一种可以自动化的计算——写一个程序，把另一种语言写的程序翻译成机器码: Translation itself is a kind of computation that can be automated—write a program to translate a program written in another language into machine code, and people no longer need to write machine instructions by hand ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]]).
编译器像流水线一样分几步：**词法分析**把源代码切成一个个\"单词\"（关键字: Compilers work like an assembly line with several steps: **Lexical analysis** chops source code into individual "words" (keywords, variable names, numbers); **Syntax analysis** organizes them into a syntax tree according to grammar rules; **Semantic analysis** checks whether types and other elements are reasonable; **Optimization** makes programs faster and smaller without changing results (such as moving invariant calculations outside loops); **Code generation** outputs instructions for the target machine. Modern compiler frameworks (such as LLVM) separate the frontend (understanding language) from the backend (generating machine code), allowing any language's frontend to reuse the same backend.
1952 年格蕾丝·霍珀（Grace Hopper）为 UNIVAC 开发了 A: In 1952, Grace Hopper developed A-0 for UNIVAC, often called the first compiler; at that time, many people did not believe machines could "write programs." In 1957, John Backus's IBM team released the first [[fortran|FORTRAN]] compiler; the code it generated was nearly as efficient as hand-written assembly, convincing the industry to accept high-level languages.
编译器让同一份源代码能在不同 CPU 上运行，也让程序员的生产力提高了几个数量级: Compilers allow the same source code to run on different CPUs and increase programmer productivity by several orders of magnitude. Compiler theory is one of the core courses in computer science.
编译器的典型阶段：从源代码到机器码，每一步都把程序变成更接近机器的形式。: Typical stages of a compiler: from source code to machine code, each step transforms the program into a form closer to the machine.
边读源代码边执行，不需要先整体编译，方便交互和调试，Python 和 JavaS: Execute line-by-line while reading source code without needing to compile the whole thing first; this facilitates interaction and debugging; Python and JavaScript both rely on it.
不必先把整个程序翻译完，可以读一句执行一句——启动更快、调试更方便，代价是运行时: You do not need to translate the entire program before running; you can read one sentence and execute one sentence—starting faster, easier debugging; the cost is increased translation overhead at runtime.
解释器逐条读取源代码（或先编译成中间形式的\"字节码\"），然后直接执行。Pyt: Interpreters read source code line-by-line (or first compile into an intermediate form called "bytecode"), then execute directly. Python, JavaScript, and Ruby run primarily in this way. To compensate for speed, modern interpreters often include "Just-In-Time compilation" (JIT): when a segment of code is found to be executed repeatedly, it compiles that segment into machine code.
解释型语言让\"写一行、马上看结果\"的交互式编程成为可能，大大降低了编程门槛（: Interpreted languages make interactive programming—"write one line, see results immediately"—possible, greatly lowering the threshold for programming (see [[basic-language]], [[python]]).
第一种被广泛使用的高级语言，为科学计算而生，至今仍在超算上运行。: The first high-level language widely used was born for scientific computing; it still runs on supercomputers today.
科学家需要的是\"把公式写进计算机\"；只要编译出的程序足够快，他们就愿意放弃汇: Scientists need to "write formulas into computers"; as long as the compiled program is fast enough, they are willing to give up assembly.
FORTRAN（意为\"公式翻译\"）让人能用接近数学的写法表达计算，如 `Y: FORTRAN (meaning 'Formula Translation') allows users to express calculations in a style close to mathematics, such as `Y = A*X + B`, and generates efficient machine code via compilers. It excels particularly with arrays and numerical computations.
1957 年由 IBM 的约翰·巴克斯团队发布，巴克斯因此获 1977 年图灵奖: Released in 1957 by John Backus's team at IBM, Backus received the Turing Award in 1977 for this achievement.
FORTRAN 证明了高级语言的可行性。至今许多气象、物理和工程模拟代码仍用现代: FORTRAN demonstrated the feasibility of high-level languages. To this day, many weather, physics, and engineering simulation codes are still written in modern versions of Fortran.
以表处理和递归为核心的语言，首创了垃圾回收，曾是早期 AI 研究的主力。: A language centered on table processing and recursion, it pioneered garbage collection and was once a primary force in early artificial intelligence research.
如果程序和数据用同一种结构（列表）表示，程序就能像处理数据一样生成和修改程序。: If programs and data are represented using the same structure (lists), programs can generate and modify themselves just like they process data.
Lisp 的一切都写成括号包裹的列表，如 `(+ 1 2)`。它大量使用 [[r: Everything in Lisp is written as bracket-wrapped lists, such as `(+ 1 2)`. It makes extensive use of [[recursion|Recursion]] and pioneered automatic [[garbage-collection|Garbage collection]], conditional expressions, and many other features later widely adopted.
1958 年约翰·麦卡锡（John McCarthy）在麻省理工学院设计，他也是: Designed in 1958 by John McCarthy at MIT; he was also the coiner of the term 'artificial intelligence'.
Lisp 是早期 AI 研究的主力语言，它的思想深刻影响了后来的函数式语言和 J: Lisp was a primary language for early AI research. Its ideas profoundly influenced subsequent functional languages and modern languages like JavaScript and Python.
面向商业数据处理、语法接近英语的语言，银行和政府系统里至今还有大量 COBOL: A language oriented toward commercial data processing with syntax close to English, COBOL still contains vast amounts of code in banking and government systems.
商业数据处理的用户是会计和管理人员，语言如果写得像英语句子，就更容易被非专业人员: The users of commercial data processing are accountants and managers; if the language is written like an English sentence, it becomes easier for non-professionals to understand and audit.
COBOL 程序读起来像英文，如 `ADD SALES TO TOTAL`。它擅: COBOL programs read like English, such as `ADD SALES TO TOTAL`. It excels at handling records, files, and decimal amount calculations, making it ideal for payroll, billing, and accounting processing.
1959 年由美国国防部召集的委员会设计，格蕾丝·霍珀的早期工作对它影响很大。: Designed by a committee convened by the US Department of Defense in 1959; Grace Hopper's early work had a significant impact on it.
据估计至今仍有数千亿行 COBOL 代码运行在银行、保险和政府的大型机上；会写: It is estimated that hundreds of billions of lines of COBOL code are still running in banks, insurance companies, and government mainframes; the number of programmers who can write COBOL is dwindling, making the maintenance of these systems a real challenge (see [[y2k]]).
为初学者设计的语言，随早期个人电脑普及，让一代人学会编程。: A language designed for beginners, it became popular with the early spread of personal computers, teaching a generation to program.
让学生在终端上马上看到结果，编程就从专家技能变成人人可学的技能。: Allowing students to see results immediately on terminals transformed programming from an expert skill into a skill anyone can learn.
BASIC 语法简单，每行有行号，可以用解释器直接交互运行，输入 `PRINT: BASIC syntax is simple; each line has a line number, and it can be interactively run directly via an interpreter. Inputting `PRINT 2+2` immediately outputs 4.
1964 年美国达特茅斯学院的凯梅尼（John Kemeny）和库尔茨（Thom: Designed in 1964 by John Kemeny and Thomas Kurtz at Dartmouth College for non-science students. In 1975, Microsoft's first product was the BASIC interpreter on the Altair 8800; thereafter, almost every home computer came with BASIC built-in.
BASIC 让一整代人在家用电脑上学会了编程，其中许多人后来成为软件产业的骨干。: BASIC enabled an entire generation to learn programming on home computers, many of whom later became pillars of the software industry.
贝尔实验室为重写 Unix 设计的语言，贴近硬件又可移植，是操作系统和嵌入式的基: A language designed by Bell Labs for rewriting Unix, it is close to hardware yet portable, serving as a cornerstone for operating systems and embedded development.
一门语言如果足够接近硬件（能直接操作内存地址），又不绑定某一种 CPU，就既能写: If a language is sufficiently close to hardware (able to directly manipulate memory addresses) without being tied to a specific CPU type, it can write efficient system software while remaining portable across different machines.
C 语言提供指针（直接表示内存地址）、结构体和简洁的控制语句，编译后的程序几乎和: C provides pointers (directly representing memory addresses), structures, and concise control statements; compiled programs are nearly as fast as hand-written assembly. The cost is that programmers must manage memory themselves, leading to issues like out-of-bounds access if not careful—this is also a source of many security vulnerabilities (see [[vulnerability]]).
Linux、Windows 和 macOS 的内核、数据库、嵌入式设备和大量编程: The kernels of Linux, Windows, and macOS, databases, embedded devices, and implementations of numerous programming languages are all written in C or its successor C++. C's syntax also influenced many languages including Java, JavaScript, and C#.
用顺序、分支、循环三种结构代替随意跳转（goto），让程序可读、可证明。: Replacing arbitrary jumps (goto) with three structures—sequence, branching, and loops—makes programs more readable and provable.
任何程序都可以只用三种结构写出来——顺序、分支（if）、循环（while）；去掉: Any program can be written using only three structures: sequence, branching (if), and looping (while). By removing arbitrary jumps, programs become readable from top to bottom like an article, making it easier to prove their correctness.
早期程序大量使用 goto 语句随意跳转，代码像一团乱麻（\"意大利面条代码\": Early programs extensively used goto statements for arbitrary jumps, resulting in code that resembled a tangled mess ("spaghetti code"). Structured programming requires each section of code to have only one entry and one exit, using functions to break large programs into small modules.
1966 年意大利学者伯姆和雅科皮尼证明了三种结构就足够；1968 年迪杰斯特拉: In 1966, Italian scholars Böhm and Jacopini proved that three structures are sufficient; in 1968, Dijkstra published the famous short paper "Goto Statement Considered Harmful," sparking widespread discussion.
几乎所有现代编程语言都以结构化编程为基础，它也是软件工程的起点之一（见 [[so: Almost all modern programming languages are based on structured programming, which is also one of the starting points of software engineering (see [[software-engineering]]).
把数据和操作它的代码打包成\"对象\"，用类、继承、封装组织大型程序。: Packaging data and the code that operates on it into an "object" organizes large programs using classes, inheritance, and encapsulation.
现实世界由一个个\"东西\"组成，每个东西有自己的状态和行为；把数据和操作它的代: The real world consists of individual "things," each with its own state and behavior; packaging data and the code that operates on it into an "object" allows large programs to be organized like building blocks ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]]).
面向对象有三个核心概念：**封装**（对象内部的数据只能通过它提供的方法访问）、: Object-oriented programming has three core concepts: **encapsulation** (data inside an object can only be accessed through methods provided by it), **inheritance** (a "cat" class can inherit attributes and methods from an "animal" class), and **polymorphism** (different objects can have different reactions to the same "speak" instruction). A "class" is a blueprint, while an "object" is an instance created according to that blueprint.
1967 年挪威的达尔（Ole-Johan Dahl）和尼加德（Kristen: In 1967, Dahl (Ole-Johan Dahl) and Nygaard (Kristen Nygaard) of Norway designed Simula 67, which first introduced classes and objects; in the 1970s, Alan Kay at Xerox PARC's Smalltalk expanded this idea. C++ and Java from the 1980–1990s made it mainstream.
面向对象是 1990 年代以来大型软件开发的主流方式，图形界面中的窗口、按钮天然: Object-oriented programming has been the mainstream way for large-scale software development since the 1990s; windows and buttons in graphical interfaces are naturally objects. Later, people realized that overusing inheritance can make code rigid, and "composition is preferred over inheritance" became a new consensus.
把程序看成数学函数的组合，避免可变状态，更易推理和并行。: Viewing programs as combinations of mathematical functions avoids mutable state, making reasoning and parallel execution easier.
如果函数像数学函数一样——相同的输入永远得到相同的输出、不偷偷修改外部状态——程: If functions behave like mathematical functions—producing the same output from the same input and not secretly modifying external state—the program becomes easier to reason about, test, and execute in parallel.
函数式编程尽量使用不可变的数据，把函数当作可以传递和组合的\"值\"，用 map: Functional programming strives to use immutable data, treating functions as "values" that can be passed and combined, replacing loops with operations like map, filter, and reduce. Haskell, Erlang, and Clojure are representative languages; JavaScript, Python, and Java have also absorbed a large amount of functional features.
它的数学基础是 1930 年代丘奇提出的 λ 演算；[[lisp|Lisp]]: Its mathematical foundation is the λ-calculus proposed by Church in the 1930s; [[lisp|Lisp]] is the first language with a functional style.
多核时代，\"不共享可变状态\"大大降低了并发编程出错的风险（见 [[concu: In the multi-core era, "not sharing mutable state" greatly reduces the risk of errors in concurrent programming (see [[concurrency]]), and distributed data processing frameworks (see [[big-data]]) have also borrowed the map/reduce idea.
给数据贴上\"整数\"\"字符串\"等标签，让编译器在运行前就抓出一大类错误。: Labeling data with tags like "integer" or "string" allows the compiler to catch a large category of errors before runtime.
给每个值标上\"类型\"，编译器就能在程序运行前自动检查出一大类错误，比如把文字: By labeling each value with a "type," the compiler can automatically check a large category of errors before program execution, such as adding text to numbers.
**静态类型**语言（如 Java、Rust、TypeScript）在编译时检查: **Static type** languages (such as Java, Rust, TypeScript) check types at compile time, discovering errors early; **dynamic type** languages (such as Python, JavaScript) check types at runtime, offering more flexibility. Modern languages often use "type inference" to automatically deduce types, balancing safety and conciseness.
大型项目越来越倾向于使用类型：微软推出的 TypeScript 给 JavaSc: Large projects increasingly tend to use types: Microsoft's TypeScript added types to JavaScript and quickly became popular; Python also added type annotations.
运行时自动找出不再使用的内存并回收，程序员不再需要手动释放。: The garbage collector automatically finds and reclaims memory that is no longer in use at runtime, so programmers do not need to manually release it.
程序是否还\"需要\"一块内存，可以通过能否从程序的变量出发找到它来判断；找不到: Whether a program "needs" a piece of memory can be determined by whether it can be traced back from the program's variables; memory that cannot be found is garbage and can be automatically reclaimed.
垃圾回收器定期从\"根\"（全局变量、调用栈上的变量）出发，标记所有能访问到的对: The garbage collector periodically starts from "roots" (global variables, variables on the call stack), marks all accessible objects, and releases those not marked. This allows programmers to avoid manually releasing memory, preventing serious errors like memory leaks and using memory after release, at the cost of occasional pauses and extra overhead.
约 1959 年由约翰·麦卡锡为 [[lisp|Lisp]] 发明。: Around 1959, John McCarthy invented it for [[lisp|Lisp]].
Java、Python、JavaScript、Go 等主流语言都采用垃圾回收。追: Mainstream languages such as Java, Python, JavaScript, and Go adopt garbage collection. Rust, which pursues extreme performance, takes a different path, using compile-time "ownership" rules to guarantee memory safety without garbage collection.
语法简洁、库极其丰富的语言，成为数据科学和 AI 的通用语。: Languages with concise syntax and extremely rich libraries have become the general language for data science and AI.
程序员的时间比机器的时间更贵；一门读起来像伪代码、拥有海量现成库的语言，能让人最: The time of a programmer is more expensive than the time of a machine; a language that reads like pseudocode and possesses a vast number of ready-made libraries allows people to turn ideas into runnable programs most quickly.
Python 用缩进表示代码块，语法简洁；它通过 [[interpreter|解: Python uses indentation to represent code blocks, has concise syntax; it runs via [[interpreter|Interpreter]], speed is not fast, but computation-intensive parts can call libraries written in C (such as NumPy), balancing ease of use and performance.
荷兰程序员吉多·范罗苏姆（Guido van Rossum）在 1989 年底开: Dutch programmer Guido van Rossum began development at the end of 1989, and publicly released it in February 1991.
凭借 NumPy、pandas、PyTorch 等库，Python 成为数据科学: Relying on libraries such as NumPy, pandas, PyTorch, etc., Python has become the general language for data science and artificial intelligence, and also one of the most popular programming languages for beginners.
编译成字节码在虚拟机上运行，\"一次编写、到处运行\"，统治了企业后端和安卓。: Compiled into bytecode to run on a virtual machine, "write once, run anywhere", ruled enterprise backend and Android.
先把程序编译成一种与具体 CPU 无关的中间代码（字节码），再在各平台上的\"虚: First compile the program into an intermediate code unrelated to specific CPUs (bytecode), then run it in the "virtual machine" on each platform; the same program can achieve "write once, run anywhere".
Java 虚拟机（JVM）负责解释或即时编译字节码，并提供 [[garbage-: The Java Virtual Machine (JVM) is responsible for interpreting or just-in-time compiling bytecode and providing [[garbage-collection|Garbage collection]] and security checks. Java syntax borrows from C++, but removed features like pointer operations that are prone to errors.
由太阳计算机系统公司的詹姆斯·高斯林（James Gosling）团队开发，19: Developed by the team of James Gosling from Sun Microsystems Company, released in 1995. In 2010, Sun was acquired by Oracle.
Java 统治了企业后端系统多年，也是 [[android|安卓]] 应用开发最: Java ruled enterprise backend systems for many years, and was also [[android|Android]]'s primary language for application development initially; later Kotlin became the official preferred language for Android.
10 天内设计出来的网页脚本语言，后来成为浏览器和全栈开发的唯一通用语言。: A web scripting language designed in 10 days, later becoming the only general language for browsers and full-stack development.
网页需要一种能直接在浏览器里运行、处理点击和动画的语言；只要所有浏览器都支持它，: Web pages need a language that can run directly in the browser, handle clicks and animations; as long as all browsers support it, it automatically possesses the largest user base ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
JavaScript 由浏览器内置的引擎执行，可以修改网页内容、响应用户操作、在: JavaScript is executed by engines built into browsers, allowing modification of web page content, response to user operations, and background data requests. Node.js that appeared in 2009 allowed it to also run on servers; just-in-time compilation by engines like Google V8 increased its speed by several tens of times.
1995 年网景公司的布兰登·艾克（Brendan Eich）用约 10 天设计: In 1995, Brendan Eich from Netscape Company designed the first version in about 10 days. It has almost no relation to Java except for the name; the name was a marketing decision at that time.
JavaScript 是唯一能在所有浏览器中原生运行的语言，构成了现代网页应用的: JavaScript is the only language that can natively run in all browsers, forming the foundation of modern web applications, and also one of the programming languages with the most users.
用\"有效数字 × 2 的幂\"表示小数，IEEE 754 标准让所有电脑算出相: Represent decimals using "significant digits × power of 2", IEEE 754 standard allows all computers to calculate the same result.
用\"有效数字 × 2 的若干次方\"表示小数（类似科学记数法），有限的比特就能: Represent decimals using "significant digits × power of 2" (similar to scientific notation); a finite number of bits can simultaneously represent extremely large and extremely small numbers, at the cost of being able to approximate only.
一个 32 位单精度浮点数分成三部分：1 位符号、8 位指数、23 位尾数。因为: A 32-bit single-precision floating-point number is divided into three parts: 1 bit for sign, 8 bits for exponent, 23 bits for mantissa. Because it uses binary representation, decimal 0.1 cannot be represented precisely; therefore in many languages 0.1 + 0.2 does not completely equal 0.3. Calculations involving money thus commonly use integers (in "cents") or decimal types. AI training then makes extensive use of low-precision floating-point numbers such as 16-bit, even 8-bit, and 4-bit, to gain speed and save memory.
1985 年发布的 IEEE 754 标准统一了浮点数格式，主要设计者威廉·卡亨: The IEEE 754 standard released in 1985 unified floating-point formats; main designer William Kahan therefore received the Turing Award in 1989.
统一标准之前，同一个程序在不同计算机上可能算出不同结果；IEEE 754 让科学: Before unifying standards, the same program might calculate different results on different computers; IEEE 754 made scientific calculations reproducible and portable.
管理硬件、调度程序、提供文件和网络服务的\"大管家\"，让应用不必直接和硬件打交: The "big manager" that manages hardware, schedules programs, and provides file and network services, allowing applications not to deal directly with hardware.
多个程序要共享同一套 CPU、内存和设备；如果让一个\"大管家\"统一分配资源、: Multiple programs need to share the same set of CPUs, memory, and devices; if a "big manager" uniformly allocates resources and hides hardware details behind simple interfaces, each program can pretend to monopolize the entire machine ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]]).
操作系统的核心叫**内核**，它主要干四件事：: The core of an operating system is called **kernel**, and it mainly does four things:
**管 CPU**：在多个 [[process-thread|进程]] 之间快速: **Manages CPU**: rapidly switches between multiple [[process-thread|Process & thread]] (hundreds over a thousand times per second), making them appear to run simultaneously;
**管内存**：用 [[virtual-memory|虚拟内存]] 给每个程序一: **Manages memory**: uses [[virtual-memory|Virtual memory]] to give each program an independent address space, mutually not interfering;
**管存储**：用 [[file-system|文件系统]] 把磁盘上的一堆数据: **File system**: Organizes a pile of data blocks on the disk into files and folders using [[file-system|File system]];
**管设备**：通过 [[device-driver|驱动程序]] 统一操作键盘: **Device driver**: Unifies operations on hardware such as keyboards, network cards, and graphics cards through [[device-driver|Device driver]].
应用程序不能直接碰硬件，必须通过\"系统调用\"请内核代办——这道边界既是安全屏: Applications cannot directly access hardware; they must request the kernel to handle it via "system calls". This boundary serves both as a security barrier and a guarantee of compatibility: as long as the interface remains unchanged, applications will continue to run even when the hardware is replaced.
1950 年代的计算机一次只运行一个作业，由人工排队；1960 年代出现了批处理: In the 1950s, computers could only run one job at a time, managed by manual queuing; in the 1960s, batch processing and [[time-sharing|Time-sharing]] emerged, with IBM developing OS/360 for System/360. In 1969, the [[unix|Unix]] team at Bell Labs established the basic form of modern operating systems. Since then, MS-DOS, [[windows|Microsoft Windows]], [[apple-os|macOS & iOS]], [[linux|Linux]], and [[android|Android]] have appeared.
操作系统是软件生态的地基：谁控制了操作系统，谁就控制了应用分发的入口（见 [[a: Operating systems are the foundation of software ecosystems: whoever controls the operating system controls the entry point for application distribution (see [[app-store]]). This is also one reason why Microsoft, Apple, and Google have long dominated the technology industry.
操作系统的分层：应用通过系统调用请求内核，内核再通过驱动程序操作硬件。: The layered architecture of an operating system: applications request the kernel via system calls, and the kernel then operates hardware through drivers.
让 CPU 在多个用户之间飞快轮转，每人都觉得自己独占一台计算机。: Allow the CPU to rapidly switch between multiple users, making each feel as though they are exclusively using a single computer.
人敲键盘、思考的速度比计算机慢上百万倍；让计算机在许多用户之间轮流快速切换，每个: Human typing speed and thinking speed are millions of times slower than computers; by allowing computers to rapidly switch among many users, each person feels as though they have exclusive control over the entire machine.
系统把 CPU 时间切成很小的\"时间片\"，轮流分给各个终端用户的程序。一个程: The system slices CPU time into very small "time slices" and distributes them in rotation to programs from various terminal users. When a program is waiting for user input, the CPU goes to serve others.
1961 年麻省理工学院的科尔巴托（Fernando Corbató）团队演示了: In 1961, Fernando Corbató's team at MIT demonstrated the compatible time-sharing system CTSS; Corbató received the Turing Award in 1990.
分时让计算从\"排队交卡片、隔天取结果\"变成\"即时交互\"，催生了电子邮件、: Time-sharing transformed computing from "queueing cards and retrieving results the next day" to "instant interaction," giving birth to email, multi-user systems, and [[unix|Unix]]. It is also the ancestor of today's [[cloud-computing|Cloud computing]] shared resource concepts.
贝尔实验室开发的操作系统，\"一切皆文件、小工具组合\"的思想影响了此后几乎所有: The operating system developed by Bell Labs, with the idea that "everything is a file and small tools are combined," influenced almost all subsequent systems.
每个程序只做好一件事，程序之间用统一的文本流连接；简单的小工具组合起来，就能完成: Each program does only one thing; programs connect via unified text streams. Simple small tools can combine to complete complex tasks ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]], [[p:standard|Standardization]]).
Unix 引入了许多今天仍在使用的思想：层级式的文件系统、\"一切皆文件\"（设: Unix introduced many ideas still in use today: hierarchical file systems, "everything is a file" (devices are also read and written as files), using "pipes" (|) to connect the output of one program to the input of another, and command-line shells. In 1973, it was rewritten using [[c-language|C (programming language)]], making it easier to port to different computers.
1969 年贝尔实验室的肯·汤普森（Ken Thompson）和丹尼斯·里奇开始: Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchich began development at Bell Labs in 1969; both received the Turing Award in 1983. The BSD version developed by the University of California, Berkeley, played an important role in its dissemination.
今天的 [[linux|Linux]]、macOS、iOS 和 [[androi: Today's [[linux|Linux]], macOS, iOS, and [[android|Android]] are descendants of Unix or deeply influenced by it; from mobile phones to supercomputers, class Unix systems are ubiquitous.
进程是运行中的程序及其独立资源，线程是进程内可并行的执行流。: A process is a running program along with its independent resources; a thread is an executable stream within a process that can run in parallel.
把\"一个正在运行的程序\"包装成操作系统可以暂停、恢复和隔离的单位，多个任务就: Wrap "a program currently running" into a unit that the operating system can pause, resume, and isolate; multiple tasks can then safely share a single computer.
**进程**是程序的一次运行，拥有自己独立的内存空间，一个进程崩溃一般不影响其他: **Process** is one execution of a program, possessing its own independent memory space; typically, one process crash does not affect other processes. **Thread** is an execution stream within a process; multiple threads in the same process share memory, making switching and communication faster but also more prone to mutual interference. The operating system's "scheduler" decides which thread gets CPU usage next; during switching, registers and other "context" must be saved and restored.
举例：浏览器常常把每个标签页放在独立的进程里，这样一个网页崩溃不会拖垮整个浏览器: For example: browsers often place each tab in an independent process; thus, if one webpage crashes, it does not bring down the entire browser.
进程与线程是多任务操作系统和 [[multicore|多核]] 编程的基本单位，: Processes and threads are the basic units of multi-task operating systems and [[multicore|Multicore & parallelism]] programming; understanding them is a prerequisite for writing efficient concurrent programs (see [[concurrency]]).
给每个程序一个独立的\"假\"地址空间，由系统映射到真实内存或硬盘，既隔离又能用: Give each program an independent "fake" address space, mapped by the system to real memory or hard disk; this provides both isolation and greater utility.
在程序和物理内存之间加一层地址翻译，每个程序就都能拥有一大片\"看起来连续、独占: Add a layer of address translation between programs and physical memory; then each program can possess a large area of memory that "appears continuous and exclusive," while real data can be scattered across various parts of memory or even temporarily stored on the disk ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]]).
内存被分成固定大小的\"页\"（常见 4 KB）。CPU 中的内存管理单元（MM: Memory is divided into fixed-size "pages" (commonly 4 KB). The Memory Management Unit (MMU) in the CPU translates virtual addresses used by programs into physical addresses according to "page tables." If the accessed page is not in memory, a "page fault" is triggered; the operating system loads it from disk. Page tables of different processes do not intercommunicate, so one program cannot peek into another program's memory.
1962 年英国曼彻斯特大学的 Atlas 计算机首次实现了虚拟内存。: In 1962, the Atlas computer at the University of Manchester in the United Kingdom was the first to implement virtual memory.
虚拟内存让程序员不必关心物理内存有多大、放在哪里，也是进程隔离和系统安全的基础。: Virtual memory allows programmers not to worry about how much physical memory is available or where it is located; it also forms the foundation for process isolation and system security.
两个进程的虚拟页通过各自的页表，映射到物理内存中不同的位置，部分页暂存在磁盘上。: The virtual pages of two processes are mapped to different locations in physical memory through their respective page tables, with some pages temporarily stored on disk.
把硬盘上的一堆字节组织成目录和文件，并记录它们存在哪里。: Organize a heap of bytes on the hard drive into directories and files, and record where they exist.
磁盘只认识编号的数据块；给它加上\"名字、文件夹和目录表\"，人和程序就能用路径: Disks only recognize numbered data blocks; by adding "names, folders, and directory tables" to them, people and programs can locate data using paths.
文件系统记录每个文件的名字、大小、权限，以及它的数据存放在哪些块里。常见的有 W: The file system records the name, size, permissions of each file, and which blocks store its data. Common examples include Windows' NTFS, Linux' ext4, and Apple's APFS. Modern file systems use "logging" or "copy-on-write" technology to maintain data consistency even in case of sudden power loss.
\"文件\"和\"文件夹\"成为人们管理数字信息最普遍的心智模型。: "Files" and "folders" have become the most common mental model for people managing digital information.
操作系统和具体硬件之间的\"翻译官\"，让同一系统能使用成千上万种设备。: The "translator" between the operating system and specific hardware allows the same system to use tens of thousands of different devices.
硬件千差万别，但操作系统只想用统一的方式和它们打交道；为每种硬件写一个\"翻译官: Hardware varies greatly, but the operating system only wants to interact with them in a unified way; by writing a "translator" for each type of hardware, differences can be blocked outside the kernel ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]]).
驱动程序一面实现操作系统规定的标准接口（如\"读一个数据块\"\"发送一个网络包: Drivers implement standard interfaces specified by the operating system (such as "read one data block" or "send one network packet") while also operating on registers and interrupts according to specific hardware specifications. Manufacturers only need to write drivers well, and new hardware can be connected to existing systems.
驱动让\"即插即用\"成为可能；但它通常运行在内核中，一个有缺陷的驱动也能让整个: Drivers make "plug and play" possible; however, they usually run in the kernel, so a defective driver can cause the entire system to crash—which is precisely the reason for many "blue screens".
多个任务同时访问同一数据时会互相踩踏，用锁、事务等机制保证结果正确。: When multiple tasks access the same data simultaneously, they may step on each other's toes; mechanisms such as locks and transactions are used to ensure correct results.
多个任务同时读写同一份数据时，结果可能取决于谁先谁后；必须用规则保证关键操作\": When multiple tasks read and write the same data simultaneously, the result may depend on who acts first or second; rules must be used to guarantee that critical operations are "indivisible," otherwise errors that are difficult to reproduce may occur.
