经典例子：两个线程同时给同一个计数器加 1，各自读到 5、各自写回 6，结果少加: A classic example: two threads simultaneously add 1 to the same counter; each reads 5 and writes back 6, resulting in one addition being missed—this is called a "race condition." Solutions include **locks** (allowing only one thread to enter critical code at a time), atomic operations, and message passing. However, improper use of locks can also lead to **deadlock**: two threads each hold a lock and wait for the other to release it first, resulting in an eternal stalemate.
迪杰斯特拉 1965 年前后提出了信号量（semaphore）和\"哲学家就餐问: Dijkstra proposed semaphores around 1965 and the "dining philosophers problem"; these laid the foundation for concurrent programming theory.
随着 [[multicore|多核]] 处理器和 [[distributed-s: With the widespread adoption of [[multicore|multiple cores]] processors and [[distributed-system|Distributed system]] systems, concurrent programming has become an unavoidable challenge for every programmer. New languages like Go and Rust have made safer concurrency a key selling point.
写在芯片里、开机最先运行的底层程序，负责唤醒硬件并加载操作系统。: The low-level program written into the chip that runs first upon booting is responsible for waking up hardware and loading the operating system.
硬件启动的第一刻，硬盘上的操作系统还读不出来；需要一段固化在芯片里的小程序先把硬: At the very moment hardware starts, the operating system on the hard drive cannot yet be read; a small program solidified in the chip must first wake up the hardware and then hand over control to the operating system.
个人电脑开机时，主板上的固件（早期叫 BIOS，现在多为 UEFI）先自检硬件，: When a personal computer turns on, the firmware on the motherboard (formerly called BIOS, now mostly UEFI) performs a hardware self-check, finds the boot disk, and loads the operating system. Firmware also exists in hard drives, keyboards, routers, automotive electronics, etc. Firmware can be upgraded through "flashing".
BIOS 一词由加里·基尔代尔（Gary Kildall）1975 年在 CP/: The term BIOS was coined by Gary Kildall in 1975 within the CP/M operating system; it became a standard with the IBM PC released in 1981.
固件是硬件和软件之间的桥梁；因为它在操作系统之前运行，固件漏洞也是最难清除的一类: Firmware acts as a bridge between hardware and software; because it runs before the operating system, firmware vulnerabilities represent one of the most difficult-to-eliminate classes of security threats.
微软的图形化操作系统，1990 年代起统治个人电脑。: Microsoft's graphical operating system began ruling personal computers starting in the 1990s.
在一套已经普及的平台上逐步升级，同时尽力保持旧程序能继续运行，用户和开发者就会被: Gradually upgrading on an already established platform while striving to keep old programs running ensures that users and developers are firmly retained within this ecosystem ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
Windows 起初是运行在 MS-DOS 之上的图形外壳，1995 年的 Wi: Windows initially served as a graphical shell running on top of MS-DOS; Windows 95 released in 1995 brought the "Start" menu and taskbar; Windows XP released in 2001 switched to a more stable NT kernel. Microsoft licensed the system to numerous computer manufacturers for pre-installation rather than manufacturing computers itself.
Windows 在个人电脑上长期占据大部分份额，让数以亿计的人第一次用上图形界面: Windows has long held the majority market share on personal computers, enabling hundreds of millions of people to experience their first graphical user interface ([[gui]]).
林纳斯·托瓦兹发起的开源操作系统内核，运行着绝大多数服务器、超算和安卓手机。: The open-source operating system kernel initiated by Linus Torvalds runs the vast majority of servers, supercomputers, and Android smartphones.
如果源代码向所有人开放，全世界的开发者都可以修改、改进并贡献回来，一个人发起的小: If source code is made available to everyone, developers worldwide can modify, improve, and contribute back; a small project started by one person can grow into one of the most important operating systems ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
严格说 Linux 只是一个内核，加上 [[gnu|GNU]] 工具、桌面环境和: Strictly speaking, Linux is just a kernel; combined with [[gnu|GNU & the free software movement]] tools, desktop environments, and software packages, it forms "distributions" such as Ubuntu, Debian, and Red Hat. It adopts the GPL license: anyone can use and modify it, but when distributing modified versions, the source code must also be made public.
1991 年芬兰赫尔辛基大学学生林纳斯·托瓦兹（Linus Torvalds）在: In 1991, Linus Torvalds, a student at the University of Helsinki in Finland, posted on a newsgroup announcing the development of an operating system "just for fun." In 2005, he also developed Git to manage Linux code (see [[version-control]]).
如今绝大多数服务器、全部 TOP500 超级计算机（见 [[supercompu: Today, the vast majority of servers, all TOP500 supercomputers ([[supercomputer]]), and [[android|Android]] smartphones run the Linux kernel; it is the most successful example of the [[open-source|open source]] movement.
苹果基于 Unix 血统的操作系统家族，iOS 定义了现代智能手机的交互方式。: Apple's operating system family based on Unix heritage has iOS defined the interaction methods for modern smartphones.
自己同时设计硬件和软件，就能把整体体验打磨得更一致，并让软件充分利用定制芯片。: Designing both hardware and software yourself allows you to refine the overall experience more consistently and enable software to fully utilize custom chips.
2001 年发布的 Mac OS X 以 Unix 风格的 Darwin 为内核: Mac OS X, released in 2001, used Darwin with a Unix-style kernel to replace the classic Mac OS. In 2007, iOS on the iPhone was based on the same kernel; it later branched off into iPadOS, watchOS, and others. Starting in 2020, Apple shifted Macs from Intel chips to self-developed [[arm-architecture|ARM architecture]] chips.
1984 年 Macintosh 带来了首个大众化的图形界面电脑；1997 年乔: The Macintosh brought the first mass-market graphical interface computer in 1984; in 1997, Jobs returned to Apple with the NeXTSTEP system, which became the foundation of Mac OS X.
iOS 与 [[app-store]] 一起定义了移动应用的生态和商业模式。: iOS and [[app-store]] together defined the ecosystem and business model for mobile applications.
基于 Linux 的开源移动操作系统，全球装机量最大的操作系统。: An open-source mobile operating system based on Linux; it is the globally installed operating system with the largest number of devices.
把手机操作系统免费开放给所有厂商使用，再靠应用商店和服务赚钱，就能以最快的速度占: Making the mobile operating system free for all manufacturers to use, then earning money through app stores and services, allows you to occupy the most devices at the fastest speed ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
安卓基于 [[linux|Linux]] 内核，应用最初主要用 [[java|J: Android is based on the [[linux|Linux]] kernel; applications were originally primarily written in [[java|Java & the JVM]], but Kotlin is now the official preferred language. Mobile manufacturers can freely customize interfaces; Google generates revenue through licensing services like Google Play.
安卓公司 2003 年创立，2005 年被谷歌收购；2008 年第一款安卓手机: The Android company was founded in 2003 and acquired by Google in 2005; the first Android phone, HTC Dream (T-Mobile G1), launched in 2008.
安卓是全球装机量最大的操作系统，让价格低廉的智能手机普及到数十亿人手中（见 [[: Android is the globally installed operating system with the largest number of devices, bringing affordable smartphones to billions of people ([[smartphone]]).
在一台物理机上模拟出多台虚拟机，各自运行独立的操作系统，是云计算的地基。: Simulating multiple virtual machines on a single physical machine, each running an independent operating system, forms the foundation of cloud computing.
用软件模拟出一整台\"虚拟的计算机\"，一台物理服务器就能同时安全地运行很多个相: Using software to simulate an entire "virtual computer" allows a single physical server to safely run many mutually isolated systems simultaneously, greatly improving hardware utilization ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]]).
一层叫\"虚拟机监视器\"（hypervisor）的软件位于硬件和操作系统之间，: A layer called "virtual machine monitor" (hypervisor) sits between hardware and the operating system, assigning virtual CPUs, memory, disks, and network cards to each virtual machine. A complete, different operating system can run inside each virtual machine. Modern CPUs include built-in hardware virtualization support, making performance loss very small.
1972 年 IBM 的 VM/370 让大型机可以同时运行多个虚拟机；1999: IBM's VM/370 in 1972 allowed mainframes to run multiple virtual machines simultaneously; VMware brought virtualization to ordinary x86 computers in 1999.
虚拟化是 [[cloud-computing|云计算]] 的技术基础：云服务商把: Virtualization is the technical foundation of [[cloud-computing|Cloud computing]]: cloud service providers slice giant data centers into tens of thousands of virtual machines rented by the hour.
虚拟机各自带一个完整的操作系统；容器共享宿主机内核，只打包应用和依赖，因此更轻、: Each virtual machine carries a complete operating system; containers share the host kernel, only packaging applications and dependencies, making them lighter and faster to start up.
把应用和它依赖的一切打包成标准\"集装箱\"，在任何机器上以同样方式运行。: Packaging applications and everything they depend on into standard "containers" allows them to run in the same way on any machine.
大多数时候我们不需要模拟一整台机器，只需要把应用和它依赖的库打包、和别的应用隔开: Most of the time, we do not need to simulate an entire machine; we only need to package the application and its dependencies, separate them from other applications, and share the same operating system kernel. This makes it much lighter than a virtual machine ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
容器利用 Linux 内核的隔离功能（命名空间、控制组），让每个容器看到自己独立: Containers utilize isolation functions in the Linux kernel (namespaces, cgroups) so that each container sees its own independent file system, network, and process list. Container images package programs and all dependencies into a standard file, allowing an environment where "it runs on my computer" to be moved as-is to any server. Containers typically start within seconds, whereas virtual machines may take tens of seconds to several minutes.
2013 年 Docker 发布，让容器技术变得简单易用。这一思路常被类比为海运: In 2013, Docker was released, making container technology simple and easy to use. This approach is often compared to standard shipping containers in maritime transport (see [[container-shipping]]).
容器成为现代软件打包和部署的标准方式，也是 [[microservices|微服: Containers have become the standard method for modern software packaging and deployment, and they form the foundation of [[microservices|Microservices]] and [[devops|DevOps & CI/CD]].
谷歌开源的容器编排系统，自动部署、扩缩和修复成千上万个容器。: Google's open-source container orchestration system automatically deploys, scales, and repairs tens of thousands of containers.
当容器有成千上万个时，人不可能逐个管理；只需声明\"我想要什么状态\"（比如\": When there are tens of thousands of containers, humans cannot manage them one by one; instead, you only need to declare "what state I want" (for example, "this service always runs 5 replicas"), allowing the system to automatically and continuously pull reality back to this state ([[p:feedback|feedback]]).
Kubernetes 把一群服务器当作一个整体资源池，自动决定每个容器放在哪台机: Kubernetes treats a group of servers as a single resource pool, automatically deciding where each container should run on which machine. If a container crashes, it restarts; if traffic increases, it automatically scales up; and it is responsible for network connections between services and rolling upgrades.
谷歌在内部集群管理系统 Borg 的经验基础上开发，2014 年开源，后捐给云原: Developed based on Google's internal cluster management system Borg experience, it was open-sourced in 2014 and later donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF).
它成为云上运行容器的事实标准，被称为\"云的操作系统\"。: It has become the de facto standard for running containers in the cloud, referred to as "the operating system of the cloud".
可靠地存储、查询和更新大量结构化数据的系统，是几乎所有应用的后台。: Systems that reliably store, query, and update large amounts of structured data serve as the backend for almost all applications.
数据一旦被多个程序、多个人同时使用，就需要一个专门的系统来负责\"存得稳、查得快: Once data is used simultaneously by multiple programs or multiple people, a dedicated system is needed to be responsible for "storing steadily, querying quickly, and modifying correctly," rather than letting each program read and write files independently.
数据库管理系统（DBMS）在应用和磁盘之间提供统一的服务：: Database Management Systems (DBMS) provide unified services between applications and disks:
**存得稳**：数据写入后即使断电也不会丢，靠的是先写日志、再改数据；: **Storing steadily**: Data written after a power outage will not be lost; this relies on writing logs first, then modifying data;
**查得快**：用**索引**（通常是 B 树，像书末的索引页）避免逐行扫描，在: **Querying quickly**: Using **indexes** (usually B-trees, like the index pages at the end of books) to avoid scanning row by row; locating one record among billions requires only a few disk reads;
**改得对**：用 [[transaction-acid|事务]] 保证多个人同: **Modifying correctly**: Using [[transaction-acid|transactions]] to ensure data does not go wrong when multiple people modify it simultaneously.
最常用的是 [[relational-database|关系数据库]]：数据存成: The most common is [[relational-database|relational database]]: data is stored in tables, described using SQL language stating "what is needed," and the database decides "how to find" it on its own. Additionally, there are [[nosql|NoSQL databases]] oriented toward massive and flexible data, [[data-warehouse|Data Warehouse]] oriented toward analysis, and vector databases serving AI retrieval.
1960 年代出现了层次型和网状数据库（如 IBM 为阿波罗计划参与开发的 IM: Hierarchical and network databases appeared in the 1960s (such as IMS developed by IBM for the Apollo program); in 1970, IBM's Edgar F. Codd proposed the relational model; in 1979, Oracle released one of the earliest commercial SQL databases.
银行转账、网购下单、机票预订、社交网络——几乎所有在线服务的背后都是数据库。: Bank transfers, online shopping orders, flight bookings, social networks—almost all online services are backed by databases.
关系数据库把数据存成表，一句 SQL 就能完成\"查询所有北京客户的订单\"这样: Relational databases store data in tables, and a single SQL statement can complete requests such as "query all orders for Beijing customers".
用表格和关系代数组织数据，用 SQL 声明\"要什么\"而不是\"怎么找\"。: Organize data using tables and relational algebra, and declare "what is needed" using SQL rather than "how to find" it.
把所有数据都表示成简单的二维表，并用数学上的集合运算来操作，就能让\"数据长什么: By representing all data as simple two-dimensional tables and operating on them using mathematical set operations, one can completely separate "what the data looks like" from "how programs use data" ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]]).
每张表的每一行是一条记录，每一列是一个属性；表与表之间通过\"键\"关联（订单表: Each row in every table is a record, and each column is an attribute; tables are associated with each other through "keys" (the order table records customer numbers). Users state "what is needed" using declarative languages like SQL, such as `SELECT name FROM customers WHERE city='Beijing'`, and the database query optimizer will automatically select the fastest execution method.
1970 年科德发表论文提出关系模型，获 1981 年图灵奖；1974 年 IB: In 1970, Codd published a paper proposing the relational model, winning the Turing Award in 1981; in 1974, IBM developed the predecessor of SQL called SEQUEL. Oracle, IBM DB2, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite are all relational databases.
SQL 诞生 50 年仍是数据行业最通用的语言之一；SQLite 嵌在几乎每部手: SQL has remained one of the most universal languages in the data industry for 50 years; SQLite is embedded in almost every mobile phone and browser, possibly being one of the most widely deployed software programs in the world.
一组操作要么全部成功要么全部撤销，保证转账这类操作不会只做一半。: A group of operations either all succeeds or all is rolled back, ensuring that operations like transfers do not succeed only partially.
一组相关的修改要么全部完成，要么一个都不做——绝不能停在\"钱已扣、却没到账\": A set of related modifications either all complete or none are done at all—never stopping in an intermediate state such as "money deducted but not yet credited".
事务的四个保证合称 ACID：**原子性**（全做或全不做）、**一致性**（规: The four guarantees of a transaction are collectively known as ACID: **Atomicity** (all do or none do), **Consistency** (rules always hold, for example, balance cannot be negative), **Isolation** (concurrent transactions do not interfere with each other, appearing to execute sequentially), and **Durability** (once confirmed, data is not lost even if power fails). The implementation mechanisms are primarily logs and locks.
吉姆·格雷（Jim Gray）在 1970 年代奠定了事务处理理论，获 1998: Jim Gray laid the foundation for transaction processing theory in the 1970s and received the Turing Award in 1998.
事务让银行、证券和电商系统可以放心地把钱和订单交给计算机。: Transactions allow banks, securities firms, and e-commerce systems to safely hand over money and orders to computers.
放弃部分关系约束换取横向扩展和灵活结构，如键值、文档、列族、图数据库。: Partially sacrificing relational constraints in exchange for horizontal scaling and flexible structures, such as key-value stores, document databases, column-family databases, and graph databases.
当数据量大到一台机器装不下、或者数据形状经常变化时，可以放弃关系数据库的部分保证: When data volume is too large for a single machine or the data shape changes frequently, one can sacrifice some guarantees of relational databases (such as strict table schemas and cross-table transactions) in exchange for easier horizontal scaling across many machines.
NoSQL 是一类数据库的统称，包括：**键值存储**（像一个超大的字典，如 R: NoSQL is a collective term for a class of databases, including: **Key-value storage** (like a huge dictionary, such as Redis), **Document databases** (storing documents in JSON format, such as MongoDB), **Column-family databases** (such as Cassandra and HBase), and **Graph databases** (such as Neo4j).
谷歌的 Bigtable（2006 年论文）和亚马逊的 Dynamo（2007: Google's Bigtable (2006 paper) and Amazon's Dynamo (2007 paper) inspired this wave; the term "NoSQL" became popular starting in 2009.
NoSQL 支撑了社交网络和大型网站的海量数据；后来的\"NewSQL\"数据库: NoSQL supports the massive data of social networks and large websites; later "NewSQL" databases attempt to balance relational models with horizontal scaling.
把海量数据切块分给成百上千台廉价机器并行处理，再汇总结果。: Splitting massive data into chunks assigned to hundreds over a thousand cheap machines for parallel processing, then aggregating results.
当数据大到一台计算机存不下、算不完时，就把数据切块分给成千上万台普通服务器并行处: When data is too large for a single computer to store or process, it is split into chunks and distributed to thousands of ordinary servers for parallel processing, with results aggregated ([[p:division|division of labor]]).
谷歌 2004 年发表的 MapReduce 论文提出了一个简单的编程模型：**: Google's 2004 MapReduce paper proposed a simple programming model: the **Map** phase lets each machine process its own share of data independently, and the **Reduce** phase aggregates intermediate results by key. The framework automatically handles task distribution and machine failures. Open-source implementations like Hadoop (2006) made this accessible to ordinary companies; later Spark placed intermediate results in memory for significantly faster speeds. People often use "3V" to summarize big data: large volume, high velocity, and diverse variety.
谷歌的杰夫·迪恩（Jeff Dean）和桑杰·格玛沃特（Sanjay Ghema: Google's Jeff Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat published the MapReduce paper; Doug Cutting led the development of Hadoop.
大数据技术让推荐系统、精准广告和用户行为分析成为可能，也为后来训练 AI 模型积: Big data technologies made recommendation systems, targeted advertising, and user behavior analysis possible, and also accumulated data and infrastructure for later training AI models; simultaneously, they raised concerns about privacy (see [[web-cookies]]).
把各业务系统的数据集中起来专门用于分析和报表。: Centralizing data from various business systems specifically for analysis and reporting.
日常业务数据库为\"快速记一笔\"而优化，而分析需要\"一次扫描几亿行\"；把数: Operational business databases are optimized for "quickly recording an entry," while analysis requires "scanning hundreds of millions of rows at once"; by replicating data into a warehouse designed specifically for analysis, these two tasks no longer interfere with each other.
数据仓库定期从各个业务系统抽取、清洗、合并数据（ETL），按\"列\"而不是按\: Data warehouses periodically extract, clean, and merge data from various business systems (ETL), storing it by "column" rather than by "row"; this means when calculating statistics for a specific column (such as sales revenue), only that column needs to be read, resulting in much faster speeds. Modern cloud data warehouses (such as Snowflake and BigQuery) separate storage from computation, allowing scaling on demand.
1980 年代末 IBM 的研究者提出数据仓库概念，比尔·因蒙（Bill Inm: In the late 1980s, IBM researchers proposed the concept of data warehouses; Bill Inmon promoted it during the 1990s.
数据仓库和\"商业智能\"报表让企业的决策更多地依靠数据而不是直觉。: Data warehouses and "business intelligence" reports allow enterprise decision-making to rely more on data than intuition.
去掉数据中的冗余和人感知不到的细节，让同样内容占更少空间。: Removing redundancy and details imperceptible to human perception from data allows the same content to occupy less space.
现实中的数据都有规律和重复（[[p:info|信息熵]]），出现越频繁的东西用越: Real-world data has patterns and repetition ([[p:info|information entropy]]); items that appear more frequently use shorter codes, reducing total length; meanwhile, details imperceptible to the human eye or ear can simply be discarded.
**无损压缩**能完全还原原始数据，如 ZIP、PNG：哈夫曼编码给常见字符分配: **Lossless compression** can fully restore original data, such as ZIP and PNG files: Huffman coding assigns short codes to common characters and long codes to rare characters; LZ series algorithms replace repeated segments with references like "start at byte number X ahead, copy for length Y." **Lossy compression** discards information imperceptible to humans, such as JPEG images, MP3 music, and H.264/H.265 video, achieving compression ratios from ten to over a hundred times (see [[video-codec]]). Shannon proved that the limit of lossless compression is the information entropy of data.
1952 年哈夫曼（David Huffman）在读研究生时提出哈夫曼编码；19: Huffman (David Huffman) proposed Huffman coding while reading for his graduate degree in 1952; Israeli scholars Jacob Ziv and Abraham Lempel published the LZ algorithm in 1977–1978.
没有压缩，网络视频、流媒体音乐和手机拍照存储都几乎不可能实现。: Without compression, network video streaming, music streaming, and mobile photography storage would almost all be impossible to achieve.
哈夫曼编码：出现次数多的字母（A）得到更短的码，整体长度减少。: Huffman coding: Letters that appear more frequently (such as 'A') are assigned shorter codes, reducing the overall length.
把任意长度的数据映射成固定长度的\"指纹\"，用于快速查找、校验和密码学。: Map data of arbitrary length into a fixed-length "fingerprint" for rapid lookup, verification, and cryptography.
用一个函数把任意数据\"搅拌\"成一个固定长度的数字，相同的输入永远得到相同的结: Use a function to "stir" any data into a fixed-length number; identical input always yields the same result. Using this number directly as an address allows immediate access to the data in one step.
**哈希表**用哈希值决定把数据放进哪个\"桶\"，查找时重新计算哈希值就能直接: **Hash tables** use hash values to decide which "bucket" data goes into; during lookup, recalculating the hash value directly locates the data, requiring on average only one step (O(1), see [[big-o]]). When two different pieces of data fall into the same bucket, it is called a "collision," requiring additional processing. **Cryptographic hashes** (such as SHA-256) require that finding collisions be extremely difficult and that the original text cannot be inferred from the result ([[p:oneway|One-way functions]]), used for storing passwords, verifying files, and [[blockchain|Blockchain]].
1953 年 IBM 的汉斯·彼得·卢恩（Hans Peter Luhn）在内部: In 1953, Hans Peter Luhn of IBM proposed the idea of hashing in an internal memorandum.
哈希表是编程中最常用的数据结构之一（Python 的字典、Java 的 Hash: Hash tables are one of the most commonly used data structures in programming (such as Python's dictionary and Java's HashMap), while cryptographic hashes form the foundation for digital signatures and blockchain.
哈希函数把每个名字映射到一个桶，查找时直接去对应的桶里找。: A hash function maps each name to a bucket; during lookup, you simply search within the corresponding bucket.
给世界上每个字符分配唯一编号，让中文、表情符号和英文可以在同一文本里共存。: Assign unique numbers to every character in the world, allowing Chinese characters, emojis, and English text to coexist within the same document.
只要全世界约定\"每个字符对应唯一一个编号\"，任何语言的文字都能在任何电脑上正: As long as the entire world agrees that "each character corresponds to exactly one number," text from any language can be displayed correctly on any computer and exchanged ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
1991 年 Unicode 1.0 发布；UTF-8 由肯·汤普森和罗布·派克: Unicode 1.0 was released in 1991; UTF-8 was designed by Ken Thompson and Rob Pike in 1992.
今天绝大多数网页都使用 UTF-8 编码，多语言互联网才得以实现。: Today, the vast majority of websites use UTF-8 encoding, making a multilingual internet possible.
汉明码等编码加入少量校验位，能自动发现并修正传输和存储中翻转的比特。: Encodings such as Hamming code add a small number of check bits to automatically detect and correct flipped bits during transmission and storage.
在数据里有规律地加入一些冗余位，即使传输或存储中有几位出错，也能自动发现甚至纠正: Regularly insert some redundant bits into data; even if several bits are corrupted during transmission or storage, the error can be automatically detected and sometimes corrected ([[p:redundancy|redundancy]]).
最简单的是\"奇偶校验\"：加 1 位让 1 的个数为偶数，能发现单个比特出错。: The simplest is "parity check": add one bit so that the count of 1s is even, which can detect a single-bit error. Hamming code uses multiple intersecting check bits to locate and correct a single error. Stronger codes such as Reed-Solomon, LDPC, and Polar codes can correct errors occurring in sequences.
1950 年贝尔实验室的汉明（Richard Hamming）发表汉明码——据说: In 1950, Richard Hamming of Bell Labs published the Hamming code—allegedly because he had grown tired of computers interrupting his calculations on weekends due to errors.
从 CD 刮花了还能播放、二维码污损了还能扫，到手机通信、深空探测器传回照片和服: From scratched CDs that still play and damaged QR codes that can still be scanned, to mobile communications, photos returned by deep-space probes, and server memory (ECC memory), error-correcting codes are ubiquitous. 5G has adopted LDPC codes and Polar codes.
把数据复制到多块硬盘或多个地点，任何一处损坏都能恢复。: Copy data to multiple hard drives or different locations; if any one fails, the data can be recovered.
任何硬盘都会坏，不能指望单一设备永远可靠；把数据多存几份、存在不同的地方，就能把: Any hard drive will fail; do not expect a single device to be reliable forever; by storing data in multiple copies at different locations, you can reduce the probability of loss to an extremely low level ([[p:redundancy|redundancy]]).
**RAID** 把多块硬盘组合使用：RAID 1 把数据同时写到两块盘上（镜像: **RAID** combines multiple hard drives for use: RAID 1 writes data simultaneously to two disks (mirroring), while RAID 5 distributes data and parity information across multiple disks, allowing recovery if one disk fails. However, RAID cannot prevent accidental deletion or ransomware attacks, so **backups** are still required. Industry professionals often cite the "3-2-1 rule": at least three copies of data, stored on two different media types, with one copy kept off-site.
1988 年加州大学伯克利分校的帕特森（David Patterson）、吉布森: In 1988, David Patterson, Gibson, and Katz from the University of California, Berkeley, published a paper proposing RAID.
RAID 让用廉价硬盘搭建可靠的存储系统成为可能；云存储服务则把多副本冗余做成了: RAID made it possible to build reliable storage systems using inexpensive hard drives; cloud storage services have turned multi-copy redundancy into standard services.
用工程方法管理大型软件的需求、设计、测试和维护，源于 1960 年代的\"软件危: Managing requirements, design, testing, and maintenance for large-scale software using engineering methods originated from the "software crisis" of the 1960s.
软件的难点不在于写出能跑的代码，而在于让很多人在很长时间里协作、修改而不崩溃；这: The challenge of software is not writing code that runs, but enabling many people to collaborate and modify it over long periods without breaking; this requires methods, processes, and discipline like engineering.
软件工程关注整个生命周期：需求分析、设计、编码、[[software-testi: Software engineering covers the entire lifecycle: requirements analysis, design, coding, [[software-testing|testing]], deployment, and maintenance. Core tools include modular design, code review, [[version-control|version control]], automated testing, and project management methodologies (from "waterfall" to [[agile|agile development]]).
1968 年北约在德国召开会议讨论\"软件危机\"——项目普遍超支、延期、充满缺: In 1968, NATO held a conference in Germany discussing the "software crisis"—projects were consistently over budget, delayed, and riddled with defects—the term "software engineering" gained popularity. Margaret Hamilton, who led software development for the Apollo spacecraft, was also an early advocate of this concept. In 1975, Brooks (Fred Brooks) published "The Mythical Man-Month," proposing that "adding manpower to a late project will only make it later."
软件工程把编程从个人手艺变成了可管理的工业活动；它的许多教训（沟通成本随人数增长: Software engineering transformed programming from a personal craft into a manageable industrial activity; many of its lessons (communication costs grow with team size, there is no "silver bullet") remain applicable today.
找出并修复程序错误的过程；1947 年哈佛 Mark II 里被夹住的飞蛾让\": The process of finding and fixing program errors; in 1947, a moth trapped inside the Harvard Mark II made the term "bug" widely known.
程序错误往往不在你以为的地方；系统地缩小范围、验证假设，比盯着代码猜更快。: Program errors often occur not where you expect; systematically narrowing down the scope and verifying assumptions is faster than guessing by staring at code.
调试的基本方法是复现问题、缩小范围（比如二分法：注释掉一半代码看错误还在不在）、: The basic method of debugging involves reproducing the problem, narrowing the scope (such as binary search: comment out half the code to see if the error persists), and observing program state. Debuggers allow a program to pause at a specific line (breakpoint), execute line-by-line, and view variable values.
1947 年哈佛 Mark II 计算机的工作人员在继电器里发现一只飞蛾，把它贴: In 1947, staff at the Harvard Mark II computer found a moth inside a relay, stuck it on a log sheet, and wrote "the first bug ever found." The term "bug" was previously used in engineering to refer to faults; this story spread because Grace Hopper often told it.
调试工具和方法是程序员日常工作的一大半；现在 AI 编程助手也能帮助定位和修复错: Debugging tools and methods account for about half of a programmer's daily work; now AI coding assistants can also help locate and fix errors (see [[ai-coding]]).
用自动化的单元测试、集成测试在上线前发现错误，并防止改动破坏旧功能。: Use automated unit tests and integration tests to find errors before deployment and prevent changes from breaking existing functionality.
测试只能证明有错误，不能证明没有错误；但自动化测试能让每次修改后都快速确认\"原: Testing can only prove the presence of errors, not their absence; but automated testing allows rapid confirmation after each change that "what was working still works.".
**单元测试**检查单个函数是否正确；**集成测试**检查多个模块能否配合；**: **Unit tests** check if individual functions are correct; **integration tests** check whether multiple modules work together; **end-to-end tests** simulate real user operations across the entire system. "Test-driven development" advocates writing tests first, then writing code to make them pass. Continuous integration systems automatically run all tests whenever code is submitted (see [[devops]]).
大型软件每天被修改成百上千次，没有自动化测试几乎无法保证质量。: Large software systems are modified hundreds of times over a thousand days; without automated testing, it is nearly impossible to guarantee quality.
记录代码每一次修改、支持多人并行开发和合并；Git 是事实标准。: Record every modification to the code, support parallel development by multiple people, and merge changes; Git is the de facto standard.
把代码的每一次修改都作为快照记录下来，就能随时回到过去、查明谁改了什么，多人还能: By recording every modification to the code as a snapshot, you can always return to the past, determine who made what changes, and allow multiple people to work on their own branches simultaneously before merging.
每次\"提交\"（commit）记录一组修改、作者和说明。**分支**让人在不影: Each "commit" records a set of modifications, the author, and a description. **Branches** allow development of new features without affecting the main line; once complete, they are merged back. **Distributed** version control systems (such as Git) give every developer a complete copy of history, enabling offline work.
早期系统有 1972 年的 SCCS、1990 年的 CVS 和 2000 年的: Early systems included SCCS from 1972, CVS from 1990, and SVN from 2000; in 2005, Linus Torvalds developed Git to manage [[linux|Linux]] kernel, writing the first version in about ten days. GitHub, launched in 2008, made Git the de facto standard.
Git 和代码托管平台让全球数千万开发者能协作开发，也是 [[open-sour: Git and code hosting platforms enable tens of millions of developers worldwide to collaborate on development and serve as infrastructure for [[open-source|open source]] communities.
Git 分支：从主线分出功能分支，开发完成后合并回主线。: Git branches: create feature branches from the main line; merge them back once development is complete.
源代码公开、任何人都能使用修改和分发的软件，Linux 和互联网基础设施大多是开: Source code is public, allowing anyone to use, modify, and distribute software; Linux and much of the internet infrastructure are open source.
软件复制的成本几乎为零，代码本身又能被任何人审查和改进；把源代码公开、允许自由修: The cost of copying software is almost zero; the code itself can be reviewed and improved by anyone; making source code public and allowing free modification and redistribution often yields collaborative power exceeding that of a single company ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
开源软件按许可证发布，主要分两类：**宽松型**（如 MIT、Apache）允许: Open source software is released under licenses, mainly divided into two categories: **permissive** (such as MIT, Apache) allow any use, including incorporation into closed-source commercial products; **copyleft** (such as GPL) require that modified versions be opened when distributed. A typical collaboration flow involves copying a codebase (fork), modifying it, submitting a merge request (pull request), and having project maintainers review before merging.
开源项目的维持靠多种方式：志愿者、公司派工程师参与（因为它们自己也依赖这些软件）: Open source projects are maintained through various methods: volunteers, engineers from companies participating (as they also depend on these software), foundations, donations, and the "open core + paid cloud services" business model.
1983 年理查德·斯托曼（Richard Stallman）发起 [[gnu|: In 1983, Richard Stallman initiated [[gnu|GNU & the free software movement]] to advocate for "free software"; in 1991, [[linux|Linux]] appeared; in 1998, Netscape made browser source code public, and that year the term "open source" was proposed and promoted, with the Open Source Initiative founded.
今天几乎所有软件都建立在开源组件之上：[[linux|Linux]] 运行着绝大: Today, almost all software is built on open-source components: [[linux|Linux]] runs the majority of servers, while [[python|Python]], PyTorch, Kubernetes, and Android are all open source. In the AI field, "open-weight" models also continue this tradition (see [[open-weight-models]]).
开源不等于\"没人负责\"或\"一定免费\"，也不等于\"更安全\"——代码公开: Open source does not mean "no one is responsible" or "must be free," nor does it mean "more secure"—making code public simply enables review. Some critical open-source components have been maintained for long periods by only a few volunteers; the 2021 Log4j vulnerability and the 2024 xz backdoor incident both exposed this risk (see [[vulnerability]]).
开源协作的典型流程：复制、修改、提交合并请求、评审、合并。: The typical flow of open-source collaboration is: copy, modify, submit a pull request, review, merge.
斯托曼发起的自由软件运动，GPL 许可证要求衍生作品也必须开源。: The free software movement initiated by Richard Stallman requires that derivative works also be open source under the GPL license.
如果用户能自由地运行、研究、修改和分享软件，并要求修改后的版本同样自由，自由就能: If users can freely run, study, modify, and share software, and demand that modified versions remain equally free, freedom can be passed down through generations of code.
GNU（\"GNU's Not Unix\"的递归缩写）计划要开发一套完全自由的: The GNU (a recursive abbreviation for "GNU's Not Unix") project aimed to develop a completely free class-Unix operating system, producing tools such as the GCC compiler, Emacs editor, and Bash. Its GPL license uses copyright law to ensure code remains open forever. GNU's own kernel progress was slow; it eventually combined with [[linux|Linux]] kernel to form the commonly referred "GNU/Linux" system.
1983 年理查德·斯托曼宣布 GNU 计划，1985 年成立自由软件基金会。: Richard Stallman announced the GNU project in 1983 and founded the Free Software Foundation in 1985.
GNU 工具和 GPL 许可证为整个 [[open-source|开源]] 运动: GNU tools and the GPL license laid the technical and legal foundations for the entire [[open-source|open source]] movement.
以短周期迭代、频繁交付和快速反馈代替一次性的大规划。: Replace long-term planning with short-cycle iteration, frequent delivery, and rapid feedback.
需求在开发过程中一定会变；与其一开始就制定一份完美的长期计划，不如每隔几周交付一: Requirements will inevitably change during development; rather than creating a perfect long-term plan at the start, deliver usable versions every few weeks and continuously adjust based on user feedback ([[p:feedback|feedback]]).
传统的\"瀑布式\"开发按需求、设计、编码、测试的顺序一次走完，往往做到最后才发: Traditional "waterfall" development proceeds sequentially through requirements, design, coding, and testing, often discovering wrong directions only at the end. Agile development breaks work into short cycles of 1–4 weeks called "sprints," delivering runnable software each cycle while teams hold brief daily meetings to synchronize progress. Scrum and Kanban (originating from the Toyota Production System, see [[toyota-production-system]]) are common practice frameworks.
2001 年 17 位软件开发者在美国犹他州发布《敏捷宣言》，主张\"个体和互动: In 2001, seventeen software developers in Utah, USA, published the "Agile Manifesto," advocating that "individuals and interactions take precedence over processes and tools; working software over comprehensive documentation; customer collaboration over contract negotiation; and response to change over following a plan".
敏捷成为软件业的主流工作方式，并被推广到产品设计、市场营销等其他领域。: Agile became the mainstream work method in the software industry and was promoted to other fields such as product design and marketing.
让开发和运维合一，代码每次提交都自动构建、测试和部署。: Unify development and operations, so that every code commit automatically builds, tests, and deploys.
开发团队想快速发布新功能，运维团队想保持系统稳定；把两者合为一体并高度自动化，就: Development teams want to release new features quickly, while operations teams want to maintain system stability; by combining them into one entity with high automation, you can achieve both speed and stability.
DevOps 的核心是自动化流水线：代码提交后自动构建、自动 [[softwar: The core of DevOps is automated pipelines: after code submission, automatically build, automatically [[software-testing|testing]] (continuous integration, CI), and upon passing, automatically deploy to servers (continuous delivery/deployment, CD). With monitoring and alerts, issues can be quickly rolled back. "Infrastructure as Code" writes server configurations as version-controlled code.
领先的互联网公司每天可以部署成百上千次，而过去软件可能一年才发布一次大版本。: Leading internet companies can now deploy hundreds over a thousand times daily, whereas software in the past might release a major version only once a year.
软件之间约定好的调用方式，像插座一样让不同程序互相连接。: Agreed-upon calling conventions between software programs act like sockets, allowing different programs to connect and communicate with each other.
只要双方约定好\"怎么提要求、会得到什么回答\"，一个程序就能使用另一个程序的功: As long as both parties agree on "how to make requests" and "what responses will be received," one program can use the functions of another without knowing its internal implementation details ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]]).
API（应用程序编程接口）规定了可以调用的功能、需要的参数和返回的结果。在网络上: APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) specify available functions, required parameters, and returned results. On networks, Web APIs typically send requests and return data in JSON format via HTTP; for example, weather applications call meteorological service APIs to obtain forecasts. The REST style that became popular in the 2000s has become the mainstream design approach for Web APIs.
API 让软件可以像乐高积木一样组合：一个应用可以同时调用支付、地图、短信和 A: APIs allow software to combine like Lego bricks: one application can simultaneously call payment, map, SMS, and AI model APIs. The "API economy" enables many companies to sell capabilities directly to developers, with large language models primarily providing services via API.
把大应用拆成许多通过 API 通信、可独立部署的小服务。: Break large applications into many small services that communicate via API and can be deployed independently.
把一个庞大的应用拆成许多小服务，每个服务只负责一件事、可以由一个小团队独立开发和: Split a massive application into many small services, where each service handles only one task and can be developed and deployed by a small team independently—thereby allowing the system's structure to follow the team's structure ([[p:division|division of labor]]).
亚马逊、Netflix 等公司在 2000 年代末到 2010 年代初的实践让这: Practices by companies like Amazon and Netflix in the late 2000s to early 2010s made this architecture popular, and the term "microservice" began to be widely used in the early 2010s.
微服务成为大型互联网公司的主流架构；但很多团队也发现，对中小项目来说，一个设计良: Microservices became the mainstream architecture for large internet companies; however, many teams also found that for medium-to-small projects, a well-designed "monolithic application" is often simpler and more efficient.
多台计算机通过网络协作完成一件事；任何一台随时可能出错，网络可能中断。: Multiple computers collaborate to complete a task via a network; any single computer can fail at any time, and the network may interrupt.
单台计算机的能力和可靠性总有上限；把任务分给许多台通过网络连接的计算机，就能突破: The capabilities and reliability of a single computer always have an upper limit; assigning tasks to many computers connected via a network allows us to break through this limit—but we must face the reality that networks introduce latency, may disconnect, and machines may crash.
1978 年兰波特（Leslie Lamport）发表论文，用\"逻辑时钟\"解: In 1978, Leslie Lamport published a paper using "logical clocks" to solve the problem of event ordering in distributed systems; he received the Turing Award in 2013.
分布式系统设计者常引用\"分布式计算的八个谬误\"，第一条就是\"网络是可靠的\: Designers of distributed systems often cite "The Eight Fallacies of Distributed Computing," with the first being "the network is reliable."
网络分区发生时，分布式系统只能在一致性和可用性之间二选一。: When a network partition occurs, a distributed system must choose between consistency and availability.
当网络断开、系统被分成两半时（分区），你只能二选一：要么拒绝部分请求以保证所有人: When the network disconnects and the system is split in half (partition), you must choose: either reject some requests to ensure all users see consistent data, or continue serving but allow temporary inconsistency.
CAP 指一致性（Consistency）、可用性（Availability）和: CAP refers to Consistency, Availability, and Partition tolerance. Since network partitions are inevitable in reality, designers actually trade off between consistency and availability: bank transfers tend toward consistency, while like counts on social networks can tolerate brief inconsistency ("eventual consistency").
2000 年伯克利的布鲁尔（Eric Brewer）提出这一猜想，2002 年由: In 2000, Eric Brewer at UC Berkeley proposed this conjecture; it was rigorously proven by Gilbert and Lynch in 2002.
CAP 定理让工程师明白分布式数据库不存在\"完美方案\"，只有针对场景的取舍。: The CAP theorem makes engineers realize that distributed databases have no "perfect solution," only trade-offs tailored to scenarios.
让多台可能出错的机器对同一个值达成一致的协议，是分布式数据库和区块链的核心。: Protocols allowing multiple potentially faulty machines to agree on the same value are at the core of distributed databases and blockchain.
多台机器中有一些可能会宕机或失联，但只要过半数的机器同意，就能就某个值达成可靠的: In a group of machines, some may crash or go offline; as long as more than half agree, reliable consensus can be reached on a certain value—because any two "majorities" must overlap by at least one machine.
兰波特在 1989 年提交了 Paxos 论文（1998 年才正式发表）；201: Lamport submitted the Paxos paper in 1989 (formally published in 1998); in 2014, Ongaro and Stubbleworth at Stanford University proposed the easier-to-understand Raft algorithm.
共识算法是分布式数据库、Kubernetes 的配置存储（etcd）和许多关键基: Consensus algorithms are at the core of reliable operation for distributed databases, Kubernetes configuration storage (etcd), and many critical infrastructures.
用文字命令操作计算机的界面，可组合、可脚本化，开发者至今离不开。: An interface using text commands to operate computers is combinable and scriptable; developers have relied on it until today.
文字命令可以精确表达、可以组合、可以保存成脚本反复执行——这是图形界面的点点按按: Text commands can be expressed precisely, combined, and saved as scripts for repeated execution—something graphical interfaces cannot achieve with mere clicks.
1971 年起 Unix 带有汤普森编写的 shell；1979 年的 Bour: Since 1971, Unix included a shell written by Thompson; the Bourne shell from 1979 and Bash from 1989 became later standards.
用窗口、图标、菜单和鼠标指针操作计算机；施乐 Alto 首创，Macintosh: Operate a computer using windows, icons, menus, and a mouse pointer; pioneered by Xerox Alto and popularized by Macintosh.
人对\"看得见、指得到\"的东西反应最快；把文件、程序画成屏幕上可以直接拖动的图: People react fastest to things they can see and touch; by drawing files and programs as icons and windows that can be dragged directly on the screen, users do not need to remember commands—they simply look at an icon to know what it can do ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]]).
图形用户界面常被概括为 WIMP：**窗口**（Window）、**图标**（I: Graphical user interfaces are often summarized as WIMP: **Window**, **Icon**, **Menu**, and **Pointer**. Users operate objects on the screen directly using a [[mouse|Computer mouse]] or their fingers ("direct manipulation"); the interface borrows metaphors from reality such as "desktop," "folder," and "recycle bin." The system constantly draws operation results onto the screen, forming immediate visual [[p:feedback|feedback]]. "What you see is what you get" ensures that what appears on the screen matches exactly what is printed out.
1968 年恩格尔巴特（Douglas Engelbart）在\"演示之母\"中: In 1968, Douglas Engelbart demonstrated the mouse, windows, and hypertext in "The Mother of All Demos"; in 1973, Xerox PARC's Alto computer first implemented a complete graphical desktop, where figures like Alan Kay developed related concepts. In 1979, Jobs visited Xerox PARC; subsequently, Apple launched the Lisa in 1983 and the Macintosh in 1984 to bring graphical interfaces to the masses; Microsoft released [[windows|Microsoft Windows]] in 1985, and Windows 95 in 1995 made it truly widespread. In 2007, the iPhone brought multi-touch to the mainstream (see [[touchscreen]]).
图形界面把计算机从专业人员的工具变成了人人都能用的日常设备，是 [[person: Graphical interfaces transformed computers from tools for professionals into everyday devices accessible to everyone; this was a key factor in the popularization of [[personal-computer|Personal computer (PC)]]. Today, voice and natural language are becoming new interaction methods (see [[ai-agent]]).
图形界面简史：从恩格尔巴特的演示到智能手机的触摸屏。: Brief history of graphical interfaces: from Engelbart's demo to touchscreen smartphones.
恩格尔巴特发明的指点设备，1968 年\"演示之母\"中首次公开。: Engelbart's pointing device, first publicly demonstrated in "The Mother of All Demos" in 1968.
人的手非常擅长指向；把手在桌面上的移动一比一地映射成屏幕上光标的移动，眼和手就形: Human hands are very good at pointing; mapping the hand's movement on a desktop one-to-one with the cursor's movement on the screen forms a tight [[p:feedback|feedback]] loop between eye and hand.
早期鼠标用底部的滚轮或滚球测量移动，现在的光电鼠标用一个微型摄像头每秒拍摄数千张: Early mice measured movement using a scroll wheel or ball at the bottom; modern optical mice use a miniature camera to take thousands of photos of the desktop per second, calculating movement direction and distance by comparing photo displacements.
1964 年恩格尔巴特和比尔·英格利希（Bill English）在斯坦福研究所: In 1964, Douglas Engelbart and Bill English created the first wooden mouse at Stanford Research Institute; it was publicly unveiled in "The Mother of All Demos" in 1968.
鼠标和 [[gui|图形界面]] 一起，让普通人也能操作计算机。: Mice and [[gui|Graphical User Interface]] together allow ordinary people to operate computers.
VisiCalc 让个人电脑第一次有了\"非买不可\"的理由，Excel 至今是: VisiCalc gave personal computers their first reason to be "must-have"; Excel remains the most widely used programming tool today.
把计算写成格子之间的关系（\"这一格 = 那两格之和\"），改一个数，所有相关结: Writing calculations as relationships between cells ("this cell equals the sum of those two cells") allows everyone to "program" without realizing it: changing one number automatically recalculates all related results.
电子表格由行和列组成的单元格构成，每个单元格可以放数据或公式。用户可以随时修改假: Electronic spreadsheets consist of cells formed by rows and columns; each cell can hold data or formulas. Users can modify assumptions at any time (such as interest rates) and immediately see result changes, known as "what-if analysis".
1979 年布里克林（Dan Bricklin）和弗兰克斯顿（Bob Frank: In 1979, Dan Bricklin and Bob Frankston developed VisiCalc for the Apple II; many people bought computers specifically to use it; Lotus 1-2-3 in 1983 and Microsoft Excel in 1985 succeeded one after another.
电子表格是最早的\"杀手级应用\"之一，彻底改变了会计、财务和管理工作，至今可能: Electronic spreadsheets were among the earliest "killer applications," fundamentally changing accounting, finance, and management work; today they may still be the programming tool used by the most people worldwide.
所见即所得地编辑排版文字，取代打字机。: Edit typesetting text with what-you-see-is-what-you-get, replacing the typewriter.
把文字先存在电子存储里而不是直接打在纸上，修改、复制、排版就都不再需要重打一遍。: Storing text in electronic storage rather than typing directly onto paper means modification, copying, and typesetting no longer require retyping everything.
文字处理软件允许插入、删除、移动文字，自动换行和分页，设置字体和格式，并检查拼写: Word processing software allows insertion, deletion, and movement of text; automatic line wrapping and page breaking; setting fonts and formats; and spell checking. The "what-you-see-is-what-you-get" interface ensures that the screen display matches the printout effect.
1974 年施乐帕克的 Bravo 是最早的所见即所得编辑器；1976 年的 E: Xerox PARC's Bravo in 1974 was the earliest what-you-see-is-what-you-get editor; Electric Pencil in 1976 was an early personal computer word processing software; WordStar in 1978 and Microsoft Word in 1983 became popular successively.
文字处理软件取代了打字机（见 [[typewriter]]），让写作和办公彻底数: Word processing software replaced the typewriter (see [[typewriter]]), making writing and office work fully digital.
用数学描述形状、光照和材质，让计算机生成图像；光线追踪模拟光的真实路径。: Use mathematics to describe shape, lighting, and material, allowing computers to generate images; ray tracing simulates the real path of light.
图像可以用数学来描述：形状是一堆三角形的坐标，颜色由光线如何照射、反射和折射决定: Images can be described mathematically: shapes are coordinates of a collection of triangles; color is determined by how light illuminates, reflects, and refracts; as long as calculations are fast enough, computers can "draw" any scene ([[p:optics|optics]]).
三维图形的基本流程是：用大量三角形组成物体的表面（建模）；把三维坐标投影到二维屏: The basic flow of 3D graphics is: compose an object's surface using a large number of triangles (modeling); project 3D coordinates onto a 2D screen; then calculate the color of each pixel (rendering). **Rasterization** is fast and is the mainstream approach for games; **ray tracing** simulates light reflection and refraction paths in scenes, producing more realistic images but requiring significantly more computation. [[gpu|Graphics processing unit (GPU)]] was born specifically for such large-scale parallel computing tasks.
1963 年萨瑟兰（Ivan Sutherland）在麻省理工学院开发 Sket: In 1963, Ivan Sutherland developed Sketchpad at MIT, which allowed drawing directly on the screen with a light pen. It is regarded as the beginning of computer graphics and graphical interfaces; he received the Turing Award in 1988. In 1980, Turner Whitted published the classic paper on ray tracing. In 1995, Pixar's Toy Story became the first fully computer-animated feature film; starting in 2018, real-time ray tracing entered consumer-grade graphics cards.
电影特效、动画、游戏、工业设计（见 [[cad-cam]]）、医学影像和虚拟现实: Film effects, animation, games, industrial design (see [[cad-cam]]), medical imaging, and virtual reality all depend on computer graphics.
从《Pong》到开放世界，游戏一直推动着图形芯片和交互技术进步。: From Pong to open-world games, the industry has consistently driven progress in graphics chips and interactive technology.
游戏程序在一个\"游戏循环\"中每秒运行几十到上百次：读取玩家输入、更新游戏世界: Game programs run dozens to hundreds of times per second within a 'game loop': reading player input, updating the game world (physics, AI, rules), and rendering images (see [[computer-graphics]]). Modern large-scale games are developed using [[game-engine|Game engine]], with teams reaching over a thousand people.
1958 年的《双人网球》和 1962 年麻省理工学院的《太空大战》是早期的电脑: The 1958 Tennis for Two and 1962 Spacewar from MIT were early computer games; in 1972, Atari's Pong launched the commercial electronic game industry, and that same year the first home console, Magnavox Odyssey, was released. Since then, consoles from Nintendo, Sony, and Microsoft, along with personal computers and mobile phones, have risen successively.
电子游戏产业的规模已超过电影和音乐产业。游戏对图形性能的需求催生了强大的 [[g: The scale of the video game industry has surpassed that of film and music industries. The demand for graphics performance in games spawned powerful [[gpu|Graphics processing unit (GPU)]], while GPUs later became the core hardware for training artificial intelligence—a classic example of technological unintended migration.
游戏引擎提供图形渲染、物理模拟、动画、音频、脚本和编辑器等工具，并能把同一个游戏: Game engines provide tools such as graphics rendering, physics simulation, animation, audio, scripting, and editors, and can publish the same game across multiple platforms including computers, game consoles, and mobile phones. Representative examples include Unreal Engine and Unity.
1993 年的《毁灭战士》（Doom）首次清晰地把游戏引擎与游戏内容分开，其引擎: In 1993, Doom clearly separated the game engine from game content for the first time; its engine was licensed to other developers. In 1998, Unreal Engine was released, followed by Unity in 2005.
游戏引擎大大降低了开发门槛；如今它也被用于电影虚拟拍摄、建筑可视化、汽车设计和: Game engines greatly lower development thresholds; they are now also used for film virtual photography, architectural visualization, automotive design, and [[digital-twin|Digital twin]].
统一分发和收费的软件市场，让个人开发者能把应用卖给全球用户。: A unified software market for distribution and monetization, enabling individual developers to sell applications to global users.
开发者把应用提交到商店，经平台审核后上架；用户一键下载和付费，平台通常抽取 15: Developers submit applications to stores; after platform review, they go live. Users download and pay with a single click; platforms typically take a 15%–30% share. More applications attract more users, and more users in turn attract more developers.
2008 年 7 月苹果推出 App Store，同年谷歌推出安卓应用市场（后更: In July 2008, Apple launched the App Store; that same year, Google launched the Android app market (later renamed Google Play).
应用商店创造了庞大的移动应用经济（见 [[mobile-internet]]），: App stores created a massive mobile application economy (see [[mobile-internet]]), but high commission rates and review authority also sparked antitrust controversies. Regulations such as the EU's Digital Markets Act now require platforms to open up third-party app distribution.
旧程序只用两位数存年份，2000 年会被当成 1900 年；全球花了巨资提前修复: Old programs stored years using two-digit numbers; in 2000, they would be interpreted as 1900. The world spent billions to fix this in advance.
日期计算错误可能影响银行利息、账单、航空调度和电力系统等。各国政府和企业在 19: Date calculation errors can affect bank interest, bills, airline scheduling, and power systems. Governments and enterprises invested heavily in the late 1990s to check and modify code (many were old systems written in [[cobol|COBOL]]); global costs are estimated at hundreds of billions of dollars.
2000 年 1 月 1 日平稳度过，只出现了少量小故障。: January 1, 2000 passed smoothly with only minor glitches.
千年虫是一次成功的大规模预防行动，但也因为\"什么都没发生\"，常被误认为是一场: The Y2K incident was a successful large-scale preventive action, but it is often mistakenly regarded as a scare because 'nothing happened.' Similar issues may arise again: many systems use 32-bit integers to record time and will overflow in 2038.
一方提供服务、另一方发请求，网页、App 和数据库几乎都是这种结构。: One party provides services while the other sends requests; websites, apps, and databases are almost always structured this way.
客户端（如浏览器或手机应用）向服务器发出请求，服务器处理后返回结果。网页、电子邮: The client (such as a browser or mobile app) sends requests to the server, which processes them and returns results. Websites, email, databases, and online games all adopt this pattern. In contrast is the 'peer-to-peer' (P2P) model, where each machine acts as both client and server.
这种架构在 1980 年代随着个人电脑和局域网的普及而流行开来，取代了\"大型机: This architecture became popular in the 1980s with the widespread adoption of personal computers and local area networks, replacing the centralized 'mainframe + dumb terminal' model.
客户端—服务器模式是 [[world-wide-web|万维网]] 和 [[cl: The client-server model is the basic structure of [[world-wide-web|World Wide Web]] and [[cloud-computing|Cloud computing]].
集中摆放成千上万台服务器的建筑，供电和散热是最大的工程挑战。: Buildings housing thousands of servers face major engineering challenges in power supply and heat dissipation.
数据中心由一排排机柜组成，配有不间断电源、备用柴油发电机、高速网络和庞大的冷却系: Data centers consist of rows of cabinets, equipped with uninterruptible power supplies, backup diesel generators, high-speed networks, and massive cooling systems. A common metric for energy efficiency is PUE (total electricity consumption ÷ IT equipment electricity consumption); the closer it is to 1, the better. Advanced data centers from major cloud providers can achieve around 1.1. GPU cabinets used for AI training have extremely high power density and are increasingly adopting liquid cooling.
据国际能源署（IEA）估计，2024 年全球数据中心用电约 4150 亿千瓦时，: According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), global data center electricity consumption was approximately 415 billion kilowatt-hours in 2024, accounting for about 1.5% of total global electricity usage; this figure is expected to grow by another 17% in 2025. In its 2026 analysis, the IEA projects that by 2030 this number will roughly double to approximately 950 billion kilowatt-hours, approaching 3% of global electricity usage, with AI being the primary driver.
数据中心是互联网和 AI 的\"工厂\"，它的选址越来越取决于能否获得充足、廉价: Data centers are the "factories" of the Internet and AI; their site selection increasingly depends on access to sufficient and affordable electricity and water resources, making technology companies important buyers in the power market.
像用水电一样按需租用计算、存储和软件，不再自建机房；AWS 2006 年开启了这: Renting computing, storage, and software on demand like water and electricity, without building your own data center facilities; AWS launched this era in 2006.
云服务商在全球建设巨型 [[data-center|数据中心]]，利用 [[vi: Cloud service providers build massive [[data-center|Data center]] globally, using [[virtualization|Virtualization]] and [[container|Container]] to slice physical resources for tens of thousands of customers. Based on how much the provider manages for you, cloud services are typically divided into three layers:
**IaaS（基础设施即服务）**：租用虚拟机、存储和网络，操作系统以上自己管；: **IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service)**: Rent virtual machines, storage, and networking; manage everything above the operating system yourself;
**PaaS（平台即服务）**：只需上传代码，运行环境由平台负责；: **PaaS (Platform as a Service)**: Simply upload code; the platform is responsible for the running environment;
**SaaS（软件即服务）**：直接使用做好的软件，如网页邮箱和在线文档（见 [: **SaaS (Software as a Service)**: Directly use pre-made software, such as web-based email and online documents (see [[saas]]).
云的关键特点是**弹性**：几分钟内就能从 1 台服务器扩展到 1000 台，用: The key characteristic of cloud computing is **elasticity**: you can scale from 1 server to 1000 servers in minutes; release when not in use, billed by the second or by the hour.
1961 年约翰·麦卡锡就设想过\"计算有朝一日会像电话一样成为公共事业\"。2: In 1961, John McCarthy envisioned "that computation will one day be like the telephone and become a public utility." In 2006, Amazon launched S3 storage services and EC2 computing services (AWS), ushering in the modern cloud computing era; subsequently, Google, Microsoft (Azure, 2010), and Alibaba Cloud (2009) and others entered the field sequentially.
创业公司不再需要先花大钱买服务器，几个人就能服务全球用户；大公司也把大量系统迁到: Startups no longer need to spend large sums buying servers first; a few people can serve global users. Large companies also migrate massive systems to the cloud. Cloud computing is also the main platform for training and running large AI models (see [[ai-accelerator]]).
\"云\"并不在天上，而是地面上一栋栋耗电巨大的数据中心；数据放在云上也不代表自: "The cloud" is not in the sky, but rather data centers on the ground that consume enormous amounts of electricity; placing data on the cloud does not mean it is automatically secure; configuration errors are one of the most common causes of data breaches on the cloud.
IaaS、PaaS、SaaS 的分工：越往右，云服务商替你管理的层次越多。: The division of labor between IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS: the further to the right, the more layers the cloud service provider manages for you.
软件不再装在本地，而是通过浏览器订阅使用，由厂商统一升级维护。: Software is no longer installed locally; it is subscribed and used through a browser, with unified upgrades and maintenance handled by the vendor.
用户按月或按年订阅，通过浏览器或客户端登录使用，数据存放在服务商的云端，功能更新: Users subscribe monthly or annually, log in and use via a browser or client, with data stored on the service provider's cloud; updates to functionality take effect simultaneously for all users.
1999 年创立的 Salesforce 以\"不要软件\"（No Softwa: Salesforce, founded in 1999, promoted online customer relationship management software with the slogan "No Software," becoming a representative of SaaS.
软件业的商业模式从\"一次性卖授权\"转向\"持续收订阅费\"；在线办公、协作、: The business model of the software industry has shifted from "one-time license sales" to "continuous subscription fees"; most online office, collaboration, and design tools are now SaaS.
开发者只写函数，服务器的分配和扩缩全部交给云平台，按调用次数计费。: Developers only write functions; server allocation and scaling are all handed over to the cloud platform, billed by call count.
开发者上传函数，并设定触发条件（如收到一个网络请求或有文件上传）。平台在事件发生: Developers upload functions and set trigger conditions (such as receiving a network request or uploading a file). The platform automatically starts the running environment to execute the function when an event occurs; no resources are consumed, nor is there a charge, when there are no requests. The cost is that initial startup may be slower ("cold start") and binding to a specific cloud platform.
2014 年亚马逊推出 AWS Lambda，让\"无服务器\"概念流行开来。: In 2014, Amazon launched AWS Lambda, making the concept of "serverless" popular.
无服务器让小团队能以极低成本运行访问量波动很大的服务。注意：服务器其实仍然存在，: Serverless allows small teams to run services with highly volatile traffic at extremely low costs. Note: servers actually still exist; you just cannot see them and do not need to manage them.
把计算放到离数据产生地更近的地方，降低延迟和带宽成本。: Place computing closer to where data is generated to reduce latency and bandwidth costs.
数据先在手机、摄像头、工厂设备或附近的边缘服务器上就地处理，只把结果或必要的数据: Data is processed locally on mobile phones, cameras, factory equipment, or nearby edge servers first; only results or necessary data are uploaded to the cloud. Content delivery networks (see [[cdn]]) represent an early form of edge computing.
自动驾驶、工业控制、增强现实等对延迟敏感的应用越来越依赖边缘计算；在手机上直接运: Applications sensitive to latency, such as autonomous driving, industrial control, and augmented reality, increasingly rely on edge computing; AI models running directly on mobile phones (edge-side AI) are also a form of edge computing.
用计算机解方程、做蒙特卡洛随机模拟，让\"计算\"成为实验和理论之外的第三种科学: Using computers to solve equations and perform Monte Carlo random simulations makes "computation" the third scientific method beyond experiment and theory.
闪存让数码相机、U 盘、智能手机和 [[ssd]] 成为可能，存储第一次摆脱了机: Solid-state drives (SSDs) made digital cameras, USB flash drives, smartphones, and [[ssd]] possible, allowing storage to finally break free from mechanical motion.
1972 年前后贝尔实验室的丹尼斯·里奇（Dennis Ritchie）设计，1: Designed around 1972 by Dennis Ritchie at Bell Labs, the [[unix|Unix]] kernel was rewritten in C in 1973. In 1978, Ritchie and Brian Kernighan published "The C Programming Language," which became a classic; the first example in the book, "hello, world," became the first line of code taught to programmers worldwide.
每个微服务有自己的数据库，通过 [[api|API]] 或消息队列与其他服务通信: Each microservice has its own database, communicating with other services via [[api|Application programming interface (API)]] or message queues, typically packaged as a [[container|Container]] running on [[kubernetes|Kubernetes]]. The advantage is independent scaling and upgrading; the drawback is that the system as a whole becomes a [[distributed-system|Distributed system]], making network calls, debugging, and data consistency more complex.
分布式系统要解决的核心问题包括：数据如何复制到多台机器（复制）、如何切分到多台机: The core problems distributed systems must solve include: how to replicate data across multiple machines (replication), how to sharding data across multiple machines (sharding), how multiple machines can reach consensus on a value (see [[consensus-algorithm]]), and how to continue functioning during machine and network failures. Without a globally unified clock, determining "who comes first" is itself a challenge.
搜索引擎、社交网络、[[cloud-computing|云计算]] 和 AI 大: Search engines, social networks, [[cloud-computing|Cloud computing]], and training for large AI models all run on distributed systems composed of tens of thousands of machines.
Paxos 和 Raft 算法选出一个\"领导者\"来提出决定，只有当多数节点确: The Paxos and Raft algorithms elect a "leader" to propose decisions; these take effect only when confirmed by a majority of nodes. When the leader fails, a new election is held. If one must also prevent nodes from intentionally lying ("Byzantine faults"), more complex algorithms are required; [[blockchain|Blockchain]]'s proof-of-work represents another approach.
用户在\"终端\"里输入命令，由一个叫 shell 的程序解释执行，例如 `ls: Users input commands in a "terminal," which are interpreted and executed by a program called a shell, such as `ls` listing files. With the help of [[unix|Unix]] pipes, several small commands can be chained together to complete complex tasks; writing a series of commands into a file becomes an automation script.
图形界面普及后，命令行依然是程序员和运维人员的主要工具；如今 AI 编程助手也常: After graphical interfaces became widespread, the command line remains the primary tool for programmers and operations personnel; today, AI coding assistants also frequently operate directly on code and systems via the command line (see [[ai-coding]]).
封装了渲染、物理、声音的通用开发平台，如今也用于影视、建筑和数字孪生。: A general development platform that encapsulates rendering, physics, and sound, now also used in film production, architecture, and digital twins.
**数值模拟**把天气、飞机周围的气流、蛋白质的运动等写成方程，在网格上逐步求解: **Numerical simulation** writes equations for weather patterns, airflow around aircraft, protein motion, etc., and solves them step-by-step on a grid; see [[climate-model]]. **Monte Carlo methods** estimate results using random sampling: for example, randomly scattering points in a square; the proportion falling inside an inscribed circle is approximately π/4; the more points scattered, the more accurate the estimate. Such calculations typically run on [[supercomputer|Supercomputer]] and are commonly written in [[fortran|FORTRAN]], C++, and Python.
1946 年数学家乌拉姆（Stanisław Ulam）在病中玩纸牌时想到用随机: In 1946, mathematician Stanisław Ulam, while playing cards while ill, conceived using random trials to estimate probability; together with John von Neumann, he developed the Monte Carlo method for nuclear weapon research, running on ENIAC starting in 1948; in 1950, ENIAC completed the first computer numerical weather prediction (see [[numerical-weather-prediction]]).
今天，新飞机、新药物、核反应堆和芯片在制造之前，都要先在计算机里\"试验\"无数: Today, new aircraft, new drugs, nuclear reactors, and chips must undergo countless "tests" inside computers before manufacturing; AI methods (such as AlphaFold) are becoming new tools for scientific computation.
蒙特卡洛方法估算 π：随机撒点，落在圆内的比例 × 4 ≈ π。: Monte Carlo method estimates π: randomly scatter points; the proportion falling inside the circle multiplied by 4 is approximately π.
不存在一个通用程序能判断任意程序是否会停下——计算机能力有严格的边界。: There does not exist a general program that can determine whether an arbitrary program will halt—computing capabilities have strict boundaries.
假设有程序 H(P) 能判断程序 P 会不会停。构造程序 D：如果 H 说 D: Suppose there exists a program H(P) that can judge whether program P will halt. Construct program D: if H says D will halt, D enters an infinite loop; if H says D will not halt, D stops immediately. So, does D halt or not? Regardless of the answer, it leads to a contradiction. This "self-referential" argument method is consistent with Gödel's incompleteness theorems.
1936 年图灵在提出 [[turing-machine|图灵机]] 的同一篇论: In 1936, Turing proved this conclusion in the same paper where he proposed [[turing-machine|Turing machine]].
停机问题说明计算机的能力存在原则性的上限，不是靠更快的硬件就能突破的。它的直接推: The halting problem demonstrates that there are principled upper limits to computer capabilities; they cannot be broken by faster hardware. Its direct implication is: no tool exists that can perfectly detect all viruses or all program errors; real-world detection tools can only be approximate (see [[malware]]).
停机问题的反证：一个\"唱反调\"的程序 D 让假想的判定程序 H 陷入矛盾。: The refutation of the halting problem: a "contrarian" program D causes the hypothetical decision procedure H to fall into a contradiction.
\"答案容易验证的问题，是否也一定容易求解？\"计算机科学最著名的未解难题。: "Is it also easy to solve?" The most famous open problem in computer science regarding problems whose answers are easy to verify.
**P** 类问题是能在\"多项式时间\"内求解的问题（规模变大时，所需时间增长: **P** class problems are those that can be solved within "polynomial time" (when the scale grows, the required time does not grow too fast; see [[big-o]]); **NP** class problems are those where the answer can be verified in polynomial time. Problems such as the Traveling Salesman Problem, scheduling, and Sudoku belong to one of the hardest categories within it—"NP-complete" problems: if any one of them has a fast solution, all NP problems will have fast solutions. Most researchers believe P ≠ NP, but no one can prove it.
1971 年库克（Stephen Cook）提出 NP 完全性概念，苏联的列文（: In 1971, Cook (Stephen Cook) proposed the concept of NP-completeness; Leonid Levin in the Soviet Union independently obtained similar results. In 1972, Karp (Richard Karp) proved that 21 classic problems are all NP-complete. In 2000, it was listed by the Clay Mathematics Institute as one of seven "Millennium Prize Problems," with a prize of $1 million.
现代密码学依赖于\"有些问题很难解\"的假设（见 [[public-key-cr: Modern cryptography relies on the assumption that "some problems are hard to solve" (see [[public-key-crypto]]); if P = NP is proven and practical algorithms exist, many encryption schemes will become ineffective, while fields such as optimization, logistics, and drug design will undergo drastic changes.
如果 P ≠ NP（多数人的看法），NP 完全问题位于 NP 中最难的边缘，P: If P ≠ NP (the view of most people), NP-complete problems lie on the hardest edge within NP, and P is only a subset of NP.
一种设想：AI 能自我改进后技术进步将失控加速；它是推测而非定论。: One hypothesis: AI can self-improve after which technological progress will accelerate out of control; it is speculation rather than a conclusion.
这一设想依赖几个前提：智能可以持续提升、AI 能有效地改进自身、而且不受算力、能: This hypothesis depends on several premises: intelligence can continuously improve, AI can effectively improve itself, and it is not constrained by physical conditions such as computing power, energy, and data. Critics point out that real-world technological progress often follows [[p:scurve|S-curve]] and encounters bottlenecks.
1965 年数学家古德（I. J. Good）提出\"智能爆炸\"的设想；199: In 1965, mathematician Good (I. J. Good) proposed the hypothesis of "intelligence explosion"; in 1993, science fiction writer and mathematician Vinge (Vernor Vinge) promoted the term "singularity" in an article; in 2005, Kurzweil (Ray Kurzweil) predicted in The Singularity is Near that the singularity will arrive around 2045.
奇点是讨论 [[agi|通用人工智能]] 和 AI 安全时常被提起的概念，但应把: The singularity is a concept often mentioned when discussing [[agi|Artificial general intelligence (AGI)]] and AI safety, but it should be regarded as a thought experiment and prediction.
用导线中电流的通断远距离传送字母，信息第一次跑得比马和船快。: Transmitting letters by turning current on and off in wires allowed information to travel faster than horses and ships for the first time.
电流在导线中以接近光速的速度传播，而在远端用电磁铁就能让它\"做动作\"（[[p: Current propagates through wires at nearly the speed of light, and an electromagnet at the far end can make it "act" ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]); as long as a convention is agreed upon that combinations of "on/off" represent which letter, information can instantly cross thousands of miles ([[p:info|Information theory]]).
电报系统有三部分：发报端的电键、连接两地的导线（以大地作为回路）、收报端的电磁铁: The telegraph system has three parts: the key at the sending end, the wire connecting two places (using the earth as the return path), and the electromagnet at the receiving end. Pressing the key connects the circuit, causing the distant electromagnet to pull its armature and emit a "click" sound or make an impression on the paper tape; releasing it disconnects the circuit. Holding the key down for a short time is a "dot," and for a long time is a "dash." Letters are spelled out using [[morse-code|Morse code]]. When lines are too long and current attenuates, relays ([[relay|Relay]]) are used at intermediate points.
1837 年英国的库克（William Cooke）和惠斯通（Charles W: In 1837, Cooke (William Cooke) of the UK and Wheatstone (Charles Wheatstone) obtained patents for a needle-point telegraph machine for railway signaling. In the same year, American painter Morse (Samuel Morse) demonstrated his telegraph machine; together with assistant Vail (Alfred Vail), he designed the code. In May 1844, the telegraph line from Washington to Baltimore was opened; the first message sent was "What hath God wrought". In 1866, [[transatlantic-cable|Transatlantic cable]] successfully operated.
电报第一次让信息的传递速度脱离了交通工具的速度。报纸能当天刊登远方的新闻，交易所: The telegraph first allowed information transmission speed to detach from the speed of transportation. Newspapers could publish distant news on the same day; exchanges could match prices within minutes; railways used it to schedule trains; empires used it to command overseas colonies. It was also the first global electronic network, sometimes called "the Internet of the Victorian era".
电报不是一个人发明的。德国的高斯和韦伯在 1833 年就用电报在哥廷根两座建筑之: The telegraph was not invented by a single person. Gauss (Carl Friedrich Gauss) and Weber (Wilhelm Eduard Weber) in Germany communicated between two buildings in Göttingen using telegraphy as early as 1833; Morse's main contribution was a simple, practical code and system.
电报：按下电键接通电路，远方电磁铁吸动衔铁，用\"点\"和\"划\"的组合拼出字: Telegraph: press the key to connect the circuit, causing the distant electromagnet to pull its armature, spelling letters with combinations of "dots" and "dashes".
用长短信号组合表示字母，常用字母用短码——一种朴素的压缩编码。: Letters are represented by combinations of long and short signals; frequently used letters use short codes—a naive form of compression encoding.
常用的字母用短码，罕用的字母用长码，平均下来传同样一段话需要的信号最少——这正是: Frequently used letters use short codes, rarely used letters use long codes; on average, the minimum number of signals needed to transmit a given passage is achieved—this is the naive version of "optimal coding" later in information theory ([[p:info|Information theory]]).
摩尔斯电码用\"点\"（短信号）和\"划\"（长信号）及不同长度的停顿表示字母和: Morse code uses "dots" (short signals) and "dashes" (long signals) as well as different lengths of pauses to represent letters and numbers. In English, the most common E uses only a dot, T is a dash, while rarely used letters like Q and Z require four symbols. The famous distress signal SOS is "···———···", representing no word, just easy to send and recognize.
1838 年前后摩尔斯和韦尔设计了最初的电码，据说韦尔到印刷厂数了各个字母铅字的: Around 1838, Morse and Vail designed the initial code; it is said that Vail counted the number of typefaces for each letter at a printing shop to determine code lengths. In 1865, the International Telegraph Conference adopted the revised "International Morse Code".
它是第一种被广泛使用的数字编码，至今仍用于业余无线电和航海应急（见 [[tele: It was the first widely used digital encoding and is still used in amateur radio and maritime emergencies (see [[telegraph]], [[data-compression]]).
横跨大西洋海底的电报线，把欧美通信从约 10 天缩短到几分钟。: The transatlantic submarine telegraph cable shortened communication between Europe and America from about 10 days to a few minutes.
电信号在长电缆中会因导线电阻和电缆的电容效应被削弱、拉长变形（[[p:ohm|欧: Telegraphic signals are weakened and distorted over long cables due to wire resistance and the capacitive effects of the cable ([[p:ohm|Ohm's law & circuits]]); the longer the cable, the more blurred the signal.
海底电报电缆的中心是铜芯，外包古塔胶（一种天然树胶）绝缘，再缠上钢丝铠装。巨轮\: The center of submarine telegraph cables is a copper core, insulated with gutta-percha (a natural tree resin), and armored with steel wires. The great ship "RMS Titanic" laid the cable while sailing across approximately 3000 km of the Atlantic seabed. Physicist Thomson (later Lord Kelvin) invented a sensitive mirror galvanometer to receive weak signals.
1858 年第一条电缆接通，维多利亚女王 98 个词的贺电用了约 16 个小时才: In 1858, the first cable was connected; Queen Victoria's congratulatory message of 98 words took about 16 hours to send, and the cable failed three weeks later; in 1866, the new cable successfully operated and has worked continuously since then.
欧美之间传递消息从坐船约 10 天缩短到几分钟，开启了全球即时通信时代（见 [[: Message transmission between Europe and America was shortened from about 10 days by sea to a few minutes, opening the era of global instant communication (see [[submarine-cable]], [[telegraph]]).
把声音的振动变成电流的起伏再还原成声音，让人可以远距离直接对话。: Converts the vibration of sound into fluctuations in electric current, then restores it back to sound, allowing people to communicate directly over long distances.
声音是空气的振动；让振动膜带动磁场变化，就能在线圈中感应出随声音起伏的电流（[[: Sound is the vibration of air; by letting a vibrating diaphragm drive changes in the magnetic field, an alternating current fluctuating with the sound can be induced in a coil ([[p:induction|Electromagnetic induction]]); this current travels to a distant location and drives another vibrating diaphragm, restoring the vibration back into sound.
早期电话的话筒用碳粒：声波压缩碳粒，改变电阻，让电池提供的电流随声音强弱变化；听: Early telephones used carbon granules in the transmitter: sound waves compressed the granules, changing resistance so that the current supplied by the battery varied with the strength of the sound; an electromagnet in the receiver vibrated a metal diaphragm to produce sound based on the current's strength. Each telephone connected to a switchboard ([[telephone-exchange|switchboard]]) via a pair of copper wires, and the exchange connected two lines together. Long-distance lines relied on amplifiers to compensate for signal attenuation.
电话网的价值随用户数急剧上升（[[p:network|网络效应]]）：只有一部电: The value of the telephone network rises sharply with the number of users ([[p:network|Network effects]]): having only one telephone is useless; each additional user means that all existing users can make one more call.
1876 年 3 月，贝尔（Alexander Graham Bell）获得电话: In March 1876, Bell (Alexander Graham Bell) received a patent for the telephone. A few days later, he said his first words to an assistant: "Mr Watson, come here, I want to talk to you." Elisha Gray in the United States submitted a similar patent description on the same day; Antonio Meucci, an Italian immigrant, had conducted experiments earlier, and the dispute over invention rights continued for many years. In 1877, the Bell Telephone Company was founded, later developing into AT&T, which monopolized the American telephone industry for nearly a century.
电话让人第一次能与远方的人实时交谈，重塑了商业、家庭和城市生活。AT&T 旗下的: The telephone enabled people to converse with distant individuals in real time for the first time, reshaping business, family, and urban life. The Bell Labs under AT&T nurtured a large number of inventions including the ([[transistor|Transistor]]), information theory, Unix, and lasers (see [[mobile-phone]], [[microphone-speaker]]).
电话的工作原理：话筒把声音的振动变成起伏的电流，经交换机接通后，听筒再把电流还原: The working principle of the telephone: the transmitter converts the vibration of sound into fluctuating current; after being connected by an exchange, the receiver restores the current back into sound.
把任意两部电话临时接通的设备，从人工接线员到自动交换再到程控数字交换。: Equipment that temporarily connects any two telephones, ranging from manual operators to automatic exchanges to programmable digital switching.
如果每两部电话之间都拉一根线，N 部电话就需要约 N²/2 根线；让所有电话都连: If a line were drawn between every pair of telephones, N telephones would require approximately N²/2 lines; by connecting all telephones to a central hub and having it connect them temporarily, the number of lines becomes proportional only to N ([[p:network|network]]).
最早由接线员手工插拔插头接通；后来出现由拨号脉冲驱动的步进制自动交换机和纵横制交: Originally, operators manually plugged and unplugged plugs to connect calls; later, step-by-step automatic exchanges driven by dial pulses and crossbar exchanges appeared; starting in the 1960s, computer-controlled programmable exchanges emerged, eventually becoming fully digital.
1878 年 1 月美国康涅狄格州纽黑文开通第一个商用电话交换局。1891 年殡: In January 1878, the first commercial telephone exchange opened in New Haven, Connecticut, USA. In 1891, Almon Strowger, an undertaker, obtained a patent for an automatic exchange, reportedly to prevent operators from diverting business calls to competitors. In 1965, the Bell System deployed its first programmable electronic exchange.
交换机让电话网可以扩展到数十亿用户；电话网\"电路交换\"的思路后来被互联网的: Switches allow the telephone network to expand to billions of users; the "circuit switching" approach of the telephone network was later challenged by the internet's ([[packet-switching|Packet switching]]) (see [[telephone]]).
逐行扫描纸面黑白并通过电话线传送，曾是办公室的标配。: Scanning black-and-white paper line by line and transmitting it over telephone lines was once standard in offices.
