任何一页图文都可以拆成一行行、一个个\"黑或白\"的小点逐个传送，接收端按相同顺: Any page of text or graphics can be decomposed into rows of individual "black or white" dots, transmitted one by one; the receiver redraws them in the same order ([[p:sampling|Sampling & digitization]]).
传真机用光电元件逐行扫描纸面，把黑白变成电信号，经 [[modem|调制解调器]: Fax machines use photoelectric elements to scan paper line by line, converting black and white into electrical signals, which are converted into audio signals via a ([[modem|Modem]]) and transmitted over telephone lines; the receiver restores the image line by line using thermal paper or a print head. Digital fax also compresses continuous white dots, allowing a page to be sent in tens of seconds.
1843 年苏格兰钟表匠贝恩（Alexander Bain）取得最早的传真专利，: In 1843, Scottish clockmaker Alexander Bain obtained the earliest patent for facsimile transmission, more than thirty years before the telephone. In 1865, Giovanni Caselli in Italy opened commercial fax services between Paris and Lyon. After international standards were unified in the 1980s, fax machines became widespread in offices globally.
传真曾是传送合同、图纸的标配，后来被电子邮件和扫描件取代（见 [[telepho: Fax was once standard for transmitting contracts and blueprints, later replaced by email and scanned documents (see [[telephone]], [[photocopier]]).
用电磁波而不是导线传递信号；马可尼 1901 年实现跨大西洋无线电通信。: Signals are transmitted using electromagnetic waves rather than wires; Marconi achieved transatlantic radio communication in 1901.
变化的电场产生磁场，变化的磁场又产生电场，二者交替向外传播，就是以光速飞行的电磁: Changing electric fields generate magnetic fields, and changing magnetic fields generate electric fields; these two alternate outwardly propagating as electromagnetic waves ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]) traveling at the speed of light; they do not require wires, can pass through air and vacuum, and are "caught" by electrons in distant wires, being converted back into current.
无线电通信有三个环节：**发射**——振荡电路产生高频电流，送进 [[anten: Radio communication has three stages: **transmission** — an oscillating circuit generates high-frequency current, fed into an ([[antenna|Antenna]]) to radiate electromagnetic waves; the sound or data to be transmitted is "ridden" on this carrier wave via ([[modulation|modulation]]); **propagation** — low-frequency long waves can follow the Earth's surface, short waves can reflect multiple times between the ionosphere and ground to reach the other side of the Earth, while high-frequency microwaves propagate essentially in straight lines; **reception** — a receiving antenna induces a weak current, a tuning circuit uses resonance to select only the desired frequency, then amplification and demodulation restore the information.
不同频率像不同的\"车道\"，互不干扰，所以无线电频谱必须由政府统一分配（见 [: Different frequencies act like different "lanes," mutually non-interfering, so the radio spectrum must be uniformly allocated by government (see [[spectrum]]).
1865 年英国物理学家麦克斯韦（James Clerk Maxwell）从方程: In 1865, British physicist James Clerk Maxwell predicted electromagnetic waves from his equations; in 1887, German Heinrich Hertz confirmed them in a laboratory. In 1895, Italian Guglielmo Marconi began experimenting with radio telegraphy; in December 1901, he achieved transatlantic communication, receiving three dots of the letter "S" from Russia's Alexander Popov also independently made a radio receiver in 1895. Marconi and Braun shared the 1909 Nobel Prize in Physics.
无线电让船只在海上第一次能求救（1912 年泰坦尼克号的求救电报使七百多人获救）: Radio enabled ships to send distress signals for the first time at sea (the Titanic's distress telegram in 1912 saved over seven hundred people), giving birth to ([[radio-broadcasting|Broadcasting]]), television, ([[radar|Radar]]), and satellite communication. Today's mobile phones, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS are essentially radio.
无线电通信：发射机把信息调制到载波上，经天线辐射成电磁波；接收天线感应出电流，调: Radio communication: The transmitter modulates information onto a carrier wave, which is radiated as electromagnetic waves by the antenna; the receiving antenna induces a current, which is then tuned and demodulated to restore the original information.
在导线中的振荡电流和空间中的电磁波之间互相转换的装置。: A device that converts oscillating currents in wires into electromagnetic waves in space and vice versa.
1887 年赫兹为验证电磁波制作了第一副偶极子天线；马可尼把天线高高架起并接地，: In 1887, Hertz built the first dipole antenna to verify electromagnetic waves; Marconi raised the antenna high and grounded it, greatly increasing communication distance.
把要传的信息\"骑\"在高频载波上（改它的幅度、频率或相位），接收端再取下来。: The information to be transmitted is 'ridden' on a high-frequency carrier wave (by changing its amplitude, frequency, or phase), and then taken down at the receiving end.
一个正弦载波有三个可以改变的量：**幅度**（调幅，AM）、**频率**（调频，: A sinusoidal carrier wave has three quantities that can be changed: **amplitude** (amplitude modulation, AM), **frequency** (frequency modulation, FM), and **phase** (phase modulation). Digital communication combines them: for example, **QAM** (quadrature amplitude modulation) changes both amplitude and phase simultaneously, arranging 16, 64, or even 4096 points on a constellation diagram, with each point representing a string of bits—4096-QAM can transmit 12 bits at once. The cleaner the signal, the denser the points can be arranged. 'Demodulation' is taking information back from the carrier wave.
调幅改变波的强弱，调频改变波的快慢；调频抗干扰强、音质好。: Amplitude modulation changes the strength of the wave; frequency modulation changes its speed; frequency modulation is more resistant to interference and has better sound quality.
**调幅**（AM）广播用中波和短波，信号能传很远，晚上甚至能收到上千公里外的电: **Amplitude** (AM) broadcasting uses medium and short waves; signals can travel very far, and even stations over a thousand kilometers away can be received at night, but they have high static and average sound quality. **Frequency** (FM) broadcasting uses very high frequencies around 88–108 MHz; each station occupies a wider frequency band, offering better sound quality and stereo capability, but it generally propagates only in straight lines with coverage of tens of kilometers.
1906 年加拿大发明家费森登（Reginald Fessenden）被认为用调: In 1906, Canadian inventor Reginald Fessenden is considered to have conducted one of the earliest voice broadcasts using amplitude modulation. In 1933, American Edwin Armstrong obtained a patent for frequency modulation but exhausted his property due to patent litigation with RCA Company and committed suicide in 1954.
同一段声音信号，调幅改变载波的\"高低\"，调频改变载波的\"疏密\"。: For the same audio signal, amplitude modulation changes the 'height' of the carrier wave, while frequency modulation changes its 'density'.
一个电台同时向无数收音机播出，第一种真正的大众电子媒体。: A single radio station broadcasts to countless radios simultaneously; this was the first true mass electronic media.
电台把节目调制到分配给它的频率上，用大功率发射机和高塔天线播出；听众只需一台收音: Radio stations modulate programs onto frequencies assigned to them and broadcast using high-power transmitters and tall antenna towers; listeners only need one radio and tune to the corresponding frequency. Commercial stations profit from advertising, while public stations are funded by governments or listeners.
1920 年 11 月 2 日美国匹兹堡的 KDKA 电台播报总统选举结果，常被: On November 2, 1920, KDKA in Pittsburgh, USA, reported the results of a presidential election, often considered the beginning of commercial radio broadcasting. In 1923, China's first radio station opened in Shanghai.
让许多路信号共享同一条线路或频段：按时间、频率、码或波长切分。: Allow many signals to share the same line or frequency band: divide them by time, frequency, code, or wavelength.
早期的 ASCII 只有 128 个字符，只够英文；各国又各自制定编码（如中国的: Early ASCII contained only 128 characters, sufficient only for English. Various countries developed their own encoding schemes (such as China's GB2312 and Taiwan's Big5), which were incompatible with each other, frequently resulting in "garbled text". Unicode assigns a unique number to each character (a "code point"). The Unicode 18.0 version released in September 2026 recorded 172,808 characters, more than half of which are Chinese characters, including various ancient scripts and emoji symbols. The most common storage method, UTF-8, represents one character using 1 to 4 bytes and is fully compatible with ASCII.
天线中来回振荡的电流会向空间辐射电磁波；反过来，经过的电磁波会在天线中感应出电流: Currents oscillating back and forth in an antenna radiate electromagnetic waves into space; conversely, electromagnetic waves passing through induce a current in the antenna ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]). When the length of the antenna matches the wavelength, the current oscillation is strongest and efficiency is highest ([[p:wave|resonance]]).
最简单的半波偶极子天线是两根总长约为半个波长的导线：调频广播约 100 兆赫，波: The simplest half-wave dipole antenna consists of two wires with a total length of approximately half a wavelength: for FM broadcasting at about 100 MHz, the wavelength is 3 meters, so the antenna is about 1.5 meters long; for mobile phone signals with wavelengths of only a few centimeters, antennas can be hidden inside the device body. Dish-shaped antennas concentrate the beam in one direction like a flashlight; [[phased-array|Phased-array antenna]] can change the pointing direction electronically.
天线是一切无线通信的\"嘴和耳朵\"（见 [[radio]]、[[mimo]]、: Antennas are the "mouth and ears" of all wireless communications (see [[radio]], [[mimo]], [[radar]]).
把低频的声音或数据\"装\"到高频载波上，就能用小天线高效发射，不同电台各用不同: By "loading" low-frequency sound or data onto a high-frequency carrier wave, efficient transmission can be achieved with small antennas, and different radio stations use different carrier waves to avoid interference ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]). Changing which characteristic of the carrier is modified and how determines how much information can be transmitted and its resistance to interference ([[p:info|Information theory]]).
20 世纪初人们用调幅传送语音；1933 年阿姆斯特朗取得调频专利；1960 年: In the early 20th century, people used amplitude modulation to transmit voice; Armstrong obtained a patent for frequency modulation in 1933; after the 1960s, digital modulation developed alongside [[modem|Modem]] and digital communications.
Wi-Fi、4G/5G、光纤都靠越来越复杂的调制把更多比特塞进有限的频谱（见 [: Wi-Fi, 4G/5G, and fiber optics all rely on increasingly complex modulation to pack more bits into limited spectrum (see [[am-fm]], [[cellular-network]]).
调幅把声音的强弱变成载波幅度的大小，调频把它变成载波频率的快慢（[[p:emwa: Amplitude modulation converts the strength of sound into the magnitude of the carrier wave's amplitude; frequency modulation converts it into the speed of the carrier wave's frequency ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]); noise generated by lightning and appliances mainly affects amplitude, so frequency modulation is naturally more resistant to interference.
调频让广播音乐有了高保真的音质；调幅和调频的思想至今仍是无线通信的入门课（见 [: Frequency modulation enabled high-fidelity audio quality for broadcast music; the concepts of amplitude modulation and frequency modulation remain fundamental courses in wireless communications today (see [[modulation]], [[radio-broadcasting]]).
电磁波向四面八方传播，一个发射台能同时被范围内所有接收机收到，多一个听众不增加任: Electromagnetic waves propagate in all directions; a single transmitter station can be received by all receivers within its range simultaneously, adding no additional cost for each extra listener ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]], [[p:network|network]]).
广播是第一种真正的电子大众媒体，罗斯福的\"炉边谈话\"、战时动员和流行音乐都借: Broadcasting was the first true electronic mass media; Franklin D. Roosevelt's "Fireside Chat", wartime mobilization, and popular music all spread to thousands of homes through it; its model was later inherited by [[television|Television]] (see [[radio]], [[transistor-radio]]).
一条线路或一个频段的容量远大于一路信号的需要（[[p:info|信息论]]）；把: The capacity of a single line or frequency band is far greater than the needs of a single signal ([[p:info|Information theory]]); by slicing it according to time, frequency, coding, or color of light, many signals can share simultaneously.
**频分复用**像收音机里的不同电台，各占一段频率；**时分复用**像轮流发言，: **Frequency Division Multiplexing** is like different radio stations in a radio receiver, each occupying a segment of frequency; **Time Division Multiplexing** is like taking turns speaking, where each signal takes turns occupying extremely short time slices; **Code Division Multiplexing** gives each signal a unique "secret code" (3G used it); **Wavelength Division Multiplexing** allows different colored lasers to share a single fiber optic cable.
1910 年代长途电话线路开始用频分复用；1962 年美国贝尔系统投入数字时分复: In the 1910s, long-distance telephone lines began using frequency division multiplexing; in 1962, the American Bell System invested in digital time-division multiplexing T1 lines; in the 1990s, dense wavelength division multiplexing caused fiber optic capacity to grow by hundreds of times.
复用让一根光缆、一段频谱承载成千上万路通信，是通信成本不断下降的关键（见 [[f: Multiplexing allows a single optical cable or segment of spectrum to carry thousands or tens of thousands of communication channels, which is a key factor in the continuous decline of communication costs (see [[fiber-optic]], [[cellular-network]]).
用一串相距几十公里的微波铁塔接力传送电话和电视信号。: Use a series of microwave towers spaced tens of kilometers apart to relay telephone and television signals.
微波频率高、能携带大量信息，但基本只走直线，会被地球曲面挡住（[[p:emwav: Microwave frequencies are high and can carry large amounts of information, but they essentially only travel in straight lines and are blocked by the curvature of the Earth ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]); by relaying station-to-station within line-of-sight ranges, one can cross continents.
每隔约 40–50 公里在山顶或高塔上建一座中继站，碟形或喇叭形天线对准相邻站点: Build a relay station on top of a mountain or high tower every approximately 40–50 kilometers; dish or horn-shaped antennas aim at adjacent stations to receive, amplify, and then transmit to the next station. A single microwave line can simultaneously carry thousands of telephone channels or several television channels without digging trenches or burying cables along the route.
1951 年美国 AT&T 开通横贯大陆的 TD-2 微波中继线路，杜鲁门总统的: In 1951, American AT&T opened the TD-2 microwave relay line crossing the continent; President Truman's speech was transmitted nationwide via it, achieving live television broadcasting across the entire United States.
微波中继让全国性的电视网和长途电话成为可能，后来逐步被光纤和卫星取代，但仍用于偏: Microwave relays made national television networks and long-distance telephony possible; they were gradually replaced by fiber optics and satellites but are still used in remote areas and for high-frequency financial trading (see [[communication-satellite]], [[television]]).
在太空中转发信号的\"高塔\"；静止轨道卫星能覆盖地球三分之一。: The "towers" that relay signals in space; geostationary orbit satellites can cover one-third of the Earth.
卫星的水平速度足够大时，会一直绕着地球\"往下掉\"却掉不下来（[[p:grav: When a satellite's horizontal speed is sufficiently large, it will continuously orbit around the Earth, "falling down" but not falling ([[p:gravity|Gravitation & orbital mechanics]]); orbiting at an altitude of about 36,000 kilometers takes exactly 24 hours to complete one circle, synchronizing with Earth's rotation, appearing motionless from the ground; transmitting electromagnetic waves from such a high "tower" can cover approximately one-third of the Earth ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]).
地面站把信号发上卫星，卫星上的转发器把它放大、换个频率再发回地面。静止轨道卫星三: Ground stations transmit signals to satellites; transponders on the satellite amplify them and change their frequency before retransmitting to the ground. Three geostationary orbit satellites can cover the entire globe except the polar regions, suitable for live television broadcasting, but there is about a half-second round-trip delay. Low Earth Orbit satellites are only hundreds of kilometers above the ground with small delays, but must use a large constellation of satellites to achieve continuous coverage.
1945 年科幻作家克拉克（Arthur C. Clarke）提出用三颗静止卫星: In 1945, science fiction author Arthur C. Clarke proposed the concept of achieving global communication using three geostationary satellites. In July 1962, the American "Telstar 1" first achieved trans-Atlantic live television broadcasting; in 1964, "Syncom 3" became the first geostationary communications satellite, broadcasting the Tokyo Olympics.
通信卫星让全球电视直播、远洋通信和偏远地区通信成为可能（见 [[geostati: Communications satellites make global television broadcasts, long-distance communications, and communications in remote areas possible (see [[geostationary-orbit]], [[satellite-internet]]).
静止轨道卫星高约 36000 公里、三颗覆盖全球但延迟大；低轨卫星高几百公里、延: Geostationary orbit satellites are approximately 36,000 km high; three such satellites can cover the globe but suffer from high latency. Low-orbit satellites are hundreds of kilometers high and have low latency, but require thousands or tens of thousands of satellites to form a network.
用数千颗低轨卫星组网提供全球宽带，星链（Starlink）是代表。: Providing global broadband using a constellation of thousands of low-orbit satellites is exemplified by Starlink.
卫星越低，信号往返越快、所需功率越小，但每颗能覆盖的范围也越小，必须用大量卫星组: The lower the satellite orbit, the faster the signal round-trip time and the less power required; however, each satellite covers a smaller area, necessitating a large network of satellites to relay signals ([[p:gravity|orbits]]). Only when both satellites and launches achieve mass production and low costs can such constellations be built ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]], [[p:network|network]]).
低轨星座的卫星在约 300–600 公里高度运行，每颗只在头顶停留几分钟，用户终: Low-orbit constellation satellites operate at an altitude of approximately 300–600 km, staying overhead for only a few minutes per pass. User terminals use a Phased-array antenna ([[phased-array|Phased-array antenna]]) to electronically track and automatically switch to the next satellite. Satellites relay data to each other via laser links; data can "run" in space for a segment before landing, covering oceans and deserts. Latency can be reduced to tens of milliseconds, approaching ground-based broadband speeds.
2019 年 5 月 SpaceX 发射第一批 60 颗星链卫星；借助可回收的: In May 2019, SpaceX launched its first batch of 60 Starlink satellites. Leveraging the reusable Falcon 9 rocket ([[reusable-rocket|Falcon 9 rocket]]) for rapid deployment, according to astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell's statistics, approximately 11,000 satellites were in orbit as of August 2026. SpaceX reported that user numbers exceeded 9 million by the end of 2025. Constellations from Amazon and multiple Chinese entities are also under deployment.
卫星互联网让偏远地区、船舶、飞机甚至战场都能接入宽带，也带来了天文观测干扰和太空: Satellite internet enables broadband access for remote areas, ships, aircraft, and even battlefields, but it has also raised concerns regarding astronomical observation interference and space debris (see [[communication-satellite]]).
控制许多小天线发射的时间差，让波束不转动天线就能电子扫描。: Controlling the time difference of emissions from many small antennas allows electronic beam scanning without physically rotating the antenna.
许多小天线同时发射，如果让每一个依次晚一点点，各自发出的波在某个方向上正好波峰对: When many small antennas transmit simultaneously, if each is delayed slightly relative to the others, their emitted waves will constructively interfere in a specific direction (where peaks align with peaks) and destructively interfere elsewhere ([[p:wave|Interference]]). By adjusting these delays, the beam can be steered without moving the antenna itself.
1905 年布劳恩演示了用多根天线控制无线电波的方向；二战期间相控阵用于雷达；1: In 1905, Braun demonstrated controlling the direction of radio waves using multiple antennas; during World War II, phased arrays were used for radar; starting in the 1960s, large phased-array radars were employed for missile warning. Today, Starlink user terminals also incorporate a flat-panel phased-array antenna.
相控阵是现代军用雷达、卫星终端和 5G 基站波束成形的核心（见 [[radar]: Phased arrays are central to modern military radar, satellite terminals, and beamforming at 5G base stations (see [[radar]], [[satellite-internet]], [[mimo]]).
先把各种频率的信号变到一个固定的中频再放大，让收音机灵敏又好调台，至今仍是接收机: First, various frequency signals are converted to a fixed intermediate frequency before amplification, making radios more sensitive and easier to tune; this remains the basic structure of receivers to this day.
两个不同频率的信号混合时会产生它们的\"差频\"（[[p:wave|干涉]]）；: When two signals of different frequencies mix, they produce their "difference frequency" ([[p:wave|Interference]]); by mixing any radio station's signal with a tunable local oscillator signal, it can be uniformly shifted to a fixed intermediate frequency.
超外差接收机先用混频器把收到的信号变到固定的中频（调幅收音机常用 465 千赫）: Superheterodyne receivers first use a mixer to convert received signals to a fixed intermediate frequency (AM radios commonly use 465 kHz), then process them using a set of filters and amplifiers optimized specifically for this frequency. Regardless of which station is received, the subsequent circuitry remains unchanged, greatly improving selectivity and sensitivity.
1918 年美国的阿姆斯特朗（Edwin Armstrong）在一战期间发明超外: In 1918, Edwin Armstrong in the United States invented the superheterodyne receiver during World War I; Lévy in France and Shockley in Germany also independently proposed similar schemes.
从 1930 年代的收音机到今天的手机、雷达和卫星接收机，绝大多数接收机都沿用超: From radios of the 1930s to today's mobile phones, radars, and satellite receivers, the vast majority of receivers continue to use the superheterodyne structure or its variants (see [[radio]], [[modulation]]).
激光在比头发还细的玻璃丝里靠全反射传输，一根光纤可承载数百万路通话。: Light is transmitted within a glass fiber thinner than a hair via total internal reflection; a single optical fiber can carry millions of telephone calls.
光从玻璃射向空气时，只要入射角足够大，就会被全部反射回来，一点也不漏出去（全反射: When light travels from glass to air, if the angle of incidence is sufficiently large, it will be totally reflected back with no loss (total internal reflection, [[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]]); the frequency of light is tens of thousands of times higher than that of radio waves, allowing it to carry a much larger information volume ([[p:info|Information theory]]).
光纤中心是直径约 9 微米（单模）的纤芯，外面包着折射率稍低的包层，总直径约 1: The core of an optical fiber has a diameter of approximately 9 micrometers (single-mode), surrounded by a cladding with a slightly lower refractive index; the total diameter is approximately 125 micrometers, comparable to the width of a hair. The transmitter uses a laser to convert electrical signals into rapid light pulses that propagate through the core; the receiver uses a photodiode to convert the light back into an electrical signal.
关键在于玻璃极其纯净：现代光纤每公里只损失约 4% 的光。再配上 [[optic: The key lies in the extreme purity of the glass: modern optical fibers lose only about 4% of light per kilometer. Coupled with [[optical-amplifier|Optical amplifier (EDFA)]] (an optical amplifier, EDFA) replenishing light every tens of kilometers and [[multiplexing|wavelength-division multiplexing]] (wavelength-division multiplexing) allowing dozens or hundreds of colors of light to transmit simultaneously, the capacity of a single fiber pair can reach tens of terabits per second.
1966 年在英国工作的华裔科学家高锟（Charles Kao）与霍克汉姆发表论: In 1966, Chinese scientist Charles Kao working in the UK and Hawking published a paper indicating that if impurities in glass are removed, optical fiber loss can be reduced below 20 dB/km, sufficient for communications. In 1970, Maier, Keck, and Schultz of Corning Glass Works in the United States produced the first fiber meeting this standard. Kao received the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physics and is hailed as the "father of optical fiber".
光纤是互联网的\"大动脉\"：城市之间、大洲之间的数据几乎全部走光纤，[[sub: Optical fibers are the "arteries" of the Internet: data between cities and continents almost entirely travels via optical fibers, with [[submarine-cable|Submarine communications cable]] (Submarine communications cable) carrying the vast majority of intercontinental traffic. Fiber-to-the-home has raised household internet speeds to the gigabit level (see [[broadband]]).
光纤通过全反射把光\"关\"在纤芯里传输；波分复用让多种颜色的光在同一根光纤里同: Optical fibers transmit light by "trapping" it within the core via total internal reflection; wavelength-division multiplexing allows multiple colors of light to be transmitted simultaneously on a single fiber.
铺在海底的光缆承载了绝大部分洲际数据流量，远多于卫星。: Optical cables laid on the ocean floor carry the vast majority of intercontinental data traffic, far exceeding that of satellites.
光纤损耗极低（[[p:optics|全反射]]），再每隔几十公里用水下中继器放大: Fiber-optic communication exhibits extremely low loss ([[p:optics|total internal reflection]]); every few tens of kilometers, an underwater repeater amplifies the signal, allowing it to cross oceans spanning over ten thousand kilometers.
海底光缆中心只有几对到几十对光纤，外面层层包裹钢丝、铜管和聚乙烯，靠近岸边的部分: The center of a submarine cable contains only a few to dozens of optical fibers. Outside, they are wrapped in layers of steel wire, copper pipes, and polyethylene; the section near shore is further reinforced with armor plating to prevent damage from fishing boats and anchors. Repeaters are remotely powered by copper conductors within the cable from land-based power sources. The laying vessel deploys the cable while sailing, with the deep-sea segment resting directly on the sea floor.
1988 年第一条跨大西洋光缆 TAT-8 投入使用。据 TeleGeograp: In 1988, the first transatlantic optical cable, TAT-8, went into service. According to TeleGeography, as of 2026, approximately 600 submarine communication systems are in operation globally, with technology companies such as Google and Meta becoming major investors.
海底光缆承载了 99% 以上的洲际数据流量，卫星只占很小一部分；它的安全也因此成: Submarine cables carry over 99% of intercontinental data traffic; satellites account for only a small fraction. Consequently, the security of these cables has become a focal point for nations (see [[fiber-optic]], [[transatlantic-cable]]).
从拨号上网到 DSL、有线电视网再到光纤入户，家庭网速提升了上万倍。: From dial-up internet to DSL, cable networks, and finally fiber-to-the-home, household network speeds have increased by tens of thousands of times.
信道能传多快取决于带宽和信噪比（[[p:info|信息论]]）；电话线本来只为: The speed at which a channel can transmit data depends on bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio ([[p:info|Information theory]]); telephone lines were originally designed for 4-kilohertz voice, but by using higher frequency bands, better modulation, or simply switching to fiber optics, speeds can increase thousands or tens of thousands of times.
**拨号上网**用 [[modem|调制解调器]] 把数据变成声音走电话线，最高: **Dial-up internet** used a Modem ([[modem|Modem]]) to convert data into sound traveling over telephone lines, reaching a maximum of 56 kilobits per second; **ADSL** utilizes high-frequency bands on telephone copper lines beyond the voice range, reaching several megabits to tens of megabits; **Cable networks** use coaxial cables, reaching hundreds of megabits; **Fiber-to-the-home** (FTTH) directly brings fiber optics into homes, achieving gigabits or even ten-gigabits per second. Fixed wireless access replaces entry cables with 5G signals.
1990 年代末 ADSL 和有线电视宽带开始大规模商用；2000 年代起日本、: In the late 1990s, ADSL and cable broadband began large-scale commercialization; starting in the 2000s, Japan and South Korea pioneered the promotion of fiber-to-the-home, while China became the country with the most fiber-optic users globally during the 2010s.
宽带让视频、在线游戏和云服务进入家庭（见 [[fiber-optic]]、[[i: Broadband brought video, online gaming, and cloud services into homes (see [[fiber-optic]], [[internet]]).
在光纤里掺入铒元素，用泵浦激光直接放大微弱的光信号，不必先转成电，让跨洋光缆成为: By doping optical fibers with erbium elements and using pump lasers to directly amplify weak light signals without first converting them to electricity, it became possible to build transoceanic cables.
受激辐射：处于高能级的原子被一个光子\"碰\"一下，会放出一个一模一样的光子（[: Stimulated emission: an atom in a high energy level, when "hit" by a photon, emits an identical photon ([[p:levels|Quantized energy levels]]); by pumping a large number of erbium ions into the high energy level, weak light passing through is replicated and amplified along the way.
掺铒光纤放大器（EDFA）是一段十几米长、掺了铒元素的特殊光纤。980 或 14: An Erbium-Doped Fiber Amplifier (EDFA) is a special fiber optic segment several tens of meters long, doped with erbium elements. 980 or 1480 nanometer pump lasers excite the erbium ions; when signal light near 1550 nanometers passes through, it triggers stimulated emission, directly amplifying the light without first converting it to an electrical signal. It can simultaneously amplify dozens of wavelengths, making it a natural partner for wavelength-division multiplexing ([[multiplexing|wavelength-division multiplexing]]).
1987 年英国南安普顿大学的佩恩（David Payne）团队和美国贝尔实验室: In 1987, David Payne's team at the University of Southampton in the UK and Emmanuel Desurvire's team at Bell Labs in the US independently demonstrated practical erbium-doped fiber amplifiers.
它让跨洋光缆不再需要昂贵复杂的光电中继器，光纤容量随之爆发式增长（见 [[fib: It made transoceanic cables no longer require expensive and complex optoelectronic repeaters; consequently, fiber-optic capacity experienced explosive growth (see [[fiber-optic]], [[submarine-cable]]).
摩托罗拉的库珀打出第一通手持移动电话，电话从\"拴在墙上\"变为\"随身携带\": Motorola's Cooper made the first handheld mobile phone call, transforming the telephone from "tethered to a wall" to "carried in hand."
电话不需要线，只要让手机和附近的基站之间用无线电通信（[[p:emwave|电磁: The telephone does not require wires; it only requires that the mobile phone communicates via radio waves ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]) with nearby base stations, which then connect to the fixed telephone network. The true challenge is not "whether wireless is possible," but how to allow thousands or tens of thousands of people to make calls simultaneously on limited frequencies—the answer lies in the Cellular network ([[cellular-network|Cellular network]]).
1973 年 4 月 3 日，摩托罗拉工程师库珀（Martin Cooper）在: On April 3, 1973, Motorola engineer Cooper (Martin Cooper) made the first handheld mobile phone call from a prototype weighing approximately 1.1 kilograms on New York City streets to colleagues at his competitor, Bell Labs. In 1983, Motorola launched its first commercial handheld mobile phone, the DynaTAC 8000X, priced at $3,995; it required 10 hours of charging for only about 30 minutes of talk time and was jokingly called a "brick."
电话从\"拴在墙上、属于一个家庭\"变成\"随身携带、属于一个人\"，人们从此可: The telephone transformed from "tethered to a wall, belonging to one family" to "carried in hand, belonging to an individual," allowing people to be found anywhere at any time. Feature phones became widespread in developing countries during the 2000s, enabling billions of people ([[smartphone|Smartphone]]) to own a phone for the first time; subsequently, it was transformed into a pocket computer (see [[sms]], [[gsm-2g]]).
移动电话的演进：从 1973 年的\"砖头\"原型，到功能手机，再到智能手机。: Evolution of mobile telephony: from the 1973 "brick" prototype, to feature phones, to smartphones.
把地区划成许多小\"蜂窝\"，相隔够远的小区重复使用同一频率，容量随之倍增。: The region is divided into many small "cells"; cells spaced far enough apart repeat use the same frequency, causing capacity to multiply accordingly.
一个频率被一部手机占用后，附近的其他手机就不能再用；但无线电信号会随距离衰减，相: Once a frequency is occupied by one mobile phone, nearby other mobile phones cannot use it; however, radio signals attenuate with distance, so two locations sufficiently far apart can repeat use the same frequency without interfering ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]). Dividing the region into many small "cells" means that the smaller the cell, the more times the same frequency can be reused, causing total capacity to grow exponentially ([[p:scale|scale]], [[p:info|Information theory]]).
每个小区中心有一座基站，相邻小区使用不同的频率组，隔开一两个小区后再重复使用。市: Each cell center has a base station; adjacent cells use different frequency groups, and the same group is repeated after one or two cells are separated. City center cells are only several hundred meters in size, while suburban cells can reach tens of kilometers. When a mobile phone moves from one cell to another, the network automatically **switches** the call to the new base station. All base stations connect to the core network via fiber optics or microwaves.
1947 年贝尔实验室的林（Douglas Ring）和扬（W. Rae You: In 1947, Lin (Douglas Ring) and Yang (W. Rae Young) at Bell Labs proposed the concept of a cellular network, but technology at the time could not realize it. In 1979, Japan's NTT opened the world's first commercial cellular network in Tokyo; in 1983, the US AMPS network opened in Chicago.
蜂窝网络：相邻小区用不同频率（不同颜色），相隔较远的小区重复使用同一频率；用户移: Cellular networks: adjacent cells use different frequencies (different colors), while distant cells reuse the same frequency; when a user moves, calls switch automatically between base stations.
第一代数字移动网络标准，带来短信和全球漫游。: The first generation of digital mobile network standards brought SMS and global roaming.
1982 年欧洲成立 GSM 工作组；1991 年 7 月 1 日芬兰前总理霍尔: In 1982, Europe established the GSM working group; on July 1, 1991, Finland's former Prime Minister Hallrik used the GSM network to make the first call.
利用信令通道顺带传送的 160 字符短消息，意外成为全球最流行的通信方式之一。: The 160-character short messages carried incidentally via signaling channels accidentally became one of the most popular communication methods globally.
手机待机时也要和基站交换控制信令，短信就塞在这些信令的空隙里传送，所以单条长度被: Even when idle, phones must exchange control signaling with base stations; SMS is transmitted in these signaling gaps, so each message is limited to 160 English characters (70 Chinese characters). SMS stores and forwards: if the recipient's phone is off, it is first stored at the SMS center and delivered again after the phone turns on.
1984 年德国工程师希勒布兰德（Friedhelm Hillebrand）等人: In 1984, German engineer Friedhelm Hillebrand and others proposed the SMS concept; he reportedly counted on a typewriter and concluded that 160 characters were sufficient to express most meanings. On December 3, 1992, British engineer Neil Papworth sent the first SMS from a computer to a mobile phone: "Merry Christmas".
让手机真正能上网的移动网络，开启移动数据时代。: Mobile networks that truly enabled phones to access the internet opened the mobile data era.
3G 主要采用码分多址（CDMA）技术：所有用户同时使用同一段较宽的频带，各自用: 3G mainly adopted Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) technology: all users simultaneously use a wider band of frequency, distinguished by different spreading codes, like speaking in different languages in a noisy room. Mainstream standards include Europe-led WCDMA, US-led CDMA2000, and China's proposed TD-SCDMA. Rates rose from hundreds of kilobits per second initially to several megabits per second.
2001 年 10 月日本 NTT DoCoMo 推出世界上第一个商用 WCDM: In October 2001, Japan's NTT DoCoMo launched the world's first commercial WCDMA network; China issued 3G licenses in 2009.
全 IP 化的高速移动网络，让手机看视频、移动支付、网约车成为日常。: High-speed mobile networks fully IP-based made video watching, mobile payments, and ride-hailing services daily routines.
LTE 的核心网完全基于 IP，语音也作为数据包传送（VoLTE），不再保留旧的: LTE's core network is fully based on IP; voice is also transmitted as data packets (VoLTE), no longer retaining old circuit switching. Download rates can reach tens to hundreds of megabits per second, latency drops to tens of milliseconds, and HD video viewing and video calls are smooth.
2009 年 12 月北欧运营商 TeliaSonera 在斯德哥尔摩和奥斯陆开: In December 2009, Nordic operator TeliaSonera opened the world's first commercial LTE networks in Stockholm and Oslo; China issued 4G licenses in 2013.
更高速率、更低延迟、更多连接的移动网络，面向工业和物联网。: A mobile network offering higher data rates, lower latency, and more connections, designed for industrial and IoT applications.
信道容量与带宽成正比（[[p:info|信息论]]），而越高的频段越容易找到大块: Channel capacity is proportional to bandwidth ([[p:info|Information theory]]), and higher frequency bands make it easier to find large blocks of idle bandwidth; however, high-frequency signals attenuate quickly and have poor wall penetration, so multiple antennas are used to direct energy like a flashlight toward the user ([[p:wave|Interference]]).
5G 同时用中低频（如 3.5 吉赫，兼顾覆盖与容量）和毫米波（24 吉赫以上，: 5G uses both mid-low frequencies (such as 3.5 GHz, balancing coverage and capacity) and millimeter waves (above 24 GHz, offering extremely large bandwidth but very limited coverage). Base stations employ massive MIMO ([[mimo|MIMO & beamforming]]), with a single antenna panel integrating over 64 transmit/receive units. 5G has three target scenarios: enhanced mobile broadband (peak rates of several gigabits per second), low latency high-reliability communications (approximately 1 millisecond, targeting industrial control), and massive IoT connectivity (millions of connections per square kilometer).
2019 年 4 月韩国和美国率先推出 5G 商用服务，同年中国发放 5G 牌照: In April 2019, South Korea and the United States were the first to launch commercial 5G services; in the same year, China issued 5G licenses. According to Ericsson, global 5G users reached 3.1 billion in Q1 2026.
5G 在消费端主要带来更快的网速，在工厂、港口、矿山的工业应用正在逐步展开（见: For consumers, 5G primarily brings faster internet speeds, while industrial applications in factories, ports, and mines are gradually expanding (see [[4g-lte]], [[iot]], [[6g]]).
正在研究的下一代移动网络，探索太赫兹、通感一体和天地一体化。: The next-generation mobile network under research explores terahertz frequencies, integrated communication and sensing, and terrestrial-satellite integration.
每一代移动通信都在向更高频段、更多天线和更智能的网络推进（[[p:emwave|: Each generation of mobile communications advances toward higher frequencies, more antennas, and smarter networks ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]).
6G 研究的方向包括：太赫兹等更高频段以获取更大带宽；**通感一体化**，让基站: Research directions for 6G include: higher frequency bands such as terahertz to achieve greater bandwidth; **integrated communication and sensing**, allowing base stations to perceive the surrounding environment like a radar while communicating; **terrestrial-satellite integration**, merging satellite networks with ground cellular networks into a single network; and deeply embedding artificial intelligence into network design and operations.
国际电信联盟在 2023 年发布了 6G（IMT-2030）的框架建议。3GPP: The International Telecommunication Union released framework recommendations for 6G (IMT-2030) in 2023. 3GPP plans to establish the first batch of 6G specifications in version 21 of its standards, with core technical specifications expected to be frozen by the end of 2028; the industry generally expects commercialization to begin around 2030—all of these are **plans** as of 2026.
6G 的具体形态和杀手级应用仍在探索中（见 [[5g]]、[[satellite: The specific form and killer applications of 6G are still under exploration (see [[5g]], [[satellite-internet]]).
用多根天线同时收发、把信号像手电筒一样对准用户，在同一频段塞进更多数据。: Using multiple antennas for simultaneous transmission and reception, directing signals like a flashlight toward the user, and packing more data into the same frequency band.
多根天线同时发送时，信号经过不同路径反射到达接收端，每条路径都略有不同；用数学方: When multiple antennas transmit simultaneously, signals reflect via different paths to reach the receiver, with each path being slightly different; mathematical methods separate them, allowing multiple data streams to be transmitted on the same frequency ([[p:info|Information theory]]). Adjusting the phase of each antenna can also concentrate energy toward a specific user ([[p:wave|Interference]]).
MIMO（多输入多输出）在收发两端都用多根天线。**空间复用**让多路数据流同时: MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) uses multiple antennas at both the transmit and receive ends. **Spatial multiplexing** allows multiple data streams to travel through different spatial paths simultaneously, increasing rates exponentially; **beamforming** directs signals like a flashlight toward the user, improving signal strength and reducing interference; **multi-user MIMO** enables the base station to send a separate beam for each of multiple users simultaneously.
1990 年代中期，斯坦福大学的保罗拉吉（Arogyaswami Paulraj: In the mid-1990s, Arogyaswami Paulraj from Stanford University and Gerard Foschini from Bell Labs laid the theoretical and experimental foundations for MIMO.
MIMO 是 Wi-Fi 和 4G/5G 速率大幅提升的关键（见 [[5g]]、: MIMO was a key factor in the significant rate improvements of Wi-Fi and 4G/5G (see [[5g]], [[wifi]], [[phased-array]]).
无线电频率是有限的公共资源，由政府分配或拍卖，越低频传得越远、越高频带宽越大。: Radio frequencies are limited public resources allocated or auctioned by governments; lower frequencies travel farther, while higher frequencies offer greater bandwidth.
电磁波按频率排列成谱，同一时间、同一地点、同一频率只能被一个发射者有效使用，否则: Electromagnetic waves are arranged in a spectrum by frequency; at any given time and location, only one transmitter can effectively use a specific frequency, otherwise they interfere with each other ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]); low frequencies have strong diffraction and travel far, while high frequencies offer large bandwidth.
无线电频谱由各国政府按用途划分给广播、移动通信、卫星、雷达、航空和军用等。移动通: Radio spectrum is divided by national governments for broadcasting, mobile communications, satellites, radar, aviation, and military use. Mobile communication spectrum is allocated to operators via auction or administrative assignment, often costing billions of dollars. Frequencies used by Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, such as 2.4 GHz, are unlicensed public bands accessible to anyone, subject to power limits.
1959 年经济学家科斯（Ronald Coase）提出用市场拍卖分配频谱；19: Economist Ronald Coase proposed using market auctions for spectrum allocation in 1959; the US Federal Communications Commission conducted its first spectrum auction in 1994.
频谱是移动通信最稀缺的资源，每一代网络都伴随着新频段的划分和争夺（见 [[cel: Spectrum is the most scarce resource in mobile communications, with each new generation of networks accompanied by the division and contestation of new frequency bands (see [[cellular-network]], [[5g]]).
把电脑、相机、GPS、传感器装进一块触摸屏，iPhone（2007）开启了移动互: Integrating computers, cameras, GPS, sensors into a single touchscreen device; iPhone (2007) launched the mobile internet era.
手机一旦有了足够强的通用处理器、触摸屏和随时在线的网络，就变成了一台可以安装任意: Once a smartphone possesses a sufficiently powerful general-purpose processor, a touchscreen, and always-online network access, it becomes a pocket computer capable of installing any software ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]); with more users, developers are more willing to write applications for it, and more applications attract even more users ([[p:network|Network effects]]). Its adoption followed a typical S-curve: becoming ubiquitous within years ([[p:scurve|S-curve]]).
一部智能手机把许多原本独立的设备集成进一块玻璃里：[[soc|片上系统]]（CP: A smartphone integrates many previously independent devices into a single piece of glass: [[soc|System on a chip (SoC)]] (CPU, GPU, AI units, baseband), large-capacity flash storage, multi-point [[touchscreen|Touchscreen]], multiple cameras, GPS, accelerometers and gyroscopes, fingerprint or facial recognition, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, NFC, and lithium batteries. The operating system (iOS, Android, etc.) manages these hardware components, while [[app-store|App store]] allows third-party developers to distribute software. The value of a smartphone increasingly comes from software and services rather than the hardware itself.
1994 年 IBM 推出的 Simon 常被称为第一部智能手机；黑莓、诺基亚塞: IBM's Simon launched in 1994 is often called the first smartphone; BlackBerry and Nokia Symbian phones were popular in the 2000s. In January 2007, Steve Jobs released the iPhone, which went on sale in June, redefining the phone with a full-screen multi-point touchscreen and a complete web browser; in 2008, the first Android phone, HTC Dream, launched, and Android subsequently became the most widely installed operating system globally.
智能手机是人类历史上普及最快的技术之一，全球每年出货十几亿部。它把相机、地图、钱: Smartphones are one of the fastest-adopted technologies in human history, with over a billion units shipped globally each year. They pack cameras, maps, wallets, televisions, game consoles, music players, and more into our pockets, giving birth to [[mobile-internet|Mobile internet]], [[mobile-payment|Mobile payment]], and [[ride-hailing|Ride-hailing]], while also bringing issues like distraction and privacy concerns.
一部智能手机里集成了哪些东西：片上系统、触摸屏、摄像头、传感器、多种无线电和电池: What a smartphone integrates: System on Chip (SoC), touch screen, camera, sensors, multiple radio interfaces, and battery.
基于 IEEE 802.11 标准的无线局域网，让设备无需网线接入网络。: A wireless local area network based on the IEEE 802.11 standard allows devices to connect to the network without physical Ethernet cables.
在免许可的公共频段上，用统一的无线标准让设备与附近的接入点通信（[[p:emwa: On unlicensed public frequency bands, a unified wireless standard enables devices to communicate with nearby access points ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]], [[p:standard|Standardization]]); multiple devices take turns "listening before talking" to avoid mutual conflicts.
Wi-Fi 路由器（接入点）通过网线或光纤连到互联网，在 2.4、5 或 6 吉: Wi-Fi routers (access points) connect to the Internet via Ethernet or fiber optics, communicating wirelessly with phones and computers on 2.4, 5, or 6 gigahertz bands, typically covering a range of tens of meters. Each generation improves speed and efficiency: Wi-Fi 4 (802.11n) introduced multiple antennas; Wi-Fi 6 improved the efficiency of simultaneous multi-device access; Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) can aggregate 320 megahertz bandwidth, with theoretical peak speeds exceeding 40 gigabits per second. "Wi-Fi" is merely a trademark name and not an abbreviation for any English word.
1997 年 IEEE 发布 802.11 标准；澳大利亚联邦科学与工业研究组织: IEEE released the 802.11 standard in 1997; John O'Sullivan's team at Australia's Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) made significant contributions to subsequent versions of this patent-protected technology. The Wi-Fi Alliance was founded in 1999 and launched this brand. The Wi-Fi 7 standard was approved in 2024 and officially released in 2025.
Wi-Fi 承载了家庭和办公室里大部分的上网流量，让笔记本、手机和各种智能设备摆: Wi-Fi carries the majority of internet traffic in homes and offices, allowing laptops, phones, and various smart devices to disconnect from Ethernet cables (see [[ethernet]], [[mimo]]).
短距离、低功耗的无线连接标准，用于耳机、手表和外设。: A short-range, low-power wireless connection standard used for headphones, watches, and peripherals.
用很小的功率在短距离内通信，耗电就极少（[[p:emwave|电磁波]]）；统一: Communicate over very short distances with minimal power consumption ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]); unified standards ensure devices from different manufacturers can pair with each other ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
蓝牙工作在 2.4 吉赫频段，用\"跳频\"技术每秒切换上千次频率，避开 Wi-: Bluetooth operates on the 2.4 gigahertz band, using "frequency hopping" technology to switch frequencies over a thousand times per second to avoid interference from Wi-Fi and microwave ovens. Classic Bluetooth is suitable for audio transmission, with a range of about 10 meters; Low Energy Bluetooth (BLE), launched in 2010, allows smartwatches and sensors to operate for months or even years on a single coin-cell battery.
1994 年瑞典爱立信的哈尔森（Jaap Haartsen）等人开始研发；199: Development began in 1994 by Jaap Haartsen and others at Ericsson in Sweden; the 1.0 specification was released in 1999. The name comes from King Harald Bluetooth, who unified Denmark and Norway in the 10th century, symbolizing the unification of various short-range communication protocols.
蓝牙让无线耳机、键盘、手表和车载电话普及（见 [[wifi]]、[[wearab: Bluetooth made wireless headphones, keyboards, watches, and car phones ubiquitous (see [[wifi]], [[wearable-device]]).
读写器发出电磁场给无源标签供电并读取信息，用于门禁卡、交通卡和手机支付。: Read/write units emit electromagnetic fields to power passive tags and read information, used for access cards, transit cards, and mobile payments.
读写器的线圈产生交变磁场，靠近的标签线圈中感应出电流，足以给标签里的芯片供电并回: The coil in the read/write unit generates an alternating magnetic field; when a nearby tag approaches, current is induced in its coil, sufficient to power the chip inside and transmit data back ([[p:induction|Electromagnetic induction]])—the tag itself does not require a battery.
RFID（射频识别）标签由芯片和天线组成，贴在商品、行李、门禁卡上，读写器在几厘: RFID tags consist of chips and antennas, affixed to products, luggage, and access cards; read/write units can detect them from several centimeters to over ten meters away, capable of scanning large groups simultaneously. NFC (Near Field Communication) is a branch of RFID that operates only within centimeters, deliberately "close" to ensure security; phones can function as both readers and tags for transit, access control, and mobile payments.
二战时的敌我识别系统是 RFID 的前身；1973 年美国的卡杜洛（Mario: The enemy identification system during World War II was the precursor to RFID; Mario Cardullo of the United States obtained the first modern RFID patent in 1973. Nokia, Philips, and Sony formed the NFC Forum in 2004.
从公交卡、身份证、高速公路电子收费到物流仓储，RFID 和 NFC 无处不在（见: From transit cards and ID cards to electronic toll collection on highways and logistics warehousing, RFID and NFC are ubiquitous (see [[mobile-payment]], [[barcode]]).
存放用户身份和密钥的小芯片，让手机号码和手机本身分离。: Small chips storing user identity and keys, separating the mobile phone number from the phone itself.
把用户身份和一把秘密密钥存进一块防篡改的芯片里，网络只需向芯片出题、核对答案就能: Store user identity and a secret key in an anti-tamper chip; the network only needs to pose questions to the chip and verify answers to confirm identity, with the key never leaving the chip ([[p:oneway|One-way functions]]).
SIM 卡里存着国际移动用户识别码和与运营商共享的密钥。入网时，网络发来一个随机: SIM cards store the International Mobile Subscriber Identity and keys shared with operators. When connecting to the network, a random number is sent by the network; the SIM card calculates a result using the key and returns it; the network verifies correctness before allowing access and generates encryption keys for this call. Cards have become smaller: from credit card size to Mini, Micro, and Nano SIM; eSIMs are directly soldered into phones and can be remotely written with operator data.
1991 年德国捷德公司为芬兰运营商 Radiolinja 制造了第一批 SIM: In 1991, Germany's Giesecke+Devrient manufactured the first batch of SIM cards for Finland's Radiolinja operator.
SIM 卡让\"号码\"和\"手机\"分离，用户可以自由换机，也让全球漫游计费成: SIM cards separate "number" from "phone," allowing users to switch devices freely and enabling global roaming billing (see [[gsm-2g]], [[public-key-crypto]]).
把数据切成小包各自寻路、到达后再重组，比独占线路的电路交换更高效、更抗毁。: Cut data into small packets that find their own paths, reassemble after arrival; this is more efficient and resilient than circuit-switched dedicated lines.
通话时大部分时间线路其实是空闲的；与其为每对用户独占一条线，不如把数据切成小包，: Most of the time during a call, the line is actually idle; rather than dedicating a line for each pair of users, cut data into packets so everyone's packets queue and share the line, greatly improving line utilization ([[p:division|division of labor]]). Each packet finds its own path; if a line breaks, it routes around, making the network resilient ([[p:redundancy|redundancy]]).
**电路交换**（传统电话）像包下一整条公路：通话期间这条路只归你，哪怕你一言不: **Circuit switching** (traditional telephony) is like reserving an entire highway: the road belongs to you exclusively during the call, even if you say nothing. **Packet switching** is like mailing packages: it breaks a long letter into many postcards, each written with the recipient's address and a sequence number, then handed over to successive [[router|Router]] stations along the way for forwarding; different postcards may take different routes, and after arrival they are reassembled in order according to their sequence numbers, with any lost ones resent.
代价是\"尽力而为\"：包可能延迟、乱序、丢失，要靠上层协议保证可靠（见 [[t: The cost is "best-effort": circuits may experience delay, disorder, or loss, requiring upper-layer protocols to ensure reliability (see [[tcp-ip]]); the benefit is that the network does not need to care whether you are sending email or video.
1960 年代初，美国兰德公司的巴兰（Paul Baran）为设计能在核打击下幸: In the early 1960s, Paul Baran of RAND Corporation in the United States proposed designing a communication network capable of surviving a nuclear strike by breaking messages into "message blocks" for forwarding across a distributed network; around 1965, Donald Davies at the National Physical Laboratory in the United Kingdom independently proposed the same idea and named it "packet".
分组交换是互联网的基石，[[arpanet|阿帕网]] 首先付诸实践；今天连电话: Packet switching is the cornerstone of the Internet, first implemented with [[arpanet|ARPANET]]; today even telephony has switched to packet switching (see [[voip]]).
常说\"互联网是为了抵御核战争而设计的\"，并不完全准确：巴兰的研究确有此目的，: The common saying that "the Internet was designed to withstand nuclear war" is not entirely accurate: while Baran's research had this purpose, the direct motivation for ARPANET was to allow researchers to share expensive computers.
电路交换为每次通话独占一条线路；分组交换把数据切成包，各自寻路、共享线路，到达后: Circuit switching dedicates an entire line for each call; packet switching cuts data into packets, each finding its own route and sharing lines, then reassembling them upon arrival.
美国国防部资助的第一个分组交换网络，1969 年 10 月发出第一条消息，是互联: The first packet-switched network funded by the U.S. Department of Defense sent its first message in October 1969; it was the precursor to the Internet.
把不同型号的计算机通过分组交换连成一张网，资源就能远程共享，联网的机构越多，网络: Connecting computers of different models into a single network via packet switching enables remote resource sharing; the more institutions that connect, the more useful the network becomes ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
每个站点放一台叫 IMP 的小型计算机专门负责转发数据包，它就是最早的路由器；各: Each site placed a small computer called an IMP (Interface Message Processor) dedicated to forwarding packets; it was the earliest router; hosts at each site only needed to connect to their local IMP. The early protocol was NCP, replaced by TCP/IP in 1983.
美国国防部高级研究计划局（ARPA）资助，罗伯茨（Larry Roberts）主: Funded by DARPA (Advanced Research Projects Agency of the U.S. Department of Defense), designed under Larry Roberts, and manufactured by BBN Company; on October 29, 1969, UCLA sent its first message to SRI (Stanford Research Institute), intending to type "LOGIN", but as soon as "LO" was entered, the system crashed. By the end of 1969, the network had four nodes.
阿帕网验证了分组交换，诞生了电子邮件等最早的网络应用，是 [[internet|: ARPANET validated packet switching and gave birth to early network applications such as email; it was the direct precursor to [[internet|Internet]] (see [[packet-switching]], [[email]]).
互联网的\"普通话\"：IP 负责把包送到地址，TCP 负责确认、重传和排序。: The "common language" of the Internet: IP is responsible for delivery to an address, while TCP is responsible for confirmation, retransmission, and ordering.
不同的网络各有各的线路和规则，只要所有网络都同意一套最小的公共约定——用统一格式: Different networks have their own lines and rules; as long as all networks agree on a minimal set of common conventions—using uniform-format addresses to label packets—they can forward each other's traffic ([[p:standard|Standardization]]). The network itself only manages "best-effort delivery"; confirmation, retransmission, and ordering work that ensure reliability are left to the computers at both ends ([[p:redundancy|Redundancy & error correction]]).
**IP**（网际协议）负责\"寄\"：给每个数据包写上源地址和目的 [[ip-: **IP** (Internet Protocol) is responsible for "mailing": it writes the source address and destination [[ip-address|IP address]] on each data packet, which routers forward hop-by-hop, but it does not guarantee delivery or order. **TCP** (Transmission Control Protocol) is responsible for "reliability": during connection establishment, it first performs a "three-way handshake" ("Can you hear me?" "Yes, and you?" "Yes."); when sending, it numbers each byte; the receiver replies with an acknowledgment after receiving them; if an acknowledgment is not received within a timeout period, the sender retransmits; the receiver reorders according to the sequence numbers. TCP also automatically adjusts sending speed based on packet loss (congestion control).
视频通话、游戏等实时应用则用不确认、不重传的 **UDP**。: Real-time applications such as video calls and games use **UDP** (User Datagram Protocol), which does not require confirmation or retransmission.
这种\"网络简单、两端聪明\"的设计叫**端到端原则**：中间只管搬包，新功能都: This design of "simple network, smart endpoints" is called the **End-to-End Principle**: the middle layer only moves packets; new functions are implemented at the endpoints; anyone can invent new applications without requiring permission from operators.
1974 年 5 月，瑟夫（Vint Cerf）和卡恩（Bob Kahn）发表论: In May 1974, Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn published a paper proposing a protocol for connecting different networks. On January 1, 1983, ARPANET fully switched to TCP/IP; this day is often regarded as the "birthday" of the Internet. The two received the Turing Award in 2004 and are known as the "fathers of the Internet".
TCP/IP 成为全世界网络的\"普通话\"，让互联网从几百台计算机扩展到几百亿: TCP/IP became the "common language" of networks worldwide, allowing the Internet to expand from hundreds of computers to tens of billions of devices (see [[internet]], [[osi-layers]]).
TCP 三次握手与确认重传：先握手建立连接，发送的每段数据都要被确认，丢失的会被: TCP three-way handshake and acknowledgment/retransmission: first, a handshake establishes the connection; each segment of data sent must be acknowledged; lost segments are retransmitted.
用统一协议把无数独立网络连成的\"网络之网\"，没有中心、任何网络都能加入。: Using a unified protocol to connect countless independent networks into a "network of networks" creates no central authority; any network can join.
用一套统一的协议，把无数各自独立管理的网络连在一起，任何网络只要遵守协议就能加入: Using a unified protocol to connect countless independently managed networks together allows any network that complies with the protocol to join without needing central approval ([[p:standard|Standardization]]); the more networks and users that join, the more people each person can connect to and services they can access, making the network more valuable ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
互联网不是\"一张网\"，而是\"网络的网络\"：你的手机先连到运营商网络，运营: The Internet is not "a single network" but a "network of networks": your phone first connects to an operator's network, which then interconnects with other operators' networks, university networks, corporate networks, and cloud service provider networks. Data packets rely on [[tcp-ip|TCP/IP]] for uniform formatting, [[router|Router]] for hop-by-hop forwarding, [[bgp|Border Gateway Protocol (BGP)]] for exchanging routes between major networks, and [[dns|Domain Name System (DNS)]] for translating URLs into addresses.
管理也是分散的：地址和域名由 ICANN 等机构协调，技术标准由开放的互联网工程: Management is also decentralized: addresses and domains are coordinated by organizations such as ICANN; technical standards are formulated by the open Internet Engineering Task Group (IETF) in the form of "Request for Comments" (RFC); no one can "shut down" the entire Internet.
1983 年阿帕网切换到 TCP/IP；1986 年美国国家科学基金会建成 NS: In 1983, ARPANET switched to TCP/IP; in 1986, the U.S. National Science Foundation built the NSFNET backbone network connecting universities across the United States; starting in 1991, commercial networks were allowed to access it; in 1995, NSFNET was decommissioned and the Internet was fully handed over to commercial operation; in 1994, China officially achieved full-function access to the international Internet.
据国际电信联盟，2025 年全球约 60 亿人使用互联网，约占世界人口的 74%: According to the International Telecommunication Union, approximately 6 billion people worldwide use the Internet in 2025, representing about 74% of the global population. The Internet has reshaped communication, commerce, media, and politics (see [[world-wide-web]], [[isp]]).
互联网（Internet）和万维网（Web）不是一回事：互联网是底层的网络，万维: The Internet and the World Wide Web are not the same thing: the Internet is the underlying network, while the World Wide Web is merely one application running on top of it; email and online games do not belong to the World Wide Web.
互联网是\"网络的网络\"：家庭、企业、移动网络经运营商与骨干网互联，各自独立管: The Internet is a 'network of networks': home, enterprise, and mobile networks connect via operators and backbones, each managed independently, communicating through unified protocols.
把通信拆成物理、链路、网络、传输、应用等层，每层只管自己的事。: Communication is split into layers such as physical, link, network, transport, and application; each layer handles only its own responsibilities.
把复杂的通信系统切成上下几层，每层只为上一层提供服务、只使用下一层的服务，接口不: The complex communication system is sliced into upper and lower layers; each layer serves the one above it and uses services from the one below it. When interfaces remain unchanged, any layer can be independently replaced ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]]).
OSI 参考模型分七层：物理层、数据链路层、网络层、传输层、会话层、表示层、应用: The OSI reference model divides into seven layers: physical, data link, network, transport, session, presentation, and application. The actual TCP/IP model used is simpler, often summarized into four or five layers: **Physical and Link Layer** (copper cables, fiber optics, Wi-Fi, Ethernet frames), **Network Layer** (IP, responsible for addressing and routing), **Transport Layer** (TCP/UDP, responsible for end-to-end reliability), and **Application Layer** (HTTP, DNS, email, etc.). When sending data, each layer wraps the data in its own 'envelope' (header); the receiver then strips them off layer by layer—like putting a letter into an envelope, the envelope into a mailbag, and the mailbag onto a truck.
1984 年国际标准化组织发布 OSI 参考模型。它的协议实现在竞争中输给了更早: The International Organization for Standardization published the OSI reference model in 1984. Its protocol implementation lost to TCP/IP, which was adopted earlier, but the seven-layer model has persisted as a framework for teaching and discussion.
分层让 Wi-Fi 可以替换网线、5G 可以替换 4G，而上面的网页和应用一行代: Layering allows Wi-Fi to replace copper cables, 5G to replace 4G, while web pages and applications above require no code changes (see [[tcp-ip]], [[api]]).
数据从上往下逐层\"加信封\"，经物理线路传输后，在接收端逐层拆开。: Data is 'enveloped' layer by layer from top to bottom, transmitted over physical lines, then stripped off layer by layer at the receiver.
局域网的标准接线方式，从办公室到数据中心无处不在。: The standard wiring method for local area networks is ubiquitous from offices to data centers.
统一的接口、线缆和帧格式，让不同厂家的设备都能插上就用（[[p:standard: Unified interfaces, cables, and frame formats allow equipment from different manufacturers to plug in and work immediately ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
每块以太网网卡有一个全球唯一的物理地址（MAC 地址）。数据被装进\"帧\"发送: Each Ethernet network interface card has a globally unique physical address (MAC address). Data is packed into 'frames' for transmission; the frame header contains the destination address. Early on, all computers shared a single coaxial cable, coordinating via 'listen before talk, back off with random delay, then retransmit'; today, switches are used, each computer connects via a twisted-pair or fiber line, and the switch forwards frames only to the destination port based on MAC addresses, eliminating conflicts. Rates have increased from an initial 3 megabits per second to 400 and 800 gigabits per second in data centers.
1973 年施乐帕洛阿尔托研究中心的梅特卡夫（Robert Metcalfe）和: Ethernet was invented by Robert Metcalfe of Xerox PARC and David Boggs in 1973; it became the IEEE 802.3 standard in 1983. Metcalfe later founded 3Com and received the 2022 Turing Award.
以太网是全球局域网和数据中心的标准连接方式（见 [[wifi]]、[[route: Ethernet is the standard connection method for global local area networks and data centers (see [[wifi]], [[router]], [[computer-network]]).
互联网上每台设备的门牌号；IPv4 只有约 43 亿个，IPv6 几乎用之不尽。: The door number for each device on the Internet; IPv4 has only about 4.3 billion addresses, while IPv6 is virtually inexhaustible.
要把包送到正确的地方，每台设备都需要一个唯一的地址；地址的长度决定了一共能有多少: To deliver packets to the correct destination, each device needs a unique address; the length of the address determines how many total there can be ([[p:info|Information theory]]).
IPv4 地址是 32 位，写成四段十进制数（如 192.168.1.1），最多: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits, written as four decimal numbers (e.g., 192.168.1.1), totaling about 4.3 billion. After the Internet boom, addresses ran out, so home routers use 'Network Address Translation' (NAT) to let many devices share a single public address. IPv6 addresses are 128 bits, numbering about 3.4×10³⁸, enough to assign infinite addresses to every grain of sand on Earth.
IPv4 定义于 1981 年；2011 年 2 月全球 IPv4 地址池分配完: IPv4 was defined in 1981; the global IPv4 address pool was exhausted in February 2011. The IPv6 specification was released in the late 1990s; according to Google statistics, by March 2026, the proportion of users accessing Google via IPv6 first exceeded 50%.
地址枯竭推动了 NAT 和 IPv6 两条路线，IPv6 正逐步成为主流（见 [: Address exhaustion drove two paths: NAT and IPv6, with IPv6 gradually becoming mainstream (see [[tcp-ip]], [[dns]], [[router]]).
把好记的网址翻译成 IP 地址的全球分布式\"电话簿\"。: A global distributed 'phonebook' that translates memorable URLs into IP addresses.
人记名字、机器认数字；用一个分层、分布式的数据库把名字翻译成地址，每一层只管自己: Humans remember names; machines recognize numbers. A layered, distributed database translates names into addresses; each layer manages only its segment, allowing the system to scale to hundreds of millions of domains ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]]). The same data has copies on servers worldwide; if any single server fails, queries remain unaffected ([[p:redundancy|redundancy]]).
你在浏览器输入 www.example.com，电脑先问本地的 DNS 解析服务: When you type www.example.com into a browser, the computer first asks its local DNS resolver. If it doesn't know, it starts from the **root servers**: 'Who manages .com?' The root servers point to the **.com top-level domain server**; then it asks: 'Who manages example.com?' and receives the **authoritative server** for that domain name, which finally tells you the IP address of www.example.com. Results at each step are **cached** for a period; subsequent queries become much faster. Behind the 13 groups of root servers lie over a thousand server instances distributed across major continents.
早期阿帕网用一个人工维护的 hosts.txt 文件记录所有主机名，网络变大后难: Early ARPANet used a manually maintained hosts.txt file to record all hostnames; as the network grew, this became unsustainable. In 1983, Paul Mockapetris of the US designed the Domain Name System.
DNS 让网址好记，也让网站可以更换服务器而不改名字。它也是网络审查、劫持和攻击: DNS makes URLs memorable and allows websites to change servers without changing names. It is also a common target for censorship, hijacking, and attacks (see [[ip-address]], [[world-wide-web]]).
一次 DNS 查询：从根服务器到顶级域、再到权威服务器，逐级问出 IP 地址，结: A single DNS query: starting from the root servers, moving to top-level domains, and then to authoritative servers, asking step-by-step for the IP address, with results cached along the way.
在网络交叉口查看每个数据包的目的地址，决定把它往哪个方向转发。: At network intersections, examine the destination address of each packet to decide which direction it should be forwarded.
在网络的每个交叉口，只需根据目的地址决定\"下一站往哪走\"，无数个这样的局部决: At every intersection in the network, only the decision of 'where to go next' based on the destination address is needed; countless such local decisions can deliver packets to any place globally ([[p:network|network]]).
路由器有多个端口连接不同的网络，内部维护一张**路由表**，记录\"去往哪一类地: Routers have multiple ports connecting different networks and internally maintain a **routing table**, recording 'for which class of addresses, from which port should it be sent to which neighbor'. When each packet arrives, the router checks the destination IP address, finds the most matching entry in the table, and forwards it out. Routing tables are automatically updated by routing protocols: within networks, protocols like OSPF are commonly used to calculate shortest paths, while between networks [[bgp|Border Gateway Protocol (BGP)]] is used. Backbone routers can forward billions of packets per second. Home 'routers' actually integrate multiple functions including routing, switching, Wi-Fi access points, and NAT.
阿帕网的 IMP 是最早的路由器；1984 年斯坦福大学的一对夫妇创办思科（Ci: The IMP at ARPANET was the earliest router; in 1984, a couple from Stanford University founded Cisco, making routers a commodity.
路由器是互联网分组交换的执行者（见 [[packet-switching]]、[: Routers are the executors of internet packet switching (see [[packet-switching]], [[ip-address]]).
各大网络之间交换\"我能到达哪些地址\"的协议，相当于互联网的全球路线图。: Protocols for exchanging 'which addresses I can reach' between major networks are equivalent to the global route map of the Internet.
互联网由几万个各自独立的网络组成，没人掌握全局；让每个网络向邻居宣告\"我能到达: The Internet consists of tens of thousands of independent networks; no one controls the whole picture. Each network announces to its neighbors 'which addresses I can reach'; information propagates layer by layer, and the global route map is automatically assembled ([[p:network|network]]).
每个独立管理的网络称为一个\"自治系统\"，有自己的编号。BGP 让相邻自治系统: Each independently managed network is called an 'autonomous system', having its own number. BGP allows adjacent autonomous systems to exchange reachable address blocks and paths; each network then selects routes based on commercial relationships and policies. BGP relies on trust; when errors are declared or malicious hijacking occurs, large amounts of traffic may be diverted to wrong places. In October 2021, Facebook interrupted global services for about 6 hours due to a single incorrect configuration that revoked its own routing.
1989 年思科的洛赫德（Kirk Lougheed）和 IBM 的雷克特（Ya: In 1989, Cisco's Kirk Lougheed and IBM's Yakov Rekhter drafted BGP using two napkins during lunch; it was released as RFC 1105 the same year.
BGP 是把互联网粘在一起的\"胶水\"（见 [[router]]、[[inte: BGP is the 'glue' that holds the Internet together (see [[router]], [[internet]]).
把网页和视频复制到离用户最近的服务器上，让全球访问都快。: Copy web pages and videos to servers closest to users so global access becomes fast.
刚被访问过的内容很可能马上被别人访问，离用户越近的副本取得越快（[[p:loca: Content recently accessed is likely to be accessed by others soon; copies closer to users are retrieved faster ([[p:locality|Locality & caching]]).
内容分发网络在全球各地的运营商机房里部署成千上万台缓存服务器。用户请求网页、图片: Content delivery networks deploy thousands or tens of thousands of cache servers in operator rooms around the world. When users request web pages, images, or videos, DNS guides them to the nearest node with the lightest load; if the node already has a cache, it returns directly without going back to the source site. This shortens latency and reduces pressure on the source site and long-distance links, while also absorbing large-scale [[ddos|Denial-of-service (DDoS) attack]] traffic.
1998 年麻省理工学院的数学家莱顿（Tom Leighton）和学生卢因（Da: In 1998, mathematician Tom Leighton from MIT and student Daniel Lewin founded Akamai, creating a commercial CDN. Lewin passed away in the 2001 'September 11' incident.
今天大部分网页和视频流量都经由 CDN 分发，没有它，热门视频和大型网站很难服务: Today, most web page and video traffic is distributed via CDNs; without them, popular videos and large websites would struggle to serve global users (see [[cache]], [[streaming-media]], [[edge-computing]]).
把数字信号调制成能在电话线上传输的声音再还原，拨号上网的\"吱吱\"声就是它。: Modulating digital signals into sound transmittable over telephone lines and then restoring them; the 'bzzzt' sound of dial-up internet is this.
电话线只能传 300–3400 赫兹的声音，数字信号必须先\"翻译\"成声音才能: Telephone lines can only transmit 300–3400 Hz sounds; digital signals must first be 'translated' into sound to pass through ([[p:sampling|Sampling & digitization]]): different tones, amplitudes, and phases represent different bit combinations.
调制解调器（modem 即\"调制器—解调器\"的缩写）发送时把比特调制成音频信: A modem (modem is an abbreviation for 'modulator-demodulator') modulates bits into audio signals when sending and demodulates them back into bits when receiving. During dial-up connections, that string of 'bzzzt' sounds is two modems testing each other and agreeing on communication speed. Rates gradually increased from 300 bits per second to 56 kilobits per second, approaching the Shannon limit of telephone lines.
1962 年 AT&T 推出 Bell 103 调制解调器，速率每秒 300 比: In 1962, AT&T launched the Bell 103 modem at a rate of 300 bits per second for commercial data communication.
调制解调器让个人电脑通过电话线接入 BBS 和互联网，开启了大众上网时代；今天的: Modems enabled personal computers to connect to BBS and the Internet via telephone lines, opening the era of mass internet access; today's optical modems and DSL modems still use this name (see [[modulation]], [[broadband]]).
在公共互联网上建一条加密\"隧道\"，像在同一个内网里一样安全通信。: Build an encrypted 'tunnel' on the public Internet, like secure communication within the same intranet.
在公共网络上把数据加密后再装进另一个数据包里传送，外人看到的只是乱码，只有隧道两: Encrypt data before packaging it into another packet for transmission on a public network; outsiders see only garbled code, and only devices holding keys at both ends of the tunnel can decrypt ([[p:oneway|One-way functions]]).
VPN 客户端和远端的 VPN 服务器之间建立一条加密\"隧道\"：电脑发出的所: A VPN client establishes an encrypted 'tunnel' with a remote VPN server: all data sent by the computer is first encrypted, then encapsulated, sent to the VPN server, which decapsulates it before forwarding to the destination. Thus, employees can access internal systems as if sitting within the company intranet even while in a coffee shop; networks along the way can only see 'you are communicating with the VPN server'. Common protocols include IPsec, OpenVPN, and WireGuard.
1996 年微软工程师开发了点对点隧道协议（PPTP），是最早被广泛使用的 VP: In 1996, Microsoft engineers developed the Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol (PPTP), which was one of the earliest VPN protocols to be widely used.
VPN 是企业远程办公的基础设施，也被普通用户用来保护公共 Wi-Fi 上的隐私: VPNs serve as the infrastructure for enterprise remote work and are also used by ordinary users to protect privacy on public Wi-Fi networks (see [[https-tls]], [[zero-trust]]).
把流量层层加密后经多个中继转发，隐藏用户的真实位置。: Traffic is encrypted in layers and forwarded through multiple relays, hiding the user's true location.
把消息层层加密，像洋葱一样包好，每个中继只能剥开一层、只知道上一站和下一站，没有: Messages are layered encryption like an onion; each relay peels off only one layer, knowing only the previous hop and the next hop. No single relay can simultaneously know "who is accessing" and "what is being accessed" ([[p:oneway|One-way functions]]).
Tor 客户端随机挑选三个中继组成线路，用三把密钥依次加密数据。入口节点知道你是: A Tor client randomly selects three relays to form a circuit, encrypting data with three keys in sequence. The entry node knows who you are but not where you are going; the exit node knows where you are going but not who you are; the middle nodes know nothing. Websites can also hide as "onion services" within the Tor network, commonly known as the "dark web." The cost is slow speed.
1990 年代中期美国海军研究实验室提出\"洋葱路由\"；2002 年 Tor: In the mid-1990s, the US Navy Research Laboratory proposed "onion routing"; in 2002, the Tor software was released; in 2006, the non-profit organization Tor Project was established.
Tor 保护了记者、异见人士和普通人的隐私，也被用于非法交易，是隐私与监管之争的: Tor protects the privacy of journalists, dissidents, and ordinary people, and has also been used for illegal transactions, making it a focal point of the struggle between privacy and regulation (see [[vpn]], [[cryptography]]).
操控大量被感染的设备同时访问目标，把服务器挤垮。: Controlling a large number of infected devices to simultaneously access a target, overwhelming the server.
任何服务器的带宽和处理能力都有限，攻击者只要能调动足够多的流量就能把它压垮（[[: The bandwidth and processing capacity of any server are limited; an attacker can overwhelm it as long as they can mobilize sufficient traffic ([[p:scale|scale]]).
攻击者先用 [[malware|恶意软件]] 感染大量电脑、摄像头和路由器，组成: Attackers first use [[malware|Malware (viruses & worms)]] to infect numerous computers, cameras, and routers, forming a "botnet," then give the command for them to simultaneously send massive requests or garbage traffic toward the target. Normal users are then excluded. An "amplification attack" forges the victim's address, using the server's large response volume to drown out the victim. Defense relies on [[cdn|Content delivery network (CDN)]] and dedicated scrubbing centers to disperse and absorb traffic, identify, and discard attack packets.
2000 年 2 月，加拿大一名 15 岁少年发动攻击，让雅虎、eBay 等网站: In February 2000, a 15-year-old boy in Canada launched an attack that paralyzed websites such as Yahoo! and eBay for several hours; in 2016, the Mirai botnet used tens of thousands of IoT devices to attack the domain name provider Dyn, causing widespread unavailability of US websites.
攻击规模逐年攀升，抗 DDoS 成为大型网站的必备能力（见 [[cybersec: Attack scales have climbed year by year, making anti-DDoS capability a necessity for large-scale websites (see [[cybersecurity]], [[iot]]).
两台以上计算机通过线缆或无线连接、按共同协议交换数据；按范围分为局域网、城域网和: Two or more computers are connected via cables or wireless connections and exchange data according to common protocols; classified by range into LANs, MANs, and WANs.
两台计算机只要遵守同样的通信规则就能交换数据（[[p:abstraction|分: Computers can exchange data as long as they follow the same communication rules ([[p:abstraction|layering]]); the more machines connected, the more resources each machine can access ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
计算机网络按范围分为：**局域网**（LAN），覆盖一间办公室或一栋楼，用 [[: Computer networks are classified by range: **LAN** (Local Area Network), covering an office or a building, using [[ethernet|Ethernet]] and Wi-Fi; **MAN** (Metropolitan Area Network), covering a city; **WAN** (Wide Area Network), spanning cities and countries, composed of carrier fiber optic lines. Networks contain terminals, switches (forwarding within LANs by physical address), and routers (forwarding between networks by IP address).
1960 年代的分时计算机已能通过电话线连接远程终端；1971 年夏威夷大学的: In the 1960s, time-sharing computers could connect remote terminals via telephone lines; in 1971, ALOHAnet at the University of Hawaii was the first to connect computers via radio, inspiring Ethernet.
把计算机连起来，让\"计算\"变成了\"通信\"，最终汇成了 [[interne: Connecting computers turned "computation" into "communication," ultimately forming [[internet|Internet]] (see [[router]], [[wifi]]).
汤姆林森首次用 @ 把信发到另一台计算机上的用户，是互联网最早的杀手级应用。: Tomlinson's use of the @ symbol to send messages to users on other computers was the internet's earliest killer application.
信不必等收件人在线，先存进对方的\"邮箱\"服务器，对方上线时再取（存储转发）；: Messages do not need to wait for the recipient to be online; they are first stored in the recipient's "mailbox" server and retrieved when the recipient comes online (store-and-forward); a globally uniform address format of "username@hostname" allows any two systems to communicate ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
你写好邮件后，邮件客户端用 SMTP 协议交给自己的邮件服务器，服务器查询 DN: After you compose an email, the mail client hands it off to your own mail server via the SMTP protocol; the server queries DNS to find the recipient domain's mail server and forwards it there; the recipient retrieves messages using the POP3 or IMAP protocols from the server. Attachments are encoded as text and sent with the message. Spam and phishing emails are long-standing problems requiring filtering and authentication technologies to combat them.
1971 年美国 BBN 公司的汤姆林森（Ray Tomlinson）在阿帕网上: In 1971, Ray Tomlinson of the US BBN company first sent a message to a user on another computer on ARPANET and selected the @ symbol to separate the username and hostname. The SMTP protocol was released in 1982.
电子邮件是互联网最早的\"杀手级应用\"，至今仍是工作沟通和账号注册的基础（见: Email is the internet's earliest "killer application"; it remains the foundation for work communication and account registration to this day (see [[arpanet]], [[instant-messaging]]).
可以点击跳转的文本；尼尔森造了这个词，它是万维网的核心思想。: Clickable text; Neilson coined this term; it is the core idea of the World Wide Web.
知识本来就是互相关联的；让文字里的词直接链接到相关内容，读者就能按自己的思路跳转: Knowledge is inherently interconnected; linking words in text directly to related content allows readers to jump according to their own train of thought without having to read from beginning to end ([[p:network|network]]).
超文本中的某些词或图片是\"链接\"，点击后跳到另一段文字、另一个文件，甚至另一: Certain words or images in hypertext are called "links." Clicking a link takes you to another section of text, another file, or even a document on a different computer. Links can interweave arbitrarily, forming a web rather than a single line.
1945 年布什（Vannevar Bush）设想了一种能把资料关联起来的机器\: In 1945, Vannevar Bush envisioned a machine called "Memex" that could associate information; in 1965, Ted Nelson of the United States coined the term "hypertext"; and in 1968, Engelbart demonstrated clickable links in his famous "Mother of All Demons."
超文本是万维网的核心思想（见 [[world-wide-web]]、[[mous: Hypertext is a core idea of the World Wide Web (see [[world-wide-web]], [[mouse]]).
蒂姆·伯纳斯-李在 CERN 提出用超链接把全球文档连起来，1991 年对外开放: Tim Berners-Lee proposed at CERN using hyperlinks to connect global documents; it was opened to the public in 1991.
给全世界每份文档一个唯一的地址（URL），用统一的格式写网页、统一的协议传网页，: Give every document on the world a unique address (URL), write web pages in a unified format, use a unified protocol to transmit web pages, and allow any web page to link to any other web page. Information scattered across the globe automatically weaves into a net ([[p:standard|Standardization]]). Every additional website makes the entire net more useful for everyone ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
关键是\"去中心化\"：任何人都能建网站、链接别人，无需许可；链接可以失效（\": The key is "decentralization": anyone can build a website or link to others without permission; links can fail ("404"), and the system does not need to guarantee consistency. This tolerance allows for explosive growth.
