AGI 虽是推测性概念（见 [[technological-singularit: Although AGI is a speculative concept (see [[technological-singularity]]), it has already substantially influenced investment, policy, and security research.
一切关于 AGI 时间表的说法都是**推测**，不宜当作事实引用。: All statements about AGI timelines are **speculation** and should not be cited as facts.
用焦炭代替木炭在高炉中还原铁矿石，让铁的产量摆脱森林限制。: Replacing coke with charcoal in blast furnaces for iron ore reduction freed iron production from forest limitations.
铁矿石是铁和氧的化合物。在高温下，焦炭燃烧生成的一氧化碳会把氧从铁矿石里\"抢\: Iron ore is a compound of iron and oxygen. At high temperatures, carbon monoxide generated by burning coke "steals" the oxygen from iron ore, leaving metallic iron ([[p:redox|redox]]); the blast furnace is tall and sealed, maximizing heat retention within the furnace ([[p:heat|heat transfer]]).
铁矿石、焦炭和石灰石从炉顶分层装入，热风从炉底鼓入。焦炭燃烧产生上千度高温和一氧: Iron ore, coke, and limestone are loaded in layers from the top of the furnace; hot air is blown in from the bottom. Coke combustion produces over a thousand degrees of high temperature and carbon monoxide; materials sink while being reduced and melted; limestone combines with impurities to form slag floating on top. What flows out from the bottom is pig iron (iron water) containing about 4% carbon, which must be further processed into steel. Large blast furnaces produce over ten thousand tons of iron water daily; once started, they operate continuously for over a decade.
1709 年英国的达比（Abraham Darby I）在科尔布鲁克代尔首次用焦: In 1709, Britain's Darby (Abraham Darby I) successfully used coke instead of charcoal to smelt iron in Colbrookdale; in 1828, Neilson (James Neilson) invented hot blast technology, significantly saving fuel.
焦炭让炼铁摆脱了森林的限制，铁产量暴涨。今天约七成钢仍走\"高炉—转炉\"路线，: Coke freed iron smelting from forest limitations, causing iron production to surge. Today, about 70% of steel still follows the "blast furnace-converter" route; it is also one of the largest sources of industrial carbon dioxide (see [[green-steel]]).
高炉是一座逆流反应器：炉料从上往下走，热气从下往上走，一氧化碳一路把氧带走。: The blast furnace is a counter-current reactor: materials move from top to bottom, hot gas moves from bottom to top; carbon monoxide continuously carries away oxygen.
向熔融生铁吹空气烧掉多余的碳，第一次让钢可以廉价大量生产。: Blowing air into molten pig iron to burn off excess carbon enabled the first cheap, mass production of steel.
生铁太脆是因为含碳太多。向熔融的生铁里吹空气，氧会把多余的碳、硅烧掉（[[p:r: Pig iron is too brittle because it contains too much carbon. Blowing air into molten pig iron causes oxygen to burn off excess carbon and silicon ([[p:redox|redox]]); the heat released by these combustion reactions is sufficient to keep the iron in a liquid state throughout the process, requiring no additional fuel.
转炉是一个可以倾转的梨形大罐，装入铁水后从底部鼓入空气，十几到二十分钟火焰冲天，: A converter is a large, pear-shaped vessel that can be tilted; after loading molten iron, air is blown in from the bottom, causing flames to shoot up for ten to twenty minutes until the carbon content drops into the steel range, after which ingots are poured out. An early challenge was phosphorus: many British iron ores contained phosphorus, resulting in very brittle steel. In 1878, Thomas (Sidney Gilchrist Thomas) switched to a basic refractory lining, which absorbed the phosphorus into the slag.
1856 年英国发明家贝塞麦（Henry Bessemer）取得专利，美国的凯利: In 1856, British inventor Henry Bessemer obtained a patent; William Kelly in the United States also independently proposed a similar method; Robert Mushet discovered that adding pig iron containing manganese could remove excess oxygen and sulfur, making steel usable.
钢从昂贵的特种材料变成大宗商品，英国钢价降到原来的几分之一。铁路钢轨、钢船、桥梁: Steel transformed from an expensive specialty material into a bulk commodity, with British steel prices falling to a fraction of their original levels. This made railway rails, steel ships, bridges, and skyscrapers possible (see [[railway]]). It was later replaced by more controllable open-hearth furnaces and oxygen-top-blowing converters.
利用余热回收的平炉可以精确控制成分，曾长期是世界主要炼钢法。: Open-hearth furnaces utilizing waste heat recovery could precisely control composition and were once the world's primary steelmaking method for a long time.
把炉子排出的热废气先引过一堆耐火砖，砖被烤热后再用来预热进炉的空气和燃气，交替进: Hot exhaust gases from the furnace are first directed over a bank of refractory bricks; these bricks are heated up and then used to preheat incoming air and fuel gas in an alternating cycle, allowing heat to be "recycled" within the furnace, reaching temperatures of approximately 1600°C or higher ([[p:heat|heat transfer]]).
平炉是一个浅而宽的炉膛，可装入大量废钢。一炉要炼几个小时，虽慢，但能中途取样、精: An open-hearth furnace is a shallow and wide hearth capable of holding large amounts of scrap steel. A single batch takes several hours to smelt; although slow, it allows sampling midway and precise adjustment of composition.
1850 年代德裔英国工程师西门子（William Siemens）发明蓄热式炉: In the 1850s, German-British engineer William Siemens invented a regenerative furnace; in 1865, Pierre-Émile Martin in France used it for steelmaking, hence it is also known as the "Siemens-Martin process".
平炉能大量回收废钢、成分稳定，从 20 世纪初到 1960 年代是世界主要的炼钢: Open-hearth furnaces could recover large amounts of scrap steel and maintain stable composition, serving as the world's primary steelmaking method from the early 20th century through the 1960s. Afterwards, they were replaced by much faster [[basic-oxygen-steelmaking|Basic oxygen steelmaking]] and [[electric-arc-furnace|Electric arc furnace]] processes; today, they have been largely phased out.
含碳约 0.02–2% 的铁合金，强度高、韧性好、价格低，是现代文明的骨架。: Iron alloys containing approximately 0.02–2% carbon are strong, tough, and low-cost, forming the backbone of modern civilization.
钢有几千年历史（如印度的乌兹钢），但直到 1856 年 [[bessemer-p: Steel has a history spanning thousands of years (such as India's Wootz steel), but it could not be cheaply mass-produced until [[bessemer-process|Bessemer converter]] appeared in 1856. According to data from the World Steel Association, global crude steel production was approximately 1.85 billion tons in 2025, with converter steel accounting for about 69% and electric arc furnace steel accounting for about 30%; China's production exceeds half of this total.
钢是建筑、桥梁、汽车、船舶和机器的骨架。钢铁生产约占全球二氧化碳排放的 7%—9: Steel forms the backbone of construction, bridges, automobiles, ships, and machinery. Steel production accounts for approximately 7%–9% of global carbon dioxide emissions; replacing coke with hydrogen in [[green-steel|green steel]] is a key focus for emission reduction.
上：碳含量决定铁的\"性格\"；下：今天的两条主要炼钢路线。: Top: Carbon content determines the "character" of iron; Bottom: Today's two main steelmaking routes.
用电弧熔化废钢再炼成新钢，流程短、排放低，适合循环利用。: Electric arc melting scrap steel to produce new steel involves a short process and low emissions, making it suitable for recycling.
电流穿过电极与炉料间的空气形成三千多度的电弧，把电能直接变成热熔化废钢（[[p:: Current passes through the air between electrodes and charge material, forming an electric arc exceeding 3000°C, which directly converts electrical energy into heat to melt scrap steel ([[p:ohm|Circuit]], [[p:heat|heat transfer]]) without first smelting iron.
几根粗大的石墨电极在废钢上方起弧，约一小时熔清，再吹氧、加合金调成分。它也能熔化: Several thick graphite electrodes arc above the scrap steel; it takes about an hour to fully melt, after which oxygen is blown in and alloying elements are added to adjust composition. It can also melt "directly reduced iron," serving as a key component of the hydrogen metallurgy route.
法国的埃鲁（Paul Héroult）在 1900 年前后发明炼钢电弧炉，190: Paul Héroult in France invented the electric arc furnace for steelmaking around 1900; the first commercial electric arc furnace was built in the United States in 1907. Starting in 1969, Nucor in the United States used it to build flexible "mini-steel mills," challenging traditional large-scale steel mills.
电弧炉让钢成为最易循环的材料之一，2025 年约占全球钢产量的 30%；用绿电时: The electric arc furnace makes steel one of the most easily recyclable materials; in 2025, it accounted for approximately 30% of global steel production. When using green electricity, emissions are only a small fraction of those from the blast furnace route.
加入铬后表面形成致密氧化膜，自己\"防锈\"。: Adding chromium forms a dense oxide film on the surface, enabling self-corrosion resistance.
铬比铁更\"爱\"氧。钢中铬含量超过约 10.5% 时，表面会自动生成一层只有几: Chromium is more "affine" to oxygen than iron. When chromium content in steel exceeds approximately 10.5%, a dense oxide chromium film only a few nanometers thick will automatically form on the surface, separating the internal iron from air and water; if scratched, this film can self-repair ([[p:redox|redox]], [[p:structure|structure]]).
常见的\"18/8\"不锈钢含铬约 18%、镍约 8%，组织稳定、可加工性好，用: Common "18/8" stainless steel contains approximately 18% chromium and 8% nickel, offering stable microstructure and good machinability; it is used for cutlery and kitchenware. Ferritic stainless steels without nickel are more magnetic and cheaper; varieties containing molybdenum offer greater resistance to seawater corrosion.
1913 年英国谢菲尔德的布里尔利（Harry Brearley）在为枪管寻找耐: In 1913, Harry Brearley of Sheffield, England, discovered that steel containing approximately 12.8% chromium did not rust while searching for wear-resistant steel for gun barrels; Krupp in Germany simultaneously developed nickel-containing stainless steel.
不锈钢让刀具、厨房、医疗器械、化工设备和建筑幕墙不再怕锈，年产量已超过 6000: Stainless steel allows knives, kitchens, medical devices, chemical equipment, and building curtain walls to no longer fear rusting; annual production has exceeded 60 million tons.
把氧化铝溶在熔融冰晶石中通电电解，铝从昂贵的贵金属变成日用品。: By dissolving alumina in molten cryolite and passing an electric current through it, aluminum is electrolytically produced, transforming from a precious metal into a daily commodity.
铝和氧结合得极牢，碳还原不了，只能用电\"硬拆\"：铝离子在阴极得到电子变成金属: The bond between aluminum and oxygen is extremely strong; carbon cannot reduce it, so electricity must be used to 'force' the separation: aluminum ions gain electrons at the cathode to become metallic aluminum ([[p:redox|Redox & electrochemistry]]). The trick is to dissolve alumina with a melting point of over 2000°C into molten cryolite, allowing electrolysis at approximately 960°C.
先用拜耳法从铝土矿中提取纯净的氧化铝。电解槽中大电流从碳阳极流向槽底阴极：液态铝: First, pure alumina is extracted from bauxite ore using the Bayer process. Inside the electrolytic cell, high current flows from the carbon anode to the bottom cathode: liquid aluminum collects at the bottom and is withdrawn, while oxygen combines with the carbon anode to form carbon dioxide. Approximately 13,000 to 15,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity are consumed per ton of aluminum.
1886 年，美国的霍尔（Charles Martin Hall）和法国的埃鲁（: In 1886, Charles Martin Hall in the United States and Paul Héroult in France independently invented this method almost simultaneously; both were born in 1863. In 1888, Carl Josef Bayer in Austria invented the alumina extraction process.
19 世纪中叶铝比银还贵；霍尔—埃鲁法让它变成易拉罐、门窗和机身材料。铝被称为\: In the mid-19th century, aluminum was more expensive than silver; the Hall-Héroult process made it a material for beverage cans, window frames, and aircraft fuselages. Aluminum is called 'solidified electricity'; most aluminum smelters are built in areas with cheap electricity; recycling aluminum requires only about 5% of the energy needed to produce primary aluminum.
电解槽里，电流把溶在冰晶石中的氧化铝拆开：铝沉到槽底，氧跑到碳阳极上变成二氧化碳: Inside the electrolytic cell, the electric current breaks down alumina dissolved in cryolite: aluminum sinks to the bottom of the cell, while oxygen travels up to the carbon anode to form carbon dioxide.
强度接近钢而重量轻近一半、耐腐蚀，用于飞机、人工关节和高端手机。: It has a strength close to steel but weighs nearly half as much and is corrosion-resistant; it is used for aircraft, artificial joints, and high-end smartphones.
钛密度约为钢的 57%，强度却相近，所以比强度高；表面自动长出致密氧化膜，极耐腐: Titanium has a density about 57% that of steel but similar strength, so its specific strength is higher; its surface automatically grows a dense oxide film, making it extremely corrosion-resistant, and it can 'grow together' with bone ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
钛和氧结合太牢，不能用碳还原。克罗尔法先把矿石变成四氯化钛，再用熔融镁把钛置换出: The bond between titanium and oxygen is too strong for carbon reduction. The Kroll process first converts the ore into titanium tetrachloride, then uses molten magnesium to displace titanium out, yielding sponge titanium which is then smelted into ingots. Production is done in batches with high energy consumption, so titanium is much more expensive than steel.
1940 年卢森堡冶金学家克罗尔（William Kroll）发明这一工艺。19: In 1940, Luxembourg metallurgist William Kroll invented this process. In the 1960s, nearly 90% of the SR-71 reconnaissance aircraft fuselage was made of titanium. In the 1950s, Brunemark in Sweden discovered that titanium could firmly combine with bone, paving the way for dental implants.
钛合金用于飞机结构和发动机、化工设备、人工关节（见 [[artificial-j: Titanium alloys are used for aircraft structures and engines, chemical equipment, artificial joints (see [[artificial-joint]]), and high-end smartphones.
把两种以上金属（或非金属）熔在一起，得到比纯金属更强、更耐用的材料。: By melting two or more metals (or non-metals) together, a material stronger and more durable than pure metals is obtained.
在金属晶格里掺进大小不同的原子，晶格被局部\"撑歪\"，原子层不易滑移，材料就更: By introducing atoms of different sizes into the metal crystal lattice, the lattice is locally 'stretched and distorted'; atomic layers are less prone to slip, making the material harder and stronger; different elements also bring properties such as corrosion resistance and heat resistance ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
常见思路：把别的原子溶进去（固溶强化，如黄铜是铜溶了锌）；析出细小颗粒卡住滑移（: Common approaches include dissolving other atoms into the matrix (solid solution strengthening, such as brass which is copper with dissolved zinc); precipitating fine particles to block slip (age hardening, such as hard aluminum). Solder utilizes the characteristic that the alloy's melting point is lower than that of its individual components.
人类最早的合金是约五千年前的青铜（铜加锡）。1906 年德国的维尔姆（Alfre: The earliest alloy used by humans was bronze about five thousand years ago (copper plus tin). In 1906, Alfred Wilm in Germany discovered that an aluminum-copper alloy hardens on its own over a few days; the resulting 'Duralumin' was used for airships and all-metal aircraft. Around 2004, Ye Junwei and others proposed 'high-entropy alloys' consisting of five or more elements mixed in nearly equal proportions.
几乎所有工程金属都是合金，合金设计决定了飞机、汽车和机器的性能上限（见 [[su: Almost all engineering metals are alloys; alloy design determines the performance ceiling of aircraft, automobiles, and machines (see [[superalloy]]).
在上千度高温下仍能保持强度的镍基合金，是喷气发动机涡轮叶片的材料。: Nickel-based alloys that maintain strength at temperatures over a thousand degrees Celsius are used for turbine blades in jet engines.
金属在高温下长期受力会慢慢\"蠕变\"变形。镍基高温合金里弥散着大量与基体紧密咬: Metals subjected to long-term stress at high temperatures will slowly 'creep' and deform. Inside nickel-based superalloys, numerous fine Ni₃Al particles are dispersed throughout the matrix, tightly interlocking with the base structure, firmly pinning the lattice; this remains effective even at high temperatures ([[p:structure|structure]], [[p:heat|heat transfer]]).
涡轮叶片要在高于自身熔点的燃气中高速旋转，靠三招：合金耐热；内部冷却通道和表面小: Turbine blades must rotate at high speeds in hot gases above their own melting point; they rely on three methods: alloy heat resistance; internal cooling channels and surface small holes spraying cold air to form an 'air film'; and ceramic thermal barrier coatings. Blades are also made as 'single crystals'—entirely consisting of a single grain, eliminating the grain boundaries that are the weakest points at high temperatures.
1940 年代初英国为惠特尔的喷气发动机研制出 Nimonic 合金；1960–: In the early 1940s, the UK developed Nimonic alloy for Whittle's jet engine; in the 1960–1970s, companies like Pratt & Whitney in the US developed directional solidification and single-crystal blades.
涡轮前温度越高，发动机效率和推力越高（见 [[jet-engine]]、[[ga: The higher the turbine inlet temperature, the higher the engine efficiency and thrust (see [[jet-engine]], [[gas-turbine]]). Single-crystal blades are considered a symbol of industrial strength.
变形后一加热就恢复原状的合金，如镍钛合金，用于血管支架和牙箍。: Alloys that return to their original shape upon heating after deformation, such as nickel-titanium alloys, are used for vascular stents and orthodontic braces.
镍钛合金在低温和高温下有两种不同的晶体结构。低温时它很\"软\"，可以被掰弯；一: Nickel-titanium alloys have two different crystal structures at low and high temperatures. At low temperatures, it is 'soft' and can be bent; upon heating, the atoms switch back to the high-temperature structure as a whole, causing the part to recover its original shape ([[p:phase|phase change]], [[p:structure|structure]]).
同样的相变还带来\"超弹性\"：在体温下，镍钛丝可以被拉伸好几个百分点而不永久变: The same phase transition also brings 'superelasticity': at body temperature, nickel-titanium wire can be stretched by several percentage points without permanent deformation; upon releasing the tension, it springs back, far exceeding ordinary metals.
1959–1962 年，美国海军军械实验室的比勒（William Buehler: Between 1959 and 1962, William Buehler and others at the U.S. Navy Armament Laboratory discovered the shape memory effect in nickel-titanium alloys, naming them Nitinol.
形状记忆合金用于血管支架（压缩后送进血管，在体温下撑开，见 [[minimall: Shape memory alloys are used for vascular stents (compressed and delivered into blood vessels, then expand at body temperature, see [[minimally-invasive-surgery]]), orthodontic wires, eyeglass frames that resist bending, and deployment mechanisms for spacecraft.
给钢铁镀一层锌，锌先被腐蚀从而保护钢。: Coating steel with zinc protects the steel because the zinc corrodes first.
锌比铁更活泼、更容易被氧化。给钢铁镀一层锌，腐蚀会先\"吃\"锌；即使镀层被划破: Zinc is more active than iron and oxidizes more easily. When coating steel with zinc, corrosion consumes the zinc first; even if the coating is scratched, the zinc continues to protect the exposed iron as a 'sacrificial anode' ([[p:redox|redox]]).
最常见的是热浸镀锌：把清洗干净的钢件浸入约 450°C 的熔融锌液，表面形成锌铁: The most common method is hot-dip galvanizing: clean steel parts are immersed in molten zinc at approximately 450°C, forming a zinc-iron alloy layer and a pure zinc layer on the surface that can protect for decades. Electroplating with zinc is also possible. The same principle applies to sacrificial anodes used on ship hulls and pipelines.
名称来自意大利科学家伽伐尼（Luigi Galvani）；1837 年法国工程师: The name comes from Italian scientist Luigi Galvani; in 1837, French engineer Stanislas Sorel obtained a patent for hot-dip galvanizing.
镀锌让输电铁塔、护栏、钢结构、汽车车身和铁皮屋顶的寿命成倍延长。全球锌产量约一半: Galvanizing extends the lifespan of transmission towers, guardrails, steel structures, car bodies, and corrugated iron roofs by multiples. About half of global zinc production is used for galvanizing.
钕铁硼等稀土永磁体是最强的永磁材料，用于电动车电机和风力发电机。: Rare-earth permanent magnets such as neodymium-iron-boron are the strongest permanent magnet materials, used in electric vehicle motors and wind turbines.
稀土原子内层的 4f 电子带来很强的磁性。把钕和铁、硼按特定晶体结构组合，就能把: The strong magnetism arises from the 4f electrons in the inner shells of rare-earth atoms. By combining neodymium with iron and boron according to a specific crystal structure, the magnetic properties can be 'locked' in place to create the strongest permanent magnets ([[p:structure|structure]]); the interaction between permanent magnets and current is precisely the foundation of electric motors ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]).
稀土并不稀少，难在分离：17 种元素化学性质极相似，要经过成百上千级萃取。钕铁硼: Rare-earth elements are not rare; the challenge lies in separation: the 17 elements have extremely similar chemical properties, requiring extraction at hundreds or thousands of times scale. Neodymium-iron-boron magnets are formed by pressing and sintering alloy powders under a magnetic field. Electric vehicle motors also add dysprosium and terbium to withstand high temperatures.
1960 年代出现钐钴磁体；1984 年前后，日本住友特殊金属的佐川真人和美国通: Samarium-cobalt magnets appeared in the 1960s; around 1984, Masatoshi Ozawa of Sumitomo Special Metals in Japan and John Croat of General Motors independently invented neodymium-iron-boron magnets.
钕铁硼让电动车电机、风机、硬盘和耳机又小又强。中国约占全球稀土开采的七成、分离和: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets make electric vehicle motors, wind turbines, hard drives, and headphones smaller and stronger. China accounts for about 70% of global rare-earth mining and roughly 90% of separation and magnet production; since April 2025, export licensing has been implemented for seven middle and heavy rare-earth elements (see [[critical-minerals]]).
用纯氧代替空气吹炼，几十分钟炼一炉钢，如今全球约七成钢由它生产。: Using pure oxygen instead of air for steelmaking allows one batch of steel to be produced in just tens of minutes; today, about 70% of global steel is produced this way.
吹空气炼钢时，空气中近八成的氮气白白带走热量，还会溶进钢里使其变脆。改用纯氧，反: When using air for steelmaking, nearly 80% of the nitrogen in the air carries away heat uselessly and dissolves into the steel, making it brittle. Switching to pure oxygen makes the reaction more vigorous and faster, with sufficient heat to melt a portion of scrap steel ([[p:redox|redox]]).
转炉装入铁水和少量废钢后，一根水冷氧枪从上方以超音速向熔池喷吹纯氧，几十分钟就能: In a basic oxygen furnace, after loading molten iron and a small amount of scrap steel, a water-cooled oxygen lance sprays pure oxygen into the molten pool from above at supersonic speeds, converting hundreds of tons of molten iron into steel in tens of minutes. Cheap pure oxygen comes from large-scale [[air-separation|Air separation]] facilities.
瑞士的杜雷尔（Robert Durrer）等人做了早期试验，1952 年奥地利林: Early experiments were conducted by Robert Durrer and others in Switzerland; the first plant went online in Linz, Austria in 1952. Because the process involves both Linz and Donawitz, it is called the 'LD method'.
氧气转炉炼一炉钢只要平炉的几分之一时间，迅速成为世界主流。2025 年全球约 6: The basic oxygen furnace requires only a fraction of the time needed by a flat-top converter, rapidly becoming the world's mainstream method. In 2025, about 69% of global steel was produced by this method.
从炸药爆破、大型矿用卡车到自动化矿山，决定了金属和能源的供应。: From explosive blasting to large-scale mining trucks and automated mines, explosives determine the supply of metals and energy.
矿石品位越来越低，只能用更大的机器、更便宜的能量搬动更多岩石（[[p:lever: As ore grades decline, only larger machines powered by cheaper energy can move more rock ([[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]]).
现代露天矿先钻孔、用炸药爆破（见 [[explosives]]），再用巨型电铲装: Modern open-pit mines first drill holes and use explosives for blasting (see [[explosives]]), then use giant electric shovels to load ore into mining trucks with a payload of 300–400 tons for transport. The ore is crushed and ground finely before entering processes such as flotation ([[froth-flotation|flotation]]) and other mineral processing steps. Some mines do not dig out the ore; instead, metals are leached directly using solutions via 'heap leaching' or 'in-situ leaching'. Many large mines now use unmanned trucks and remote operation centers.
1867 年诺贝尔发明达纳炸药，彻底改变了采矿；2008 年起力拓等公司在澳大利: Nobel invented dynamite in 1867, fundamentally changing mining; since 2008, companies like Rio Tinto have tested autonomous mining trucks in Australia.
现代采矿让每一吨铜、铁、锂的成本大幅下降，但也带来尾矿、水污染和社区冲突。全球铜: Modern mining has significantly reduced the cost per ton of copper, iron, and lithium, but it also brings tailings, water pollution, and community conflicts. The average grade of global copper mines has dropped below 1%, meaning over 100 tons of rock must be processed to obtain one ton of copper.
利用矿物表面亲水或疏水的差异，让有用矿物附着气泡浮起来分离。: Use the difference in hydrophilicity or hydrophobicity of mineral surfaces to attach useful minerals to bubbles so they float up for separation.
有的矿物表面\"怕水\"（疏水），有的\"亲水\"。向矿浆里鼓入气泡，疏水的有用: Some minerals are 'water-fearing' (hydrophobic), while others are 'water-loving' (hydrophilic). Bubbles are blown into a slurry; hydrophobic useful mineral particles adhere to the bubbles and float up, while hydrophilic gangue sinks down ([[p:structure|structure]], [[p:diffusion|separation]]).
先把矿石磨成细粉、加水调成矿浆，再加入\"捕收剂\"让目标矿物表面变得更疏水，加: First, the ore is ground into fine powder, mixed with water to form a slurry, and then "reagent" (collector) is added to make the surface of target minerals more hydrophobic. "Reagent" (foamer) is added to stabilize the foam. The foam floating to the surface is scraped out, resulting in concentrate enriched by tens of times.
1905 年英国的矿物分离公司取得关键专利，并在澳大利亚布罗肯希尔的铅锌矿大规模: In 1905, a British mineral separation company obtained key patents and applied them on a large scale at the lead-zinc mine in Broken Hill, Australia.
浮选让原本无法利用的低品位铜、铅、锌矿变得有经济价值，是 20 世纪金属供应能够: Flotation makes low-grade copper, lead, and zinc ores that were previously unusable economically viable. It was crucial for meeting electrification demands with metal supplies in the 20th century. Today, most global copper, zinc, and many other metals undergo flotation.
锂、钴、镍、稀土、镓等对新能源和芯片至关重要、供应高度集中的矿产。: Lithium, cobalt, nickel, rare earths, gallium, and other minerals critical to new energy and chips have highly concentrated supply chains.
新能源和芯片离不开锂、钴、镍、稀土、镓、石墨等少数矿产，而它们的开采和加工高度集: New energy and chips rely on a few key minerals such as lithium, cobalt, nickel, rare earths, gallium, and graphite. Their extraction and processing are highly concentrated in a few countries—specialized division of labor brings efficiency but also "choke point" risks ([[p:division|division of labor]]).
各国把重要又易断供的矿产列为\"关键矿产\"，用储备、补贴和回收降低风险。按国际: Countries list important and easily supply-disrupted minerals as "critical minerals," using reserves, subsidies, and recycling to mitigate risks. According to data from the International Energy Agency and others: DRC produces about 70% of global cobalt; Indonesia produces more than half of nickel; China dominates refining of rare earths, graphite, gallium, lithium, and cobalt.
2023 年中国开始管制镓、锗出口，此后扩展到石墨和部分稀土；2024 年欧盟通: China began controlling exports of gallium and germanium in 2023, later expanding to graphite and some rare earths. The EU passed the "Critical Raw Materials Act" in 2024.
关键矿产成为能源转型和地缘政治的焦点（见 [[semiconductor-geo: Critical minerals have become a focal point for energy transition and geopolitics (see [[semiconductor-geopolitics]]), driving battery recycling and development of alternative materials like [[sodium-ion-battery|Sodium-ion battery]].
从盐湖卤水蒸发浓缩或从锂辉石矿中提炼锂，是电池产业链的源头。: Extracting lithium from brine in salt lakes or from spodumene ore is the source of the battery supply chain.
锂溶在盐湖卤水里，或藏在锂辉石等硬岩矿物中。前者靠太阳把水晒干、让锂盐慢慢浓缩（: Lithium dissolves in salt lake brines or hides in hard rock minerals like spodumene. The former relies on the sun to dry water and slowly concentrate lithium salts ([[p:diffusion|diffusion and separation]]); the latter uses high-temperature roasting and acid leaching to extract lithium from crystal lattices.
南美\"锂三角\"（智利、阿根廷、玻利维亚）的盐湖把卤水抽进大片蒸发池，晒一到两: The South American "Lithium Triangle" (Chile, Argentina, Bolivia) pumps brine into large evaporation ponds, drying it for one to two years before processing into lithium carbonate. Australia mines spodumene, mostly shipped to China for refining into lithium carbonate or lithium hydroxide. Emerging "direct lithium extraction" uses adsorbents or membranes to directly capture lithium from brines, reducing the process to days and saving water.
1990 年代后锂离子电池兴起，锂从玻璃、润滑脂的原料变成\"白色石油\"；20: After the 1990s, lithium-ion batteries rose; lithium transformed from a raw material for glass and lubricating grease into "white oil." Lithium prices surged about tenfold in 2022, then dropped sharply in 2023–2024.
锂是 [[lithium-ion|锂离子电池]] 产业链的源头，其供应、价格和环: Lithium is the source of the [[lithium-ion|Lithium-ion battery]] supply chain; its supply, price, and environmental impact (salt lake water consumption, mine extraction) drive costs for electric vehicles and energy storage.
在高温高压和铁催化剂下把空气中的氮变成氨，养活了全球约一半人口。: Converting nitrogen from air into ammonia under high temperature and pressure with iron catalysts has fed about half of the global population.
1909 年德国化学家哈伯（Fritz Haber）在实验室用台式装置连续合成出: In 1909, German chemist Fritz Haber synthesized ammonia continuously in a lab using benchtop equipment. BASF's Carl Bosch solved problems with high-pressure reactors and scale-up production; Alwin Mittasch tested thousands of formulas to find cheap iron catalysts; factories went online in Oppau in 1913. Haber won the 1918 Nobel Prize in Chemistry; Bosch won the 1931 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
合成氨回路：氢、氮压缩后过铁催化剂，生成的氨被冷凝分离，未反应的气体循环再用。: Synthetic ammonia loop: hydrogen and nitrogen are compressed, passed through iron catalysts; generated ammonia is condensed and separated; unreacted gases are recycled.
产量最大的化学品之一，用于化肥、冶金和电池，曾被视为工业实力的指标。: One of the largest chemicals produced, used for fertilizers, metallurgy, and batteries; once seen as an indicator of industrial strength.
二氧化硫与氧气直接结合成三氧化硫很慢；让它们在钒等催化剂表面反应，速度大大加快，: Direct combination of sulfur dioxide and oxygen into sulfur trioxide is slow; making them react on catalyst surfaces like vanadium greatly accelerates the rate, then absorbing sulfur trioxide into concentrated sulfur yields more concentrated sulfuric acid ([[p:catalysis|Catalysis]]).
接触法分三步：燃烧硫磺（多来自石油天然气脱硫）或焙烧硫化矿得到二氧化硫；在约 4: Contact process has three steps: burning sulfur (mostly from petroleum/natural gas desulfurization) or roasting sulfide ores to get sulfur dioxide; oxidizing to sulfur trioxide over vanadium pentoxide catalyst at about 400–600°C; absorbing with 98% concentrated sulfuric acid to avoid difficult-to-collect acid mist formed by direct water contact.
1831 年英国的菲利普斯（Peregrine Phillips）取得接触法专利: British Peregrine Phillips obtained the contact process patent in 1831; starting in the 1920s, cheap and durable vanadium catalysts were adopted.
硫酸是产量最大的化学品之一，年产两亿多吨，一半以上用于磷肥，也用于金属浸出和铅酸: Sulfuric acid is one of the largest chemicals produced annually at over 200 million tons; more than half is used for phosphate fertilizers, also for metal leaching and lead-acid batteries. Sulfuric acid consumption was once used as an indicator of industrial level.
电解食盐水同时得到氯气、烧碱和氢气，是 PVC、造纸和水消毒的原料。: Electrolysis of brine simultaneously produces chlorine gas, caustic soda, and hydrogen, serving as raw materials for PVC, papermaking, and water disinfection.
通电时，食盐水中的氯离子在阳极失去电子变成氯气，水在阴极得到电子变成氢气和氢氧化: During electrolysis, chloride ions in brine lose electrons at the anode to become chlorine gas; water gains electrons at the cathode to form hydrogen gas and sodium hydroxide ([[p:redox|Redox & electrochemistry]]). Key is separating the two sides; otherwise chlorine gas would react with caustic soda again.
现代用只让钠离子通过的离子交换膜隔开两极，一套电解槽同时产出氯气、烧碱和氢气。: Modern electrolysis cells use ion-exchange membranes that allow only sodium ions to pass through, separating the two electrodes. A single electrolytic cell simultaneously produces chlorine gas, caustic soda (sodium hydroxide), and hydrogen gas.
1892 年美国的卡斯特纳（Hamilton Castner）和奥地利的克尔纳（: In 1892, Hamilton Castner from the United States and Karl Kellner from Austria invented mercury-cell electrolysis. Starting in the 1970s, ion-exchange membrane methods gradually replaced the mercury process. The "Water Chlorination" convention requires the elimination of mercury-containing processes.
氯气用于 PVC 塑料、自来水消毒（见 [[water-chlorination: Chlorine gas is used for PVC plastic production, water disinfection (see [[water-chlorination]]), and drug and pesticide manufacturing; caustic soda is used for papermaking, soap production, and alumina extraction.
用食盐、石灰石和氨生产纯碱；侯德榜改进为联合制碱法，同时产出化肥氯化铵。: Pure soda ash (sodium carbonate) is produced from salt, limestone, and ammonia. Hou Debang improved this into the joint alkali process, which simultaneously produces ammonium chloride fertilizer.
在饱和食盐水中通入氨和二氧化碳，溶解度较小的碳酸氢钠（小苏打）会析出，加热分解就: Ammonia and carbon dioxide are introduced into saturated brine; sodium bicarbonate (baking soda), which has lower solubility, precipitates out. Upon heating, it decomposes to yield pure soda ash. Ammonia can be recovered and recycled for reuse (a clever combination of [[p:bond|chemical reactions]]).
索尔维法留下大量氯化钙废液。侯氏制碱法把制碱和合成氨联合：从母液中再析出氯化铵作: The Solvay process left behind large amounts of calcium chloride waste liquid. Hou Debang's joint alkali process combines soda ash production with ammonia synthesis: ammonium chloride is further precipitated from the mother liquor as nitrogen fertilizer, improving salt utilization and eliminating waste slag.
1861 年比利时化学家索尔维（Ernest Solvay）开发出氨碱法，取代了: In 1861, Belgian chemist Ernest Solvay developed the ammonia-soda process, replacing the highly polluting Leblanc process. During the War of Resistance (1939–1943), Chinese chemist Hou Debang led a team to develop the joint alkali process, later named "Hou's soda ash process".
纯碱是制玻璃（约占一半用量）、洗涤剂和化工产品的基础原料。侯氏制碱法是中国化学工: Soda ash is a basic raw material for glass manufacturing (accounting for about half of usage), detergents, and chemical products. Hou's soda ash process is one of the landmark achievements in Chinese chemical engineering.
珀金意外合成苯胺紫，开启了从煤焦油制造化学品的现代有机化学工业。: Perkin accidentally synthesized aniline purple, launching the modern organic chemical industry based on manufacturing chemicals from coal tar.
煤焦油里的苯胺等芳香族化合物，经过氧化、偶合等反应，能形成带有长串交替双键的分子: Aromatic compounds such as aniline in coal tar undergo oxidation, coupling, and other reactions to form molecules with long alternating double bonds; this structure absorbs specific wavelengths of light, resulting in vivid colors ([[p:bond|chemical bonds]]).
天然染料提取难、昂贵。化学家弄清它们的分子结构后，从煤焦油出发人工合成，产量和色: Natural dye extraction is difficult and expensive. After chemists understood their molecular structures, they were able to artificially synthesize them starting from coal tar, achieving production volumes and color spectra far exceeding those of natural dyes.
1856 年，18 岁的英国学生珀金（William Henry Perkin）: In 1856, 18-year-old British student William Henry Perkin attempted to synthesize quinine but accidentally obtained "aniline purple," immediately setting up a factory where the purple dye became fashionable across Europe. In 1897, BASF achieved the industrialization of indigo synthesis.
合成染料催生了巴斯夫、拜耳等德国化工巨头，它们又从染料扩展到药物（如阿司匹林）和: Synthetic dyes gave rise to German chemical giants such as BASF and Bayer; they later expanded from dyes into pharmaceuticals (such as aspirin) and fertilizers, marking the beginning of the modern pharmaceutical industry (see [[drug-discovery]]).
把空气液化后按沸点分出氧、氮、氩，供炼钢、医疗、芯片和火箭使用。: Air is liquefied and then separated by boiling point into oxygen, nitrogen, and argon for use in steelmaking, medicine, chip manufacturing, and rocketry.
空气是氮、氧、氩的混合物，它们的沸点不同：氮约 −196°C，氩约 −186°C: Air is a mixture of nitrogen, oxygen, and argon with different boiling points: nitrogen at approximately −196°C, argon at approximately −186°C, and oxygen at approximately −183°C. After cooling air to its liquefaction point, it can be separated layer by layer like distilling wine to obtain pure components ([[p:phase|phase change]]).
林德法把空气压缩后突然膨胀降温，再用冷气体预冷后来的空气，一圈圈降温直到液化；液: The Linde process compresses air and suddenly expands it for cooling; subsequent air is pre-cooled by cold gas in a cyclic manner until liquefaction. Liquid air enters a fractionation tower where oxygen, nitrogen, and argon are separated according to their boiling points.
1895 年德国工程师林德（Carl von Linde）实现空气的大规模液化，: In 1895, German engineer Carl von Linde achieved large-scale air liquefaction; in 1902, an oxygen production facility was built.
廉价纯氧让 [[basic-oxygen-steelmaking|氧气转炉]]: Cheap pure oxygen makes [[basic-oxygen-steelmaking|Oxygen Converter]] possible and is also used for medical applications and rocket propellants (see [[liquid-rocket-engine]]); nitrogen is used for ammonia synthesis and inert gas protection in chip factories; argon is used for welding.
绝大多数化工产品的生产都要用催化剂加速反应、降低能耗。: The production of the vast majority of chemical products requires catalysts to accelerate reactions and reduce energy consumption.
反应要先翻过一道\"能量门槛\"（活化能）。催化剂提供一条门槛更低的路，让反应更: Reactions must first overcome an "energy threshold" (activation energy). Catalysts provide a path with a lower threshold, allowing reactions to proceed faster without being consumed themselves ([[p:catalysis|Catalysis]]); good catalysts can also "select" desired products.
工业催化剂主要有三类：**多相**——反应物吸附在固体表面，键被削弱后重组，如合: Industrial catalysts mainly fall into three categories: **Heterogeneous** – where reactants adsorb onto solid surfaces, bonds are weakened and reorganized, such as iron for ammonia synthesis, platinum-rhodium for exhaust gas purification (see [[catalytic-converter]]), and zeolites for oil refining; **Homogeneous** – metal complexes dissolved in the reaction liquid; **Enzymes** – biological catalysts.
1835 年瑞典化学家贝采利乌斯提出\"催化\"一词。萨巴蒂埃（Paul Sab: In 1835, Swedish chemist Berzelius proposed the term "catalysis." Paul Sabatier received the 1912 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for nickel-catalyzed hydrogenation. In October 2026, the Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Henri Kagan from France and Kenso Soai from Japan, recognizing their discovery of nonlinear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric catalysis, which is crucial for manufacturing single "chiral" drug molecules.
据估计约九成的化工过程使用催化剂，化肥、燃料、塑料、药物都离不开它（见 [[ha: It is estimated that approximately 90% of chemical processes use catalysts; fertilizers, fuels, plastics, and pharmaceuticals all depend on them (see [[haber-bosch]], [[catalytic-cracking]]).
用催化剂把重油大分子\"剪\"成汽油小分子，大幅提高汽油产量。: Catalysts "cut" heavy oil large molecules into gasoline small molecules, significantly increasing gasoline production.
原油里大量是又长又重的分子。在酸性催化剂表面，长链更容易在特定位置断开，\"剪\: Crude oil consists largely of long and heavy molecules. On the surface of an acidic catalyst, these long chains are more easily broken at specific sites, "cut" into molecules the size of gasoline with high octane ratings ([[p:catalysis|Catalysis]], [[p:bond|chemical bonds]]).
流化催化裂化（FCC）让粉状沸石催化剂与热重油在提升管里混合，几秒钟完成裂化；积: Fluid catalytic cracking (FCC) mixes powdered zeolite catalysts with heavy thermal oil in a riser; cracking is completed in seconds. Carbon-coated catalysts are sent to a regenerator where the carbon is burned off, and the heat is returned to the reactor.
1937 年法国工程师胡德利（Eugène Houdry）的催化裂化装置在美国投: In 1937, French engineer Eugène Houdry's catalytic cracking unit began production in the United States; in 1942, the first fluidized bed unit was completed, providing a large amount of aviation gasoline for World War II. Starting in the 1960s, zeolite catalysts significantly increased gasoline yield.
催化裂化是现代炼油厂的核心装置之一（见 [[petroleum-refining: Catalytic cracking is one of the core units in modern refineries (see [[petroleum-refining]]), allowing more gasoline to be produced per barrel of crude oil, and serving as an important source for chemical raw materials such as propylene.
以石油和天然气为原料生产乙烯、丙烯等基础化学品，再做成塑料、纤维和橡胶。: Ethylene and propylene and other basic chemicals are produced from petroleum and natural gas, then used to make plastics, fibers, and rubber.
石油和天然气中的碳氢分子，在高温下可以被\"砸\"成乙烯、丙烯这样带双键的小分子: Carbon-hydrogen molecules in petroleum and natural gas can be "crushed" into small molecules like ethylene and propylene with double bonds under high temperatures; these double bonds are very active and can connect one after another to form long chains, becoming plastics, fibers, and rubber ([[p:bond|chemical bonds]], [[p:polymer|Polymerization]]).
核心装置是蒸汽裂解炉：把乙烷或石脑油与蒸汽混合，在 800°C 以上的炉管中停留: The core unit is a steam cracker: ethane or naphtha mixed with steam are held in furnace tubes above 800°C for less than one second, cracking into ethylene, propylene, butadiene, and aromatics, followed by quenching and separation; these "basic chemicals" then polymerize into plastics, fibers, and rubber.
1920 年新泽西标准石油公司用炼油副产的丙烯生产异丙醇，常被视为第一个石化产品: In 1920, Standard Oil of New Jersey used propylene produced as a refinery by-product to produce isopropyl alcohol, often regarded as the first petrochemical product; the petrochemical industry experienced explosive growth after World War II.
现代消费品大多含石化产品。据国际能源署估计，石化约占全球石油需求的 14%、天然: Most modern consumer goods contain petrochemicals. According to estimates by the International Energy Agency, petrochemicals account for about 14% of global oil demand and 8% of natural gas demand, representing the largest driver of oil demand growth.
把实验室反应放大成连续、安全、经济的工厂流程的工程学科。: The engineering discipline that scales up laboratory reactions into continuous, safe, and economical factory processes.
把实验室反应放大一万倍，不是\"把烧杯换成大罐\"：体积按立方增长，散热面积只按: Scaling a laboratory reaction up by ten thousand times is not simply "replacing a beaker with a large tank": volume grows according to the cube law, while heat dissipation area only grows according to the square ([[p:squarecube|Square–cube law]]); heat transfer, mixing, and safety issues will change completely. Chemical engineering researches how to scale reactions economically and safely ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]).
化学工程师把千差万别的工厂拆成几种通用的\"单元操作\"：流体输送、传热、蒸馏、: Chemical engineers break down vastly different factories into several general "unit operations": fluid transport, heat transfer, distillation, absorption, filtration, drying... then combine them with reactors and process control to build continuous-running processes.
1888 年麻省理工学院开设美国第一个化学工程课程；1915 年利特尔（Arth: In 1888, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened the first chemical engineering course in the United States; in 1915, Arthur D. Little proposed the concept of "unit operations".
化学工程让化肥、燃料、塑料和药品能以百万吨计稳定生产。1984 年印度博帕尔毒气: Chemical engineering enables the stable production of fertilizers, fuels, plastics, and pharmaceuticals on a scale of millions of tons. The 1984 Bhopal gas leak in India made "process safety" a core focus of the discipline.
分子一头亲水一头亲油，把油污包起来带进水里；硬水中也不像肥皂那样结垢。: Molecules with one hydrophilic end and one hydrophobic end can wrap oil stains and carry them into water; they do not form scale like soap does in hard water.
洗涤剂分子一头亲水、一头亲油。在水中，成千上万个分子把亲油的尾巴扎进油污里，亲水: Detergent molecules have one hydrophilic end and one hydrophobic end. In water, thousands or tens of thousands of molecules insert their hydrophobic tails into the oil stains while their hydrophilic heads face outward, wrapping oil droplets into small balls (micelles) that are carried into the water and washed away ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
肥皂也是这个原理，但在硬水中会生成\"皂垢\"。合成表面活性剂不怕硬水，配方里还: Soap also follows this principle, but it forms "soap scum" in hard water. Synthetic surfactants are not affected by hard water; formulations also include builders to aid cleaning and enzymes to decompose stains.
一战期间德国因油脂短缺开始研制合成洗涤剂；1946 年宝洁公司推出含磷酸盐助洗剂: During World War I, Germany began developing synthetic detergents due to shortages of oils and fats; in 1946, Procter & Gamble launched Tide containing phosphate builders, and synthetic detergents rapidly became widespread.
合成洗涤剂与 [[washing-machine|洗衣机]] 一起改变了家务劳动: Synthetic detergents changed household labor together with [[washing-machine|Washing machine]]. Early formulations that were difficult to degrade once caused rivers to foam up, and phosphorus-containing laundry powders led to eutrophication in lakes; starting in the 1970s, countries promoted switching to biodegradable formulations and phosphate-free laundry powders.
由成千上万个重复单元连成的长链分子；施陶丁格证明了它的存在。: Long-chain molecules formed by thousands or tens of thousands of repeating units connected together; Staudinger proved their existence.
1920 年德国化学家施陶丁格（Hermann Staudinger）发表论文，: In 1920, German chemist Hermann Staudinger published a paper proposing that rubber and cellulose are "macromolecules" linked by covalent bonds, while the mainstream view at the time held that they were merely loose aggregations of small molecules. In the 1930s, Wallace Carothers at DuPont synthesized nylon according to design, confirming this theory. Staudinger received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1953.
高分子科学让人类能\"按需设计\"材料，诞生了塑料、合成纤维、合成橡胶和涂料等庞: Polymer science enables humans to "design materials on demand," giving birth to vast industries such as plastics, synthetic fibers, synthetic rubber, and coatings (see [[plastics]], [[nylon]], [[synthetic-rubber]]).
单体连成长链；链的排列方式（直链、支链、交联）决定了材料的性格。: Monomers connect into long chains; the arrangement of the chain (straight chain, branched chain, cross-linked) determines the character of the material.
在天然橡胶中加硫加热，让分子链交联，橡胶从黏软变得坚韧耐用。: Adding sulfur to natural rubber and heating it causes molecular chains to cross-link, making rubber change from sticky and soft to tough and durable.
天然橡胶的长链分子之间没有连接，受热就黏、受冷就硬。加入硫磺加热后，硫原子在链与: Natural rubber long-chain molecules are not connected to each other; they become sticky when heated and hard when cooled. When sulfur is added and heated, sulfur atoms form "bridges" between chains (cross-linking), turning the rubber into an elastic network: it can stretch and return to its original shape, remaining stable in both hot and cold conditions ([[p:polymer|Polymerization]]).
交联越多，橡胶越硬：少量硫得到柔软的橡皮筋，大量硫得到坚硬的\"硬质橡胶\"。1: The more cross-linking occurs, the harder the rubber becomes: a small amount of sulfur yields a soft eraser, while a large amount produces hard "hard rubber." Starting in 1906, organic accelerators added significantly shortened vulcanization time.
1839 年美国人固特异（Charles Goodyear）据说是在把橡胶和硫磺: In 1839, it is said that American Charles Goodyear accidentally discovered the mixture of rubber and sulfur when dropped into a hot oven; he received a U.S. patent in 1844. Thomas Hancock in Britain applied for a patent just weeks earlier.
硫化橡胶让防水布、密封圈、传动带和 [[pneumatic-tire|充气轮胎]: Vulcanized rubber made waterproof cloth, sealing rings, drive belts, and [[pneumatic-tire|Pneumatic tire]] possible, thereby supporting the development of the bicycle and automotive industries.

复合材料让飞机、风机叶片、赛车和体育器材更轻更强。它的难题是回收困难（热固性树脂: Composites make aircraft, wind turbine blades, race cars, and sports equipment lighter and stronger. Its challenges are difficult recycling (thermoset resins cannot be remelted) and hard-to-detect internal delamination damage.

物体小到 1—100 纳米时，两件事改变了性质：表面原子比例急剧增大（[[p:s: When objects are as small as 1–100 nanometers, two things change properties: the proportion of surface atoms increases sharply ([[p:squarecube|Square–cube law]]), making particles more active; electrons confined in extremely small spaces exhibit quantum effects, causing particles of the same material to change color with size ([[p:structure|structure]]).
纳米材料可以\"自上而下\"刻小（如芯片光刻），也可以\"自下而上\"让分子自组: Nanomaterials can be "top-down" etched small (such as chip lithography) or "bottom-up" self-assembled by molecules; scanning tunneling microscopes allow people to see and move individual atoms.
1959 年 12 月，物理学家费曼（Richard Feynman）发表演讲《: In December 1959, physicist Richard Feynman delivered a speech titled "There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom," envisioning manipulation of matter at the atomic scale; in 1974, Japanese researcher Noboru Tanaka proposed the term "nanotechnology"; in 1989, IBM researchers used 35 xenon atoms to spell out "IBM." The 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to the discoverers of [[quantum-dot|Quantum dot]], and the 2025 Nobel Prize was awarded to the pioneers of metal-organic frameworks (MOF)—a class of crystals filled with nanometer-sized pores that are designable.
纳米技术已进入日常：防晒霜里的纳米氧化锌、量子点电视、芯片中的纳米结构，以及包裹: Nanotechnology has entered daily life: nano-zinc oxide in sunscreens, quantum dot televisions, nanoscale structures in chips, and lipid nanoparticles wrapping mRNA vaccines.
60 个碳原子组成的足球状分子，开启了碳纳米材料研究。: A football-shaped molecule composed of 60 carbon atoms opened up the research on carbon nanomaterials.
碳原子除了排成石墨和金刚石，还能围成封闭的球：12 个五边形让平面弯曲闭合，20: Carbon atoms can form closed spheres in addition to arranging into graphite and diamond: 12 pentagons make a plane bend and close, 20 hexagons fill the rest, exactly forming a "football" of 60 carbon atoms ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
用激光或电弧蒸发石墨，碳原子在冷却过程中自组装成 C60 等笼状分子。笼子里还能: Using lasers or electric arc evaporation of graphite, carbon atoms self-assemble into cage-like molecules such as C60 during cooling. Other atoms can also be enclosed inside the cages.
1985 年，英国的克罗托（Harold Kroto）与美国莱斯大学的柯尔（Ro: In 1985, Harold Kroto from the UK and Robert Curl and Richard Smalley from Rice University in the US discovered C60 while simulating interstellar carbon chemistry; they named it after architect Fuller, who designed domes, and the three received the 1996 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
富勒烯掀起了碳纳米材料研究的浪潮，引出了 [[carbon-nanotube|碳: Fullereness sparked a wave of research on carbon nanomaterials, leading to [[carbon-nanotube|Carbon nanotube]] and [[graphene|Graphene]]; its own applications are limited.
石墨片卷成的纳米管，强度和导电性都极好，规模化应用仍有限。: Graphene sheets rolled into nanotubes have excellent strength and conductivity, but large-scale application is still limited.
把一层石墨烯卷成无缝圆管，就是碳纳米管。管壁全是强韧的碳—碳键，理论强度极高；卷: Rolling a single layer of graphene into a seamless round tube creates carbon nanotubes. The tube walls consist entirely of strong carbon-carbon bonds, with extremely high theoretical strength; depending on the curl angle, tubes can conduct electricity like metals or be semiconductors ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
常用化学气相沉积：含碳气体在高温金属催化剂颗粒上分解，碳原子\"长\"成管子。难: Common chemical vapor deposition: carbon-containing gases decompose on hot metal catalyst particles, and carbon atoms "grow" into tubes. The challenge is controlling the curling method and arranging them neatly.
1991 年日本电气公司的饭岛澄男在电子显微镜下发现多壁碳纳米管，使它广为人知（: In 1991, Sumio Iijima of Tokyo Electron Limited discovered multi-walled carbon nanotubes under an electron microscope, making it well-known (prior to this there were sporadic observation reports); in 1993, single-walled carbon nanotubes were discovered.
目前最大的用途是锂离子电池电极里的导电添加剂。2019 年麻省理工学院用碳纳米管: Currently the largest use is as a conductive additive in lithium-ion battery electrodes. MIT used carbon nanotube transistors to create a 16-bit processor in 2019; "space elevator" is still limited by inability to produce sufficiently long perfect nanotubes.
只有一个原子厚的碳层，用胶带从石墨上剥离获得，导电导热极佳。: A carbon layer only one atom thick, obtained by peeling from graphite with tape, has excellent conductivity and thermal conductivity.
石墨烯是一个原子厚的碳蜂窝薄片。每个碳原子以强共价键连着三个邻居，所以它是已测得: Graphene is a carbon honeycomb thin sheet only one atom thick. Each carbon atom is connected to three neighbors via strong covalent bonds, so it is among the strongest materials measured; electrons move at high speed like having no mass, with excellent conductivity and thermal conductivity ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
石墨就是一层层石墨烯叠成的，层间结合很弱。最初的方法简单得惊人：用透明胶带反复粘: Graphite is composed of stacked layers of graphene, with very weak bonding between the layers. The original method was astonishingly simple: repeatedly sticking and peeling graphite with clear tape. Today, large-area thin films are primarily grown via chemical vapor deposition on copper foil, while powders are exfoliated from graphite.
2004 年英国曼彻斯特大学的盖姆（Andre Geim）和诺沃肖洛夫（Kons: In 2004, Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov from the University of Manchester in the UK isolated single-layer graphene and measured its electrical properties; the two were awarded the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics. In 2018, Cao Pran and others at MIT discovered that when two layers of graphene are stacked at an approximate "magic angle" of about 1.1°, superconductivity emerges.
石墨烯开启了\"二维材料\"研究。应用比预期慢：它没有带隙，难做晶体管，高质量量: Graphene launched research into "two-dimensional materials." Applications have been slower than expected: it lacks a bandgap, making transistors difficult to fabricate; high-quality mass production is also expensive. Currently, it is mainly used for phone heat dissipation films, composite material additives, and coatings.
石墨烯的蜂窝晶格：每个碳原子与三个邻居相连；把它卷起来就是碳纳米管，一层层叠起来: The honeycomb lattice of graphene: each carbon atom connects to three neighbors; rolling it up forms a carbon nanotube, while stacking layers creates graphite.
90% 以上是空气的固体，极轻且隔热性极好。: Over 90% is solid air, extremely light with excellent thermal insulation properties.
把凝胶里的液体换成气体，同时保住它纳米级的骨架，就得到孔隙率常超过 90% 的固: Replacing the liquid in a gel with gas while preserving its nanoscale framework yields a solid with porosity often exceeding 90%. The pores are smaller than the distance molecules of air travel freely; therefore, heat cannot easily pass through via conduction or convection from the gas, resulting in excellent thermal insulation ([[p:heat|heat transfer]], [[p:structure|structure]]).
直接晾干凝胶，液体蒸发时的表面张力会把骨架压塌。解决办法是\"超临界干燥\"：把: Simply drying a gel allows the surface tension during liquid evaporation to collapse the framework. The solution is "supercritical drying": heating and pressurizing the liquid to a supercritical state that is neither liquid nor gas, then slowly releasing it, allowing the framework to remain intact.
1931 年美国化学家基斯特勒（Samuel Kistler）在《自然》发表论文: In 1931, American chemist Samuel Kistler published a paper in Nature describing the first preparation of aerogel. In 1999, the US "Stardust" probe used aerogel to "catch" comet dust and returned it to Earth in 2006.
气凝胶用于航天器、火星车、石油管道和建筑的隔热，以及户外服装。它脆、贵，是限制大: Aerogels are used for thermal insulation on spacecraft, Mars rovers, oil pipelines, and buildings, as well as outdoor clothing. They are brittle and expensive, which are the main reasons limiting large-scale applications.
用人工设计的微结构而非化学成分实现自然界没有的性质，如负折射。: Properties not found in nature are achieved using artificially designed microstructures rather than chemical composition, such as negative refraction.
材料对波的响应不仅取决于原子，也取决于比波长更小的微结构。人工排列成千上万个微小: A material's response to waves depends not only on atoms but also on microstructures smaller than the wavelength. By artificially arranging thousands or tens of thousands of tiny "units," properties not found in nature can be created, such as negative refractive index ([[p:structure|structure]], [[p:wave|interference and resonance]]).
每个单元像一个小谐振器，对特定频率强烈响应；整体看就像折射率可\"定制\"的介质: Each unit acts like a small resonator, responding strongly to specific frequencies; overall, it resembles a medium with tunable refractive index. This enables prototype "invisibility cloaks" that bend microwaves around objects and extremely thin planar "superlenses".
1967 年苏联物理学家韦谢拉戈（Victor Veselago）理论预言负折射: In 1967, Soviet physicist Victor Veselago theoretically predicted negative-refraction materials; John Pendry proposed specific structures; in 2000, David Smith and others achieved this in the microwave band; in 2006, an invisibility cloak was demonstrated.
超材料用于新型天线、卫星通信的平板相控阵（见 [[phased-array]]）: Metamaterials are used for novel antennas, flat phased-array systems for satellite communications (see [[phased-array]]), superlenses for phone cameras, soundproofing and noise reduction, and [[stealth-technology|Stealth technology]].
用计算模拟和 AI 预测成千上万种候选材料的性质，再挑出最有希望的去合成。: Using computational simulation and AI to predict the properties of thousands or tens of thousands of candidate materials, then selecting the most promising ones for synthesis.
材料性质由原子排列和电子行为决定，可以用量子力学在计算机里算。先用计算和 AI: Material properties are determined by atomic arrangement and electron behavior and can be calculated using quantum mechanics on computers. First, use computation and AI to screen from a massive pool of candidates to identify the most promising; then synthesize them, which greatly reduces "trial and error" ([[p:optimization|optimization]]).
研究者批量计算成千上万种晶体的稳定性、带隙等性质，建成公开数据库；再训练模型预测: Researchers batch-calculate the stability, bandgap, and other properties of thousands or tens of thousands of crystals, building public databases; then train models to predict new materials, allowing robots to automatically synthesize and test them, forming a closed loop.
2011 年美国启动\"材料基因组计划\"，同年劳伦斯伯克利国家实验室推出\"材: In 2011, the US launched the "Materials Genome Initiative"; in the same year, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory released the "Materials Project" database. In 2023, DeepMind's GNoME predicted approximately 2.2 million new crystals, of which about 380,000 are considered stable; however, how many are truly novel and synthesizable remains controversial.
计算材料学正在加快电池、催化剂、光伏和半导体材料的研发（见 [[ai-for-s: Computational materials science is accelerating the development of battery, catalyst, photovoltaic, and semiconductor materials (see [[ai-for-science]], [[scientific-computing]]).
把玻璃拉成细丝，用于隔热棉、玻璃钢和电路板基材。: Drawing glass into fine filaments is used for insulation cotton, fiberglass-reinforced plastic, and substrates for printed circuit boards.
块状玻璃脆，是因为表面布满微裂纹；拉成几微米的细丝后裂纹少得多，强度大增，还柔软: Bulk glass is brittle because its surface is filled with microcracks; when drawn into filaments a few micrometers in diameter, the cracks are far fewer, leading to greatly increased strength, along with softness and flexibility ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
熔融玻璃从带有上千个小孔的铂铑合金漏板中流出、被高速拉成连续长丝，再织成布或切成: Molten glass flows from platinum-rhodium alloy leach plates with over a thousand small holes, is drawn into continuous long filaments at high speed, then woven into fabric or cut into short fibers. Fluffy glass cotton traps large amounts of stationary air, making it an excellent thermal insulation and soundproofing material; fiberglass combined with resin becomes "fiberglass-reinforced plastic".
1930 年代美国欧文斯—伊利诺伊公司的斯莱特（Games Slayter）发明: In the 1930s, Games Slayter of Owens-Illinois Company in the US invented a method for large-scale production of glass cotton; in 1938, Owens Corning Company was established, specializing in the production of fiberglass.
玻璃纤维用于建筑保温、游艇和浴缸、风机叶片，以及几乎所有电路板的基材（见 [[p: Fiberglass is used for building insulation, yachts and bathtubs, wind turbine blades, and as the substrate for almost all printed circuit boards (see [[pcb]]). It is the highest-volume and most inexpensive reinforcing fiber.
以蒸汽动力、机器纺织和工厂为标志的生产方式变革，人均产出开始持续增长。: The transformation of production methods, marked by steam power, machine spinning, and factories, saw per capita output begin to grow continuously.
一般把开端定在 1760 年代前后：1764 年前后哈格里夫斯的 [[spinn: The beginning is generally dated around the 1760s: around 1764, Hargreaves' [[spinning-jenny|Spinning jenny]]; in 1769, Arkwright's [[water-frame|Water frame]] patent; in 1769, Watt's patent for improving [[steam-engine|Steam engine]]; and in 1771, the first water-frame spinning factory. In 1830, the Liverpool-Manchester railway opened (see [[railway]]).
此前几千年人均收入几乎停滞；此后人均产出持续增长，至今涨了几十倍。人口涌向城市，: For several millennia prior, per capita income was almost stagnant; thereafter, per capita output grew continuously, rising by tens of times to date. Populations flocked to cities, where child labor and poor urban environments spurred reforms in labor laws, unions, and public health. It subsequently spread to Europe, the United States, and Japan, leading to [[second-industrial-revolution|Second Industrial Revolution]].
上：纺织—煤铁—蒸汽—交通互相推动的创新链；下：人均产出的长期变化（示意）。: Top: The innovation chain of textile-coal-iron-steam-transport mutually promoting each other; Bottom: Long-term changes in per capita output (illustrative).
用穿孔卡片控制花纹的织机，是\"可编程机器\"的鼻祖。: The loom that controlled patterns using punched cards was the ancestor of "programmable machines."
织花纹的本质是\"每一行抬起哪几根经线\"。把这个选择写成卡片上的\"有孔 /: The essence of weaving patterns is "which warp threads to raise for each row." Writing this selection as "hole/no-hole" on a card allowed the machine to do so automatically—this is an early example of controlling a machine with binary information ([[p:boolean|binary representation and logic]]).
每张卡片对应花纹的一行。探针压向卡片：遇孔穿过，带起对应经线；没孔被挡住。卡片连: Each card corresponded to one row of the pattern. A probe pressed against the card: if it encountered a hole, it passed through and raised the corresponding warp thread; if no hole was present, it was blocked. Cards were linked into a long chain for repeated use, allowing complex patterns to be woven automatically; changing a set of cards changed the pattern.
1804 年法国织工雅卡尔（Joseph Marie Jacquard）在前人基: In 1804, French weaver Joseph Marie Jacquard completed this loom based on prior work.
它让提花织物大幅降价，也引发了里昂丝织工人的抗议。巴贝奇设计分析机时借用了穿孔卡: It significantly reduced the price of figured fabrics and triggered protests by silk weavers in Lyon. When Babbage designed his Analytical Engine, he borrowed the punched card concept; later Hollerith's tabulating machines and early computers also followed this approach (see [[punched-card]]).
纺纱就是一边拉长棉纤维、一边加捻。让一个轮子同时带动多个纱锭，一个人的一次动作就: Spinning involves elongating cotton fibers while twisting them. Using a wheel to drive multiple spindles at once meant that one person's single action could spin multiple threads simultaneously ([[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]]).
纺纱工一手转动大轮，一手推拉夹住粗纱的横杆，把纤维拉细、加捻再绕到锭子上。最初是: The spinner turned a large wheel with one hand and pushed/pulled a crossbar holding the coarse yarn with the other, drawing out the fibers, twisting them, and winding them onto the spindle. Initially, there were 8 spindles; later, this increased to over 80. The yarn produced was relatively fine and weak, suitable for weft.
英国兰开夏郡的织工兼木匠哈格里夫斯（James Hargreaves）约在 17: James Hargreaves, a weaver and carpenter from Lancashire, England, invented it around 1764 and obtained the patent in 1770.
珍妮机体积小，可以放在家里使用，大大提高了纺纱效率，缓解了\"织得快、纺得慢\": The Spinning Jenny was small enough to be used at home, greatly improving spinning efficiency and alleviating the bottleneck of "weaving fast, spinning slow." Many hand-spinning workers became unemployed; some even smashed machines.
阿克赖特用水力驱动的纺纱机，催生了第一批真正的工厂。: Arkwright's water-frame spinning machine spawned the first true factories.
用水车提供持续、强大的动力（[[p:energy|能量]]），再用几对转速不同的: Using a water wheel to provide continuous, powerful power ([[p:energy|energy]]), and then using several pairs of rollers with different speeds to gradually draw out cotton fibers—the later rollers turned faster, elongating the fiber.
水力纺纱机纺出的纱结实，可以做经纱，从此纯棉布能完全在英国生产。但它又大又重，要: The yarn spun by the water-frame was strong enough for warp use, enabling pure cotton cloth to be fully produced in Britain. However, it was large and heavy, driven by water wheels at riverbanks, not suitable for home use; workers had to go to work beside the machines.
1769 年英国的阿克赖特（Richard Arkwright）取得专利；177: In 1769, Richard Arkwright of England obtained the patent; in 1771, he built a water-frame spinning factory in Cromford, where workers worked in shifts.
阿克赖特的工厂被视为现代 [[factory-system|工厂制度]] 的原型: Arkwright's factory is regarded as the prototype of modern [[factory-system|Factory system]]. In 1779, Crompton combined the advantages of the Spinning Jenny and the water-frame to invent the "Mule Spinning Machine," after which the British cotton textile industry dominated the world.
用水力或蒸汽驱动的织布机，让织布速度追上纺纱。: Looms powered by water or steam brought weaving speed up to spinning speed.
织布的动作——开口、投梭、打纬——可以分解成固定的往复运动，由凸轮和连杆机构按节: The motions of weaving—opening, shedding, picking—can be decomposed into fixed reciprocating motions, repeated rhythmically by cams and link mechanisms ([[p:division|division of labor]]). Connecting them to water or steam power allowed machines to weave continuously.
经线由机构轮流抬起和压下形成开口，梭子带着纬线穿过，再由筘把纬线打紧。一个工人可: Warp threads were raised and lowered in turn by the mechanism to form an opening; the shuttle carried weft through, and the reed tightened the weft. One worker could tend several looms simultaneously, only intervening when a thread broke.
1785 年英国牧师卡特赖特（Edmund Cartwright）取得专利。早期: In 1785, English clergyman Edmund Cartwright obtained the patent. Early machines were unreliable; they became widespread only after improvements by many people in the 1820s.
动力织机让织布速度追上了纺纱，棉布价格大幅下降。手工织布工的收入暴跌，数以十万计: Power looms brought weaving speed up to spinning speed, causing cotton cloth prices to drop sharply. Wages for hand weavers plummeted; tens of thousands of weavers fell into poverty, and the "Luddite Movement" from 1811–1816 was a protest where workers smashed machines.
快速把棉籽从棉纤维中分离出来，极大提高了棉花产量，也强化了美国南方奴隶制。: Rapidly separating cotton seeds from cotton fibers greatly increased cotton production and reinforced the slave system in the American South.
用带钩齿的转筒从棉花中钩出纤维，再让纤维穿过窄缝——棉籽太大，过不去，就被留下（: Using a rotating cylinder with hook teeth to pull fibers out of cotton, then letting the fibers pass through narrow slits—the seeds are too large to fit through and are left behind ([[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]]).
手摇或畜力带动转筒，钩齿抓住棉纤维拉过格栅，旋转刷子再把纤维从钩齿上刷下来。一人: Hand-cranked or animal-powered rotation drives the cylinder; hook teeth grab cotton fibers and pull them across a grate, while a rotating brush brushes the fibers off the hooks. By hand, one person could remove seeds from about one pound of cotton per day, whereas the cotton gin could achieve around fifty pounds.
1793 年美国的惠特尼（Eli Whitney）发明，1794 年取得专利。: Invented by Eli Whitney in the United States in 1793 and patented in 1794.
去籽不再是瓶颈，种植短绒棉一下子有利可图，美国南方迅速变成\"棉花王国\"，为英: With seed removal no longer a bottleneck, planting short-staple cotton suddenly became profitable, and the American South rapidly transformed into a "cotton kingdom," supplying raw materials to British textile factories. Tragically, this labor-saving machine instead greatly increased demand for slave labor: the number of American slaves grew from about 700,000 in 1790 to about 4 million in 1860.
让衣服可以批量缝制，是最早普及到家庭的复杂机器之一。: Making clothes mass-sewable was one of the most complex machines to be widely adopted in households.
手缝靠一根针来回穿过布。缝纫机把针眼开在针尖，再用一根梭子在布下面送出第二根线，: Hand sewing relies on a needle going back and forth through fabric. The sewing machine opens the eye at the tip of the needle, then uses a shuttle to send out a second thread underneath the fabric; the two threads interlock, requiring the machine only to move the needle up and down ([[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]]).
针带着上线刺穿布料，在下面形成一个线圈；梭子穿过线圈后，针拉紧，形成\"锁式线迹: The needle pierces the fabric with the upper thread, forming a loop underneath; the shuttle passes through the loop, and the needle tightens it, creating a "locked stitch"; the feed dog advances the fabric by one step, repeating this cycle hundreds of times per minute.
1846 年美国的豪（Elias Howe）取得锁式线迹缝纫机专利；1851 年: Elias Howe obtained the patent for the locked-stitch sewing machine in the United States in 1846; Isaac Singer launched a practical model in 1851. The Singer Company pioneered installment payments and a global sales network, becoming the first multinational enterprise.
缝纫机让成衣工业诞生，也成为最早进入千家万户的复杂机器之一。在 20 世纪的中国: The sewing machine gave birth to the ready-to-wear industry and also became one of the most complex machines to enter households. In 20th-century China, it was called one of the "three major items" along with bicycles and watches.
把工人和机器集中在一个屋檐下、按时间和分工组织生产。: Concentrating workers and machines under one roof, organizing production by time and division of labor.
把工人、机器和动力集中到一个地方，按统一时间和精细分工组织生产（[[p:divi: Concentrating workers, machines, and power sources in one place, organized by unified timing and refined division of labor ([[p:division|division of labor]]). Concentration allows sharing of a large power source; the larger the scale, the lower the unit cost ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]); factory owners can also directly supervise quality and progress.
工厂之前主流是\"外包制\"：商人把原料送到农户家纺织再收回。工厂把这一切搬进厂: Before factories, the mainstream was "outsourcing": merchants sent raw materials to households for spinning and weaving, then collected them. Factories moved all this into buildings: workers came and went on bells and shifts, with work broken down into simple processes.
1721 年英国德比的丝织厂已有工厂雏形；1771 年阿克赖特的克罗姆福德纺纱厂: By 1721, silk-weaving factories in Derby, England, already had factory prototypes; Cromford's spinning mill in Arkwright, England, in 1771 is usually considered the first modern factory. The British Factory Act of 1833 was the first to limit working hours for child labor and establish factory inspectors.
工厂制度把人从田间和家庭作坊带进了按钟表运转的车间，改变了家庭、时间观念和城市形: The factory system brought people from fields and home workshops into clockwork-operated workshops, changing notions of family, time, and urban form. It brought child labor, long working hours, and accidents, but also spawned unions, labor laws, and social security; it remains the production method for most goods in the world today.
以电力、钢铁、化工、内燃机和大规模生产为标志，诞生了现代大企业。: Marked by electricity, iron, chemicals, internal combustion engines, and mass production, modern large enterprises were born.
第一次工业革命靠蒸汽和铁；第二次工业革命让科学直接成为生产力：电、化学和钢铁都要: The First Industrial Revolution relied on steam and iron; the Second Industrial Revolution made science directly into productivity: electricity, chemistry, and iron all required laboratory research to break through ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]). Electric grids, railways, and telephones connected factories, markets, and cities into a large network ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
几大新技术同时爆发：廉价 [[steel|钢铁]]、[[electrificat: Several new technologies exploded simultaneously: cheap [[steel|iron and steel]], [[electrification|Electrification]], chemicals (dyes, fertilizers, explosives), [[internal-combustion-engine|Internal combustion engine]], and telephone/telegraph. Electric motors gave each machine its own power source, freeing factory layouts from being constrained by a single main drive shaft. Enterprises needed huge investments and national markets, leading to the emergence of large corporations, professional managers, and corporate research laboratories.
一般指约 1870–1914 年。1876 年爱迪生在门洛帕克建起\"发明工厂\: Generally refers to approximately 1870–1914. In 1876, Edison built an "invention factory" in Menlo Park, pioneering enterprise research laboratories.
美国和德国超过英国成为工业领袖，出现了标准石油、通用电气、西门子、巴斯夫等巨型企: The United States and Germany surpassed Britain as industrial leaders; giants like Standard Oil, General Electric, Siemens, and BASF emerged. Electric lights, telephones, automobiles, and [[assembly-line|Assembly line]] shaped 20th-century lifestyles.
按统一公差制造零件，任意一件都能装进任意一台机器，是大规模生产的前提。: Manufacturing parts with uniform tolerances allows any part to fit into any machine, which is a prerequisite for mass production.
如果每个零件都按同一份图纸、在规定的误差范围（公差）内制造，那么任意一个零件都能: If each part is manufactured according to the same drawing within specified error limits (tolerances), then any one part can fit into any machine without needing craftsmen to file and match each piece individually ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
靠三样东西：专用机床和夹具，让普通工人也能重复做出同样形状；\"通 / 止\"量: Relies on three things: dedicated machine tools and fixtures allowing ordinary workers to repeatedly produce identical shapes; "go/no-go" gauges for checking dimensions (see [[precision-measurement]]); unified drawings and tolerances.
18 世纪后期法国的布朗（Honoré Blanc）为火枪展示了可互换零件。功劳: In the late 18th century, Honoré Blanc of France demonstrated interchangeable parts for a flintlock musket. The credit is often given to Whitney, but his demonstration may have been selective; what truly achieved it was John Hall at the Harpers Ferry Arsenal in the 1820s, using dedicated machine tools to produce interchangeable rifle parts. This practice later became known as the "American system of manufacturing".
可互换零件是缝纫机、自行车、汽车和 [[mass-production|大规模生: Interchangeable parts are a prerequisite for sewing machines, bicycles, automobiles, and [[mass-production|Mass production]], making maintenance simple. It transforms "craftsmanship" into "craft": skills shift from workers' hands to machine tools, fixtures, and blueprints.
惠特沃思提出统一螺纹规格，任何厂家的螺丝和螺母都能互配。: Whitworth proposed unified thread specifications, allowing screws and nuts from any manufacturer to mate with each other.
螺丝和螺母要配上，牙型角度、螺距和直径都必须一致。只要全行业统一一套尺寸，任何厂: For screws and nuts to mate, the thread angle, pitch, and diameter must all be consistent. If the entire industry standardizes on a single set of dimensions, a screw from one manufacturer can mate with a nut from any other manufacturer ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
此前各厂各有各的螺纹，换螺丝要连螺母一起换。惠特沃思收集各厂样品取平均，定出牙型: Previously, each factory had its own threads; changing screws required replacing the nuts as well. Whitworth collected samples from various factories to determine an average, establishing a 55° thread angle specification; the United States adopted the 60° Sellers standard; today, the general metric ISO thread is used.
1841 年英国工程师惠特沃思（Joseph Whitworth）提出统一螺纹；: In 1841, British engineer Joseph Whitworth proposed unified threads; in 1864, American William Sellers proposed the U.S. standard. The inability of British and American threads to intermate during World War II caused maintenance difficulties, leading to the 1948 Anglo-American-Canadian "unified thread" agreement.
螺纹标准是最早的工业标准之一，也是后来各种国家和国际标准组织的起点。: Thread standards were among the earliest industrial standards and served as the starting point for various national and international standardization organizations later on.
泰勒用秒表研究每个动作并标准化，以提高工人效率。: Taylor used stopwatches to study each motion and standardize it, thereby improving worker efficiency.
把一项工作拆成一个个动作，用秒表测量，找出最快、最省力的那一种，再让所有人照做（: A task is broken down into individual motions, measured with a stopwatch, the fastest and most energy-efficient method identified, and then everyone is instructed to follow it ([[p:division|division of labor]]). Work methods are designed by managers rather than relying on workers' experience and habits.
方法包括时间研究、动作研究、标准化工具、挑选训练工人和按件计酬。: Methods include time study, motion study, standardization of tools, training and selection of workers, and piece-rate pay.
1880–1890 年代美国工程师泰勒（Frederick Winslow Ta: In the 1880–1890s, American engineer Frederick Winslow Taylor conducted experiments in steel mills; his book "The Principles of Scientific Management" was published in 1911. He stated that a worker moving iron ore increased their daily output from approximately 12.5 tons to 47 tons.
科学管理影响了流水线、工业工程和管理学。批评者认为它把人当成机器零件，剥夺了工作: Scientific management influenced assembly lines, industrial engineering, and management studies. Critics argued it treated humans as machine parts, stripped away autonomy in work, and faced strong opposition from labor unions.
让工件在传送带上移动、工人站定只做一道工序，福特 T 型车的装配时间从 12 小: Parts were made to move on a conveyor belt while workers stood still performing only one operation; the assembly time for Ford Model T cars dropped from 12 hours to approximately 1.5 hours.
1913 年，福特汽车公司在密歇根州海兰帕克工厂建成移动装配线。底盘装配时间从约: In 1913, Ford Motor Company built a moving assembly line at its Highland Park factory in Michigan. Chassis assembly time dropped from approximately 12.5 hours to approximately 1.5 hours, with inspiration partly drawn from the "disassembly lines" of Chicago's meat processing plants. In 1914, Ford raised the daily wage to $5 to retain workers who had grown weary of the assembly line.
上：传统装配（工人围着车转）与流水线（车在工人间移动）；下：福特底盘装配时间的变: Top: Traditional assembly (workers surrounding the car) versus assembly line (car moving between workers); Bottom: Changes in chassis assembly time for Ford cars.
用标准化、专用机器和流水线高速生产同一产品，单件成本大幅下降。: Using standardization, dedicated machines, and assembly lines to mass-produce a single product results in a significant reduction in unit cost.
开模具、造专用机床、建流水线要花一大笔固定成本，但一旦建好，每多造一件的成本很低: Creating molds, building dedicated machine tools, and constructing assembly lines incur a large fixed cost; however, once built, the cost per additional unit produced is very low. The greater the volume, the fewer fixed costs allocated to each unit ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]); the more products and parts are standardized, the more skilled and efficient machines and workers become ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
大规模生产的典型组合是：[[interchangeable-parts|可互换零: The typical combination of mass production is: [[interchangeable-parts|Interchangeable parts]], dedicated machine tools, [[assembly-line|Assembly line]], bulk purchasing, and national sales networks. The drawback is poor flexibility: changing a product requires retooling the entire line.
福特 T 型车是代表，1913 年起大量生产。福特曾说顾客可以要任何颜色的车，\: Ford Model T was the representative example, with mass production starting in 1913. Ford once said customers could have any color of car as long as it was black. In the 1920s, Alfred Sloan of General Motors launched different-priced brands and annual model changes, introducing variety into mass production.
大规模生产让汽车、家电、衣服和食品变得人人买得起，催生了消费社会和中产阶级。它的: Mass production made automobiles, home appliances, clothing, and food affordable for everyone, giving rise to consumer society and the middle class. Its weaknesses—large inventories, slow model changes, and batch quality issues—were later improved by [[toyota-production-system|Toyota Production System]].
准时化（JIT）和自働化，只在需要时生产需要的量，持续消除浪费。: Just-in-time (JIT) and jidoka produce only what is needed when it is needed, continuously eliminating waste.
大批量生产堆出大量库存，而库存会把次品、停机和等待都藏起来。丰田反其道而行：只在: Mass production accumulates large inventories, while inventory hides defects, stoppages, and waiting. Toyota did the opposite: producing only the required quantity at the time of need, exposing problems immediately and resolving them right away ([[p:feedback|feedback]]).
两大支柱：**准时化（JIT）**——后道工序用\"看板\"向前道领取刚好需要的: The two pillars are: **Just-in-time (JIT)**—the downstream process uses "kanban" to pull exactly the parts needed from the upstream process; the upstream process replenishes only what has been taken ("pulling" rather than "pushing"); and **jidoka**—stopping the line immediately upon detecting an anomaly and pulling the "andon" cord, preventing defective products from flowing downstream. Plus continuous improvement (kaizen).
源于丰田佐吉的自动织机（断线自动停机）；1950 年丰田英二考察福特后，大野耐一: Originating from Toyoda's automatic loom (automatic stop on breakage); in 1950, Eiji Toyoda of Toyota visited Ford; then Taiichi Ohno gradually established this system. In 1990, the book "The Machine That Changed the World" referred to it as "lean production".
丰田凭高质量、低库存成为最大的汽车制造商之一，精益思想扩展到医院、软件和创业。弱: Toyota became one of the largest automobile manufacturers by achieving high quality and low inventory. Lean thinking has expanded to hospitals, software, and startups. Its weakness is having little buffer; this was exposed by the 2011 Japan earthquake and the chip shortage during the pandemic.
\"推\"与\"拉\"：大批量生产把零件推给下一道工序，丰田用看板让下一道工序按: "Push" vs "Pull": Mass production pushes parts to the next process step, while Toyota uses kanban to have the next step pull parts as needed.
用控制图监测生产过程的波动，在出次品之前发现问题。: Use control charts to monitor fluctuations in the production process and identify problems before defective products are produced.
任何生产过程都有波动。关键是区分正常的随机波动和\"出了问题\"的异常波动：前者: All production processes have fluctuations. The key is distinguishing between normal random fluctuations and "out-of-control" abnormal fluctuations: the former are described by statistical laws, while the latter require stopping to find the cause ([[p:probability|probability and statistics]]).
控制图按时间画出抽样测得的尺寸，标出中心线和上下控制限（通常是平均值 ±3 个标: Control charts plot sampled measurements of dimensions over time, marking a center line and upper and lower control limits (typically mean ±3 standard deviations). Points within limits with no pattern indicate a stable process; once a point exceeds limits or shows continuous bias to one side, the cause must be found before many defective products are produced.
1924 年贝尔实验室的休哈特（Walter Shewhart）提出控制图。二战: Walter Shewhart at Bell Labs proposed control charts in 1924. After World War II, W. Edwards Deming taught statistical quality control in Japan; Japan established the "Deming Prize" in 1951.
统计质量控制让质量从\"事后检验挑次品\"变成\"事前控制过程\"，是日本制造业: Statistical quality control transformed quality from "post-production inspection to pick defective items" into "pre-control of the process," which is one of the important reasons for the rise of Japanese manufacturing.
把缺陷率压到百万分之 3.4 的质量管理方法。: A quality management method that reduces defect rates to 3.4 per million.
如果产品规格的允许范围足够宽，过程波动足够小，次品就会极少（[[p:probab: If the allowable range for product specifications is wide enough and process fluctuations are small, defective products will be extremely rare ([[p:probability|probability and statistics]]). "Sigma" refers to standard deviation. By convention, allowing a long-term shift of 1.5 standard deviations, a Six Sigma level corresponds to only 3.4 defects per million opportunities.
