按定义、测量、分析、改进、控制（DMAIC）的流程推进项目，用数据而非直觉找原因: Advance projects using the Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control (DMAIC) process, finding causes with data rather than intuition; trained "Black Belts" lead these projects.
1986 年摩托罗拉的工程师史密斯（Bill Smith）提出；1995 年起通: Proposed by Motorola engineer Bill Smith in 1986; General Electric president Jack Welch promoted it company-wide starting in 1995, making it popular.
六西格玛在制造、金融和医疗等行业广泛推广，常与精益结合为\"精益六西格玛\"。批: Six Sigma has been widely promoted across industries such as manufacturing, finance, and healthcare, often combined with Lean as "Lean Six Sigma." Critics argue it can easily become cumbersome certification and paperwork.
用一套软件统一管理采购、库存、生产、财务和人力。: Use a single software system to manage procurement, inventory, production, finance, and human resources uniformly.
采购、库存、生产、销售和财务本来是同一件事的不同侧面，只要放进同一个数据库，任何: Procurement, inventory, production, sales, and finance were originally different sides of the same thing; as long as they are placed in the same database, changes at any point can be immediately transmitted to other departments without layered manual reconciliation ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]]).
各模块共享同一套数据：销售接到订单，系统自动算出要多少原料、何时采购、怎么排产，: All modules share the same set of data: when sales receive an order, the system automatically calculates how much raw material is needed, when to procure it, and how to schedule production, while finance synchronizes accounting. The predecessor was Material Requirements Planning (MRP) from the 1960s.
1972 年，五名前 IBM 员工在德国创立 SAP；1990 年咨询公司高德纳: In 1972, five former IBM employees founded SAP in Germany; in 1990, consulting firm Gartner proposed the term "ERP." Oracle, Yonyou, and Kingdee are also major vendors.
ERP 成为大企业的\"中枢神经\"，但实施耗时长、费用高，失败案例不少；如今正: ERP has become the "central nervous system" for large enterprises, but implementation takes a long time, costs a lot, and there are many failed cases; it is now migrating to the cloud (see [[saas]]).
用来\"造机器的机器\"；莫兹利的螺纹车床让精密金属零件可以复制。: Used to "make machines that make machines"; Molesley's thread lathe allowed precision metal parts to be replicated.
机床是\"造机器的机器\"。刀具沿导轨和丝杠约束的路线移动，零件精度不靠工人的手: Machine tools are "machines that make machines." Cutting tools move along constrained paths defined by guideways and leadscrews; part accuracy does not depend on the worker's hand but on the machine tool itself ([[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]]). Precision machine tools can produce even more precise next-generation machine tools, with accuracy "bootstrapping" up generation after generation ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
车床让工件旋转、刀具直线移动，加工轴和螺纹；铣床让刀具旋转、工件移动，加工平面和: Lathes rotate workpieces while cutting tools move linearly to process shafts and threads; milling machines rotate the cutting tool while workpieces move to process flat surfaces and complex shapes; drilling machines, boring machines, and grinding machines each have their specialties.
1774 年英国的威尔金森（John Wilkinson）发明精密镗床，让瓦特蒸: John Wilkinson of England invented a precision boring machine in 1774, making Watt's steam engine cylinders sufficiently round; around 1800, Henry Maudslay created an all-metal thread lathe driven by a leadscrew, allowing threads to be precisely replicated for the first time; his apprentices like Whitworth became famous names of their generation.
机床让蒸汽机、枪械、缝纫机和汽车能够精确量产，是工业的\"母机\"。高端机床至今: Machine tools enabled precise mass production of steam engines, firearms, sewing machines, and automobiles, serving as the "mother machine" of industry. High-end machine tools remain a marker of a nation's manufacturing capability today and later developed into [[cnc|Computer numerical control (CNC)]].
零件尺寸允许的误差范围；测得准才能做得准。: The allowable error range for part dimensions; accurate measurement leads to accurate making.
做不出比自己测不准更准的东西。零件的尺寸永远有误差，关键是规定一个允许的误差范围: One cannot make something more accurate than one can measure it. Part dimensions always have errors; the key is to specify an allowable error range (tolerance) and have the capability to measure whether parts fall within that range ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
游标卡尺读到 0.02 毫米，千分尺读到 0.001 毫米；量块是一组极平整的钢: A vernier caliper reads to 0.02 millimeters, while a micrometer reads to 0.001 millimeters; gauge blocks are a set of extremely flat steel blocks that can be combined to form any standard length, serving as the 'ruler of rulers' for factories. All measurements ultimately trace back to the meter defined by the International System of Units.
1840–1850 年代惠特沃思制造的测量机能分辨百万分之一英寸；1848 年法: During the 1840–1850s era, Whitworth manufactured measuring instruments capable of resolving one-millionth of an inch; in 1848, Jean Laurent Palmer of France obtained a patent for the micrometer; around 1896, Carl Edvard Johansson of Sweden invented the set of gauge blocks.
精密测量是 [[interchangeable-parts|可互换零件]] 和现: Precision measurement is the foundation of [[interchangeable-parts|Interchangeable parts]] and modern manufacturing. From engines to chips, tolerances are becoming smaller, and measurement technology must also advance in sync.
小活塞上的小力通过液体传到大活塞变成巨大压力，用于锻压和成形。: Small force on a small piston is transmitted through fluid to become huge pressure on a large piston, used for forging and forming.
密闭液体中的压强处处相等（帕斯卡原理）。小活塞上的力，传到面积大一百倍的大活塞上: Pressure in a closed liquid is equal everywhere (Pascal's Principle). The force on the small piston is magnified one hundred times when transmitted to the large piston with an area one hundred times larger ([[p:fluid|fluid mechanics]], [[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]]). The cost is that the distance the large piston moves is only one-hundredth of the small piston.
液压泵把油压入大油缸，推动活塞向下加压，用于锻造、冲压、拉伸、粉末压制和打包。同: A hydraulic pump pumps oil into a large cylinder, pushing the piston downward to apply pressure, used for forging, stamping, stretching, powder pressing, and bundling. The same principle is used for car brakes, jack stands, and excavators (see [[construction-machinery]]).
1795 年英国发明家布拉马（Joseph Bramah）取得液压机专利，他的工: In 1795, British inventor Joseph Bramah obtained a patent for the hydraulic press; his craftsman Joseph Motzley solved the sealing problem.
液压机能产生巨大而平稳的压力，让大型锻件和冲压件成为可能。今天的万吨级模锻压机能: Hydraulic machines can generate huge and stable pressure, making large forged parts and stamped parts possible. Today's ten-thousand-ton die forging presses can forge the overall titanium alloy framework of aircraft, serving as key equipment for the aviation industry.
铸造把熔融金属倒进模具成形，锻造用压力让金属变形并变得更致密结实。: Casting forms molten metal into molds; forging uses pressure to deform metal and make it denser and stronger.
铸造利用液体能填满任何形状的特性，把熔化的金属倒进模具，凝固后就成形（[[p:p: Casting utilizes the characteristic that liquid can fill any shape: molten metal is poured into a mold and solidifies to form the shape ([[p:phase|phase change]]). Forging uses pressure to cause plastic deformation in solid metal, compacting internal voids and breaking down and refining grains, so forged parts are stronger than castings ([[p:structure|structure]]).
砂型铸造适合缸体等复杂件；压铸把金属液高速压入钢模，适合大批量铝件；熔模（失蜡）: Sand casting is suitable for complex parts like engine blocks; die casting presses molten metal into steel molds at high speed, suitable for large-volume aluminum parts; investment (lost-wax) casting is used for turbine blades. Forging includes free forging and die forging.
铸造和锻造都有几千年历史。1839 年英国的内史密斯（James Nasmyth: Casting and forging both have a history of several thousand years. In 1839, James Nasmyth of the UK designed a steam hammer. Starting in 2020, Tesla used ultra-large die casting machines for 'one-piece die casting' of car rear substrates, replacing dozens of stamped and welded parts.
曲轴、连杆、齿轮、飞机起落架等关键零件靠锻造；发动机缸体、机床床身和水龙头靠铸造: Critical parts like crankshafts, connecting rods, gears, and aircraft landing gear rely on forging; engine blocks, machine tool beds, and faucets rely on casting.
用电弧、激光等高温把金属局部熔化连接在一起。: Using high temperatures such as electric arcs or lasers to locally melt metal connects them together.
把两块金属的接缝处局部加热到熔化，让它们的原子重新混在一起凝固，就连成了一个整体: The seam between two metals is locally heated to melting point, allowing their atoms to mix and solidify again, forming a single whole ([[p:heat|heat transfer]]). Weld seams must prevent oxygen and nitrogen from mixing in the air, otherwise they will become brittle.
电弧焊用几千度的电弧加热，药皮或保护气体（氩气、二氧化碳）隔绝空气；电阻点焊让大: Arc welding uses an electric arc of several thousand degrees to heat; flux coating or protective gas (argon, carbon dioxide) isolates the air; resistance spot welding melts two steel plates with high current, with thousands of weld points on a car body; laser welding is fast and precise.
1881 年前后，俄国的贝纳尔多斯（Nikolai Benardos）与波兰的奥: Around 1881, Nikolai Benardos of Russia and Stanisław Olszewski of Poland invented carbon arc welding; in 1907, Oscar Kjellberg of Sweden invented flux-coated welding rods. During World War II, the US used welding instead of riveting to rapidly build over 2,700 'Liberty ships'.
焊接让船体、桥梁、管道、压力容器和汽车车身更轻更快地制造。它也是 [[indus: Welding makes ship hulls, bridges, pipelines, pressure vessels, and car bodies lighter and faster to manufacture. It is also one of the top uses for [[industrial-robot|Industrial robot]].
把熔化的塑料高压注入模具冷却成形，几秒钟就能做出一个零件。: Molten plastic is injected into a mold under high pressure and cooled to form parts; a single part can be made in seconds.
塑料加热后变成可流动的熔体，冷却后又变回固体（[[p:phase|相变]]、[[: After heating, plastic becomes a flowable melt, then returns to solid upon cooling ([[p:phase|phase change]], [[p:polymer|Polymerization]]). By injecting the melt rapidly under high pressure into a precise steel mold, parts with identical shapes can be replicated.
螺杆旋转把塑料颗粒推进加热筒熔化，再像注射器一样高压注入模具，冷却后顶出零件，一: Rotating screws push plastic granules into a heated barrel to melt them, then inject them into a mold under high pressure like a syringe; after cooling, the part is ejected. A cycle often lasts only tens of seconds. Molds are expensive, but the cost per unit decreases as volume increases.
1872 年美国的海厄特兄弟取得注塑机专利，用来成型赛璐珞；1946 年美国的亨: In 1872, the Haught brothers of the US obtained a patent for injection molding machines to form celluloid; in 1946, James Hendry of the US invented screw injection molding machines, laying the foundation for modern injection molding.
从乐高积木、瓶盖、手机外壳到汽车保险杠和医疗器械，大部分塑料零件靠注塑生产（见: From Lego bricks, bottle caps, phone shells, car bumpers, and medical devices, most plastic parts are produced via injection molding (see [[plastics]]).
用程序代替人手控制刀具轨迹，能重复加工出复杂精密的零件。: Using programs to replace human hands in controlling tool paths enables the repeated processing of complex and precise parts.
把刀具应该走的路线写成一串坐标和指令，让计算机控制电机按程序移动；位置传感器不断: Write the path the tool should follow as a string of coordinates and instructions, allowing the computer to control the motor to move according to the program; position sensors continuously report actual positions, and the controller corrects deviations in real time ([[p:feedback|feedback]]). The skill of the worker is "abstracted" into a program that can be replicated infinitely ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]]).
[[cad-cam|CAD/CAM]] 软件生成刀具路径，转成 G 代码（如 \: [[cad-cam|CAD / CAM]] software generates tool paths, converting them to G code (such as "G01 X10 Y20" indicating a straight line move to a specific point). The numerical control system drives each axis using [[servo-motor|Servo motor]] and ball screws, while controlling the spindle, coolant, and automatic tool changing. Five-axis machine tools can machine complex surfaces like turbine blades from almost any angle.
1940 年代末，美国的帕森斯（John T. Parsons）为加工直升机旋翼: In the late 1940s, John T. Parsons of the United States proposed using numerically controlled machine tools for helicopter rotor machining; in 1952, the Servo Mechanism Laboratory at MIT demonstrated the first numerical control milling machine using punched paper tape to input programs. In the 1970s, microprocessors enabled numerical control to become computer numerical control (CNC).
数控让复杂精密零件可以稳定重复制造，为柔性制造和\"黑灯工厂\"打下基础；高端五: Numerical control allows complex and precision parts to be manufactured stably and repeatedly, laying the foundation for flexible manufacturing and "black light factories"; high-end five-axis machine tools are subject to export controls.
数控机床的闭环：程序给出目标位置，传感器测量实际位置，控制器根据误差驱动电机。: The closed loop of a numerical control machine: the program specifies the target position, sensors measure the actual position, and the controller drives the motor based on the error.
在电脑上画三维模型、做仿真，再直接生成加工程序。: Draw three-dimensional models on a computer, perform simulations, and then directly generate machining programs.
在计算机里，一个零件可以表示为精确的几何模型：点、线、曲面和实体（[[p:abs: In a computer, a part can be represented as an exact geometric model: points, lines, surfaces, and solids ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]]). The same model can be used for drafting, strength simulation, assembly interference checking, and direct generation of machining programs, eliminating the need for repeated manual drafting and translation.
设计师在 CAD 软件中通过草图、拉伸、旋转等操作建立三维模型，用有限元分析检验: Designers establish three-dimensional models in CAD software through operations like sketching, extruding, and rotating; finite element analysis is used to check strength and heat dissipation; CAM software then calculates tool paths based on the model and outputs them to [[cnc|Computer numerical control (CNC)]] or [[3d-printing|3D printer]]. Surfaces on cars and airplanes are often described using mathematical curves such as Bezier curves and NURBS.
1963 年麻省理工学院的萨瑟兰（Ivan Sutherland）开发了 Ske: In 1963, Ivan Sutherland of MIT developed Sketchpad, allowing drawing with a light pen on a screen. In the 1960s, Pierre Bézier of Renault in France promoted Bezier curves for car body design. In 1977, Dassault developed CATIA; in 1982, Autodesk released AutoCAD. The Boeing 777 became the first passenger aircraft designed entirely using digital models in the 1990s.
CAD/CAM 取代了绘图板和石膏模型，让产品开发周期大大缩短，也让全球分工协作: CAD/CAM replaced drafting boards and plaster models, greatly shortening product development cycles and making global collaborative design possible (see [[computer-graphics]]).
把三维模型切成薄层、一层层堆叠材料成形，适合复杂结构和小批量定制。: Slice a three-dimensional model into thin layers and stack materials layer by layer to form shapes; this is suitable for complex structures and small-batch customization.
1980–1981 年日本的小玉秀男发表光固化成型方法；1984 年美国的赫尔（: In 1980–1981, Hideki Nishiyama of Japan published the photopolymerization molding method; in 1984, Chuck Hull of the United States applied for a patent on photopolymerization, which was approved in 1986 and led to the founding of 3D Systems. In 1989, Scott Crump applied for a patent on fused deposition modeling. Around 2009, when this patent expired, open-source projects like RepRap brought desktop printers down to hundreds of dollars.
3D 打印最大的影响在原型和定制：隐形牙套模具、助听器外壳和骨科植入物大量个性化: The greatest impact of 3D printing lies in prototyping and customization: personalized production of dental aligner molds, hearing aid shells, and orthopedic implants. GE's LEAP engine fuel nozzle printed approximately 20 parts into one, reducing weight by about 25%; rocket companies also extensively print engine components.
上：切片原理——三维模型被切成薄层，再逐层堆叠；下：三种主要工艺。: Up: Slicing principle—three-dimensional models are sliced into thin layers and then stacked layer by layer; Down: three main processes.
用聚焦激光切割、焊接、打标金属和其他材料，精度高、无接触。: Use focused lasers to cut, weld, and mark metals and other materials with high precision and without contact.
把激光聚焦到很小的光斑上，能量密度极高，能在瞬间把材料加热到熔化甚至汽化（[[p: Focus the laser on a very small spot with extremely high energy density, heating the material to melting or even vaporization in an instant ([[p:levels|energy levels]], [[p:heat|heat transfer]]). With a small spot size and small heat-affected zone, cuts are narrow and neat, non-contacting the workpiece, and without tool wear.
数控系统驱动激光头沿程序移动，辅助气体吹走熔化的材料。按功率和脉冲不同，可以切钢: The numerical control system drives the laser head to move along the program; auxiliary gas blows away molten material. Depending on power and pulse settings, steel plates can be cut, batteries welded, parts marked, or micro-machining performed using ultra-short pulses.
1960 年梅曼造出第一台 [[laser|激光器]]；1965 年美国西部电气: In 1960, Terman built the first [[laser|Laser]]; in 1965, Western Electric Company of the United States used lasers to drill holes on diamond molds. After 2000, efficient and durable fiber lasers rapidly became widespread, with Chinese manufacturers significantly lowering prices.
激光切割已成为钣金加工的标准方法，激光焊接用于汽车车身和动力电池，激光打标让零件: Laser cutting has become the standard method for sheet metal processing; laser welding is used for car bodies and power batteries; laser marking enables traceability for all parts.
把纸浆铺在移动的网带上连续成纸，让纸张和印刷品变得便宜。: Spread paper pulp on a moving mesh belt to continuously form paper, making paper and printed materials cheaper.
把纸浆稀释在水中，铺在一条不断移动的细网上，水滤掉后纤维交织成湿纸，再经压榨、烘: Dilute paper pulp in water, spread it on a continuously moving fine mesh, filter out the water so fibers interweave into wet paper, then pass through pressing and drying to become continuous paper rolls—transforming manual sheet-by-sheet papermaking into continuous production ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]).
长网造纸机由网部（成形脱水）、压榨部和烘干部组成。现代纸机宽达 10 米，车速每: Long-reel paper machines consist of the forming section (formation dewatering), press section, and dryer section. Modern paper machines are up to 10 meters wide, with speeds exceeding 1500 meters per minute, capable of producing over a thousand tons of paper per day. With raw materials expanding from rags to wood pulp, paper prices dropped significantly.
1799 年法国的罗贝尔（Louis-Nicolas Robert）取得专利；英: In 1799, Louis-Nicolas Robert of France obtained the patent; the Fourdrinier brothers in England funded improvements and began production in Britain in the early 1800s, so long-reel paper machines are often named after them. In the 1840s, Germany began using wood pulp for papermaking.
廉价的纸张与 [[rotary-printing|轮转印刷]] 结合，让报纸、杂: Cheap paper combined with [[rotary-printing|rotary printing]] brought newspapers, magazines, and books into everyday life.
用钢球或滚子把滑动摩擦变为滚动摩擦，几乎所有旋转机械都离不开它。: Using steel balls or rollers to convert sliding friction into rolling friction, almost all rotating machinery relies on it.
滚动摩擦远小于滑动摩擦（[[p:newton|牛顿力学]]）。在轴和轴座之间放一: Rolling friction is far less than sliding friction ([[p:newton|Newtonian mechanics]]). Placing a ring of steel balls or rollers between the shaft and its housing greatly reduces resistance and wear; however, the contact area is very small and stress is extremely high, so the steel balls must be extremely hard and perfectly round ([[p:stress|stress and strength]]).
轴承由内圈、外圈、滚动体和保持架组成：球轴承转速高，滚子轴承承重大。高等级钢球的: Bearings consist of an inner ring, outer ring, rolling elements, and a cage: ball bearings have high rotational speeds, while roller bearings support heavy loads. High-grade steel balls have a roundness error of less than 1 micron.
1794 年英国的沃恩（Philip Vaughan）取得球轴承专利；1883: In 1794, Philip Vaughan in the UK obtained a patent for ball bearings; in 1883, Friedrich Fischer in Germany invented a ball-grinding machine, allowing steel balls to be precisely mass-produced; in 1907, Sven Wingquist in Sweden invented the self-aligning ball bearing and founded SKF.
几乎所有旋转机械都有轴承：电动机、汽车、风机和高铁。二战中盟军曾专门轰炸德国施韦: Almost all rotating machinery has bearings: electric motors, automobiles, wind turbines, and high-speed rail. During World War II, Allied forces specifically bombed Germany's Schaeffler bearing factory.
根据误差的大小、累积和变化速度来调整控制量，是工业控制的通用公式。: Adjusting the control quantity based on the magnitude, accumulation, and rate of change of errors is a universal formula for industrial control.
核心是反馈：测量实际值，与目标比较，按误差调整输出（[[p:feedback|反: The core is feedback: measure the actual value, compare it with the target, and adjust the output according to the error ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]). PID examines three aspects of error: **Proportional (P)**—the larger the error, the more aggressive the correction; **Integral (I)**—accumulates past errors to eliminate "total small discrepancies"; **Derivative (D)**—observes the rate of change of error to take the brake early, reducing overshoot.
以空调为例：室温 28°C、目标 24°C，控制器加大制冷，接近目标时逐渐减小。: Taking air conditioning as an example: if room temperature is 28°C and the target is 24°C, the controller increases cooling; as it approaches the target, it gradually reduces output. Tuning parameters involves selecting the three coefficients P, I, and D: too weak results in slow response, too strong causes oscillation. Today, the vast majority of industrial control loops remain PID-based.
1868 年麦克斯韦用数学分析了调速器的稳定性。1922 年俄裔美国工程师米诺尔: In 1868, Maxwell used mathematics to analyze the stability of governors. In 1922, Russian-American engineer Nicolas Minorsky observed a helmsman steering a ship and proposed theoretical analysis of PID. In 1960, Rudolf Kálmán proposed the Kalman filter for Apollo navigation.
自动控制让化工厂、电网、发动机、飞机 [[autopilot|自动驾驶仪]]、机: Automatic control allows chemical plants, power grids, engines, aircraft ([[autopilot|Autopilot]]), robots, and hard drives to operate stably, making it one of the most universal theories in modern engineering.
反馈回路：目标与测量值相减得到误差，PID 控制器据此调整执行器，被控对象的输出: Feedback loop: subtracting the measured value from the target yields an error; the PID controller adjusts the actuator based on this; the output of the controlled object is then measured back by a sensor.
瓦特用转速越快飞球张得越开、进汽越少的装置稳定蒸汽机转速，是自动控制的经典起点。: Watt used a device where the faster the speed, the more the flyball opens and the less steam enters to stabilize steam engine speed; this is the classic starting point for automatic control.
转速越快，旋转的飞球受离心作用张得越开；飞球通过杠杆把进汽阀门关小，转速就降下来: The faster the rotational speed, the more the flyball opens due to centrifugal force; the flyball uses levers to close the steam valve, reducing speed; when speed drops, the flyball falls and the valve opens again. The system regulates its own input using its own output—this is negative feedback ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
两个金属球挂在由蒸汽机带动的竖轴上。负载变小，发动机加速，飞球张开，阀门关小；反: Two metal balls hang on a vertical shaft driven by a steam engine. When load decreases, the engine accelerates, the flyballs open, and the valve closes; conversely, when load increases, speed drops, the flyballs close, and the valve opens, keeping speed roughly constant.
类似装置早已用于风车磨坊调节磨盘间隙；1788 年瓦特和博尔顿把它用于蒸汽机。1: Similar devices were long used in windmill mills to adjust millstone gaps; Watt and Boulton applied it to steam engines in 1788. Maxwell analyzed in 1868 why it sometimes "oscillates," founding control theory.
离心调速器让蒸汽机能稳定驱动纺织机等机器，是工业自动控制的标志性起点，也成为\": The centrifugal governor allowed steam engines to stably drive machines like textile looms, marking the beginning of industrial automatic control and becoming a classic image of "feedback" (see [[control-theory]]).
代替大量继电器的工业专用计算机，控制生产线的每个动作。: Industrial-purpose computers replacing large numbers of relays, controlling every action on production lines.
生产线上的控制逻辑——\"传感器 A 检测到工件且门已关闭，就启动电机 B\"—: Control logic on production lines—"Sensor A detects a workpiece and the door is closed, so start Motor B"—is essentially a string of Boolean logic ([[p:boolean|binary representation and logic]]). Using one programmable computer replaces hundreds or thousands of relays and wiring; changing logic only requires changing the program ([[p:feedback|feedback]]).
PLC 周而复始地\"扫描\"：读所有输入 → 执行程序 → 刷新所有输出，每周: PLCs cyclically "scan": read all inputs → execute program → refresh all outputs, every cycle in a few milliseconds. Programs are commonly written in "ladder diagrams," resembling relay circuit diagrams, so electricians can easily handle them; they are vibration-resistant and anti-interference, capable of continuous operation for years.
1968 年通用汽车提出需求，希望换车型时不必重新布线；1969 年莫利（Dic: In 1968, General Motors proposed the requirement to avoid rewiring when changing vehicle models; in 1969, Modicon, founded by Dick Morley and others, delivered the first PLC—Modicon 084.
PLC 成为工厂自动化的\"大脑\"，控制着生产线、电梯、水处理和楼宇设备，至今: PLCs have become the "brains" of factory automation, controlling production lines, elevators, water treatment, and building equipment, remaining the mainstay of industrial control to this day.
远程监控电网、管道、水厂等大型设施的系统，也是网络攻击的目标。: Systems for remote monitoring of large facilities such as power grids, pipelines, and water plants are also targets of network attacks.
电网、油气管道、水厂这类设施分布在很大范围内，必须把各处的传感器数据实时汇总到控: Facilities like power grids, oil and gas pipelines, and water plants are distributed over a vast range; sensor data from various locations must be aggregated in real time at the control center, where humans and programs uniformly monitor and issue commands ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
现场的 PLC 和远程终端采集压力、电压等数据传到控制中心，操作员远程开关阀门和: On-site PLCs and remote terminals collect pressure, voltage, and other data and transmit them to the control center; operators remotely switch valves and circuit breakers. Many systems were designed in an era of "isolation from the outside," with weak protection, yet must run for decades without stopping, making patching difficult.
1960 年代电力行业开始使用远程监控系统。2010 年曝光的\"震网\"病毒破: During the 1960s, the power industry began using remote monitoring systems. In 2010, the "Stuxnet" virus was exposed and destroyed Iran's uranium centrifuges (see [[stuxnet]]); in 2015, a cyberattack on Ukraine's power grid caused approximately 230,000 users to lose power.
SCADA 让大型基础设施能集中、高效运行（见 [[power-grid]]），: SCADA enables large-scale infrastructure to operate in a centralized and efficient manner (see [[power-grid]]), but it also makes such systems targets for cyber warfare, making industrial control security a key focus for nations worldwide.
用相机和算法在生产线上检测缺陷、读码和引导机器人。: Cameras and algorithms are used on production lines to detect defects, read codes, and guide robots.
相机把图像变成一格格像素的数字（[[p:sampling|采样]]），算法从这些: Cameras convert images into digital grids of pixels ([[p:sampling|sampling]]), while algorithms extract edges, shapes, colors, and text from these numbers to determine whether parts are qualified, where they are located, and what they are.
工业相机配合专门的光源拍下工件，软件测量尺寸、检测缺陷、读码，或告诉机器人零件的: Industrial cameras work with specialized lighting sources to capture workpieces; software then measures dimensions, detects defects, reads codes, or tells robots the position of parts. In recent years, deep learning has been used to detect defects such as scratches that are difficult to describe using rules (see [[computer-vision]]).
1981 年美国康耐视（Cognex）公司成立，推出最早的商用机器视觉系统之一；: In 1981, American Cognex Inc. was founded and launched one of the earliest commercial machine vision systems; in the 2000s, "smart cameras" integrated processors directly into the camera bodies.
机器视觉让全检取代了抽检，广泛用于电子、汽车、药品、食品和物流分拣，也是 [[i: Machine vision has enabled full inspection to replace sampling, and is widely used in electronics, automotive, pharmaceutical, food, and logistics sorting industries. It also serves as the "eyes" of [[industrial-robot|Robotics]].
为实物建立实时同步的虚拟模型，在电脑里预测和优化它的运行。: A real-world object is established with a virtual model that synchronizes in real time; its operation is predicted and optimized within the computer.
给一台实物设备或一座工厂建一个虚拟模型，并用传感器数据让它实时同步。在模型里做实: A virtual model is built for a physical device or an entire factory, and it is made to synchronize in real time using sensor data. Experiments are conducted and failures predicted within the model, which is far cheaper and safer than trial-and-error on actual machines ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
它包括实物、虚拟模型和两者间的数据流。例如航空发动机回传温度、振动数据，模型据此: It includes the physical object, the virtual model, and the data flow between them. For example, an aircraft engine returns temperature and vibration data; the model uses this to estimate remaining life for parts and schedule maintenance; before a factory begins production, the production line is debugged in a virtual environment.
数字孪生用于发动机、风电场、工厂和城市，是 [[industry-4-0|工业: Digital twins are used for engines, wind farms, factories, and cities; they represent one of the core concepts of [[industry-4-0|Industry 4.0]]. However, many projects are merely elaborate three-dimensional displays.
用物联网、数据和 AI 把工厂里的设备、物料和系统连起来，实现柔性和自优化生产。: Using the Internet of Things, data, and AI to connect devices, materials, and systems within a factory, achieving flexible and self-optimizing production.
把机器、物料、产品和管理系统都接上网（[[p:network|网络效应]]），按: Connecting machines, materials, products, and management systems all onto the network ([[p:network|Network effects]]) allows automatic adjustment based on real-time data, forming a closed loop from order to equipment ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]), enabling personalized products with the efficiency of mass production.
智能工厂里：工业 [[iot|物联网]] 实时采集设备数据；制造执行系统（MES: In smart factories: industrial [[iot|Internet of Things (IoT)]] collects device data in real time; Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and [[erp|Enterprise resource planning (ERP)]] schedule production; vision and AI perform quality inspection and predictive maintenance; robots handle material transport and assembly; [[digital-twin|Digital twin]] debugs and optimizes in virtual environments.
\"工业 4.0\"一词 2011 年在德国汉诺威工业博览会上提出，2013 年: The term "Industry 4.0" was proposed at the Hannover Fair in Germany in 2011, became a national strategy for Germany in 2013; China proposed "Made in China 2025" in 2015. Among the "Lighthouse Factories" selected by the World Economic Forum starting in 2018, Chinese factories account for the largest number.
一些工厂已实现夜间无人值守的\"黑灯工厂\"。落地难点在于老设备改造、数据标准不: Some factories have already achieved "dark factory" operations with no human staff during night shifts. The main challenges to implementation include retrofitting old equipment, inconsistent data standards, and investment return periods.
\"1.0—4.0\"的划分是一种宣传框架：机械化、电气化、自动化、联网化，并不: The classification of "1.0—4.0" is a promotional framework: mechanization, electrification, automation, and networking; it is not a strict historical periodization.
维纳提出的研究动物和机器中控制与通信的学科，\"反馈\"成为跨学科的通用概念。: Wiener proposed the discipline studying control and communication in animals and machines; "feedback" became a universal concept across disciplines.
动物、机器和社会组织里的\"控制\"有共同的逻辑：获取信息、与目标比较、根据偏差: The logic of "control" in animals, machines, and social organizations shares commonalities: acquiring information, comparing with goals, acting based on deviations, and observing results—that is, feedback ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]). Control requires communication, which conveys information ([[p:info|Information theory]]).
控制论研究\"目的性行为\"的一般规律：恒温器保温、人伸手拿杯子、政策调控通胀，: Cybernetics studies the general laws of "purposeful behavior": a thermostat maintaining temperature, a person reaching for a cup, or policy regulating inflation can all be analyzed using the same framework. It was born concurrently with information theory and early computers, mutually inspiring each other.
1948 年美国数学家维纳（Norbert Wiener）出版《控制论：或关于在: In 1948, American mathematician Norbert Wiener published "Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine"; in 1954, Qian Xuesen published "Engineering Cybernetics".
控制论的思想渗入了自动控制、[[neural-network|神经网络]]、系统: The ideas of cybernetics have permeated automatic control, [[neural-network|neural networks]], systems biology, and management. The term "cyber" originates from it and later evolved into terms such as "cyberspace" and "cybersecurity".
把复杂项目拆成分系统、管理接口和风险，是阿波罗、高铁和芯片项目背后的方法论。: Breaking complex projects into subsystems, managing interfaces, and assessing risks is the methodology behind projects like Apollo, high-speed rail, and chips.
复杂的系统由许多分系统组成，最难的问题往往出在分系统之间的接口上。系统工程把总目: Complex systems consist of many subsystems, and the most difficult problems often arise at the interfaces between these subsystems. Systems engineering decomposes the overall goal into layers that can be developed and verified independently, while managing their interfaces, schedules, and risks ([[p:abstraction|abstraction]], [[p:division|division of labor]]).
从需求出发，分解成分系统并规定指标和接口；各自开发后逐级集成测试，最后验证是否满: Starting from requirements, subsystems are decomposed with specifications for metrics and interfaces defined; after independent development, they undergo hierarchical integration testing, finally verifying whether the requirements are met. This process is often depicted as a "V-shape": on the left, decomposition proceeds layer by layer, while on the right, verification proceeds layer by layer.
1940 年代贝尔实验室开始使用\"系统工程\"一词；1950 年代美国的洲际导: The term "systems engineering" was first used at Bell Laboratories in the 1940s; it matured in the 1950s with the US intercontinental ballistic missile project and later [[apollo|Apollo program]]. In 1978, Tsien Hsue-shen and others published "Technology of Organization and Management—Systems Engineering," which promoted the application of this discipline in China.
系统工程是航天、核电、高铁、大型芯片和 [[software-engineeri: Systems engineering is the methodology behind aerospace, nuclear power, high-speed rail, large-scale chip projects, and [[software-engineering|large software systems]].
可编程的机械臂，第一台 Unimate 在通用汽车搬运压铸件，如今主要用于焊接、: Programmable robotic arms: the first Unimate at General Motors transported die-cast parts; today they are primarily used for welding, spraying, and assembly.
1954 年美国的德沃尔（George Devol）申请专利，1961 年获批，: In 1954, George Devol of the US filed a patent; it was approved in 1961, and he co-founded Unimation with Joseph Engelberger. In 1961, the first Unimate removed hot die-cast parts from a press at General Motors' New Jersey plant. In 1974, Sweden's ASEA (now ABB) launched the fully electric, microprocessor-controlled IRB 6; Japanese companies Fanuc and Yaskawa enabled robots to enter automobile factories on a large scale.
机器人承担了焊接、喷涂、搬运等又脏又累又危险的工作。据国际机器人联合会（IFR）: Robots undertake dirty, tiring, and dangerous tasks such as welding, spraying, and material handling. According to a report by the International Federation of Robotics (IFR), approximately 603,000 new industrial robots were installed globally in 2025, setting a record high, with about 5.08 million currently in operation; China is the largest market. It will reduce some conventional positions while also creating new roles such as maintenance and programming.
带位置反馈的电机，能精确转到指定角度，是机器人关节和数控机床的执行器。: Motors with position feedback can rotate precisely to specified angles and serve as actuators for robot joints and computer numerical control machines.
伺服系统是一个闭环：电机上的编码器不断报告实际位置和速度，驱动器把它与指令比较，: A servo system is a closed loop: an encoder on the motor continuously reports actual position and speed; the driver compares this with the command, adjusts current based on the error, allowing the motor to reach the specified angle accurately and rapidly and stop ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
伺服电机多为永磁同步电机，编码器每圈可分辨上百万个位置。电机转速高、力矩小，机器: Servo motors are mostly permanent magnet synchronous motors; encoders can distinguish over a million positions per revolution. Motors have high speed but low torque; robot joints require harmonic or RV reducers to reduce speed and increase force.
\"伺服机构\"的理论在二战中为火炮和雷达瞄准而发展；1950 年代用于 [[c: Theoretical foundations of "servo mechanisms" were developed during World War II for artillery and radar aiming; in the 1950s, they were used for [[cnc|Computer numerical control (CNC)]]. In 1957, C. Walton Musser of the US invented the harmonic reducer, which later became a key component of robot joints.
伺服系统是机器人、数控机床和自动化产线的\"肌肉\"（见 [[electric-: The servo system serves as the "muscle" (see [[electric-motor]]) of robots, computer numerical control machines, and automated production lines.
能感知碰撞、可以和人在同一空间安全协作的轻型机械臂。: Lightweight robotic arms capable of sensing collisions and safely collaborating with humans in the same space.
传统机器人只按程序运动，不知道撞到了人。协作机器人在关节里装上力矩传感器或监测电: Traditional robots move according to programs but do not know if they have collided with a person. Collaborative robots install torque sensors or current monitors within their joints; upon feeling unexpected resistance, they stop immediately; by further restricting speed and force, humans can work safely in the same space as them ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
它轻巧，可以手拉着示教，几小时就能部署到新工位，无需围栏，适合拧螺丝、上下料等工: They are lightweight, allowing teaching via hand guidance; new workstations can be deployed in a few hours without fences, suitable for tasks such as screwing and loading/unloading; however, their speed and load capacity are relatively lower.
1996 年美国西北大学的科尔盖特（J. Edward Colgate）和佩什金: In 1996, J. Edward Colgate and Michael Peshkin of Northwestern University in the US proposed the term "cobot"; in 2008, Denmark's Universal Robots company sold the first commercial collaborative robot, UR5.
能自己导航的移动机器人，用于仓储搬运、配送和扫地。: Mobile robots capable of autonomous navigation are used for warehouse material handling, delivery, and cleaning.
移动机器人要不断回答\"我在哪里、周围有什么、怎么走过去\"。它一边用激光雷达和: Mobile robots must continuously answer "Where am I? What is around me? How do I get there?". They measure the surrounding environment using LiDAR and cameras while estimating their own position and correcting routes ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
早期的自动导引车（AGV）沿地面磁条行驶；自主移动机器人（AMR）用激光雷达和相: Early automated guided vehicles (AGVs) traveled along magnetic strips on the ground; autonomous mobile robots (AMR) use LiDAR and cameras for real-time mapping and localization (SLAM, see [[lidar]]), enabling them to avoid obstacles and plan their own routes.
1950 年代美国出现最早的自动导引车；1966–1972 年斯坦福研究所的 S: The earliest automated guided vehicles appeared in the US in the 1950s; Shakey at Stanford Research Institute combined perception, planning, and action for the first time between 1966 and 1972. In 2002, iRobot launched the Roomba vacuum cleaner.
移动机器人进入仓库、工厂、医院、餐厅和家庭（扫地机器人），是 [[logisti: Mobile robots enter warehouses, factories, hospitals, restaurants, and homes (vacuum cleaners), serving as the main force in [[logistics-automation|Logistics Automation]].
模仿人体结构的机器人，希望能直接在为人设计的环境中工作，正借 AI 快速发展。: Robots mimicking human structures aim to work directly in environments designed for humans; they are developing rapidly with the aid of artificial intelligence.
门、楼梯、工具和工位都是按人体设计的。做成人形，机器人就能直接进入这些环境、使用: Doors, stairs, tools, and workstations are designed for the human body. By creating humanoid robots, machines can enter these environments directly and use human tools. The challenge lies in that bipedal walking is inherently unstable; it requires adjusting joint torques hundreds of times per second to maintain balance ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]) ([[p:newton|Newtonian mechanics]]).
人形机器人有几十个由电机和减速器驱动的关节，用相机、力传感器和惯性测量单元感知。: Humanoid robots have dozens of joints driven by motors and reducers, using cameras, force sensors, and inertial measurement units for perception. Recent progress comes from two aspects: practicing walking in simulation using [[reinforcement-learning|Reinforcement learning]] before transferring to real machines; and using "vision-language-action" large models to understand instructions and manipulate objects (see [[embodied-ai]]). Dexterous hands, battery life, and cost remain bottlenecks.
1973 年日本早稻田大学造出 WABOT-1；2000 年本田发布 ASIMO: WABOT-1 was created by the University of Tokyo in 1973; Honda released ASIMO in 2000. Starting in 2013, Boston Dynamics' Atlas demonstrated running, jumping, and backflips; Tesla announced the Optimus plan in 2021; Chinese companies like Unitree and iRobot have reduced prices to tens of thousands or even hundreds of thousands of yuan. According to estimates from Counterpoint and other agencies, global shipments of humanoid robots were approximately 20,000 units in the first half of 2026, with Chinese manufacturers leading.
人形机器人目前主要用于科研、展示和工厂试点，离可靠地做家务和通用工作仍有距离，但: Currently, humanoid robots are mainly used for research, exhibitions, and factory pilots; they are still far from reliably performing household chores or general work, but are seen as an important carrier for AI entering the physical world.
用机器人、分拣系统和算法让仓库自动存取和分拣包裹。: Using robots, sorting systems, and algorithms enables warehouses to automatically store, retrieve, and sort packages.
仓库里最费时的是\"人走向货\"。让机器人把货架或货箱搬到拣货员面前（\"货到人: The most time-consuming task in a warehouse is "human walking to goods." By having robots move shelves or cargo boxes to pickers ("goods-to-person"), and using algorithms to decide where to place goods and the order of retrieval, movement can be significantly reduced ([[p:optimization|optimization]]).
常见方案：成群的机器人顶起货架送到拣货站；堆垛机在几十米高的立体货架间存取；交叉: Common solutions include: fleets of robots lifting shelves to delivery stations; stacker cranes storing and retrieving in multi-story racks up to dozens of meters high; cross-belt sorters separating tens of thousands of packages per hour by destination.
2012 年亚马逊以约 7.75 亿美元收购 Kiva Systems，大规模部: In 2012, Amazon acquired Kiva Systems for approximately 775 million US dollars, deploying shelf-handling robots on a large scale. According to Amazon's July 2025 announcement, it has deployed over 1 million robots.
物流自动化支撑了 [[e-commerce|电子商务]] 的次日达和当日达，也改: Logistics automation supports [[e-commerce|E-commerce]]'s next-day and same-day delivery, and also changes the nature of warehouse work: pickers no longer walk long distances, but their work rhythm is strictly controlled by algorithms.
把蒸汽机装上车轮在铁轨上奔跑；斯蒂芬森的\"火箭号\"（1829）奠定了基本构造: Mounting a steam engine on wheels to run on iron rails; Stephenson's "Rocket" (1829) established the basic construction.
蒸汽机把燃煤的热能变成活塞的往复运动，再由连杆变成车轮的转动（[[p:energ: Steam engines convert thermal energy from coal combustion into reciprocating motion of pistons, which is then converted into rotational motion of wheels by connecting rods ([[p:energy|Conservation of energy]]); wheels press against smooth iron rails with low friction, allowing a single locomotive to pull dozens of carriages.
锅炉把水烧成高压蒸汽，推动汽缸里的活塞来回运动，连杆带动主动轮转动。用过的蒸汽从: Boilers heat water into high-pressure steam, pushing pistons back and forth in cylinders; connecting rods drive the driving wheels to rotate. Used steam is expelled through chimneys, incidentally "drawing" the fire hotter. Locomotives advance via wheel-rail friction: the heavier and more driving wheels, the less likely they are to slip.
1804 年英国工程师特里维西克（Richard Trevithick）造出第一: In 1804, British engineer Richard Trevithick created the first steam locomotive running on iron rails. In 1829, George & Robert Stephenson's "Rocket" won the Rainhill Trials; its multi-tube boiler, exhaust blower, and nearly horizontal cylinders became the basic construction of steam locomotives for over a hundred years thereafter.
陆地上第一次出现了比马跑得快、拉得多的机器。20 世纪中叶后，它逐渐被内燃机车和: For the first time on land, a machine appeared that was faster and stronger than horses. After the mid-20th century, it was gradually replaced by diesel-electric and electric locomotives.
钢轮钢轨摩擦小、可编组长列车，让陆上运输成本骤降，重塑了经济地理。: Steel wheels on steel rails have low friction, allowing long trains to be formed, causing transportation costs on land to drop sharply and reshaping economic geography.
钢轮压在钢轨上，接触面只有硬币大小，滚动阻力只有汽车轮胎在公路上的五分之一到十分: Steel wheels pressing on steel rails have contact areas the size of a coin; rolling resistance is only one-fifth to one-tenth of that of automobile tires on roads ([[p:newton|Newton's laws of motion]]: the same force can push greater mass). Connecting carriages into long trains allows one driver and one locomotive to transport over a thousand tons, with costs diluted by volume ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]).
铁路由四部分组成：**轨道**（钢轨、轨枕和道砟把重量分散到路基上）、**机车车: Railways consist of four parts: **tracks** (steel rails, sleepers, and ballast disperse weight to the subgrade), **locomotives and rolling stock**, **signaling and dispatching** (ensuring only one train per section at a time, called "block"), **stations and marshalling yards**.
车轮踏面略呈锥形：过弯时外侧车轮自动滚到直径更大的位置，列车自己\"找正\"，不: Wheel treads are slightly conical: when turning, the outer wheel automatically rolls to a larger diameter position, allowing the train to self-center without a steering wheel. Also due to low friction, train braking distances are long; intervals must be controlled several kilometers in advance via signals.
1825 年英国斯托克顿—达灵顿铁路开通，是第一条使用蒸汽机车的公共铁路。183: In 1825, the Stockton and Darlington Railway in Britain opened, being the first public railway using steam locomotives. In 1830, the Liverpool-Manchester Railway opened, being the first intercity railway fully using steam locomotives and operating on a timetable. In 1869, the first transcontinental railway in the United States was completed.
铁路让煤、钢和粮食的运价大降，工厂不必再建在河边，城市沿着铁路生长。它还催生了第: Railways greatly reduced transportation costs for coal, steel, and grain; factories no longer needed to be built near rivers, and cities grew along railways. It also spawned the first modern large corporations and unified standard time (see [[standard-gauge]]).
铁路的核心发明是\"轨道 + 信号 + 调度\"这套系统，机车只是其中一部分。马: The core invention of railways is the "tracks + signaling + dispatching" system; locomotives are only part of it. Horse-drawn rail cars existed before steam locomotives.
火车为什么拉得动上千吨：钢轮钢轨滚动阻力极低；锥形踏面让列车过弯时自动对中。: Why trains can pull over a thousand tons: steel wheels on steel rails have extremely low rolling resistance; conical treads allow trains to self-center when turning.
统一轨距让火车跨线直通；铁路时刻表还催生了统一的标准时间和时区。: Unified track gauge allows trains to run directly across lines; railway timetables also spawned unified standard time and time zones.
铁路是一张网，只有轨距一致，车辆才能从一条线开到另一条线（[[p:standar: Railways are a network; only with consistent track gauge can vehicles travel from one line to another ([[p:standard|Standardization]]); a globally unified timetable requires all stations to use the same time.
标准轨距是两条钢轨内侧相距 1435 毫米，来自斯蒂芬森在英国煤矿铁路上的习惯尺: The standard gauge is the distance of 1435 millimeters between the inner sides of two steel rails, a conventional dimension from Stephenson's railway in British coal mines. When lines with different gauges connect, cargo must be unloaded and reloaded, or the vehicles' bogies must be changed.
1846 年英国议会通过《轨距法》，规定新建客运铁路采用标准轨距。1847 年英: In 1846, the British Parliament passed the "Railway Act", stipulating that new passenger railways adopt standard gauge. In 1847, most British railway companies switched to Greenwich Mean Time; on November 18, 1883, railways in the United States and Canada unified to adopt the standard time zone.
今天全世界约六成铁路使用标准轨距，俄罗斯、印度等仍用宽轨。铁路时间则演变成了今天: Today, about sixty percent of railways worldwide use standard gauge, while Russia, India, and others still use broad gauge. Railway time has evolved into today's time zone system (see [[time-standard]]).
把铁路建到城市地下，伦敦大都会铁路是第一条，后来改用电力。: Building railways underground in cities: the London Metropolitan Railway was the first, later switching to electric power.
城市地面寸土寸金，把轨道放到地下或高架上，列车就不必和行人、汽车抢路；一列地铁能: Urban land is extremely valuable; placing tracks underground or on elevated structures means trains do not need to compete with pedestrians and automobiles for road space. A single metro train can carry over a thousand people, and a channel of the same width has a capacity several times that of a road ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]).
早期地铁用\"明挖回填\"法：挖开街道、修好隧道再盖上，后来改用盾构机在地下推进: Early metros used the "cut-and-cover" method: excavating streets, building tunnels, then covering them; later, shield tunneling machines were adopted to push underground (see [[tunnel-boring-machine]]). Modern metros are all electrically driven; signal systems can shorten train intervals to about two minutes, and some new lines have already achieved fully automatic driverless operation.
1863 年 1 月，伦敦大都会铁路（Metropolitan Railway）: In January 1863, the London Metropolitan Railway opened, becoming the world's first metro, initially using steam locomotives with smoke-filled tunnels. In 1890, London opened its first deep-buried electric metro line; in 1904, the New York City Subway opened. In January 1969, Phase I of Beijing Metro Line 1 opened, marking China's first metro.
地铁让大城市能容纳上千万人口而不被交通拖垮，也决定了城市沿哪些方向扩张：地铁站周: Metros enable large cities to accommodate over ten million people without being crippled by traffic, and they determine urban expansion directions: areas around metro stations are often where housing prices and commercial activity are most concentrated.
由接触网或第三轨供电的电力牵引，比蒸汽和内燃更强劲、更干净。: Electric traction powered by overhead catenary or third rail is more powerful and cleaner than steam and internal combustion engines.
磁场中的通电导线会受力（[[p:lorentz|电磁力]]），电动机把电网送来的: A current-carrying wire in a magnetic field experiences force ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]); motors convert the electricity sent from the grid directly into wheel rotation, eliminating the need to burn coal or oil on board.
电力经接触网（架空线）或第三轨送到列车，驱动牵引电机。电力机车没有锅炉和发动机，: Electricity is delivered to trains via overhead catenary (aerial lines) or third rail to drive traction motors. Electric locomotives have no boilers or engines; under the same weight, they offer greater power and faster acceleration. During deceleration, motors can generate electricity backfed to the grid, known as "regenerative braking".
1879 年，德国西门子（Werner von Siemens）在柏林工业博览会: In 1879, German Werner von Siemens demonstrated the first practical electric locomotive at the Berlin Industrial Exposition. Countries like Switzerland, rich in hydroelectric power, pioneered large-scale electrification.
电气化让地铁、长大隧道和山区铁路变得可行，也是高速铁路的前提；铁路因此能用上越来: Electrification makes metros, long tunnels, and mountain railways feasible, and is a prerequisite for high-speed rail; railways can thus utilize increasingly clean electricity.
时速 250 公里以上的铁路系统；日本新干线首开，中国建成了世界最大的高铁网。: Railway systems exceeding 250 km/h: the Japanese Shinkansen opened first; China has built the world's largest high-speed rail network.
空气阻力大约随速度的平方增长，克服它所需的功率随速度的立方增长（[[p:flui: Aerodynamic drag increases approximately with the square of speed, while the power required to overcome it increases with the cube of speed ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]). Therefore, higher speeds require more streamlined front ends; simultaneously, requirements for turning radius and track smoothness increase drastically—high-speed rail is essentially "rebuilding a whole set of lines for speed" ([[p:newton|Newton's laws of motion]]).
高铁有三个关键：: High-speed rail has three key elements:
**专用线路**：大半径曲线、极其平顺的无砟轨道、大量的桥梁和隧道，不与慢车混跑: **Dedicated tracks**: large-radius curves, extremely smooth ballastless tracks, extensive bridges and tunnels, without sharing tracks with slow trains. **Distributed power multiple units**: traction motors are distributed under multiple carriages, offering fast acceleration and low pressure on tracks. **Automatic train control**: at 300 km/h, a driver cannot see signals several kilometers away; train speed and intervals are continuously monitored by onboard computers and ground systems; overspeed triggers automatic braking.
1964 年 10 月，日本东海道新干线在东京奥运会前夕开通，最高时速 210: In October 1964, the Tokaido Shinkansen in Japan opened just before the Tokyo Olympics, reaching a maximum speed of 210 km/h, becoming the world's first high-speed rail. The French TGV opened in 1981. In 2008, the Beijing-Tianjin Intercity Railway opened, marking China's entry into the high-speed rail era; by 2025, China's high-speed rail operating mileage exceeded 50,000 kilometers, accounting for about two-thirds of the world.
在几百到一千多公里的距离上，高铁从市中心直达市中心，门到门时间常常不输飞机，能耗: Over distances ranging from hundreds to over a thousand kilometers, high-speed rail goes directly from city center to city center; door-to-door time often rivals air travel, with far lower energy consumption. It compresses the "time distance" between cities, making cross-city commuting a reality.
速度翻倍，空气阻力约变成 4 倍，所需功率约变成 8 倍。高铁在 300 公里时: Doubling speed increases aerodynamic drag to approximately four times, and required power to approximately eight times. At 300 km/h, most traction power on high-speed rail is spent pushing air aside.
用电磁力让列车悬浮并推进，没有轮轨摩擦；上海磁浮是首条商业高速线。: Using electromagnetic force to levitate and propel trains eliminates wheel-rail friction; the Shanghai Maglev was the first commercial high-speed line.
利用电磁力（[[p:lorentz|电磁力]]）让列车浮起、离开轨道，再用\"展: Using electromagnetic force ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]) to lift the train off the track, then using "linear motors" to push it forward, eliminating wheel-rail friction and wear.
常导磁浮（如德国 Transrapid）靠电磁铁吸向导轨，悬浮间隙约 1 厘米，: Conventional electromagnet levitation (such as Germany's Transrapid) uses electromagnets attracted to guide rails, with a suspension gap of about 1 centimeter, adjusted by computers over a thousand times per second; superconducting magnet levitation (such as Japan's L0 series) can lift approximately 10 centimeters. Propulsion relies on linear motors: coils in the guide rail are sequentially energized to "pull" the train forward.
2004 年 1 月，上海磁浮示范线投入商业运营，全长约 30 公里，最高运营时: In January 2004, the Shanghai Maglev Demonstration Line entered commercial operation, with a total length of about 30 kilometers and a maximum operating speed of 431 km/h; since 2021, it has been reduced to 300 km/h. Japan's Central Nankai Shinkansen (Tokyo-Nagoya) adopts superconducting magnet levitation and is currently under construction.
磁浮证明了无接触高速运行可行，但造价高、不能与现有铁路互通，至今只有少数线路。: Maglev demonstrates that contactless high-speed operation is feasible, but it has high costs and cannot connect with existing railways; to date, only a few lines exist.
链条传动、前后同大轮子的\"安全自行车\"成型于 1880 年代，是能效最高的交: Chain drive with front and rear wheels of equal size, known as the 'safety bicycle,' emerged in the 1880s and became one of the most energy-efficient modes of transport.
链条和大小齿轮组成一套杠杆系统（[[p:leverage|机械增益]]），让人用: Chains and gears of different sizes form a lever system ([[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]]), allowing riders to achieve suitable speeds with comfortable pedal cadence. When calculated by energy consumption per kilometer, cycling is several times easier than walking and ranks among the most energy-efficient transportation methods.
\"安全自行车\"改用链条驱动后轮，比早期大前轮的\"高轮车\"稳得多；充气轮胎: The 'safety bicycle' became much more stable after adopting chain drive for the rear wheel compared to early 'penny-farthing' bicycles with large front wheels; pneumatic tires (see [[pneumatic-tire]]) further enhanced its comfort. Bicycles do not rely on leaning to stay upright: when the bike leans to one side, the front wheel turns that way, effectively 'steering' the body back into balance.
1885 年英国人斯塔利（John Kemp Starley）推出\"罗孚\"（: In 1885, British engineer John Kemp Starley launched the 'Rover' safety bicycle, establishing the basic form of bicycles used today.
自行车是第一种平民买得起的个人交通工具，它带动的滚珠轴承、钢管车架等技术后来用到: The bicycle was the first personal transportation mode affordable to the general public; technologies such as ball bearings and steel tube frames it drove later found applications in automobiles and aircraft.
由内燃机驱动的个人交通工具；本茨的三轮车被视为第一辆现代汽车。: Personal transportation powered by internal combustion engines; Benz's tricycle is regarded as the first modern automobile.
内燃机让燃料在汽缸里燃烧，把化学能直接变成推动活塞的力（[[p:energy|能: Internal combustion engines allow fuel to burn within cylinders, directly converting chemical energy into force that pushes pistons ([[p:energy|Conservation of energy]]); gasoline has high energy density, enabling hundreds of kilometers per tank. Friction between tires and ground then converts engine torque into forward motion ([[p:newton|Newton's laws of motion]]).
一辆汽车可以拆成五个系统：**动力**（发动机或电机）；**传动**（离合器和变: A single automobile can be decomposed into five systems: **Power** (engine or motor); **Transmission** (clutch and gearbox adjust engine speed to appropriate wheel speed, while differential allows left and right wheels to rotate at different speeds during cornering); **Chassis** (suspension, steering, braking); **Body**; and **Electrical & Electronics** (today, a single vehicle contains dozens to hundreds of electronic control units). Engines operate in a four-stroke cycle: 'intake—compression—power—exhaust' (see [[internal-combustion-engine]]).
1886 年德国人卡尔·本茨（Karl Benz）为他的三轮\"奔驰专利汽车\": In 1886, German engineer Karl Benz filed a patent for his three-wheeled 'Benz Patent-Motorwagen,' which is regarded as the first modern automobile; in the same year, Gottlieb Daimler and Wilhelm Maybach built four-wheeled automobiles. In 1908, the Ford Model T launched the era of mass-produced automobiles (see [[model-t]]).
汽车重塑了城市形态（郊区、购物中心、停车场）、石油地缘政治和日常生活。今天全世界: Automobiles reshaped urban forms (suburbs, shopping malls, parking lots), petroleum geopolitics, and daily life. Today, over 1 billion automobiles are in use worldwide; the cost is approximately 1.19 million deaths annually from road traffic accidents (World Health Organization data) as well as massive carbon emissions.
本茨不是唯一的\"汽车发明人\"。更早已有居纽（Nicolas-Joseph C: Benz was not the sole 'inventor of the automobile.' Earlier, there were steam-powered vehicles by Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot in 1769 and various trials of internal combustion engine vehicles; Benz's contribution was designing the engine and chassis as an integrated whole and investing in sales.
汽车的五大系统。燃油车和电动车的主要区别在\"动力\"和\"传动\"两块，底盘和: The five major systems of automobiles. The primary differences between fuel-powered cars and electric vehicles lie in 'Power' and 'Transmission'; chassis and body remain largely similar.
第一款真正的大众汽车，流水线让基本款售价从 825 美元一路降到 260 美元。: The first truly mass-produced automobile; assembly lines drove the base model price down from $825 to $260.
产量越大，每辆车分摊的设备和设计成本越低，工人也越熟练（[[p:scale|规模: Higher production volumes result in lower equipment and design costs per vehicle, with workers becoming more skilled ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]); price reductions attract more buyers, forming a positive cycle.
T 型车结构简单坚固，能跑乡间土路，零件可以互换，农民自己就能修。1913 年福: The Model T had a simple, robust structure capable of handling rural dirt roads, with interchangeable parts that allowed farmers to repair it themselves. In 1913, Ford introduced the moving assembly line, reducing total assembly time from over ten hours to approximately one and a half hours (see [[assembly-line]]); in 1914, the daily wage for workers was raised to $5.
1908 年 10 月上市。1909 年基本款售价 825 美元，到 1925: Launched in October 1908. The base model price was $825 in 1909, dropping to $260 by 1925; production ceased in 1927 after approximately 15 million units were manufactured.
T 型车让汽车从富人的玩具变成普通家庭的工具，\"福特制\"大规模生产方式影响了: The Model T transformed automobiles from a toy for the wealthy into a tool for ordinary families; the 'Fordist' mass production method influenced manufacturing throughout the entire 20th century.
用空气垫缓冲震动，让车辆更舒适、更快。: Using air cushions to buffer vibrations, making vehicles more comfortable and faster.
密闭的空气受压后会把力均匀地传向四周（[[p:fluid|流体压力与升力]]）。: Compressed air in a closed system transmits force evenly in all directions ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]). Compressed air inside tires acts like a spring pad, absorbing road bumps while keeping tires firmly in contact with the ground for better grip.
现代轮胎由胎面、帘布层和胎圈组成，橡胶要经过硫化（见 [[vulcanizati: Modern tires consist of tread, carcass layers, and bead circles; rubber must undergo vulcanization (see [[vulcanization]]) to achieve wear resistance and heat tolerance. Tread patterns are responsible for water drainage, preventing 'hydroplaning' in rainy conditions. Radial tires that emerged in the late 1940s offer better fuel economy and durability.
1888 年苏格兰兽医邓禄普（John Boyd Dunlop）为儿子的三轮车发: In 1888, Scottish veterinarian John Boyd Dunlop invented a practical pneumatic tire for his son's tricycle. In the 1890s, French Michelin brothers applied detachable pneumatic tires to bicycles and automobiles.
没有充气轮胎，自行车和汽车都快不起来，也坐不舒服。: Without pneumatic tires, both bicycles and automobiles would be slow and uncomfortable.
装上发动机的两轮车，在亚洲等地是最普及的机动交通工具。: Two-wheeled vehicles equipped with engines are the most widely used motorized transportation modes in Asia and other regions.
把小型内燃机装到两轮车上，用最少的金属和燃料换来机动性（[[p:energy|能: Mounting a small internal combustion engine on a two-wheeled vehicle trades minimal metal and fuel for mobility ([[p:energy|Conservation of energy]]).
摩托车的发动机多为单缸或双缸，功率与重量之比很高。它靠骑手的转向和身体倾斜保持平: Motorcycle engines are typically single-cylinder or dual-cylinder, offering a high power-to-weight ratio. They maintain balance through the rider's steering and body lean; during cornering, the vehicle body must press inward toward the curve to balance gravity with centrifugal effects. Today, electric motorcycles and electric bicycles are rapidly gaining popularity in Asia, replacing engines with batteries and hub motors.
1885 年，戴姆勒和迈巴赫造出\"骑式车\"（Reitwagen），被视为第一: In 1885, Daimler and Maybach built the "Reitwagen," regarded as the first internal combustion motorcycle. Japanese companies such as Honda pushed small-displacement motorcycles to a global market during the 1950s–1960s.
在东南亚、南亚和非洲，摩托车是最普及的机动交通工具，常常是一个家庭买得起的第一辆: In Southeast Asia, South Asia, and Africa, motorcycles are the most widely used motorized transportation mode; they are often the first "car" a family can afford. They also serve as the main force for ride-hailing services, food delivery, and courier logistics.
三点式安全带、安全气囊、防抱死制动等让车祸死亡率大幅下降。: Three-point seatbelts, airbags, and anti-lock braking systems have drastically reduced mortality rates from traffic accidents.
车祸伤害来自身体在极短时间内的速度骤变。安全带和气囊把\"停下来\"的时间拉长、: Injuries from traffic accidents stem from rapid changes in velocity within extremely short time intervals. Seatbelts and airbags extend the duration of "stopping" and increase the area over which force is applied; for the same change in momentum, the impact force becomes much smaller ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]]); anti-lock braking systems prevent wheel lockup through feedback control ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
**三点式安全带**把冲击力分散到骨盆和胸骨；**安全气囊**在碰撞后几十毫秒内: **Three-point seatbelts** distribute impact forces to the pelvis and sternum; **airbags** inflate within tens of milliseconds after a collision; **crumple zones** absorb energy through controlled deformation; **ABS** releases and re-applies brakes multiple times per second, allowing steering even during hard braking; **ESC** independently brakes specific wheels to prevent skidding.
1959 年沃尔沃工程师博林（Nils Bohlin）发明三点式安全带，沃尔沃把: In 1959, Volvo engineer Nils Bohlin invented the three-point seatbelt; Volvo opened the patent for free use by all car manufacturers. In 1978, Bosch launched modern electronic ABS.
美国按行驶里程计算的交通死亡率比 1970 年下降了约四分之三。: Traffic mortality rates in the United States have dropped by approximately three-quarters when calculated per mile traveled since 1970.
全封闭、立体交叉的快速公路，塑造了郊区化和公路货运。: Fully enclosed, grade-separated expressways shaped suburbanization and highway freight transport.
把汽车和行人、自行车、路口彻底分开，没有红绿灯和横穿，车流就能以高速稳定流动；道: By completely separating cars from pedestrians, cyclists, and intersections—eliminating traffic lights and crosswalks—traffic flows at high speeds with stability; the denser the road network, the more places each car can reach, and the greater the value of automobiles ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]).
高速公路有四个特征：**全封闭**（只能从匝道进出）、**立体交叉**、**中央: Expressways possess four characteristics: **fully enclosed** (access only via ramps), **grade separation**, **central median separation**, and **high design speed** (large-radius curves, gentle slopes). Consequently, their capacity is several times higher than ordinary roads, and accident rates per mile are lower.
1932 年德国科隆—波恩高速公路开通，被视为第一条现代高速公路。1956 年美: The Cologne-Bonn expressway in Germany opened in 1932, regarded as the first modern expressway. In 1956, the United States passed the Federal-Aid Highway Act, constructing an interstate highway network totaling approximately 78,000 kilometers. The Shanghai-Jiaxing Expressway opened in 1988, marking China's first expressway; today, China's total expressway mileage ranks first globally.
高速公路让卡车承担了大部分中短途货运，也推动了美国的郊区化。批评者认为，穿城高速: Expressways enabled trucks to bear most medium- and short-distance freight loads, also driving American suburbanization. Critics argue that urban expressways fragmented communities and intensified dependence on automobiles.
碎石分层压实再覆盖沥青，让道路平整防水。: Layered compaction of crushed stone followed by asphalt creates a smooth, waterproof road surface.
把碎石按大小分层压实，石块互相嵌锁，把车轮的压力分散到更大的地面上（[[p:st: Compacting crushed stone in layers by size allows stones to interlock, distributing wheel pressure over a larger ground area ([[p:stress|Stress, strain & strength]]); an asphalt layer is then applied on top to bind and waterproof the surface.
苏格兰工程师麦克亚当（John Loudon McAdam）发现，只要路基排水良: Scottish engineer John Loudon McAdam discovered that with good subgrade drainage, several layers of compacted small crushed stone can support vehicles. Later, people used tar or asphalt to bind the stones together (the English word "tarmac" derives from tar + macadam). Modern road surfaces are divided into flexible asphalt roads and rigid concrete roads.
麦克亚当在 1820 年前后推广他的筑路法。1902 年英国人胡利（Edgar: McAdam promoted his road construction method around 1820. In 1902, British engineer Edgar Purnell Hooley obtained a patent for tar-crushed-stone roads.
平整、防水的路面让汽车和自行车跑得起来，下雨天的道路也不再是一片泥泞。: Smooth, waterproof road surfaces enable cars and bicycles to move; roads on rainy days are no longer muddy.
用红黄绿灯分配路口通行权，早期用煤气灯，后来改用电灯并联网协调。: Traffic right-of-way at intersections is allocated using red-yellow-green lights; early systems used gas lamps, later switched to electric lights with network coordination.
路口是两股车流的\"冲突点\"，红绿灯按时间轮流分配通行权，把空间上的冲突变成时: Intersections are "conflict points" where two streams of traffic meet; traffic lights allocate right-of-way in time turns, converting spatial conflicts into temporal queues; connected signal systems can also adjust timing based on real-time traffic flow ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
最简单的信号灯按固定周期切换；感应式信号灯用地下线圈或摄像头检测排队车辆；\"绿: The simplest signal lights switch at fixed cycles; inductive signal lights use underground coils or cameras to detect queued vehicles; "green wave bands" allow a series of intersections to turn green sequentially. Many cities also use AI to optimize timing for entire regions in real time.
1868 年，伦敦议会大厦前装了一盏手动操作的煤气信号灯，不久因爆炸停用。191: In 1868, a manually operated gas signal light was installed before London's Palace of Westminster; it was soon discontinued due to an explosion. In 1914, Cleveland, USA, installed the first set of electric traffic lights; red-yellow-green three-color lights appeared in the 1920s.
信号灯和统一的交通规则让汽车大规模进入城市成为可能。: Signal lights and unified traffic rules made it possible for automobiles to enter cities on a large scale.
用电池和电机驱动的汽车，能效约为燃油车的 3 倍，锂电池降价让它成为主流。: Cars powered by batteries and electric motors achieve an energy efficiency approximately three times that of internal combustion engine vehicles. The declining cost of lithium-ion batteries has made them the mainstream choice.
燃油发动机把燃料的大部分能量变成废热，电动机则很高效（[[p:energy|能量: Internal combustion engines convert most fuel energy into waste heat, whereas electric motors are highly efficient ([[p:energy|Conservation of energy]]): according to data from the U.S. Department of Energy, electric vehicles can deliver over 77% of grid electricity to the wheels, while gasoline vehicles achieve only about 12%–30%. The price of lithium batteries has fallen rapidly with increased production ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]), accelerating adoption after crossing a tipping point ([[p:scurve|technology S-curves]]).
电动车的核心是\"三电\"：**电池包**由几千个锂离子电芯组成，由电池管理系统: The core components of an electric vehicle are "three electrics": the **battery pack** consists of thousands of lithium-ion cells and is monitored by a battery management system; the **motor** is typically a permanent magnet synchronous motor; and the **electronic control unit** contains an inverter that converts direct current into alternating current to drive the motor (see [[inverter]]). Electric motors can output maximum torque from zero speed, enabling rapid acceleration. During deceleration, the motor generates electricity, storing kinetic energy back into the battery. They lack transmissions and exhaust pipes, resulting in significantly fewer moving parts.
19 世纪末纽约就有电动出租车，但铅酸电池又重又贵，很快败给了燃油车。2008: Electric taxis existed in New York at the end of the 19th century, but lead-acid batteries were too heavy and expensive, quickly yielding to gasoline vehicles. In 2008, Tesla's Roadster demonstrated that lithium-ion battery electric vehicles could be both fast and long-range; China began promoting new energy vehicles from 2009, with manufacturers like BYD rising in the 2020s. According to the International Energy Agency, global sales of electric vehicles (purely electric plus plug-in hybrids) exceeded 20 million units in 2025, accounting for approximately one-quarter of new vehicle sales.
电池成了汽车上最贵的部件，产业重心向电池、芯片和软件转移；中国成为最大的电动车生: Batteries have become the most expensive component on an automobile, shifting industrial focus toward batteries, chips, and software; China has emerged as the world's largest producer and exporter of electric vehicles.
电动车不是\"零排放\"：发电和造电池都有排放，减排效果取决于电网有多清洁；但按: Electric vehicles are not "zero-emission": emissions occur during electricity generation and battery manufacturing, so emission reduction effectiveness depends on how clean the grid is; however, when calculated over the full lifecycle, they remain significantly lower than gasoline vehicles in most countries.
同样 100 份能量，汽油车大部分变成发动机和排气的废热；电动车大部分到达车轮（: For the same 100 units of energy, most becomes waste heat from the engine and exhaust in a gasoline vehicle; in an electric vehicle, most reaches the wheels (data: U.S. Department of Energy fueleconomy.gov).
发动机加电机协同工作并回收制动能量，丰田普锐斯开创了量产。: The synergy between the engine and motor, combined with regenerative braking energy recovery, was pioneered by mass production in the Toyota Prius.
发动机在低速和频繁起停时效率最差。让电机在这些时候帮忙或单独驱动，刹车时再把动能: Internal combustion engines operate least efficiently at low speeds and during frequent stop-and-go conditions. Allowing motors to assist or drive alone during these periods, and recovering kinetic energy into the battery during braking ([[p:energy|Conservation of energy]]), enables the engine to work more within its efficient operating range.
**油电混合（HEV）**不用插电，靠发动机和刹车回收充电，如丰田的行星齿轮\": **Hybrid electric vehicles (HEV)** do not require plugging in; they charge via the engine and regenerative braking from brakes, such as Toyota's planetary gear "power split" system; **plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEV)** have larger batteries allowing pure electric driving for daily commutes; in **extended-range electric vehicles**, the engine generates electricity only while wheels are driven entirely by motors.
1997 年丰田普锐斯在日本上市，是第一款大规模量产的混合动力汽车。: The Toyota Prius launched in Japan in 1997 as the first mass-produced hybrid vehicle.
混动车显著降低了油耗，也为电动车培养了电机、电池和电控的供应链。在中国，插电混动: Hybrid vehicles significantly reduce fuel consumption and have cultivated a supply chain for electric motors, batteries, and electronic controls. In China, plug-in hybrids and extended-range electric vehicles have been important drivers of new energy vehicle growth during the 2020s.
公共快充、家用充电桩和换电站组成的\"新加油站\"。: Public fast-charging stations, home charging piles, and battery swap stations form a "new gas station" ecosystem.
充电功率 = 电压 × 电流（[[p:ohm|欧姆定律与电路]]）。要在十几分钟: Charging power equals voltage multiplied by current ([[p:ohm|Ohm's law & circuits]]). To charge dozens of kilowatt-hours within tens of minutes, hundreds to over a thousand volts of high voltage and hundreds of amperes of large current are required, with simultaneous thermal management control.
**交流慢充**（家用桩约 7 千瓦）充满要几个小时；**直流快充**直接给电池: **AC slow charging** (home chargers at approximately 7 kilowatts) takes several hours to fully charge; **DC fast charging** directly charges the battery with power ranging from tens to hundreds of kilowatts, while next-generation "megawatt-class" ultra-fast charging can reach 1000 kilowatts. **Battery swap stations** allow full battery replacement in minutes. Interface standards vary by region, such as China's GB/T, Europe's CCS, and North America's NACS.
2012 年特斯拉开始建设超级充电网络。中国的公共充电桩数量居世界首位。: Tesla began constructing its Supercharger network in 2012. China hosts the largest number of public charging piles in the world.
\"车少桩不建、桩少车不买\"是个鸡生蛋的问题，往往需要政府和企业一起先投入。: "Few cars, no need to build piles; few piles, no reason to buy cars" is a chicken-and-egg problem, often requiring joint investment by governments and enterprises.
用摄像头、雷达、激光雷达和 AI 感知环境并自主驾驶；DARPA 挑战赛是起点。: Using cameras, radar, LiDAR, and AI to perceive the environment and enable autonomous driving; the DARPA Grand Challenge was the starting point.
自动驾驶是一个\"感知—预测—规划—控制\"的反馈回路（[[p:feedback: Autonomous driving operates as a "perception-prediction-planning-control" feedback loop ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]): sensors continuously measure, computers compare "where it should be" with "where it actually is," and continuously adjust steering and throttle. Uncertainty always exists on roads, so perception and prediction must be expressed using probability ([[p:probability|Probability & statistical inference]]).
**摄像头**识别车道线、红绿灯和行人；**毫米波雷达**测距测速，不怕雨雾；*: **Cameras** identify lane markings, traffic lights, and pedestrians; **millimeter-wave radar** measures distance and speed, remaining unaffected by rain or fog; **LiDAR** generates three-dimensional point clouds (see [[lidar]]). Deep learning models fuse this information to predict the position of surrounding objects several seconds ahead, then plan safe and comfortable trajectories. Recent "end-to-end" methods use a single large model to directly output driving actions from images.
行业用 SAE 的 0–5 级划分自动化程度：L2 仍需司机全程监督，L4 在限: The industry uses SAE's 0–5 level scale to classify automation levels: L2 still requires driver supervision throughout, while L4 achieves full autonomy within defined geographic areas.
2004 年美国 DARPA 大挑战赛，没有一辆车跑完全程；2005 年斯坦福大: In the 2004 U.S. DARPA Grand Challenge, no vehicle completed the course; Stanford University's Stanley won in 2005. Google launched its autonomous driving project (later Waymo) in 2009, and Waymo One began passenger service in Phoenix in December 2018. According to TechCrunch, by September 2026, Waymo operated paid autonomous ride-hailing services in approximately 15 U.S. cities, handling about 500,000 rides per week; Baidu's "Apollo Go" and others also operate in multiple Chinese cities.
无人驾驶出租车已在一些城市成为日常服务，但要在所有天气和道路上替代人类司机，还要: Autonomous ride-hailing services have become routine in some cities, but replacing human drivers across all weather conditions and road types requires solving rare scenarios, regulatory issues, and accident liability problems.
市售汽车的\"智能驾驶\"大多是 L2 级驾驶辅助（见 [[adas]]），司机: Most "intelligent driving" features in consumer vehicles are Level 2 driver-assistance systems (see [[adas]]), requiring constant driver monitoring with no hands-off or eyes-off allowed.
自动驾驶的反馈回路：感知 → 预测 → 规划 → 控制，每秒循环数十次；底部是: The feedback loop of autonomous driving: Perception → Prediction → Planning → Control, cycling dozens of times per second; at the bottom are SAE Levels 0–5.
自适应巡航、车道保持、自动紧急制动等，介于人驾和自动驾驶之间。: Adaptive cruise control, lane keeping, automatic emergency braking, and similar functions sit between human driving and full autonomy.
用传感器替司机\"盯着\"路面，发现危险就报警或直接干预（[[p:feedbac: Sensors replace the driver in 'watching' the road; upon detecting danger, they alert or directly intervene ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]): humans remain responsible for judgment, while machines ensure the driver does not get distracted.
常见功能有**自适应巡航**（自动跟车加减速）、**车道保持**、**自动紧急制: Common features include **adaptive cruise control** (automatic following and acceleration/deceleration), **lane keeping**, **automatic emergency braking** (AEB), **blind spot monitoring**, and **automatic parking**. Cruise control combined with lane keeping is commonly referred to as Level 2 'combined driving assistance'; some systems can now drive according to navigation on urban roads.
1990 年代后期，日本和德国车企开始提供自适应巡航。欧盟从 2022 年起要求: In the late 1990s, Japanese and German automakers began offering adaptive cruise control. The EU mandated automatic emergency braking and other safety features as standard equipment for new models starting in 2022.
驾驶辅助能减少追尾等事故，但也带来\"过度信任\"的风险：司机以为车能自己开，注: Driving assistance can reduce accidents such as rear-end collisions, but it also brings the risk of 'over-trust': drivers believe the car can drive itself, leading to decreased attention.
发射激光并测量回波时间，生成周围环境的三维点云。: Laser pulses are emitted and their round-trip time is measured to generate a three-dimensional point cloud of the surrounding environment.
光速已知，测出激光脉冲从发出到反射回来的时间，就能算出距离（[[p:optics: Since the speed of light is known, measuring the time from emission to reflection allows calculation of distance ([[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]]); rapidly scanning the laser beam across the surroundings yields a three-dimensional 'point cloud' composed of hundreds of thousands of points.
机械式激光雷达靠旋转扫描 360 度；固态和半固态方案用微振镜或光学相控阵改变光: Mechanical LiDARs rotate to scan 360 degrees; solid-state and semi-solid solutions use micro-electromechanical systems or optical phased arrays to steer the beam, making them smaller and cheaper. They can precisely measure distances at night, but performance degrades in heavy rain or dense fog.
激光发明后不久，激光雷达就用于气象和测绘，1971 年阿波罗 15 号用它测绘月: Shortly after the invention of lasers, LiDAR was used for meteorology and surveying; the Apollo 15 mission used it to map the lunar surface in 1971. In the 2020s, Chinese manufacturers reduced automotive-grade LiDAR costs to a few hundred dollars.
激光雷达给了机器人和汽车精确的\"立体视觉\"，也用于测绘森林、发现丛林下的古代: LiDAR provides robots and cars with precise 'stereoscopic vision'; it is also used for forest mapping and discovering ancient sites beneath jungles.
用手机定位和匹配算法即时连接乘客与司机。: Mobile phone positioning and matching algorithms instantly connect passengers with drivers.
手机定位加匹配算法（[[p:optimization|优化与梯度下降]]），把\: Mobile phone positioning plus matching algorithms ([[p:optimization|Optimization & gradient descent]]) transform 'hailing' from a chance-based roadside activity into real-time matchmaking; the more drivers and passengers, the faster cars wait, making the platform more attractive ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
乘客下单后，平台根据位置、路况和预计到达时间为订单挑选司机，用动态定价在高峰期调: After a passenger places an order, the platform selects a driver based on location, traffic conditions, and estimated arrival time; dynamic pricing adjusts supply and demand during peak hours, while carpooling combines passengers traveling in the same direction. A two-way rating system builds trust between strangers. All of this relies on satellite positioning (see [[gnss]]) and mobile internet.
2009 年优步（Uber）在旧金山成立；2012 年滴滴打车成立，2016 年: Uber was founded in San Francisco in 2009; Didi Chuxing was established in 2012, and Didi acquired Uber's China business in 2016.
网约车改变了城市出行习惯和出租车行业，也引发了关于零工劳动者权益、数据安全和算法: Ride-hailing services have changed urban travel habits and the taxi industry, sparking debates over gig worker rights, data security, and algorithmic pricing.
共享单车、电动滑板车等短途交通，解决\"最后一公里\"。: Shared bicycles, electric scooters, and other short-distance transport modes solve the 'last mile' problem.
城市里大多数出行只有几公里，用又小又轻的车辆完成\"最后一公里\"，能量和道路空: Most urban trips are only a few kilometers long; completing the 'last mile' with small, lightweight vehicles achieves the highest efficiency for energy and road space; mobile phone scanning and positioning allow vehicles to be picked up and returned on demand, where denser deployment means greater convenience ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
共享单车用智能锁、卫星定位和移动支付实现无桩借还；电动滑板车把骑行距离扩大到 5: Shared bicycles use smart locks, satellite positioning, and mobile payment for un-stationed borrowing and returning; electric scooters extend riding distances to 5–10 kilometers. Operators schedule vehicles based on demand forecasts.
