2015 年 ofo 在北京大学推出无桩共享单车，2016 年摩拜进入上海，共享: In 2015, ofo launched un-stationed shared bicycles at Peking University; Mobike entered Shanghai in 2016, triggering an explosion of shared bicycles in China; starting in 2017, American companies Bird and Lime promoted shared electric scooters. Around 2018, over-investment and capital chain breakage left large areas of 'bicycle graveyards'.
共享单车让城市自行车出行明显回升，也逼着城市重新规划自行车道和停车空间。: Shared bicycles have significantly increased urban bicycle travel and forced cities to replan bicycle lanes and parking spaces.
柴油卡车承担了大部分陆上货运，\"门到门\"灵活性是铁路比不了的。: Diesel trucks bear most land freight; their 'door-to-door' flexibility is unmatched by rail.
柴油机热效率高、扭矩大（[[p:energy|能量守恒]]），一辆重型卡车能拉几: Diesel engines have high thermal efficiency and high torque ([[p:energy|Conservation of energy]]); a heavy truck can haul tens of tons of cargo; with an extensive road network, trucks can deliver goods directly from factory gates to warehouse gates, where larger batches yield greater economies of scale ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]).
重型卡车多由牵引车和半挂车组成，挂车可以随时更换，牵引车不必等装卸。集装箱下船后: Heavy trucks are typically composed of tractor units and semi-trailers, which can be swapped as needed without waiting for loading/unloading; containers offloaded by ship are mostly transported by truck for the final leg (see [[container-shipping]]); electric heavy-duty trucks are being promoted on fixed routes such as ports and mines.
1896 年戴姆勒造出第一辆汽油卡车。高速公路网建成后，公路货运在许多国家超过了: In 1896, Daimler built the first gasoline-powered truck. After the highway network was completed, road freight surpassed rail transport in many countries.
卡车让工厂不必建在铁路旁，支撑了现代零售和电商，也是道路碳排放的重要来源。: Trucks allowed factories to be built away from railways, supporting modern retail and e-commerce, and are also a major source of road-related carbon emissions.
专用道上的快速公交以较低成本获得接近地铁的运量，起源于巴西库里蒂巴。: Bus rapid transit on dedicated lanes achieves passenger volumes comparable to subways at lower costs, originating in Curitiba, Brazil.
一辆公交车能装几十到上百人，占用的道路却只相当于两三辆小汽车；给它专用道和优先信: A single bus can carry dozens to over a hundred people while occupying road space equivalent to only two or three small cars; by providing it with dedicated lanes and signal priority, one can achieve passenger volumes comparable to subways at very low cost ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]).
快速公交（BRT）的关键是：**专用道**、**车外售检票和水平登车**（像地铁: The key elements of Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) are: **dedicated lanes**, **fare collection outside the vehicle and level boarding** (like subway rapid entry/exit), **signal priority at intersections**, and **large-capacity vehicles**. Construction costs are typically only a fraction of those for subways.
1974 年巴西库里蒂巴在建筑师出身的市长勒讷（Jaime Lerner）推动下: The BRT system in Curitiba, Brazil, was launched in 1974 under the leadership of Jaime Lerner, an architect-turned-mayor; subsequently, systems such as TransMilenio in Bogotá, Colombia (2000) and Guangzhou BRT in China (2010) were built.
BRT 为发展中国家的城市提供了买得起的大运量交通。城市公交也在电动化：深圳在: BRT provided affordable, high-capacity transportation for cities in developing countries. Urban bus systems are also undergoing electrification: Shenzhen achieved full electric bus operation by the end of 2017.
在街道上行驶的电力轨道车，曾遍布城市，后在许多地方复兴为轻轨。: Electric rail vehicles that ran on city streets once covered many urban areas and have since been revived in many places as light rail.
在街道上铺轨、用架空线供电，由电动机驱动车厢（[[p:lorentz|电磁力]]: Railways laid on streets, powered by overhead lines, driven by electric motors ([[p:lorentz|Lorentz force]]); with low rolling resistance from steel wheels on steel rails, a tram carries more passengers and runs more smoothly than a bus.
有轨电车可以与汽车共用路面，也可以走专用轨道；现代轻轨车辆采用低地板设计，乘客平: Trams can share the road with cars or use dedicated tracks; modern light rail vehicles adopt low-floor designs for level boardings; some sections in older urban areas switch to ground power supply, eliminating overhead lines to protect streetscapes.
1881 年，西门子在柏林郊外的利希特费尔德开通了世界上第一条商业运营的电车线。: In 1881, Siemens opened the world's first commercially operated electric tram line in Lichterfelde, just outside Berlin. In the early 20th century, trams were widespread across European and American cities; during the 1930s to 1960s, many cities dismantled trams in favor of buses and cars; since the 1980s, countries like France have seen a revival of tramways.
有轨电车塑造了早期的\"电车郊区\"，今天的轻轨则常被用来带动旧城更新。: Trams shaped early "tram suburbs," while today's light rail is often used to drive urban renewal in old city areas.
让舱体在低压管道中高速运行的设想，多家公司已倒闭，至今没有商业线路。: Concepts involving high-speed operation of cabins within low-pressure pipelines have led to the bankruptcy of many companies, with no commercial lines built to date.
空气阻力随气压降低而减小（[[p:fluid|流体压力与升力]]）。把管道抽成低: Air resistance decreases as atmospheric pressure drops ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]). By evacuating the pipeline to create low pressure and using magnetic levitation to eliminate friction, passenger cars could theoretically operate at speeds approaching those of airplanes on the ground.
按设想，乘客舱在接近真空的密封钢管里由直线电机推进、磁力悬浮。难点在于：上百公里: As envisioned, passenger cabins would be propelled by linear motors and magnetically suspended within sealed steel tubes near a vacuum. Challenges include maintaining low pressure and extreme straightness over hundreds of kilometers, accommodating thermal expansion and contraction, earthquakes, emergency evacuation, and astronomical costs.
真空管道列车的想法 20 世纪初就有人提出；2013 年马斯克（Elon Mus: Ideas for vacuum tube trains were proposed in the early 20th century; Elon Musk published a "Hyperloop" white paper in 2013, reviving interest. The most prominent startup company, Hyperloop One, ceased operations at the end of 2023.
至今没有任何商业线路建成。它更像一个提醒：物理上可行，不等于工程上和经济上可行。: To date, no commercial lines have been built. It serves more as a reminder that physical feasibility does not imply engineering or economic feasibility.
用蒸汽机驱动的船，摆脱了对风的依赖，后来发展为钢铁船体和螺旋桨推进。: Steam-powered ships broke their dependence on wind; they later evolved into steel hulls with screw propeller propulsion.
蒸汽机提供不依赖风向的持续动力（[[p:energy|能量守恒]]）；把水向后推: Steam engines provided continuous power independent of wind direction ([[p:energy|Conservation of energy]]); by pushing water backward, the ship moves forward ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]]).
早期蒸汽船用船侧的明轮划水，后来改用船尾的螺旋桨（见 [[screw-prope: Early steamships used side-mounted paddle wheels to push water; later, they adopted rear-mounted screw propellers (see [[screw-propeller]]). Starting in the mid-19th century, hulls shifted from wood to iron and steel, allowing larger and more robust vessels; multi-stage expansion steam engines, followed by turbines and diesel engines, continuously reduced fuel consumption, making long-distance voyages no longer require frequent stops for coal refueling.
1807 年美国人富尔顿（Robert Fulton）的蒸汽船\"克莱蒙特号\": In 1807, Robert Fulton's American steamship "Clermont" began regular service on the Hudson River, becoming the first commercially successful steamship. In 1838, the "Great Western" launched regular trans-Atlantic steam shipping; in 1843, the "Great Britain," designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel, combined iron hulls with screw propellers.
蒸汽船让航期变得可以预测，横渡大西洋从一个多月缩短到两周左右，推动了移民潮、殖民: Steamships made voyage durations predictable, reducing the crossing of the Atlantic from over a month to about two weeks, driving immigration waves, colonial expansion, and global trade.
水下旋转的螺旋桨把水向后推，比明轮更高效，成为船舶标准推进方式。: Underwater rotating screw propellers push water backward more efficiently than paddle wheels, becoming the standard propulsion method for ships.
螺旋桨的每片桨叶都像一个旋转的小\"机翼\"，把水向后加速推出，反作用力推动船前: Each blade of a propeller acts like a rotating small "wing," accelerating water backward; the resulting reaction force pushes the ship forward ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]], [[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]).
螺旋桨装在船尾水下，比明轮更不受风浪影响，也不易被击毁。转得太快时，桨叶背面压力: Propellers are mounted at the stern below the waterline, making them less susceptible to wind and waves than paddle wheels, and harder to destroy. If they spin too fast, low pressure on the back of the blades creates bubbles (cavitation), which damages the blades and generates noise; this is especially fatal for submarines.
1836 年英国的史密斯（Francis Pettit Smith）和瑞典的埃里: In 1836, Francis Pettit Smith from Britain and John Ericsson from Sweden almost simultaneously applied for patents for propellers. In 1845, the British Navy connected a screw-propelled ship, the 'HMS Nautilus', to the stern of a paddle-wheel ship, the 'HMS Alektor', in a tug-of-war; the screw-propelled ship dragged its opponent backward.
螺旋桨成为几乎所有船舶的标准推进方式；同样的原理也用在飞机螺旋桨、风扇和水泵上。: The propeller has become the standard propulsion method for almost all ships; the same principle is also used in aircraft propellers, fans, and water pumps.
苏伊士运河（1869）和巴拿马运河（1914）大幅缩短全球航线。: The Suez Canal (1869) and the Panama Canal (1914) significantly shortened global shipping routes.
海运成本大致与航程成正比，挖开一条地峡就能把航程缩短成千上万公里，成本随之大降（: Shipping costs are roughly proportional to the distance traveled. Digging a strait can shorten the route by thousands or tens of thousands of kilometers, causing costs to drop dramatically ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]).
苏伊士运河连接地中海和红海，是没有船闸的海平面运河；巴拿马运河要翻过中部山地，用: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea; it is a sea-level canal without locks. The Panama Canal crosses central mountain ranges, using locks to lift ships about 26 meters into an artificial lake before lowering them down.
1869 年苏伊士运河开通，由法国人雷赛布（Ferdinand de Lesse: The Suez Canal opened in 1869, constructed under the direction of Frenchman Ferdinand de Lesseps; the United States completed the Panama Canal in 1914, whereas previous attempts by France failed due to malaria, yellow fever, and funding issues.
苏伊士运河让阿拉伯海到伦敦的航程缩短约 8900 公里。运河也是全球贸易的\"咽: The Suez Canal shortened the voyage from the Arabian Sea to London by approximately 8,900 kilometers. The canal is also the 'choke point' of global trade: in March 2021, the 'Ever Given' ran aground, blocking the Suez Canal for six days and disrupting global supply chains.
用标准尺寸的铁箱装货，船、火车、卡车直接换装，海运成本暴跌，造就了全球化。: Using standard-sized iron boxes for cargo allowed ships, trains, and trucks to be directly transshipped, causing shipping costs to plummet and creating globalization.
货物千奇百怪，装卸就慢。把它们全部装进统一尺寸的钢箱，船、火车、卡车和起重机只需: Cargo is incredibly varied, making loading and unloading slow. By putting everything into uniform steel containers, ships, trains, trucks, and cranes only need to handle one type of 'standard part' ([[p:standard|Standardization]]). The larger the ship, the lower the fuel and crew cost per box: cargo capacity grows with the cube of size, while water resistance mainly grows with the ship's surface area, which is proportional to the square of size ([[p:squarecube|Square–cube law]], [[p:scale|Economies of scale]]).
国际标准集装箱宽 8 英尺，长 20 或 40 英尺，运量用\"标准箱\"（TE: International standard containers are 8 feet wide and 20 or 40 feet long; capacity is calculated using 'standard containers' (TEU, one 20-foot container). The eight corners of each box have standard corner fittings, allowing them to be lifted by lifting gear, stacked in layers, and secured with twist locks. Container ships, railway flatcars, and truck trailers are all designed to the same dimensions, allowing boxes to be transshipped between them without opening; this is called 'intermodal transport'.
1956 年 4 月，美国卡车运输商麦克莱恩（Malcom McLean）用改装: In April 1956, American trucking merchant Malcom McLean used a modified oil tanker, the 'Ideal X', to transport 58 containers from New Jersey; this is considered the beginning of modern container shipping. In the late 1960s, the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) established container standards. Today's largest container ships can carry over 24,000 standard containers.
装卸一艘船从一周左右缩短到一两天，海运费在商品价格里变得微不足道，全球分工的产业: Loading and unloading a ship was shortened from about a week to one or two days; ocean freight became negligible in commodity prices, making global industrial division of labor possible. Today, about ninety percent of non-bulk cargo worldwide is transported by container ships.
集装箱本身没有什么高科技。它的威力来自\"所有人都用同一个尺寸\"，标准化带来的: Containers themselves have no high-tech features. Their power comes from 'everyone using the same dimension'; the system effect brought by standardization far exceeds any improvement in a single piece of equipment.
集装箱之前，货物要一件件搬上搬下；之后，同一个箱子在船、火车和卡车之间直接换装，: Before containers, goods had to be moved up and down one by one; afterwards, the same box could be directly transshipped between ships, trains, and trucks without opening it throughout the entire journey.
能下潜到深海的耐压舱；中国\"奋斗者号\"2020 年坐底马里亚纳海沟。: Pressure-resistant compartments capable of submerging to deep sea depths; China's 'Fendouzhe' reached the bottom of the Mariana Trench in 2020.
水深每增加 10 米，压力增加约 1 个大气压（[[p:fluid|流体压力与升: For every 10 meters increase in water depth, pressure increases by approximately one atmosphere ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]). At a depth of ten thousand meters, there are about 1,100 atmospheres of pressure, equivalent to more than a ton pressing down on a fingernail; therefore, pressure-resistant vessels must be made spherical to evenly distribute stress using high-strength materials ([[p:stress|Stress, strain & strength]]).
深潜器由耐压球舱、浮力材料、压载和推进器组成。下潜时带着压载铁，到底后抛掉一部分: Deep-sea submersibles consist of a pressure-resistant sphere, buoyancy material, ballast, and propulsion units. When descending, they carry iron ballast; upon reaching the bottom, part of it is jettisoned to hover, and all of it is jettisoned when ascending.
1960 年 1 月，皮卡德（Jacques Piccard）和沃尔什（Don: In January 1960, Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh descended to the Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench aboard the 'Trieste' for the first time. In November 2020, China's 'Fendouzhe', carrying three people, reached the bottom of the Challenger Deep at a depth of 10,909 meters.
载人深潜让科学家亲眼看到深海热液、冷泉和深渊生物。: Crewed deep-sea submersibles allowed scientists to see deep-sea hydrothermal vents, cold seeps, and abyssal organisms firsthand.
哈里森的精密钟表让船员能在海上准确测定经度。: Harrison's precise timekeeper enabled sailors to accurately determine longitude at sea.
地球每小时自转 15 度。船上带一只走得准的钟，始终显示出发港的时间，再与当地正: The Earth rotates 15 degrees per hour. By carrying an accurate clock on board that always displays the departure port's time and comparing it with the local noon moment, the time difference can be converted into longitude ([[p:standard|Standardization]]).
难点是让钟在颠簸和温度变化中走几个月也不偏：误差一分钟，在赤道上就差约 28 公: The challenge was to keep the clock running for months without deviation despite bumps and temperature changes; a one-minute error equates to approximately 28 kilometers at the equator. Harrison used bimetallic strips to compensate for temperature changes, ultimately creating an H4 the size of a pocket watch.
1714 年英国议会悬赏征集测定海上经度的方法。1761–1762 年，哈里森（: In 1714, the British Parliament offered a prize for a method to determine longitude at sea. Between 1761 and 1762, Harrison's H4 was tested during an 81-day voyage to Jamaica; after deducting the previously determined daily difference, it lagged by only about 5 seconds.
精确的经度让海图和航行安全大幅改善。直到 20 世纪，无线电授时和卫星导航（见: Precise longitude greatly improved nautical charts and navigation safety. Until the 20th century, radio time signals and satellite navigation (see [[gnss]]) replaced the marine astronomical chronometer.
蒙戈尔菲耶兄弟用热空气比冷空气轻的原理首次载人升空。: The Montgolfier brothers achieved the first manned flight by utilizing the principle that hot air is lighter than cold air.
热空气比冷空气轻，气球内外的密度差产生向上的浮力（[[p:fluid|流体压力与: Because hot air is lighter than cold air, the density difference between the inside and outside of the balloon generates an upward buoyant force ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]], Archimedes' principle).
把一立方米空气从 20°C 加热到 100°C，大约只能多托起 0.25 公斤，: Heating one cubic meter of air from 20°C to 100°C can only support an additional 0.25 kg; therefore, a manned hot air balloon must be several thousand cubic meters in size. Modern hot air balloons use propane burners for heating and can only control vertical ascent and descent; horizontal movement relies entirely on seeking different wind directions at different altitudes.
1783 年 11 月，法国蒙戈尔菲耶兄弟（Montgolfier brothe: In November 1783, the French Montgolfier brothers made the first manned free flight with a hot air balloon; in December of the same year, Jacques Charles ascended in a hydrogen balloon.
人类第一次离开地面。气球随后被用于气象观测、军事侦察和高空科学研究，探空气球至今: For the first time, humans left the ground. Balloons were subsequently used for meteorological observation, military reconnaissance, and high-altitude scientific research, with weather balloons still being released globally every day.
用轻于空气的气体浮起、带发动机可操控的飞行器，因兴登堡号事故而衰落。: Airships capable of floating on gases lighter than air and equipped with engines for maneuverability declined due to the Hindenburg disaster.
用比空气轻的氢气或氦气提供浮力（[[p:fluid|流体压力与升力]]），再装上: By using hydrogen or helium (gases lighter than air) to provide buoyancy ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]) and equipping them with engines and control surfaces, one can fly against the wind to a designated location.
硬式飞艇有铝合金骨架，里面装着多个气囊；软式飞艇没有骨架，靠内部气压撑住外形。飞: Rigid airships have aluminum alloy skeletons containing multiple gas bags; soft airships lack skeletons and rely on internal pressure to maintain their shape. Airships do not require runways, can hover for long periods, but are slow, susceptible to strong winds, and extremely large in volume.
1900 年德国齐柏林（Ferdinand von Zeppelin）的 LZ: In 1900, Ferdinand von Zeppelin of Germany achieved the first flight of LZ 1. In May 1937, when the hydrogen-filled "Hindenburg" landed in New Jersey, USA, it caught fire, resulting in 36 fatalities, marking the end of the passenger airship era.
飞艇开辟了最早的定期空中客运，今天仍用于广告、监测和科研，也有公司在研制货运飞艇: Airships pioneered the earliest scheduled air passenger transport; today they are still used for advertising, monitoring, and research, and some companies are developing cargo airships.
莱特兄弟首次实现有动力、可操纵的持续飞行；关键是三轴控制。: The Wright brothers achieved the first powered, controllable, sustained flight; the key was three-axis control.
机翼把迎面的气流向下偏转，空气就给机翼一个向上的反作用力，这就是升力（[[p:f: Wings deflect incoming airflow downward, and the air exerts an upward reaction force on the wing, which is lift ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]], [[p:newton|Newton's laws of motion]]). Lift is proportional to the square of speed, so aircraft must accelerate sufficiently fast on a runway before taking off.
飞行中有四个力：**升力**向上、**重力**向下、**推力**向前（来自螺旋桨: There are four forces in flight: **lift** upward, **gravity** downward, **thrust** forward (from propellers or jet engines), and **drag** backward. Pilots use three sets of control surfaces to rotate the aircraft around three axes: the **elevator** controls pitch (nose up/down), the **ailerons** control roll (left/right tilt), and the **rudder** controls yaw (nose left/right). When turning, one must first bank the wings to tilt lift, using the horizontal component of lift to "pull" the aircraft through the turn rather than relying solely on rudder input like a ship.
1903 年 12 月 17 日，美国莱特兄弟（Wilbur & Orville: On December 17, 1903, near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, USA, the Wright brothers (Wilbur & Orville) completed the first powered, controllable, sustained flight in human history, flying for 12 seconds and approximately 37 meters. Their key breakthrough was not the engine but three-axis control: using "wing warping" to control roll and self-built wind tunnels testing over two hundred wing profiles.
飞机在 20 世纪改变了战争（见 [[fighter-aircraft]]）、邮: In the 20th century, aircraft changed warfare (see [[fighter-aircraft]]), postal services, and travel. Intercontinental travel shrank from weeks to just a few hours, making aviation one of the most important arteries of globalization.
常听到的\"上表面路程长，气流必须同时到达后缘，所以更快\"（等时说）是错误解释: The commonly heard explanation that "the upper surface path is longer, so airflow must arrive at the trailing edge simultaneously, thus being faster" (often cited) is incorrect. While true that upper-surface airflow is indeed faster and pressure lower, the reason is not "must arrive simultaneously"; a more intuitive understanding is: the wing pushes a large amount of air downward, thereby pushing itself upward.
飞机上的四个力和三根控制轴：升降舵管俯仰，副翼管滚转，方向舵管偏航。: The four forces and three control axes on an aircraft: the elevator controls pitch, ailerons control roll, and the rudder controls yaw.
研究空气流过物体时产生的升力和阻力，风洞是它最重要的实验工具。: Researching lift and drag generated by airflow over objects requires wind tunnels as its most important experimental tool.
空气是流体，流速快的地方压力低、流速慢的地方压力高（伯努利原理）；物体改变气流的: Air is a fluid; where flow speed is high, pressure is low, and where flow speed is low, pressure is high (Bernoulli's principle); when an object changes the direction of airflow, it experiences a reaction force ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]). Both lift and drag are roughly proportional to air density, frontal area, and the square of velocity.
空气动力学用几个\"无量纲数\"描述流动：**马赫数**（速度与音速之比）决定会: Aerodynamics uses several "dimensionless numbers" to describe flow: **Mach number** (ratio of speed to speed of sound) determines whether shock waves will occur; **Reynolds number** (ratio of inertial force to viscous force) determines whether airflow is smooth laminar or chaotic turbulent. Engineers place scaled models in wind tunnels to measure forces within artificial airflow, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation on computers is now widely used.
1871 年英国人韦纳姆（Francis Wenham）建造了第一座封闭风洞。1: In 1871, Francis Wenham of the UK built the first closed wind tunnel. In 1904, Ludwig Prandtl of Germany proposed boundary layer theory, laying the foundation for modern aerodynamics.
从飞机、火箭、高铁、赛车，到风力发电机和摩天大楼，凡是在空气里快速运动、或要抵抗: From aircraft, rockets, high-speed rail, race cars, to wind turbines and skyscrapers, anything that moves rapidly in air or must resist strong winds relies on aerodynamics for design.
攻角增大，升力增加；超过临界攻角后，上表面气流分离，升力骤降，这就是\"失速\": As angle of attack increases, lift increases; after exceeding the critical angle of attack, airflow separates from the upper surface, causing a sudden drop in lift, which is called "stall".
用旋转的主旋翼产生升力，可垂直起降和悬停。: Generate lift using a rotating main rotor, enabling vertical takeoff and landing and hovering.
旋转的旋翼就是一副不停转圈的机翼（[[p:fluid|流体压力与升力]]）：飞机: A rotating rotor is essentially an airfoil that spins continuously ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]): An airplane gains forward airflow by moving forward, while a helicopter generates airflow by spinning its own rotor, allowing it to hover in place.
飞行员用**总距杆**同时改变所有桨叶的角度来升降，用**周期变距杆**让桨叶转: The pilot uses the **collective pitch control** to change the angle of all blades simultaneously for climbing and descending, and uses the **cyclic pitch control** to increase the blade angle on one side, tilting the entire rotor disk and enabling movement forward, backward, left, or right. The rotation of the main rotor causes the fuselage to yaw in the opposite direction, so a tail rotor is needed to counteract torque, or two rotors rotating in opposite directions can be used.
1939 年西科斯基（Igor Sikorsky）的 VS-300 首飞，确立了: In 1939, Igor Sikorsky's VS-300 achieved its first flight, establishing the classic 'single main rotor plus tail rotor' configuration.
直升机能在没有跑道的地方起降，成为救援、医疗转运、海上石油平台和军事行动的关键工: Helicopters can take off and land without runways, becoming key tools for rescue operations, medical transport, offshore oil platforms, and military actions.
吸入空气压缩、燃烧后高速喷出产生推力；惠特尔和冯·奥海恩分别独立发明。: Air is drawn in, compressed, burned, and expelled at high speed to generate thrust; Frank Whittle and Hans von Ohain independently invented them.
发动机把大量空气吸进来，加热后以更高的速度向后喷出；空气获得向后的动量，发动机就: The engine draws in a large mass of air, heats it, and expels it backward at higher speeds; the air gains rearward momentum, giving the engine forward thrust ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]]). The more compressed the air and the higher the combustion temperature, the higher the thermal efficiency ([[p:carnot|Carnot efficiency limit]]).
涡轮喷气发动机像一根\"吸—压—烧—喷\"的管子：前部的**压气机**把空气压缩: A turbojet engine is like a 'compressor-combustor-turbine-nozzle' tube: The front **compressor** compresses air by dozens of times; In the **combustion chamber**, fuel is continuously injected and burned; High-temperature gases pass through the **turbine**, driving the compressor on the same shaft; The remaining energy is expelled at high speed from the **nozzle**, generating thrust. It operates on the same principle as gas turbines used for ground-based power generation (see [[gas-turbine]]).
涡轮叶片工作在比金属熔点还高的燃气里，要靠单晶高温合金、陶瓷涂层和叶片内部的冷却: Turbo blades operate in hot gases hotter than the melting point of metal, relying on single-crystal superalloys, ceramic coatings, and internal cooling holes within the blades to work long-term.
英国人惠特尔（Frank Whittle）1930 年申请了喷气发动机专利；德国: Frank Whittle, a British engineer, filed a patent for jet engines in 1930; Hans von Ohain, a German engineer, independently designed an engine mounted on the He 178, completing the world's first jet flight in August 1939. In 1941, Whittle's engine achieved its first flight on the Gloster E.28/39.
喷气发动机让飞机飞上万米高空，时速从几百公里提高到 900 公里左右，催生了喷气: Jet engines enabled aircraft to fly at altitudes over ten thousand meters, increasing speeds from hundreds of kilometers per hour to around 900 km/h, giving birth to jet airliners and modern air combat.
喷气发动机不能在太空中工作：它要吸入空气，既用空气做\"往后扔\"的工作物质，又: Jet engines cannot operate in space: they require air intake, using air both as the 'mass ejected backward' and as oxygen for combustion. Rockets carry their own oxidizer (see [[rocket]]).
涡轮喷气发动机：压气机、燃烧室、涡轮装在同一根轴上，涡轮从燃气中取出一部分能量带: Turbojet engine: The compressor, combustion chamber, and turbine are mounted on a single shaft; the turbine extracts some energy from the gas stream to drive the compressor.
大风扇把大部分空气从发动机外侧推过，更安静、更省油，是现代客机的标配。: A large fan pushes most air over the outside of the engine, making it quieter and more fuel-efficient; this is standard equipment for modern airliners.
推力约等于\"每秒推动的空气质量 × 速度增量\"（[[p:momentum|动: Thrust is approximately equal to 'mass flow rate per second × velocity increment' ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]]). To achieve the same thrust, accelerating a large mass of air slightly wastes far less energy than violently accelerating a small mass; therefore, large fans are more fuel-efficient and quieter.
涡扇发动机最前面有一个巨大的风扇，由核心机的涡轮带动。大部分空气不进核心机，而是: The most forward part of a turbofan engine is a massive fan driven by the core turbine. Most air does not enter the core engine but is pushed directly backward from the outer 'bypass duct'. The ratio of airflow in the bypass duct to that in the core is called the **bypass ratio**; modern airliner engines can reach values over 10.
1960 年代初，低涵道比涡扇投入使用；1970 年随波音 747 服役的普惠: In the early 1960s, low-bypass turbofans were put into service; In 1970, the Pratt & Whitney JT9D, which entered service with the Boeing 747, was the first high-bypass turbofan deployed on commercial routes.
高涵道比涡扇让宽体客机的油耗和噪声大幅下降，是航空旅行大众化的幕后功臣。: High-bypass turbofans significantly reduced fuel consumption and noise for wide-body airliners, being a key factor behind the massification of air travel.
涡扇发动机的大部分推力来自外涵道的\"冷\"气流，核心机主要负责带动风扇。: Most thrust from a turbofan engine comes from the 'cold' airflow in the bypass duct; the core engine primarily drives the fan.
用喷气发动机的客机，飞得更高更快；波音 707 和 747 让航空旅行大众化。: Airliners powered by jet engines fly higher and faster; the Boeing 707 and 747 made air travel accessible to the masses.
飞机越大、飞得越多，每个座位分摊的成本越低（[[p:scale|规模效应]]）；: The larger the aircraft and the more flights it operates, the lower the cost per seat ([[p:scale|Economies of scale]]); At an altitude of ten thousand meters, the air is thin and resistance is low, making jet engines most efficient.
喷气客机在约 1 万米高度巡航，客舱增压到大约相当于海拔 2000 多米的气压。: Jet airliners cruise at approximately 10,000 meters altitude, with cabin pressure boosted to roughly equivalent to sea level at over 2,000 meters. Wide-body airliners have two aisles and can carry three to four hundred passengers. With improved engine reliability under Extended-Range Operations (ETOPS) rules, transoceanic routes no longer require four engines.
1952 年，英国德哈维兰\"彗星\"成为第一种投入航线的喷气客机，但不到两年就: In 1952, the British de Havilland Comet became the first jet airliner put into service, but within less than two years it suffered consecutive in-flight disintegrations due to metal fatigue, leading people to learn 'fatigue design'. In 1958, the Boeing 707 entered service; In 1970, the Boeing 747 'Jumbo Jet' ushered in the era of wide-body airliners. In May 2023, China's C919 began commercial operations.
喷气客机把跨洋旅行变成普通人负担得起的事，催生了大众旅游业和全球化的商务往来；空: Jet airliners made transoceanic travel affordable for ordinary people, giving birth to mass tourism and globalized business exchanges; Airbus and Boeing continue to almost monopolize the large airliner market.
协和式飞机以两倍音速飞行，但油耗和音爆限制了它的商业成功。: The Concorde flew at twice the speed of sound, but high fuel consumption and sonic booms limited its commercial success.
飞机超过音速时，前方的空气来不及\"让路\"，被压缩成激波（[[p:fluid|: When an aircraft exceeds the speed of sound, the air in front does not have time to 'make way' and is compressed into a shockwave ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]), causing drag to increase sharply. A thunderous sonic boom can be heard on the ground.
协和式飞机用细长的三角翼和带加力燃烧的涡喷发动机，以约 2 倍音速在约 1.8: The Concorde used slender delta wings and turbofan engines with afterburners, cruising at approximately 2 times the speed of sound at an altitude of about 18,000 meters. The flight from London to New York took only about 3.5 hours. Upon landing, its nose could be lowered so pilots could see the runway clearly.
1969 年协和首飞，1976 年投入航线，2003 年退役；2000 年巴黎空: The Concorde made its first flight in 1969, entered service in 1976, and was retired in 2003; it was grounded for over a year after the Paris air disaster in 2000. The Soviet Tupolev Tu-144 made its first flight two months earlier than the Concorde.
协和是技术上的奇迹、商业上的失败：只造了 20 架，票价昂贵，又被许多国家禁止在: The Concorde was a technical miracle but a commercial failure: only 20 were built, ticket prices were exorbitant, and many countries banned supersonic flights over land. Currently, some companies are researching supersonic passenger aircraft with reduced sonic booms.
用陀螺仪感知姿态、自动修正舵面，让飞机保持航向和高度。: Using gyroscopes to sense attitude and automatically correct control surfaces keeps the aircraft on its heading and altitude.
陀螺仪感知飞机姿态的变化，控制器比较\"实际姿态\"和\"目标姿态\"，用差值驱: Gyroscopes detect changes in aircraft attitude; the controller compares 'actual attitude' with 'target attitude' and uses the difference to drive corrections of control surfaces ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
早期的自动驾驶仪只能保持航向和高度；现代飞行管理系统能按预定航路自动爬升、巡航和: Early autopilots could only maintain heading and altitude; modern flight management systems can automatically climb, cruise, and descend along a predetermined route, working in conjunction with instrument landing systems, even allowing automatic landings in dense fog. The pilot's primary task becomes monitoring the system and handling anomalies.
1912 年，美国人劳伦斯·斯佩里（Lawrence Sperry）发明了陀螺稳: In 1912, American Lawrence Sperry invented the gyro-stabilized autopilot; in 1914 he performed a demonstration in Paris where a mechanic walked onto the wing while he himself removed his hands from the control stick, yet the aircraft continued to fly smoothly.
自动驾驶仪大大减轻了长途飞行的疲劳；同时，飞行员对自动化的过度依赖，也成了航空安: Autopilots greatly reduced fatigue during long flights; at the same time, over-reliance by pilots on automation has also become an important subject of study in aviation safety research.
驾驶杆的指令变成电信号由计算机执行，计算机还能防止飞机进入危险状态。: Commands from the control column are converted into electrical signals executed by computers, which can also prevent the aircraft from entering dangerous states.
驾驶杆不再拉动钢索，而是把指令变成电信号交给计算机；计算机根据传感器反馈算出舵面: The control column no longer pulls steel cables but converts commands into electrical signals delivered to computers; computers calculate control surface movements based on sensor feedback ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]) and can refuse operations exceeding safe limits.
系统通常有三到四套相互独立的计算机和线路，一套出故障不影响飞行。电传还让战斗机可: Systems typically consist of three to four mutually independent computers and wiring sets, so a failure in one set does not affect flight. Fly-by-wire also allows fighter aircraft to be designed with 'naturally unstable' configurations, relying on dozens of corrections per second by computers to maintain balance, which in turn enables more flexible maneuvering.
1972 年，美国 NASA 用改装的 F-8 战斗机首次实现纯数字电传飞行。1: In 1972, the US NASA achieved pure digital fly-by-wire flight using a modified F-8 fighter jet. The Airbus A320, which made its first flight in 1987, was the first commercial aircraft to fully adopt digital fly-by-wire.
电传减轻了重量、提高了安全性，也引出\"人和自动化谁说了算\"之争：空客偏向计算: Fly-by-wire reduced weight and improved safety, but also sparked the debate of 'who has the final say between humans and automation': Airbus tends to favor computer-set protection boundaries, while Boeing emphasizes the pilot's ultimate authority.
用雷达、无线电和规则把天空划分成航路，避免飞机相撞。: Using radar, radio communications, and rules, the sky is divided into airways to prevent aircraft collisions.
天空看似空旷，机场附近和繁忙航路上的飞机却非常密集。管制员用雷达测量每架飞机的位: Although the sky appears empty, aircraft near airports and on busy airways are extremely dense. Controllers use radar to measure the position of each aircraft and direct them via radio to maintain safe separation ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
空域分为塔台、进近和航路三层，飞机从一个管制区\"移交\"到下一个，彼此保持水平: Airspace is divided into three layers: tower, approach, and en-route; an aircraft is 'transferred' from one control area to the next, maintaining a horizontal separation of about 5 nautical miles or more, or a vertical separation of about 300 meters. The new generation ADS-B system allows each aircraft to automatically broadcast its position using satellite positioning.
1920 年，伦敦克罗伊登机场率先提供空中交通管制服务。1956 年美国大峡谷上: In 1920, London's Croydon Airport was the first to provide air traffic control services. In 1956, a collision between two passenger aircraft over the Grand Canyon in the US prompted the US to establish the Federal Aviation Agency in 1958 to uniformly manage airspace.
空管系统让越来越繁忙的天空保持了极低的事故率，也是航班延误和航线容量的关键瓶颈。: The air traffic control system has maintained an extremely low accident rate despite increasingly busy skies, and it is also a key bottleneck for flight delays and airway capacity.
用多个电动旋翼垂直起降的\"空中出租车\"，属于低空经济。: 'Air taxis' using multiple electric rotors for vertical takeoff and landing belong to the low-altitude economy.
电动机容易小型化，可以分布到多个旋翼上，由计算机独立控制每个旋翼的转速来保持平衡: Electric motors are easy to miniaturize and can be distributed across multiple rotors; computers independently control the rotation speed of each rotor to maintain balance ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]). However, the energy density of batteries is only a fraction of that of aviation fuel, limiting range and payload ([[p:energydensity|Energy density]]).
eVTOL 起降时用多个旋翼垂直升降；有的机型巡航时把旋翼转向前方，或改用机翼产: During takeoff and landing, eVTOLs use multiple rotors for vertical ascent and descent; some models orient rotors forward during cruise or switch to using wings for lift, achieving higher efficiency. Electric motors are quieter than helicopter engines and have a much simpler structure.
2020 年代，多家公司进入适航取证阶段。2023 年 10 月，中国亿航的 E: In the 2020s, numerous companies entered the certification phase. In October 2023, China's EHang EH216-S obtained the world's first type certificate for unmanned passenger-carrying eVTOL.
eVTOL 被看作\"低空经济\"的核心，可能用于城市空中出租车、医疗转运和观光: eVTOL is regarded as the core of 'low-altitude economy,' potentially used for urban air taxis, medical transfers, and sightseeing; safety, noise, airspace management, and cost remain to be verified.
由遥控或自主飞行的无人飞行器，广泛用于航拍、植保、物流和军事。: Unmanned aerial vehicles that are remotely piloted or autonomously flown, widely used for aerial photography, crop protection, logistics, and military operations.
多旋翼无人机靠改变各个旋翼的转速产生不同的升力（[[p:fluid|流体压力与升: Multi-rotor drones generate different lift by changing the rotational speed of each rotor ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]); flight control computers correct hundreds of times per second based on data from gyroscopes and accelerometers ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]), so inherently unstable multi-rotors can hover steadily.
消费级无人机的核心是微机电惯性传感器（见 [[mems]]）、卫星定位、无刷电机: The core of consumer-grade unmanned aircraft is microelectromechanical inertial sensors (see [[mems]]), satellite positioning, brushless DC motors (see [[bldc-motor]]), and lithium batteries. In quadcopters, two diagonally opposite rotors rotate in the same direction while adjacent ones rotate in opposite directions, canceling each other's torque; speeding up one rotor causes the aircraft to tilt and move toward the opposite side. Fixed-wing drones fly like small airplanes, achieving longer ranges.
无人机最早是军用靶机和侦察机。2006 年成立的深圳大疆在 2013 年推出\": Unmanned aerial vehicles were originally military target drones and reconnaissance aircraft. Shenzhen DJI, founded in 2006, launched the 'Mavic' series in 2013, bringing aerial photography drones to the mass market; since then, it has long held the majority share of the global consumer-grade unmanned aircraft market.
无人机用于航拍、测绘、农业植保（见 [[agricultural-drone]]: Unmanned aerial vehicles are used for aerial photography, surveying, agricultural crop protection (see [[agricultural-drone]]), power line inspection, and food delivery; during the Russia-Ukraine war, numerous inexpensive unmanned aircraft profoundly changed battlefield morphology (see [[military-drone]]).
利用高速旋转陀螺保持方向不变的特性导航，不依赖外部信号。: Navigation using the property that high-speed rotation keeps the axis direction unchanged, without relying on external signals.
高速旋转的陀螺会保持转轴方向不变（[[p:momentum|动量守恒]]，这里是: A high-speed rotating gyroscope maintains its axis direction unchanged ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]], which is angular momentum); a gyrocompass uses Earth's rotation to make the gyroscope axis point to true north, unaffected by magnetic interference from steel ship hulls.
惯性导航用陀螺仪测转动、用加速度计测加速度，积分一次得速度、再积分得位置，完全不: Inertial navigation uses gyroscopes to measure rotation and accelerometers to measure acceleration; integrating once yields velocity, and integrating again yields position, completely independent of external signals; the disadvantage is that errors accumulate over time, so it is often combined with satellite navigation. Today, lasers, fiber optics, or microelectromechanical gyroscopes are commonly used.
1908 年，德国人安许茨（Hermann Anschütz-Kaempfe）发: In 1908, German Hermann Anschütz-Kaempfe invented a practical gyrocompass; subsequently, the American Sperry Corporation also launched its own product.
陀螺罗经给钢铁战舰和潜艇提供了可靠的方向基准；惯性导航用于导弹、潜艇、飞机和航天: Gyrocompasses provided reliable direction references for steel warships and submarines; inertial navigation is used for missiles, submarines, aircraft, and spacecraft, and cannot be interfered with or deceived.
把货物码在标准托盘上用叉车整体搬运，是仓储物流的\"集装箱\"。: Storing goods on standard pallets and moving them as a whole with forklifts constitutes the 'container' of warehouse logistics.
把零散货物码在标准托盘上，叉车一次就能搬走一整托（[[p:standard|标准: Storing scattered goods on standard pallets allows a forklift to remove an entire pallet ([[p:standard|Standardization]]) in one go; hydraulic lifting enables a single driver to lift several tons of cargo ([[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]]).
叉车把货叉插进托盘下方，液压缸推动门架升起，能把货物送上十几米高的货架。托盘尺寸: Forklifts insert forks into the bottom of pallets, and hydraulic cylinders push the mast up to elevate goods onto shelves tens of meters high. Pallet dimensions are gradually standardized, such as 1200×800 millimeters commonly used in Europe, and 1200×1000 millimeters recommended in China.
1920 年代出现带升降平台的搬运车；1930 年代后期托盘随新型叉车普及，第二: Lift trucks with elevating platforms appeared in the 1920s; by the late 1930s, pallets became widespread with new forklift models, were massively used by the US military during World War II, and were promoted to the entire warehousing industry after the war.
托盘和叉车让仓库装卸效率提高了好几倍，可以看作集装箱之前的\"小号集装箱\"；今: Pallets and forklifts improved warehouse loading and unloading efficiency by several times, which can be regarded as 'small containers' before the container era; today they are being further automated by autonomous guided vehicles and warehouse robots (see [[logistics-automation]]).
用泵把石油、天然气和水通过管道连续输送，运量大、成本低。: Using pumps to continuously transport oil, natural gas, and water through pipelines achieves large volume and low cost.
管道里的流体总是从高压处流向低压处（[[p:fluid|流体压力与升力]]）；沿: Fluids in pipelines always flow from high pressure to low pressure ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]); along the line, pumping stations or compressor stations constantly supplement pressure, enabling continuous delivery of oil and natural gas for thousands of kilometers.
输油管用泵加压，输气管用压缩机加压；管道大多埋在地下，由传感器监测压力和泄漏。建: Oil pipelines use pumps for pressurization, while gas pipelines use compressors; most pipelines are buried underground, monitored by sensors for pressure and leaks. After completion, unit transportation costs are far lower than those of railways and highways, but investment is huge and routes are fixed.
1865 年，美国宾夕法尼亚油田建成第一条成功运营的输油管道，长约 8 公里；1: In 1865, the first successfully operational oil pipeline was built in the Pennsylvania oilfield in the United States, about 8 kilometers long; the Tidewater Pipeline, completed in 1879, was about 175 kilometers long, the first long-distance oil pipeline.
管道网络是现代能源体系的\"血管\"。跨国油气管道也常常成为地缘政治的筹码，例如: Pipeline networks are the 'blood vessels' of modern energy systems. Cross-border oil and gas pipelines often become geopolitical chips, such as the September 2022 incident involving the destruction of the 'Nord Stream' pipeline.
自带燃料和氧化剂、靠向后高速喷出燃气获得推力，在真空中也能工作。: Self-contained fuel and oxidizer, obtaining thrust by expelling high-speed exhaust gases backward; it can work in a vacuum.
中国宋代已有火药火箭。1903 年俄国的齐奥尔科夫斯基（Konstantin T: Firework rockets existed in China during the Song Dynasty. In 1903, Russian Konstantin Tsiolkovsky derived the rocket equation; in 1926, American Robert Goddard launched the world's first liquid-fueled rocket, flying for only 2.5 seconds and reaching a height of about 12 meters. Germany's V-2 (see [[v2-rocket]]) turned rockets into large-scale engineering projects, and the Cold War pushed them toward space.
火箭是人类唯一能把东西送进太空的工具，卫星、空间站和深空探测都建立在它之上。它也: Rockets are the only tool capable of sending things into space; satellites, space stations, and deep space exploration all rest upon them. They also form the basis for intercontinental ballistic missiles (see [[icbm]]), with aerospace and national defense intertwined from the outset.
火箭的基本结构：大部分是推进剂贮箱，燃气经拉瓦尔喷管加速向后喷出，火箭获得向前的: The basic structure of a rocket consists mostly of propellant tanks. Gas flows through a de Laval nozzle and accelerates backward, generating forward thrust for the rocket.
火箭能达到的速度由喷气速度和\"满载/空载质量比\"的对数决定——这是航天的根本: The velocity a rocket can achieve is determined by the exhaust velocity and the logarithm of the 'full-load/empty-mass ratio'—this is the fundamental constraint of aerospace engineering.
1903 年齐奥尔科夫斯基在论文《用反作用装置探索宇宙空间》中发表这一方程，并提: In 1903, Konstantin Tsiolkovsky published this equation in his paper 'Exploration of Outer Space by Means of Reaction Devices,' proposed the concept of multi-stage rockets and liquid hydrogen-oxygen propellants, and was known as the 'father of astronautics'.
它告诉人们，太空不是造不出更大的大炮那么简单，而是一道受指数约束的算术题。几乎所: It tells people that space is not simply about building bigger cannons; it is an arithmetic problem constrained by exponential growth. Almost all spacecraft designs begin with this problem: first calculate delta-v, then work backward to determine how much fuel and how large a rocket are needed.
要想获得的速度越大，推进剂占起飞质量的比例就越接近 100%（按液氢液氧喷气速度: The greater the desired velocity, the closer the proportion of propellant to takeoff mass approaches 100% (calculated based on an exhaust velocity of 4.4 km/s for liquid hydrogen-oxygen).
用泵把液态燃料和液氧送入燃烧室，推力可调、可关机重启。: Pumps deliver liquid fuel and liquid oxygen into the combustion chamber, allowing adjustable thrust and restart capability.
燃料（煤油、液氢、甲烷）和氧化剂（通常是液氧）分别储存，用泵按比例送进燃烧室燃烧: Fuel (kerosene, liquid hydrogen, or methane) and oxidizer (usually liquid oxygen) are stored separately and fed into the combustion chamber in proportion by pumps. The higher the temperature of combustion products and the lighter the molecular weight, the greater the exhaust velocity ([[p:energydensity|Energy density]], [[p:bond|Chemical bonds & chemical energy]]).
核心是涡轮泵——一台小型燃气轮机驱动的泵，每秒把几百公斤到一吨多的推进剂压进燃烧: The core is the turbopump—a pump driven by a small gas turbine that forces hundreds of kilograms to over a ton of propellant into the combustion chamber every second. Combustion chamber temperatures exceed 3000°C; this is prevented from burning through by allowing low-temperature fuel to flow first through internal cooling channels. Valve regulation adjusts flow rate to change thrust, and cutting off supply shuts down the engine—this is a prerequisite for reusable rockets to perform retrograde landing. Liquid oxygen comes from industrial [[air-separation]].
1926 年戈达德发射首枚液体火箭。德国的 V-2 首次使用涡轮泵。土星五号第一: In 1926, Robert Goddard launched the first liquid-fuel rocket. Germany's V-2 was the first to use turbopumps. The F-1 engine on the first stage of Saturn V remains the most powerful single-chamber liquid-fuel engine to date.
几乎所有大型运载火箭都以液体发动机为主力。近年液氧甲烷发动机兴起：燃烧更干净、积: Almost all large launch vehicles rely primarily on liquid-fuel engines. Recently, liquid oxygen-methane engines have emerged: they burn cleaner with less carbon buildup, making them more suitable for reusability.
燃料和氧化剂预先混合浇注成药柱，结构简单、随时可发射，但点燃后难以关机。: Fuel and oxidizer are pre-mixed and cast into solid propellant columns; the structure is simple, ready for launch at any time, but difficult to shut down once ignited.
燃料和氧化剂预先混合，浇注成橡皮一样的\"药柱\"装进壳体，点燃后从内表面向外燃: Fuel and oxidizer are pre-mixed and cast into rubber-like 'propellant columns' inside the casing. After ignition, combustion proceeds from the inner surface outward, with gas exiting through the nozzle ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]]). The shape of the central channel determines the burning area, which in turn dictates the thrust curve.
没有泵和阀门，结构简单，能长期储存、随时发射，推力也大。代价是喷气速度比液体发动: Without pumps or valves, the structure is simple, capable of long-term storage and immediate launch, with high thrust. The drawback is lower exhaust velocity compared to liquid-fuel engines, making shutdown or throttling difficult after ignition.
火药火箭起源于中国宋代；现代复合固体推进剂（高氯酸铵加铝粉和橡胶粘合剂）在 20: Powder-propelled rockets originated in China during the Song Dynasty; modern composite solid propellants (ammonium perchlorate plus aluminum powder and rubber binder) matured in the 1940s–1950s.
固体火箭是导弹的首选（见 [[icbm]]），也常做运载火箭的助推器；小型固体火: Solid-fuel rockets are the preferred choice for missiles (see [[icbm]]) and are often used as boosters for launch vehicles; small solid-fuel rockets are suitable for rapid deployment of small satellites.
纳粹德国研制的弹道导弹，第一个进入太空的人造物体，战后成为美苏航天的起点。: The ballistic missile developed by Nazi Germany was the first artificial object to enter space; after the war, it became the starting point for aerospace programs in the United States and the Soviet Union.
酒精加液氧、涡轮泵供料、陀螺仪自动制导——V-2 第一次把火箭原理放大成工业规模: Alcohol plus liquid oxygen, turbopump-fed, gyro-stabilized guidance—the V-2 was the first time rocket principles were scaled up into an industrial-scale weapon ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]]).
弹长 14 米，发动机工作约一分钟后关机，弹头沿弹道惯性飞到约 300 公里外，: With a length of 14 meters, the engine operated for about one minute before shutting down; the warhead traveled along its ballistic trajectory with inertia to approximately 300 km away and fell at supersonic speed, which could not be intercepted at that time.
1942 年在冯·布劳恩（Wernher von Braun）主持下首次试射成功: First successful test launch was conducted in 1942 under Wernher von Braun; in 1944, a vertical test flight exceeded 100 km, becoming the first artificial object to enter space. It was produced by prisoners of concentration camps; more people died during its production than were killed by its attacks.
战后美国通过\"回形针行动\"带走冯·布劳恩团队，苏联也接收了大批技术和人员，V: After the war, the United States brought Wernher von Braun's team away via 'Operation Paperclip'; the Soviet Union also received large amounts of technology and personnel. The V-2 became the common starting point for missiles and aerospace programs in both the US and USSR.
把火箭分成几级，用完一级就扔掉一级\"空壳\"，绕过火箭方程的限制。: Dividing a rocket into multiple stages allows discarding the empty shell of each stage after use, bypassing the limitations of the rocket equation.
燃料烧完了，空箱子还得跟着加速，这是火箭方程的难点（[[p:momentum|动: Once fuel is burned, the empty tank must still accelerate—this is the difficulty of the rocket equation ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]]). Multi-stage rockets discard the tanks and engines of each stage sequentially; subsequent stages only need to push lighter masses, breaking an impossible arithmetic problem into several solvable ones.
第一级推力最大，负责穿过稠密大气；上面几级在真空中工作，用效率更高的发动机。也可: The first stage provides maximum thrust to penetrate dense atmosphere; upper stages operate in vacuum using more efficient engines. Booster engines can also be bundled on either side of the core stage, burning and separating sequentially.
齐奥尔科夫斯基在 20 世纪初提出\"火箭列车\"设想。土星五号用三级结构把约: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky proposed the 'rocket train' concept in the early 20th century. Saturn V used a three-stage structure to deliver approximately 45 tons to the Moon.
至今几乎所有入轨火箭都是多级的；可回收火箭则是把被扔掉的那一级飞回来。: To date, almost all orbiting rockets are multi-stage; recoverable rockets bring back the stage that is discarded.
多级火箭每扔掉一级空箱，剩下的部分就更轻，同样的燃料能多加速一截。: Each time a multi-stage rocket discards an empty stage, the remaining portion becomes lighter, allowing the same amount of fuel to accelerate another section further.
让火箭第一级反推着陆后再次使用；SpaceX 猎鹰 9 号 2015 年首次成功: The first stage of the rocket is allowed to land after reverse thrust and then be reused; SpaceX's Falcon 9 achieved its first successful recovery in 2015.
航天飞机曾部分重复使用，但每次翻修费用高昂。2015 年 12 月 21 日，S: The Space Shuttle was partially reusable, but each refurbishment cost was high. On December 21, 2015, SpaceX's Falcon 9 first stage successfully landed vertically after an orbital launch; full reusability was achieved in 2017. By August 2026, a single booster (B1067) had flown 37 times. On July 10, 2026, China's Long March 10 Ye made its first flight, capturing and recovering the first stage using a sea-based 'net,' marking China's first successful recovery of an orbiting rocket.
复用让发射频率和价格同时改变：2025 年猎鹰 9 号一年发射约 165 次，超: Reusability changes both launch frequency and price: in 2025, Falcon 9 launched approximately 165 times per year, exceeding the total number of launches worldwide for many prior years. Cheap launches made it possible to form constellations consisting of tens of thousands of satellites (see [[satellite-internet]]), and forced nations to regard recoverable rockets as standard equipment for next-generation launch vehicles.
猎鹰 9 号第一级的回收过程：分离、调头、再入点火、着陆点火，最后落在无人船或陆: The recovery process of Falcon 9's first stage involves separation, turning around, re-entry ignition, landing ignition, and finally landing on an unmanned ship or a land-based landing site.
SpaceX 研制的完全可重复使用超重型运载火箭，目标是大幅降低发射成本并登陆火: SpaceX has developed a fully reusable super heavy-lift launch vehicle, aiming to significantly reduce launch costs and enable landing on Mars.
如果火箭两级都能像飞机一样落地、加注、再飞，发射成本就只剩燃料和维护，可能降低一: If both stages of the rocket can land like airplanes, refuel, and fly again, launch costs would be reduced to just fuel and maintenance, potentially lowering by one or two orders of magnitude ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]).
由\"超重\"助推器和\"星舰\"上面级组成，全高约 120 米，用 30 多台: Composed of a 'Super Heavy' booster and a 'Starship' upper stage, it stands about 120 meters tall, uses over 30 liquid oxygen methane 'Raptor' engines, and is the largest rocket in history. The boosters return to the launch tower and are directly gripped by 'chopstick' mechanical arms; the upper stage re-enters using heat shields, glides down while decelerating, flips over, and lands with reverse thrust.
2023 年 4 月首次整箭试飞，约 4 分钟后解体；2024 年 10 月第五: The first full vehicle test flight occurred in April 2023, disintegrating after about 4 minutes. The fifth test flight in October 2024 was the first time a booster was 'gripped.' The 14th test flight in September 2026 achieved orbit for the first time and released Starlink satellites.
SpaceX 把失败当作获取数据的代价，快速迭代；星舰也是阿尔忒弥斯登月着陆器方: SpaceX treats failure as the cost of acquiring data, iterating rapidly; Starship is also one of the options for the Artemis lunar landing craft plan (see [[lunar-return]]).
用电场把离子加速到极高速度喷出，推力很小但非常省燃料，适合深空和卫星。: Using an electric field to accelerate ions to extremely high speeds and eject them produces very little thrust but saves fuel very efficiently, making it suitable for deep space and satellite applications.
喷气越快越省燃料（[[p:momentum|动量守恒]]）。化学火箭的喷气速度最: The faster the exhaust, the more fuel is saved ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]]). Chemical rockets have a maximum exhaust speed of about 4.5 km/s; electric propulsion uses an electric field to accelerate ions to 20–50 km/s, allowing the same amount of fuel to yield much more speed ([[p:charge|Electric charge & field]]).
把氙气等工质电离，用高压栅极加速喷出。推力极小，常常只相当于一张纸的重量，但能连: Ionized gases such as xenon are accelerated by high-voltage grids and ejected. The thrust is extremely small, often equivalent to the weight of a single sheet of paper, but it can operate continuously for months or even years; electricity comes from solar panels.
1964 年美国 SERT-1 首次在太空验证离子推力器；1998 年\"深空一: The US SERT-1 first verified ion thruster thrust in space in 1964; 'Deep Space One' first used it as a main engine for a probe in 1998.
电推进已是卫星保持轨道和深空探测的常用动力，星链卫星也靠它。它推不动火箭离开地面: Electric propulsion has become a common power source for satellites to maintain orbit and for deep space exploration, including Starlink satellites. It cannot push a rocket off the ground but is best suited for slowly traveling long distances in space.
速度约 7.9 km/s 时，物体一直绕地球\"下落\"而不落地；11.2 km: At a speed of about 7.9 km/s, an object continuously 'falls' around Earth without hitting the ground; at 11.2 km/s, it can escape Earth's gravity.
1687 年牛顿在《自然哲学的数学原理》中用\"山顶大炮\"的思想实验解释了这一: In 1687, Newton explained this point in 'Principia: Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy' using the thought experiment of a 'cannon on a mountain'; Kepler summarized the three laws of planetary motion in the early 17th century. In 1957, Sputnik 1 turned this thought experiment into reality (see [[sputnik]]).
理解轨道之后，\"进入太空\"的关键就从\"飞多高\"变成\"飞多快\"：100: After understanding orbits, the key to 'entering space' changes from 'how high' to 'how fast': reaching 100 km altitude takes only a few minutes; the challenge is achieving a horizontal speed of nearly 8 km/s. All space missions—from satellites and space stations to lunar exploration—are designed around orbital mechanics.
牛顿的\"山顶大炮\"：炮弹越快落得越远，快到第一宇宙速度时，就绕地球一圈回到原: Newton's 'cannon on a mountain': the faster the projectile, the farther it falls; when it reaches the first cosmic velocity, it circles Earth once and returns to its starting point.
苏联发射的第一颗人造卫星，引发美国震惊并开启太空竞赛。: The Soviet Union's first artificial satellite, which shocked the US and launched the space race.
只要把物体加速到第一宇宙速度并让它的轨迹高出大气层，它就会绕地球一直转下去（[[: As long as an object is accelerated to the first cosmic velocity and its trajectory remains above the atmosphere, it will continue to orbit Earth indefinitely ([[p:gravity|Gravitation & orbital mechanics]]). Sputnik 1 was designed to prove this point: human-made objects can remain in space.
它是一个直径 58 厘米、重 83.6 千克的抛光金属球，带四根天线，内部只有电: It is a polished metal sphere with a diameter of 58 cm and a weight of 83.6 kg, equipped with four antennas; internally it contains only batteries, a thermometer, and a radio transmitter, continuously emitting 'beep-beep' signals. Amateur radio enthusiasts worldwide can receive them; it orbits Earth once every 96 minutes. It was launched by a rocket modified from the R-7 intercontinental ballistic missile.
1957 年 10 月 4 日由苏联发射，总设计师是科罗廖夫（Sergei Ko: Launched by the Soviet Union on October 4, 1957, with Sergei Korolev as chief designer. It burned up in the atmosphere after operating in orbit for about three months.
一颗能被收音机听到的小球，让美国社会陷入\"斯普特尼克危机\"：既然苏联能把卫星: A small ball that could be heard by a radio caused the United States to fall into a "Sputnik crisis": since the Soviet Union could launch a satellite into space, it could also deliver nuclear warheads to the United States. The United States subsequently established NASA (1958), increased investment in science education, and the Space Race began (see [[space-race]]).
美苏在冷战中以航天成就比拼国力，从首颗卫星一路竞赛到登月。: The United States and the Soviet Union competed for national power during the Cold War through space achievements, racing from the first satellite to landing on the moon.
冷战中的美苏不能直接开战，航天就成了比拼技术、工业和制度的竞技场；同一枚火箭既是: During the Cold War, the United States and the Soviet Union could not engage in direct war; space became an arena to compete in technology, industry, and systems ([[p:incentives|Incentives & game theory]]). The same rocket serves as both prestige and proof of missile capability.
比赛由一连串\"第一\"组成：第一颗卫星、第一个人、第一次太空行走、第一次登月。: The competition consisted of a series of "firsts": the first satellite, the first human, the first spacewalk, and the first moon landing. NASA's budget exceeded 4% of the United States federal budget at its peak; the Apollo program employed approximately 400,000 people.
1957 年斯普特尼克 1 号、1961 年加加林首飞，苏联领先；1961 年肯: Sputnik 1 in 1957 and Gagarin's first flight in 1961 showed Soviet leadership; Kennedy announced a moon landing within ten years in 1961, which was achieved in 1969. In 1975, American and Soviet spacecraft docked in orbit, symbolizing the easing of the competition.
竞赛催生了卫星产业和大规模系统工程方法，也是集成电路早期的大客户。: The competition spawned the satellite industry and large-scale systems engineering methods, and also served as an early major customer for integrated circuits.
绕地球运行的航天器，用于通信、导航、气象、遥感和科研。: Spacecraft orbiting the Earth are used for communications, navigation, meteorology, remote sensing, and scientific research.
卫星的价值来自\"高度\"：从几百到几万公里的高处，一颗卫星能看到、照顾到地面上: The value of a satellite comes from its "altitude": from heights ranging from hundreds to tens of thousands of kilometers, a single satellite can see and cover a large area on the ground; moreover, as long as it remains in orbit, it almost does not need propulsion to maintain its position ([[p:gravity|Gravitation & orbital mechanics]]).
一颗卫星分两部分：**平台**提供电力（太阳能板和电池）、姿态控制、温度控制和与: A satellite consists of two parts: the **platform** provides power (solar panels and batteries), attitude control, thermal control, and communication with the ground; the **payload** is the part that actually performs work, such as communication transponders, cameras, or navigation signal generators. Classified by altitude into three categories: **Low Earth Orbit** (hundreds to 2000 kilometers) is suitable for photography and low-latency communications; **Medium Earth Orbit** (approximately 20,000 kilometers) is suitable for navigation; **Geostationary Orbit** (approximately 36,000 kilometers) is suitable for communications and meteorology.
1957 年斯普特尼克 1 号是第一颗人造卫星。到 2026 年 9 月，在轨工: Sputnik 1 in 1957 was the first artificial satellite. By September 2026, approximately 17,000 satellites were operational in orbit; about two-thirds belong to the Starlink constellation (see [[satellite-internet]]).
卫星已成为看不见的基础设施：通信（见 [[communication-satel: Satellites have become invisible infrastructure: communications (see [[communication-satellite]]), navigation, weather forecasting, Earth observation, and military reconnaissance all depend on them.
赤道上空约 35786 公里处，卫星绕地一圈恰好一天，看起来静止在天上。: At an altitude of approximately 35,786 kilometers above the equator, a satellite orbits the Earth once in exactly one day, appearing stationary in the sky.
轨道越高，绕一圈越慢（[[p:gravity|万有引力与轨道]]）。在赤道上空约: The higher the orbit, the slower the period for one revolution ([[p:gravity|Gravitation & orbital mechanics]]). At an altitude of approximately 35,786 kilometers above the equator, a satellite's orbital period equals the Earth's rotation period; from the ground, it appears motionless, "hanging" in the sky.
地面天线对准固定方向即可，不必跟踪；三颗均匀分布的静止卫星就能覆盖两极以外的几乎: Ground antennas can be aimed at a fixed direction without tracking; three geostationary satellites uniformly distributed can cover almost the entire Earth outside the polar regions. The cost is the long distance, with signal round-trip time requiring approximately 0.24 seconds.
1945 年科幻作家克拉克（Arthur C. Clarke）设想用三颗静止卫星: In 1945, science fiction author Arthur C. Clarke envisioned achieving global communications using three geostationary satellites; in 1964, Syncom 3 became the first Earth-geostationary satellite, broadcasting the Tokyo Olympics.
静止轨道成了通信、电视直播和气象卫星的\"黄金地段\"，轨道位置由国际电信联盟分: Geostationary orbit has become the "prime real estate" for communications, television broadcasts, and meteorological satellites; orbital positions are allocated by the International Telecommunication Union.
静止轨道卫星与地球同步转动；三颗卫星就能覆盖地球大部分地区。: Geostationary orbit satellites rotate synchronously with the Earth; three satellites can cover most of the Earth's surface.
以 10 厘米立方体为单元的标准化小卫星，让大学和创业公司也能上太空。: Standardized small satellites based on 10-centimeter cubic units allow universities and startup companies to access space.
把卫星做成标准\"积木\"：10 厘米见方、约 1–2 公斤为一个单元（1U），: Making satellites into standard "building blocks": a unit is approximately 10 centimeters in size and about 1–2 kilograms (1U); they can be assembled into 3U, 6U, or 12U configurations. With standardized dimensions, components can be purchased in bulk, and during launch, they can also "piggyback" ([[p:standard|Standardization & interchangeability]]).
立方星装在标准弹射盒里，搭乘大火箭的剩余运力入轨，大量使用商用电子元件，成本低、: CubeSats are loaded into standard launchers, riding on the remaining capacity of large rockets to reach orbit; they make extensive use of commercial electronic components, resulting in low cost and fast updates, but also lower lifespan and reliability.
1999 年加州州立理工大学的帕克（Jordi Puig-Suari）和斯坦福大: In 1999, Jordi Puig-Suari from California State Polytechnic University of San Diego and Bob Twiggs from Stanford University proposed the CubeSat standard, initially for student teaching purposes.
太空向大学、小国和创业公司敞开了大门；成百上千颗小卫星组成的星座，可以每天把整个: Space opened its doors to universities, small nations, and startup companies; constellations composed of hundreds or thousands of small satellites can photograph the entire Earth every day.
接收机测量来自 4 颗以上卫星的信号时间差算出自己的位置，必须修正相对论效应。: Receivers calculate their position by measuring the time difference of signals from four or more satellites; they must correct for relativistic effects.
美国 1978 年发射第一颗 GPS 试验卫星，1995 年系统完全运行；198: The United States launched its first GPS test satellite in 1978, and the system became fully operational in 1995. After a South Korean airliner was shot down in Soviet airspace due to navigation errors in 1983, the United States announced that GPS would be opened to civilian use. Russia has GLONASS; Europe has Galileo; China's BeiDou-3 was completed and provided global services in July 2020.
卫星导航把精确的位置和时间变成免费的公共品：手机地图、网约车（见 [[ride-: Satellite navigation converts precise location and time into free public goods: mobile maps, ride-hailing and shared mobility (see [[ride-hailing]]), logistics dispatch, aviation, and maritime navigation all rely on it; communication networks, power grids, and financial transactions also use it for clock synchronization. Signal interference and spoofing therefore become new security threats.
接收机测出到 4 颗卫星的距离，就能同时解出自己的三维位置和时钟误差。: A receiver measures distances to 4 satellites, which allows it to simultaneously solve for its three-dimensional position and clock error.
卫星从太空拍摄地球的可见光、红外和雷达图像，监测农业、灾害、城市和气候。: Satellites capture visible light, infrared, and radar images of the Earth from space, monitoring agriculture, disasters, cities, and climate.
不同物体反射和发射不同波长的电磁波：健康植物强烈反射近红外，水吸收红外，热的地方: Different objects reflect and emit electromagnetic waves of different wavelengths: healthy plants strongly reflect near-infrared, water absorbs infrared, and hotter areas radiate more strongly ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]). By taking photos simultaneously across multiple bands, satellites can reveal information invisible to the naked eye.
**光学多光谱相机**拍摄可见光和红外，商业卫星分辨率可达约 30 厘米；**合: **Optical multispectral cameras** capture visible light and infrared; commercial satellite resolution can reach approximately 30 centimeters. **Synthetic Aperture Radar **(SAR) emits its own microwaves, enabling operation through clouds and at night, while also measuring ground deformation at the millimeter level; **Thermal infrared** measures surface temperature. Satellites typically orbit in sun-synchronous orbits, passing over the same location with identical lighting conditions each time, facilitating comparison.
1972 年美国发射第一颗陆地卫星（Landsat 1），其数据 2008 年起: The United States launched the first Landsat satellite (Landsat 1) in 1972, and its data has been made free since 2008; the European Union's Copernicus Programme also provides Sentinel satellite data for free.
遥感让人类能定期给地球\"体检\"：估产、监测森林和冰川、评估灾情、核查排放，也: Remote sensing allows humanity to regularly "check up" on Earth: estimating harvests, monitoring forests and glaciers, assessing disaster damage, verifying emissions, and serving as an important data source for climate research (see [[climate-model]]).
从太空连续观测云图和大气，让台风预报提前数天。: Continuous observation of cloud patterns and the atmosphere from space allows typhoon forecasts to be made several days in advance.
天气系统动辄上千公里，从地面看不全，从太空一目了然。卫星测量云和大气在可见光、红: Weather systems span over a thousand kilometers; they cannot be fully observed from the ground but are clear from space. Satellites measure radiation from clouds and the atmosphere across visible light, infrared, and microwave bands, inferring cloud cover, temperature, humidity, and wind ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]).
**静止气象卫星**盯着同一面地球，每隔几分钟拍一张云图，追踪台风；**极轨气象: **Geostationary meteorological satellites** watch one side of the Earth, taking a cloud image every few minutes to track typhoons; **Polar-orbiting meteorological satellites** sweep across the globe daily, measuring atmospheric temperature and humidity distribution, serving as the most critical input for numerical weather prediction (see [[numerical-weather-prediction]]).
1960 年 4 月 1 日美国发射泰罗斯 1 号（TIROS-1），传回第一张: The United States launched TIROS-1 on April 1, 1960, returning the first space cloud image; China launched its first Fengyun meteorological satellite in 1988.
台风路径如今可以提前数天预报，沿海居民有时间疏散，风暴死亡人数大幅下降。: Typhoon tracks can now be forecast several days in advance, giving coastal residents time to evacuate and significantly reducing storm-related fatalities.
从轨道上拍摄军事目标；早期用胶片舱返回地面冲洗。: Military targets are photographed from orbit; early missions used film capsules returned to Earth for processing.
从数百公里高空用大口径望远镜拍摄地面；能看多清，取决于镜头口径和轨道高度（[[p: Ground targets are imaged from the surface using large-aperture telescopes from hundreds of kilometers in altitude; clarity depends on lens aperture and orbital height ([[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]], [[p:wave|Interference, diffraction & resonance]]).
早期没有数字传输，美国\"日冕\"（Corona）卫星把胶片装进回收舱抛下，由飞: Early missions lacked digital transmission; the US "Corona" satellite carried film capsules dropped into recovery pods, which were caught by aircraft using tethers. Starting in 1976, KH-11 switched to electronic sensors, transmitting images in real time.
1960 年 8 月\"日冕\"首次成功回收胶片，一次拍到的苏联领土超过此前所有: On August 1, 1960, "Corona" successfully recovered its film for the first time; a single pass captured Soviet territory exceeding the combined coverage of all prior U-2 reconnaissance flights.
侦察卫星让美苏能核实对方的导弹数量，使军控条约有了核查手段；今天商业遥感卫星也让: Reconnaissance satellites allowed the US and USSR to verify each other's missile counts, providing verification means for arms control treaties; today, commercial remote sensing satellites also allow journalists to see conflict zones.
废弃卫星和碎片以每秒数公里的速度绕地飞行，碰撞可能连锁产生更多碎片。: Defunct satellites and debris orbit Earth at speeds of several kilometers per second; collisions can trigger cascading events that produce more debris.
近地轨道物体每秒飞行 7–8 公里，相撞时相对速度常超过每秒 10 公里；动能与: Objects in low Earth orbit travel at 7–8 km/s; upon collision, relative speeds often exceed 10 km/s. Kinetic energy is proportional to the square of velocity: a 1 cm fragment striking with this force is comparable to a hand grenade ([[p:energy|Conservation of energy]]).
太空垃圾包括失效卫星、火箭末级和碰撞碎片。地面雷达跟踪着数万个较大的物体，更小的: Space debris includes defunct satellites, rocket boosters, and collision fragments. Ground-based radar tracks tens of thousands of larger objects; smaller ones are too numerous to count, so spacecraft can only evade by changing orbit after warning.
1978 年 NASA 的凯斯勒（Donald Kessler）提出\"凯斯勒综: In 1978, NASA's Donald Kessler proposed "Kessler Syndrome": when debris reaches a certain density, cascading collisions make certain orbits unusable. Both the 2007 anti-satellite test and the 2009 satellite collision each produced over a thousand fragments.
新卫星如今被要求在寿命结束后限期离轨，主动清除碎片的技术也在试验中。: New satellites are now required to de-orbit within a set timeframe after their service life ends; technologies for active debris removal are also under trial.
加加林乘东方 1 号绕地球一圈，成为第一个进入太空的人。: Gagarin orbited Earth once aboard Vostok 1, becoming the first human in space.
把人送进轨道和发射卫星需要同样的速度（[[p:gravity|万有引力与轨道]]: Sending humans into orbit and launching satellites require the same speed ([[p:gravity|Gravitation & orbital mechanics]]); the challenge is bringing them back alive: heat protection during re-entry, life support systems, and escape procedures in case of accidents.
东方 1 号由直径约 2.3 米的球形返回舱和仪器舱组成，飞行基本由自动系统控制: Dongfanghong-1 consisted of a spherical reentry vehicle with a diameter of approximately 2.3 meters and an instrument compartment, with flight operations primarily controlled by automatic systems. The reentry vehicle passed through the atmosphere using an ablative heat shield, at an altitude of about 7 kilometers cosmonauts ejected from the capsule and landed separately via parachutes.
1961 年 4 月 12 日，苏联航天员加加林（Yuri Gagarin）绕地: On April 12, 1961, Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth once for a duration of 108 minutes, becoming the first person to enter space. In 1963, Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman to enter space.
它证明人能在失重中生存和工作；不到一个月，美国完成首次载人亚轨道飞行，肯尼迪随即: It proved that humans could survive and work in microgravity; less than a month later, the United States completed its first crewed suborbital flight, after which Kennedy subsequently announced the goal of landing on the Moon (see [[apollo]]).
把人送上太空并安全返回，需要解决生命保障、再入防热和逃逸救生。: Sending humans into space and safely returning them requires solving issues related to life support systems, reentry heat shielding, and escape life-saving systems.
人体只适应很窄的环境范围：气压、氧气、温度、重力。载人航天要在真空里造一个\"移: The human body is adapted only to a very narrow range of environmental conditions: atmospheric pressure, oxygen levels, temperature, and gravity. Crewed spaceflight must create a 'moving little Earth' in a vacuum and ensure that anyone can be brought back in case of any incident ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]], [[p:redundancy|Redundancy & error correction]]).
载人飞船比卫星多出三大系统：**生命保障**（见 [[life-support]: Crewed spacecraft have three additional systems compared to satellites: **life support** (see [[life-support]]), **reentry heat shielding** (see [[reentry-heat-shield]]), and **escape life-saving**—rapidly separating the crew module when a rocket failure occurs. Key equipment has two to three levels of redundancy. Long-term microgravity causes bone loss and muscle atrophy; cosmonauts must exercise for about two hours daily.
1961 年加加林首次进入太空，1965 年列昂诺夫首次太空行走。2003 年杨: Yuri Gagarin first entered space in 1961; Alexei Leonov performed the first spacewalk in 1965. In 2003, Yang Liwei flew on Shenzhou-5, making China the third independent nation to send humans into space.
人类有了在太空长期生活和做实验的能力，也付出了生命代价。用人还是用机器人，一直有: Humans have gained the ability to live and conduct experiments in space for long periods, but this came at a cost of human lives. Whether to use humans or robots has always been debated: robots are cheaper, while humans are more flexible.
1969 年 7 月阿波罗 11 号首次载人登月，共 12 人踏上月球。: On July 20, 1969, Apollo 11 made the first crewed lunar landing, with 12 people stepping onto the Moon's surface.
1961 年肯尼迪宣布十年内登月。1967 年阿波罗 1 号在地面测试中起火，三: Kennedy announced a goal to land on the Moon within ten years in 1961. In 1967, Apollo-1 caught fire during ground testing, resulting in the deaths of three cosmonauts. On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin of Apollo-11 stepped onto the Moon, while Michael Collins waited in orbit. Between 1969 and 1972, there were six successful lunar landings with 12 people walking on the surface; Apollo-13 exploded en route, but its crew returned safely using the Lunar Module as a 'lifeboat'.
阿波罗带回约 382 千克月球样品，让科学家推断月球可能起源于一次大撞击。它也是: Apollo brought back approximately 382 kilograms of lunar samples, allowing scientists to infer that the Moon may have originated from a large impact. It was also one of the largest systems engineering projects of the 20th century, with about 400,000 people involved at its peak, promoting the development of integrated circuits, reliability engineering, and project management. The 'Earth-out' photos also helped promote modern environmental movements.
阿波罗的月球轨道交会方案：只有登月舱下到月面，指令舱留在月球轨道等待，最后只有指: Apollo's lunar orbit rendezvous plan: only the Lunar Module descended to the Moon's surface, while the Command Module remained in lunar orbit waiting; finally, only the Command Module returned to Earth.
部分可重复使用的有翼航天器，执行 135 次任务，两次事故造成 14 人遇难。: Some partially reusable winged spacecraft executed 135 missions; two accidents resulted in 14 fatalities.
像飞机一样反复使用航天器，以降低每次发射的成本（[[p:scale|规模效应与学: Like aircraft, spacecraft are reused repeatedly to reduce the cost of each launch ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]). The orbiter has wings and lands like a glider on a runway upon return.
由轨道器、两枚可回收的固体助推器和一个一次性外贮箱组成，货舱能装下哈勃望远镜。但: Composed of an orbiter, two reusable solid rocket boosters, and one expendable external tank, the cargo bay could carry the Hubble Telescope. However, after each flight, it required extensive maintenance, with actual costs far exceeding expectations.
1981 年首飞。1986 年挑战者号因低温下助推器密封圈失效解体；2003 年: First flight in 1981. In 1986, Challenger disintegrated due to a booster seal failure at low temperatures; in 2003, Columbia disintegrated during reentry after foam damage to its wing heat shield, with two incidents resulting in 14 fatalities combined. Retired in 2011, it flew 135 times.
它建造了国际空间站的主体、发射并维修了哈勃；\"把异常当正常\"的教训成为工程安: It built the main structure of the International Space Station, launched and repaired Hubble; the lesson of 'treating anomalies as normal' became a classic case study in engineering safety.
长期在轨的载人实验室；国际空间站和中国天宫空间站是当前代表。: Long-duration crewed laboratories in orbit; the International Space Station and China's Tiangong Space Station are current representatives.
在轨道上建一个长期有人的\"实验室兼宿舍\"，研究长期失重对人体的影响，在微重力: Building a long-term inhabited 'laboratory and dormitory' in orbit to study the effects of long-term microgravity on the human body and conduct experiments impossible under ground gravity ([[p:gravity|Gravitation & orbital mechanics]]). It operates at an altitude of about 400 kilometers; although the atmosphere is extremely thin there, it still causes gradual altitude loss, requiring periodic engine burns for 'reboosting'.
空间站由多个舱段在轨拼装而成，太阳能板提供电力，货运飞船定期补给食物、水和推进剂: The space station is assembled in orbit from multiple modules; solar panels provide power, cargo spacecraft regularly supply food, water, and propellant, while crewed spacecraft rotate crews. The station's life support system recovers most of the water (see [[life-support]]).
1971 年苏联发射第一个空间站礼炮 1 号；1986 年起建造和平号。国际空间: The Soviet Union launched the first space station, Kosmos-1, in 1971; construction of Mir began in 1986. The International Space Station launched its first module in 1998 and has been continuously inhabited since November 2000, operated cooperatively by the United States, Russia, Europe, Japan, Canada, and others. China's Tiangong Space Station was completed in 2022 and has been permanently inhabited since that year.
人类已经在太空连续生活了二十多年。空间站积累的长期飞行经验，是将来登月基地和载人: Humans have now lived continuously in space for over twenty years. The long-duration flight experience accumulated by space stations forms the foundation for future lunar bases and crewed Mars missions.
在密闭舱内提供氧气、水、温度和气压，并清除二氧化碳，尽量循环利用。: Provide oxygen, water, temperature, and atmospheric pressure within a sealed compartment, and remove carbon dioxide, aiming for maximum recycling.
密闭舱里的人每天消耗约 0.8 千克氧气和几升水，呼出二氧化碳、排出汗和尿。生命: People in a sealed compartment consume approximately 0.8 kilograms of oxygen and several liters of water daily, exhaling carbon dioxide and excreting sweat and urine. The life support system must maintain these quantities within safe ranges like the body's homeostatic regulation ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]).
早期飞船带储存的氧气，用氢氧化锂吸收二氧化碳。长期空间站必须循环：电解水制氧，把: Early spacecraft carried stored oxygen, using lithium hydroxide to absorb carbon dioxide. Long-term space stations must cycle: electrolyze water to produce oxygen, react carbon dioxide and hydrogen to regenerate water, and purify urine and condensate into drinking water; the International Space Station can recover about 98% of water.
1970 年阿波罗 13 号事故中，航天员用胶带和塑料袋把方形滤罐接到圆形接口上: During the 1970 Apollo 13 accident, astronauts used tape and plastic bags to connect a square filter canister to a circular interface, temporarily solving carbon dioxide overpressure.
闭环生命保障是长期太空生活的前提，其水回收技术也启发了地面应用。: Closed-loop life support is a prerequisite for long-term space living; its water recovery technology also inspired terrestrial applications.
航天器以极高速度返回大气层时把动能变成热，防热罩通过烧蚀或隔热保护舱体。: When spacecraft return to the atmosphere at extremely high speeds, kinetic energy converts to heat; thermal protection shields protect the cabin through ablation or insulation.
从轨道返回的飞船速度约每秒 7.8 公里，巨大的动能只能变成热（[[p:ener: A spacecraft returning from orbit travels at about 7.8 kilometers per second; its massive kinetic energy can only convert to heat ([[p:energy|Conservation of energy]]), compressing front air to thousands of degrees Celsius. The key to thermal protection is preventing heat transfer into the cabin ([[p:heat|Heat transfer]]).
钝头外形在前方推出一层激波，大部分热量留在空气里。**烧蚀防热层**一层层熔化、: A blunt-body shape pushes a shockwave ahead, leaving most heat in the air. **Ablative thermal protection** melts and vaporizes layer by layer, carrying heat away; both Shenzhou and Apollo used it. **Thermal tiles** (see [[advanced-ceramics]]) have extremely poor thermal conductivity and are reusable. During re-entry, surrounding air ionization causes several minutes of communication "blackout".
20 世纪 50 年代，美国工程师艾伦（H. Julian Allen）提出钝头: In the 1950s, American engineer H. Julian Allen proposed blunt-body theory, overturning the intuition that "pointed shapes are better".
没有防热就没有返回式卫星和载人航天；哥伦比亚号说明，防热层一处破损就足以致命。: Without thermal protection, there would be no return satellites or crewed spaceflight; Columbia demonstrated that damage to a single spot in the thermal protection layer could be fatal.
