从东方红一号（1970）到神舟载人、嫦娥探月、天问探火和天宫空间站。: From Dongfanghong-1 (1970) to Shenzhou crewed flights, Chang'e lunar exploration, Tianwen Mars exploration, and Tiangong space station.
中国航天走\"一步一个台阶、成体系推进\"的路线：先火箭卫星，再载人，再探月、深: China's aerospace follows a "step-by-step, systematic advancement" route: first rockets and satellites, then crewed flight, then lunar exploration, deep space, and space station; each step accumulates technology for the next ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]).
**长征系列火箭**承担绝大多数发射；**载人航天**按飞船、空间实验室、空间站: **Long March series rockets** bear the majority of launches; **crewed spaceflight** follows a "three-step" path of spacecraft, space laboratory, and space station; **lunar exploration program** implements via "orbit, land, return"; **Beidou** builds a global navigation system in three generations (see [[gnss]]). In recent years, many commercial aerospace companies have emerged, and reusable rockets have also been successfully tested (see [[reusable-rocket]]).
1970 年东方红一号卫星发射，钱学森被视为中国航天的奠基人。2003 年杨利伟: Dongfanghong-1 satellite launched in 1970; Qian Xuesen is regarded as the founder of China's aerospace. In 2003, Yang Liwei entered space aboard Shenzhou-5; in 2019, Chang'e-4 made the first landing on the far side of the Moon; in 2021, Zhurong landed on Mars; in 2022, Tiangong space station was completed; in 2024, Chang'e-6 made the first sample return from the far side of the Moon.
中国成为第三个独立掌握载人航天、空间站和月球采样返回能力的国家，并计划在 203: China became the third independent nation to master crewed spaceflight, space station, and lunar sample return capabilities, and plans to achieve crewed lunar landing before 2030.
一件可穿的\"微型飞船\"，提供气压、氧气、温控和防护，让人能出舱行走。: A wearable "microspacecraft" providing pressure, oxygen, temperature control, and protection, enabling extravehicular activity.
真空中没有外部气压，体液会沸腾、肺里的空气会膨胀。航天服是一件穿在身上的\"微型: In vacuum, there is no external pressure; body fluids would boil, and air in the lungs would expand. A spacesuit is a "microspacecraft" worn on the body, maintaining pressure and oxygen, and regulating temperature ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]).
出舱服有十几层：里层是布满细管的液冷服，中间的气密层保持约 0.3 个大气压的纯: The extravehicular suit has a dozen or so layers: the inner layer is a liquid-cooled suit covered with fine tubes; the middle hermetic layer maintains pure oxygen at about 0.3 atmospheres; the outer layer protects against micrometeoroids. The backpack provides oxygen, carbon dioxide filtering, and power, capable of independent operation for 7–8 hours.
1965 年列昂诺夫首次太空行走时，航天服膨胀到进不了气闸舱，他冒险放气才挤回去: Leonov's first spacewalk in 1965 saw the spacesuit expand so much it could not enter the airlock; he risked releasing air to squeeze back inside. In 2008, Zhai Zhengguang completed China's first spacewalk wearing the domestic "Feitian" spacesuit.
航天服让人能在舱外组装空间站、维修望远镜、在月面行走。: Spacesuits enable assembly of space stations outside the cabin, telescope maintenance, and walking on the lunar surface.
苏联/俄罗斯的载人飞船，服役半个多世纪，是史上使用最久的载人飞船。: Soviet/Russian crewed spacecraft have served for over half a century; they are the longest-serving crewed spacecraft in history.
联盟号的设计哲学是\"简单、保守、可靠\"：把能用的设计长期沿用、逐步改进，而不: The Soyuz design philosophy is "simple, conservative, reliable": using proven designs long-term with gradual improvements rather than starting from scratch each generation ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]).
三个舱：轨道舱供在轨生活，钟形返回舱是唯一回到地面的部分，服务舱装发动机和太阳能: Three modules: the orbital module provides in-orbit living; the bell-shaped re-entry module is the only part returning to Earth; the service module houses engines and solar panels. Just before landing, the re-entry module ignites retro-thrust engines to reduce impact.
1967 年首飞时，科马罗夫因降落伞故障遇难；1971 年联盟 11 号返回时失: During the first flight in 1967, Komarov died due to parachute failure; in 1971, Soyuz 11 lost pressure on return, killing all three crew members. Since then, improvements have maintained a good record over the long term.
普通人付费进入太空；从搭乘联盟号到亚轨道飞行和私人轨道任务。: Ordinary people pay to enter space; from riding Soyuz to suborbital flights and private orbital missions.
太空旅游的本质是价格问题：发射成本足够低，就会有人愿意花钱看一眼弯曲的地平线（[: The essence of space tourism is a matter of price: if launch costs become sufficiently low, people will be willing to pay money to look at the curved horizon ([[p:incentives|Incentives & game theory]]).
**亚轨道飞行**飞到约 80–100 公里，体验几分钟失重，票价数十万美元；*: **Suborbital flight** reaches approximately 80–100 km, experiences minutes of weightlessness, and tickets cost tens of millions of dollars; **Orbital flight** stays aboard Soyuz or Dragon spacecraft for several days, costing tens of millions of dollars.
2001 年美国商人蒂托（Dennis Tito）乘联盟号访问国际空间站，成为第: In 2001, American businessman Dennis Tito traveled to the International Space Station aboard a Soyuz spacecraft, becoming the first self-funded space tourist. In 2021, Virgin Galactic and Blue Origin successively carried passengers on flights, while SpaceX's "Inspiration4" became the first orbital flight with an all-civilian crew.
它仍是富人的体验，但为商业载人飞船提供了收入，也引发了排放和公平性的争议。: It remains an experience for the wealthy but provides revenue for commercial crewed spacecraft and has sparked debates over emissions and equity.
飞向其他天体的无人航天器；旅行者 1 号已飞出日球层进入星际空间。: Unmanned spacecraft flying to other celestial bodies; Voyager 1 has already left the heliosphere and entered interstellar space.
飞往其他行星不靠一直开着发动机，而是靠一次精确加速，进入一条绕太阳、正好与目标相: Flying to other planets does not rely on keeping engines running continuously, but rather on a single precise acceleration to enter an orbit around the Sun that meets the target exactly, after which it relies almost entirely on inertia and gravity to "coast" ([[p:gravity|Gravitation & orbital mechanics]]).
探测器要独立工作多年：靠太阳能板或核电池供电（见 [[nuclear-rtg]]: Probes must operate independently for many years: powered by solar panels or nuclear batteries (see [[nuclear-rtg]]), communicating with Earth at very low power using large antennas; ground stations use deep-space antennas with diameters of tens of meters to receive signals. Command round-trips take from tens of minutes to tens of hours, and many operations can only be pre-programmed or completed autonomously.
1977 年发射的旅行者 1 号、2 号飞掠木星和土星，2 号还飞掠了天王星和海: Voyager 1 and 2, launched in 1977, flew by Jupiter and Saturn; Voyager 2 also flew by Uranus and Neptune. Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012; as of 2026, it is more than 25 billion km from Earth, with a one-way signal travel time of nearly one day. New Horizons flew by Pluto in 2015.
探测器把行星从\"光点\"变成具体的世界：木卫二冰层下的海洋、土卫六的甲烷湖，也: Probes turn planets from "dots of light" into concrete worlds: oceans beneath the ice shell of Europa, methane lakes on Titan, and also provide clues for the search for extraterrestrial life.
探测器掠过行星时\"借\"行星的速度加速或转向，不用额外燃料。: When a probe passes close to a planet, it can "borrow" the planet's velocity to accelerate or change direction without using extra fuel.
探测器掠过行星时，相对行星飞进多快、飞出也多快；但行星在绕太阳运动，探测器被\": When a probe passes close to a planet, how fast it flies in relative to the planet determines how fast it flies out; however, since the planet is moving around the Sun, the probe is "carried" along for a stretch, changing its velocity relative to the Sun ([[p:gravity|Gravitation & orbital mechanics]], [[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]]). It is like a tennis ball hitting an oncoming train and bouncing faster.
从行星后方掠过可以加速，从前方掠过可以减速，还能顺便转向。代价是要等行星排到合适: Passing behind a planet can accelerate; passing in front can decelerate; one can also turn around as a side effect. The cost is having to wait for the planet to align into a suitable position.
1974 年水手 10 号借金星引力飞往水星，首次实用引力弹弓。旅行者号利用 2: In 1974, Mariner 10 used Venus's gravity to fly to Mercury, achieving the first practical gravity assist. The Voyager probes utilized the rare alignment of outer planets in the late 1970s to conduct sequential flybys of multiple planets.
没有它，大多数外太阳系任务要么飞不到，要么要多花几十年。: Without it, most missions to the outer solar system would either not reach their targets or would have to spend decades more.
探测器从行星后方掠过，\"搭\"上行星绕日运动的顺风车，相对太阳的速度变大。: When a probe passes behind a planet, it "hitches a ride" on the planet's motion around the Sun, increasing its velocity relative to the Sun.
用钚-238 衰变的热量通过热电偶发电，供远离太阳的探测器使用几十年。: Electricity is generated from the heat of Pu-238 decay through thermocouples, powering probes far from the Sun for decades.
放射性同位素衰变持续放热（[[p:decay|放射性衰变]]），热电材料把温差直: Radioactive isotopes continue to release heat ([[p:decay|Radioactive decay]]); thermoelectric materials convert the temperature difference directly into electricity (see [[thermoelectric-effect]]). The half-life of Pu-238 is approximately 87.7 years, allowing stable power supply for decades without moving parts.
中心是钚-238 燃料块，外包热电材料，冷端用散热片向太空散热。效率只有约 6%: The core consists of a Pu-238 fuel block, wrapped in thermoelectric material, with the cold end using heat sinks to radiate heat into space. Efficiency is only about 6%, with power output ranging from tens to hundreds of watts, but it is almost the only viable option in places where sunlight is too weak or there are long nights and dust storms. The fuel casing is designed so as not to rupture even in launch accidents.
1961 年美国导航卫星 Transit 4A 首次在太空使用核电池；旅行者号至: In 1961, the US Transit 4A navigation satellite first used a nuclear battery in space; Voyager still relies on it today, though power output declines year by year.
它让人类能探索木星以远的外太阳系；钚-238 产量稀少，一直是深空任务的瓶颈。: It enables humanity to explore the outer solar system beyond Jupiter; Pu-238 production is scarce and has always been a bottleneck for deep-space missions.
在火星表面行驶、采样和分析的机器人；中国祝融号于 2021 年着陆。: Robots that drive across the Martian surface, sample materials, and analyze them; China's Zhurong landed in 2021.
火星离地球远时信号单程要二十多分钟，无法实时遥控，火星车必须自己看路、自己判断（: When Mars is far from Earth, the one-way signal takes over twenty minutes, making real-time remote control impossible; the Mars rover must see the path itself and judge independently ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
用立体相机构建地形、自主规划路线，用机械臂、钻头和光谱仪分析岩石。最难的是着陆：: Using stereo cameras to construct terrain maps, autonomously planning routes, using robotic arms, drills, and spectrometers to analyze rocks. The most difficult part is landing: the Martian atmosphere is too thin; besides parachutes, retro-rockets, airbags, or "sky cranes" must be added.
1997 年索杰纳号成为第一辆火星车；机遇号原计划工作 90 天，实际工作近 1: Sojourner became the first Mars rover in 1997; Opportunity was originally planned to work for 90 days but actually operated for nearly 15 years. In 2021, Perseverance landed, carrying Ingenuity which completed the first powered flight on another world; that same year, China's Zhurong landed on Mars.
火星车证明火星曾长期有液态水，并为未来的采样返回封存了样品。: Mars rovers have proven that Mars once had liquid water for a long period and has preserved samples for future sample return missions.
在大气层外观测宇宙，不受大气扰动和吸收；韦布望远镜看红外宇宙。: Observing the universe from outside the atmosphere avoids atmospheric disturbance and absorption; the James Webb Telescope observes the infrared universe.
地球大气会让星光闪烁模糊，还会吸收大部分紫外线、红外线和 X 射线（[[p:em: Earth's atmosphere causes starlight to twinkle and blur, while also absorbing most ultraviolet, infrared, and X-ray radiation ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]]). Placing telescopes outside the atmosphere allows for clearer views and observation of more spectral bands ([[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]]).
哈勃望远镜口径 2.4 米，在 500 多公里高的轨道上观测可见光和紫外线。韦布: The Hubble Telescope has a 2.4-meter aperture and observes visible light and ultraviolet from an orbit over 500 kilometers high. The James Webb Telescope's primary mirror is composed of 18 gold-coated hexagonal segments, totaling a 6.5-meter aperture; it was folded for launch and deployed in space. Located near the Sun-Earth L2 point approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, it uses a sunshield the size of a tennis court to cool the mirrors to around -230°C, enabling observation of extremely faint infrared radiation—light from the earliest galaxies in the universe, which has been "redshifted" into the infrared band due to cosmic expansion.
1990 年哈勃发射后发现主镜磨错了约 2 微米，1993 年航天员上天加装了\: After Hubble was launched in 1990, it was discovered that the primary mirror was ground incorrectly by about 2 micrometers; astronauts flew up in 1993 to install "glasses" for correction. The James Webb Telescope was launched on December 25, 2021.
哈勃帮助精确测定了宇宙的年龄，并参与发现宇宙在加速膨胀；韦布正在观测宇宙诞生后几: Hubble helped precisely determine the age of the universe and participated in the discovery that the universe is expanding at an accelerated rate; the James Webb Telescope is currently observing galaxies and exoplanet atmospheres within the first few hundred million years after the birth of the universe.
嫦娥四号首次在月背着陆，嫦娥五号、六号采样返回；各国计划建月球基地。: Chang'e 4 made the first landing on the far side of the Moon; Chang'e 5 and Chang'e 6 returned samples; various countries plan to build lunar bases.
月球只有约 3 天航程，是检验深空生存技术的\"近郊\"。南极阴影坑里可能有水冰: The Moon offers only about a 3-day transit time, serving as a "suburb" for testing deep space survival technologies. Water ice may exist in shadowed craters at the south pole, which can be electrolyzed into oxygen and propellant—using local resources saves the enormous cost of transporting materials from Earth ([[p:energydensity|Energy density]]).
先由无人探测器着陆、采样、勘探资源，再过渡到载人登月和长期基地。美国有阿尔忒弥斯: The process begins with unmanned probes landing, sampling, and exploring resources, then transitions to crewed lunar landings and long-term bases. The United States has the Artemis program; China plans to use the Long March 10 rocket for crewed lunar missions.
2019 年嫦娥四号首次在月球背面着陆；2020 年嫦娥五号、2024 年嫦娥六: Chang'e 4 made the first landing on the Moon's far side in 2019; Chang'e 5 and Chang'e 6 returned samples from the near side and far side respectively in 2020 and 2024. In April 2026, Artemis 2 will carry four people on a lunar orbit flight, marking the first time since 1972 that humans have left low Earth orbit.
月球重新成为大国和商业公司的竞争目标，月面资源归属等国际规则仍在形成。: The Moon has once again become a target for competition among major powers and commercial companies; international rules regarding resource ownership on the lunar surface are still being formed.
用航天器撞击小行星改变其轨道；DART 任务在 2022 年首次验证。: Using spacecraft to impact asteroids alters their orbits; the DART mission first verified this in 2022.
小行星撞击罕见但可能是毁灭性的，6600 万年前的一次撞击被认为导致了恐龙灭绝。: Asteroid impacts are rare but potentially devastating; an impact 66 million years ago is believed to have led to the extinction of dinosaurs. As long as it is discovered years in advance, a gentle nudge is sufficient: changing speed by only a few centimeters per second can accumulate over many years to cause the asteroid to miss Earth ([[p:momentum|Conservation of momentum]]).
先**发现**：巡天编目所有可能危险的近地天体，推算上百年的轨道；再**偏转**: First **discover**: catalog all potentially hazardous near-Earth objects and calculate their orbits for up to 100 years; then **deflect**: the most mature method is "kinetic impact," where ejected debris from the impact provides additional thrust.
2022 年 9 月 26 日，NASA 的 DART 探测器撞击小行星\"迪莫: On September 26, 2022, NASA's DART probe impacted the asteroid Dimorphos, shortening its orbital period around its primary by approximately 32 minutes, first proving that humans can alter celestial orbits.
行星防御已成为有预算、有演练的国际合作项目。: Planetary defense has become an international cooperative project with budgets and exercises.
私营公司承担发射、卫星和载人任务，竞争与复用让发射成本大幅下降。: Private companies undertake launch, satellite, and crewed missions; competition and reusability have significantly reduced launch costs.
过去航天多用\"成本加成\"合同，承包商花得越多赚得越多。改为\"按服务付费\": In the past, spaceflight relied on "cost-plus" contracts where contractors earned more the more they spent. After switching to fixed-price "pay-for-service" contracts, enterprises must reduce their own costs; competition and reusability only truly take effect then ([[p:incentives|Incentives & game theory]]).
政府从\"自己造火箭\"转为\"购买发射和运输服务\"，企业设计、拥有并运营火箭: Governments shifted from "building rockets themselves" to "purchasing launch and transport services." Enterprises design, own, and operate rockets and spacecraft, spreading costs through vertical integration, mass production, and their own satellite constellations (see [[satellite-internet]]). Launch prices have dropped significantly, driving new markets such as small satellites and space tourism.
2006 年 NASA 启动商业轨道运输服务（COTS）。2008 年 Spac: In 2006, NASA launched the Commercial Orbital Transportation Services (COTS) program. In 2008, SpaceX's Falcon 1 became the first privately developed and orbital liquid-fuel rocket. In 2020, Dragon spacecraft first carried astronauts to the International Space Station. In 2023, LandSpace's Zhuque-2 became the first orbital liquid-oxygen methane rocket.
如今每年入轨的航天器绝大多数是商业卫星，航天正从\"国家工程\"变成产业，也带来: Today, the vast majority of spacecraft reaching orbit each year are commercial satellites; spaceflight is transforming from a "national project" into an industry, though this also brings issues such as orbital congestion and interference with astronomical observations.
用无害或减弱的\"假病原体\"预先训练免疫系统，真病原体来时就能迅速消灭它。: Using harmless or weakened "fake pathogens" to pre-train the immune system allows for rapid elimination when the real pathogen arrives.
免疫系统靠\"认形状\"识别入侵者：抗体和免疫细胞能与病原体表面特定的分子（抗原: The immune system identifies invaders by "recognizing shapes": antibodies and immune cells can precisely bind to specific molecules (antigens) on the pathogen's surface ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]). Upon first encountering a new pathogen, the body takes one or two weeks to produce enough "weapons," often too late; however, after fighting once, **memory cells** are left behind, allowing a massive counterattack within days next time. Vaccines use harmless "fake pathogens" for a preliminary drill, enabling the body to possess memory in advance ([[p:germ|Germ theory]]).
疫苗有几类：**减毒活疫苗**（麻疹、口服脊灰）用削弱了的活病原体；**灭活疫苗: Vaccines come in several categories: **live attenuated vaccines** (measles, oral polio) use weakened live pathogens; **inactivated vaccines** use killed pathogens; **subunit vaccines** use only a small piece of the pathogen's protein (hepatitis B, HPV); **toxoid vaccines** target bacterial toxins (tetanus); **mRNA vaccines** directly provide cells with a "blueprint" for an antigen (see [[mrna-vaccine]]). When a sufficient proportion of the population has immunity, pathogens cannot find the next host; unvaccinated individuals are also protected, known as **herd immunity**. The stronger the transmissibility, the higher the required vaccination ratio; measles requires approximately 95%.
1796 年英国医生詹纳（Edward Jenner）发现接种牛痘能预防天花，\: In 1796, British doctor Edward Jenner discovered that inoculation with cowpox could prevent smallpox. The word "vaccine" comes from the Latin word for "cow." In 1885, Pasteur (Louis Pasteur) used a weakened rabies vaccine to save a boy who had been bitten. Subsequently in the 20th century, vaccines for diphtheria, tetanus, polio, and measles were developed one after another.
天花被彻底消灭（见 [[smallpox-eradication]]），脊灰接近: Smallpox was completely eradicated (see [[smallpox-eradication]]), and polio is close to eradication. The World Health Organization estimates that over the past 50 years, global immunization programs have saved at least 154 million lives, most of whom were infants. Vaccines require cold chain storage and high vaccination rates to be effective; therefore, "vaccine hesitancy" has become a new challenge for public health.
第一次感染时抗体上升慢、峰值低；接种疫苗后再遇到病原体，记忆细胞让抗体又快又多。: Upon first infection, antibody levels rise slowly with a low peak; after vaccination, when encountering the pathogen again, memory cells allow antibodies to form quickly and in large quantities.
通过全球疫苗接种和\"环形接种\"策略，天花成为第一个被人类彻底消灭的传染病。: Through global vaccination and the "ring vaccination" strategy, smallpox became the first infectious disease completely eradicated by humans.
天花病毒只感染人，没有动物宿主；病人症状明显、容易识别；疫苗一针就能长期免疫。只: The smallpox virus infects only humans and has no animal host; patient symptoms are obvious and easy to identify; a single dose of vaccine provides long-term immunity. As long as the chain of human-to-human transmission is cut, the virus has nowhere to go ([[p:germ|Germ theory]]).
后期改用**环形接种**：一发现病例就隔离病人，并给接触者、接触者的接触者接种，: Later, "ring vaccination" was adopted: upon discovering a case, the patient is isolated, and those who have been in contact with them, and their contacts, are vaccinated, similar to digging an isolation belt around a fire. Bifurcated needles make vaccination simple and conserve vaccine supply.
1967 年世界卫生组织启动强化根除计划；1977 年索马里出现最后一例自然病例: In 1967, the World Health Organization launched an intensified eradication program; the last natural case appeared in Somalia in 1977, and smallpox was declared eradicated by the WHO in 1980.
天花仅在 20 世纪就夺去约 3 亿人的生命。它是至今唯一被彻底消灭的人类传染病: Smallpox took away approximately 300 million lives during the 20th century alone. It is the only human infectious disease that has been completely eradicated to date.
用统计和地图追踪疾病在人群中的分布和原因；斯诺通过霍乱地图锁定了污染的水泵。: Using statistics and maps to track the distribution and causes of diseases within populations; Snow used a cholera map to identify contaminated water pumps.
谁得病、在哪里、什么时候得，背后藏着原因。比较不同人群的发病率，就能在弄清机理之: Who gets sick, where they get sick, and when they get sick—behind these patterns lie causes. By comparing infection rates among different populations, one can first identify the cause before understanding the mechanism ([[p:probability|Probability & statistical inference]]).
比较暴露组和未暴露组的发病率（队列研究），或比较病人和健康人过去的暴露（病例对照: Compare infection rates between exposed and unexposed groups (cohort study), or compare past exposures between patients and healthy individuals (case-control study), then exclude interfering factors such as age; infectious diseases also require tracking contact chains.
1854 年伦敦霍乱爆发，斯诺（John Snow）把死亡病例标在地图上，发现它: In 1854, a cholera outbreak occurred in London; Snow (John Snow) marked death cases on a map and found they clustered around a water pump on Broad Street. In the 1950s, Doll and Hill proved that smoking causes lung cancer.
清洁饮水、控烟、接种策略和疫情应对，都以流行病学数据为依据。: Clean drinking water, smoking control, vaccination strategies, and epidemic response all rely on epidemiological data as their basis.
把牛奶等食品加热到 60–70°C 左右保持一段时间，杀死大部分病菌而不破坏风味: Heat milk and other foods to approximately 60–70°C for a period of time to kill most pathogens without destroying flavor.
多数致病菌怕热，不必煮沸：在 60–70°C 维持一段时间就能杀灭绝大多数病菌，: Most pathogenic bacteria are heat-sensitive; boiling is not necessary: maintaining them at 60–70°C for a period can kill the vast majority of pathogens without making milk taste bad ([[p:germ|Germ theory]], [[p:heat|Heat transfer]]).
传统做法是 63°C 保持 30 分钟；现代乳品厂多用 72°C、15 秒的高温: The traditional method was to hold at 63°C for 30 minutes; modern dairy factories mostly use high-temperature short-time continuous processing at 72°C for 15 seconds. It cannot kill all spores, so pasteurized milk still requires refrigeration; ultra-high temperature sterilization at approximately 135°C for a few seconds allows milk to be stored at room temperature for several months.
1864 年巴斯德发现适度加热能防止葡萄酒变酸，后来这一方法用于牛奶。: In 1864, Pasteur discovered that moderate heating could prevent wine from going sour; later this method was applied to milk.
生牛奶曾是结核、伤寒的重要传播途径，巴氏消毒大大降低了城市婴儿死亡率。: Raw milk was once an important transmission route for tuberculosis and typhoid fever; pasteurization greatly reduced infant mortality rates in cities.
科赫分离出结核杆菌等病原体并提出判定标准，医学开始\"按病原对症\"。: Koch isolated pathogens such as the tubercle bacillus and proposed criteria for pathogenicity, marking the beginning of medicine shifting to "treat based on the cause."
每种传染病都有一个特定的病原体。把它分离出来、单独培养，就能研究它、检测它，并对: Each infectious disease has a specific pathogen. By isolating it and culturing it separately, one can study it, test it, and find vaccines and drugs that target it ([[p:germ|Germ theory]]).
固体培养基让单个细菌长成菌落，得到纯种；染色加显微镜区分细菌。判断致病菌要看它是: Solid culture media allow individual bacteria to grow into colonies, obtaining pure strains; staining combined with microscopy distinguishes bacteria. To judge pathogenic bacteria, one must observe whether they always appear in patients, whether they can be isolated and cultured, and whether they cause the same disease after inoculation; this is known as Koch's postulates.
1882 年德国医生科赫（Robert Koch）发现结核杆菌，次年发现霍乱弧菌: In 1882, German doctor Robert Koch discovered the tubercle bacillus; the following year he discovered Vibrio cholerae; in 1905, he received the Nobel Prize.
医学从\"对症\"转向\"对因\"，为疫苗、消毒和抗生素铺平了道路。: Medicine shifted from "treating symptoms" to "treating causes," paving the way for vaccines, disinfection, and antibiotics.
向自来水中加入少量氯杀灭病菌，是 20 世纪最大的公共卫生成就之一。: Adding a small amount of chlorine to drinking water to kill pathogens was one of the greatest public health achievements of the 20th century.
氯是强氧化剂，溶于水生成次氯酸，能破坏细菌和病毒的膜与酶（[[p:redox|氧: Chlorine is a strong oxidizing agent. When dissolved in water, it forms hypochlorous acid, which can destroy the membranes and enzymes of bacteria and viruses ([[p:redox|Redox & electrochemistry]]). A small residual amount of chlorine remains in the distribution network, continuing to prevent secondary contamination ([[p:germ|Germ theory]]).
水厂先混凝、沉淀、过滤去除泥沙，再按剂量加氯，确保管网末梢仍有余氯。臭氧和紫外线: Water treatment plants first coagulate, settle, and filter out silt and mud, then add chlorine according to dosage to ensure that residual chlorine remains at the farthest ends of the network. Ozone and ultraviolet light can also disinfect, but they do not provide a sustained effect.
1908 年美国泽西城开始对公共供水连续加氯，是美国第一座这样做的城市。: In 1908, Newark, New Jersey, began continuous chlorination of public water supplies, making it the first city in the United States to do so.
伤寒、霍乱等水源性传染病在发达国家几乎绝迹，它常被列为 20 世纪最重要的公共卫: Waterborne infectious diseases such as typhoid and cholera have almost disappeared in developed countries; they are often listed among the most important public health achievements of the 20th century.
用糖和盐按比例配水，就能让腹泻病人肠道重新吸收水分，挽救了数千万儿童。: By mixing sugar and salt in proportion with water, diarrhea patients can reabsorb water in their intestines, saving tens of millions of children.
腹泻致死的直接原因往往是脱水。肠道吸收钠时会同时带走葡萄糖，水分随之进入体内；按: The direct cause of death from diarrhea is often dehydration. When the intestine absorbs sodium, it simultaneously carries away glucose, causing water to enter the body; by dissolving sugar and salt in water at an appropriate ratio, even during diarrhea, the intestine can absorb water back ([[p:diffusion|Diffusion & membranes]]).
一小包配好的葡萄糖和电解质，用干净水冲开即可。便宜、易储存、不用打点滴，经过简单: A small packet of prepared glucose and electrolytes can be dissolved with clean water. It is inexpensive, easy to store, does not require intravenous infusion, and can be used by parents after simple training.
1968 年前后，孟加拉国达卡和印度加尔各答的临床试验证明了它的效果；1971: Around 1968, clinical trials in Dhaka, Bangladesh, and Calcutta, India, proved its effectiveness; in 1971, it was used on a large scale to save cholera patients in a refugee camp in Bangladesh.
口服补液盐挽救了数千万人的生命，主要是发展中国家的儿童。: Oral rehydration salts have saved tens of millions of lives, mainly children in developing countries.
用高压把水加热到 121°C 以上，杀死包括芽孢在内的所有微生物。: By using high pressure to heat water above 121°C, all microorganisms, including spores, are killed.
有些细菌的芽孢能耐受沸水。加压让水的沸点升高，约 2 个大气压时蒸汽可达 121: Some bacterial spores can withstand boiling water. Pressurization raises the boiling point of water; at approximately two atmospheres of pressure, steam can reach 121°C. When steam condenses on instrument surfaces, it releases a large amount of latent heat ([[p:phase|Phase change & latent heat]]), which is sufficient to kill even spores.
高压灭菌器像一口大压力锅：排出冷空气，充入饱和蒸汽，在 121°C 保持 15–: An autoclave is like a large pressure cooker: it expels cold air, fills with saturated steam, maintains 121°C for 15–20 minutes, then vents and dries. Effectiveness is confirmed using indicator cards and biological indicators.
1879 年巴斯德的助手尚贝兰（Charles Chamberland）发明了高: In 1879, Charles Chamberland, an assistant of Pasteur, invented the autoclave.
可靠灭菌是无菌手术、微生物实验和疫苗生产的基础（见 [[antiseptic]]: Reliable sterilization is the foundation for sterile surgery, microbiological experiments, and vaccine production (see [[antiseptic]]).
利用带静电的熔喷无纺布吸附微粒，能过滤至少 95% 的细小颗粒。: Using electrostatically charged melt-blown nonwoven fabric to adsorb particles can filter at least 95% of fine particles.
口罩滤层不是筛子。细小颗粒在纤维间穿行时会因惯性撞上纤维、被拦截，或因布朗运动碰: The filter layer of a mask is not a sieve. Fine particles that pass between fibers may collide with and be intercepted due to inertia, or encounter fibers due to Brownian motion ([[p:diffusion|Diffusion & membranes]]); electrostatic charges on the fibers also attract particles ([[p:charge|Electric charge & field]]). The most difficult particles to filter are those approximately 0.3 micrometers in size.
核心是带静电的熔喷无纺布，在不增加呼吸阻力的情况下提高过滤效率。\"95\"指对: The core is electrostatically charged melt-blown nonwoven fabric, which improves filtration efficiency without increasing breathing resistance. "95" refers to intercepting at least 95% of the hardest-to-filter particles; it must fit closely to the face, or leakage will significantly reduce effectiveness.
1995 年美国国家职业安全卫生研究所发布这一认证标准；华裔科学家曹培生（Pet: In 1995, the U.S. National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health issued this certification standard; Chinese scientist Peter Tsai improved electrostatic filter materials.
它从工厂防尘用品变成了疫情中医护人员的关键防护装备。: It has transformed from factory dust protection equipment into essential protective gear for medical personnel during epidemics.
沙利度胺致畸事件后，各国要求新药上市前证明安全有效。: After the thalidomide teratogenicity incident, countries required that new drugs prove safety and efficacy before market approval.
药是否安全有效，不能由厂商说了算，也不能只看个别病例，必须在上市前用严格的试验证: Whether a drug is safe and effective cannot be decided by manufacturers alone, nor can it rely solely on individual cases; it must be proven through rigorous trials before market approval ([[p:probability|Probability & statistical inference]]), with continued monitoring of rare adverse effects after launch.
新药先做动物实验，再做三期人体临床试验（见 [[clinical-trial]]: New drugs first undergo animal experiments, then phase III human clinical trials (see [[clinical-trial]]); regulatory agencies review data before approving market entry. After launch, adverse reactions are collected; if necessary, the instruction sheet is modified or the drug is withdrawn from the market.
20 世纪 50 年代末，孕妇服用镇静剂沙利度胺导致上万名婴儿肢体残缺。美国药监: In the late 1950s, pregnant women taking the sedative thalidomide caused thousands of infants to be born with limb deformities. Frances Kelsey, an FDA reviewer, refused approval due to insufficient data. In 1962, U.S. legislation required proof of efficacy before new drug market entry.
现代药品审批制度由此建立，新药更安全，研发也更慢、更贵。: The modern drug approval system was thus established; new drugs are safer, but research and development become slower and more expensive.
索尔克灭活疫苗（1955）和萨宾口服疫苗（1960 年代初）让小儿麻痹症病例减少: The Salk inactivated vaccine (1955) and the Sabin oral vaccine (early 1960s) reduced polio cases by more than 99%, with wild virus now spreading only in a few countries.
脊灰病毒只感染人，少数感染者会因脊髓运动神经受损而瘫痪。疫苗诱导抗体，阻断感染和: Poliovirus infects only humans, and a minority of infected individuals become paralyzed due to damage to spinal motor nerves. Vaccines induce antibodies that block infection and transmission ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]], [[p:germ|Germ theory]]).
**灭活疫苗**（注射）安全；**口服减毒活疫苗**便宜，还能在肠道阻断传播，但: **Inactivated vaccines** (injection) are safe; **oral live-attenuated vaccines** are cheap and can block transmission in the gut, but in rare cases the virus may mutate to regain virulence. Therefore, countries have gradually switched to inactivated vaccines in later eradication efforts.
1955 年索尔克（Jonas Salk）的灭活疫苗获准使用；1961 年起萨宾: Jonas Salk's inactivated vaccine was approved for use in 1955; Albert Sabin's oral vaccine began deployment starting in 1961. Virus culture relies on [[cell-culture]].
1988 年全球根除计划启动时每年约 35 万儿童瘫痪，如今病例减少 99% 以: When the global eradication program launched in 1988, about 350,000 children were paralyzed annually; now cases have decreased by more than 99%, with wild virus circulating only in Pakistan and Afghanistan.
发现人体需要微量\"维生素\"后，往食盐里加碘、面粉里加铁和叶酸等，以极低成本预: After discovering that humans require trace "vitamins," iodine was added to salt, iron and folic acid to flour, etc., preventing large-scale nutritional deficiencies at extremely low costs.
人体需要一些自己不能合成的微量物质：缺维生素 C 得坏血病，缺碘造成甲状腺肿和儿: Humans need some trace substances they cannot synthesize themselves: lack of vitamin C causes scurvy; lack of iodine leads to goiter and impaired child intelligence; lack of folic acid during pregnancy increases the risk of neural tube defects in the fetus ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]).
**食品强化**把营养素加进人人都吃的食物：食盐加碘，面粉加铁和叶酸，牛奶加维生: **Food fortification** adds nutrients to foods consumed by everyone: iodine added to salt, iron and folic acid added to flour, vitamin D added to milk. Per capita cost is almost negligible, yet it can cover the entire population.
1912 年冯克（Casimir Funk）提出\"维生素\"概念；1924 年: Casimir Funk proposed the concept of "vitamins" in 1912; the US began selling iodized salt in 1924, after which many countries implemented universal iodization.
加碘盐大幅减少了可预防的智力损害，叶酸强化显著降低了神经管缺陷。: Iodized salt significantly reduced preventable intellectual impairment; folic acid fortification substantially lowered neural tube defects.
急救电话、救护车和院前急救组成的\"移动急诊室\"，核心是抢在黄金时间内开始救治: Emergency call centers, ambulances, and pre-hospital emergency care form a "mobile emergency room," with the core goal of initiating treatment within the golden time window.
心脏骤停、严重创伤和中风的损伤每分钟都在加重。把救治从医院\"搬\"到现场和路上: Damage from cardiac arrest, severe trauma, and stroke worsens every minute. Moving treatment from the hospital to the scene and road allows intervention within the critical time window, significantly improving survival rates ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]).
急救体系包括统一的急救电话、调度中心、带设备的救护车和医院急诊的衔接。调度员可在: The emergency care system includes a unified emergency call number, dispatch centers, ambulances equipped with devices, and coordination with hospital emergency departments. Dispatchers can guide bystanders in cardiopulmonary resuscitation over the phone (see [[cpr]]), and ECG data is transmitted to the hospital while the ambulance is en route.
1965 年北爱尔兰医生潘特里奇（Frank Pantridge）把便携除颤器装: In 1965, North Irish doctor Frank Pantridge installed portable defibrillators on ambulances, establishing mobile coronary care units; in 1968, the US opened the 911 hotline, and China's emergency number is 120.
院前急救网络的覆盖程度，直接关系到急症患者的存活机会。: The coverage level of the pre-hospital emergency network directly relates to the survival chances of acute patients.
让病人在手术中失去痛觉和意识，外科从\"比速度\"变成可以精细操作。: Making patients lose pain sensation and consciousness during surgery transformed surgery from "competing for speed" to allowing fine manipulation.
痛觉要经过神经传到大脑才会被感受到。麻醉药与神经细胞膜上特定的受体或离子通道结合: Pain must be transmitted via nerves to the brain before being felt. Anesthetics bind to specific receptors or ion channels on nerve cell membranes ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]), temporarily blocking signals: **local anesthesia** causes a region of nerves to go "offline," while **general anesthesia** puts the brain into a reversible unconscious state.
现代全麻通常组合用药：静脉药物让人入睡，吸入麻醉气体维持，肌肉松弛剂让手术区放松: Modern general anesthesia typically uses combination drugs: intravenous drugs induce sleep, inhaled anesthetic gases maintain it, muscle relaxants relax the surgical area, and opioid drugs provide analgesia. Because patients cannot breathe voluntarily after muscle relaxation, intubation and connection to a ventilator are required; anesthesiologists monitor heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, and exhaled carbon dioxide throughout the procedure, adjusting doses as needed.
1846 年 10 月 16 日，美国牙医莫顿（William Morton）在: On October 16, 1846, US dentist William Morton publicly demonstrated ether anesthesia at Massachusetts General Hospital, with patients undergoing pain-free removal of neck tumors. The following year, Simpson in Britain began using chloroform. Cocaine was used as a local anesthetic in 1884.
麻醉之前，外科医生以快为荣，截肢要在一两分钟内完成；麻醉之后，手术可以从容精细地: Before anesthesia, surgeons took pride in speed, needing to ampute within one or two minutes; after anesthesia, surgery could be performed calmly and finely for hours, making thoracotomy and craniotomy possible (see [[surgery-modern]]).
李斯特用石炭酸消毒手术器械和伤口，术后感染死亡率大幅下降。: Lister used carbolic acid to disinfect surgical instruments and wounds, causing a sharp decline in postoperative infection mortality.
手术后伤口化脓、败血症致死，罪魁是从手、器械和空气进入伤口的细菌（[[p:ger: Postoperative wound pus and sepsis leading to death were caused primarily by bacteria entering the wound from hands, instruments, and air ([[p:germ|Germ theory]]). **Antibiotics** kill bacteria that have already entered the wound, while **asepsis** prevents bacteria from entering in the first place.
早期的抗菌术用石炭酸喷洒伤口、器械和手术区域。后来发展为无菌术：器械高压灭菌（见: Early antiseptic methods used carbolic acid sprayed on wounds, instruments, and surgical areas. This later developed into asepsis: instruments undergo high-pressure sterilization (see [[autoclave-sterilization]]); doctors wash hands, wear sterile gowns, gloves, and masks; sterile drapes cover the surgical area; sterile zones are demarcated; personnel and items flow according to rules.
1847 年匈牙利医生塞麦尔维斯（Ignaz Semmelweis）要求医生用漂: In 1847, Hungarian doctor Ignaz Semmelweis required doctors to wash hands with lime water, causing a sharp decline in puerperal fever mortality, but it was not accepted at the time. In 1867, British surgeon Joseph Lister published methods for disinfection with carbolic acid; his ward showed a marked reduction in mortality after amputation.
手术从\"成功了也可能死于感染\"变成相对安全的治疗手段。洗手至今仍是医院预防感: Surgery has transformed from a treatment where success was often followed by death due to infection into a relatively safe therapeutic option. Hand washing remains one of the most effective measures for hospitals to prevent infections.
麻醉、无菌、输血和抗生素四大支柱让开胸、开颅等大手术成为可能。: Anesthesia, asepsis, blood transfusion, and antibiotics serve as the four pillars that made major surgeries such as thoracotomy and craniotomy possible.
大手术要过四道关：疼痛、感染、失血、术后感染。**麻醉**解决疼痛，**无菌术*: Major surgeries must pass through four hurdles: pain, infection, blood loss, and postoperative infection. **Anesthesia** addresses pain, **asepsis** prevents infection, **blood transfusion** compensates for blood loss, and **antibiotics** treat residual infections; additionally, intensive care after surgery allows procedures like thoracotomy, craniotomy, and organ transplantation to become routine ([[p:germ|Germ theory]]).
一台现代手术是团队作业：外科医生、麻醉医生、护士和技师分工协作，影像检查提前规划: A modern operation is a team effort: surgeons, anesthesiologists, nurses, and technicians collaborate with specialized roles. Imaging examinations are planned in advance, intraoperative monitors alert at any moment, and patients spend the most dangerous phase in intensive care units after surgery. Operating rooms also use standardized verification processes to prevent low-level errors such as "operating on the wrong site" or "leaving gauze behind".
19 世纪中后期，麻醉和无菌术先后出现；20 世纪前半叶输血和抗生素普及。200: In the mid-to-late 19th century, anesthesia and asepsis emerged sequentially; in the first half of the 20th century, blood transfusion and antibiotics became widespread. In 2008, the World Health Organization launched the "Surgical Safety Checklist," resulting in a significant decline in postoperative mortality and complications at pilot hospitals.
外科从\"最后的手段\"变成治疗创伤、肿瘤、心脏病等的主力。今天的方向是创伤更小: Surgery has evolved from a "last resort" to the primary force for treating trauma, tumors, heart disease, and other conditions. Today's direction is toward smaller incisions (see [[minimally-invasive-surgery]]) and greater precision (see [[surgical-robot]]).
带空心针的注射器让药物可以直接打入体内，是疫苗大规模接种的工具。: Needleless syringes allow drugs to be injected directly into the body, serving as tools for large-scale vaccination.
注射器活塞后拉形成低压，液体被大气压\"压\"进针筒；前推则产生高压，把药液从空: Pulling back the plunger of a syringe creates low pressure, causing liquid to be "pushed" into the barrel by atmospheric pressure; pushing forward generates high pressure, forcing the medication out through the hollow needle ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]). Hollow needles can penetrate skin, delivering drugs directly into subcutaneous tissue, muscle, or blood vessels.
一次性塑料注射器用完即弃；\"自毁式\"注射器推到底后活塞锁死，无法重复使用。: Disposable plastic syringes are discarded after use; "self-destructing" syringes lock the plunger in place once fully depressed, preventing reuse.
1853 年苏格兰医生伍德（Alexander Wood）和法国医生普拉瓦兹（C: In 1853, Scottish doctor Alexander Wood and French doctor Charles Pravaz independently invented hollow-needle subcutaneous injectors. Starting in the 1950s, disposable plastic syringes gradually became widespread.
注射让胰岛素、疫苗和许多药物得以高效给药（见 [[insulin]]）；重复使用: Injection enables efficient administration of insulin, vaccines, and many other drugs (see [[insulin]]); the lesson learned from repeated needle use spreading hepatitis drove the widespread adoption of disposable syringes.
兰德施泰纳发现 ABO 血型，配型输血才变得安全；后来又建立了血库。: Landsteiner discovered ABO blood types, making matched blood transfusion safe; later, blood banks were established.
红细胞表面有不同的\"标签\"分子（抗原），血浆里有针对异型标签的抗体。输错血，: Red blood cells have different "label" molecules (antigens) on their surfaces, while plasma contains antibodies targeting foreign labels. If the wrong blood is transfused, antibodies bind to and destroy foreign red blood cells, causing a fatal reaction ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]). Blood transfusion is only safe when matched by blood type.
最重要的是 ABO 和 Rh 血型，输血前还要交叉配血。抗凝剂加冷藏让血液能储存: The most critical factors are ABO and Rh blood types; cross-matching is required before transfusion. Anticoagulants and refrigeration allow blood to be stored for several weeks, and it can be separated into red blood cells, plasma, and platelets as needed.
1901 年奥地利医生兰德施泰纳（Karl Landsteiner）发现 ABO: In 1901, Austrian doctor Karl Landsteiner discovered ABO blood types; he received the Nobel Prize in 1930. In 1940, he participated in discovering Rh blood types. The first hospital blood bank was established in Chicago, USA, in 1937.
输血是大手术、创伤急救、分娩大出血和癌症治疗的基础，也让献血成为一项社会制度。: Blood transfusion is foundational for major surgeries, trauma emergencies, childbirth with severe hemorrhage, and cancer treatment, also making blood donation a social institution.
手术中暂时代替心脏和肺工作，让心脏直视手术成为可能。: During surgery, it temporarily replaces the function of the heart and lungs, making open-heart surgery possible.
心脏直视手术需要让心脏停跳、排空血液，但大脑几分钟缺氧就会受损。心肺机在体外接管: Open-heart surgery requires stopping the heart and emptying the blood, but brain damage occurs within minutes of oxygen deprivation. Cardiopulmonary machines take over the "pump" function of the heart and the "gas exchange" function of the lungs ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]) outside the body.
静脉血经管道引出，流过氧合器，排出二氧化碳、吸收氧气，再由血泵打回动脉。同时控制: Venous blood is drawn out through a tube, flows through an oxygenator where carbon dioxide is expelled and oxygen is absorbed, then pumped back into the artery by a blood pump. Blood temperature is controlled simultaneously, and anticoagulants are used to prevent clotting within the tubes.
1953 年 5 月，美国外科医生吉本（John Gibbon）用自己研制了近二: In May 1953, American surgeon John Gibbon successfully repaired a heart defect in an 18-year-old girl using a cardiopulmonary machine he had spent nearly two decades developing himself.
修补先天性心脏病、换瓣膜、冠状动脉搭桥等手术由此成为可能。它的原理后来发展出体外: Surgeries such as repairing congenital heart defects, replacing valves, and coronary artery bypass grafting have become possible. Its principles later evolved into extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), used to rescue critically ill patients with heart-lung failure.
让血液流过半透膜，把肾脏无法排出的废物和多余水分滤掉。: Allowing blood to flow through a semi-permeable membrane filters out waste products that the kidneys cannot excrete and excess water.
肾脏衰竭后，尿素等废物和多余的水分、盐分积在体内。让血液和透析液隔着一层半透膜流: After kidney failure, waste products such as urea and excess fluids and salts accumulate in the body. Blood flows on one side of a semi-permeable membrane while dialysate flows on the other; small-molecule wastes diffuse from the high-concentration blood into the dialysate, while blood cells and proteins remain ([[p:diffusion|Diffusion & membranes]]).
**血液透析**把血引出体外，流过由上万根中空纤维膜组成的透析器，通常每周 3: **Blood dialysis** draws blood out of the body, passes it through a dialyzer composed of tens of thousands of hollow fiber membranes, typically three times a week for about four hours each time; **peritoneal dialysis** uses the patient's peritoneum as the semi-permeable membrane and can be performed at home.
1943 年荷兰医生科尔夫（Willem Kolff）在二战占领下用香肠肠衣和转: In 1943, under the occupation of Nazi Germany, Dutch physician Willem Kolff created the first artificial kidney using sausage casings and a rotating drum. In 1945, he successfully saved his first patient. By 1960, long-term vascular access became available, making chronic dialysis a reality.
肾衰竭从绝症变成可长期控制的疾病，也让许多病人能等到肾移植（见 [[organ-: The transformation of renal failure from an incurable disease to one that can be managed for life has allowed many patients to wait for organ transplantation (see [[organ-transplant]]).
起搏器用电脉冲维持心跳节律，除颤器用强电击让乱颤的心脏恢复正常。: Pacemakers maintain the heart's rhythm using electrical pulses, while defibrillators use strong electric shocks to restore normal function in a chaotic heart.
心脏有自己的\"电路\"：窦房结定时放电，电信号沿传导系统扩散，心肌依次收缩（[: The heart has its own "circuit": the sinoatrial node discharges periodically, and electrical signals spread through the conduction system, causing the myocardium to contract sequentially ([[p:charge|Electric charge & field]]). If this circuit is broken, the heart rate may become too slow or stop entirely; if it becomes chaotic, it results in fatal ventricular fibrillation.
**起搏器**埋在锁骨下，导线伸入心脏，监测到心跳过慢才发出电脉冲（[[p:ho: **Pacemakers** are implanted under the clavicle with leads extending into the heart, delivering an electrical pulse only when the heart rate is too slow ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]). Batteries typically last about ten years. **Defibrillators** use strong electric shocks to reset all myocardial cells simultaneously; implantable defibrillators can automatically detect ventricular fibrillation and deliver a shock.
1958 年瑞典医生森宁（Åke Senning）和工程师埃尔姆奎斯特（Rune: In 1958, Swedish physician Åke Senning and engineer Rune Elmqvist implanted the first pacemaker in a patient, who lived for over forty years afterward. In 1980, the first implantable defibrillator was used in clinical practice.
起搏器是最早的\"电子植入物\"，为人工耳蜗、脑机接口铺了路。: Pacemakers were the earliest "electronic implants," paving the way for cochlear implants and brain-computer interfaces.
把健康器官移植给患者，配合抗排斥药物，肾、肝、心、肺都可移植。: Healthy organs can be transplanted into patients when combined with anti-rejection drugs; kidneys, livers, hearts, and lungs are all viable for transplantation.
移植的难点不在手术缝合，而在免疫系统：身体会把别人的器官当作入侵者攻击。细胞表面: The challenge of transplantation lies not in surgical suturing but in the immune system: the body attacks foreign organs as invaders. Human leukocyte antigens (HLA) on cell surfaces act like "ID cards"; the more closely they match, the lighter the rejection response. This is further managed by immunosuppressants to suppress the attack ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]).
器官来自去世或活体捐献者，离体后要低温保存、快速运输，按配型、病情和等待时间分配: Organs come from deceased or living donors. After removal, they must be preserved at low temperatures and transported rapidly, then allocated based on HLA matching, patient condition, and waiting time. Post-transplant patients typically require lifelong anti-rejection medication (see [[immunosuppression]]).
1954 年美国医生默里（Joseph Murray）在一对同卵双胞胎之间完成第: In 1954, American physician Joseph Murray performed the first successful kidney transplant between identical twins; because their genetics were identical, there was no rejection, earning him the Nobel Prize in 1990. In 1967, Christiaan Barnard of South Africa completed the first human heart transplant. After cyclosporine was approved in 1983, long-term survival rates for transplants increased significantly.
肾、肝、心、肺、胰腺都已能移植，挽救了大量终末期病人。最大的瓶颈是器官短缺，这也: Kidneys, livers, hearts, lungs, and pancreas are now all capable of transplantation, saving numerous patients with end-stage organ failure. The greatest bottleneck remains organ scarcity, which has driven research into xenotransplantation and artificial organs (see [[artificial-heart]]).
环孢素等药物抑制免疫系统攻击移植器官，让移植的长期存活率大幅提升。: Drugs such as cyclosporin suppress the immune system's attack on transplanted organs, significantly improving long-term survival rates.
免疫排斥的主力是 T 细胞。免疫抑制剂阻断 T 细胞被激活所需的信号，让它们\": The main force behind immune rejection is T cells. Immunosuppressants block the signals required for T cell activation, allowing them to "recognize" foreign organs without acting ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]).
常用钙调磷酸酶抑制剂（环孢素、他克莫司）、抗增殖药和激素联合使用，既压住排斥，又: Commonly used calcium channel inhibitors (cyclosporin, tacrolimus), antiproliferative drugs, and hormones are used in combination to suppress rejection while minimizing toxicity. The trade-off is reduced resistance to infection and certain cancers, requiring regular monitoring of drug blood concentrations.
环孢素是 1970 年代初瑞士山德士公司从一种真菌中发现的，1983 年在美国获: Cyclosporin was discovered in the early 1970s by Swiss Sandoz Company from a fungus; it was approved for use in organ transplantation in the United States in 1983.
它把肾、肝、心移植从高风险的实验变成了常规治疗，同类药物也用于治疗某些自身免疫病: It transformed kidney, liver, and heart transplants from high-risk experiments into routine treatments. Similar drugs are also used to treat certain autoimmune diseases.
用金属、塑料或陶瓷替换磨损的髋、膝关节，让患者重新行走。: Worn-out hip or knee joints are replaced with metal, plastic, or ceramic prostheses, allowing patients to walk again.
关节软骨磨损后，骨头直接摩擦，疼痛难忍。人工关节用光滑耐磨的金属、陶瓷和高分子材: After cartilage wears down, bones rub directly against each other, causing severe pain. Artificial joints replace worn joint surfaces with smooth, wear-resistant metals, ceramics, and polymers; the material's strength, coefficient of friction, and method of bone integration determine how long it can be used ([[p:stress|Stress, strain & strength]]).
髋关节置换把带球头的金属柄插入股骨，在骨盆一侧装聚乙烯或陶瓷内衬的髋臼杯，用骨水: Hip replacement involves inserting a metal stem with a ball head into the femur, while a cup made of polyethylene or ceramic with a ball insert is installed in the acetabulum on one side of the pelvis. These are fixed with bone cement or allowed to grow into porous surfaces. Modern artificial joints typically last 15–20 years or more.
1962 年英国外科医生查恩利（John Charnley）用金属股骨柄、聚乙烯: In 1962, British surgeon John Charnley completed a low-friction hip replacement using a metal femoral stem, polyethylene acetabulum, and bone cement, laying the foundation for modern joint replacement surgery.
髋、膝关节置换已成为最常见、效果最好的手术之一，让大量关节炎患者重新行走。: Hip and knee replacements have become among the most common and effective surgeries, enabling numerous arthritis patients to walk again.
通过几个小孔插入内窥镜和器械完成手术，创伤小、恢复快。: Surgery is completed by inserting endoscopes and instruments through several small incisions, resulting in minimal trauma and rapid recovery.
手术创伤主要来自切口而不是病灶本身。把大切口换成几个 0.5–1 厘米的小孔，伸: Surgical trauma primarily comes from the incision rather than the lesion itself. Replacing large incisions with several 0.5–1 cm small holes allows cameras and slender instruments to be inserted; operations are then performed on a screen, greatly reducing pain, bleeding, and infection ([[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]]).
腹腔镜手术先向腹腔充入二氧化碳撑出空间，再从小孔插入镜头和器械。医生看着屏幕操作: Laparoscopic surgery begins by inflating the abdominal cavity with carbon dioxide to create space, then inserting a camera and instruments through small incisions. The surgeon operates while viewing the screen on a monitor; this requires specialized training. The same approach is also used for arthroscopy and endovascular intervention (see [[angioplasty-stent]]).
1985 年德国医生米厄（Erich Mühe）完成第一例腹腔镜胆囊切除；198: In 1985, German doctor Erich Mühe completed the first laparoscopic cholecystectomy; in 1987, French doctor Philippe Mouret performed a similar surgery using video-assisted laparoscopy. Following this, the technique spread rapidly.
胆囊、阑尾、疝气等许多手术的住院时间从一两周缩短到一两天。: Hospitalization time for many surgeries such as cholecystectomy, appendectomy, and hernia repair has been shortened from one to two weeks down to one or two days.
医生操纵机械臂完成精细手术，可过滤手抖、放大视野。: Doctors manipulate robotic arms to perform delicate surgeries; this filters hand tremors and magnifies the field of view.
机器人并不自己做手术，而是放大医生的手：把医生手柄的动作按比例缩小、过滤掉手的颤: Robots do not perform surgery themselves; instead, they amplify the surgeon's hands: they scale down the surgeon's handle movements proportionally, filter out hand tremors, and transmit them to fine instruments inside the body ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
医生坐在控制台前，看着三维高清画面操作手柄；机械臂末端的器械有\"手腕\"，能在: The surgeon sits at a console, operating handles while viewing three-dimensional high-definition images; the instruments at the end of the robotic arms have 'wrist' capabilities, allowing flexible rotation within the body and offering greater dexterity than conventional laparoscopic instruments. The disadvantages are that equipment and consumables are expensive, and the results for most surgeries are comparable to those achieved by skilled laparoscopic surgeons.
2000 年美国直觉外科公司的达芬奇手术系统获美国药监局批准用于普通腹腔镜手术。: In 2000, Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci surgical system in the United States received FDA approval for routine laparoscopic surgery. In 2001, doctors remotely completed a cholecystectomy in Strasbourg, France, from New York.
手术机器人在前列腺癌、妇科和泌尿外科手术中广泛使用，5G 远程手术也在试验中。: Surgical robots are widely used in prostate cancer, gynecological, and urological surgeries; remote surgery using 5G is also under trial.
把声音转成电信号直接刺激听神经，让重度耳聋者重获听觉。: Converting sound into electrical signals directly stimulates the auditory nerve, restoring hearing for those with severe deafness.
内耳的耳蜗像一架\"琴键\"，不同位置的毛细胞对应不同音高。毛细胞坏死后，人就听: The cochlea in the inner ear functions like a 'piano keyboard,' where hair cells at different positions correspond to different pitches. When hair cells die, people become deaf, but the auditory nerve often remains intact. The cochlear implant decomposes sound into different frequencies and directly stimulates nerves at corresponding positions within the cochlea using electrical current ([[p:sampling|Sampling & digitization]]).
耳后的处理器用麦克风收音，把声音分成十几到二十多个频段，通过无线方式传给皮下的接: The processor behind the ear uses a microphone to capture sound, divides it into ten to twenty frequency bands, transmits it wirelessly to an under-skin receiver, and then delivers it to an electrode array implanted in the cochlea. After implantation, device tuning and auditory rehabilitation training are required; the brain must learn to understand this new kind of 'sound'.
1978 年澳大利亚的克拉克（Graeme Clark）为病人植入了多通道人工耳: In 1978, Graeme Clark in Australia implanted a multi-channel cochlear implant for a patient.
全球已植入超过一百万个人工耳蜗；先天耳聋的儿童若早期植入，多数能学会说话、进入普: Over one million cochlear implants have been performed globally; children born with deafness who receive early implantation can usually learn to speak and enter regular schools.
读取肌肉电信号控制的电动假肢，可实现抓握等精细动作。: Reading muscle electrical signals controls electric prosthetic limbs, enabling fine movements such as grasping.
截肢后，残肢的肌肉仍能收缩，并产生微弱的肌电信号。电极读取这些信号，就能判断使用: After amputation, muscles in the residual limb can still contract and produce weak myoelectric signals. Electrodes read these signals to determine what action the user 'wants' to perform, then drive motors to execute it ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
肌电假手用残肢皮肤上的电极采集信号，算法识别出张开、握拳、转腕等意图。更先进的做: Myoelectric prosthetic hands use electrodes on the skin of the residual limb to collect signals; algorithms identify intentions such as opening, making a fist, or rotating the wrist. More advanced approaches involve transferring nerves that originally control the arm to chest muscles to obtain more control signals; some prosthetics also install sensors at fingertips to transmit tactile feedback back to nerves via electrical stimulation.
20 世纪 60 年代苏联和欧洲出现了早期的肌电假手；21 世纪以来，多关节仿生: Myoelectric prosthetic hands appeared in the Soviet Union and Europe in the 1960s; since the 21st century, multi-joint bionic hands and prosthetics with sensory feedback have emerged successively.
截肢者能完成拿杯子、系鞋带等精细动作；成本和训练门槛仍是普及的难题。: Amputees can perform fine movements such as holding a cup or tying shoelaces; cost and training thresholds remain barriers to widespread adoption.
读取大脑神经信号直接控制电脑或机械，帮助瘫痪患者打字和操控设备。: Reading brain neural signals directly controls computers or machines, helping paralyzed patients type and operate equipment.
想动手时，大脑运动皮层中的神经元会按特定模式放电，即使瘫痪的手已经动不了。记录这: When intending to move the hand, neurons in the motor cortex of the brain discharge in specific patterns, even if the paralyzed hand cannot move. Recording these electrical signals and using algorithms to 'translate' them into intentions allows control of computers, robotic arms, or synthetic speech to bypass damaged spinal cords or nerves ([[p:sampling|Sampling & digitization]], [[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
**侵入式**把微电极阵列植入大脑皮层，信号最清晰，但需开颅；**半侵入式**把: **Invasive** methods implant microelectrode arrays into the cerebral cortex; signals are clearest but require craniotomy. **Semi-invasive** methods place electrodes under the skull or within blood vessels. **Non-invasive** methods use scalp electroencephalography (see [[eeg]]); they are safe but yield blurry signals. Decoding algorithms and users adapt to each other during use.
2004 年美国的 BrainGate 团队为一名四肢瘫痪者植入电极阵列，他能用: In 2004, the BrainGate team in the United States implanted an electrode array for a patient with quadriplegia, enabling them to move a computer cursor with their mind. In 2023, researchers enabled speech at dozens of words per minute for aphasic patients via brain-computer interfaces. Starting in 2024, companies such as Neuralink have launched human trials; multiple teams in China have also entered clinical research.
脑机接口让瘫痪和失语患者重新获得沟通和控制能力。它也带来神经数据隐私和植入物长期: Brain-computer interfaces restore communication and control capabilities for paralyzed and aphasic patients. They also raise ethical issues regarding neural data privacy and long-term safety of implants.
从\"铁肺\"到正压呼吸机，替病人完成呼吸，是重症监护的核心设备。: Transitioning from the 'iron lung' to positive-pressure ventilators, replacing a patient's breathing function is a core piece of equipment in intensive care.
呼吸靠胸腔扩张形成负压，把空气\"吸\"进肺里。呼吸机替代这个过程：要么在胸外制: Breathing relies on the expansion of the thoracic cavity to create negative pressure, which "sucks" air into the lungs. Ventilators replace this process: either by creating negative pressure outside the chest, or by directly "blowing" gas into the lungs with positive pressure ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]).
早期\"铁肺\"把病人身体装进密封箱周期性抽气。现代呼吸机通过插管或面罩送气，控: Early "iron lungs" placed the patient's body inside a sealed box and cycled air out. Modern ventilators deliver gas via intubation or a face mask, controlling tidal volume, pressure, and oxygen concentration, while coordinating with the patient's own breathing ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]).
1928 年美国的德林克（Philip Drinker）发明铁肺。1952 年丹: In 1928, Philip Drinker in the United States invented the iron lung. In 1952, during an epidemic of poliomyelitis in Copenhagen, Denmark, anesthetist Bjørn Ibsen organized medical students to work in shifts manually squeezing airbags to provide positive pressure ventilation for patients; mortality rates dropped significantly and this is regarded as the starting point of intensive care medicine.
呼吸机是重症监护室的核心设备，在新冠疫情中一度成为全球最紧缺的医疗物资。: Ventilators are core equipment in intensive care units and once became the most scarce medical supply globally during the COVID-19 pandemic.
把声音放大后送入耳道，晶体管让它小到可以藏在耳后。: Amplifying sound into the ear canal, transistors make it small enough to hide behind the ear.
多数听力下降是因为内耳毛细胞受损，对声音不够敏感。助听器把声音放大后送进耳道，让: Most hearing loss is caused by damage to hair cells in the inner ear, making them less sensitive to sound. Hearing aids amplify sound and deliver it into the ear canal, allowing residual hearing to perceive it ([[p:sampling|Sampling & digitization]]).
现代数字助听器把声音数字化，按频段分别放大（通常高频损失更多），压缩过响的声音，: Modern digital hearing aids digitize sound, amplify different frequency bands separately (usually high frequencies are lost more), compress overly loud sounds, suppress noise and whistling, and can use multiple microphones to focus on the direction of the speaker.
1952 年美国推出第一款使用晶体管的助听器，体积和耗电大幅减小；20 世纪 9: In 1952, the United States launched the first hearing aid using transistors, with volume and power consumption significantly reduced; in the 1990s, fully digital hearing aids appeared.
助听器小到可以藏在耳后或耳道里。研究提示，中年听力下降与日后认知衰退风险相关，改: Hearing aids are small enough to be hidden behind or inside the ear canal. Research suggests that age-related hearing loss is associated with an increased risk of cognitive decline later in life, so improving hearing is also considered part of healthy aging.
用导管把球囊送到堵塞的冠状动脉撑开，再放入支架，许多心梗不再需要开胸。: Using a catheter to inflate a balloon into a blocked coronary artery to dilate it, then placing a stent; many myocardial infarctions no longer require open-chest surgery.
心肌梗死多是冠状动脉被斑块和血栓堵塞，心肌缺血坏死。与其开胸搭桥，不如从血管里面: Myocardial infarction is mostly caused by blockage of the coronary artery by plaques and thrombi, leading to ischemic necrosis of the myocardium. Rather than open-chest bypass surgery, it is better to dilate the blocked area from within the vessel ([[p:stress|Stress, strain & strength]]).
医生从手腕或大腿的动脉插入细导管，在 X 光透视下送到堵塞处，充起导管头上的球囊: Doctors insert a thin catheter into an artery in the wrist or thigh, deliver it to the blockage under X-ray fluoroscopy, inflate the balloon at the head of the catheter to dilate the vessel, then leave a mesh metal stent to prevent recoil. **Drug-eluting stents** slowly release medication on their surface to reduce restenosis.
1977 年德国医生格吕恩齐格（Andreas Grüntzig）在瑞士苏黎世完: In 1977, German doctor Andreas Grüntzig completed the first coronary artery balloon angioplasty in Zurich, Switzerland. In the late 1980s, stents began being used clinically; by the early 21st century, drug-eluting stents were introduced.
急性心梗可以在发病后数小时内开通血管，死亡率显著下降；许多病人不必开胸，几天就能: Acute myocardial infarction can have its vessels opened within hours of onset, significantly reducing mortality; many patients do not need open-chest surgery and can be discharged after a few days.
用支架、细胞和生长因子培育人工组织，3D 生物打印尝试直接\"打印\"器官。: Using stents, cells, and growth factors to cultivate artificial tissue; 3D bioprinting attempts to directly "print" organs.
器官由细胞、支撑它们的\"脚手架\"（细胞外基质）和调控信号组成。如果提供合适的: Organs consist of cells, the "scaffolding" that supports them (extracellular matrix), and regulatory signals. If appropriate scaffolds, cells, and growth factors are provided, cells may self-organize into tissue ([[p:dogma|Central dogma]], [[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
在可降解支架上接种病人自己的细胞，培养后植入，支架降解后留下新生组织。3D 生物: Patient's own cells are seeded on degradable scaffolds; after culture and implantation, the scaffold degrades leaving newly formed tissue. 3D bioprinting uses cellular "bioinks" to layer-print tissue structures; the challenge is how to grow blood vessels to supply oxygen to thick tissue.
1993 年美国科学家兰格（Robert Langer）和瓦坎蒂（Joseph: In 1993, American scientists Robert Langer and Joseph Vacanti systematically proposed the concept of "tissue engineering." In 2006, researchers reported successful transplantation of an engineered bladder using tissue engineering for a patient.
人工皮肤、软骨等简单组织已用于临床；复杂的实体器官仍处在研究阶段。: Simple tissues such as artificial skin and cartilage have already been used clinically; complex solid organs remain in the research stage.
胸外按压让血液继续流向大脑，自动体外除颤器（AED）能自动判断心律并电击，旁观者: Chest compressions allow blood to continue flowing to the brain; automatic external defibrillators (AEDs) can automatically analyze heart rhythm and deliver an electric shock, saving lives if bystanders learn to use them.
心脏骤停后血液停止流动，大脑几分钟就开始不可逆地受损。用力按压胸骨，把心脏挤在胸: After cardiac arrest, blood flow stops; the brain begins irreversible damage within minutes. Forceful compression of the sternum, squeezing the heart between the sternum and spine, allows a small amount of blood to continue flowing to the brain ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]). Most arrests initially involve ventricular fibrillation, requiring defibrillation to restore normal heart rhythm ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]).
**心肺复苏**以持续、有力、快速的胸外按压为核心；**自动体外除颤器**（AE: **Cardiopulmonary resuscitation** centers on continuous, forceful, and rapid chest compressions; **automatic external defibrillators** (AEDs) automatically analyze heart rhythm and prompt an electric shock only when needed, allowing ordinary people to operate them by following voice prompts.
1960 年美国约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的考温霍文（William Kouwenho: In 1960, William Kouwenhoven and others at Johns Hopkins University in the United States published the method of closed-chest cardiac compression; modern cardiopulmonary resuscitation was thus established.
旁观者及时实施心肺复苏，能让心脏骤停者的存活机会成倍提高。许多城市因此在公共场所: Timely cardiopulmonary resuscitation by bystanders can multiply the survival chances for victims of cardiac arrest. Many cities therefore install AEDs in public places.
把健康的造血干细胞输入患者体内，重建血液和免疫系统，用于治疗白血病等血液病。: Healthy hematopoietic stem cells are infused into a patient's body to rebuild the blood and immune systems, treating conditions such as leukemia and other blood disorders.
血液中的各种细胞都由骨髓里的造血干细胞不断产生。白血病等血液病可以先用大剂量化疗: All various cells in the blood are continuously produced by hematopoietic stem cells residing in the bone marrow. Blood diseases such as leukemia can first be treated with high-dose chemotherapy or radiation therapy to clear the diseased hematopoietic system; healthy hematopoietic stem cells are then infused so they can 'settle' in the bone marrow, rebuilding the entire blood and immune system ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]).
干细胞来自病人自己或配型相合的供者，取自骨髓、外周血或脐带血。异体移植要求 HL: Stem cells may come from the patient themselves or from a donor with compatible HLA matching. They are harvested from bone marrow, peripheral blood, or umbilical cord blood. For allogeneic transplantation, HLA compatibility must be as close as possible; otherwise, the donor's immune cells may attack the patient (graft-versus-host disease).
20 世纪 50 年代末，美国的托马斯（E. Donnall Thomas）和法: In the late 1950s, Thomas (E. Donnall Thomas) from the United States and Mathé (Georges Mathé) from France carried out the earliest attempts at bone marrow transplantation; Thomas received the Nobel Prize in 1990.
许多白血病、淋巴瘤和再生障碍性贫血患者因此获得治愈机会。各国为此建立了志愿者骨髓: Many patients with leukemia, lymphoma, and aplastic anemia have thus gained a chance for cure. Countries have established volunteer bone marrow banks for this purpose.
用机械泵部分或完全代替心脏泵血，多数用作等待心脏移植的\"桥梁\"。: Mechanical pumps partially or completely replace the heart's blood-pumping function; most are used as 'bridges' while awaiting heart transplantation.
心脏本质上是一台泵。在等不到供体心脏时，可以用机械泵部分或全部替它推动血液（[[: The heart is essentially a pump. When a donor heart cannot be obtained in time, a mechanical pump can partially or fully take over the job of driving blood flow ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]).
**心室辅助装置**（VAD）只帮衰竭的心室泵血，现代产品多用连续旋转的叶轮，体: **Ventricular Assist Devices** (VADs) assist only the failing ventricle in pumping blood; modern products typically use continuously rotating impellers that are compact and durable, powered by external batteries connected via wires through the skin. **Total Artificial Hearts** remove the patient's own ventricles and fully replace them. Major risks include thrombosis, bleeding, and infection at wire connection sites.
1969 年美国医生库利（Denton Cooley）为病人植入第一颗全人工心脏: In 1969, American dentist Denton Cooley implanted the first total artificial heart in a patient as a bridge to transplantation. In 1982, the patient with the Jarvik-7 artificial heart survived for 112 days.
心室辅助装置已成为晚期心衰的常规治疗，既能作为等待移植的\"桥梁\"，也能让不适: Ventricular assist devices have become standard treatment for advanced heart failure; they can serve as 'bridges' while awaiting transplantation or enable patients unsuitable for transplantation to use them long-term.
折叠式钢管轮椅和电动轮椅让行动不便的人能自主出行，也推动了\"无障碍设计\"。: Folding steel-tube wheelchairs and electric wheelchairs allow people with mobility impairments to travel independently, promoting 'universal design'.
轮子把行走变成滚动，大大减少移动所需的力气；大后轮配手推圈，相当于一套省力的轮轴: Wheels turn walking into rolling, greatly reducing the force required for movement; large rear wheels paired with hand rims function as a set of force-saving wheel-and-axle levers ([[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]]).
**手动轮椅**用轻质钢管或铝合金、碳纤维车架，可以折叠；**电动轮椅**用电池: **Manual wheelchairs** use lightweight steel tubes or aluminum alloys and carbon fiber frames that can fold; **electric wheelchairs** are driven by batteries and motors, controlled via joysticks, and in severe cases, control can be achieved through the chin, head, or even breathing.
1933 年美国工程师埃弗勒斯特（Herbert Everest）和詹宁斯（Ha: In 1933, American engineers Herbert Everest and Harry Jennings designed a foldable steel-tube wheelchair, which subsequently became the standard design. Practical electric wheelchairs emerged in the 1950s.
轮椅让行动不便的人能独立出行，也推动了坡道、无障碍电梯和低地板公交等\"无障碍设: Wheelchairs enable people with mobility impairments to travel independently and have promoted 'universal design' including ramps, accessible elevators, and low-floor buses, making cities more friendly to all.
白内障手术用人工晶体替换浑浊的晶状体，准分子激光则重塑角膜来矫正近视。: Cataract surgery replaces cloudy lenses with artificial crystals; excimer laser reshapes the cornea to correct myopia.
眼睛像一台相机，角膜和晶状体负责把光线聚焦到视网膜上（[[p:optics|反射: The eye is like a camera; the cornea and lens focus light onto the retina ([[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]]). Clouding of the lens is cataract; when the cornea or eyeball shape is incorrect, causing the focal point not to land on the retina, this results in myopia, hyperopia, or astigmatism.
**白内障手术**把浑浊的晶状体乳化吸出，换上一片折叠的人工晶体。**激光矫视*: **Cataract surgery** emulsifies and removes the cloudy lens, replacing it with a foldable artificial crystal. **Laser refractive surgery** uses excimer laser to precisely cut the cornea, altering its curvature so that the focal point is repositioned onto the retina.
1949 年英国眼科医生里德利（Harold Ridley）植入了第一枚人工晶体: In 1949, British ophthalmologist Harold Ridley implanted the first artificial crystal; his inspiration came from plastic fragments in WWII pilots' cockpits not causing rejection. Excimer laser refractive surgery became widespread in the 1990s.
白内障曾是全球致盲的首要原因，如今手术只需十几分钟，是世界上最常做的手术之一。: Cataracts were once the leading cause of blindness worldwide; today, surgery takes only a few dozen minutes and is one of the most frequently performed surgeries globally.
局部麻醉、高速牙钻、氟化物和种植牙，让牙科从\"拔牙\"变成\"保牙\"和\"补: Local anesthesia, high-speed dental drills, fluorides, and dental implants have transformed dentistry from 'tooth extraction' to 'preserving teeth' and 'filling cavities'.
龋齿是口腔细菌分解糖产酸、溶解牙釉质的结果。氟离子能让牙釉质的晶体结构更耐酸（[: Caries result from oral bacteria decomposing sugar to produce acid, which dissolves enamel. Fluoride ions make the crystal structure of enamel more resistant to acid ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]), reducing cavities at the source.
现代牙科的几项关键技术：局部麻醉让治疗无痛；高速涡轮牙钻每分钟数十万转，快速精确: Key technologies in modern dentistry include: local anesthesia making treatment painless; high-speed turbine drills rotating tens of thousands of times per minute for rapid and precise removal of decay; resin materials for repairing teeth; fluoride toothpaste and fluoridated water to prevent cavities; and dental implants that place titanium roots into the jawbone, where bone tightly bonds with titanium ([[p:stress|Stress, strain & strength]]).
1945 年美国大急流城开始在饮用水中加氟。20 世纪 50 年代瑞典学者布伦马: In 1945, Great Falls, Indiana, began adding fluoride to drinking water. In the 1950s, Swedish scientist Per-Ingvar Brånemark discovered that bone could firmly bond with titanium, laying the foundation for dental implants.
牙科从\"疼了就拔\"变成\"预防和保留\"，许多国家儿童的龋齿率大幅下降。: Dentistry has shifted from 'extract when it hurts' to 'prevent and retain', with caries rates in children dropping significantly in many countries.
雷奈克用一卷纸筒听心肺声音，开创了用仪器辅助诊断的时代。: Rene Laennec used a rolled paper tube to listen to heart and lung sounds, inaugurating the era of diagnosis aided by instruments.
心脏瓣膜开合、血液流动和肺泡进出气，都会发出声音（[[p:wave|干涉、衍射与: The opening and closing of heart valves, blood flow, and air movement into and out of alveoli all produce sounds ([[p:wave|Interference, diffraction & resonance]]). Placing an ear against the chest can hear them, but they are vague; using a tube to concentrate and conduct the sound to the ears makes it much clearer.
胸件的膜片收集高频声音（如心脏杂音），钟形面收集低频声音，声波沿软管传到双耳。医: The diaphragm of the stethoscope collects high-frequency sounds (such as heart murmurs), while the bell surface collects low-frequency sounds. Sound waves travel along the hose to both ears. Doctors use this to assess heart rhythm, valve disorders, and whether there is fluid accumulation or wheezing in the lungs.
1816 年法国医生雷奈克（René Laennec）卷起一卷纸筒听诊一位年轻女: In 1816, French physician Rene Laennec rolled a paper tube to listen to a young female patient, subsequently inventing the wooden stethoscope; by the 1850s of the 19th century, double-eared stethoscopes appeared.
医生第一次能用仪器客观地\"探查\"体内，开创了物理诊断的时代。: For the first time, doctors could objectively 'investigate' inside the body using instruments, inaugurating the era of physical diagnosis.
1895 年 11 月 8 日，德国物理学家伦琴（Wilhelm Röntgen: On November 8, 1895, German physicist Wilhelm Röntgen, while conducting experiments with cathode rays, discovered that the screen glowed in the dark. Weeks later, he took a photograph of his wife's hand bones. He was awarded the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 and chose to forgo patenting the discovery. Early users were unaware of the dangers of radiation; many were injured or even died as a result.
医生第一次不开刀就能\"看进\"活人体内：骨折、肺结核、异物一目了然。X 射线还: For the first time, doctors could 'see inside' living bodies without surgery: fractures, pulmonary tuberculosis, and foreign bodies are all immediately visible. X-rays also led to Computed Tomography (see [[ct-scan]]), radiation therapy (see [[radiation-therapy]]), and X-ray crystallography for determining molecular structures (see [[x-ray-crystallography]]); the double helix of DNA was discovered using it.
X 光管中高速电子撞击钨靶产生 X 射线；骨骼吸收多、软组织吸收少，探测器上留下: High-speed electrons striking a tungsten target in an X-ray tube produce X-rays; bones absorb more, while soft tissues absorb less, leaving images with different brightness levels on the detector.
从多个角度拍 X 光，再用计算机重建出身体横截面的图像。: By taking X-rays from multiple angles and then using a computer to reconstruct cross-sectional images of the body.
普通 X 光片把三维的身体压成一张二维图，前后重叠的结构分不清。CT 从几百个角: Conventional X-rays compress the three-dimensional body into a single two-dimensional image, making it impossible to distinguish overlapping structures in front and back. CT scans take X-ray projections from hundreds of angles, then use mathematical methods to reverse-engineer how much radiation each small volume unit absorbed, reconstructing cross-sectional images of the body ([[p:emwave|Electromagnetic waves]], [[p:sampling|Sampling & digitization]]).
X 光管和探测器围绕病人快速旋转，病床同时移动，几秒内就能扫完胸腹部，重建成一层: The X-ray tube and detector rotate rapidly around the patient while the bed moves simultaneously; within seconds, the chest and abdomen can be scanned to reconstruct thin slices or three-dimensional images. Contrast agents make blood vessels and tumors clearer. The radiation dose for CT is far higher than for conventional X-rays, so necessity must be weighed.
1971 年英国 EMI 公司的工程师豪恩斯菲尔德（Godfrey Hounsf: In 1971, British engineer Godfrey Hounsfield of EMI Company used his designed CT scanner to scan the head of the first patient, discovering a brain tumor. He shared the 1979 Nobel Prize with Cormack (Allan), who proposed the mathematical method for reconstruction.
CT 让医生能快速发现脑出血、肿瘤、内脏损伤，成为急诊最重要的检查之一，也让\": CT allows doctors to quickly detect brain hemorrhages, tumors, and internal organ injuries, becoming one of the most important examinations in emergency medicine. It also made 'image-guided' precise surgery and radiation therapy possible.
X 光管和探测器绕身体旋转，从几百个角度测量投影，计算机算出每个小方格的吸收值，: The X-ray tube and detector rotate around the body, measuring projections from hundreds of angles; the computer calculates the absorption value for each small square, reconstructing a cross-sectional image.
用强磁场和射频脉冲让体内氢原子\"共鸣\"，根据回波重建软组织图像，没有电离辐射: Using strong magnetic fields and radiofrequency pulses to make hydrogen atoms inside the body 'resonate', soft tissue images are reconstructed based on echoes. There is no ionizing radiation involved.
人体内大部分是水，水中的氢原子核像小磁针，在强磁场里按磁场排列。用特定频率的无线: Most of the human body is water; the hydrogen nuclei in water act like tiny magnets, aligning according to the magnetic field under a strong magnetic field. A radio wave of a specific frequency 'pushes' them slightly off direction; they then return to their original position and emit weak wireless signals ([[p:levels|Quantized energy levels]], [[p:wave|Interference, diffraction & resonance]]). Different tissues have different return times, thus forming contrast.
核心是液氦冷却的超导线圈（见 [[superconductivity]]），磁场: The core is a superconducting coil cooled by liquid helium (see [[superconductivity]]); the magnetic field is commonly 1.5 or 3 Tesla, which is tens of thousands of times stronger than Earth's magnetic field. After superimposing gradient magnetic fields, hydrogen nuclei at different positions 'sing' at different frequencies, and the computer uses this for positioning. There is no ionizing radiation in the examination, but it takes a long time and generates high noise; people with certain metal implants inside the body cannot undergo it.
1973 年美国化学家劳特布尔（Paul Lauterbur）提出用梯度磁场成像: In 1973, American chemist Paul Lauterbur proposed imaging using gradient magnetic fields; British physicist Peter Mansfield developed rapid imaging methods. The two shared the 2003 Nobel Prize. In 1977, Raymond Damadian's team completed the first human scan.
磁共振看软组织尤其清楚：脑、脊髓、关节、心脏和肿瘤。功能磁共振还能显示大脑哪些区: Magnetic resonance images soft tissues especially clearly: brain, spinal cord, joints, heart, and tumors. Functional magnetic resonance can also show which areas of the brain are active.
发射高频声波并接收回声成像，安全便宜，广泛用于产检。: High-frequency sound waves are emitted and echoes received to form images; it is safe, inexpensive, and widely used in prenatal examinations.
声波遇到不同组织的交界面会反射回来，像回声一样。测量回声返回的时间就知道界面有多: When sound waves encounter interfaces between different tissues, they reflect back like echoes. Measuring the time for the echo to return reveals how deep the interface is; the strength of the echo reflects tissue properties ([[p:wave|Interference, diffraction & resonance]]).
探头里的压电晶体（见 [[piezoelectric-effect]]）通电时振: The piezoelectric crystal inside the probe (see [[piezoelectric-effect]]) vibrates and emits ultrasound at 2–15 MHz when powered, converting echoes back into electrical signals. A row of crystals scans line by line to form a real-time image. Using the Doppler effect also allows measurement of blood flow direction and speed.
超声源自声呐（见 [[sonar]]）。1956 年起英国格拉斯哥的唐纳德（Ia: Ultrasound originates from sonar (see [[sonar]]). Starting in 1956, Ian Donald of Glasgow, UK, used ultrasound for obstetric examinations; results were published in 1958.
超声没有电离辐射、便宜、可移动，成为产检、心脏和腹部检查最常用的手段。: Ultrasound has no ionizing radiation, is inexpensive, and portable, making it the most commonly used method for prenatal, cardiac, and abdominal examinations.
