注射带放射性标记的葡萄糖，看哪里代谢旺盛，常用于发现肿瘤。: Injecting glucose labeled with radioactive markers allows clinicians to identify areas of high metabolic activity, a technique frequently used to detect tumors.
癌细胞生长快，消耗的葡萄糖比正常细胞多。给葡萄糖分子挂上会放出正电子的放射性氟-: Cancer cells grow rapidly and consume more glucose than normal cells. Radioactive fluorine-18, which emits positive electrons when its molecules decay, is attached to glucose molecules. After injection into the body, areas with high metabolic activity accumulate more of this tracer ([[p:decay|Radioactive decay]]). When a positive electron meets an electron, they annihilate, converting their mass into two gamma photons traveling in opposite directions ([[p:massenergy|Mass–energy equivalence]]).
环形探测器捕捉成对的光子，连线交汇处就是示踪剂的位置。氟-18 半衰期不到两小时: Ring detectors capture pairs of photons; the intersection point of the connecting lines indicates the location of the tracer. Fluorine-18 has a half-life of less than two hours and must be produced by a nearby particle accelerator (see [[particle-accelerator]]). Today, this technology is often combined with CT scanners into a single machine.
1975 年前后，美国华盛顿大学的特波戈西安（Michel Ter-Pogoss: Around 1975, Michel Ter-Pogossian, Michael Phelps, and others at the University of Washington in the United States developed the earliest PET scanners.
PET 用于发现肿瘤转移、评估疗效，也用于研究阿尔茨海默病等脑部疾病。: PET is used to detect tumor metastases, evaluate treatment efficacy, and study brain diseases such as Alzheimer's disease.
记录心脏每次跳动时的电信号，用来诊断心律失常和心肌梗死。: Recording electrical signals from the heart with each beat is used to diagnose arrhythmias and myocardial infarction.
心脏每次跳动前，心肌细胞会依次去极化，形成在胸腔里传播的电场，皮肤表面能测到毫伏: Before each heartbeat, cardiac muscle cells depolarize in sequence, forming an electric field that propagates through the thoracic cavity. Voltage changes on the order of millivolts can be measured at the skin surface ([[p:charge|Electric charge & field]]).
标准心电图用 12 个导联从不同\"角度\"记录心脏电活动，波形中的 P 波、Q: Standard electrocardiograms record cardiac electrical activity from 12 leads at different "angles." The P wave, QRS complex, and T wave in the waveform correspond respectively to atrial contraction, ventricular contraction, and recovery. Abnormal waveforms indicate arrhythmias, myocardial ischemia, or infarction. Holter monitors can record continuously for more than 24 hours.
1903 年荷兰生理学家爱因托芬（Willem Einthoven）用灵敏的弦线: In 1903, Dutch physiologist Willem Einthoven recorded a clear electrocardiogram using a sensitive string galvanometer; he received the Nobel Prize in 1924.
心电图至今是诊断心脏病最快、最便宜的检查，如今连智能手表也能做单导联心电图（见: Electrocardiography remains the fastest and most inexpensive method for diagnosing heart disease. Today, even smartwatches can perform single-lead electrocardiograms (see [[wearable-device]]).
在头皮上记录大脑神经元的集体电活动，用于诊断癫痫和睡眠研究。: Collective electrical activity of neurons on the scalp is recorded to diagnose epilepsy and conduct sleep research.
大量神经元同步放电时，会在头皮上产生微伏级的电位变化（[[p:charge|电荷: When large numbers of neurons fire synchronously, they produce potential changes on the scalp on the order of microvolts ([[p:charge|Electric charge & field]]). The frequency and morphology of brain waves differ across various stages: wakefulness with relaxation, focus, and sleep.
在头皮上按标准位置放置数十个电极，放大并记录各点之间的电位差。癫痫发作时会出现特: Dozens of electrodes are placed at standard positions on the scalp to amplify and record potential differences between points. During epileptic seizures, characteristic sharp waves and spines appear; sleep monitoring relies on electroencephalography to distinguish light sleep, deep sleep, and rapid eye movement sleep. Electroencephalography has high temporal resolution but makes it difficult to precisely locate the source of signals.
1924 年德国精神科医生伯格（Hans Berger）首次记录到人类脑电图，并: In 1924, German psychiatrist Hans Berger first recorded the human electroencephalogram and discovered the alpha wave that appears when eyes are closed and the subject is relaxed.
脑电图是诊断癫痫和研究睡眠的基本工具，也是非侵入式脑机接口的信号来源（见 [[b: Electroencephalography is a basic tool for diagnosing epilepsy and studying sleep, and it serves as the signal source for non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (see [[brain-computer-interface]]).
用光纤或微型摄像头深入消化道等腔道直接观察和取样。: Using fiber optics or miniature cameras to directly observe and sample inside body cavities such as the digestive tract.
光在细玻璃纤维里不断发生全反射，即使纤维弯曲也能把光从一端传到另一端（[[p:o: Light undergoes total internal reflection repeatedly within thin glass fibers; even when the fiber bends, light can still be transmitted from one end to the other ([[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]]). Thousands or tens of thousands of fibers arranged in order can transmit an image (see [[fiber-optic]]).
内窥镜从口、肛门或小切口伸入体内，前端有光源和镜头，现代产品多用微型图像传感器直: Endoscopes enter the body through the mouth, anus, or small incisions; their front ends contain light sources and lenses. Modern products often use miniature image sensors to capture images directly. Through working channels, biopsies can be taken, polyps removed, and bleeding stopped. Capsule endoscopes are swallowed like pills and take photos along the way.
1957 年美国医生赫希奥维茨（Basil Hirschowitz）测试了第一台: In 1957, American doctor Basil Hirschowitz tested the first fiber-optic gastroscope; it was subsequently used on patients the following year.
医生能直接看到并处理消化道病变，许多早期肿瘤不必开刀就能在内镜下切除，也为微创手: Doctors can directly observe and treat lesions in the digestive tract. Many early-stage tumors can be removed endoscopically without surgery, laying the foundation for minimally invasive surgery (see [[minimally-invasive-surgery]]).
用两种颜色的光穿过指尖，根据吸收差算出血氧饱和度。: Using two colors of light to pass through a fingertip, blood oxygen saturation is calculated based on the difference in absorption.
结合了氧的血红蛋白和没结合氧的血红蛋白颜色不同，对红光和红外光的吸收比例也不同（: Hemoglobin combined with oxygen and hemoglobin not combined with oxygen have different colors, resulting in different absorption ratios for red and infrared light ([[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]]). By measuring the ratio of absorption for both types of light, blood oxygen saturation can be calculated.
指夹一侧有发红光和红外光的发光二极管（见 [[led]]），另一侧是光探测器。只: One side of a finger clip contains light-emitting diodes emitting red and infrared light (see [[led]]), while the other side contains a light detector. Only the portion of the signal that fluctuates with the pulse is analyzed to exclude interference from unchanging parts such as skin and bone. Studies have found that it may overestimate blood oxygen in people with darker skin tones, so this should be noted.
1972 年日本光电公司的工程师青柳卓雄（Takuo Aoyagi）提出利用脉搏: In 1972, Takuo Aoyagi, an engineer at a Japanese optical-electric company, proposed the principle of measuring blood oxygen saturation using pulse waveforms.
血氧仪让麻醉和重症监护更安全，新冠疫情期间成为家庭常备设备。: Pulse oximeters make anesthesia and intensive care safer, becoming common household equipment during the COVID-19 pandemic.
样本沿试纸流动、遇到抗体就显色，十几分钟出结果，如验孕棒和抗原检测。: Samples flow along the test strip; when they encounter antibodies, color develops. Results appear in about ten minutes, similar to pregnancy tests and antigen detection kits.
抗体能像钥匙配锁一样只抓住特定的目标分子（[[p:recognition|分子识: Antibodies can grab specific target molecules like a key fits a lock ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]). By fixing antibodies on the test strip and using colored gold-nanoparticle 'tags', the appearance of target molecules causes a colored line to show up.
样本滴在试纸一端，靠毛细作用流动，先溶解带金颗粒的抗体，与目标分子结合，流到检测: Samples are dropped at one end of the strip; capillary action moves them, first dissolving the antibody-gold-particle mixture so it binds with target molecules. When flowing to the detection line, they are caught by a second antibody and aggregate into a visible red line; the control line proves the strip is effective. The whole process takes about ten minutes without needing an instrument.
1988 年英国联合利华推出基于侧流层析技术的家用验孕棒。: In 1988, Unilever in the UK launched a home pregnancy test based on lateral flow chromatography technology.
同样原理用于疟疾、艾滋病和新冠抗原检测，让诊断走出实验室，进入家庭和偏远地区。: The same principle is used for malaria, HIV, and COVID-19 antigen tests, allowing diagnosis to move out of laboratories and into homes and remote areas.
皮下微小传感器每隔几分钟测一次血糖，配合胰岛素泵形成\"人工胰腺\"。: Subcutaneous micro-sensors measure blood glucose every few minutes; combined with insulin pumps, they form an 'artificial pancreas'.
维持血糖稳定本来是胰腺的工作，需要随时\"测量—调整\"（[[p:homeost: Maintaining stable blood glucose is naturally the pancreas's job, requiring constant 'measure-then-adjust' ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]). Diabetic patients who can continuously monitor their blood glucose levels can adjust insulin intake and diet more timelyly ([[p:feedback|Feedback & control]]).
一根细如发丝的传感器插在皮下，表面的葡萄糖氧化酶与组织液中的葡萄糖反应产生电流，: A sensor as thin as a hair is inserted under the skin; surface glucose oxidase reacts with glucose in interstitial fluid to produce an electric current, reporting readings every few minutes. Data travels to a smartphone or insulin pump. Algorithms automatically adjust the insulin pump system based on these readings, known as an 'artificial pancreas'.
1999 年美国药监局批准第一款连续血糖监测设备。: In 1999, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the first continuous glucose monitoring device.
病人不必一天多次扎手指，还能看到血糖的变化趋势和夜间低血糖，糖尿病管理更精细。: Patients do not need to prick their fingers multiple times a day; they can also observe trends in blood glucose levels and nighttime hypoglycemia, making diabetes management more refined.
把病历数字化并在医院之间共享，是医疗 AI 的数据基础。: Digitizing medical records and sharing them between hospitals forms the data foundation for medical AI.
纸质病历分散在各个医院和科室，查找难、易出错。病历数字化并按统一标准编码，信息就: Paper medical records are scattered across various hospitals and departments, making retrieval difficult and prone to errors. Digitizing records and encoding them according to unified standards allow information to be retrieved, shared, and statistically analyzed ([[p:info|Information theory]]).
电子病历记录诊断、检验、影像、用药和手术，医生开药时系统可自动提示过敏和药物相互: Electronic medical records document diagnoses, laboratory tests, imaging, medication prescriptions, and surgeries. When doctors prescribe drugs, the system can automatically alert about allergies and drug interactions. Different systems must rely on unified data standards to exchange information. Medical record data also serves as raw material for medical research and medical AI; privacy protection is a core issue.
20 世纪 60–70 年代美国一些医院开始试用计算机病历；2009 年美国立法: In the 1960s–70s, some U.S. hospitals began trial use of computerized medical records; in 2009, U.S. legislation subsidized hospitals adopting electronic medical records, leading to rapid increases in adoption rates.
电子病历提高了医疗的连续性和安全性，但录入负担也成为医生职业倦怠的来源之一。: Electronic medical records improve continuity and safety in healthcare, but the burden of data entry also becomes a source of physician burnout.
通过视频、远程监测设备看病，疫情期间迅速普及。: Telemedicine, including video consultations and remote monitoring devices, rapidly became widespread during the pandemic.
许多诊疗环节其实是信息交换：询问病史、看检查结果、调整用药。只要信息能远程传递，: Many diagnostic and treatment steps are essentially information exchanges: asking about medical history, reviewing test results, adjusting medication. As long as information can be transmitted remotely, patients and doctors do not need to be in the same place ([[p:network|Network effects]]).
形式包括视频问诊、远程会诊（基层医生请大医院专家看片子）、远程监测（家用血压计、: Forms include video consultations, remote conferences (primary care doctors consulting with experts from large hospitals to review imaging), and remote monitoring (home blood pressure monitors, glucose meters, and heart rate patches automatically uploading data). Diagnostic and treatment procedures requiring physical examinations and operations must still be completed offline.
20 世纪 60 年代起，美国就有用电视连线进行远程会诊的尝试；2020 年新冠: Since the 1960s, attempts at teleconferencing for remote consultations existed in the U.S.; during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, remote consultations were massively adopted in many countries within a short time.
远程医疗缓解了偏远地区缺医少药的问题，也带来了服务质量、医保支付和数据安全等新课: Telemedicine alleviates the problem of lack of medical and pharmaceutical resources in remote areas but also brings new challenges regarding service quality, insurance payment, and data security.
比较个体 DNA 中高度可变的片段识别身份，革新了刑侦和亲子鉴定。: Identifying individuals by comparing highly variable segments within individual DNA has revolutionized criminal investigation and paternity testing.
人与人的 DNA 有 99.9% 相同，但某些片段中短序列重复的次数因人而异。检: Human DNA is 99.9% identical between people, but the number of repetitions in certain short sequence fragments varies from person to person. By detecting multiple such loci, the resulting 'barcode' is almost unique ([[p:dogma|Central dogma]], [[p:probability|Probability & statistical inference]]).
用 PCR 扩增十几到二十个短串联重复位点（见 [[pcr]]），再用毛细管电泳: Use polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to amplify approximately ten to twenty short tandem repeat loci (see [[pcr]]), then separate them by length using capillary electrophoresis and read the number of repeats for each locus. When all loci in two samples are identical, the probability of random coincidence can be as low as one in billions.
1984 年 9 月，英国遗传学家杰弗里斯（Alec Jeffreys）在莱斯特: In September 1984, British geneticist Alec Jeffreys discovered DNA fingerprinting at the University of Leicester. In 1988, it was first used in a criminal case in the United Kingdom to convict the true culprit and exonerate an innocent suspect.
DNA 鉴定革新了刑侦、亲子鉴定和灾难遇难者身份识别，也帮助许多被错判的人平反。: DNA analysis revolutionized criminal investigation, paternity testing, and identification of disaster victims, and helped many wrongly convicted individuals be acquitted.
在电场中让带负电的 DNA 片段穿过凝胶，小片段跑得快，从而按大小分开。: Allow negatively charged DNA fragments to pass through a gel under an electric field; smaller fragments move faster, thereby separating them by size.
DNA 的磷酸骨架带负电，在电场中会向正极移动（[[p:charge|电荷与电场: The phosphate backbone of DNA carries a negative charge and moves toward the positive electrode in an electric field ([[p:charge|Electric charge & field]]). When passing through the mesh pores of a gel, smaller fragments move quickly while larger ones move slowly, thus separating them by length.
把样本加进凝胶的小孔里，通电一段时间后，用荧光染料染色，在紫外或蓝光下看到一条条: Place samples into small wells of a gel, apply voltage for a period, stain with fluorescent dye, and observe distinct "bands" under ultraviolet or blue light. Comparing these bands to standards of known lengths allows determination of fragment size. Proteins can also be separated by size using similar methods.
1937 年瑞典化学家蒂塞利乌斯（Arne Tiselius）发明电泳分析蛋白质: In 1937, Swedish chemist Arne Tiselius invented electrophoresis for protein analysis; he received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1948. Since the 1970s of the 20th century, gel electrophoresis has become a routine tool in molecular biology.
它是基因克隆、PCR 结果检查和早期 DNA 测序的基本步骤。: It is a fundamental step for gene cloning, checking PCR results, and early DNA sequencing.
血常规、生化等检验用仪器自动测定血液中的细胞和分子，是现代诊断最常用的依据之一。: Automated instruments used in complete blood count and biochemical tests measure cells and molecules in blood; this is one of the most commonly relied-upon bases for modern diagnosis.
血液中的细胞数量和化学成分反映着全身的状况。让细胞逐个通过小孔，会引起电阻的瞬间: Cell counts and chemical compositions in blood reflect the overall condition of the body. Passing cells one by one through small pores causes instantaneous changes in resistance; counting these "pulses" allows cell enumeration ([[p:ohm|Ohm's law & circuits]]). Allowing serum to react with reagents produces coloration, where the depth of color corresponds to concentration ([[p:optics|Reflection & refraction]]).
血细胞分析仪几十秒内报告红细胞、白细胞、血小板数量；生化分析仪测定血糖、血脂、肝: Hematology analyzers report red blood cell, white blood cell, and platelet counts within tens of seconds; biochemical analyzers measure indicators such as blood glucose, lipids, and liver and kidney function. Automated assembly lines complete sample sorting, testing, and result review, enabling large hospitals to process tens of thousands of samples daily.
1953 年美国工程师库尔特（Wallace Coulter）发明了电阻法细胞计: In 1953, American engineer Wallace Coulter invented the principle of resistance-based cell counting; automated biochemical analyzers appeared in the late 1950s.
检验从手工显微镜计数变成了快速、标准化的流水线，是现代诊断最常用的依据之一。: Testing transformed from manual microscopic counting to rapid, standardized assembly lines, becoming one of the most commonly relied-upon bases for modern diagnosis.
用袖带压住动脉再慢慢放气测血压、用体温计测体温，把\"生命体征\"变成可记录、可: Using a cuff to compress an artery and then slowly releasing it to measure blood pressure, or using a thermometer to measure body temperature, turns "vital signs" into recordable and comparable numbers.
用袖带压住上臂动脉，压力大于动脉内最高压时血流被阻断；慢慢放气，血流重新冲过时出: Compressing the upper arm artery with a cuff blocks blood flow when the pressure exceeds the maximum pressure within the artery; as the cuff is slowly released, blood flow resumes and produces pulsating sounds. At this point, the pressure represents systolic pressure, and when the sound disappears, it indicates diastolic pressure ([[p:fluid|Fluid pressure & lift]]).
传统方法用水银柱压力计配合听诊器听声音；现代电子血压计测量袖带里的压力振荡，由算: Traditional methods used mercury column manometers combined with stethoscopes to listen for sounds; modern electronic blood pressure meters measure pressure oscillations within the cuff, with algorithms automatically calculating blood pressure. Thermometers have evolved from mercury glass tubes to electronic and infrared measurement devices.

青霉素阻断细菌细胞壁的交联，细菌在生长和分裂时细胞壁出现缺口，被内部压力撑破；人: Penicillin blocks cross-linking in bacterial cell walls; when bacteria grow and divide, gaps appear in the cell wall, which are ruptured by internal pressure. Human cells lack cell walls and are thus unaffected.

青霉素推广仅几年就出现了耐药菌；1961 年英国发现耐甲氧西林金黄色葡萄球菌（M: Resistant strains emerged within just a few years of penicillin promotion; MRSA (methicillin-resistant *Staphylococcus aureus*) was discovered in the UK in 1961. 耐药被世界卫生组织列为全球公共卫生的重大威胁之一。应对需要减少不必要的处方、限制: Antibiotic resistance has been listed by the World Health Organization as one of the major global public health threats. 免疫系统本来能识别并杀死癌细胞，但癌细胞会利用免疫系统自带的\"刹车\"（免疫检: The immune system can normally recognize and kill cancer cells, but cancer cells exploit the immune system's built-in 'brakes' (immune checkpoints, such as PD-1, CTLA-4) to stop T cells. Using antibodies to block these brakes releases the attacking power of T cells ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]).
免疫检查点抑制剂是单克隆抗体（见 [[monoclonal-antibody]]: Immune checkpoint inhibitors are monoclonal antibodies (see [[monoclonal-antibody]]), administered via intravenous infusion. They show lasting efficacy in some patients with melanoma, lung cancer, etc.; some late-stage patients achieve long-term remission; however, not everyone responds, and overactivation of the immune system may attack normal organs, causing immune-related adverse reactions. Another approach involves modifying the patient's own immune cells (see [[car-t]]).
美国免疫学家艾利森（James Allison）研究 CTLA-4，日本免疫学家: Immunologist James Allison from the US studied CTLA-4; immunologist Yoshiki Shouji from Japan studied PD-1; they shared the 2018 Nobel Prize. The first checkpoint inhibitor, ipilimumab, was approved in 2011.
免疫疗法成为手术、放疗、化疗、靶向治疗之外的又一大类癌症疗法。如何预测哪些患者有: Immunotherapy has become another major class of cancer treatments beyond surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, and targeted therapy. Predicting which patients will respond is a current research focus.
把患者的 T 细胞改造成能识别癌细胞的\"导弹\"再输回体内。: Transform the patient's T cells into "missiles" capable of recognizing cancer cells, then reinfuse them into the body.
T 细胞是免疫系统的\"杀手\"，但常常认不出癌细胞。给它装上一个人工设计的\": T cells are the "killers" of the immune system, but they often fail to recognize cancer cells. Equip them with an artificially designed "navigation" receptor (chimeric antigen receptor, CAR), and T cells can identify specific molecules on the surface of cancer cells and initiate an attack ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]], [[p:dogma|Central dogma]]).
从患者血液中分离 T 细胞，用病毒载体导入 CAR 基因，扩增后输回体内，在体内: Separate T cells from the patient's blood, introduce the CAR gene using a viral vector, expand them, and reinfuse them into the body. They continue to replicate within the body, becoming "living drugs." The primary risk is severe reactions such as cytokine release syndrome, requiring treatment in experienced hospitals.
2017 年美国批准第一款 CAR-T 疗法，用于儿童和青年急性淋巴细胞白血病；: In 2017, the United States approved the first CAR-T therapy for children and young adults with acute lymphoblastic leukemia; China also began approving CAR-T products in 2021.
一部分复发难治的血液肿瘤患者获得长期缓解。高昂的价格和对实体瘤效果有限，是它面临: Some patients with recurrent, refractory hematological tumors achieve long-term remission. High costs and limited efficacy against solid tumors are its main challenges.
2005 年匈牙利裔科学家卡里科（Katalin Karikó）和美国免疫学家韦: In 2005, Hungarian scientist Katalin Karikó and American immunologist Drew Weissman published their key discovery of modified bases; the two were awarded the 2023 Nobel Prize. In December 2020, the COVID-19 mRNA vaccine developed by Pfizer and German BioNTech was approved in the UK, taking less than a year from the publication of the viral sequence to approval; Moderna's vaccine followed shortly thereafter.
mRNA 疫苗在新冠大流行中接种了数十亿剂，证明了这一平台的速度和规模。研究者正: mRNA vaccines administered billions of doses during the global pandemic, proving the speed and scale of this platform. Researchers are now applying it for influenza, personalized tumor vaccines, and other diseases. Early products required ultra-low-temperature storage, also exposing issues with cold chains and unequal global distribution.
mRNA 疫苗的工作流程：脂质纳米颗粒把 mRNA 送入细胞，核糖体按图纸生产病: The workflow of mRNA vaccines: lipid nanoparticles deliver mRNA into cells; ribosomes produce viral proteins according to the blueprint; the immune system generates antibodies and memory cells based on this.
用脂肪微球包裹脆弱的 mRNA 和药物，保护它们并送入细胞。: Encapsulate fragile mRNA and drugs in fat microspheres to protect them and deliver them into cells.
mRNA、小干扰 RNA 等核酸药物带负电、体积大，又容易被酶分解，自己进不了细: mRNA, small interfering RNA, and other nucleic acid drugs carry a negative charge, have large volumes, are easily degraded by enzymes, and cannot enter cells themselves. Enclose them in a nanoshell composed of lipids, like putting an "envelope" that can fuse with the cell membrane onto "express delivery" ([[p:diffusion|Diffusion & membranes]], [[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]).
关键成分是可电离脂质：在酸性条件下带正电，能把带负电的核酸包裹进去；在血液的中性: The key component is ionizable lipid: it carries a positive charge under acidic conditions, wrapping the negatively charged nucleic acid inside; it remains uncharged in the neutral environment of blood, exhibiting low toxicity; upon entering the acidic endosome within the cell, it becomes charged again, helping the nucleic acid escape into the cytoplasm. Particle diameter is approximately 100 nanometers.
加拿大科学家卡利斯（Pieter Cullis）等人长期研究脂质载体；2018: Canadian scientist Pieter Cullis and colleagues have long studied lipid carriers; in 2018, the first lipid nanoparticle-encapsulated small interfering RNA drug was approved (see [[rna-interference]]).
没有它就没有 mRNA 疫苗，它也是基因编辑药物体内递送的主要载体。: Without it, there would be no mRNA vaccines; it is also the main carrier for intracellular delivery of gene editing drugs.
模仿肠道激素 GLP-1 调节血糖和食欲，司美格鲁肽等成为降糖和减重的重磅药。: Mimicking the glucose and appetite-regulating function of the intestinal hormone GLP-1, drugs such as semaglutide have become major treatments for lowering blood sugar and reducing weight.
进食后，肠道会分泌一种激素 GLP-1，告诉胰腺\"该分泌胰岛素了\"，同时让胃: After eating, the intestine secretes a hormone called GLP-1, telling the pancreas "it's time to secrete insulin," while slowing gastric emptying and making the brain feel full ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]). Natural GLP-1 is broken down in the blood within minutes; GLP-1 drugs are "enhanced versions" that bind to the same receptor for a long duration ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]).
多为每周注射一次，也有口服剂型。它只在血糖升高时促进胰岛素分泌，单用时低血糖风险: Most are administered once weekly, with some oral formulations available. They promote insulin secretion only when blood glucose rises; monotherapy carries a lower risk of hypoglycemia. Large trials show an average weight loss of approximately 15% in obese individuals, and a reduction in cardiovascular events for some patients. Common side effects include gastrointestinal reactions; weight often returns after discontinuation, requiring use according to medical advice.
从美洲毒蜥唾液中发现的类 GLP-1 多肽，被开发成艾塞那肽，2005 年获批治: A GLP-1-like peptide discovered from the saliva of an American gila monster was developed into exenatide, approved in 2005 for diabetes treatment. Semaglutide was approved for diabetes in 2017 and for weight loss in 2021.
肥胖第一次有了效果显著的药物疗法；它也成为销售额最高的药物之一，引发了供应短缺和: Obesity finally has a drug therapy with significant efficacy; it also became one of the highest-selling drugs, sparking discussions on supply shortages and insurance payment.
屠呦呦团队从青蒿中提取的抗疟药，挽救了数百万生命，2015 年获诺贝尔奖。: Tu Youyou's team extracted an antimalarial drug from sweet wormwood, saving millions of lives; she was awarded the Nobel Prize in 2015.
疟原虫寄生在红细胞里，以血红蛋白为食，体内积累了大量含铁的血红素。青蒿素分子中有: Malaria parasites reside inside red blood cells, feeding on hemoglobin, accumulating large amounts of iron-containing heme within the body. The artemisinin molecule contains a special peroxide bridge that breaks upon encountering iron, generating free radicals that destroy malaria parasite proteins ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]).
青蒿素起效快但维持时间短，世卫组织推荐与长效抗疟药组成联合疗法，提高疗效、延缓耐: Artemisinin acts quickly but has a short duration of effect; the World Health Organization recommends combining it with long-acting antimalar drugs to improve efficacy and delay resistance.
1967 年中国启动抗疟药研究的\"523 项目\"。屠呦呦受东晋葛洪《肘后备急: In 1967, China launched the "Project 523" for antimalarial drug research. Inspired by Ge Hong's *Handbook of Prescriptions for Emergencies* from the Eastern Jin Dynasty stating "one handful of sweet wormwood, two liters of water to soak, squeeze out the juice," Tu Youyou switched to low-temperature ether extraction, obtaining a highly efficient extract in 1971–1972. She was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2015.
青蒿素联合疗法挽救了数百万疟疾患者的生命，主要在非洲；东南亚已出现部分耐药，需要: Artemisinin-based combination therapy has saved millions of lives from malaria, primarily in Africa; partial resistance has emerged in Southeast Asia, requiring continuous monitoring.
用系统收集的研究证据而不是个人经验来决定治疗；随机试验和系统综述处在证据等级的顶: Decide on treatment based on systematic research evidence rather than personal experience; randomized trials and systematic reviews are at the top of the evidence hierarchy.
医生的经验和直觉会受记忆偏差和个案影响。循证医学主张，临床决策应当基于系统收集、: A doctor's experience and intuition can be influenced by memory bias and individual cases. Evidence-based medicine advocates that clinical decisions should be based on research evidence that has been systematically collected and rigorously evaluated, combined with the physician's professional judgment and the patient's wishes ([[p:probability|Probability & statistical inference]]).
证据有等级：多项随机对照试验的系统综述最可靠，其次是单个随机试验，再次是观察性研: Evidence has levels: systematic reviews of multiple randomized controlled trials are most reliable, followed by single randomized trials, then observational studies, and finally personal experience as weakest. Clinical guidelines provide recommendations based on evidence strength by expert panels.
1972 年英国流行病学家科克伦（Archie Cochrane）呼吁系统整理随: In 1972, British epidemiologist Archie Cochrane called for the systematic organization of evidence from randomized trials; in 1991, Canadian scholar Gordon Guyatt coined the term 'evidence-based medicine'; in 1993, the Cochrane Collaboration was established.
循证医学改变了医学教育和临床指南的制定方式，让许多无效或有害的常规做法被淘汰。: Evidence-based medicine has changed medical education and the formulation of clinical guidelines, leading to the elimination of many ineffective or harmful routine practices.
从鸦片中提纯的吗啡是第一种被分离出来的植物有效成分；阿片类药物镇痛最强，也最易成: Morphine, purified from opium, was the first plant-derived active ingredient to be isolated; opioid analgesics provide the strongest pain relief but are also most prone to addiction.
人体自身会分泌\"内啡肽\"等物质，与神经细胞上的阿片受体结合来抑制疼痛。吗啡等: The human body itself secretes substances such as 'endorphins' that bind to opioid receptors on nerve cells to inhibit pain. Opioid drugs like morphine mimic them, binding to the same receptor and exerting extremely strong analgesic effects ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]).
阿片类药物用于手术、癌痛等剧烈疼痛。它们也会抑制呼吸，长期使用会产生耐受和依赖；: Opioids are used for severe pain such as post-surgical pain and cancer pain. They also suppress respiration; long-term use leads to tolerance and dependence; overdose can be fatal, but naloxone can rapidly reverse the effect. Medical use must strictly follow prescriptions and regulations.
1804 年前后，德国药剂师泽尔蒂纳（Friedrich Sertürner）从: Around 1804, German pharmacist Friedrich Sertürner isolated morphine from opium, marking the first effective ingredient purified from a plant.
阿片类药物是疼痛治疗不可替代的工具；但美国自 20 世纪 90 年代末起的阿片类: Opioids are an irreplaceable tool for pain treatment; however, the opioid crisis in the United States since the late 1990s has caused hundreds of thousands of deaths, while patients in many low-income countries lack access to analgesics.
氯丙嗪（1952）开启了用药物治疗精神疾病的时代，此后有了抗抑郁药、抗焦虑药和情: Chlorpromazine (1952) opened the era of treating mental disorders with drugs, followed by antidepressants, anxiolytics, and mood stabilizers.
大脑中的神经细胞靠多巴胺、5-羟色胺等神经递质传递信号。精神类药物通过与递质的受: Nerve cells in the brain transmit signals via neurotransmitters such as dopamine and 5-hydroxytryptamine. Psychiatric medications work by binding to receptors or 'reuptake pumps' of these neurotransmitters, regulating the strength of these signals ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]). However, the mechanisms of many mental disorders remain incompletely understood.
抗精神病药主要阻断多巴胺受体；常用抗抑郁药抑制 5-羟色胺回收；锂盐用于稳定双相: Antipsychotic drugs primarily block dopamine receptors; common antidepressants inhibit 5-hydroxytryptamine reuptake; lithium salts are used to stabilize mood in bipolar disorder. Drugs often take weeks to work and are frequently combined with psychotherapy, requiring guidance from specialists.
1952 年法国医生发现氯丙嗪能显著缓解精神分裂症症状，开启了精神药理学时代。1: In 1952, French doctors discovered that chlorpromazine significantly alleviated symptoms of schizophrenia, opening the era of psychopharmacology. In 1987, the US approved fluoxetine (Prozac) for market release.
许多患者得以回归社会，大型精神病院的住院人数大幅下降；药物的副作用和疗效个体差异: Many patients have been able to return to society, and hospitalization numbers in large psychiatric hospitals have dropped significantly; side effects and individual differences in drug efficacy remain challenges.
1953 年 4 月，英国剑桥的沃森（James Watson）和克里克（Fra: In April 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick at Cambridge University in the UK proposed the DNA double helix model in 'Nature'. Key evidence came from Rosalind Franklin's X-ray diffraction photo 'Photo 51' taken at King's College London, as well as research by Maurice Wilkins. In 1962, Watson, Crick, and Wilkins received the Nobel Prize; Franklin had already died in 1958.
双螺旋揭示了遗传的物质基础，开启了分子生物学。此后的遗传密码、基因工程、PCR、: The double helix revealed the material basis of heredity, opening molecular biology. Subsequent genetic codes, gene engineering, PCR, sequencing, and gene editing all rest on 'reading and manipulating these four letters'. Crick's final sentence in his paper, 'the pairing rules suggest a possible mechanism for replication', is known as one of the most understated sentences in the history of science.
DNA 双螺旋：糖—磷酸骨架在外，碱基在内配对（A—T、G—C）；复制时双链解开: DNA double helix: sugar-phosphate backbone outside, bases inside paired (A—T, G—C); during replication, the double strands unwind, and each old strand serves as a template to synthesize a new strand.
每三个碱基对应一个氨基酸，64 个密码子在几乎所有生物中通用。: Every three bases correspond to one amino acid; 64 codons are universal in almost all organisms.
DNA 只有 4 种碱基，蛋白质却由 20 种氨基酸组成。每 3 个碱基组成一个: DNA has only 4 types of bases, while proteins are composed of 20 types of amino acids. Every 3 bases form a 'codon' corresponding to one amino acid; 4×4×4 = 64 combinations are sufficient, with surplus ([[p:info|Information theory]], [[p:dogma|Central dogma]]).
64 个密码子中，61 个编码氨基酸，3 个表示\"终止\"；多数氨基酸有好几个: Of the 64 codons, 61 code for amino acids, and 3 indicate 'termination'; most amino acids have several codons, so a single base mutation does not necessarily change the protein. This code is universal in almost all organisms; human genes placed in bacteria can be correctly read.
1961 年美国的尼伦伯格（Marshall Nirenberg）和马特海用只含: In 1961, American Marshall Nirenberg and Matthaei deciphered the first codon using artificial RNA containing only uracil; by 1966, all codons were deciphered, and Nirenberg et al. received the 1968 Nobel Prize.
密码的通用性是基因工程能够实现的前提（见 [[recombinant-dna]]: The universality of the code is a prerequisite for gene engineering (see [[recombinant-dna]]) and strong evidence for the common ancestry of life on Earth.
细菌用来剪切入侵病毒 DNA 的\"分子剪刀\"，成为基因工程的基本工具。: Bacteria use 'molecular scissors' to cut out invading viral DNA, becoming basic tools for gene engineering.
细菌用一类酶保护自己：它们识别入侵病毒 DNA 上特定的短序列并在此处切断，而细: Bacteria use a class of enzymes to protect themselves: they recognize specific short sequences on invading viral DNA and cut there, while the bacteria's own identical sequences are chemically marked so they are not cut ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]).
每种限制酶只认一种序列，比如 EcoRI 只在 GAATTC 处下刀。许多酶切出: Each restriction enzyme recognizes only one specific sequence; for example, EcoRI cuts only at the GAATTC site. Many enzymes produce ends with complementary single-stranded "sticky ends." DNA from different sources can be spliced together like a puzzle when cut by the same enzyme.
瑞士的阿尔伯（Werner Arber）提出了限制酶的理论；1970 年美国的史: Werner Arber of Switzerland proposed the theory of restriction enzymes; in 1970, Hamilton Smith of the United States isolated the first restriction enzyme capable of cutting at specific sites, and Nathanson used it to map DNA. The three shared the Nobel Prize in 1978.
限制酶是基因工程的\"分子剪刀\"，让科学家第一次能精确地剪切和拼接 DNA。: Restriction enzymes are the "molecular scissors" of genetic engineering, allowing scientists for the first time to precisely cut and splice DNA.
1972 年美国斯坦福大学的伯格（Paul Berg）首次构建重组 DNA 分子: In 1972, Paul Berg of Stanford University in the United States first constructed a recombinant DNA molecule. In 1973, Stanley Cohen of Stanford and Herbert Boyer of the University of California, San Francisco introduced recombinant plasmids into *E. coli* and proved they could replicate stably. In 1975, scientists met at Asilomar in the United States and voluntarily formulated safety guidelines for recombinant DNA research.
1982 年重组人胰岛素上市，此后生长激素、乙肝疫苗、促红细胞生成素、单克隆抗体: In 1982, recombinant human insulin went on the market; subsequently, growth hormone, hepatitis B vaccine, erythropoietin, monoclonal antibodies, and others were successively introduced, giving birth to the biotechnology industry (see [[biotech-industry]]). The same technology is also used for genetically modified crops (see [[gmo-crops]]) and almost all modern biological research.
重组 DNA 的基本步骤：用同一种限制酶切开目标基因和质粒，连接后导入细菌，细菌: The basic steps of recombinant DNA: use the same restriction enzyme to cut the target gene and plasmid, ligate them, introduce into bacteria, let the bacteria reproduce and produce the target protein.
基因泰克等公司把基因工程变成生意，1982 年重组人胰岛素成为首个基因工程药物。: Companies such as Genentech turned genetic engineering into business; in 1982, recombinant human insulin became the first genetically engineered drug.
一旦能让细菌按基因图纸生产蛋白质，药物生产就从\"从动物器官中提取\"变成\"在: Once bacteria can be made to produce proteins according to gene blueprints, drug production changes from "extraction from animal organs" to "cultivation in fermenters," allowing scalable amplification ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]).
生物技术公司通常以一项核心技术或一个候选药起步，靠风险投资支撑多年研发，再通过上: Biotechnology companies typically start with a core technology or a candidate drug, relying on venture capital support for years of R&D, then achieving returns through listing, licensing, or acquisition by large pharmaceutical enterprises. Patent protection is the foundation of this business model.
1976 年博耶与风险投资人斯旺森（Robert Swanson）创立基因泰克公: In 1976, Herbert Boyer founded Genentech with venture capitalist Robert Swanson; in 1980, the United States Supreme Court ruled that genetically modified microorganisms could be patented; in 1982, Genentech's recombinant human insulin became the first genetically engineered drug to go on the market.
生物技术从实验室走向产业，\"科学家 + 风险投资\"的创业模式此后被许多领域效: Biotechnology moved from the laboratory to industry; the "scientists + venture capital" startup model has since been emulated by many fields.
1983 年美国 Cetus 公司的化学家穆利斯（Kary Mullis）在夜间: In 1983, chemist Kary Mullis of Cetus in the United States conceived this method while driving at night; he received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1993. Starting in 1988, heat-resistant Taq polymerase enabled PCR to achieve automation.
PCR 让极微量的 DNA 也能被检测和研究：一根头发、一滴血就能做 DNA 鉴: PCR allows even minute amounts of DNA to be detected and studied: a single strand of hair or a drop of blood can perform DNA identification (see [[dna-profiling]]), and several viruses can be identified. It is the foundational tool for gene cloning, sequencing, genetic disease diagnosis, and ancient DNA research, and also the core technology for global nucleic acid testing during the COVID-19 pandemic.
PCR 的一个循环：高温解链、降温让引物结合、聚合酶延伸；每个循环目标 DNA: One cycle of PCR: high-temperature denaturation, cooling to allow primers to bind, polymerase extension; each cycle doubles the target DNA, and 30 cycles amplify approximately 1 billion-fold.
1977 年英国生化学家桑格（Frederick Sanger）发表双脱氧链终止: In 1977, British biochemist Frederick Sanger published the dideoxy chain-termination sequencing method; he received his second Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1980; that same year, Maxam and Gilbert of the United States also published a chemical sequencing method. In 1987, the first commercial automated fluorescent sequencer was introduced.
测序让\"读基因\"成为日常：诊断遗传病、为肿瘤找靶点、追踪病毒变异、鉴定物种和: Sequencing makes "reading genes" a daily task: diagnosing genetic diseases, identifying targets for tumors, tracking viral mutations, identifying species, and studying evolution. The genome sequence of the novel coronavirus was measured and made public in the early stages of the pandemic, enabling rapid initiation of vaccine development.
桑格测序法：带荧光的终止剂让新链在不同位置停下，按长度排序后依次读出末端颜色，就: Sanger sequencing method: fluorescent terminators cause new chains to stop at different positions; after sorting by length, the terminal colors are read sequentially to obtain the sequence; below is a chart showing the cost change for sequencing a human genome (logarithmic coordinates).
多国合作测出人类约 30 亿个碱基对的序列，1990 年启动、2003 年完成。: Multiple countries collaborated to sequence approximately 3 billion base pairs of the human genome; initiated in 1990 and completed in 2003.
要理解人的基因，先得有一份完整的\"参考书\"。基因组太大，任何一个实验室都测不: To understand human genes, one must first have a complete "reference book." The genome is too large for any single laboratory to measure; only through division of labor and collaboration can data be measured and shared in real time worldwide ([[p:division|Division of labor]], [[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]).
多国的测序中心分别承担不同染色体区段，先绘制图谱再测序；计算机把数以千万计的短片: Sequencing centers from multiple countries respectively undertake different chromosomal segments; first a map is drawn, then sequencing is performed; computers splice millions of short fragments into a complete sequence. All parties agreed to make the sequenced sequences public within 24 hours. Concurrently, the American company Celera launched competition using "whole-genome shotgun" methods, which objectively accelerated progress.
1990 年计划正式启动，美、英、日、法、德、中六国参与，中国承担了约 1% 的: The Human Genome Project was officially launched in 1990; six countries—United States, United Kingdom, Japan, France, Germany, and China—participated, with China undertaking approximately 1% of the sequencing task. A draft was announced in 2001, completion declared in 2003, costing approximately 2.7 billion US dollars. The remaining approximately 8% difficult-to-measure regions were not completed until 2022 by the "Telomere to Telomere" consortium.
人类基因组只有约两万个编码蛋白质的基因，远少于预期。这份参考序列成为现代医学和生: The human genome contains only about twenty thousand genes encoding proteins, far fewer than expected. This reference sequence became the infrastructure for modern medicine and biology, also driving rapid progress in sequencing technology (see [[ngs]]).
同时并行读取数百万到数十亿个 DNA 片段，让个人基因组测序降到千美元级。: Simultaneously reading millions to billions of DNA fragments allows personal genome sequencing to drop to the level of thousands of dollars.
一次只读一条 DNA，太慢。高通量测序把 DNA 打碎成数以亿计的短片段，固定在: Reading only one DNA strand at a time is too slow. High-throughput sequencing breaks DNA into hundreds of millions of short fragments, fixes them on chips for parallel sequencing, and then uses computers to reassemble them ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]).
主流的\"边合成边测序\"每次只让聚合酶接上一个带荧光的碱基，拍一张照片记录每个: The mainstream "sequencing by synthesis" method allows only one polymerase to attach a fluorescently labeled base at a time, taking a photograph to record the color of each point, then washing away the fluorescence to enter the next round. This process is repeated hundreds of times. Third-generation sequencing directly reads individual long molecules: one type lets DNA pass through a nanopore and identifies bases based on current changes; another observes single polymerases working in real time. Long-read sequencing is better at assembling complex regions.
2005 年 454 公司推出第一台商用高通量测序仪；2006–2007 年 S: In 2005, 454 Company launched the first commercial high-throughput sequencer; in 2006–2007, Solexa technology (later acquired by Illumina) emerged and became mainstream. Chinese companies such as BGI also developed their own sequencing platforms.
测一个人类基因组从数年、数亿美元降到一两天、数百美元。肿瘤基因检测、无创产前筛查: Sequencing a human genome has dropped from several years and hundreds of millions of dollars to one or two days and hundreds of dollars. Consequently, tumor gene testing, non-invasive prenatal screening, rapid pathogen identification, and large-scale population genetic studies have become reality.
检测基因变异来诊断遗传病、指导用药或做产前筛查。: Detecting genetic variations is used to diagnose hereditary diseases, guide medication, or perform prenatal screening.
许多疾病与特定基因变异有关：有的单个变异就会致病（如囊性纤维化），有的只增加风险: Many diseases are associated with specific genetic variations: some cause disease when a single variation occurs (such as cystic fibrosis), while others only increase risk (such as BRCA mutations increasing breast cancer risk). Detecting these variations can help with diagnosis, prediction, and treatment guidance ([[p:probability|Probability & statistical inference]]).
从血液或唾液中提取 DNA，用 PCR、芯片或测序检测目标基因，用于新生儿筛查、: DNA is extracted from blood or saliva; target genes are detected using PCR, chips, or sequencing for newborn screening, hereditary disease diagnosis, prenatal testing, and tumor medication. Many variations have unknown significance and require interpretation by genetic counselors.
1996 年起 BRCA 检测在美国商业化；2013 年美国最高法院裁定天然人类: BRCA testing began commercialization in the United States in 1996; in 2013, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that naturally occurring human genes cannot be patented.
基因检测让一些疾病能提前预防和精准治疗，也带来了隐私、歧视和心理负担等伦理问题。: Genetic testing enables early prevention and precise treatment for some diseases but also brings ethical issues such as privacy, discrimination, and psychological burden.
用计算机分析海量基因和蛋白质数据，是现代生物学的\"显微镜\"。: Using computers to analyze massive amounts of gene and protein data serves as the "microscope" of modern biology.
一个人的基因组就有 30 亿个字母，人眼看不过来。生物信息学用计算机比对、拼接和: A single human genome contains 3 billion letters, which the human eye cannot process. Bioinformatics uses computers to compare, assemble, and annotate sequences, finding patterns from massive data sets; it is the "new microscope" of biology ([[p:info|Information theory]]).
基本工具包括序列比对（看两段序列有多相似）、基因组组装、基因注释和进化树构建。公: Basic tools include sequence alignment (comparing how similar two sequences are), genome assembly, gene annotation, and phylogenetic tree construction. Public databases archive sequences from around the world, accessible to anyone for retrieval; machine learning is increasingly used to predict gene function and protein structure.
1965 年美国的戴霍夫（Margaret Dayhoff）编纂了第一部蛋白质序: In 1965, Margaret Dayhoff in the United States compiled the first protein sequence atlas; in 1982, the GenBank database was established; BLAST, released in 1990, became one of the most commonly used bioinformatics software programs.
从基因组计划到病毒变异追踪，现代生物学离不开计算。: From the genome project to viral variant tracking, modern biology cannot function without computation.
2012 年美国的杜德纳（Jennifer Doudna）和法国的卡彭蒂耶（Em: In 2012, Jennifer Doudna (American) and Emmanuelle Charpentier (French) proved that CRISPR-Cas9 can cut DNA according to design; they received the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. In 2013, Zhang Feng's team in the United States applied it to human cells. In 2018, He Jiankui violated regulations by editing a human embryo and causing its birth, receiving global condemnation and criminal punishment. In 2023, the UK and US approved the first CRISPR therapy for treating sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia.
基因编辑从少数实验室的高难技术，变成几乎所有生物实验室的日常工具，用于研究基因功: Gene editing has evolved from a difficult technology available only in a few laboratories to a daily tool for almost all biological laboratories, used for studying gene function, cultivating crops, and developing therapies. It also forces society to face the ethical question of "whether human genetics can be modified"; current international consensus is that heritable human embryo editing should not be conducted.
CRISPR-Cas9 的工作方式：向导 RNA 与目标 DNA 配对，Cas9: The working mechanism of CRISPR-Cas9: guide RNA pairs with target DNA, Cas9 cuts the double strand there; during cellular repair, a gene may be knocked out, or the sequence may be rewritten according to a template.
不切断 DNA 双链，直接把一个碱基改成另一个，更精准更安全。: Without cutting the DNA double strand, directly changing one base to another is more precise and safer.
许多遗传病只是一个碱基写错了。与其把 DNA 双链剪断再修，不如直接把错字\"涂: Many hereditary diseases are caused by a single base being written incorrectly. Rather than cutting the DNA double strand and repairing it, it is better to simply "correct" the typo, avoiding accidental insertions or deletions ([[p:dogma|Central dogma]]) brought by double-strand breaks.
碱基编辑器把一个\"只切单链\"的 Cas9 和一种能化学转换碱基的酶连在一起，: Base editors connect a "single-strand-cutting" Cas9 with an enzyme capable of chemically converting bases; guided by guide RNA, they are delivered to the target position to change C to T or A to G. Later "prime editing" can also perform small insertions and deletions.
2016 年美国华裔化学家刘如谦（David Liu）团队发表第一种碱基编辑器，: In 2016, David Liu's team (Chinese-American chemist in the United States) published the first base editor; in 2019, they invented prime editing. In 2025, an American doctor used a base editing therapy customized for a single patient to treat a rare metabolic disease.
碱基编辑让大量单碱基突变导致的疾病有了被\"直接修正\"的可能，已有多项疗法进入: Base editing makes it possible to "directly correct" many diseases caused by single-base mutations; numerous therapies have entered clinical trials.
把正常基因送入患者细胞或修复缺陷基因，治疗遗传病；2023 年首个 CRISPR: Introducing normal genes into patient cells or repairing defective genes treats hereditary diseases; in 2023, the first CRISPR therapy was approved.
如果疾病来自一个基因缺陷，最根本的办法就是把正常基因送进细胞，或者直接修复缺陷基: If a disease stems from a gene defect, the most fundamental method is to introduce a normal gene into cells or directly repair the defective gene ([[p:dogma|Central dogma]]).
**体外**疗法取出患者的细胞（如造血干细胞），在实验室中导入正常基因或进行编辑: **In vitro** therapies take patient cells (such as hematopoietic stem cells), import normal genes or perform editing in the laboratory, and then return them; **in vivo** therapies use modified harmless viruses (commonly aden-associated virus) or lipid nanoparticles to directly deliver genes to tissues such as eyes, liver, and muscle. Challenges lie in delivery efficiency, immune response, and long-term safety.
1990 年美国医生为一名患重症联合免疫缺陷的 4 岁女孩实施了第一例获批的基因: In 1990, a US doctor performed the first approved gene therapy on a 4-year-old girl suffering from severe combined immunodeficiency. In 1999, a young American died in a trial, causing the field to experience a low point. Starting in 2017, gene therapies for hereditary retinal diseases and spinal muscular atrophy were approved one after another; in 2023, the first CRISPR therapy was approved (see [[crispr]]).
一些过去无药可治的遗传病有了\"一次治疗、长期有效\"的可能。动辄上百万美元的价: Some genetic diseases that were once untreatable now have the possibility of "one-time treatment, long-term efficacy." Prices often reaching millions of dollars make payment and accessibility new challenges.
把体细胞核移入去核卵细胞培育出遗传上相同的个体，多莉羊是首个体细胞克隆哺乳动物。: Transferring a somatic cell nucleus into an enucleated egg cell to cultivate a genetically identical individual: Dolly the sheep was the first mammal cloned via somatic cell nuclear transfer.
每个体细胞的细胞核都带着全套基因组。把它放进去掉核的卵细胞，卵细胞能把它\"重新: Each somatic cell's nucleus carries a complete genome. Placing it into an enucleated egg cell allows the egg to "reprogram" it back to an embryonic state, developing into a genetically identical individual ([[p:dogma|Central dogma]]).
这种方法叫体细胞核移植。效率很低，多数重构胚胎无法正常发育，克隆动物也可能出现健: This method is called somatic cell nuclear transfer. Efficiency is very low; most reconstructed embryos fail to develop normally, and cloned animals may also experience health issues.
1962 年英国的格登（John Gurdon）用蛙证明成熟细胞核仍能发育成完整: In 1962, John Gurdon from the UK demonstrated that a mature cell nucleus could still develop into a complete organism using frogs. In July 1996, Ian Wilmut's team at the Roslin Institute in the UK cloned Dolly the sheep using adult sheep mammary gland cells, attempting over 270 times before success. In 2018, Chinese scientists cultivated the first batch of somatic cell-cloned monkeys.
多莉证明成熟细胞可以被重编程，启发了诱导多能干细胞研究（见 [[stem-cel: Dolly proved that mature cells can be reprogrammed, inspiring research on induced pluripotent stem cells (see [[stem-cells]]). Many countries prohibit human reproductive cloning.
能分化为多种细胞的\"种子细胞\"；山中伸弥用 4 个基因把普通细胞重新编程为干: "Seed cells" capable of differentiating into multiple cell types; Yoshiki Sasai from Japan used 4 genes to reprogram ordinary cells into stem cells.
受精卵能发育成身体的所有细胞，越往后发育，细胞的\"可能性\"越窄。干细胞是保留: A fertilized egg can develop into all body cells; the further development proceeds, the narrower the cell's "possibility." Stem cells are "seed cells" retaining differentiation potential: pluripotent stem cells can become almost any cell type, while adult stem cells (such as hematopoietic stem cells) can only become specific few types. Which direction to differentiate depends on which genes are turned on or off ([[p:dogma|Central dogma]]).
胚胎干细胞取自早期胚胎，有伦理争议。诱导多能干细胞（iPS）则通过导入几个关键基: Embryonic stem cells are derived from early-stage embryos and raise ethical controversies. Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPS) achieve a return to pluripotent state by introducing several key genes into ordinary skin or blood cells, then inducing differentiation into neural, cardiac, pancreatic, and other cell types for disease research, drug screening, and cellular replacement therapy (see [[organoid]]).
1998 年美国的汤姆森（James Thomson）首次培养出人类胚胎干细胞。: In 1998, James Thomson from the US first cultured human embryonic stem cells. In 2006, Yoshiki Sasai from Kyoto University in Japan used 4 genes to reprogram mouse cells into iPS cells; the following year it was achieved in human cells, and he received the Nobel Prize in 2012.
干细胞来源的视网膜细胞、神经元和胰岛细胞已进入临床试验。许多商业\"干细胞疗法\: Retinal cells, neurons, and pancreatic cells derived from stem cells have entered clinical trials. Many commercial "stem cell therapies" lack rigorous verification and require caution.
用干细胞在培养皿中长出的微型器官，用于研究疾病和测试药物。: Micro-organoids grown from stem cells in culture dishes are used for disease research and drug testing.
干细胞在合适的三维环境和信号分子作用下，会按照自身的发育程序自我组织，长出具有器: Under appropriate three-dimensional environments and signaling molecules, stem cells self-organize according to their own developmental programs, growing into miniature tissues with partial organ structures and functions ([[p:dogma|Central dogma]]).
把干细胞包埋在凝胶状的基质里，加入特定的生长因子，培养数周就能形成肠、肝、肾、脑: Encapsulating stem cells in gelatinous matrices and adding specific growth factors allows formation of millimeter-sized organoids such as intestinal, hepatic, renal, and cerebral types after several weeks of culture. Using a patient's own cells for culture enables testing which drug is more effective against their tumor in the culture dish. They still lack blood vessels and complete immune systems.
2009 年荷兰的克莱弗斯（Hans Clevers）团队用单个肠道干细胞培养出: In 2009, Hans Clevers' team from the Netherlands cultured intestinal organoids from a single intestinal stem cell; in 2013, cerebral organoids appeared.
类器官为研究人类疾病提供了比动物更接近人体的模型，有望减少部分动物实验。: Organoids provide models for studying human diseases that are closer to humans than animal experiments, potentially reducing some animal testing.
在体外让卵子受精、培养成胚胎后移回子宫；第一个试管婴儿于 1978 年诞生。: Fertilizing eggs in vitro and culturing them into embryos before transferring them back to the uterus: the first test-tube baby was born in 1978.
受精和最初几天的胚胎发育不一定要在体内进行。只要模拟输卵管里的温度、营养和气体环: Fertilization and initial embryonic development do not necessarily need to occur within the body. As long as temperature, nutrition, and gas environments inside fallopian tubes are simulated, eggs and sperm can combine in culture dishes to develop into early-stage embryos, which are then transferred back to the uterus for implantation ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]).
先用激素促使卵巢一次排出多个卵子，用细针取出，在实验室中与精子结合；精子太弱时，: First, hormones are used to induce the ovaries to release multiple eggs at once; they are extracted via fine needles and combined with sperm in the laboratory. When sperm is too weak, single sperm can be directly injected into the egg. Embryos are cultured for 3–5 days before being transferred back to the uterus; excess ones can be frozen for storage. Chromosome testing of embryos can also be conducted before transplantation.
1978 年 7 月 25 日，第一个试管婴儿路易丝·布朗在英国诞生，主导者是生: On July 25, 1978, Louise Brown, the first test-tube baby, was born in the UK under the leadership of physiologist Robert Edwards (who received the Nobel Prize in 2010) and obstetrician Steptoe. In 1988, China's first test-tube baby was born in Beijing.
全球已有超过一千万人通过辅助生殖技术出生。它也引发了关于胚胎地位、代孕和胚胎检测: Over ten million people worldwide have been born through assisted reproductive technologies. It has also sparked discussions regarding embryo status, surrogacy, and boundaries of embryo testing.
像设计电路一样设计基因线路，让微生物生产药物、材料和燃料。: Designing gene circuits like designing electronic circuits allows microorganisms to produce drugs, materials, and fuels.
如果把基因、启动子等 DNA 片段看作标准化的\"元件\"，就能像设计电路一样，: If genes, promoters, and other DNA fragments are viewed as standardized "components," one can combine them like designing circuits to create "gene circuits" with specific functions: switches, oscillators, sensors ([[p:abstraction|Abstraction & layering]], [[p:dogma|Central dogma]]).
先在计算机上设计线路，再合成 DNA，装进细菌或酵母，测试、调整，形成\"设计—: First, design the circuit on a computer, then synthesize DNA, load it into bacteria or yeast, test and adjust, forming the 'design-build-test-learn' cycle. Automation platforms and AI make this cycle faster and faster. Applications include using yeast to produce precursors for anti-malarial drugs and spices, using bacteria to detect pollutants, and modifying cells for therapy.
2000 年 1 月，美国两个团队在同一期《自然》上分别发表了人工\"拨动开关\: In January 2000, two teams in the US published artificial 'toggle switch' and 'oscillator' gene circuits in the same issue of *Nature*, regarded as the starting point of synthetic biology. In 2010, J. Craig Venter's institute created the first bacterium controlled by an artificially synthesized genome.
部分药物、材料和食品成分改由微生物生产（见 [[precision-fermen: Some drugs, materials, and food components are now produced by microorganisms (see [[precision-fermentation]]); it also brings concerns about biosafety, requiring corresponding regulation.
在大罐中培养微生物或细胞，量产抗生素、疫苗、酶和蛋白药。: Cultivate microorganisms or cells in large tanks to mass-produce antibiotics, vaccines, enzymes, and protein drugs.
微生物和细胞是微型化工厂。只要给它们合适的温度、酸碱度、营养和氧气，并防止杂菌污: Microorganisms and cells are miniature factories. As long as they are given suitable temperature, pH, nutrients, and oxygen, and contamination by other microbes is prevented, antibiotics, enzymes, vaccines, and protein drugs can be produced on a large scale in large tanks ([[p:scale|Economies of scale & learning curves]]).
不锈钢发酵罐可达数百立方米，搅拌桨和通气系统让氧气均匀溶解，传感器实时监测温度、: Stainless steel fermenters can reach several hundred cubic meters; stirring paddles and aeration systems ensure uniform dissolution of oxygen, while sensors monitor temperature, dissolved oxygen, and pH in real time and automatically adjust. Complex protein drugs like antibodies are often produced by culturing Chinese hamster ovary cells in bioreactors.
1943–1944 年美国药厂开发出青霉素的深罐发酵工艺，产量剧增，赶上了诺曼底: In 1943–1944, US pharmaceutical companies developed deep-tank fermentation processes for penicillin, causing a dramatic increase in yield to meet the demand of the Normandy landings.
发酵工程是抗生素、疫苗和生物药能便宜、大量供应的基础，也是合成生物学走向产业的关: Fermentation engineering is the foundation that allows antibiotics, vaccines, and biopharmaceuticals to be supplied cheaply and in large quantities; it is also a key link for synthetic biology to move toward industry.
从 X 射线晶体学到冷冻电镜，再到 AlphaFold 预测，看清蛋白质的三维形: From X-ray crystallography to cryo-electron microscopy, and then to AlphaFold prediction: only by seeing the three-dimensional shape of proteins can one design drugs.
蛋白质由氨基酸链折叠而成，三维形状决定了它能和什么分子结合、发挥什么功能（[[p: Proteins are folded from chains of amino acids; their three-dimensional shape determines what molecules they can bind to and what functions they perform ([[p:structure|Structure determines properties]]). Seeing the shape allows understanding disease mechanisms and designing drugs that fit exactly 'into' them ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]).
**X 射线晶体学**从蛋白质晶体的衍射图案反推原子位置（见 [[x-ray-c: **X-ray crystallography** infers atomic positions from diffraction patterns of protein crystals (see [[x-ray-crystallography]]); **cryo-electron microscopy** takes photos of proteins flash-frozen from thousands or tens of thousands of angles and then reconstructs them (see [[electron-microscope]]), without needing crystallization; **AI prediction** directly calculates structure from amino acid sequences (see [[ai-for-science]]).
1958 年英国的肯德鲁（John Kendrew）解析出第一个蛋白质（肌红蛋白: In 1958, John Kendrew in the UK solved the structure of the first protein (myoglobin), sharing the 1962 Nobel Prize with Perutz. The founders of cryo-electron microscopy won the 2017 Nobel Prize. In 2020, AlphaFold's prediction accuracy approached experimental results; its developers Demis Hassabis, John Jumper, and protein design pioneer David Baker shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
已知结构从几十万个跃升到上亿个（多为 AI 预测），药物设计和酶工程大大提速，\: Known structures jumped from hundreds of thousands to over a hundred million (mostly AI-predicted), greatly speeding up drug design and enzyme engineering, making 'de novo design' of new proteins possible.
人体内外数以万亿计的微生物参与消化、免疫和代谢，测序技术让我们第一次看清它们。: Trillions of microorganisms inside and outside the human body participate in digestion, immunity, and metabolism; sequencing technology allows us to see them for the first time.
人体内外生活着数量与人体细胞相当的微生物，主要在肠道。它们帮我们消化纤维、合成维: Microorganisms living inside and outside the human body are as numerous as human cells, mainly in the gut. They help us digest fiber, synthesize vitamins, train the immune system, and have co-evolved with humans over a long period ([[p:evolution|Natural selection]]).
多数肠道细菌无法在实验室培养。高通量测序（见 [[ngs]]）可以直接读取粪便中: Most gut bacteria cannot be cultured in the laboratory. High-throughput sequencing (see [[ngs]]) can directly read microbial DNA in feces to statistically identify which types exist and their proportions. Studies found associations between the microbiome with obesity, colitis, and other diseases, but many are correlations rather than causation.
2007 年美国国立卫生研究院启动人类微生物组计划。粪菌移植治疗反复发作的艰难梭: In 2007, the US National Institutes of Health launched the Human Microbiome Project. Fecal microbiota transplantation treatment for recurrent *Clostridioides difficile* infection shows significant efficacy; related products were approved in the US in 2022.
微生物组让人们重新认识\"人体\"；市售益生菌的功效则大多缺乏充分证据。: The microbiome has led people to reconsider what 'human' means; however, the efficacy of most commercially available probiotics lacks sufficient evidence.
把感光蛋白基因装入神经元，用光精确开关特定神经细胞。: Load photoprotein genes into neurons and use light to precisely switch on or off specific nerve cells.
某些藻类有一种感光蛋白，受蓝光照射就打开离子通道。把它的基因装进特定神经元，光一: Certain algae have a photoprotein that opens ion channels upon exposure to blue light. Load its gene into specific neurons; when exposed to light, these neurons fire; switching to other photoproteins can also make neurons 'quiet' ([[p:dogma|Central dogma]]).
用病毒载体把感光蛋白基因只送进某一类神经元，再通过植入的光纤照射脑区，以毫秒级精: Use viral vectors to deliver photoprotein genes only into a certain type of neuron, then use implanted optical fibers to irradiate brain regions with millisecond precision to switch these cells on or off, observe changes in animal behavior, and determine 'which cells are responsible for what'.
2005 年美国斯坦福大学的戴瑟罗斯（Karl Deisseroth）和博伊登（: In 2005, Karl Deisseroth and Edward Boyden at Stanford University in the US first used light to precisely control mammalian neurons. In 2021, researchers reported using optogenetic therapy to partially restore vision in a blind person.
光遗传学成为神经科学最重要的工具之一，帮助解析了记忆、恐惧、成瘾等行为的神经回路: Optogenetics has become one of the most important tools in neuroscience, helping to analyze neural circuits for memory, fear, addiction, and other behaviors.
让细胞在体外培养皿中持续生长；1951 年建立的 HeLa 细胞系是第一株人类\: Allow cells to grow continuously in vitro culture dishes; the HeLa cell line established in 1951 was the first human 'immortal' cell line, supporting vaccine production and countless research studies.
细胞离开身体后，只要有营养、生长因子、适宜温度和无菌环境，就能继续生存和分裂（[: Once a cell is removed from the body, it can continue to survive and divide as long as it has nutrients, growth factors, suitable temperature, and a sterile environment ([[p:homeostasis|Homeostasis]]). Normal cells stop dividing after several dozen generations, but some cell lines can be passed indefinitely.
细胞在培养瓶里生长，放在 37°C、含 5% 二氧化碳的培养箱中，长满后分瓶继续: Cells grow in culture flasks and are placed in incubators at 37°C containing 5% carbon dioxide. After they become confluent, they are subcultured into new flasks for continued growth or frozen for storage. They are used to study diseases, test drugs, and produce viral vaccines and biologics.
1951 年美国约翰斯·霍普金斯医院的研究者从癌症患者亨丽埃塔·拉克斯的肿瘤组织: In 1951, researchers at Johns Hopkins Hospital in the United States established the HeLa cell line from tumor tissue of cancer patient Henrietta Lacks. This was the first human cell line capable of long-term passage, which was quickly used for polio vaccine development (see [[polio-vaccine]]). Consent was not obtained from the patient when the sample was taken.
细胞培养是生物医学研究和生物制药的基础；HeLa 的故事也推动了知情同意的伦理讨: Cell culture is the foundation of biomedical research and biopharmaceutical production; the story of HeLa also advanced ethical discussions regarding informed consent.
一小段双链 RNA 能让细胞销毁对应的信使 RNA，从而\"关掉\"一个基因；2: A short segment of double-stranded RNA allows cells to destroy the corresponding messenger RNA, thereby "turning off" a gene; the first RNAi drug was approved in 2018.
基因要先转录成信使 RNA，才能指导合成蛋白质（[[p:dogma|中心法则]]: Genes must first be transcribed into messenger RNA before they can guide the synthesis of proteins ([[p:dogma|Central dogma]]). Inside cells, there is a mechanism: a short segment of double-stranded RNA guides a protein complex to find and cut up messenger RNA with complementary sequences; this gene is then "silenced" ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]).
药物人工合成针对致病基因的小干扰 RNA，用脂质纳米颗粒或能被肝细胞识别的化学\: Drugs are artificially synthesized to target small interfering RNAs against pathogenic genes, delivered into cells using lipid nanoparticles or chemical "tags" that can be recognized by liver cells. Some drugs require only two injections per year.
1998 年美国的法尔（Andrew Fire）和梅洛（Craig Mello）: In 1998, Andrew Fire and Craig Mello in the United States discovered RNA interference in nematodes; they received the Nobel Prize in 2006. The first RNA interference drug was approved in 2018 for a rare hereditary amyloidosis.
RNA 干扰是研究基因功能的常用工具，也开辟了\"沉默致病基因\"的新一类药物。: RNA interference is a common tool for studying gene function and has opened up a new class of drugs for "silencing pathogenic genes".
给酶制造随机突变、挑出表现最好的再突变，像育种一样在试管里\"进化\"出新蛋白；: Enzymes are subjected to random mutations, the best performers are selected, and then mutated again; this is like "evolving" new proteins in test tubes. The Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded in 2018.
自然选择不需要设计师：随机突变加严格筛选，就能一代代积累有益的变化（[[p:ev: Natural selection does not require a designer: random mutation combined with strict selection can accumulate beneficial changes over generations ([[p:evolution|Natural selection]]). Simulating this process in a test tube allows for the "evolution" of enzymes that better meet human needs.
给某个酶的基因制造大量随机突变，表达出成千上万种变体，挑出性能最好的几个，再以它: A large number of random mutations are introduced into the gene of an enzyme, resulting in thousands or tens of thousands of variants; the best-performing ones are selected, and then used as starting points to repeat mutation and selection. After several rounds, the enzyme may become heat-stable, solvent-tolerant, or even catalyze entirely new reactions.
1993 年美国加州理工学院的阿诺德（Frances Arnold）首次用定向进: In 1993, Frances Arnold from Caltech in the United States first used directed evolution to make an enzyme work efficiently in organic solvents; she received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2018.
定向进化得到的酶用于洗涤剂、生物燃料和药物合成，减少了化工过程的能耗和污染，也是: Enzymes obtained through directed evolution are used in detergents, biofuels, and drug synthesis, reducing energy consumption and pollution in chemical processes. They are also a core method of protein engineering.
塔尔发明的条播机把种子按行按深度播下，出苗率更高。: Tull's seed drill planted seeds in rows and at specific depths, resulting in higher germination rates.
把种子放到统一的深度和间距，每粒种子得到的水、光和养分更均匀，出苗率和产量就更稳: Placing seeds at uniform depth and spacing ensures that each seed receives more even water, light, and nutrients, leading to more stable germination rates and yields—this was the earliest form of "standardization" in agriculture.
条播机由马拉动，前面的开沟器在土里划出浅沟，种子从料斗经过带槽的旋转滚筒一粒粒落: The seed drill was pulled by a horse; the furrow opener cut shallow grooves in the soil, seeds fell one by one from a hopper through a rotating roller with slots, and the subsequent harrow covered the soil immediately.
英国农学家杰思罗·塔尔（Jethro Tull）1701 年前后造出实用的马拉条: British agriculturalist Jethro Tull created a practical horse-drawn seed drill around 1701 and promoted "planting in rows with frequent hoeing" in his 1731 work, "Horse-Ploughing".
条播让播种从凭手感变成可重复的机械动作，也为后来的播种机、精量播种机开了头。: The seed drill turned planting from a matter of feel into a repeatable mechanical action, paving the way for later seeders and precision planters.
中国早在汉代就有\"耧车\"这种畜力条播工具；塔尔的贡献是把它机械化并在欧洲推广: China had such animal-drawn seed drills as the "louche" as early as the Han Dynasty; Tull's contribution was to mechanize it and promote it in Europe.
小麦、芜菁、大麦、苜蓿四年轮种，豆科植物固氮，田地不必休耕。: Wheat, turnip, barley, and alfalfa were rotated in four-year cycles; leguminous plants fixed nitrogen, so fields did not need fallow periods.
豆科植物根部的根瘤菌能把空气中的氮\"固定\"成植物可用的氮肥；把它排进轮作，田: Rhizobia bacteria at the roots of leguminous plants can "fix" atmospheric nitrogen into plant-available nitrogen fertilizer; by rotating them into the crop sequence, fields can "recharge" themselves.
诺福克四区轮作把田分成四块，按小麦 → 芜菁 → 大麦 → 三叶草（或苜蓿）的顺: The Norfolk four-field system divided fields into four plots, rotating annually in the order: wheat → turnip → barley → clover (or alfalfa). Turnips and clover could feed livestock, whose manure returned to the field; clover fixed nitrogen while cereal crops consumed it, so soil fertility no longer needed fallow periods for recovery.
18 世纪 30 年代起在英国诺福克郡推广，政治家\"芜菁\"汤森勋爵（Char: Promoted from the 1730s in Norfolk County, England; Lord Townshend (Charles Townshend), known as "the turnip lord," was a famous advocate. It replaced the medieval "three-field system" practice of leaving one-third of land fallow each year.
同样的土地既多产粮又多养牲畜，是英国农业革命的核心，为工业革命提供了粮食和劳动力: Land capable of producing both grain and livestock was the core of the British Agricultural Revolution, providing food and labor for the Industrial Revolution.
麦考密克收割机让一个人一天能收割的面积成倍增加。: The McCormick reaper allowed one person to harvest an area that increased multiple times per day.
把镰刀的往复切割交给齿轮和刀片，用马的力量代替人的手臂——[[p:leverag: By entrusting the reciprocating cutting of a sickle to gears and blades, using horse power instead of human arms—[[p:leverage|Mechanical advantage]] allowing one person to do the work of ten.
收割机由马拉动，轮子转动时通过齿轮带动一排锯齿状刀片来回切割；前方的拨禾轮把麦秆: The reaper was pulled by horses; when the wheels turned, gears drove a row of serrated blades back and forth to cut; the header in front pushed stalks against the blades, cutting wheat that fell onto a platform behind, where people raked and bundled it.
美国人赛勒斯·麦考密克（Cyrus McCormick）1831 年演示收割机，: American Cyrus McCormick (Cyrus McCormick) demonstrated the reaper in 1831, obtained a patent in 1834, later built factories in Chicago for mass production; at the same time, Obed Hussey also created a reaper, and the two engaged in long-running patent lawsuits.
收割是农忙中最缺人手的环节，收割机让美国中西部的大平原得以大面积种麦，也让大量农: Harvesting was the most labor-intensive part of farming; the reaper allowed the Great Plains of the American Midwest to be cultivated on a large scale, and enabled a large flow of rural labor into urban factories.
便宜的带刺铁丝让大面积圈地放牧成为可能，改变了美国西部，也被用于战争。: Cheap barbed wire made it possible to fence off large areas for grazing, changing the American West and also being used in wars.
铁丝本身很便宜，但扭上尖刺后，牲畜碰到会疼而后退——用一点点材料制造\"心理障碍: The wire itself was cheap, but when twisted with sharp points, livestock would feel pain and retreat upon contact—creating a 'psychological barrier' with a small amount of material was far cheaper than building walls.
两股钢丝绞在一起，每隔一段夹进一根短的带尖铁丝。拉紧后钉在木桩上，几道铁丝就能围: Two strands of steel wire were twisted together, with short barbed wires inserted between them at intervals. After tightening, they were driven into wooden stakes; several strands of wire could enclose a large pasture. Galvanized steel wire resists rust, and machines can produce hundreds of kilometers per day.
1874 年美国伊利诺伊州农民约瑟夫·格利登（Joseph Glidden）获得: In 1874, American farmer Joseph Glidden (Joseph Glidden) from Illinois obtained a patent for an easily mass-produced barbed wire, which was then produced on a large scale and quickly spread across the American West.
铁丝网让大草原上的开放放牧结束，土地被私有化和分割，牛仔时代随之落幕。它后来又被: Barbed wire ended open grazing on the Great Plains; land was privatized and subdivided, marking the end of the cowboy era. It was later used in trenches, borders, and concentration camps, becoming a symbol of conflict and isolation.
用内燃机代替牛马拉犁，农业劳动力需求大幅下降。: Replacing oxen with internal combustion engines for plowing drastically reduced the demand for agricultural labor.
内燃机把石油里的化学能变成持续的牵引力，一台拖拉机的功率相当于几十匹马，而且不用: Internal combustion engines converted chemical energy from petroleum into continuous traction; one tractor's power equaled that of dozens of horses, and it did not need to eat grass or get tired—[[p:energy|energy]] brought in from outside the fields.
拖拉机用低转速、大扭矩的发动机驱动大轮子，后部有牵引挂钩和动力输出轴（PTO）。: Tractors used low-speed, high-torque engines to drive large wheels; the rear had a drawbar and a Power Take-Off (PTO). Equipped with plows, harrows, seeders, or harvesters, one machine could complete most farm work throughout the year; hydraulic lift mechanisms allowed tools to be raised and lowered at any time.
1892 年美国人约翰·弗罗利克（John Froelich）造出了可工作的汽油: In 1892, American John Froelich (John Froelich) created a working gasoline tractor. In 1917, Ford launched the affordable Fordson, using assembly-line production to make it affordable for small farms. In the 1920s, British Harry Ferguson (Harry Ferguson) invented the three-point hitch system, connecting implements and tractors into a single unit, which remains the standard today.
拖拉机替代了数以千万计的役畜，原来用来种饲料的土地改种粮食。美国农业人口占比从: Tractors replaced tens of millions of draft animals; land previously used to grow feed was converted to grain crops. The proportion of the US population engaged in agriculture fell from about 40% in 1900 to less than 2% today; modern large tractors are also equipped with satellite autonomous driving (see [[precision-agriculture]]).
一台机器同时完成收割、脱粒和清选。: One machine simultaneously completes harvesting, threshing, and cleaning.
把收割、脱粒、清选三道工序串在一台机器里流水作业，省掉了中间的搬运和晾晒——这是: By stringing together the processes of harvesting, threshing, and cleaning in one machine for continuous flow production, intermediate transport and drying were eliminated—this is [[p:division|division of labor]] being 'compressed' into one machine.
机器前方的割台把作物割下送入机身，滚筒高速旋转把籽粒从穗上打下来，筛子和风扇把籽: The header at the front cuts crops and feeds them into the body; a roller rotates at high speed to knock grains off the stalks; screens and fans separate grains from straw and chaff, with clean grain entering the grain bin and straw exiting from the rear or being chopped and returned to the soil. Drivers can change headers based on crop types.
1830 年代美国人海勒姆·摩尔（Hiram Moore）造出由马队牵引的联合收: In the 1830s, American Hiram Moore (Hiram Moore) created a horse-drawn combine harvester. From the 1930s, self-propelled combines became widespread; modern large models are equipped with yield sensors and satellite navigation.
小麦从割到入仓可以在一天内完成，收获季节的劳动力需求下降了一个数量级。: Wheat could be harvested from cutting to storage within one day; labor demand during harvest season decreased by an order of magnitude.
直接给作物补充氮、磷、钾；合成氨氮肥支撑了 20 世纪的人口增长。: Directly supplementing crops with nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium; synthetic ammonia-based nitrogen fertilizer supported population growth in the 20th century.
作物的产量受最缺的那种养分限制（\"最小因子定律\"）。氮、磷、钾是最常见的短板: Crop yield is limited by the most scarce nutrient ('Law of the Minimum Factor'). Nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium are the most common bottlenecks, with nitrogen being most critical: nearly 80% of the atmosphere is nitrogen, but plants cannot use it directly; only by converting it into ammonium or nitrate, [[p:photosynthesis|Photosynthesis]] created sugars can become protein.
**氮肥**主要来自合成氨：在高温高压和铁催化剂下，让空气中的氮和天然气制得的氢: **Nitrogen fertilizer** mainly comes from synthetic ammonia: under high temperature and pressure with iron catalysts, nitrogen from the air combines with hydrogen obtained from natural gas to form ammonia (see [[haber-bosch]]), which is then processed into urea and other products. **Phosphate fertilizer** is made by treating phosphate ore with sulfuric acid to produce superphosphate that plants can absorb. **Potassium fertilizer** comes from mined potassium salt deposits.
施肥就是给土壤\"补账\"：每收走一吨粮食，就带走了土里的一部分氮磷钾，不补回来: Fertilization is essentially 'making up for the soil's account': for every ton of grain harvested, a portion of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium in the soil is removed; if this is not replenished, the land will become increasingly depleted with each planting cycle.
1840 年德国化学家李比希（Justus von Liebig）提出植物靠矿物: In 1840, German chemist Justus von Liebig proposed that plants grow by absorbing mineral nutrients. In 1842, Britisher John Bennet Lawes obtained a patent for superphosphate and founded the Rothamsted Experimental Station the following year. During the 19th century, the main sources of nitrogen were Peruvian guano and Chilean nitre; in 1913, the Haber-Bosch process for synthesizing ammonia went into production, allowing nitrogen fertilizers to be produced infinitely from the air.
据研究者估算，今天全世界约一半人口的口粮依赖合成氮肥。代价同样巨大：作物只吸收施: Researchers estimate that today, about half of the global population's staple food depends on synthetic nitrogen fertilizers. The cost is equally huge: crops only absorb a portion of the applied nitrogen fertilizer; the remainder flows into rivers and lakes, causing [[eutrophication|eutrophication]], or transforms into the potent greenhouse gas nitrous oxide; the synthesis of ammonia itself also consumes approximately 1–2% of global energy.
\"化肥让土地变坏\"不准确。问题在于用量和方式：只施化肥、不还有机质，土壤结构: "Fertilizers make land worse" is inaccurate. The issue lies in usage quantity and method: applying only fertilizers without organic matter causes soil structure to deteriorate; however, applying fertilizers according to need in combination with organic fertilizer makes them a part of sustainable agriculture.
氮从空气到餐桌的旅程。合成氨把惰性的氮气变成作物可吸收的形态，但施入田里的氮只有: The journey of nitrogen from the air to the table. Synthetic ammonia converts inert nitrogen gas into a form that crops can absorb, but only a portion of the nitrogen applied to fields ultimately enters the food supply.
杀灭害虫、杂草和病菌的化学品；DDT 曾挽救无数生命，也因生态危害被禁用。: Chemicals used to kill pests, weeds, and pathogens; DDT once saved countless lives but was banned due to ecological harm.
农药是专门针对某类生物的\"钥匙\"：它卡住害虫神经或杂草酶等特定分子（[[p:: Pesticides are 'keys' specifically targeting certain organisms: they block specific molecules such as pest nerves or weed enzymes ([[p:recognition|Molecular recognition]]). However, whenever pesticides are used, it is essentially screening for individuals that can resist them—[[p:evolution|Natural selection]] will inevitably lead to the emergence of resistance.
按对象分为杀虫剂、除草剂和杀菌剂。早期有机氯杀虫剂（如 DDT）残留期长、在食物: Categorized by target object into insecticides, herbicides, and fungicides. Early organic chlorine insecticides (such as DDT) had long residual periods and accumulated in the food chain; later organic phosphorus, pyrethroid, and neonicotinoid types are easier to degrade but each has its own toxicity issues. The herbicide glyphosate kills weeds by blocking a specific type of synthesis enzyme unique to plants, and is most widely used in conjunction with glyphosate-resistant genetically modified crops.
1939 年瑞士化学家保罗·穆勒（Paul Müller）发现 DDT 的杀虫作: In 1939, Swiss chemist Paul Müller discovered the insecticidal effect of DDT; he received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1948. DDT was extensively used for mosquito control and malaria prevention during World War II and after the war. In 1962, Rachel Carson published 'Silent Spring', revealing the harm of pesticides to birds and ecosystems. The United States banned DDT for agricultural use in 1972.
农药大幅减少了虫害和杂草造成的减产，也催生了现代环境保护运动和农药登记制度。: Pesticides significantly reduced yield losses caused by pests and weeds, and also gave birth to modern environmental protection movements and pesticide registration systems.
结合天敌、轮作、监测和精准用药控制害虫，减少农药用量和抗药性。: Control pests by combining natural enemies, crop rotation, monitoring, and precise application of pesticides, thereby reducing pesticide usage and resistance.
把害虫数量压到\"不造成经济损失\"的水平就够了，不必赶尽杀绝；用多种手段一起控: It is sufficient to keep pest numbers at a level that 'does not cause economic loss'; there is no need to kill them all. Using multiple means together for control makes it difficult for pests to develop resistance to all methods simultaneously.
